recommendations.summary: No young player is being starved of opportunity he's earned; the scratched group all sit below 0.25 pts/g and the dressed group are producing at their assigned roles.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza 0.19 pts/g in 26 games, Gardener 0 in 23, Colaiacovo 0.12 in 25, Upshall 0.21 in 33 — all scratched on production, not deployment. Chlup, Nash, Chistov and Klesla carry full roles and produce. Spacek at 20 on the fourth line at 4.8 MPG is appropriately slotted.

recommendations.summary: Spezza's season is a development write-off; his next camp assignment is the only lever that matters for him.
recommendations.rationale: 5 points in 26 games on 5.4 MPG at age 22 with POTE 99. His minutes collapsed from 9.1 to 4.8 and his rate fell simultaneously. No in-season deployment fix recovers a season at 0.19 pts/g.

recommendations.summary: Chlup is confirmed as the first-line centre: 0.76 pts/g on 21.1 minutes at 19, holding his production on doubled minutes from last season.
recommendations.rationale: Went 0.62 to 0.88 last season on rising minutes, now 0.76 on 21.1 MPG this year. The step-up is real and he is holding it.

recommendations.summary: Chistov has broken through: 0.69 pts/g on 21.1 minutes at 22. He belongs in the top six permanently.
recommendations.rationale: Minutes went from 6 to 21 and his rate held at 0.69 across 43 games. That is a top-six winger proving himself on a top-six load.

recommendations.summary: Spezza's season is a write-off at 0.19 pts/g on 5.4 minutes. Flag him for a hard camp assignment next offseason.
recommendations.rationale: 26 games at 0.19 and 5.4 MPG at age 22. POTE 99 means the upside is there but this season teaches him nothing. The only lever is next camp's line assignment.

recommendations.summary: Gardener (0 pts, 3 MPG), Upshall (0.19, 5.2 MPG), and Spacek (0.19, 4 MPG) are all in the collapse pattern for a second season. The fix is a camp rule, not a mid-season change.
recommendations.rationale: Third season of the same pattern: young forwards get 13-17 MPG early, collapse below 6 with no production. Mid-season scratching is already happening via minutes. Next camp needs a hard role assignment or the cycle repeats.

recommendations.summary: Eminger at 0.53 in 17 games on 16.1 minutes with an expiring contract is a live trade card right now. His contract expires after this season.
recommendations.rationale: Recovered from last season's 0.38 slide to 0.53 this year. A buyer sees current production at 22 with 16 MPG. After July he is a UFA loss.

recommendations.summary: Jackman's rate is 0.62, sliding from 0.70. His sell trigger is 0.55. The trade window is still open but closing; if he crosses 0.55 he stays.
recommendations.rationale: Dec 29 heater ended. Rate: 0.70 at 37 GP, now 0.62 at 43 GP. Five to eight more games at this pace puts him below the trigger.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes warranted by development trends tonight. The two bright spots (Chlup, Chistov) are already in top roles; the struggling kids are already benched by minutes.
recommendations.rationale: The development story this season is structural (camp assignments, not tonight's lines). The veterans are holding: Sundin 0.86 at 34, Mogilny 0.74 at 36, Kaberle 0.57 at 27.

recommendations.summary: Move Richards up to the second line; 30 points in 43 games on 12.5 MPG earns closer to 17, and his morale at 88 is the lowest on the dressing list.
recommendations.rationale: Richards is producing 0.70 pts/g and is an 80s-calibre centre. At 12.5 MPG he's getting 70% of what his calibre expects. The morale drop is the signal.

recommendations.summary: Luongo at 85 is results-driven and not fixable from the lines; no action available.
recommendations.rationale: Goalie morale tracks wins. At 60 MPG there is no minutes lever. Winning will bring it back.

recommendations.proposed: Insert Roberts on L4 if this is a maximize night
recommendations.summary: Put Roberts on the fourth line for games where we cannot afford a faceoff mean of 52 and a checking mean of 63.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts has 84 checking and 72 toughness, second on the roster behind Jackman. L4's current checking mean is 63 and toughness 58. He fixes the identity problem without breaking any working unit.

recommendations.summary: L1, L2, L3, P1, P2, K1 and K2 are correctly composed.
recommendations.rationale: K1 has a checking mean of 84 with Jackman at 94 carrying the top. P1 pairs Sundin's 95 faceoffs with Jackman's 93 toughness at net-front. L2 has Nash at 92 checking. No unit is misbuilt.

recommendations.slot: shutdown defenceman or second elite checker
recommendations.summary: We are one elite checker deep. Jackman (92) is the only dressed player above 84 checking; Roberts (84) is the next and he is 38. A seven-game playoff series against a physical team needs two players who can shadow a top line for 20 minutes.
recommendations.rationale: The checking inventory is Jackman 92, Roberts 84 (scratched), McCabe 83, Nash 82. Below those the next name is Eminger at some grade below 83. No arrangement of this roster produces two sustained shutdown units.

recommendations.summary: No line changes for NYR. Our current construction already matches well: pair one against their aging first pair, pair two wears down Malakhov, pair three faces a 68 OVR defenceman.
recommendations.rationale: We are 3-0-0 vs NYR this season (15-7 goals). Their first pair Leetch/Jonsson cannot cover Klesla (SPEE 99) or Gaborik (99 OVR). Their third line is gutted without Kelly. No structural mismatch to fix.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo. No fatigue icon on the sheet today.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 95 OVR against Blackburn at 83. NYR scores 3.70 per game; Luongo's SREC 98 and AGIL 99 are built for this kind of night.

recommendations.summary: Sell McCabe before the deadline while his last-8-game line (6 pts, 0.75 pts/g) makes the trade sheet look palatable; season rate 0.50 is below the 0.60 threshold and he is 30 at $3.00M x 3.
recommendations.rationale: McCabe jumped from 0.30 in 10 games to 0.50 in 18, a 0.75 stretch rate over his last 8. That is the best window since I put him back on the sell list in December. After this cools the card gets harder to move.

recommendations.summary: Jackman at 0.63 pts/g (27 in 43) stays above the 0.55 sell trigger; no change this week, but he is on pace to cross it in roughly 20 games.
recommendations.rationale: The slide from the Dec 29 heater (0.70 at 37 GP) slowed to about 0.17 pts/g over the last 6 games. He is still sellable through the deadline. Reassess after 5 more games.

recommendations.summary: Klesla confirmed deadline sell unchanged: 87 OVR, 0.42 pts/g over 43 games, $0.90M expiring. Rate dipped slightly from 0.45 last report.
recommendations.rationale: The buyer sees 87 and a cheap expiring contract. The 0.42 production is invisible to him. Sell window remains wide.

recommendations.summary: Line Tucker (83 CHKG) on K2 to give K1 a same-level backup before a trade deadline acquisition is even needed.
recommendations.rationale: The coach flags that K1 carries three of four active checkers and an injury to Jackman (87) or McCabe (86) leaves no replacement. Tucker at 83 CHKG is unlined and available. He is 30 and POTE 79, so this is a bridge move through the playoffs, not a long-term solution.

recommendations.summary: Line Wallin (83 FACE) at a bottom-six centre slot to relieve Sundin (90 FACE, 34) of faceoff duty on lower lines.
recommendations.rationale: Only two players are above 80 FACE: Sundin at 90 and Wallin at 83, and Wallin is unlined. Chlup at 75 is the next option but he is 19 and still developing. Wallin gives the coach a reliable draw on L3 or L4 without asking Sundin to win every important face.

recommendations.summary: If Upshall is reduced or sat for his 0.21 pts/g, line Tucker first so active 80+ checkers never drop below three.
recommendations.rationale: Upshall at 80 CHKG is one of only six players above 80 checking and one of four who are active. Sitting him alone drops the active checking count to three (Jackman 87, McCabe 86, Fischer 82), all potentially on K1. The coach's own K1 concern makes this sequence important.

recommendations.summary: Kurka (CAR, 88 TOUG, 90 CHKG, POTE 99, $0.60M expiring, package Upshall + R3) remains the primary toughness target; zero rostered players are above 80 TOUG.
recommendations.rationale: Confirmed again in January: Jackman leads the roster at 75 TOUG and nobody reaches 80. No internal fix exists at any age. Kurka is 23, productive at 0.65 pts/g, and CAR at 16 points with 14 expiring and $63.79M payroll must move him.

recommendations.summary: Hartnell (BUF, 89 TOUG, 90 CHKG, POTE 95, $1.10M expiring, package Alexeev + R3) is the alternative toughness target at one grade higher but a higher package cost.
recommendations.rationale: Hartnell edges Kurka on toughness (89 vs 88) but costs Alexeev plus R3 versus Upshall plus R3. Kurka's $0.60M salary is cheaper than Hartnell's $1.10M. Both close the same gap; whichever package the GM can close wins.

recommendations.summary: Mogilny at 36 with one year left and 94 SCOR, 93 PASS is the single biggest departure the roster faces; the scoring core loses both its top producer and top playmaker after this season.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin at 34 carries 92 SCOR and 91 PASS. Together they are the top two in both roles. Gaborik (92, 23) and Afinogenov (90, 26) replace one layer, but the depth behind them drops. Heatley (ATL, 91 base, 82 TOUG, 24) would close the scoring gap and add toughness in one move, but his package is Spezza + Koltsov + R1.

recommendations.summary: Sign Chlup to a 5-6 year extension in July 2006 before his 1-year deal expires.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup is 19, 32 points in 42 games, POTE 95, on $2.34M for one year. He is the franchise centre and the cheapest elite player on the roster; losing him to free agency would be unrecoverable.

recommendations.summary: Sign Luongo to a 5-6 year extension in July 2006 before his 1-year deal expires.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is 26, POTE 97, $1.60M, one year left. The backup behind him is Tellqvist at POTE 91 or Ouellet at 81, both a step down. Lock him the same week as Chlup.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Klesla on a 4-year deal in July 2006; do not trade him.
recommendations.rationale: Klesla is 23, 18 points in 42 games, POTE 97, $0.90M expiring. He is the kind of young defender the manual says to hoard, and 42 games played proves he is already a top-four option.

recommendations.summary: Plan to extend Richards and Nash in July 2007 to break the July 2009 cluster of eleven players and $37.40M.
recommendations.rationale: Richards ($6.70M) and Nash ($3.90M) are both on 4-year deals expiring July 2009 at ages 28 and 24. By 2009 they command market-setting deals. Extending them two years early splits the summer and controls cost.

recommendations.summary: The age shape is healthy — five veterans, twelve players at 23 or under, eight carrying POTE 95+. Do not reshape the roster for age reasons.
recommendations.rationale: The manual asks for 5-7 veterans and 20 young players with six carrying real potential. Toronto have exactly that. The risk is contract timing, not aging.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Kurka (CAR, LW, 23, 26pts/40GP, TOUG 88, CHKG 90, POTE 99, $0.60M expiring) for Upshall plus a third-round pick at the March deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Kurka carries the checking and toughness the coach flagged as missing while producing 0.65 pts/g. CAR at 44 points and 10th in the East will sell expiring contracts. Upshall is a roster drain at 0.21 pts/g per the coach's January report.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Vandermeer (PHI, D, 25, TOUG 92, CHKG 90, POTE 92, $0.40M expiring) if PHI falls further from the playoff line by late February.
recommendations.rationale: He fills the K1 depth problem the coach flagged. PHI at 45 points with nine expirers become a seller if they fall below the line. Package needs Koltsov or St. Jacques plus a pick.

recommendations.summary: Move Mogilny (36, $5.50M, 89 displayed, expiring) via the over-80 pick-recovery mechanic at the March deadline.
recommendations.rationale: He is above 80, expiring, and $5.50M. The mechanic trades any over-80 expiring player for a draft pick without needing a specific buyer.

recommendations.summary: Trade Tucker (30, $1.30M, expiring, above 80) either in a Kurka/Vandermeer package or via the pick-recovery mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: Second over-80 expiring asset. Better used as a package piece for a young player we keep than burned for a pick alone, but a pick is better than losing him for nothing.

recommendations.summary: Sign Luongo to a 5-year extension in July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base, age 26, $1.60M current. He is the best goalie in the building and the dynasty's number one. Losing him would set the franchise back two years.

recommendations.summary: Sign Chlup to a 5-year extension in July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: 19 years old, first-line centre, $2.34M expiring. Locking the centre position through the competitive window is the priority after Luongo.

recommendations.summary: Sign Klesla to a 4-year extension in July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: 23 years old, defenceman, $0.90M. Cheap and young enough to anchor the third pair for four more seasons.

recommendations.summary: Sign Ouellet to a 2-year extension as backup goalie in July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: 24 years old, 81 base, $0.90M. Two years is the right term for a backup and avoids a second renewal cycle before we know if Tellqvist overtakes him.

recommendations.summary: Move or release Spezza (73 base, 5pts/26GP, 5.4 MPG, $1.00M expiring) before July if he is not a package piece.
recommendations.rationale: At 22 with 73 base and 5 points in 26 games he is not a prospect the roster needs. Better as a third body in a deadline deal than released, but either way he is gone.

recommendations.summary: Trade Koltsov (24, $1.10M, expiring) as the third body in a Vandermeer or Kurka package before July.
recommendations.rationale: Expiring, young enough to interest a seller, and the coach's Upshall drain note shows the roster has no room for a fourth-line winger at his rate.

recommendations.summary: Trade St. Jacques (25, $0.80M, expiring) as a package body or release before July.
recommendations.rationale: Expiring defenceman at $0.80M. Useful as a throw-in in a Vandermeer deal; otherwise released.

recommendations.proposed: Kurka (CAR, LW, 23, 88 TOUG, 90 CHKG, POTE 99, $0.60M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Primary toughness target: 88 TOUG and 90 CHKG at 23 with POTE 99 for Upshall + R3 closes our zero-toughness gap in one move.
recommendations.rationale: Kurka's 27 points in 42 games (0.64/g) confirms the November projection. CAR at 44 points with 14 expiring and $65.29M payroll creates sell pressure even if they remain fringe-contenders. Package costs Upshall (coach wants him sat) plus our lowest pick.

recommendations.proposed: Hartnell (BUF, LW, 23, 89 TOUG, 90 CHKG, POTE 95, $1.10M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Backup toughness winger if Kurka is not available; same profile at $0.50M more salary and BUF at 43 points is a fringe seller.
recommendations.rationale: BUF has 6 expiring contracts and at 43 points sit on the same playoff fringe as CAR. Package: Alexeev + R3. Costs the man the coach wants dressed, so only pursue if Kurka fails.

recommendations.proposed: Vandermeer (PHI, D, 25, 92 TOUG, 90 CHKG, POTE 92, $0.40M expiring)
recommendations.summary: 92 TOUG and 90 CHKG at 25 on $0.40M expiring solves the K1 fragility the coach flagged; PHI at 45 with 9 expirers becomes a seller if they miss the line.
recommendations.rationale: PHI with 9 expiring cannot retain all of them at season end. Vandermeer at $0.40M costs PHI nothing to move. At 92 TOUG/90 CHKG he pairs with Jackman on K1 and gives us a 25-year-old with POTE 92 for the future.

recommendations.proposed: Witt (WSH, D, 89 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 80 base, $1.70M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Highest certainty of any deal: WSH at 33 points is the most motivated seller in the league and Witt's 93 CHKG matches Jackman's checking from the D-side.
recommendations.rationale: WSH at 10-21-7 is 12 points behind 8th and will sell. Their 5 expirers at $57.05M payroll need to clear. Package: Alexeev + Tucker (designated chip). Witt's 80 base is lower than Kurka's but 93 CHKG is our team-leading grade.

recommendations.proposed: Sean Hill (CAR, D, 84 TOUG, 85 CHKG, 81 base, 32 pts/36 GP, $2.30M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Toughness plus first-pairing offense from the blue line at 81 base; bundle with Kurka if CAR opens to a full teardown.
recommendations.rationale: 32 points in 36 games from a D who hits is rare. At $2.30M expiring CAR cannot keep him. Same destination as Kurka so a two-for-one package is logical. Slightly lower TOUG/CHKG than Witt or Vandermeer but vastly more production.

recommendations.proposed: Heatley (ATL, RW, 24, 91 base, 82 TOUG, 2 years left)
recommendations.summary: Addresses toughness (82 TOUG) AND the Mogilny successor question in one acquisition; ATL at 39 points may still sell but the climb from 16 makes acceptance uncertain.
recommendations.rationale: At 91 base and 82 TOUG, Heatley is the single highest-graded toughness forward available and would replace Mogilny's 94 SCOR production long-term. Cost is Spezza + Koltsov + R1, our entire draft capital. ATL at 39 with 6 expiring could go either way. Low confidence they deal in March.

recommendations.proposed: Vasicek (CAR, C, 25, 82 overall, 18 pts/22 GP, FACE 80, POTE 87, $0.40M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Depth centre at $0.40M with POTE 87; same CAR destination as Kurka and Hill so a three-for-one conversation is possible.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup (75 FACE, 19) is developing but Wallin (83 FACE) is the only other centre above 80 draws. Vasicek at $0.40M costs almost nothing to acquire (Koltsov + R3, net saving $0.70M) and gives insurance if Chlup's development stalls.

recommendations.current: Upshall (RW, 22, POTE 99, CHKG 87, $1.50M, 4 yrs) + Toronto R3 (3rd round, late by seeding)
recommendations.proposed: Kurka (LW, 23, TOUG 88, CHKG 90, POTE 99, 27 pts/42 GP, $0.60M expiring) from Carolina
recommendations.summary: Send Upshall and our 3rd-round pick to Carolina for Kurka at the March deadline if CAR is below the Eastern playoff line in late February.
recommendations.rationale: Closes the only unfillable roster gap (zero players above 80 TOUG). CAR at 44 points with 14 expirers and $65.29M payroll will be collecting POTE 95+ players if they miss the line. Upshall at POTE 99 and CHKG 87 is exactly what a rebuilding team wants. We shed $1.50M and absorb $0.60M (net saving $0.90M). Upshall is the coach's designated bench player; Kurka would play every night. Acceptance uncertain — AI values Upshall's POTE 99 highly and CAR may hold him if they sneak into 8th.

recommendations.current: Alexeev (RW, 24, BALA 90, SPEE 89, POTE 94, 16 pts/30 GP, $1.50M, 4 yrs) + Tucker (LW, 30, CHKG 92, TOUG 88, POTE 79, $1.30M expiring, 0 GP)
recommendations.proposed: Witt (D, 89 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 80 base, $1.70M expiring) from Washington
recommendations.summary: Send Alexeev and Tucker to Washington for Witt at the March deadline; WSH at 33 points are the league's most motivated seller and will take prospects.
recommendations.rationale: Witt at 93 CHKG matches Jackman and adds 89 TOUG to the blue line, closing both the checking depth concern and the toughness gap on defense. WSH at 33 points (12 behind 8th) with 5 expirers are rebuilding and want young players: Alexeev at 24, POTE 94, BALA 90 is a real prospect; Tucker at 80+ base can be flipped to a contender for a pick before July. We shed $2.80M and absorb $1.70M (net saving $1.10M). Tucker is a designated chip with zero games played. Acceptance uncertain — WSH may want a defenceman back rather than a winger.

recommendations.current: Upshall (RW, 22, POTE 99, CHKG 87, $1.50M, 4 yrs) + Toronto R3 (3rd round, late by seeding)
recommendations.proposed: Hartnell (LW, 23, TOUG 89, CHKG 90, POTE 95, 16 pts/42 GP, $1.10M expiring) from Buffalo
recommendations.summary: Fallback if CAR rejects the Kurka package: same assets go to Buffalo for Hartnell, whose 89 TOUG and 90 CHKG are within 1 point of Kurka's on both axes.
recommendations.rationale: Hartnell at 89 TOUG and 90 CHKG is statistically nearly identical to Kurka on the grades that matter, but his production is half (0.38 vs 0.65 pts/g) and he costs $0.50M more. BUF at 43 points with 6 expirers is the same fringe-seller profile as CAR. Use only if Kurka is unavailable. Acceptance uncertain — BUF may value Hartnell's POTE 95 similarly to how CAR values Kurka's POTE 99.

recommendations.summary: Goalie monitoring task (#2) is complete and closed per the GM's own order of 2005-03-19; no new goalie targets without his say-so.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo was acquired in March 2005 and is on the roster at 95 overall, $1.60M, 1 year left. DiPietro is 86 at NYI on an expiring deal but the GM closed all goalie trade monitoring. The open question is Luongo's renewal, not a trade window.

recommendations.summary: Dress Eminger more often. His share is 38% with a 0.50 rate and the club's highest scouting number, and he has been available since November 6th.
recommendations.rationale: 16 GP in 42 games at 16.3 MPG and 0.50 pts/g with POTE 99 at age 22. His form flag lapsed on November 6th and nothing is keeping him out. Klesla at 25.5 MPG every night needs a real partner to spread the load.

recommendations.summary: Upshall is a roster drain at 79% share and 0.21 pts/g. Consider reducing his role or sitting him so another body can fill the slot.
recommendations.rationale: 7 points in 33 games at 5.6 MPG on the fourth line. At 22 with POTE 99 he's had two full seasons to translate potential into production and hasn't. His share is the highest of any young forward while his rate is the second-worst.

recommendations.summary: Gardener, Spezza and Colaiacovo stay scratched. None is earning a recall.
recommendations.rationale: Gardener has zero points in 23 games. Spezza is at 0.19 pts/g on 5.4 MPG. Colaiacovo is at 0.12 pts/g. All three are below the level needed to take a spot from a player who produces.

recommendations.summary: Chlup, Nash, Chistov, Klesla and Gaborik are all getting the games they've earned. No development concern.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup 32 pts/42 GP at 20.7 MPG, Chistov 30/42 at 20.6, Nash 26/42 at 15.7, Klesla 18/42 at 25.5, Gaborik 14/22 at 22.2. Each one is producing at his line tier.

recommendations.summary: Gaborik at 0.64 pts/g on 22.2 MPG in 22 games at 23 is the best young-player trend and belongs on the first line permanently.
recommendations.rationale: He missed ten weeks and still posted 0.64 on elite minutes. No other TOR forward 23 or under has that rate on that ice time.

recommendations.summary: Chlup at 0.76 on 21.0 MPG at 19 is on track. The rate dip from 0.88 is minutes-related, not regression.
recommendations.rationale: His minutes rose from 18 to 21 while the rate eased from 0.88 to 0.76. A 19-year-old adjusting to a heavier load.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev's rate recovered to 0.48 in 30 games, back above the 0.45 floor. The December 20th scratch recommendation is withdrawn; dress him.
recommendations.rationale: He was 0.40 in 26 games on Dec 20th and now reads 0.48 in 30. The recovery is small but crosses the threshold.

recommendations.summary: Gardener at 0.00 pts/g in 23 games on 3.0 MPG is the collapse pattern. Stop dressing him; the minutes belong elsewhere.
recommendations.rationale: Zero points in 23 games. Minutes fell from 16 to 3.0. Same pattern as Spezza, Upshall, and Spacek.

recommendations.summary: Klesla at 0.44 in 42 games, 87 OVR, $0.90M expiring. Deadline sell confirmed. Rate is flat so the card holds its value now.
recommendations.rationale: 0.44 at 42 games matches 0.45 at 40 from January 5th. No regression to erode the card before the deadline.

recommendations.summary: Eminger at 0.50 pts/g in 16 games has recovered past the 0.38 flagged in March. His card reads better than the prior-season rate, making him more tradeable now.
recommendations.rationale: The 0.50 recent rate on 16.3 MPG makes a buyer's read stronger than the March sell case, when I was working off 0.38.

recommendations.summary: McCabe at 0.47 in 17 games is below the 0.60 sell threshold at $3.00M x 3 and 30 years old. Sell list.
recommendations.rationale: Improved from 0.30 in 10 games seen on December 24th but still well under the 0.60 threshold from March 30th.

recommendations.summary: Fischer at 0.43 on 19.2 MPG in 15 games at 25 validates the GM's keeper decision. No change.
recommendations.rationale: His minutes doubled from 10 to 19.2 across the window and he held a 0.43 rate. That is a second-pair-to-first-pair trajectory.

recommendations.summary: Sundin at 0.85 on 23.7 MPG in 42 games at 34 shows no age decline. No planning changes needed.
recommendations.rationale: 0.85 pts/g on 23.7 MPG at age 34 is elite production. No flag.

recommendations.summary: Room is fine. Everyone trending up on the winning streak; no minutes adjustment needed tonight.
recommendations.rationale: L3 (Richards 88, Lundmark 88) and L4 (Koltsov/Upshall/Spacek all 83) are under their band by 5-12 MPG but climbing 3-7 points per save on results. No player is in a danger zone. The structural minutes gap is a streak-risk, not a tonight-problem.

recommendations.summary: We have only four skaters above 80 checking (Jackman 91, McCabe 82, Nash 81, Roberts 83) and K1 already carries three of them. Any injury to Jackman or McCabe leaves K1 unrecoverable.
recommendations.rationale: The role inventory shows Roberts (83) is our only backup checker and he is already a healthy scratch. The deadline is the window to add one more body at 80+ checking; after that we're hoping nobody on K1 gets hurt in April.

recommendations.summary: All units are correctly staffed with the personnel available. L1 through L3, P1, P2, K1 and K2 each have the attributes the role demands.
recommendations.rationale: L1 checks 78 mean with Jackman's 91 as the anchor. K1 checks 83 mean with three of our top four. P1 scores 89 mean and runs 93 speed. The only structural gap is depth behind K1, which is a roster problem, not a lineup one.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo if his fatigue icon is clear. Ouellet covers if tired.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 95 OVR vs a 2.90-goal-per-game offence. Their only 90+ player is Thornton. Ouellet at 86 handles this level too if needed.

recommendations.summary: Keep all lines unchanged for BOS. The matchups favour us on every pair and every line.
recommendations.rationale: Our D pairs beat theirs by 6-10 OVR each. Our centres outrun all four of theirs. The 0-2-1 record is a confidence issue, not a structural one. Go all out against this quality opponent per the standing framework.

recommendations.summary: Klesla remains the primary sell candidate: 87 OVR, expiring, 0.43 pts/g and declining.
recommendations.rationale: His rate fell from 0.45 (Jan 5) to 0.43 over two games. The card is at its peak before the deadline. $0.90M x 1 means we recapture something or lose him free.

recommendations.summary: McCabe stays on the sell list: $3.00M x 3 at age 30, 0.47 pts/g.
recommendations.rationale: He improved from 0.30 to 0.47 since my December 24th check but is still far below the 0.60 threshold. His contract is the biggest dead weight on the blue line.

recommendations.summary: Jackman's sell window is narrowing. 0.62 pts/g, down from 0.70 on Dec 29. Trigger at 0.55.
recommendations.rationale: The heater ended. If he hits 0.55 before the deadline he becomes a sell despite his age and cost; if not, he stays. Monitor every save.

recommendations.summary: Line Roberts at L4 as the coach recommends; his 86 CHKG adds a fifth lined checker at no cost.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts is at 86 checking and 90 clutch but carries no unit. Moving him to L4 raises lined checkers from 4 to 5 without spending any asset.

recommendations.summary: Toughness remains a zero; acquire Hartnell (89 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 23) or Kurka (88 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 23) at the March deadline.
recommendations.rationale: No player on the roster reaches 76 toughness. Hartnell also closes the checking gap simultaneously. Both are 23 with POTE 95+, expiring, and on sellers.

recommendations.summary: Avery (LA, C, 25, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, $400K, 2 years) is the only player who closes the faceoff and toughness gaps in one move.
recommendations.rationale: Only Sundin can win draws among lined centres. Avery at 93 FACE and 83 TOUG and 25 years old at $400K for two years is the cheapest single-body fix for two of the three structural gaps.

recommendations.summary: Move Gaborik at the March deadline; his $11.90M/year for 5 years at 11 pts/21 GP is the single worst value-to-cost contract on the roster and there is no renegotiation path.
recommendations.rationale: He is 13.2% of payroll producing 0.52 pts/g. The contract runs through July 2010. Every month he stays undressed or underproducing erodes his trade value. Even a salary-relief return (half his money, a fringe player) improves the trajectory by freeing $11.90M/year toward the 2009 renewal wave.

recommendations.summary: Lock Chlup on a 5-6 year deal the week July 2006 opens; he has 32 points in 41 games at age 19 on $2.34M expiring and will not remain at that rate.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 95, 32 pts, 19 years old. He is the single most valuable contract on the roster and walks July 2006 without a new deal. Luongo (26, 1yr, $1.60M) is the same-summer priority.

recommendations.summary: Begin early extensions of Richards, Chistov, and Nash in July 2007 to break the 11-player, $37.40M cluster that expires July 2009.
recommendations.rationale: These three are $15.60M of the cluster and will be 28, 25, and 24 respectively in 2009. Extending them two years early resets their clocks and prevents a summer where the entire core is simultaneously available.

recommendations.proposed: Hartnell (BUF, LW, 23, 79 base, 89 CHKG, 85 TOUG, $1.10M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Acquire Hartnell for Upshall plus R3 at the March 19 deadline to fill the 80+ checking gap.
recommendations.rationale: Coach needs one forward with 80+ CHKG; Hartnell displays 89. BUF at 41 points (11-17-3) are clear sellers. Upshall produces 0.19 pts/g in 31 games and the coach says stop dressing him — we lose nothing, BUF gains a POTE-99 22-year-old.

recommendations.proposed: Draft pick via over-80 pick-recovery to a non-contender
recommendations.summary: Ship Mogilny to a non-contender for a draft pick at the deadline using the over-80 expiring mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: Above 80 base, expiring, $5.50M salary we will not extend at age 36. Pure value recovery. Frees the largest single salary on the roster for July renewals.

recommendations.proposed: Draft pick via over-80 pick-recovery or summer release
recommendations.summary: Move Tucker for a pick at the deadline if his base exceeds 80; otherwise release in July.
recommendations.rationale: Age 30, expiring, we will not re-sign. If base clears 80 the mechanic applies; if not, the $1.30M is dead money in July.

recommendations.summary: Renew Chlup on a five-year deal in July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: 19-year-old franchise centre whose value ratchets each season he produces. Stars get 5-6 years per the manual.

recommendations.summary: Renew Luongo on a five-year deal in July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: 26-year-old starter on an expiring deal is the highest-risk position. The manual warns explicitly about forgetting goalies. Lock him before any bidding war.

recommendations.summary: Renew Klesla on a four-year deal in July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: Young defenceman with room to grow at $0.90M. Fits the depth-win principle.

recommendations.summary: Renew Ouellet as backup on a two-year deal in July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: Goalie insurance behind Luongo. Cheap, young, no cap risk. The manual says check the goalies.

recommendations.summary: Release Koltsov and St. Jacques in July if not traded at the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Both expiring, both cheap but neither fills a role we lack. Roster spots are more valuable than $0.90M each when the coach has five young players stalled.

recommendations.proposed: Include as third name in the Hartnell package or move to another club
recommendations.summary: Move Spezza at the deadline as a package sweetener; his POTE 99 has value to a rebuilding club even if his current production does not.
recommendations.rationale: Coach says no path in this lineup (0.19 pts/g, 5.4 MPG, morale 82). Keeping a non-playing POTE 99 wastes the asset. BUF or another seller may take him as a third name.

recommendations.summary: No deadline action before late February; GM's standing order holds.
recommendations.rationale: Deadline is 70 days away. We are first in the East with no injuries forcing urgency. Negotiations open late February.

recommendations.summary: Primary toughness target: CAR LW, 23, 26 pts/40GP, TOUG 88, CHKG 90, $0.60M expiring, package Upshall + R3.
recommendations.rationale: Kurka is the most productive toughness forward on a desperate seller (CAR 43 pts, 14 expirers, $65.29M). His 0.65 pts/g at age 23 on a 11-16-5 team is genuine value, and $0.60M means net savings. Package removes Upshall whom the coach wants benched.

recommendations.summary: Primary faceoff and scoring target: ATL C, 28, 37 pts/39GP, FACE 87, $1.00M expiring. Re-evaluate cost — his value has nearly doubled since December.
recommendations.rationale: Savard's 37 points in 39 games (0.95 pts/g) makes him the best centre on any seller. ATL at 37 pts with lowest payroll cannot re-sign him. FACE 87 closes the gap where only Sundin (90) is above 80. The Tucker-alone package from December likely no longer suffices given his production surge.

recommendations.summary: D-side toughness target: PHI D, 25, TOUG 92, CHKG 90, POTE 92, 32 MPG, $0.40M expiring. Gated on PHI falling below the line.
recommendations.rationale: Vandermeer is the only D in the league above 90 on both toughness and checking. At 32 MPG he is a top-pairing keeper at $0.40M. PHI at 45 pts with 15-15-3 is borderline; if they miss they must dump 9 expirers. Package requires Alexeev.

recommendations.summary: Alternate toughness target if CAR overprices Kurka: BUF LW, 23, TOUG 89, CHKG 90, POTE 95, $1.10M expiring, package Upshall + R3.
recommendations.rationale: Hartnell's POTE 95 is the highest of any toughness target, but his 0.38 pts/g is well below Kurka's 0.65. Take Hartnell only if Kurka is unavailable. Same package (Upshall + R3) means these are mutually exclusive.

recommendations.summary: Cheap depth toughness D from the league's worst team: WSH, TOUG 89, CHKG 91, 74 base, $0.60M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Yonkman at 74 base is a bottom-pairing D, but 91 CHKG from a defenceman is rare and WSH at 33 pts are desperate sellers. If we target both forward and D toughness, Yonkman pairs with Kurka at $0.60M combined.

recommendations.summary: Bertuzzi and Naslund are off the board — VAN at 48 pts (15-14-4) are now above .500 and likely will not sell.
recommendations.rationale: Both were December targets when VAN sat at 33 pts. They have climbed to 48 pts at 1.45 pts/game pace. Revisit only if they collapse in February.

recommendations.summary: Avery (LA, C, 25, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, $400K, 2yr) closes faceoffs and toughness in one body but production data is missing from this scan — follow up in February.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 34 pts with 5 expirers could sell, but Avery has 2 years left so they will demand more than a pick. His current GP and points were not captured in this round. Re-evaluate when February data arrives.

recommendations.summary: Trade Upshall plus our third-round pick to Carolina for Kurka; closes toughness and checking simultaneously at a net salary savings of $0.90M.
recommendations.rationale: CAR at 43 points with 14 expirers on $65.29M payroll cannot retain Kurka, who costs only $0.60M but has no re-signing path for a rebuilding club. Upshall at POTE 99 and age 22 is a development asset they would draft if he were available. Coach has flagged Upshall for scratching, making him surplus here.

recommendations.summary: Trade Koltsov, St. Jacques, and our second-round pick to Atlanta for Savard; closes the faceoff gap and adds a 0.95 pts/g second-line centre.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 37 points with six expirers and $40.34M payroll (league-second-lowest) must move Savard or lose him for nothing. They get two players with POTE 94 at combined $1.90M and a second-rounder. Koltsov and St. Jacques are expiring, barely playing (1 pt/9 GP and 0 pts/15 GP), and have no path here.

recommendations.summary: Trade Tucker plus our second-round pick to Los Angeles for Avery; closes faceoffs and toughness in one body with a 2-year contract at $0.40M.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 34 points with five expirers are sellers. Avery at 25 with 2 years left is acquirable only because LA gets a return rather than losing him next year. Tucker at CHKG 92 and TOUG 88 is a tough body for the stretch run. I lack Avery's current production, so his fit in our top-nine is unconfirmed.

recommendations.summary: Line Roberts at fourth-line left wing; adds 86 CHKG and 92 TOUG to the lineup at zero cost if healthy.
recommendations.rationale: The coach's own report recommends this. Roberts at 86 CHKG and 92 TOUG partially addresses the checking gap for free. If no trade lands by March, this is the internal fix.

recommendations.summary: Goalie monitoring task is closed per GM's 2005-03-19 order; Luongo is on the roster at 95 and is our starter.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo acquired and playing (95, 23 GP, $1.60M, 1 yr). The GM explicitly closed all goalie trade monitoring on 2005-03-19. The only open goalie question is Luongo's contract renewal in the summer, not a deadline acquisition.

recommendations.summary: Replace Upshall with Spacek on the fourth line on non-premium nights; at 22 and 0.22 rate, Upshall's development is over and Spacek at 20 is producing a better rate (0.27) in less ice.
recommendations.rationale: Upshall: age 22, 5.7 MPG, 0.22 pts/g, the same collapse pattern as last season (13.4 to 4.9 MPG). Spacek: age 20, 0.27 pts/g in 15 games at 5.3 MPG. Against Pittsburgh (15-11) this is not the night; on lesser opponents, give the 20-year-old the rep.

recommendations.summary: Chlup, Nash, Chistov and Klesla are where they should be. No adjustment needed for the young top-end.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup: 32 pts in 41 games, 20.8 MPG. Nash: 24 pts, 15.7 MPG. Chistov: 28 pts, 20.5 MPG. Klesla: 18 pts, 25.4 MPG. All at 98 morale, all full-time. No development intervention warranted.

recommendations.summary: Gaborik's problem is availability (51%), not deployment. 22.1 MPG when healthy is right. No lineup change addresses a health issue.
recommendations.rationale: 21 GP in 41 games with 22.1 MPG when he plays. The rate (0.52) is below what a first-line winger should give, but that's a fitness and form issue, not an ice-time or role problem.

recommendations.summary: Reinstate Alexeev to the rotation; his rate has recovered to 0.48 at 30 games, above the 0.45 floor.
recommendations.rationale: Dec 20 note set 0.45 as the stop-dressing floor. He's at 0.48 over 30 games on 10.7 MPG. The recovery is driven by a hot 4-game window but the floor is met.

recommendations.summary: Stop dressing Gardener permanently. Zero points in 23 games at 3.0 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: He is the textbook young-forward-minutes-collapse pattern: 16 MPG to 3 MPG, zero production throughout. His roster spot is blocking a body who will play real minutes.

recommendations.summary: Stop dressing Spacek permanently. 0.21 pts/g in 15 games at 4.5 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: Same collapse pattern: 17 MPG to 4.5 MPG, rate from 1.00 (noise) to 0.21. He is not developing and is not playing enough to develop.

recommendations.summary: Flag Afinogenov for offseason system-fit review. His rate is 0.62 at 26 on 18 MPG, a third consecutive decline.
recommendations.rationale: 1.17 last season, 0.73 mid-season, 0.62 now. At 26 with top-six minutes he should be ascending or flat. Three straight drops means the problem is role or system, not age.

recommendations.summary: Give the third line more of the game; Richards at 12.3 MPG is under his band and at 88 his grades take a -1 penalty that vanishes at 90.
recommendations.rationale: Richards has 27 points in 41 games on 12.3 MPG -- a 2.2 pts/60 rate that exceeds Chlup (32 pts, 20.8 MPG). His 17-MPG expectation for an 80-89 player means he is 4.7 minutes short. More ice for the unit lifts his morale into the 90s without breaking chemistry.

recommendations.summary: Give the fourth line a few extra shifts; Upshall and Spaček at 5.7 and 5.3 MPG are under their 10-MPG band and sitting at 83 morale.
recommendations.rationale: Both recovered from -15 dips on the winning streak but remain in the 80s penalty range. Slightly more ice is the smaller intervention before they slip again if the streak ends.

recommendations.summary: Brendl, Gardener, Spezza, Roberts, Abid, Tucker, Wallin all stable at 81-95 as scratches. No line move fixes a scratch.
recommendations.rationale: These players are out of the lineup by roster decision. Their morale is stable or recovering on team results. No action available to me.

recommendations.summary: We have no fourth dressable checker above 80. K2 cannot be built to kill penalties with the bodies available.
recommendations.rationale: K1 holds Jackman 92, McCabe 83, Nash 82. Roberts at 84 is scratched. No other dressed player checks above 83. K2's best checker is Eminger around 87 on paper but the unit mean sits at 76 with three offensive players alongside him.

recommendations.summary: No player on this roster carries 80+ in toughness. Jackman 78 is the ceiling. We have no enforcer role available.
recommendations.rationale: Toughness leaders: Jackman 78, Sundin 72, McCabe 72. Nobody is built to impose physically. This is a structural identity of the roster (speed and skill), not a lineup arrangement problem.

recommendations.summary: L4 faceoffs mean 53, best 57. No dressed forward on that line can win draws. Wallin at 88 is scratched.
recommendations.rationale: Against any opposing centre above 57%, L4 surrenders every shift-start. Fixing this requires either dressing Wallin (costing his development minutes) or finding a fourth-line centre in a trade. No arrangement of currently dressed players solves it.

recommendations.summary: K1 is correctly built: checking 84 mean, toughness 73, speed 89. No change.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup, McCabe, Jackman, Nash hold three of our four best checkers plus speed to chase. This is the best kill unit the roster can produce and it is well constructed.

recommendations.summary: PP1 is complete: shots, setup, net-front, speed, faceoffs. No change.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin (94 scoring, 95 faceoffs), Richards and Chistov (93 playmaking each), Jackman (92 checking for traffic), Klesla (99 speed). Every role on a power play is covered.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo if his fatigue icon is clear. Ouellet covers if tired.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is 95 OVR against a 2.80-goal-per-game offence with a 7.0% power play. Check the tired icon before confirming.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes. Every matchup is favorable as currently set.
recommendations.rationale: Our D1 (Klesla 87, Jackman 86) auto-pairs against their aging top line (Lemieux 88 at age 40, Straka 86 at 33). Our scoring lines face their bottom-two D pairs at 66-68 OVR. Their 7.0% power play cannot test our PK. We win faceoffs on three of four lines tonight.

recommendations.summary: Jackman's heater broke — zero points in last 4, rate 0.70 down to 0.63. Sell window closing at the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: At 41 GP he has 26 points (0.634 pts/g). The heater peaked at 0.70 on December 29th. If he crosses 0.55 the card weakens materially. $0.70M x 2 at 86 OVR is still attractive to a buyer but the window narrows each game.

recommendations.summary: McCabe's new hot streak (6 points in 6 games, rate up to 0.50) opens a sell window on dead weight.
recommendations.rationale: $3.00M x 3 at 30 years old is rebuild poison. His season rate just crossed from 0.30 to 0.50 on a hot streak. A buyer sees a productive veteran; we should move him before the streak reverts. First sell window since I put him back on the list on December 24th.

recommendations.summary: Klesla confirmed sell unchanged. 87 OVR card, 0.44 pts/g keeps bleeding, expiring contract.
recommendations.rationale: Rate has moved from 0.45 at 40 GP to 0.44 at 41. The production behind the 87 grade is gone. $0.90M x 1 expiring makes him urgent — maximum urgency before his grade drops too.

recommendations.summary: Roberts at 86 checking on L4 closes the coach's checking gap without trade capital, provided he is healthy.
recommendations.rationale: The coach already recommends this move. Roberts is unlined, has 86 CHKG, 98 INJU, 90 clutch. Four active 80+ checkers is adequate for a four-line team; adding Tucker at 83 as a fifth is available if needed.

recommendations.summary: Hartnell at 89 TOUG, 90 CHKG, age 23, $1.10M expiring remains the only acquisition that closes the zero-toughness gap.
recommendations.rationale: No rostered player reaches 80 toughness at any age. Hartnell supersedes Hill and Kurka as the primary target per the January 4 note. Gated on GM confirming Alexeev is expendable in the package.

recommendations.summary: Savard at FACE 88, $1.00M expiring gives Toronto a second 80+ faceoff man and replaces the expiring Mogilny production.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin at 34 is the only 80+ faceoff man in the lineup. Wallin at 83 is unlined and not a centre. Chlup at 75 loses draws on L2. Savard fills both the faceoff and production gaps simultaneously.

recommendations.summary: Goalies are covered. Luongo 94 glove, Ouellet 86 glove. No action needed.
recommendations.rationale: GM closed goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19 and the situation has not changed. Two 85+ glove goalies dressed for a playoff run.

recommendations.summary: Move Gaborik at the March deadline; his $11.90M for 0.50 pts/g is the single largest payroll inefficiency and his trade value is highest while he is lined and producing.
recommendations.rationale: He carries 13.2% of payroll through July 2010 at $1.19M per point produced. At 23 with POTE 90 and now playing, he has market value that only exists while he is in the lineup and scoring.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Luongo to a five-year deal in July 2006; he is the best player on the roster and has one year left at $1.60M.
recommendations.rationale: 94 displayed overall, 97 POTE, 26 years old. Behind him is Ouellet at 81 base. If Luongo walks, the franchise loses its only NHL-calibre goaltender.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Chlup to a six-year deal in July 2006; at 19 with 31 points and $2.34M salary he is the most underpaid player in the league.
recommendations.rationale: 31 points in 40 GP at age 19 with POTE 95 on a contract that expires in six months. If the market discovers him before he is locked, Toronto will pay a multiple of his current rate.

recommendations.summary: Take no trade action before late February; the deadline is 73 days away and sellers will still be sellers in March.
recommendations.rationale: GM's standing order from 2005-01-15: negotiations open late February. Toronto at 63 points and 1st in the East are not in a position where inaction costs anything this month.

recommendations.summary: Open talks with VAN for Bertuzzi in late February; package is Tucker plus our 2006 R2.
recommendations.rationale: Bertuzzi carries TOUG 83 and CHKG 87 at 94 base with 1.25 pts/g, the only player clearing 80 on both axes while producing top-six. VAN at $46.36M with 13 expirers must sell.

recommendations.summary: Keep Hartnell (BUF) as the fallback toughness target if Bertuzzi is unreachable; package is Alexeev plus R3.
recommendations.rationale: Hartnell at 89 TOUG, 90 CHKG, POTE 95 and $1.10M expiring is the value option. Gated on GM confirming Alexeev is expendable.

recommendations.summary: Open talks with ATL for Savard in late February; package is Koltsov plus St. Jacques plus R3.
recommendations.rationale: Savard at FACE 88 and 26 pts/30 GP on $1.00M expiring fills the faceoff gap. ATL has three expiring centres. The return pieces are both flagged by the coach as not developing.

recommendations.summary: Move Mogilny at the deadline via the over-80 expiring mechanic to recover a draft pick and clear $5.50M.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny at 90 base and $5.50M is our highest-value chip. He is expiring, above 80, and we will not re-sign him at 36. The mechanic trades him for a pick.

recommendations.summary: Sign Luongo to a 5-year deal in July; he is 26, 81 base, and the franchise goaltender.
recommendations.rationale: He is the one piece of this renewal list that cannot slip. GM's standing order says goalies are solved with Luongo and Belfour for the playoffs; Luongo is the long-term answer.

recommendations.summary: Sign Chlup to a 5-year deal in July; he is 19, 82 base, already a top-nine centre.
recommendations.rationale: 87 displayed at 19 years old, $2.34M salary the coach says he earns on the ice. Lock him on term before his next renewal ratchets.

recommendations.summary: Sign Klesla to a 4-year deal in July; 23, 78 base, $0.90M is the cheapest upside on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: 87 displayed, 78 base, age 23 at under a million. The coach has him in the top-nine and he is growing.

recommendations.summary: Sign Ouellet to a 2-year backup deal in July at $0.90M.
recommendations.rationale: 81 base at 24 gives a capable second option without market spending. GM's Feb 2005 order requires a second capable goalie for the playoffs.

recommendations.summary: If Savard lands, move or release Spezza at the deadline; the coach says he has no path in this lineup.
recommendations.rationale: 0.19 pts/g on 5.4 MPG at age 22 with morale at 82. At $1.00M and expiring, he is either a swap piece or a released roster spot. Coach flagged him on Jan 5.

recommendations.summary: Primary toughness target: Hartnell (BUF, LW, 23, TOUG 91, CHKG 92, POTE 95, SPEE 95, $1.10M expiring, 10pts/26GP) for Alexeev plus R3.
recommendations.rationale: Zero Toronto forwards at 80+ toughness. Hartnell at 91/92 with 95 potential and 95 speed fills both the toughness and checking gaps at age 23 on an expiring $1.10M salary. BUF at 40 points with five expirers.

recommendations.summary: Best value target on the board: Vandermeer (PHI, D, 25, TOUG 92, CHKG 90, POTE 92, 14pts/38GP, $0.40M expiring).
recommendations.rationale: A 25-year-old with 92 toughness, 90 checking and 92 potential at $0.40M. PHI have nine expirers at 45 points. If they fall out of the race he is acquirable for a late pick plus a depth body. No other player on the board combines this grade profile with this salary.

recommendations.summary: Faceoff target upgraded: Savard (ATL, C, 28, FACE 89, 36pts/38GP, 79 base, $1.00M expiring) for Koltsov plus St. Jacques plus R3.
recommendations.rationale: Savard has gone from 19 points in 22 games to 36 in 38 since December. He fills the faceoff gap behind Sundin while producing top-six centre numbers at $1.00M expiring. ATL at 35 points with six expirers cannot re-sign him.

recommendations.summary: WSH toughness pair: Witt (TOUG 91, CHKG 95, 19pts/40GP, $1.70M) plus Yonkman (TOUG 91, CHKG 93, POTE 89, $0.60M) both expiring on a 32-point club.
recommendations.rationale: Two 91-toughness defencemen for $2.30M combined. WSH at 32 points with five expirers is the most motivated seller in the East. Blocked by the GM's Eminger veto on the proposed return; an alternative package is needed.

recommendations.summary: Backup toughness option: Wanvig (PHX, RW, 24, TOUG 82, CHKG 83, POTE 95, 13pts/40GP, $0.60M expiring).
recommendations.rationale: Does not reach Hartnell's 91 toughness but at $0.60M with POTE 95 and age 24 he is the cheapest developmental toughness option. PHX at 35 points with nine expirers.

recommendations.summary: Faceoff backup: Conroy (CGY, C, 31, FACE 87, 27pts/31GP, 85 base, $2.00M expiring).
recommendations.rationale: Real scoring at FACE 87 on an expiring deal. CGY at 45 points with nine expirers. Inferior to Savard on age and cost but available if ATL holds firm.

recommendations.summary: Elite faceoff specialist: Draper (DET, C, 34, FACE 96, CHKG 86, 22pts/39GP, $1.20M expiring).
recommendations.rationale: Best faceoff man in the league at 96 with 86 checking and 22 points. Age 34 means he solves the problem for one year then recreates it. DET at 43 points may not sell.

recommendations.summary: Centre depth at no cost: Vasicek (CAR, C, 25, FACE 80, 82 base, 24pts/39GP, $0.40M expiring) for Koltsov plus R3.
recommendations.rationale: Below the 85 faceoff threshold but at $0.40M and age 25 with 24 points he gives centre depth that Chlup and Richards cannot cover alone. CAR at 41 points with 14 expirers.

recommendations.summary: Highest-overall seller: Bertuzzi (VAN, RW, 30, 91 overall/94 base, 54pts/39GP, $2.60M expiring) for Spezza plus Alexeev plus R2.
recommendations.rationale: Does not fill toughness or faceoffs but at 54 points and 94 base he is the best player on any seller. His 83 TOUG and 87 CHKG are respectable. VAN at 46 points with 13 expirers is the most motivated seller. Package requires Spezza, which also answers the coach's flag on his minutes.

recommendations.summary: Elite offensive D: Gonchar (WSH, D, 30, 86 base, 29pts/40GP, $3.30M expiring).
recommendations.rationale: Upgrades the top pair without addressing toughness. WSH at 32 points will move him. Expensive at $3.30M and does not fill either named gap; only pursue if the toughness targets clear on cheap packages and payroll room remains.

recommendations.summary: Elite young scorer: Heatley (ATL, RW, 23, 91 base, 46pts/38GP, $1.10M expiring) for Tucker plus R1.
recommendations.rationale: Age 23, 91 base, 46 points on $1.10M. Does not fill toughness or faceoffs. The R1 cost is the issue: trajectory says protect it unless the return is POTE 95+ top-six. Heatley at POTE 86 does not clear that bar.

recommendations.summary: Elite young scorer: Kovalchuk (ATL, LW, 23, 89 base, 48pts/38GP, $1.10M expiring).
recommendations.rationale: Same logic as Heatley: 23, 89 base, 48 points, $1.10M. POTE 86. Costs Tucker plus R1. Same bar: only if the R1 can be justified by a POTE 95+ player, which Kovalchuk at 86 is not.

recommendations.summary: Do not pursue Jovanovski despite his grades; Vandermeer gives 92/90/92 POTE at $0.40M versus Jovanovski's 91/92/71 POTE at $2.30M plus Klesla and R1.
recommendations.rationale: Jovanovski is older (29), more expensive, and costs the R1 that trajectory says to protect. Vandermeer at 25 with 92 potential dominates him on every axis except overall grade (79 vs 86), which is a one-year difference.

recommendations.summary: Sillinger is off the board: 4 points in 13 games at $1.80M. His production has collapsed and he is age 35.
recommendations.rationale: December memory tracked him at FACE 90, 87 overall as primary faceoff target. 4 points in 13 games since then means he cannot contribute in a playoff run. Savard at 36 points replaces him entirely.

recommendations.summary: Send Koltsov + St. Jacques + R3 to Atlanta for Savard; fills the faceoff gap (FACE 89, 36 pts/38 GP) with no cost beyond surplus players.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 35 points with six expirers will lose Savard for nothing in July. Koltsov and St. Jacques are both expiring, both POTE 94, both not in our plans — ATL get two bodies plus a pick instead of zero. Payroll effect: TOR saves $0.90M this season.

recommendations.summary: Send Upshall + R2 to Buffalo for Hartnell; the roster's zero players at 80+ toughness becomes TOUG 91 with CHKG 92, POTE 95, age 23.
recommendations.rationale: Coach says stop dressing Upshall (0.19 pts/g, 5.7 MPG). BUF at 40 points project 10+ points out of a playoff spot and must sell Hartnell or lose him for nothing in July. They get POTE-99, CHKG-87, age 22 plus a second-rounder. Payroll effect: TOR saves $0.40M.

recommendations.summary: Send Alexeev to Philadelphia for Vandermeer; adds TOUG 92, CHKG 90, age 25, POTE 92 at $0.40M expiring. Gated on GM confirming Alexeev is expendable.
recommendations.rationale: PHI at 45 points with nine expiring contracts become a seller if they fall below the line by February. Alexeev (POTE 94, $1.50M, 4 years) gives them a developmental winger at a team-friendly price. Payroll effect: TOR saves $1.10M. Risk: PHI at 45 are borderline and may still be buying in March.

recommendations.summary: If no deal lands, put Roberts (TOUG 92, CHKG 86) on the fourth line per the coach's recommendation and accept toughness and faceoffs as summer problems to solve via free agency.
recommendations.rationale: The coverage phase confirms zero internal fix for 80+ toughness among active players. Roberts at 39 with 2 points in 8 games is not a long-term answer but closes the checking deficiency for a playoff run if healthy.

recommendations.summary: Eminger at 14 GP and POTE 99 needs to be dressed every game if healthy; 35% share is not developing a 22-year-old third-pairing D who produces 0.43 pts/g when used.
recommendations.rationale: At 0.43 pts/g on 17 MPG he outperforms Colaiacovo (0.12) and Stahle (0.22) who are scratched. The 26 games he missed are the development loss, not his production when on ice.

recommendations.summary: Stop dressing Upshall; 0.19 pts/g at 5.7 MPG over 31 games at age 22 is not development, and the L4 RW spot is available for Spacek or a younger body to get real minutes.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 at 0.19 pts/g in 31 games at age 22 with no path to more ice. The sample is large enough. Carrying him blocks a real audition for someone else.

recommendations.summary: Spezza at POTE 99, age 22, 0.19 pts/g on 5.4 MPG with morale 82 has no path in this lineup; the GM should explore whether he can be moved or placed where he gets real minutes.
recommendations.rationale: Flagged in March, now 26 games in. At 22 the development clock is running. We cannot develop him on 5 MPG and he cannot earn more here.

recommendations.summary: Chlup, Nash, Chistov, Klesla and Gaborik are all earning their roles by production and ice time; no adjustment needed.
recommendations.rationale: 0.78, 0.60, 0.68, 0.45 and 0.50 pts/g respectively on 15-25 MPG. Each is getting what his output has earned.

recommendations.summary: Richards and Afinogenov system-fit review is now a two-season problem; offseason coaching change required before either is pencilled as a top-six forward next year.
recommendations.rationale: Richards: 0.69 (this year) after 0.71 (last year) after 1.08 (the year before). Afinogenov: 0.62 after 0.73 after 1.17. Two full seasons at the depressed rate with flat or rising minutes and no injury.

recommendations.summary: Klesla at 0.46 pts/g and Jackman at 0.64 are both at peak sell value with the deadline six weeks away. Klesla is 87 OVR expiring; Jackman is 86 OVR at $0.70M x 2.
recommendations.rationale: Klesla's 0.46 is his best rate and his OVR recovered to 87. Jackman reverted from 0.70 to 0.64 but is still well above the 0.55 sell trigger. Both rates have historically bled after peaking.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev's rate moved back above the 0.45 floor to 0.48 at 30 games, but that is 2 points in his last 4. Keep him on probation, not in the regular rotation.
recommendations.rationale: From 0.40 at 26 games (Dec 20) to 0.48 at 30 games (now) means a 4-game hot streak. One sample does not reverse the development case.

recommendations.summary: McCabe at 0.53 over 15 games (up from 0.30 over 10) is a 5-game hot stretch, not recovery. Hold on sell-list status until 20 games.
recommendations.rationale: The jump from 0.30 to 0.53 implies 5 points in 5 games. At $3.00M x 3 and age 30, a hot week does not restore trade value.

recommendations.summary: Four young forwards (Gardener, Spacek, Upshall, Spezza) plus Colaiacovo at D are all in the minutes-collapse pattern with sub-0.25 rates. Next camp must enforce the 8-MPG scratch rule or these five consume roster spots again in February.
recommendations.rationale: Gardener 0.00/3.0 MPG, Spacek 0.23/4.3, Upshall 0.17/5.3, Spezza 0.19/5.4, Colaiacovo 0.12/12.6. The systemic pattern from October is confirmed at scale.

recommendations.summary: Chlup at 19, Nash at 21 and Chistov at 22 are all growing and deserve continued top-nine minutes. No reduction warranted.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup 0.77/21.0 MPG in 40 GP. Nash 0.59/15.5 in 40. Chistov 0.64/20.8 in 40. All three are producing above replacement level with stable or rising loads.

recommendations.summary: No ice-time changes needed; the room is healthy and trending up after recent wins.
recommendations.rationale: Lowest morale on the roster is Brendl at 81, a deliberate GM scratch. Every active player is at 83 or above and gaining. Richards at 88 and 12.3 MPG is the closest to a concern but his trend is positive and he has not re-crossed below 85.

recommendations.summary: Put Roberts on L4 to fix the checking deficiency (mean 65) if he is healthy.
recommendations.rationale: L4 checking mean is 65 and toughness mean 59, both lowest on the roster. Roberts at 84 checking and 72 toughness is the only available player who raises the mean. He is currently scratched and not injured.

recommendations.summary: K2 checking mean of 76 is thin but there is no better personnel available to swap in.
recommendations.rationale: Only Fischer (92) clears 80 on K2. Roberts at 84 could relieve Fischer but K1 already has three of our four other 80+ checkers. Until a fifth checker arrives on the roster, K2 stays as-is.

recommendations.summary: We need one more forward with 80+ checking. Five players cover every defensive assignment on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: Checking above 80: Jackman 92, Fischer 92, Roberts 84, McCabe 83, Nash 82. All five are already deployed across K1, K2, and three even-strength lines. A sixth checker relieves K2 and gives L4 a defensive identity.

recommendations.summary: No lineup change for BOS. Every line is a talent mismatch in our favour and the D pair order already puts our best pair against Thornton.
recommendations.rationale: BOS has one player above 80 OVR (Thornton, 86). Their second-line centre Hilbert is 77, third-line Vernarsky is 69. Our D pairs at 87/86, 85/84 and 84/82 face D pairs at 75/77, 72/76 and 74/70. The 0-2-0 season record is not explained by talent; it likely reflects discipline against their 3.9 PP chances per game.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo if his fatigue icon is clear. Ouellet covers if tired.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 95 against Raycroft at 80 is a 15-point edge. Check the streak cell before confirming per the January 19th standing order.

recommendations.summary: Trade Klesla before the deadline. 87 OVR, expiring, 0.45 pts/g. Buyer sees the grade, we see the rate.
recommendations.rationale: 18 points in 40 games is second-pair production behind a first-pair grade. $0.90M x 1 means we either get value now or lose him free. His rate recovered from 0.40 (Dec 15) to 0.45 which keeps OVR optics at 87 but won't last.

recommendations.summary: Jackman's heater is fading (0.70 at 37 games to 0.65 at 40). If no trade call arrives within 5-6 games he reverts to keep permanently.
recommendations.rationale: Sell trigger is 0.55 (set Nov 13). At current 0.10/g scoring pace he crosses in roughly 10 games. At 86 OVR and $0.70M x 2 he is a bargain if we keep him. The only reason to move him is the streak optics, and those are disappearing.

recommendations.summary: McCabe remains an end-of-season trade candidate at $3.00M x 3, age 30, 0.53 pts/g.
recommendations.rationale: Rate improved from 0.30 (Dec 24) to 0.53 at 15 games but still below the 0.60 threshold. Not a deadline urgency but dead weight for next season if rate doesn't stabilize above 0.60.

recommendations.slot: faceoff duty, third or fourth line
recommendations.summary: Line Wallin for faceoff duty on L3 or L4; at 83 FACE he is the second-best draw-taker on the roster and is not lined.
recommendations.rationale: Only Sundin (90) and Wallin (83) carry 80+ faceoffs. Chlup at 75 and Richards at 70 lose most draws on the bottom two lines. Wallin is on the roster and currently unlined.

recommendations.summary: Dress Roberts if healthy for 86 checking depth; he is on the roster and not in any unit.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts carries 86 CHKG, 90 HERO, and 98 durability at 39. Without him the lined 80+ checkers drop to four (Jackman, McCabe, Fischer, Upshall). The coach already flagged this on December 29.

recommendations.summary: Kurka at 88 TOUG, 90 CHKG, $0.60M expiring, age 23 is the primary toughness target when the February window opens.
recommendations.rationale: Zero players at 80+ toughness on this roster. Kurka closes the gap with 88 toughness and 90 checking at 23 for a salary that barely moves payroll. CAR's $63.79M payroll and 14 expiring deals make them the most motivated seller.

recommendations.summary: Bell at 88 FACE, 82 TOUG, $0.90M expiring, age 25 closes faceoffs and toughness in one acquisition; prepare the package for late February.
recommendations.rationale: He is the only single player who addresses both thin columns simultaneously. At 25 and $0.90M expiring, CHI cannot re-sign him and will listen. Package: Tucker + St. Jacques + R3.

recommendations.summary: No trade action before late February per the GM's standing order; these are targets to prepare, not moves to make now.
recommendations.rationale: The GM set January urgency aside on January 15, 2005 and confirmed negotiations should not open until late February. The deadline is in March. TOR at 26-8-1 and 61 points are not a seller.

recommendations.proposed: Hejduk (COL) or equivalent 90+ base winger on a short deal
recommendations.summary: Move Gaborik before the March 2006 deadline; his value is falling with every scratched game and $11.90M/yr through 2010 is unresolvable otherwise.
recommendations.rationale: 9 pts in 19 GP at $11.90M/year is the worst money-to-production ratio on the roster. Coach demands he play; if he plays and stays at 0.47 pts/g the contract is still a burden. The Hejduk package saves $9.40M annually and COL cannot retain four expirers.

recommendations.proposed: Chlup, Luongo, Klesla, Spezza — all locked 5-6 years in July 2006
recommendations.summary: Lock Chlup, Luongo, Klesla and Spezza on 5-6 year deals the same week in July 2006 before any can walk.
recommendations.rationale: All four expire July 2006. Chlup is 19 with 30 points and POTE 95; Luongo is the franchise goalie at POTE 97; Klesla is 23 with 17 points and POTE 97; Spezza is 22 with POTE 99. Losing any one restarts the timeline.

recommendations.proposed: Richards, Chistov, Nash extended early in July 2007
recommendations.summary: Begin early extensions of Richards, Chistov and Nash in July 2007 to break the July 2009 eleven-player cluster into two manageable summers.
recommendations.rationale: 11 players at $37.40M expire simultaneously in July 2009. Moving three of them to 2011 splits the burden. Richards at 26 in 2007 will accept a raise but not a prime-age one; Chistov and Nash at 23-24 are at their cheapest.

recommendations.summary: Package Spezza + R2 to Vancouver for Bertuzzi (94 base, TOUG 83, CHKG 87, $2.60M expiring) at the March 19 deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto have zero players above 80 toughness; Bertuzzi carries 83/87 with 94 base and is expiring on a team with 13 expirers and the league's lowest payroll.

recommendations.summary: Package Tucker + R1 to Atlanta for Heatley (91 base) at the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Atlanta are a rebuild with multiple expirers; they collect a first-rounder and a veteran. We acquire a 91-base winger without touching the core.

recommendations.summary: Package Koltsov + St. Jacques + R3 to Atlanta for Savard (79 base, FACE 88, $1.00M expiring).
recommendations.rationale: Savard gives a 88 FACE centre on a cheap expiring deal; Atlanta shed two more expirers and get three players plus a pick for their rebuild.

recommendations.summary: Trade Mogilny (90 base, $5.50M, 36, expiring) to any non-contender for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: At $5.50M and 36, he is the highest-salary chip on the roster. The pick-recovery mechanic converts him to draft capital we keep.

recommendations.summary: Renew Luongo (26, 91 base, $1.60M) on a 5-year star deal in July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: Prime-age franchise goalie at a cheap salary; re-signing yearly ratchets demands per the guide.

recommendations.summary: Renew Chlup (19, 82 base, $2.34M) on a 5-year deal in July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: Franchise centre at 19 with high potential; locking him young on long term is the cheapest path.

recommendations.summary: Renew Klesla (23, 78 base, $0.90M) on a 4-year deal in July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: Young defenceman on a cheap deal with growth remaining; 4 years secures him through his development window.

recommendations.summary: Renew Ouellet (24, 81 base, $0.90M) on a 2-year backup deal in July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: Capable backup, older-player term rule applies; no need for a long deal at this role.

recommendations.summary: Take no trade action before late February; sellers remain sellers and the deadline is 74 days away.
recommendations.rationale: Standing order from 2005-01-15: no January urgency. Negotiations open late February when sellers are desperate.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bertuzzi (VAN) at the March deadline — 94 base, 85 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 54 pts/39GP, $2.60M expiring closes toughness and replaces Mogilny's production in one move.
recommendations.rationale: VAN at 46 pts have 13 expirers on $46.36M league-lowest payroll and cannot keep Bertuzzi, Jovanovski, and Naslund simultaneously. Bertuzzi is 27, the youngest of the three, and the highest-overall player on any seller.

recommendations.summary: Target Hartnell (BUF) — 23, 89 TOUG, 90 CHKG, POTE 95, $1.10M expiring. Closes toughness tonight and is a five-year piece.
recommendations.rationale: BUF at 38 pts are bottom-third with 5 expiring deals. Hartnell has only 17.6 MPG and 10 pts in 26 games — underused at his age and cost. Package: Alexeev plus R3.

recommendations.summary: Bell (CHI, 25, LW) closes faceoffs (FACE 92) and toughness (86 TOUG) simultaneously at $0.90M expiring. One body, two gaps.
recommendations.rationale: CHI at 31 pts with 8 expirers are rebuilding and will not re-sign a 25-year-old at 80 base. He is the league's best faceoff specialist on a deal expiring this summer.

recommendations.summary: Jovanovski (VAN, D, 29) is 93 TOUG, 94 CHKG, 89 base, 31.4 MPG, $2.30M with 1 year left — the best shutdown defenceman available.
recommendations.rationale: VAN's 13 expirers force triage and Jovanovski at 29 is the oldest of their three big expirers. Package must avoid core defense: Tucker plus R1 is the realistic ask.

recommendations.summary: Heatley (ATL, 23) at 91 base, 43 pts/37GP, $1.10M expiring replaces Mogilny's scoring with a player who will be a top-liner until 2015.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 33 pts with $40.34M league-lowest payroll cannot re-sign Heatley, Kovalchuk, and Savard. Package: Tucker plus R1. Fallback if Bertuzzi is unobtainable.

recommendations.summary: Kurka (CAR, LW, 23) — 88 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 78 base, 26 pts/38GP, $0.60M expiring. Cheapest toughness that also produces points.
recommendations.rationale: CAR hold 14 expiring deals on $65.29M and must shed players. Kurka at $0.60M is nearly free and his grades have not decayed since November. Package: Upshall plus R3.

recommendations.summary: Witt (WSH, D, 29) — 84 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 80 base, 31.7 MPG, $1.70M expiring. Shutdown pair anchor for a playoff run.
recommendations.rationale: WSH at 30 pts (10-21-6) are the worst record in the East with 5 expirers and $57.05M payroll. Yonkman (84/86, POTE 89, $0.60M) is available in the same deal.

recommendations.summary: Sean Hill (CAR, D, 35) — 84 TOUG, 85 CHKG, 81 base, $2.30M expiring. Pure playoff rental toughness for the blue line.
recommendations.rationale: CAR at 41 pts with 14 expirers cannot keep a 35-year-old. He brings 32 pts/36GP production on a physical game. Package: Mogilny plus R3 — both are expiring rentals.

recommendations.summary: Naslund (VAN, LW, 32) — 92 base, 59 pts/39GP, $4.40M with 1 year. Highest-scoring player on any seller; fallback for Mogilny's production.
recommendations.rationale: His $4.40M is the largest single salary on any seller's expiring list. VAN must shed him or Bertuzzi; if they keep Bertuzzi (younger, physical) they will move Naslund. Does not close toughness.

recommendations.summary: Play Gaborik in the top six through February. His 0.47 pts/g will rise with minutes, which protects his $11.90M trade value when a destination appears.
recommendations.rationale: The Hejduk package to COL is now unlikely — COL are 3rd in the Western conference at 47 points and will not trade their top winger mid-race. Gaborik's value is eroding with every scratched game; minutes are the only lever until a new target materializes.

recommendations.summary: Trade Upshall plus R2 to BUF for Hartnell — the single best value on the board, closing the toughness gap with a 23-year-old who can stay.
recommendations.rationale: Hartnell (89 TOUG, 90 CHKG, POTE 95, $1.10M expiring) is surplus production at BUF who are 38 points with 5 expirers. Upshall (22, POTE 99, CHKG 87) is surplus here per the coach. BUF get a younger high-ceiling winger plus a pick; we get the toughness we have zero of internally.

recommendations.summary: Trade Koltsov plus R3 to CHI for Bell — closes faceoffs (FACE 92) and toughness (TOUG 86) in one 25-year-old body at $0.90M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Bell is 80 base and expiring; CHI at 31 points with 8 expirers have no reason to keep him. Koltsov (ACCE 96, POTE 94, $1.10M expiring) gives CHI elite straight-line speed on a project that costs them nothing long-term. Both clubs are swapping expiring deals.

recommendations.summary: Trade Gardener plus R1 to CAR for Sean Hill — a playoff-only toughness fix at 84 TOUG and 85 CHKG for a blue line that has none.
recommendations.rationale: CAR are $65.29M with 14 expirers; Hill at 35 walks in July regardless. Gardener (20, POTE 98, $1.20M for 5 years) is cheap controlled upside. The R1 is expensive for a rental — this is the lowest-priority proposal and the GM should only spend the first if proposals one and two both fail.

recommendations.summary: The Hejduk route is dead: COL are 3rd in the Western conference at 47 points and will not trade him mid-race. Gaborik's $11.90M stays unless a new destination appears before March.
recommendations.rationale: The coach's recommendation to play Gaborik is now the only lever on his value. At 9 pts/19 GP as a scratch, his trade value erodes weekly. Top-six minutes and production are the only path to a February package that recovers anything.

recommendations.summary: Close the goalie trade monitoring task; Luongo at 91 base IS the target, DiPietro at 79 base does not qualify.
recommendations.rationale: The original Jan 2005 objective was a 90+ goalie from a non-contender. Luongo (91 base, $1.60M) already fills it. DiPietro sits at 79 base in 32 starts, well below the bar. The GM's March 2005 order ('Goalies are solved') remains in force.

recommendations.summary: Plan Luongo's 5-year extension for July 2006; his contract has one year left at $1.60M.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo turns 27 in April and is our starter at 91 base. A 5-year deal locks the position through his prime. Contract clustering risk if left too long.

recommendations.summary: Stop dressing Gardener for the remainder of the season; 0 points in 23 games at 3.6 MPG does not earn a roster spot.
recommendations.rationale: Gardener is 20 with POTE 98 but has produced zero points in 23 games. His 3.6 MPG shows the coaches do not trust him in any situation. His spot as a dressed extra should go to a young body who will actually play.

recommendations.summary: Spacek is at 5.4 MPG over 13 games, below the 8-MPG floor. If he stays under 8 through January he follows Gardener out of the rotation.
recommendations.rationale: At POTE 91 and age 20 he has runway, but 0.31 pts/g on 5.4 MPG is the start of the collapse pattern I have tracked across Spezza, Upshall and last year's Spacek himself. One more month of this confirms it.

recommendations.summary: No change tonight. NJ is a quality opponent (22-8) and the go-all-out framework applies, so development rotations are not the priority this week.
recommendations.rationale: The standing order from January 15th is clear: against quality opponents we maximize quality. Spezza and Upshall at 5 MPG are a camp problem, not a tonight problem.

recommendations.summary: Stahle's scratch is correct and should hold. 0.22 pts/g on 12.5 MPG at age 21 with POTE 96 is underperforming the third pair.
recommendations.rationale: He has 4 points in 18 games. The other young D (Eminger) is producing at double his rate on similar ice. The spot goes to whoever performs, not to whoever has the highest scouting number.

recommendations.summary: Stop dressing Gardener; he has 0 points in 23 games on 3.0 MPG and the pattern is confirmed.
recommendations.rationale: The young-forward minutes-collapse pattern now has five confirmations across two seasons. Gardener at 0.00 pts/g over 23 games on 3.0 MPG has no development happening. Those roster spots belong to Stahle or another young body getting real minutes.

recommendations.summary: Spacek at 0.25 on 4.4 MPG over 13 games is another minutes-collapse case. Stop carrying him.
recommendations.rationale: He went from 17 MPG to 4.4 with a rate of 0.25. Same pattern as Upshall, Gardener, Spezza. He cannot sustain the role we tried to give him.

recommendations.summary: Colaiacovo at 0.12 pts/g over 25 games with zero goals is the weakest regular D and the sell candidate among the young defence.
recommendations.rationale: His minutes rose from 6 to 12.6 and he still produced only 3 points. Stahle is trending up at 0.24 on 12.9 MPG and can absorb the role. Deadline is the window.

recommendations.summary: Chlup at 0.76 on 21 MPG at 19 is handling a first-line role. Keep him there.
recommendations.rationale: His rate is strong for his age and minutes are where they need to be for development. No adjustment.

recommendations.summary: Richards stuck at 0.71 on flat minutes for a second season. Flag for offseason system review; no in-season fix available.
recommendations.rationale: The May finding identified system fit. Six months and 39 games later the number is identical. I have no lever inside the season that changes this.

recommendations.summary: No morale-driven line change tonight; the room is recovering on winning and no player is at a level that forces intervention.
