recommendations.rationale: Every dressed player is at 88+ and climbing. Richards (88 morale, 12.4 MPG) and Lundmark (88, 7.9 MPG) carry structural minute deficits against their displayed grades but are recovering on results, not deteriorating. Against NJ tonight the GM's standing order is maximize quality, which means no development scratches and no minutes reshuffles.

recommendations.slot: left wing on the second penalty-kill unit
recommendations.summary: Put Roberts on K2 tonight in place of Richards; his 83 checking is the second-best on the roster and K2's mean of 75 is a liability against NJ.
recommendations.rationale: K2 has no player above 80 in checking. Roberts at 83 and toughness 71 is the only available upgrade. Richards stays on L3 as centre where his 77 faceoffs matter; he does not need to also kill penalties.

recommendations.summary: We have exactly four skaters above 80 checking (Jackman 91, Roberts 83, McCabe 82, Nash 81) and cannot build two PK units with a checking mean above 80.
recommendations.rationale: K1 gets three of the four. K2's best available checker is Chlup at below 80 or Roberts at 83 if he's dressed. A fifth checker above 80 would let both units function without pulling a top-six forward off his line.

recommendations.slot: even-strength lines 1-3 and both power-play units
recommendations.summary: No change to L1, L2, L3, P1 or P2 for NJ.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has the scoring (91 mean), L2 has Nash's 81 checking alongside Kaberle, L3 has Richards drawing at 77. Both PPs carry 87+ scoring means. Against a quality opponent, this is our best configuration.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo if his fatigue icon is clear. Ouellet covers if tired.
recommendations.rationale: 95 OVR vs NJ's 3.00 GF/game offense and Brodeur at 93. We need our best man in net against an equal-quality opponent. Check fatigue per standing order.

recommendations.summary: No line changes for NJ.
recommendations.rationale: NJ's D is built for our attack: Brown (67 OVR) faces our L2, Hecl (66) and Cullen (67) face our L3, and Kubina (79/72/74 speed) cannot track Chistov or Gaborik. Our first line already wins every matchup on speed, and our centres win all four faceoffs (Sundin 94 vs Gomez 63). The structure exploits their weaknesses without intervention.

recommendations.summary: Top sell candidate: 87 OVR, $0.90M expiring, 0.44 pts/g trending up. Move him at the deadline while the grade is peak.
recommendations.rationale: His rate has recovered from 0.29 (Nov 26) through 0.40 (Dec 15) to 0.44 now. A buyer sees 87 and cheap; the sub-0.50 production is invisible on the trade screen. Window closes if he breaks 0.55.

recommendations.summary: Second sell candidate. The 4-game point-per-game heater at 0.57 pts/g makes him marketable NOW for the first time since I flagged him.
recommendations.rationale: He was at 0.30 (Dec 24), unsellable. At 0.57 over 14 games the recent tape looks fine. $3.00M x 3 at age 30 is the anchor; sell into the run before it reverts.

recommendations.summary: Third sell candidate. 86 OVR, $0.70M x 2, 0.67 pts/g. Still above the 0.55 keep trigger but the heater is cooling.
recommendations.rationale: Was 0.70 at 37 GP on Dec 29, now 0.67 at 39. If he hits 0.55 the recommendation reverses. Sell window closing from the top.

recommendations.summary: Fourth sell candidate and the one who definitely goes. Zero goals, 3 points in 25 games, 76 OVR, $1.40M x 4. No development path visible.
recommendations.rationale: Unchanged from the last three reports. The question is whether a buyer exists for the contract, not whether he stays.

recommendations.summary: Add Nash to K2 as the coach recommends; at 82 CHKG he is the only rostered forward outside the top four checkers with a real penalty-killing grade.
recommendations.rationale: Checking sits at only six players at 80+ and two of them (Tucker, Roberts) are not lined. Nash at 82 checking gives a fifth usable body on the PK without touching deadline chips.

recommendations.summary: Keep Chlup on the first line permanently; at 75 FACE and 0.79 pts/g in 20.9 MPG at age 19, he is the only internal answer to the faceoff thinness below Sundin.
recommendations.rationale: Only two players at 80+ FACE (Sundin 90, Wallin 83 not lined). Chlup at 75 is the next-best draw-taker and the youngest by five years. Moving him off the top line drops L1 faceoffs to Sundin-level only when he is out.

recommendations.summary: Toughness remains at zero across the entire roster with no internal fix at any age; Kurka (CAR, 23, 88 TOUG, 90 CHKG, $0.60M expiring) is still the only player on the market closing this gap.
recommendations.rationale: The best Toronto toughness is Jackman at 75. The next two are Roberts at 73 (age 39, expiring) and McCabe at 73 (age 30). A playoff series against a physical team has no answer. CAR at 16 points with 14 expiring and $63.79M payroll remains a forced seller per the November note.

recommendations.summary: Faceoff thinness below Sundin and Chlup is a real gap but no acquisition at a reasonable price closes it; the Bell and Avery options from earlier this year addressed wing faceoffs, not the centre-slot need.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin at 90 FACE is 34. Chlup at 75 is 19 and developing. Wallin at 83 is a defenceman not lined at centre. The GM killed the Bell faceoff argument on 2005-01-25 because Bell is a wing. No rostered centre carries above 75 FACE after Chlup, but acquiring a top centre would conflict with Chlup's development timeline.

recommendations.summary: Lock Chlup on a 5-6 year deal in July 2006 at 19 years old, 30 points in 37 games, POTE 95, currently $2.34M on one year.
recommendations.rationale: He is the future first-line centre, his contract expires July 2006, and at 19 with POTE 95 he will command a large raise the moment his stock rises further. Five years at a controlled cost while he develops is the single highest-leverage renewal on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Lock Luongo on a 5-6 year deal in July 2006 at 26 years old, POTE 97, currently $1.60M on one year.
recommendations.rationale: Behind him is Ouellet at 81 base and Tellqvist at 91 base. If Luongo walks, the starter slot is a competition between two men who are one clear step below him. Re-sign him the same week as Chlup.

recommendations.summary: Release Roberts immediately; he is 39, POTE 52, 2 points in 8 games, scratched, and carries $4.90M per year for two more years.
recommendations.rationale: No trade partner will absorb a 39-year-old scratched wing at $4.90M. Releasing saves $9.80M over two years with zero competitive loss. His POTE of 52 means he cannot even qualify for the over-80 pick-recovery mechanic.

recommendations.proposed: Begin early extensions of Richards, Chistov, Nash in July 2007
recommendations.summary: Start breaking the July 2009 cluster by extending Richards, Chistov, and Nash in July 2007, removing $15.60M from a single-summer renewal pile.
recommendations.rationale: Eleven players on four-year deals ($37.40M combined) expire simultaneously in July 2009. Re-signing eleven men in one window forces market-rate payments on all of them. Extending the three highest-value pieces two years early staggers the obligation and avoids the cascade the manual warns about.

recommendations.summary: Execute the Gaborik-plus-R2-for-Hejduk trade at the March 2006 deadline; after that window closes there is no lever on a locked contract.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik at $11.90M for five years is the single largest line on the payroll and he is a scratch at 8 points in 17 games. Every week he sits reduces what a partner gives. The March deadline is the last exit before his contract runs another four years. Hejduk at 91 base on $2.50M saves $9.40M annually and plays every night.

recommendations.summary: Sign Luongo to a five-year deal at the July 2006 renewal window; he is 26, 91 base, $1.60M, and the single most important contract on the board.
recommendations.rationale: He is a franchise goaltender in his prime expiring on a $1.60M salary. Without a five-year lock, every contender bids for him and we lose the player around whom the next half-decade is built.

recommendations.summary: Sign Chlup to a five-year deal at renewal; he is 19, first-line centre, $2.34M, and the youngest cornerstone on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: A 19-year-old first-line centre with POTE in the 90s will be the most contested restricted free agent in the league by 2007. Lock him at $2.34M plus a modest raise before his 0.79 pts/g at 20.9 MPG makes his price double.

recommendations.proposed: First-round pick plus a high-potential young forward
recommendations.summary: Trade Mogilny at the March 19 deadline via the over-80 pick-recovery mechanic; he is 36, $5.50M, 90 base, expiring, and his 0.76 pts/g is replaceable with Chlup and Gaborik.
recommendations.rationale: He clears the mechanic that turns an expiring 80+ player into a draft pick. The $5.50M freed pays for a new acquisition, and the pick funds the next development cycle. If we keep him, he walks in July for nothing.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Savard at the deadline via Koltsov + St. Jacques + R3; all three currency pieces are expiring and ATL at 20 points cannot re-sign him.
recommendations.rationale: Savard gives us the 88 FACE we lack behind Chlup at 75. His $1.00M is expiring, so worst case he is a playoff rental. Best case he fills a hole that lets us avoid trading Spezza.

recommendations.summary: Move Tucker at the deadline for a draft pick; he is 30, $1.30M, expiring, and was the designated chip at last March.
recommendations.rationale: At 30 with an expiring deal he is a one-year rental for whoever buys. A pick is the floor return via the over-80 mechanic if his displayed rating clears 80.

recommendations.summary: Renew Ouellet on a two-year deal as the backup to Luongo; he is 24, 81 base, $0.90M.
recommendations.rationale: Two-year deals for backups are cheap and flexible. If Luongo re-signs five years, Ouellet gives insurance without blocking Tellqvist's path to a starting job.

recommendations.proposed: Bertuzzi (VAN, 94 base, $2.60M expiring) via Spezza + Alexeev + R2
recommendations.summary: Backup plan if Savard fails: acquire Bertuzzi for a 94-base wing alongside Chlup; Spezza at 73 base and 0.19 pts/g in 26 GP is the cost.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza's POTE 99 says he might develop, but 5 points in 26 games at 22 suggests the window is closing. Bertuzzi's 1.25 pts/g and 94 base are certain; Spezza at 73 base is not.

recommendations.summary: No deadline action before late February. Negotiations open then per the standing order; sellers remain sellers for 80 days.
recommendations.rationale: The deadline is 80 days away. VAN, ATL, and PHX all have losing records today and will have worse ones by March. Their desperation increases with each passing week.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Sean Hill (CAR, D) via Mogilny or Tucker package; 84 TOUG, 85 CHKG, 32 pts/36 GP at $2.30M expiring solves toughness and D depth simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Hill's 32 points in 36 games at 23.7 MPG is top-four offensive production wrapped in 84/85 toughness-checking. CAR at 41 points with 14 expiring deals at $63.79M payroll cannot retain him. Mogilny is expiring at $5.50M and above 80, making him eligible for the pick-recovery mechanic or a direct swap.

recommendations.summary: Add Kurka (CAR, LW) to the CAR shopping list alongside Hill; 88 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 26 pts/36 GP at $0.60M is the cheapest toughness body in the league.
recommendations.rationale: Kurka's 26 points in 36 games at $0.60M expiring is better value than Hartnell (10 pts, $1.10M) or any internal option. He was absent from November queries but is confirmed back on an expiring deal. Same destination as Hill makes a double-package feasible.

recommendations.summary: Keep Witt (WSH, D) as the backup toughness target if CAR negotiations stall; 89 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 18 pts/36 GP at $1.70M on the most desperate seller in the league.
recommendations.rationale: WSH at 26 points with 5 expiring and $57.05M payroll are the clearest sellers. Witt's 93 CHKG is the best checking grade among available expirers. Yonkman ($0.60M, 89/91) sits beside him for a two-for-one.

recommendations.summary: If the faceoff-centre slot is still open when March arrives, redirect the Savard package to CGY for Conroy; 95 FACE vs 88, 25 pts/30 GP vs 32 pts/34 GP, $2.00M vs $1.00M.
recommendations.rationale: Conroy's 95 FACE is seven points above Savard and 25 points in 30 games (0.83 PPG) outpaces Savard's 0.94 PPG only marginally, but the faceoff gap is the one Toronto cannot manufacture internally. CGY at 41 points with 9 expiring and $52.08M payroll will move him.

recommendations.summary: Target Marleau (SJ, C) in July 2006 free agency if he is not re-signed; 89 base, POTE 81, age 26, 34 pts/35 GP, SJ cannot re-sign him at $7.57M with 14 other expirers.
recommendations.rationale: Marleau at 26 with POTE 81 and 89 base is the post-Sundin centre. A deadline trade would require the R1 the GM wants to keep; a summer signing from a $70M payroll with $33M profit is feasible and cheaper in assets.

recommendations.summary: Track Hossa (OTT, RW); 89 base, POTE 69, age 26, $2.30M expiring is cheap top-six scoring but only 31 GP suggests a health or role issue to verify before building a package.
recommendations.rationale: Ottawa at 32 points with 4 expiring and $59.27M payroll are less motivated sellers than VAN or ATL. Hossa's 26 points in 31 games is solid but the missing 6 games need explanation before targeting.

recommendations.summary: Hartnell (BUF, LW) at 89 TOUG, 90 CHKG, $1.10M expiring remains a viable alternative to Kurka if CAR negotiations stall; BUF at 36 points will move him.
recommendations.rationale: Hartnell's 10 points in 26 games is half Kurka's production for double the salary ($1.10M vs $0.60M). Lower priority than Kurka but same role and BUF are a more desperate seller (36 pts, 5 expiring) than CAR.

recommendations.summary: Trade Alexeev and Tucker to WSH for Witt and Yonkman, filling the zero-toughness hole with two expiring physical D's at no draft-pick cost.
recommendations.rationale: Witt (89 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 80 base) and Yonkman (89 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 74 base) are the only pairing of toughness D's available without spending a pick. WSH at 26 points, bottom of the league, $57.05M payroll they are cutting, cannot re-sign either. They get Alexeev (24, POTE 94, 4yr, $1.50M, 16 pts/30GP) as a rebuild asset. Alexeev is below the coach's 0.45 floor and Tucker has zero GP.

recommendations.summary: Trade Tucker and Gardener to CAR for Sean Hill (81 base, 84 TOUG, 85 CHKG, 32 pts/36GP, $2.30M expiring), solving toughness and scoring-D in one move.
recommendations.rationale: CAR at $63.79M with 14 expiring deals cannot retain Hill. They get Gardener (20, POTE 98, 5yr, $1.20M) as a controlled youth asset plus Tucker (expiring, releasable). Gardener produces zero points at 3.6 MPG and the coach is making his scratch permanent; we are not developing him. Salary is neutral ($2.50M out vs $2.30M in).

recommendations.current: Koltsov + St. Jacques + R3 to ATL for Savard
recommendations.proposed: Koltsov + St. Jacques + R3 to CGY for Conroy
recommendations.summary: Redirect the Savard package to CGY for Conroy (FACE 95, 85 base, 25 pts/30GP, $2.00M expiring) if they engage; seven faceoff points better than Savard at identical package cost.
recommendations.rationale: Conroy at FACE 95 changes playoff matchups in a way 88 does not. CGY at 41 points with nine expiring deals are in sell mode, but less desperate than ATL at 20 points. If CGY refuses or demands more, ATL remains the fallback and the original Savard package is unchanged.

recommendations.summary: If no toughness trade lands, Nash on K2 (88 TOUG, 82 CHKG) is the internal fallback giving one physical body on the PK alongside Jackman, McCabe and Fischer.
recommendations.rationale: The coach already recommended adding Nash to K2. Without an external acquisition, four practical checkers (Jackman 87 CHKG, McCabe 89, Fischer 90, Nash 82) is thin but playable for a playoff run. Faceoff gap remains unsolved without Conroy or Savard.

recommendations.summary: Luongo's contract has 1 year left; he must be re-signed in July 2006 or he walks and the backup is Ouellet at 86 displayed.
recommendations.rationale: He is 26 at 95 displayed with 19 GP this season. A 5-year deal locks our franchise goalie. The backup option (Ouellet, 86 displayed, 8 GP) is not a viable number one.

recommendations.summary: Put Gaborik back in the lineup. 0.47 pts/g on 22.6 MPG in 17 games means he has earned top-six minutes.
recommendations.rationale: He's producing at a top-six rate when given the ice and sitting scratched at 46% share. No other winger on the roster can match that rate on that ice time.

recommendations.summary: Stop dressing Upshall for token minutes. 0.21 pts/g on 5.4 MPG is not development; it is a slow morale bleed at 83.
recommendations.rationale: Same pattern Spezza showed in March. Five to six minutes a night develops nobody and his morale is dropping. Either find him a real role (there isn't one) or scratch him completely so he can be recalled when there is.

recommendations.summary: Same call as Upshall. 5 points in 26 games at 5.4 MPG with morale at 82 is the collapse pattern, not development.
recommendations.rationale: He has POTE 99 but at 0.19 pts/g he is nowhere near earning more than garbage minutes. Dressing him without a role costs him morale and gives us no better player on the ice.

recommendations.summary: The core four (Chlup, Nash, Chistov, Klesla) are all 100% share and earning every minute they get. Leave them alone.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup 0.81 pts/g at 20.6 MPG, Chistov 0.70 at 20.5, Nash 0.59 at 15.2, Klesla 0.46 at 25.7. They are the development story this season and none of them need a change.

recommendations.summary: Reinstate Alexeev into the dressing rotation; his rate recovered to 0.48 at 30 games, above the 0.45 floor.
recommendations.rationale: I scratched him at 0.40 over 26 games on December 20th. He has scored in the last four and the rate is back above threshold at 0.48 over 30 games.

recommendations.summary: Stop dressing Gardener; 0 points in 23 games on 3.0 MPG is a wasted roster spot.
recommendations.rationale: Fits the young-forward-minutes-collapse pattern exactly. Started at 16 MPG, now 3.0 with zero production. Those minutes belong to a younger body who will use them.

recommendations.summary: Pull Spacek from the rotation; 4.2 MPG and 0.30 rate over 11 games at 20 is no development.
recommendations.rationale: Collapsed from 17 MPG to 4.2 with no production. Same pattern as Gardener and Upshall. He needs real minutes or he needs to sit out and wait.

recommendations.summary: Eminger must move at this trade deadline or he is a UFA loss in July.
recommendations.rationale: Age 22, 0.45 pts/g over 11 games on 17.9 MPG, $1.2M expiring. The March window passed with him still here. One more deadline missed and the asset is gone.

recommendations.summary: McCabe stays on the sell list despite scoring in his last two.
recommendations.rationale: 0.42 over 12 games, well below the 0.60 threshold. Two good games lifted the rate from 0.30 but do not change the profile: 30 years old, $3.00M x 3.

recommendations.summary: Chlup is confirmed as the first-line centre; no development intervention needed.
recommendations.rationale: 0.81 pts/g on 21.0 MPG over 37 games at age 19. He is doing exactly what the role demands. Give him more of the game, not a different role.

recommendations.summary: No morale action needed. The entire dressed roster is climbing; the lowest reading is Luongo at 83 (+9) and he is recovering on wins alone.
recommendations.rationale: Nash at 15.2 MPG against a 98 OVR is the only structural minutes deficit but his morale reads 98 on the back of winning. No intervention until the streak breaks.

recommendations.summary: No change to L1, L2, P1, P2, K1, or K2. Each unit suits its role.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has Jackman's 91 checking plus 89 scoring mean. L2 has Fischer 84 and Nash 81 checking with 86 scoring mean. K1 averages 83 checking with both top checkers. P2 wins draws via McCabe's 79 faceoffs to feed Mogilny and Kaberle.

recommendations.summary: No change to L4 composition. The 64 checking mean is a roster gap we cannot close with these bodies.
recommendations.rationale: Spacek, Koltsov, Upshall have 93 speed mean — that is their identity. Nobody available raises their checking mean without pulling a checker off L1 or L2.

recommendations.summary: If Roberts (83 checking, 71 toughness) is healthy, dress him on L4. If he is injured, we are one true checker short behind Jackman and Nash.
recommendations.rationale: The role inventory shows only Jackman 91, McCabe 82, Nash 81 as active checkers. Roberts at 83 is scratched. Against a physical fourth line, L4's 64 checking mean and 59 toughness mean get overrun.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo if his fatigue icon is clear. Ouellet covers if tired.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is 95 OVR against a 2.30-goal-per-game offence. We're on a 9-game point streak and want to protect it with the best available.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes for VAN. The current setup wins every matchup on the sheet.
recommendations.rationale: VAN's top line (Bertuzzi 91, Naslund 89) is the only unit that threatens, and Jackman's 93 checking plus Klesla's 99 speed already answer them. Their bottom eight are 64-74 OVR and our depth owns those shifts.

recommendations.summary: Sell Jackman at the deadline while his heater has him at 0.70 pts/g and 86 OVR on $0.70M x 2.
recommendations.rationale: 4 points in 2 games lifted his rate from 0.63 to 0.70, reversing the decay that had him crossing the 0.55 sell trigger around game 45. His career rate is 0.48; this streak will regress. The card reads best right now.

recommendations.summary: Klesla stays on the deadline sell list but urgency is moderate — his rate is climbing (0.46 at 37 GP) so the window closes if he reaches 0.55.
recommendations.rationale: 87 OVR expiring at $0.90M is attractive to a buyer, but his improving trend means waiting costs nothing and a 0.55+ rate makes him worth keeping. Reassess at deadline.

recommendations.summary: McCabe remains the release candidate: $3.00M x 3 at 30 years old, 0.42 pts/g in 12 games.
recommendations.rationale: No improvement that changes the picture. Too little value to trade; the contract is the problem.

recommendations.summary: Line Tucker on L4 to add the team's fifth 80+ checker (83 CHKG) to active duty.
recommendations.rationale: Checking sits at only 4 lined players above 80; Tucker at 83 is the next available and the coach already recommended this.

recommendations.summary: Dress Wallin in a faceoff-specific role to give the lineup a second 80+ draw-taker (83 FACE).
recommendations.rationale: Faceoffs sit at 2 above 80 (Sundin 90, Wallin 83); Chlup at 75 and Richards at 70 cannot win draws against top centres.

recommendations.summary: Place Gaborik on the top line with Sundin rather than L4; his 92 PLAY and 98 SPEED need a distributor.
recommendations.rationale: The coach puts him on L4 citing underproduction, but 0.47 pts/g at 22.6 MPG on the fourth line reflects linemate quality as much as skill; every scratched game erodes his $11.90M trade value.

recommendations.summary: Dress Eminger every night at top-pair minutes; the GM's standing order keeps him, so the coach's binary resolves to minutes.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 at age 21 with NHL experience is the best defensive asset on the roster by potential; the GM's order of 2005-02-19 explicitly prohibits selling him.

recommendations.summary: Toughness reads 0 players above 80, but the GM closed all toughness targets in December and I do not reopen it.
recommendations.rationale: The Dec 4 finding that eleven players sat at 80+ on displayed toughness conflicts with today's reading of zero; the discrepancy may be methodological (role composite vs individual TOUG grade) rather than real movement.

recommendations.summary: Trade Gaborik by the March 2006 deadline; his $11.90M/year through July 2010 is dead money and his trade value drops with every scratched game.
recommendations.rationale: 8 points in 17 games at $11.90M is 13.2% of payroll with zero output. His value declines monotonically while scratched; moving him in February preserves more than waiting until March.

recommendations.summary: Renew Luongo on a 5-6 year deal in July 2006; he is 26, 97 POTE, $1.60M expiring, and the backup behind him (Ouellet, 97 POTE but 81 base) is a clear step down in production tonight.
recommendations.rationale: He has 1 year left at $1.60M. Without a new contract he walks in July and the team starts the season with a 24-year-old who has played 8 games. This is the highest-priority renewal on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Renew Chlup on a 5-6 year deal in July 2006 alongside Luongo; 19 years old, 28 points in 35 games, POTE 95, $2.34M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: He is the franchise centre and his asking price will double after this season. Signing him at 19 on a long deal locks the position through his mid-twenties at a fraction of his eventual worth.

recommendations.summary: Renew Klesla on a 4-5 year deal in July 2006; 23, 16 points in 35 games, POTE 97, $0.90M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: He is the best value on the roster and plays every night. Without a new deal the top defensive pairing (Klesla + Eminger) disassembles at the same time Eminger's development still needs a partner.

recommendations.summary: Begin Richards' extension in July 2007, two years before his current deal expires, to break the 11-player 2009 cluster.
recommendations.rationale: 11 players on $37.40M expire in July 2009. Richards at $6.70M and 25 now will be 27 and more expensive by 2009; locking him at 25 with 88 POTE is cheaper than re-signing him at 27 with a proven track record.

recommendations.summary: Do not add salary this season; payroll exceeds revenue by $9.63M and profit depends on playoff revenue, not regular-season attendance at $112 tickets.
recommendations.rationale: Adding a $4M+ player before resolving Gaborik's dead money pushes the deficit past comfort. The structure is already the manual's target shape; the fix is contract timing, not more bodies.

recommendations.summary: Move Mogilny before the March 19 deadline for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: He is 90 base, $5.50M expiring, and 36. The pick-recovery mechanic applies. He is the single highest-value chip we hold.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Heatley from ATL with Tucker plus R1 before the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: ATL are a 16-point club with three elite expirers they cannot all keep. Heatley at 91 base fills the scoring gap the coach flagged. Tucker is the GM's designated chip.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Savard from ATL with Koltsov plus St. Jacques plus R3 before the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Savard at FACE 88 and $1.00M expiring is available on the same seller as Heatley. The package uses entirely different assets, so both deals can execute simultaneously.

recommendations.summary: Sign Luongo to a 5-year extension in July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: 26 years old, 91 base, $1.60M expiring. The backup is Ouellet at 81 base. Losing him to UFA would be the worst outcome of the summer.

recommendations.summary: Sign Chlup to a 5-year extension in July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: 19 years old, $2.34M expiring. He is the franchise centre and must be locked through his prime.

recommendations.summary: Sign Klesla to a 4-year extension in July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: 23 years old, $0.90M expiring. Young, cheap defenceman worth keeping.

recommendations.summary: Sign Ouellet to a 2-year deal as backup in July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: 24 years old, 81 base, $0.90M. Two years is correct for a backup once Luongo's five-year is in place.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Milan Hejduk at the March deadline as the Mogilny replacement; 91 base, 36 pts/33 GP, $2.50M expiring, age 29.
recommendations.rationale: COL hold three other expirers at combined $26.95M (Forsberg, Kariya, Selanne) and cannot retain all four. Hejduk is the cheapest to move. Fills the 94-scoring/93-playmaking hole Mogilny leaves in July.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Daniel Briere if payroll allows; FACE 86, 30 pts/32 GP, POTE 82, $3.59M expiring, age 28, the only faceoff center in the league who also produces top-six offense.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto carry no center above 76 FACE besides Sundin. Briere at 86 with 30 points closes both the draw and the scoring gap simultaneously. BUF at 34 pts with 5 expiring are moderate sellers.

recommendations.slot: faceoff specialist, third or fourth line centre
recommendations.summary: Acquire Mike Sillinger as a pure faceoff specialist if Briere is too expensive; FACE 96, $1.80M expiring, age 34, 4 pts/13 GP.
recommendations.rationale: PHX at 30 points with 9 expiring are the most motivated sellers in the league. Sillinger's 96 FACE on a $1.80M salary closes the draw gap at the lowest cost available. His 4 points in 13 games confirm he is specialist-only.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Marian Hossa as the long-term wing for the post-Mogilny era; 89 base, 26 pts/31 GP, $2.30M expiring, age 26.
recommendations.rationale: OTT carry Alfredsson at $11.40M expiring and will prioritize him. Hossa at 26 with 89 base is the cheapest elite winger in the league and outlasts Gaborik's uncertainty. OTT at 29 points with 4 expiring.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Ari Ahonen per the January 2005 standing order; 89 overall, POTE 94, $800K expiring, age 24, on a 25-point club with 8 expiring.
recommendations.rationale: The GM's standing order from 2005-01-15 is to fetch a high-90s-potential goalie from a non-contender. Ahonen at POTE 94 and CHI's 25 points fit exactly. 81 base means he develops over 1-2 seasons.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Marc Savard for 30 pts/33 GP at $1.00M expiring even though his FACE dropped to 83; still above any Toronto center except Sundin and Wallin.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 27 points with 6 expiring cannot re-sign him. His 83 FACE is below November's 87 but still closes the gap identified by the coverage phase. Best salary-to-production ratio of any target.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Jarret Stoll as a development center; FACE 94, POTE 98, CHKG 86, $700K expiring, age 23, 67 base.
recommendations.rationale: His 67 base means he cannot play tonight but the profile is exactly the manual's shape: young, elite at one thing, high potential, cheap. EDM at 34 points with 5 expiring may move him for a late pick.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Vaclav Nedorost at $1.00M expiring, age 23, POTE 94, 25 pts/33 GP; a center with legitimate scoring upside at minimal cost.
recommendations.rationale: FLA at 29 points with 4 expiring may keep or move him. At 23 with 94 potential and 25 points in 33 games, he is the best cheap young center on a losing club.

recommendations.summary: Naslund remains the highest-scoring seller at 52 pts/34 GP and 92 base but $4.40M and age 32 make him a rental only; pursue only if no younger winger is available.
recommendations.rationale: Already tracked since December 22. VAN at 36 points with 13 expiring are desperate sellers. At 32 he is one year of elite production, not two. Hejduk or Hossa are better for the trajectory.

recommendations.summary: Hemsky at 75 base, POTE 91, $1.10M expiring, age 22, is a second development target from the same club as Stoll; pair them in one package.
recommendations.rationale: 19 points in 34 games at 22 with 91 potential is a useful bottom-six winger now and a top-six candidate in two years. EDM at 34 points with 5 expiring.

recommendations.summary: Do not pursue Peter Forsberg ($9.90M) or Paul Kariya ($10.11M) despite their expiring status; adding either pushes the payroll deficit past the point where profit turns negative.
recommendations.rationale: Payroll already exceeds revenue by $9.63M. Forsberg at $9.90M or Kariya at $10.11M would push the annual cost to $99.84M+ against $80.31M revenue.

recommendations.summary: Trade Gaborik and our second-round pick to Colorado for Milan Hejduk at the March deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Saves $9.40M annually, moves payroll from $9.63M deficit to near surplus. COL are transitioning — Forsberg, Kariya, Selanne all expiring at $26.95M combined — and a 23-year-old with 98 speed plus draft capital is their rebuild profile. We get proven 91-base production for the playoff run at $2.50M. Acceptance is uncertain because $11.90M for four years is a massive commitment in a no-cap league.

recommendations.current: Mogilny ($5.50M, 1yr, 90 base, 28pts/35GP) + Koltsov ($1.10M, 1yr, POTE 94, 0pts/3GP) + St. Jacques ($800K, 1yr, POTE 94, CHKG 84) + R3 pick
recommendations.summary: Trade Mogilny, Koltsov, St. Jacques and our third-round pick to Atlanta for Martin Savard at the March deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Saves $5.40M net, closes the faceoff gap (nothing on Toronto above 76 except Sundin and Wallin). ATL at 27 points with league-lowest payroll get Mogilny as a rental they release in July, two POTE-94 prospects at low cost, and a late pick. We gain 30 points and FACE 83 from a player 8 years younger at one-fifth the salary. Koltsov and St. Jacques are not playing for us.

recommendations.summary: If Atlanta refuse the Savard package, trade Koltsov and our third-round pick to Phoenix for Martin Sillinger as a pure faceoff specialist.
recommendations.rationale: Sillinger's FACE 96 is unmatched in the league. PHX at 30 points with 9 expiring deals are the most motivated sellers. Koltsov at POTE 94 and 86 speed is a prospect they can develop; the R3 is late capital they don't need. Saves nothing on payroll versus the Savard deal but costs fewer assets. His 4pts/13GP confirms he is a specialist, not a scorer.

recommendations.summary: Goalie monitoring task is closed per GM standing order 2005-03-19; Luongo is acquired and on the roster at 95 displayed.
recommendations.rationale: The January 2005 objective was to fetch a high-90s goalie; Luongo is here at 91 base / 95 displayed. The GM ordered all goalie trade monitoring closed on 2005-03-19. The live question is now his July 2006 renewal (1 year left), not availability.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev's season rate has recovered to 0.50 at 28 games, above the 0.45 floor. The December 20th threshold breach self-corrected. Keep him on the third line.
recommendations.rationale: He went from roughly 10 points in 26 games (0.40) to 14 in 28 (0.50) on two multi-point nights. His 10.5 MPG and L3 role match his current production.

recommendations.summary: Make Gardener's scratch permanent. Zero points in 23 games at 3.6 MPG is not a development opportunity at any age.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 98 with zero points means the scouting number is describing something other than NHL production. His games should go to Spacek.

recommendations.summary: Colaiacovo stays scratched. 3 points in 25 games at 0.12 per game with zero goals is the weakest D on the roster by a wide margin.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 again with no production. The November 27th scratch recommendation holds and is now confirmed over a larger sample.

recommendations.slot: fourth line left wing or centre
recommendations.summary: Give Spacek a regular fourth-line role. At 20 he is outproducing every other young forward on a per-minute basis at 0.44 points per game.
recommendations.rationale: Four points in 9 games on 6.3 MPG beats Gardener (0.00), Colaiacovo (0.12), Spezza (0.19) and Upshall (0.23). POTE 91 with a real rate.

recommendations.summary: Spezza and Upshall are both 22 with POTE 99 and neither is getting or earning meaningful ice. The club has no centre depth behind Chlup and it is not being solved by spot minutes.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza: 5.4 MPG, 0.19 pts/g. Upshall: 6.2 MPG, 0.23 pts/g. Both scratched. This is the same collapse pattern from last season and neither has found a role at 22.

recommendations.summary: Gaborik should dress every game at 23. He is at 0.47 points per game on 22.6 MPG when he plays but has only appeared in 49% of games.
recommendations.rationale: No injuries showing. At 23 with top-six ice time available in his games played, in-and-out status wastes his best development window.

recommendations.summary: Keep Chlup on the first line permanently and do not rotate him off. 0.79 at 20.9 MPG at 19 is franchise trajectory.
recommendations.rationale: He came in at 1.00 in 1 game and has settled to 0.79 over 35 games with minutes rising from 6 to 20.9. The rate-drop is the expected correction from spot duty to a full role, not regression.

recommendations.summary: Pull Alexeev from the regular rotation. 0.44 at 28 games breaches the 0.45 floor set on November 17th.
recommendations.rationale: His rate has not moved from 0.40 (my November 20th note) to 0.44 now at 28 games. He is not developing at 10.7 MPG and those minutes belong to Stahle or another young body.

recommendations.summary: Give Stahle's minutes to Colaiacovo. Stahle is at 0.24 in 18 games with minutes rising from 6 to 12.9; Colaiacovo is 0.12 in 25 games.
recommendations.rationale: Stahle at 21 is the only young D trending up. Colaiacovo at 0.12 with zero goals in 25 games is below replacement at 12.6 MPG.

recommendations.summary: Gaborik at 0.47 in 17 games at 22.6 MPG justifies top-six minutes. Let him keep building.
recommendations.rationale: He missed the first save window entirely and came in at 0.47 immediately. At 23 that rate on those minutes is exactly what we need from him.

recommendations.summary: Monitor Jackman closely. At 0.62 pts/g he is 0.07 above the 0.55 sell trigger and the trend is down.
recommendations.rationale: Rate has fallen from 1.00 in the opener to 0.62 over 35 games. My November 13th note set 0.55 as the re-sell trigger. If he crosses it before the deadline he goes back on the sell list.

recommendations.summary: McCabe goes back on the sell list. 0.30 over 10 games is well below the 0.60 threshold from March.
recommendations.rationale: My March 30th note said if his final rate holds below 0.60 he returns to the sell list. At 0.30 in 10 games, 30 years old, 16.4 MPG, the threshold is met.

recommendations.summary: The room is healthy; no morale-driven lineup change needed.
recommendations.rationale: Almost every dressed player is at 97 and climbing on the winning streak. Richards (87, 12.1 MPG) and Lundmark (87, 7.4 MPG) are under their minute band but both are recovering on team results; the GM's development priorities explain the gap. No player is in a morale hole that a line move fixes.

recommendations.summary: Add Nash to K2; he has 82 checking and is on neither penalty-kill unit.
recommendations.rationale: K2 checking mean is 74 with no one above Sundin's 76. Nash at 82 is the best free checker. His L2 linemates are untouched so chemistry cost is zero.

recommendations.summary: Scratch Alexeev against CGY. 0.40 pts/g at 26 games is below the 0.45 floor from November 17th.
recommendations.rationale: His rate has not recovered in the eight games since the floor was set. Against a 3-11-1 opponent this is the night to pull him without cost.

recommendations.summary: L4 faceoff mean of 54 is a roster gap, not a lineup problem. Koltsov is the least-bad option available.
recommendations.rationale: Wallin at 88 draws and 78 OVR is the only replacement and he's a downgrade everywhere else. The fix is a draft or trade, not a line move.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes for CGY. Our depth and D-pair quality mismatch them across all four lines and three pairs.
recommendations.rationale: CGY tops out at Iginla 92 with supporting cast of 79 and 83. Their blue line is 79/74/73/71/71/68. We are 87+ on every forward line and 82+ on every D pair. Their PP is 11.8%. No structural adjustment is needed.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo if his fatigue icon is clear. Ouellet covers if tired.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 95 against a 2.30-goal offence with 11.8% PP is the obvious read. Standing order: check fatigue icon before confirming.

recommendations.summary: Klesla sell window remains open at deadline: 87 OVR, expiring $0.90M, rate 0.46 pts/g over 35 games.
recommendations.rationale: Rate improved from 0.40 to 0.46 but is still well below the 0.55 that closes the window. A buyer sees the grade and salary, not the underlying production decline.

recommendations.summary: Jackman's rate has dropped to 0.63 pts/g at 35 games, approaching the 0.55 sell trigger. Monitor weekly; sell if he crosses before the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Rate trajectory: 0.88 at 16 games, 0.68 at 25, 0.63 now. At this pace he hits the trigger around game 45. Bargain contract ($0.70M x 2) makes him a keep if the rate stabilizes.

recommendations.summary: McCabe at 0.30 pts/g in 10 games with $3.00M x 3 remaining is dead weight. Explore summer trade or buyout.
recommendations.rationale: 3 points in 10 games at 16.4 MPG for a 30-year-old at 84 OVR. Clearly depth, not a top-four option. The salary and term are the problem, not the grade.

recommendations.summary: St. Jacques at 66 OVR and 0 points in 15 games (expiring) should be cut.
recommendations.rationale: Zero production, lowest grade on the roster, no role. No path to contributing at this level.

recommendations.summary: Colaiacovo remains untradeable at 76 OVR, 0.12 pts/g, $1.40M x 3. Flag for end-of-season decision.
recommendations.rationale: 3 assists in 25 games with zero goals confirms the development has stalled. Not dressed. The contract makes him nearly impossible to move; likely a buyout candidate.

recommendations.summary: Trade Gaborik at the March 2006 deadline before his game count erodes his value further; $11.90M/year through July 2010 buys nothing at 8 pts in 17 GP as a scratch.
recommendations.rationale: He is the largest contract on the roster at 13.2% of payroll, generating zero value. Mid-contract renegotiation is impossible. Moving him now recovers assets and frees the money for Luongo and Chlup renewals in July 2006.

recommendations.summary: Renew Luongo on a 5-year deal in July 2006; at 91 base and $1.60M this is the cheapest he will ever be.
recommendations.rationale: He is 26 with POTE 97, the only goalie above 85 base on the roster besides himself. Ouellet behind him is 81 base. Losing Luongo without compensation (1 year left) would be the single worst contract outcome available this summer.

recommendations.summary: Renew Chlup on a 5-6 year deal in July 2006; at 19 with POTE 95 and 27 pts in 34 GP, his current $2.34M is well below market.
recommendations.rationale: His production this season (27 points, top-nine scoring) means his next contract will be a major raise. Locking him now at 19 prevents him from hitting the market as a 20-year-old restricted free agent with a 25-point season on tape.

recommendations.summary: Extend Richards in July 2007 (when 2 years remain) to break the 11-player 2009 cluster; do not let 11 contracts worth $37.40M all expire simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: He is 25 with POTE 88 and $6.70M on a deal to 2009. His production has declined three straight seasons (0.53 this year), so his next contract may actually be cheaper than his current one. Extending early caps the exposure and splits the cluster.

recommendations.summary: Trade Mogilny at the March 2006 deadline for a draft pick using the over-80 pick-recovery mechanic; at 36 and expiring, he is a rental.
recommendations.rationale: He is 89 displayed, 90 base, $5.50M, 1 year left, 36 years old. The coach projects a step down next season regardless. Recovering a pick for a player who walks for nothing in July is the cleanest value play on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Trade Mogilny at the March deadline to a non-contender for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic; saves $5.50M and recovers a pick from a player who walks in July otherwise.
recommendations.rationale: 90 base, expiring, 36 years old. The pick-recovery mechanic converts him into a pick. Send to a non-contender per the March 4 standing order.

recommendations.summary: Offer Tucker plus our first-round pick to Atlanta for Heatley (91 base, 22 years old); ATL at 27 pts with three expirers and $40.34M payroll cannot keep him.
recommendations.rationale: Heatley is a keeper at 22 and 91 base. The draft-capital constraint from 2005 is reset. Tucker is the GM's designated chip from the March 2005 order.

recommendations.summary: Offer Koltsov plus St. Jacques plus our third-round pick to Atlanta for Savard (FACE 88, 26 pts/30 GP, $1.00M expiring) to fill the faceoff centre gap.
recommendations.rationale: Savard supersedes Sillinger as the faceoff target. Same seller (ATL, 27 pts) and entirely different assets from the Heatley package. ATL may only do one deal; Heatley takes priority if forced.

recommendations.summary: Do not pursue Bertuzzi at the deadline if the Heatley and Savard deals land; 30 years old, $2.60M, pure rental, and the R2 is better kept.
recommendations.rationale: The manual says prefer young players with potential over rentals. Bertuzzi at 30 with expiring $2.60M is exactly the rental we should avoid spending a second-rounder on. Revisit only if both ATL deals collapse.

recommendations.summary: Sign Luongo to a five-year extension in July 2006 before he walks; 91 base, $1.60M, one year remaining.
recommendations.rationale: Without a new deal he becomes a UFA and we are left with Ouellet at 81 base as the only goalie. Stars get 5-6 years per the manual.

recommendations.summary: Sign Chlup to a five-year extension in July 2006; 19 years old, 82 base, $2.34M.
recommendations.rationale: Elite prospect at 19. Lock him on star-length terms now before he prices up.

recommendations.summary: Sign Klesla to a four-year extension in July 2006; 23 years old, 78 base, $0.90M.
recommendations.rationale: Developing defenceman at a reasonable salary. Four years avoids a renewal in 2009 when the cluster hits.

recommendations.summary: Sign Ouellet to a two-year deal as backup goalie in July 2006; 24 years old, 81 base, $0.90M.
recommendations.rationale: Cheaper and younger than any free-agent alternative. Two years matches the manual's guidance for role players.

recommendations.summary: Take no action before late February; negotiations open then per the January 15 standing order. Sellers remain sellers.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 27 points and VAN at 34 are not going to panic-sell in December. There is no cost to waiting 60 more days.

recommendations.summary: Primary deadline target: 94 base, 44pts/33GP, $2.60M expiring, 87 CHKG. Package Spezza + Alexeev + R2 to VAN.
recommendations.rationale: VAN at 34 points with 13 expiring deals and $46.36M payroll is the most motivated seller in the league. Bertuzzi fills the wing scoring gap AND brings 87 CHKG/83 TOUG checking that Toronto lacks on the top lines.

recommendations.summary: Primary checking fix: 94 CHKG, 92 TOUG, 93 SPEE, 25pts/34GP, $0.60M expiring. Package Upshall + R3 to CAR.
recommendations.rationale: Kurka is the only lined-forward checking solution in the league at a below-slot salary. He scores at 0.74 pts/g while checking at 94. CAR at 40 points with 14 expiring deals cannot keep a 23-year-old rental.

recommendations.summary: If ATL accepts: 91 base, 36pts/32GP, 97 SHPW, 22 years old, POTE 86, $1.10M. Package Tucker + R1.
recommendations.rationale: Heatley is 22 with a 91 base and 97 shot power at $1.10M. ATL at 27 points with league-lowest payroll cannot re-sign him. Unlike a rental, he carries the first line for a decade post-Sundin.

recommendations.summary: Defensive depth insurance: 89 base, 92 CHKG, 91 TOUG, $2.30M, 1 year left. Requires a new package (Spacek or D depth + R1).
recommendations.rationale: The Coach flagged that no quality first-pair replacement exists if Jackman or Klesla goes down. Jovanovski is the only blueliner above 90 on both CHKG and TOUG in the league. VAN has 13 expiring and will move him.

recommendations.summary: Centre depth at $0.40M: 82 base, FACE 80, CHKG 81, 23pts/34GP, 25 years old, POTE 87. Package Koltsov + R3 to CAR.
recommendations.rationale: Vasicek is the cheapest quality centre available and provides both faceoff help and 23 points from the second line. CAR's 14 expiring deals force them to move him. Alternative to Savard from ATL.

recommendations.summary: Best producer on any seller: 92 base, 50pts/33GP, $4.40M, 1 year left. Secondary VAN target after Bertuzzi.
recommendations.rationale: Naslund outscored everyone on this list except Kovalchuk and Heatley (both 22-year-olds at $1.10M). At $4.40M and 1 year left, VAN will eventually move him but may want more than a single package. Approach after Bertuzzi.

recommendations.summary: Faceoff specialist: 79 base, FACE 89, 29pts/32GP, $1.00M expiring. Package Koltsov + R3 to ATL.
recommendations.rationale: Savard gives a stronger faceoff draw (89 FACE) than Wallin's 88, with 29 points at 32 games. Same ATL logic as Heatley. Choose Savard OR Vasicek, not both.

recommendations.summary: Bertuzzi backup: 85 base, 86 CHKG, 18pts/34GP, $1.50M expiring. PHX at 28 points with 9 expiring will sell.
recommendations.rationale: If VAN rejects the Bertuzzi package, Konowalchuk is the second-best checking winger on a motivated seller. PHX at $55.41M with 9 expiring and 28 points has no reason to keep a 29-year-old rental.

recommendations.summary: Development option: 79 base, 92 CHKG, 91 TOUG, POTE 95, $1.10M expiring. Not a March plug — summer or late-deadline target.
recommendations.rationale: Hartnell at 23 with POTE 95 is the highest-ceiling toughness option, but 10 points in 26 games means he does not help tonight. Better as a depth piece acquired alongside another package or in July.

recommendations.summary: Secondary defensive depth: 80 base, 93 CHKG, 89 TOUG, $1.70M expiring. WSH at 23 points with 5 expiring. Lower priority than Jovanovski.
recommendations.rationale: Witt offers 93 CHKG at $1.70M but at 30 years old his ceiling is set. He is the fallback if Jovanovski is unavailable. WSH at 23 points have no retention incentive.

recommendations.summary: Offer Spezza, Alexeev, and our 2nd-round pick to Vancouver for Bertuzzi at the March deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Bertuzzi at 94 base with 87 CHKG fills wing scoring and checking simultaneously. Spezza (5pts/26GP) is a Coach-flagged write-off and Alexeev (12pts/27GP, below the 0.45 threshold) is surplus. VAN at 34 points with 13 expiring deals and $46.36M payroll is the most motivated seller in the league. Payroll net +$0.10M.

recommendations.summary: Offer Tucker and our 1st-round pick to Atlanta for Heatley at the March deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Heatley at 22 with 98 SPEE and 97 SHPW is the best long-term right wing available. ATL at 27 points, $40.34M league-lowest payroll, six expirers, cannot re-sign him. Tucker (30, 0 GP, $1.30M expiring, CHKG 92) provides PK depth for their final 30 games. Uses different assets than the Bertuzzi package; both can close simultaneously. Payroll net -$0.20M.

recommendations.summary: If neither deal lands, hold the roster intact through the March deadline and play the playoffs with what we have.
recommendations.rationale: At 53 points first in the East with Sundin (26pts), Mogilny (28pts), and Chlup (27pts), the roster is adequate. Roberts at 86 CHKG narrows the checking gap if healthy. No deadline move is better than a forced one when you lead your conference.

recommendations.summary: Close the goalie trade window task — Luongo was acquired during the January–February 2005 window, and the GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is on our roster at 95 overall with 1 year left at $1.60M. DiPietro at 86 and expiring on NYI has no roster fit given two 90+ goalies already present. The monitoring period ended February 2005.

recommendations.summary: Dress Gaborik on the fourth line in place of Upshall.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik at 0.47 pts/g in 17 games on 22.6 MPG outproduces Upshall's 0.24 pts/g in 25 games on 6.0 MPG by a factor of two. The minutes Upshall gets (6 per game) aren't developing him either.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev stays in the lineup one more week despite sitting at 0.44 pts/g.
recommendations.rationale: He is at 12 points in 27 games, one point above the 0.45 floor. If he goes another game without a point the floor triggers and the scratch recommendation renews.

recommendations.summary: Either dress Eminger every night at top-pair minutes or decide he is a trade candidate, not both.
recommendations.rationale: 8 games at 19.6 MPG and 0.50 pts/g is inconsistent deployment. At 22 with POTE 99 the development argument favours playing him, but the March sell window was set on a declining full-season rate that no longer matches this sample.

recommendations.summary: Flag Gaborik's underproduction: 0.47 pts/g at 22.6 MPG at age 23 mirrors the Afinogenov/Richards pattern. Monitor through January; if under 0.50 at 30 games, system-fit review applies.
recommendations.rationale: He is getting top-six minutes and producing a third-line rate. At 23 the expected direction is up, not sideways. 17 games is enough to raise a flag but not enough to act.

recommendations.summary: Jackman's rate has fallen from 0.68 to 0.64 over nine games. My sell trigger is 0.55 and he is losing 0.01 per three games. A deadline call is coming within two weeks.
recommendations.rationale: The trend from December 4th is unambiguous decline. At 24 and $0.70M with two years left, his card value is at or near peak right now. The GM should be thinking about what return he wants.

recommendations.summary: Klesla back at 0.45 over 34 games. The sell window at 87 OVR and $0.90M expiring remains wide. Move before the rate bleeds again.
recommendations.rationale: His rate recovered from 0.29 in late November to 0.45 now, but the pattern is oscillating downward across the season. Each recovery peak is lower than the last.

recommendations.summary: Chlup's 0.79 at 21.2 MPG at 19 is not a decline. His role tripled and production held. No change.
recommendations.rationale: The 1.00 at 1 game is noise. The real trend is 21.2 MPG at 0.79, which is growth for a 19-year-old centring the first line.

recommendations.summary: Richards at 0.58 over 34 games on 11.8 MPG is no longer a top-six centre by output. His role should be reduced permanently this season.
recommendations.rationale: Three consecutive seasons of decline (1.08, 0.71, 0.58) at 25 confirms this is structural. He is costing ice time the team gets no return on.

recommendations.summary: No ice-time changes warranted. The room is at 95+ and trending up.
recommendations.rationale: Richards at 84 is the only player still in the morale penalty zone; he has recovered from 78 without intervention and the winning is working. Luongo at 82 has a full workload (16 starts) so his dip is results-based, not minutes-based.

recommendations.summary: Replace Spacek on L4 with Tucker.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker carries checking 89 and toughness 85; Spacek carries 57 and 50. L4's checking mean jumps from 65 to 76. The GM called Tucker our checking guy in January and he has not dressed since.

recommendations.summary: Put Tucker on the second penalty kill in place of Richards.
recommendations.rationale: K2's checking mean is 74; Richards at 78 is the weakest of the four. Tucker at 89 raises it. Richards keeps P1 and L3 so his minutes do not collapse.

recommendations.summary: No changes. Our first line and first D pair already see Kovalchuk/Heatley via auto-pairing, and the rest of their roster is no deeper than 82.
recommendations.rationale: Kovalchuk 92 and Heatley 91 are their only elite weapons and they share a line. Our first line (Sundin/Chistov/Mogilny) auto-pairs with Klesla/Jackman, which is the correct response. Their PP is 10/122 (8.2%), their D tops out at 75, and we are 2-0-0 in the series outscoring them 10-5. Nothing to fix.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo. 95 OVR against a 2.80-goal-per-game offence with a 8.2% power play.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 95 with 97 glove ratings is more than enough for this opponent. No fatigue flag visible in the brief. ATL's offence has no answer for him tonight.

recommendations.summary: Trade Klesla before the deadline; his 87 OVR and hot streak make this the peak sell window at $0.90M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Rate climbed from 0.40 to 0.44 over last 4 games (3 points). A buyer sees the grade and the streak; we see 0.44 on the season behind Jackman.

recommendations.summary: Jackman stays — 0.65 pts/g at 34 games is still above the 0.55 sell trigger, and $0.70M x 2 at age 24 is cheap.
recommendations.rationale: Bleeding slowly from 0.68 on Dec 4th. Reassess if he crosses 0.55.

recommendations.proposed: Tucker and Fischer on penalty kill
recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker (83 CHKG) and Fischer (82 CHKG) for PK duty to restore two checking-above-80 units with Roberts out.
recommendations.rationale: The coach flags he cannot build two PK units at 78+ checking. Tucker and Fischer are rostered at 83 and 82 respectively and currently unlined. Adding them to K1 alongside Jackman (87) and McCabe (86) closes the immediate gap without a trade.

recommendations.proposed: Gaborik on top-six wing at 16 MPG max
recommendations.summary: Put Gaborik back in the lineup on the top-six wing with minutes capped at 16 per the coach's instruction.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik at 92 scoring, 92 playmaking, 98 speed is not lined. Every scratched game erodes his $11.90M trade value per the December 11 finding. The coach's 16-MPG cap addresses the efficiency concern while restoring production.

recommendations.summary: Scratch Spezza (5 pts/26 GP, 5.4 MPG) or raise to 10+ MPG; the current arrangement develops nobody per the coach.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza at 5 points in 26 games on 5.4 MPG is replacement-level ice time. The coach's flag is correct. Either commit to developing him with real minutes or free the roster spot for someone else on the night.

recommendations.summary: Give Spacek 12+ MPG or stop dressing him; morale 76 is the lowest on the roster and 6 games in 32 helps nobody.
recommendations.rationale: Coach flags Spacek's morale at 76, the roster floor, with only 6 appearances from 32 games. The current arrangement is a morale liability with no development benefit.

recommendations.summary: No new toughness target needed; the GM closed this line of inquiry in December and base-grade toughness, while structurally absent, is masked by form on most days.
recommendations.rationale: Base TOUG tops out at 75 (Jackman). Displayed grades have shown 11 players at 80+ on good form days (Dec 4 finding). The GM's position stands; reopening it would contradict his decision and I have no evidence the form-based coverage has failed.

recommendations.summary: Trade Gaborik before the March deadline; his $11.90M scratched salary is $47.60M of dead money and his value erodes every game he sits.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik is at 8 points in 17 GP as a scratch at $11.90M/year through 2010. Mid-contract renegotiation is impossible. At 23 with POTE 90 he still has market value, but it drops with every scratched game. Moving him frees 13.2% of payroll.

recommendations.summary: Trade Mogilny at the March deadline for a draft pick using the over-80 expiring mechanic; $5.50M expiring at 90 base.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny is 36 with 26 points in 33 GP and an expiring $5.50M deal. At 90 base he qualifies for the pick-recovery mechanic. He is the highest-value chip on the roster for recovering draft capital after the Heatley trade commits the R1.

recommendations.summary: Renew Luongo on a 5-6 year deal in July 2006; without him the backup is Ouellet at 81 base.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is 91 base, POTE 97, $1.60M, 1 year left. His contract dropped to 1 year as of December 2005. If he walks, the backup behind whoever is starter is Ouellet (81 base) or Tellqvist (10 GP this year). He is the franchise goalie and the renewal is existential.

recommendations.summary: Renew Chlup on a 5-6 year deal in July 2006 at age 19; he is the franchise centre at 26 points in 33 GP with POTE 95.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup is 19, 26 points in 33 GP, POTE 95, on a 1-year $2.34M deal. He and Luongo expire the same summer. Lock him before the market finds him at 20 with a full season of top-six production.

recommendations.summary: Begin breaking the 2009 cluster by extending Richards, Chistov, and Nash in July 2007, two years before their deals expire.
recommendations.rationale: Eleven players on 4-year deals worth $37.40M all expire July 2009. Extending three of them in 2007 splits the renewal into two manageable summers instead of one that costs the club its core.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla in July 2006 as the bridge across the Mogilny/Sundin scoring void; he closes the gap without requiring a 21-year-old to take a 0.20 pts/g jump.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny (36), Sundin (34), and Roberts (39) carry the veteran production and no player under 30 is positioned to absorb it. Iginla at 27 with 93 base and 140 points in 73 games is the only available player who fills the top-six RW role without a development bet. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring deals cannot retain him.

recommendations.proposed: draft pick via over-80 expiring mechanic
recommendations.summary: Move Mogilny by March 19 for a draft pick using the over-80 expiring mechanic; he is 36, $5.50M, 90 base, expiring, and the only pick-recovery asset on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: If he is not traded he walks in July for nothing. He is 89 days from eligibility and 89 days from the deadline; execute late February or early March per the GM's timing preference.

recommendations.summary: Trade Tucker plus first-round pick to Atlanta for Heatley at the deadline; he addresses the top-six scoring gap the Coach flags.
recommendations.rationale: Atlanta at 20 points with three elite expirers cannot re-sign any of them. Heatley at 91 base is the best available scorer. Tucker is expiring salary that funds the deal.

recommendations.summary: Trade Koltsov plus St. Jacques plus R3 to Atlanta for Savard; he fills the faceoff and centre-depth gap simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Savard's FACE 88 and 26 points in 30 games at $1.00M expiring on a 20-point team with triple expiring makes ATL a forced seller. The package uses different assets from the Heatley deal so both can execute.

recommendations.summary: Trade Spezza at the deadline for a late-round pick or release him in July; he is 5 points in 26 games on 5.4 MPG at $1.00M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach confirms he is replacement-level. His trade value is low but a fifth-rounder is realistic via the over-80 mechanic if his overall is above 80, otherwise release.

recommendations.summary: Renew Luongo on a 5-year deal in July 2006; he is 26, 91 base, $1.60M, one year left, and the undisputed starter.
recommendations.rationale: Without an extension he walks and the backup is Ouellet at 81 base. This is the single highest-priority renewal in the July 2006 class.

recommendations.summary: Renew Chlup on a 5-year deal in July 2006; he is 19, 82 base, $2.34M, and the franchise centre.
recommendations.rationale: At 19 with 82 base and rising, locking him long-term is the foundation of the next three seasons.

recommendations.summary: Renew Klesla on a 4-year deal in July 2006; he is 23, 78 base, $0.90M, and a young top-pairing defenceman.
recommendations.rationale: At 23 and $0.90M, four years locks a cheap young D who anchors the blue line alongside Eminger and McCabe.

recommendations.summary: Renew Ouellet on a 2-year deal at $0.90M as backup to Luongo; he is 24, 81 base.
recommendations.rationale: The GM needs a capable backup for playoffs without burning Ouellet as the only option if Luongo is hurt. Two years is the right term for a backup at 24.

recommendations.summary: Do not open trade negotiations before late February; the deadline is 89 days away and sellers remain sellers.
recommendations.rationale: Per the GM's standing order of 2005-01-15, negotiations should not open until late February. The plan is set; execution happens when sellers panic.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Bertuzzi from VAN for Spezza + Alexeev + R2; he pairs with Heatley as a 94-base scorer on a desperate seller.
recommendations.rationale: VAN at 33 points with 13 expiring and $46.36M league-lowest payroll must sell. They get two players under 25 with POTE 99 and 94 plus a second-round pick, and shed $2.60M of expiring salary. Net payroll change for Toronto is -$0.40M. Acceptance is uncertain but VAN's motivation is the highest of any club.

recommendations.proposed: Vandermeer (PHI, 89 base, CHKG 90, TOUG 92, POTE 92, 25, $0.40M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Acquire Vandermeer from PHI for Upshall + R2; he fills the checking-defence void with zero current Torontonian above 90 on both CHKG and TOUG.
recommendations.rationale: PHI at 34 points with 9 expiring deals may sell at the deadline, but they are on the playoff bubble which makes them a less motivated seller than VAN. Upshall (22, POTE 99, CHKG 87) gives them a young body at $1.50M. Net payroll saving is $1.10M. If Bertuzzi goes through first, this is blocked on the R2; Upshall alone might work as PHI gets a player cheaper than what they'd pay in the trade market.

recommendations.proposed: A draft pick (second or third round)
recommendations.summary: Trade Mogilny straight up for a draft pick at the March deadline to recover draft capital lost in the Heatley deal.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny at 90 base qualifies for the over-80 pick-recovery mechanic. He is 36, expiring, $5.50M, and produces 26 points in 33 games. A contender pays a late-round pick for him; any club that needs a veteran goal-scorer for a playoff push says yes. This is the independent fallback: it works whether or not Bertuzzi or Vandermeer land.

recommendations.summary: Owed item #2 (Luongo/DiPietro goalie trade monitoring) is closed by the GM's own 2005-03-19 order; Luongo is on our roster at 95 overall and the only live question is his July 2006 renewal.
recommendations.rationale: The task was to monitor Luongo's availability from another club and DiPietro's development as a trade target. Luongo is now our own starter at 95 overall, 15 GP, $1.60M with 1 year left. The GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19. Nothing further to deliver.

recommendations.summary: Going forward, give Gaborik the regular RW spot over Upshall. He's at 0.47 pts/g vs Upshall's 0.21 and was getting 22.6 MPG before being scratched.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik outproduces Upshall by more than double (0.47 vs 0.21) and was given top-6 minutes when in the lineup. The in-and-out pattern isn't developing him. Tonight against STL keep the all-out approach, but after tonight Gaborik should be in consistently.

recommendations.summary: Commit to Spacek as the second centre or stop dressing him. Seven games at 20 years old with POTE 91 and 0.43 pts/g in a sample that small will become the Spezza pattern if left unresolved.
recommendations.rationale: Spacek is at morale 82 on 5.0 MPG in 7 games. The young-forward-minutes-collapse pattern (Spezza, Upshall) starts with sporadic dressing and no committed role. Decide which side of the line he's on before the pattern locks in.

recommendations.summary: Chlup, Nash, Chistov and Klesla are getting every game and earning it. No development concern for this group.
recommendations.rationale: All four at 33/33 GP with 15-26 MPG and strong production (26, 20, 24, 14 points respectively). They are the team.

recommendations.summary: Gardener, Colaiacovo, Eminger, Stahle and Spezza stay scratched. Their production does not earn a roster spot.
recommendations.rationale: Gardener 0 pts in 23 GP, Colaiacovo 0.12, Eminger 0.29, Stahle 0.22, Spezza 0.19. None are close to justifying ice over the players currently in the lineup.

recommendations.summary: Stop dressing Alexeev as a regular; his 0.40 rate at 26 games is below the 0.45 threshold set November 17th and he is not trending up at 11.1 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: My November 17th note set a reassessment at 25 games with a 0.45 floor. He is at 26 games and 0.40. The Chistov comparison (0.69 at 20.7 MPG) shows the gap is role, not potential.

recommendations.summary: Flag Richards for an offseason system-fit review; 0.53 over 33 games is the third consecutive season of decline and he should not be pencilled top-six without that review.
recommendations.rationale: 1.08, 0.71, 0.53 across three seasons at ages 23, 24, 25. Minutes flat at 12 MPG. The pattern matches Afinogenov's collapse. Offseason fix, not a line change.

recommendations.summary: Flag Afinogenov for the same offseason system-fit review as Richards; 0.62 over 33 at 18 MPG continues the 1.17→0.73→0.62 slide.
recommendations.rationale: Third consecutive year of rate decline at age 26. Same pattern as Richards: production falling while ice time holds. Neither is injured. The system is the variable.

recommendations.summary: Accept Spezza's season is a write-off (0.19 over 26 on 5.4 MPG) and make next camp's roster spot the only development decision that matters for him.
recommendations.rationale: Already flagged in the March minutes-collapse note. No change since. POTE 99 with no games is a waste that only camp can fix.

recommendations.summary: No change for Chlup or Chistov; both are on the right trajectory and need more of the game, not different roles.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup 0.78 over 33 at 21.2 MPG at 19, close to last year's 0.88. Chistov 0.69 over 33 at 20.7 MPG at 22. Both belong where they are.

recommendations.summary: Mogilny is at 0.81 over 33 at 36 years old; enjoy it now but plan for a step down next season in any roster construction.
recommendations.rationale: 0.81 pts/g at 23.1 MPG at age 36 is not a repeatable number. Sundin at 34 and 0.75 has a similar two-year window. The top-six needs a succession plan by next camp.

recommendations.summary: Give the third line two or three more minutes a night to lift Richards off 84 without rebuilding the line.
recommendations.rationale: Richards is at 84, the lowest of the regulars, on 11.9 minutes in 33 games with 17 points; every other regular is 90 or better, so ice time is the lever and the smaller tool is more minutes, not a shift up the card.

recommendations.summary: No other morale-driven change: the room is healthy and the low men are on development minutes.
recommendations.rationale: Upshall, Spezza, Gardener, Spacek and Brendl sit at 81-82 on 3.6-5.8 minutes, one point off each grade, which is the development rotation's cost; Klesla and Jackman are over their band at 26.0 and 25.3 minutes and sitting at 97.

recommendations.summary: Reinstate Wallin to center L4 tonight against STL.
recommendations.rationale: L4 faceoff mean is 53, the worst unit stat on the board. Wallin is at 88 faceoffs and is a healthy scratch. STL at 20-6 qualifies for the maximize-quality principle — this is not a night to develop depth centres at the cost of zone time.

recommendations.summary: Keep K2 as-is; monitor whether it is getting too much of the kill.
recommendations.rationale: K2 checking mean is 74, acceptable for a second unit. Moving Sundin or Richards off it would require bench pieces below the current level. The risk is opportunity cost, not quality, and I cannot see the K1/K2 minute split to act on it.

recommendations.summary: P1 stays. Scoring 90, playmaking 88, speed 94 — the best unit on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: No weakness to address. This unit has every role covered: shooter, distributor, puck-mover, and two skaters at 99 speed.

recommendations.summary: If Jackman or Klesla goes down, we have no quality first-pair replacement.
recommendations.rationale: Colaiacovo is 0.14 pts/g over 22 games. Hainsey is a depth option with no offensive production. The GM should be aware this is a single-point-of-failure situation heading into the second half.

recommendations.summary: L2 stays. Checking mean 75, scoring 83 — a capable 1C group.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup's faceoff 80 is the best available after Sundin and Wallin, and he is centering the line that pairs with Kaberle. No argument for breaking this unit.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo. 95 OVR against a 2.60-goal-per-game offence, no fatigue icon showing.
recommendations.rationale: Johnson is 82 in their net. A 13-point goaltending gap against a low-event opponent is the kind of edge that wins 2-1 games, which is how they win. No tired flag on Luongo in today's readings.

recommendations.summary: Keep all four lines as they are. The auto-pairing gives us Sekeras (73), Junker/Khavanov (74/77), and Salvador/Timander (71/70) against our top three lines.
recommendations.rationale: STL's bottom two forward lines read 69-74 OVR and their power play converts at 11.6%. The game will be an even-strength grind where our top three lines each face a defense pair below 78. No structural adjustment improves that.

recommendations.summary: Klesla is the primary deadline sell: 87 OVR, $0.90M expiring, 0.42 pts/g. His rate has improved to 0.42 from 0.40, making his card more sellable now than last week.
recommendations.rationale: From 0.30 floor on Nov 13, through 0.29 on Nov 26, to 0.35 on Nov 30, 0.40 on Dec 15, now 0.42. The recovery makes him more attractive to a buyer while the grade and cheap expiring deal hold. Move before regression resumes.

recommendations.summary: Jackman at 0.67 pts/g over 33 games is above my 0.55 sell trigger. Keep monitoring monthly; if he crosses 0.55 in January he goes back on the sell list.
recommendations.rationale: Rate trajectory: 0.88 (16 GP) to 0.68 (25 GP) to 0.67 (33 GP). The decline is flattening. At $0.70M x 2 he is cheap enough to ride unless the rate falls off sharply.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker on L4 to add the only 80+ checker the coach is not using; CHKG 83 versus Gardener's 0 points in 22 games.
recommendations.rationale: Checking coverage drops to 5 if Tucker sits. The coach already proposed this on Dec 17. Tucker at 30 and $1.30M is expiring but his 83 CHKG and 70 TOUG are the best available without an acquisition.

recommendations.summary: Dress Gaborik to add SPEE 98 and POTE 92 to the top six; every scratched game erodes his $11.90M value.
recommendations.rationale: At 23 with 98 speed he is the fastest player in the league and currently not lined. The coach flagged this on Dec 17. His production (8 pts/17 GP) is depressed by the scratch itself.

recommendations.summary: Pull Sundin off K2; his 94 clutch and 92 scoring are wasted on PK shifts.
recommendations.rationale: The coach flagged this Dec 17. Sundin at 34 should spend those minutes on the ice at even strength or power play where his hands matter, not killing.

recommendations.summary: Sillinger (PHX, FACE 96, 87 overall, $1.20M expiring) remains the fix for the faceoff thinness; package is Koltsov + St. Jacques + R3.
recommendations.rationale: Only Sundin (90) and Wallin (83, not lined) sit at 80+ on base FACE. PHX at 24 points with 9 expiring deals will dump him. The December target stands unchanged.

recommendations.summary: No acquisition needed for toughness despite the base-grade void; displayed grades clear 80 on normal days and spending assets here steals from scoring depth.
recommendations.rationale: The Dec 4 finding confirmed 11 players at 80+ displayed TOUG. The base-grade gap is real for long-term construction but not an urgent fix at the deadline when the team is 21-7-0 and competing. Spend Tucker on Heatley or faceoffs, not on an enforcer.

recommendations.summary: Three of the six top scorers (Mogilny 36, Roberts 39, Sundin 34) will be 37, 40, 35 by next season and two are expiring; the July 2006 renewal list must protect Chlup, Klesla, and Ouellet.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny and Roberts are both expiring and both over 35. When they leave, scoring drops from 11 players at 80+ to 7 and checking from 6 to 4. The Dec 17 renewal priority already flags this.

recommendations.summary: Move Gaborik at the February/March 2006 deadline before his game count drops his return further.
recommendations.rationale: $11.90M/year through July 2010 at 13.2% of payroll with 8 pts/17 GP scratched. POTE 90 means he is still tradeable at 23, but his value is a decaying asset. After March, 4 years and $47.60M of dead money remains and mid-contract renegotiation is impossible.

recommendations.summary: Lock Luongo on a five-year deal in July 2006; he has one year left at $1.60M and POTE 97.
recommendations.rationale: He is 26, entering his prime, and the backup is Ouellet at 81 base. Losing him to UFA with no compensation is the worst financial outcome available. A five-year deal at 26 buys his entire prime window.

recommendations.proposed: Early extensions in July 2007 to break the 2009 renewal cluster
recommendations.summary: Begin extending Richards, Chistov, and Nash in July 2007 to dismantle the $37.40M/11-player renewal cliff hitting simultaneously in July 2009.
recommendations.rationale: Eleven players on four-year deals expire the same summer. Extending the three highest-POTE members (Richards 88, Chistov 95, Nash 95) two years early removes their contracts from the cluster and resets their clocks to 2012.

recommendations.proposed: First-round pick plus high-potential young player
recommendations.summary: Move Mogilny at the March deadline via the over-80 pick-recovery mechanic; open negotiations late February.
recommendations.rationale: 90 base, $5.50M, 36 years old, expiring. The highest-value chip on the roster. Every contender needing right-wing depth is a buyer.

recommendations.proposed: Atlanta for Heatley (Tucker + R1), or Vancouver for Bertuzzi (Tucker + R2)
recommendations.summary: Move Tucker at the deadline for Heatley or Bertuzzi; do not renew a 30-year-old expiring checker.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker at 30, $1.30M expiring, is worth more as a package piece than as a fourth-line checker. The Heatley deal (91 base) and Bertuzzi (94 base, 1.25 pts/g) both use Tucker as the lead asset.

recommendations.summary: Renew Chlup on 5 years in July 2006. He is the franchise centre at 19.
recommendations.rationale: 82 base, $2.34M, 19 years old, expiring. A 5-year deal locks him through age 24 at the start of his prime. Stars get 5-6 years per the manual.

recommendations.summary: Renew Luongo on 5 years in July 2006. He is the number one and the backup situation depends on him staying.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base, $1.60M, 26 years old, 1 year left. Without him the backup is Ouellet at 81. Priority one on the renewal list.

recommendations.summary: Renew Ouellet on 2 years as the backup. Old-player rule, cheap, functional.
recommendations.rationale: 81 base, $0.90M, 24 years old. Two years is the right length for a backup; cheaper than 4-5 and he has not proven he is a starter.

recommendations.summary: Renew Klesla on 4 years. Young defenceman at $0.90M, cheap depth that fits the development timeline.
