recommendations.rationale: 78 base, $0.90M, 23 years old. Four years covers his development window at below-market cost. Not a chip, not a star, a keeper.

recommendations.proposed: Phoenix for Sillinger (Koltsov + St. Jacques + R3)
recommendations.summary: Move Koltsov as part of the Sillinger package at the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: 24, $1.10M expiring, 11 points in 19 games. He is package filler, not a renewal candidate. PHX at 24 points with 9 expirers will take depth plus a pick.

recommendations.summary: Release or dump Spezza before the deadline. 0.20 points per game on 5.4 minutes a night is a confirmed bust.
recommendations.rationale: 22, $1.00M expiring. The Coach reports the collapse pattern. At 1 year and $1.00M he has no trade value above a late pick. Release saves $1.00M and a roster spot.

recommendations.proposed: Phoenix for Sillinger (Koltsov + St. Jacques + R3)
recommendations.summary: Move St. Jacques as part of the Sillinger package. Not a renewal candidate.
recommendations.rationale: 25, $0.80M expiring. The cheapest contract on the roster. His value is as package filler to balance the Sillinger trade.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Savard from Atlanta: 79 base, FACE 88, 26pts/30GP, $1.00M expiring, age 28. Closes faceoff and scoring gaps in one move.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 26 points cannot re-sign Savard, Heatley, and Kovalchuk simultaneously. He is the cheapest elite faceoff centre in the league and produces 0.87 pts/gp. Package: Koltsov plus St. Jacques plus R3.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Heatley from Atlanta: 91 base, POTE 85, 31pts/30GP, $1.10M expiring, age 24. Replaces Mogilny's production at 20% of his cost.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 26 points with $40.34M payroll cannot retain all three elite expirers. Heatley at 24 is the best RW available in any deal. Package: Tucker plus R1.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Jovanovski from Vancouver: 89 base, TOUG 93, CHKG 94, 10pts/20GP, $2.30M expiring, age 29. Only player above 90 on both toughness and checking.
recommendations.rationale: VAN carry 13 expiring deals on $46.36M payroll at 33 points. They will not re-sign him. Fills the structural toughness hole (zero players at 80+ base TOUG on our roster). Package: Klesla plus R1.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Hartnell from Buffalo: 79 base, POTE 94, TOUG 89, CHKG 92, 10pts/26GP, $1.10M expiring, age 23. Toughness and development in one package.
recommendations.rationale: BUF at 30 points with 5 expiring and $57.55M payroll has no reason to retain a depth-scoring tough wing over their own prospects. POTE 94 means he improves into a top-six regular. Package: Alexeev plus R2.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Hejduk from Colorado: 91 base, 34pts/31GP, $2.50M expiring, age 29. Best scoring-per-salary available.
recommendations.rationale: COL hold Forsberg ($9.90M), Kariya ($10.11M), and Hejduk ($2.50M) all expiring — $22.5M they cannot all carry on a 35-point team. Hejduk is cheapest to move and most valuable per dollar. Gates on whether COL decide to sell at 35 points.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Naslund from Vancouver: 92 base, 48pts/32GP (1.50 pts/gp league lead), $4.40M expiring, age 32. Elite scorer if VAN overload forces his movement.
recommendations.rationale: VAN have 13 expiring deals and must shed multiple bodies. Naslund at 48 points is the league's best player right now. At 32 he is the same age problem as Mogilny but producing twice as much. Only pursue if we are not already getting Jovanovski from VAN.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Comrie from Edmonton: 87 base, 29pts/32GP at 22.2 MPG, $1.00M expiring, age 25. Best young-centre value available.
recommendations.rationale: EDM at 32 points (10-14-4, .412) with 5 expiring are rebuilding candidates. 29 points at $1.00M at age 25 is exceptional production-to-cost. Risk: EDM at 32 points may fight for a wildcard until February before deciding.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Allen from Vancouver: 78 base, TOUG 90, CHKG 84, 11pts/27GP at 22.4 MPG, $0.90M expiring, age 25. Budget toughness-D if Jovanovski is unavailable.
recommendations.rationale: VAN's 13 expiring deals make him available at $0.90M. TOUG 90 gives us a second player above 80 on base toughness. Young enough to develop further. Lower package cost than Jovanovski.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Yonkman from Washington: 74 base, POTE 88, TOUG 88, 8pts/32GP at 19.5 MPG, $0.60M expiring, age 24. Development-grade toughness D at depth-pick cost.
recommendations.rationale: WSH at 23 points (7-18-5) with 5 expiring and $57.05M payroll are among the most desperate sellers. $0.60M for a 24-year-old with POTE 88 and TOUG 88 is almost free. Pairs with the existing defence to add the toughness layer we lack.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Daze from Chicago: 89 base, 35pts/32GP, $3.00M expiring, age 30. Rental scorer who wins games in April but does not improve.
recommendations.rationale: CHI at 23 points (6-17-7) with 8 expiring are the second-worst team in the league and must sell. At 30 with POTE 77 he is a one-year upgrade only. Pursue as a secondary target if the primary deals fall through.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Smyth from Edmonton: 89 base, 33pts/32GP, $2.50M expiring, age 30. Rental scorer at a lower cost than Daze.
recommendations.rationale: EDM at 32 points with 5 expiring face the same wildcard-or-sell decision as EDM's Comrie. At $2.50M for 33 points, his per-dollar efficiency matches Hejduk. Same age profile as Daze — rental only.

recommendations.summary: Trade Koltsov, St. Jacques, and our 3rd-round pick to Atlanta for Savard (FACE 88, 26pts/30GP, $1.00M expiring, 79 base).
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 26 points cannot re-sign Savard, Heatley, or Kovalchuk on $40.34M payroll. He fixes our faceoff hole (only Sundin at 90 is reliable). We save $0.90M net. Both Koltsov and St. Jacques have 0 GP and are expiring. Acceptance is likely given ATL's situation but the AI's valuation is unknown.

recommendations.summary: Trade Alexeev and our 2nd-round pick to Vancouver for Jovanovski (TOUG 93, CHKG 94, 89 base, $2.30M expiring, age 29).
recommendations.rationale: We carry zero players above 80 base TOUG. Jovanovski is the only 90/90+ in the league. VAN at 33 points with 13 expiring deals will not re-sign him. Alexeev is the coach's scratch target (below 0.45 threshold) and POTE 94 is what a rebuilding GM prices. Costs us 12 pts/25 GP of depth scoring and our second-rounder. Acceptance uncertain because VAN at 33 may still chase the wildcard.

recommendations.summary: Trade Tucker and our 1st-round pick to Atlanta for Heatley (91 base, 31pts/30GP, $1.10M expiring, age 24).
recommendations.rationale: Heatley replaces Mogilny's production (25 pts, $5.50M, age 36) at 20% the cost. ATL cannot keep three elite expirers. Tucker's CHKG 92 gives their young roster a veteran presence; the 1st-rounder is what a 26-point team values most. Net saving $0.20M. This costs our only first-rounder and should only proceed if deals 1 and 2 land first.

recommendations.summary: If none of the three proposals land, use Mogilny (90 base, $5.50M, expiring, 25 pts) as the pick-recovery chip at the March deadline for a 2nd or 3rd rounder.
recommendations.rationale: The pick-recovery mechanic trades any 80+ expiring player for a draft pick. Mogilny is our highest-value chip by that rule. Tucker at CHKG 92 expiring is the second chip. Together they could yield 2-3 picks to rebuild June capital.

recommendations.summary: Task #2 is closed — Luongo acquired February 2005, GM closed goalie monitoring March 2005; the live item is now his 1-year renewal in July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo reads 95 displayed at $1.60M with 1 year left. The trade-window framing is dead; the renewal framing is tracked under summer-2006-renewal-list-dec2005.

recommendations.summary: Do not dress Gardener. 0 points in 23 games at 3.6 MPG is not a development opportunity.
recommendations.rationale: He accumulated another 1-2 games since the December 8th scratch recommendation and still has zero points in 23 games. His roster spot is better used giving Spacek or another young forward real minutes.

recommendations.summary: Either dress Spacek with 12+ MPG or stop dressing him entirely; morale 76 is the lowest on the roster and 6 games in 32 is neither developing nor helping the team.
recommendations.rationale: Spacek has 3 points in 6 games (0.50 pts/g) and POTE 91 at 20. His January scratch window expired months ago. At 5.8 MPG in limited action he's below the 8-MPG floor that triggers my scratch rule, and his morale reflects that.

recommendations.summary: Spezza at 5 points in 26 games on 5.4 MPG is replacement-level. Move him to healthy scratch or raise his minutes to 10+; the current arrangement develops nobody.
recommendations.rationale: His rate is 0.19 pts/g, the same pattern that ended Spezza's previous two seasons. Morale 82 and falling. Fourth-line garbage minutes with POTE 99 are a waste.

recommendations.summary: Upshall at 5 points in 23 games on 6.0 MPG (0.22 pts/g) is producing at replacement level. Same decision as Spezza: raise or scratch.
recommendations.rationale: Identical profile to Spezza: POTE 99, morale 84, collapsed minutes, no production above the fourth-line floor. The pattern from last season continues.

recommendations.summary: When Gaborik returns, cap his minutes at 16. 22.6 MPG for 0.47 pts/g is top-pairing ice at bottom-six production.
recommendations.rationale: 8 points in 17 games is a 0.47 rate. He's currently scratched which is fine, but the ice-time-to-production gap needs correcting if he re-enters the lineup.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev is at 0.42 pts/g over 25 games, below the 0.45 threshold where I said the dressing recommendation weakens.
recommendations.rationale: Set at 25 games as planned. Rate is below the line. Next reassessment at 35 games; if he has not recovered to 0.50 by then he comes out of the regular rotation.

recommendations.summary: Richards' third consecutive season of decline (1.08, 0.71, 0.55) at age 25 confirms a system-fit problem. Offseason review is mandatory before he is pencilled as a top-six centre again.
recommendations.rationale: No injury, no role change explains it. Minutes at 11.6 are below his band. The pattern has held for three full seasons.

recommendations.summary: McCabe at 0.29 pts/g in 7 games is well below the 0.60 sell threshold. He goes back on the sell list.
recommendations.rationale: My March note said if the final rate held below 0.60 he goes back on the list. At 30, his 0.29 in a small sample is consistent with decline.

recommendations.summary: Chlup at 0.77 over 32 games on 21.4 MPG at 19 confirms the franchise trajectory. No change needed.
recommendations.rationale: Production held through a full 32-game sample after doubling his minutes. The April call was right. Protect his role.

recommendations.summary: Room is healthy at average 93. Richards (84) is the only name below band but his structural decline says 11.7 MPG is his level and his morale is recovering with the team.
recommendations.rationale: Richards at 84 morale and 11.7 MPG: five minutes under his 80s band, but three seasons of rate decline (1.08→0.71→0.54) confirm this is his level. Chlup (0.78 pts/g, 20.9 MPG) is outperforming him on the second line. Morale rose from 78 to 84 without intervention. Luongo at 82 is a backup-goalie problem, not a line problem.

recommendations.summary: Keep PK2 as-is tonight; TB's 13.4% PP (18 for 134) does not punish our 74 checking mean.
recommendations.rationale: Jackman and McCabe both sit on PK1, leaving PK2 without an elite checker. Against TB's bottom-tier PP the risk is minimal, so the matchup does not warrant a change.

recommendations.summary: No line changes tonight. The top three lines are role-appropriate and chemistry is intact.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has scoring (90 mean) with Jackman anchoring defensively. L2 has Nash's 82 checking and Chlup's 80 faceoffs doing the support work. L3 has McCabe (83 checking) covering Richards' defensive end. All three units suit their roles.

recommendations.summary: We cannot build two PK units with checking above 78 simultaneously with Roberts out. He is the fix: 88 checking, 90 toughness, 89 morale.
recommendations.rationale: Only Jackman (92), McCabe (83), and Nash (82) are available checkers. Jackman and McCabe are both consumed by PK1, leaving PK2 at a 74 checking mean. Roberts at 84 OVR and 88 checking slots directly onto PK2 and lifts it above 80. If his scratch is a development rotation, we need to know that the cost is a fragile second PK unit against elite PP teams.

recommendations.summary: Start Ouellet against Khabibulin; check his fatigue icon before confirming.
recommendations.rationale: Ouellet at 86 OVR matches Khabibulin's 87. Tellqvist at 73 gives them a six-point grade advantage in net against a team that already has one clear weapon in Lecavalier.

recommendations.summary: No line changes. Auto-pairing already gives us favourable matchups on all four lines.
recommendations.rationale: Their top pair is 78/74, second pair 72/74, third pair 69/70. Our D pairs at 87/86, 85/68, 84/66 all match or exceed them. Sundin's 95 FACE vs Lecavalier's 62 locks the top matchup. Their PP at 13.4% is not a threat.

recommendations.summary: No change to the sell list since December 15th: Klesla (0.44 pts/g, 87 OVR, expiring) is the one to move at the deadline, Colaiacovo (0.12 pts/g, 0 goals in 25) is the one to move at any cost, St. Jacques walks at year end.
recommendations.rationale: Klesla recovered slightly from 0.40 to 0.44, Jackman stable at 0.66 (above 0.55 trigger, keeps), Colaiacovo still at zero goals in 25 games. No new injuries to D since last report.

recommendations.summary: Line Gaborik on a top-six wing; he carries 98 speed, 92 scoring, and 92 playmaking and is in no unit at all.
recommendations.rationale: The coach already recommends third or fourth line, but his grades (92/92/98) justify a top-six slot over any current L2 or L3 winger. At 23 with 1 year left on his deal, every game he scratches devalues him for the July 2006 window.

recommendations.summary: Put Tucker on the second penalty kill; his 83 checking is the best available from the not-lined pool.
recommendations.rationale: The coach flags Tucker for K2 and the coach is right. Tucker at 83 checking, 30 years old, and not currently in any unit is wasted depth. Upshall at 80 checking but sub-6 MPG and 0.21 rate is the better scratch candidate.

recommendations.summary: Faceoff depth is the only role this roster cannot fix internally; Savard (FACE 87) or Vasicek (FACE 80) are the cheap closes.
recommendations.rationale: Only Sundin (90) and Wallin (83, not lined) are above 80 on faceoffs. The next best is Chlup at 75. The GM killed the Bell argument in January because both are wings, but Savard and Vasicek are centres. Vasicek is cheaper (FACE 80, 82 overall, $0.40M, CAR); Savard is better (FACE 87, 79 overall, $1.00M, ATL).

recommendations.summary: Toughness reads 0 at 80+ on base grades but 11 reach 80+ on displayed grades; no acquisition needed.
recommendations.rationale: The December 4 query confirmed 11 Toronto players at 80+ displayed toughness. The GM has closed this target list three times. The base-grade void is a roster construction characteristic (speed/skill over size) that does not affect game play.

recommendations.summary: Spezza and Upshall both collapse-pattern at 22 with under 6 MPG and sub-0.21 rates; stop dressing them before March.
recommendations.rationale: The coach flagged both on Dec 15. Upshall at 80 checking is the only reason he stays, but Tucker at 83 covers that. Spezza at POTE 99 is the long-term keeper, but 22 with sub-6 MPG means his development is stalled by not playing. Offseason camp or trade him as package filler.

recommendations.summary: Sign Luongo to a 5-year extension in July 2006 on the first available day.
recommendations.rationale: He is 95 displayed, 91 base, age 26, $1.60M expiring. He is the most valuable contract on the roster and enters his prime next season. A 5-year deal expires July 2011, clear of the 2009 cluster.

recommendations.summary: Sign Chlup to a 5-year extension in July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: He is 19 with 87 displayed and 82 base. A 5-year rookie deal is the cheapest way to lock a young first-round centre through his development window.

recommendations.summary: Sign Klesla to a 4-year extension in July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: He is 23 with 87 displayed, 78 base, $0.90M. A 4-year deal through July 2010 captures his development at low cost without joining the 2009 cluster.

recommendations.proposed: Trade at March deadline for young player or draft pick
recommendations.summary: Move Mogilny before March 19 via the over-80 expiring mechanic or a direct trade for a young forward with potential.
recommendations.rationale: He is 36, $5.50M, 89 displayed. His salary is the largest on the roster and his ceiling is set at his age. He can fetch a pick even without a named taker.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Heatley from Atlanta at the March deadline for Tucker plus a first-round pick.
recommendations.rationale: Heatley is 91 base. Atlanta are a 20-point club with the league's lowest payroll and three elite expirers they cannot re-sign. The package uses Tucker (79, expiring) plus the 2006 R1 and does not overlap with the Sillinger deal.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Sillinger from Phoenix at the March deadline for Koltsov plus St. Jacques plus a third-round pick.
recommendations.rationale: Sillinger carries FACE 96 and 87 overall at $1.20M expiring. Phoenix are at 24 points with 9 expiring deals. Koltsov (75, 68 base) and St. Jacques (66) are the cheapest package pieces available.

recommendations.proposed: 2-year extension if no better backup materializes
recommendations.summary: Renew Ouellet on a 2-year deal at $0.90M in July 2006 if no better backup goalie is acquired.
recommendations.rationale: He is 24 with 86 displayed and 81 base. With Luongo signed long-term and Belfour likely walking, Ouellet at $0.90M is a capable backup. The standing order says to seek a high-90s goalie from a non-contender; if that fails, Ouellet fills the role.

recommendations.proposed: Release or trade for a late-round pick
recommendations.summary: Do not renew Spezza. Try to trade him for a late-round pick before March, or release him in July.
recommendations.rationale: He is 22 with 73 displayed and is in the coach's collapse pattern under 6 MPG with sub-0.21 rates. At 73 he is below the 80 threshold for the pick-recovery mechanic, so trade value is minimal. $1.00M is wasted on a player who cannot dress.

recommendations.summary: Do not open trade negotiations until late February.
recommendations.rationale: Per the GM's standing order of January 15, 2005: sellers remain sellers through January. Open negotiations in late February for all three deadline packages.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Heatley from Atlanta at the March deadline; package Tucker plus our R1.
recommendations.rationale: Heatley: 90 overall/91 base, 31 pts/30 GP, 97 speed, POTE 86, $1.10M expiring, age 22. ATL at 26 points with $40.34M payroll and 6 expiring deals cannot re-sign him. He is the Mogilny successor at one-fifth the cost.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Sillinger from Phoenix; package Koltsov plus St. Jacques plus R3.
recommendations.rationale: Sillinger: FACE 96, 87 overall, $1.20M expiring. Our only other FACE above 80 is Sundin (90) and Wallin (83, not lined). PHX at 26 points with 9 expiring and $55.41M payroll must move him. Koltsov gives them 92 speed for a rebuild.

recommendations.summary: Explore Havlat from Ottawa; package Alexeev plus R2.
recommendations.rationale: Havlat: 86 overall/87 base, 98 speed, POTE 84, 28 pts/28 GP, $0.90M expiring. OTT at 25 points with only 4 expiring deals are reluctant but $0.90M for 98 speed is below-market. Alexeev (92 speed, 0.36 pts/g here) is the cheapest piece we can send.

recommendations.summary: Secondary target: Kovalchuk from Atlanta if Heatley package fails or if ATL moves both.
recommendations.rationale: Kovalchuk: 91 overall/89 base, 99 speed, 34 pts/30 GP, 19 goals, $1.10M expiring. Same situation as Heatley but 23 and slightly past his POTE development window. Better scorer tonight, Heatley is the better player in 2008.

recommendations.summary: Drury from Buffalo as fallback faceoff target if Sillinger package is rejected.
recommendations.rationale: Drury: 87 overall/89 base, FACE 85, TOUG 76, CHKG 76, POTE 81, $2.00M expiring, 27 pts/29 GP. BUF at 30 points with 5 expiring are reluctant sellers and $2.00M is double Sillinger's salary. Inferior to Sillinger on faceoffs (85 vs 96) at higher cost.

recommendations.summary: Do not pursue Bertuzzi despite 42 points. Pass.
recommendations.rationale: Bertuzzi: 93 overall/94 base, 42 pts/31 GP, $2.60M expiring, but age 31 with POTE 58 and zero development value. We already have Chistov (0.66 pts/g), Nash, Sundin producing. This is a rental at full price with no path to 2007.

recommendations.summary: Do not pursue Daze. FACE 50, TOUG 50, $3.00M is the worst value on the board.
recommendations.rationale: Daze: 85 overall/89 base, $3.00M expiring, but FACE 50 and TOUG 50 make him useless for both gaps we are filling. CHI at 21 points will sell cheap, but cheap is still $3.00M we do not need to spend on a 29-year-old with zero defensive game.

recommendations.summary: Offer Tucker plus first-round pick to Atlanta for Heatley; he is 91 base at 22 on $1.10M, 31 pts/30 GP, on a 26-point club that cannot re-sign him.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 26 points and $40.34M payroll hold six expiring deals. Tucker gives them a 92-checking veteran for 30 games of development while the R1 is the future asset a rebuilding GM prices above a rental. We replace Mogilny's wing with a player 14 years younger at $1.10M versus $5.50M. Acceptance uncertain.

recommendations.summary: Offer Koltsov, St. Jacques, and our third-round pick to Phoenix for Sillinger; his FACE 96 closes the only genuine role gap on this roster.
recommendations.rationale: PHX at 26 points with 9 expiring deals and $55.41M payroll are active sellers. Koltsov's POTE 94 and 96 speed give their rebuild a young asset; St. Jacques is first-out D per the Coach. We save $0.70M net (both players we give are expiring at 1 year). Sillinger's 96 FACE at $1.20M gives L3/L4 real draws. Non-competing with the Heatley deal. Acceptance uncertain.

recommendations.current: Alexeev + R1 or R2 (depending on which primary deal fails)
recommendations.summary: If either primary deal fails, approach Ottawa with Alexeev plus a pick for Havlat; 98 speed, 28 pts/28 GP, $0.90M expiring, POTE 84 at 24.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 25 points with only 4 expiring deals are the least motivated sellers on this board. Open this in late February only if Heatley and Sillinger both fail. Alexeev brings 89 speed and POTE 94 at 23. Acceptance is uncertain given OTT's low urgency.

recommendations.summary: Prepare a 5-year offer for Luongo in July 2006; his 1 remaining year expires and Ouellet at 81 base is not a number-one backup.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is 95 overall at 26 on a $1.60M salary with 1 year left. A 5-year deal locks a franchise goalie at a below-market rate before his value ratchets at renewal. The renewal-cluster finding says 11 players expire July 2009; adding Luongo there clusters 12 deals, so consider a 4-year instead.

recommendations.summary: Scratch Gardener permanently. Zero points in 22 games after two scratch-and-return cycles.
recommendations.rationale: 0 points, 3.5 MPG, 71% share. The GM took scratch recommendations on 4 and 8 December; Gardener returned both times and still has not registered a point. No development case survives 22 scoreless games.

recommendations.summary: Scratch Colaiacovo permanently. 0.12 pts/g over 25 games is below replacement.
recommendations.rationale: 3 points in 25 games, zero goals, at 12.3 MPG. The November 27 recommendation was right; the sample has only grown and the rate has not moved. He is the weakest regular defenceman by a wide margin.

recommendations.summary: Dress Gaborik and scratch Upshall or Spezza to free the roster spot.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik produces 0.47 pts/g on 22.6 MPG in 17 games. Spezza is at 0.20 on 5.4 MPG; Upshall 0.23 on 6.1. A 23-year-old getting top-four minutes and outproducing the fourth line by double should not be watching from the press box.

recommendations.summary: Stop dressing Spezza. 0.20 pts/g on 5.4 MPG is the collapse pattern, not development.
recommendations.rationale: 5 points in 25 games, 5.4 MPG, morale 82. Same pattern as Upshall and Gardener: early minutes, a collapse, and now scraps too small to grow anything. A camp audition next summer is the real lever, not February ice time.

recommendations.summary: No change for Chlup, Nash, Chistov, Klesla, Alexeev.
recommendations.rationale: All five play every game or near every game at appropriate minutes with production matching role. Alexeev is at 0.46 pts/g in 24 games, one game short of the 25-game reassessment threshold set on 17 November.

recommendations.summary: Chistov at 0.67 pts/g on 20.5 MPG over 31 games has confirmed his top-six role; no change needed but the GM should know this is real, not a hot streak.
recommendations.rationale: He went from scratch (0 GP in first save) to 31 games at 0.67 with the ice time to match. The development trend is strongly positive at age 22.

recommendations.summary: Scratch Alexeev. At 0.39 pts/g over 24 games he is below the 0.45 threshold I set on November 17th for retaining a dressing spot.
recommendations.rationale: His rate fell from 0.55 last season to 0.39 this year on 10.7 MPG. He is at 24 of 25 reassessment games and the answer is no. Give the slot to a young player on an upward trajectory rather than a fading one.

recommendations.summary: Scratch Lundmark or raise his minutes above 10 MPG. At 6.4 MPG over 23 games and 0.18 pts/g he is in the collapse pattern, not developing.
recommendations.rationale: Minutes fell from 11.0 to 6.4 within the window, the same trajectory as Upshall and Spezza before their rates cratered. Half-measures keep him in the pattern.

recommendations.summary: Klesla remains the top defense sell candidate. 0.43 pts/g at 87 OVR expiring is the best trade window we have on the blue line.
recommendations.rationale: Rate recovered above my 0.30 floor. Buyers see 87 and an expiring contract; the 0.43 is invisible to them. End-of-season review says move him before regression takes the value down.

recommendations.summary: Chlup is 19 and producing 0.80 pts/g at 21.4 MPG over 31 games. No adjustment. He is the centrepiece and the trend confirms it.
recommendations.rationale: Rate held while minutes nearly quadrupled. That is the development curve we want at his age.

recommendations.summary: Jackman at 0.67 pts/g over 31 games is stable and above the 0.55 sell trigger. Keep him.
recommendations.rationale: His November 4th rate of 0.68 has barely moved. No bleed, no sell case right now.

recommendations.summary: Give Spacek Gardener's spot on the fourth line. Spacek at morale 76 needs minutes to climb out of the -2 penalty zone; Gardener at 0 points in 22 games has earned nothing.
recommendations.rationale: Spacek is producing at 0.50 pts/g (3 in 6 games) but sits at the roster's lowest morale (76) because he gets 5.8 MPG. The -2 morale penalty costs the team more than his development value at this stage. Gardener at 0 points in 22 games at 3.5 MPG is the same collapse pattern I flagged on November 27th.

recommendations.summary: No further ice-time change for Richards. Morale has climbed from 78 to 84 without intervention and is still trending up.
recommendations.rationale: The structural 5-minute deficit persists (11.6 MPG vs ~17 target), but morale at 84 and rising +3 to +5 means the cost is now just -1 per grade. I recommended promoting him on December 8th and the GM declined. The trend says the situation is healing on its own.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker on L4 instead of Gardener; checking 80 versus zero points in 18+ games.
recommendations.rationale: Gardener has produced nothing in any measurable capacity and is at roughly 3 MPG, which is below his band expectation. Tucker at checking 80 is a role fit on a line that needs a forechecker. The GM confirmed Tucker stays as our checking guy.

recommendations.summary: Three true centres force Sundin onto K2, wasting a 93-scoring, 98-clutch player on penalty kills.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin, Chlup and Richards are our only centres above third-line quality. With no fourth centre who can draw, Sundin must cover K2. No lineup arrangement solves this; it requires a roster addition at centre.

recommendations.summary: Lines 1 through 3 are correctly built for their roles; no composition changes needed.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has speed and scoring (89/99, 93/99) with Jackman anchoring at 91 checking. L2 is balanced with Nash at 81 checking and Afinogenov at 92 scoring. L3 has the right defensive profile at mean 70 with Richards' 92 playmaking as the counterbalance.

recommendations.summary: Leave the D-pair order alone despite the Jokinen-Safronov mismatch.
recommendations.rationale: Jokinen (85) against Safronov (68) is a gap, but swapping D2/D3 puts Safronov against Rolston (81) instead, and we are 20-7 playing an 8-15 team with an 8.4% PP. The talent advantage absorbs it.

recommendations.summary: Start Ouellet.
recommendations.rationale: Ouellet is 86 OVR with no fatigue flag. Tellqvist is 73. Aebischer is 89 on the other side and we need our best available.

recommendations.summary: Sell Klesla at the deadline: 87 OVR on the card, expiring, 0.42 pts/g that a buyer cannot see.
recommendations.rationale: Rate recovered from 0.29 to 0.42 but still well below what 87 implies. $0.90M expiring makes him cheap to move. Window closes in August when he walks.

recommendations.summary: Move Colaiacovo: 3 points in 25 games with zero goals at $1.40M x 4. Try to dump the salary before the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: 0.12 pts/g is replacement-level or below. 76 OVR with 4 years and $1.40M makes him hard to move but not impossible if a contender needs a seventh D.

recommendations.summary: Jackman stays. Rate held at 0.68 over 31 games (4 points in the last 6), $0.70M x 2 is elite value.
recommendations.rationale: The sell trigger is 0.55. He is nowhere near it and his recent form is flat rather than declining. Keep.

recommendations.summary: Acquire a faceoff centre above 80 FACE before the February deadline; no internal option above 75.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin at 90 is a winger; Chlup 75 and Richards 70 are the best internal centres. Savard (ATL, FACE 87, $1.00M expiring, 19pts/22GP) closes the gap for Tucker alone at zero draft cost per the Dec 1 finding. Avery (LA, FACE 93, TOUG 83, $0.40M, 2 years) closes faceoffs, toughness, and checking simultaneously at the cheapest cost in the league.

recommendations.summary: Put Jackman (CHKG 87, 24 years old) on PK2 in place of the collapse-pattern depth forwards; his grade is the highest available.
recommendations.rationale: Coach flagged PK2 checking mean at 71 vs target 76. Jackman at 87 composite checking is the only unlined player above 85 who can play tonight. Tucker at 83 is scratched by design. Upshall at 80 is in the collapse pattern per the Coach's own report.

recommendations.summary: Dress Abid (86 scoring, 90 durability, 86 clutch, 25 years old) on the third or fourth line; he provides energy, physicality, and late-game trust.
recommendations.rationale: Abid carries 90 durability which is the highest on any unlined forward. His 86 scoring and 86 clutch make him a legitimate top-nine option. The Coach already recommended Gaborik to a bottom line; Abid is the same argument with physical presence and late-game reliability added.

recommendations.summary: Toughness is covered; the Dec 4 audit found 11 players at 80+ on displayed TOUG and all targets (Hartnell, Kurka, Jovanovski) were correctly closed.
recommendations.rationale: The composite role-coverage metric averages TOUG with fighting and aggression, pulling the score down. The specific attribute is fine. Spending draft capital on toughness would be wasted.

recommendations.summary: Dress Gaborik immediately per the Coach's proposal to rebuild trade value, then move him at the February deadline for a top-six winger we keep long-term.
recommendations.rationale: At $11.90M/year through July 2010 with 8 pts in 17 GP as a scratch, he is 13.2% of payroll earning nothing. His value drops every undressed game. Chistov at $5.00M with POTE 95 and 0.66 pts/g already fills his role at less than half the cost.

recommendations.summary: Sign Luongo to a 5-6 year deal at renewal in July 2006 before he walks on a 1-year expiring at $1.60M.
recommendations.rationale: 94 overall, age 26, $1.60M is below-market for a franchise goalie. Without a new contract he leaves and the backup is Ouellet at 81 base. Lock him first, Chlup the same week.

recommendations.summary: Sign Chlup to a 5-6 year deal at July 2006 renewal; he is the future first-line centre at 19 with POTE 95.
recommendations.rationale: 24 points in 30 games at age 19 on a $2.34M expiring deal. He will not re-sign yearly at increasing cost. Lock him the same week as Luongo.

recommendations.summary: Begin breaking the 2009 cluster by extending Richards, Chistov and Nash in July 2007 — three full seasons before the other eight come due.
recommendations.rationale: Eleven players on 4-year deals worth $37.40M all expire July 2009 simultaneously. Splitting three off two years early turns one $37.40M cliff into manageable windows.

recommendations.summary: The age curve is already at target: 13 under 23, 16 at 24-29, 5 at 30+. No structural roster change needed.
recommendations.rationale: The manual wants 5-7 veterans and ~20 young players. Toronto have exactly that. The problem is contracts, not composition.

recommendations.summary: Move Mogilny at the March deadline for a pick or young player; he is 36 at $5.50M expiring and will walk in July.
recommendations.rationale: 89 base, 21 pts in 30 GP, age 36, $5.50M salary relief. His value peaks now; every contender needs a RW at that level and the over-80 expiring mechanic converts him to a pick if no package materializes.

recommendations.summary: Open negotiations with Atlanta for Heatley in late February; he is 91 base expiring on a 24-point club that cannot re-sign him.
recommendations.rationale: ATL sits 24 points (9-15-4) per q165 with $40.34M league-low payroll. Heatley, Kovalchuk, and Savard are all expiring at $3.20M combined. They cannot keep any of them. Package: Tucker plus R1.

recommendations.summary: Secondary deadline target: Bertuzzi at VAN (94 base, TOUG 83, CHKG 87, 1.25 pts/g) fills the checking-scoring gap the Coach flags.
recommendations.rationale: VAN had 13 expiring players and league-lowest payroll in October. Their structural situation makes them sellers regardless of record. Package: Tucker plus R2 if Tucker is not going to ATL.

recommendations.summary: Renew Luongo on 5-6 years immediately in July 2006; he is 26, 91 base, $1.60M with one year remaining.
recommendations.rationale: The backup is Ouellet at 81 base. Luongo is our franchise goaltender and without a new deal he walks. This is the single most important summer action.

recommendations.summary: Renew Chlup on 5-6 years in July 2006; he is 19, 24 pts in 30 GP at 20.9 MPG on a $2.34M expiring deal.
recommendations.rationale: He scored 27 pts over 58 GP as a 19-year-old last season and is on pace to match or exceed that. A second-round centre at 19 producing at this rate needs a star-length deal before the market finds him.

recommendations.summary: Renew Klesla on 3-4 years; he is 23, 12 pts in 30 GP (33 pace), $0.90M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Projected 33 pts over 82 is top-four D production. At $0.90M he is far below market value and must not reach the open market.

recommendations.summary: Renew Ouellet on 2 years as backup; 24 years old, 81 base, $0.90M.
recommendations.rationale: He is the playoff backup the GM identified in January 2005 when ruling out Luongo carrying the post-season alone. Two years is appropriate for a backup.

recommendations.summary: Do not renew Spezza; he is 22 with 5 pts in 46 GP last season and 2 in 24 this season on under 6 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: Coach flagged him in the collapse pattern. $1.00M for a player not dressing regularly is payroll we should not extend.

recommendations.summary: Do not renew St. Jacques; zero points in 12 games at 11.8 MPG, 25 years old, 81 base.
recommendations.rationale: Coach named him first out at third-pairing defence. He has not shown at 25 enough to justify a second look.

recommendations.summary: Use Tucker (79 base, $1.30M, age 30) as trade currency at the deadline for Heatley or Bertuzzi rather than renewing him.
recommendations.rationale: 79 overall base at 30 on an expiring deal is deadline currency. The Coach's K2 role is fillable by Roberts or another checking forward. His trade value is real now and gone in July.

recommendations.summary: Do not open deadline negotiations before late February; the GM's standing order from January 2005 holds and the deadline is 94 days away.
recommendations.rationale: Sellers remain sellers. Atlanta will still be selling in March. Moving in December or January surrenders leverage.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Kris Draper (DET) as the primary February faceoff rental: FACE 97, 31 pts/26 GP, $1.20M expiring, DET at 31 pts with only 3 picks left (active seller).
recommendations.rationale: He is the only 97-FACE centre in the league and the only faceoff elite on a club this far out of the race. At $1.20M expiring he costs nothing to acquire beyond a mid-round pick.

recommendations.summary: Secondary faceoff target: Sillinger (PHX), FACE 96, 87 overall, 24 pts/27 GP, $1.80M expiring. PHX at 24 pts with 9 expiring will dump him.
recommendations.rationale: He scores more than Draper (0.89 pts/g vs 1.19 but at 87 overall he is a stronger two-way player). If Draper is too expensive for DET's remaining picks, Sillinger is the same gap filled by the league's most desperate seller.

recommendations.summary: Best value centre available: Vasicek (CAR), 84 overall, FACE 80, POTE 87, 37 pts/37 GP, $0.40M expiring. Package: Koltsov plus R3.
recommendations.rationale: He is 25 with POTE 87 producing a point a game. His FACE at 80 does not match Draper or Sillinger but he scores at a top-six rate for slot salary. CAR at 37 points with 14 expiring cannot re-sign him.

recommendations.summary: Cheapest faceoff answer: Avery (LA), FACE 90, 79 base, $0.40M expiring, 25 years old. LA at 20 points will sell anyone.
recommendations.rationale: At 25 with POTE 71 and 79 base he is not a playoff starter but he solves zone draws at the lowest possible cost. His contract is expiring at $0.40M so the return to LA is a late-round pick or depth body.

recommendations.summary: Long-term faceoff answer if available: Hilbert (BOS), FACE 86, POTE 95, 82 displayed / 77 base, $0.90M expiring, 24 years old.
recommendations.rationale: He is the only 85+ faceoff centre under 25 with POTE above 90. The risk is BOS at 38 points with only 4 expiring deals keeping him. Worth a February call but cannot be plan-a.

recommendations.summary: Budget faceoff option: Bates (NYI), FACE 89, 83 base, 37 pts/37 GP, $0.90M expiring, 30 years old.
recommendations.rationale: NYI at 37 points with 7 expiring deals are in rebuild mode and will shed salary. At $0.90M he is cheaper than Sillinger and produces at a similar rate with 7 fewer years of age.

recommendations.summary: Heatley (ATL, 91 base, expiring) remains the primary scoring target. ATL at 24 points cannot re-sign him. Package: Tucker plus R1.
recommendations.rationale: Already tracked since December. He fills the depth-scoring gap the GM identified in February 2005. Competes for the same draft capital as Jovanovski, so only one deadline move is possible without a Gaborik return.

recommendations.summary: Jovanovski (VAN, TOUG 93, CHKG 94, 89 base, $2.30M expiring) remains the physical-D target. VAN at 30 points with 13 expiring will not re-sign.
recommendations.rationale: Only player above 90 on both checking and toughness. Competes with Heatley for the R1. Choose one before February; both is impossible with three picks remaining.

recommendations.summary: Dress Gaborik on the third or fourth line tonight; his 92 base and 98 speed are worth $11.90M in trade value only if he plays and scores for six weeks before February.
recommendations.rationale: Coach's recommendation aligns with the trajectory analysis. Every scratched game at $11.90M erodes his value on a deal through July 2010 that cannot be renegotiated.

recommendations.proposed: Lock Luongo on 5-6 years at the start of July 2006
recommendations.summary: Luongo at 94 overall, $1.60M, 26 years old is the cheapest elite asset in the league and cannot be allowed to walk.
recommendations.rationale: Already noted. Without a new deal he leaves and the backup is Ouellet at 81. Chlup at POTE 95 must be locked the same week.

recommendations.summary: The PK2 checking problem is deployment, not roster. Tucker (CHKG 83) and Roberts (CHKG 86) are available; the Coach needs to use them on the kill rather than acquire a new body.
recommendations.rationale: Six players at 80+ on checking already exist on this roster. No acquisition fixes a coach who scratches his best checkers.

recommendations.summary: Offer Tucker plus our first-round pick to Atlanta for Dany Heatley.
recommendations.rationale: ATL are 24 points on $40.34M payroll with three elite expirers they cannot re-sign. Heatley's 91 base is the biggest available scoring addition. Tucker fills their lineup for the balance of the season; the R1 is their rebuild currency.

recommendations.current: Koltsov ($1.10M LW, 24, expiring, 0 GP) + St. Jacques ($0.80M D, 25, expiring, 0 pts/12 GP) + R3
recommendations.proposed: Sillinger (PHX, C, 34, FACE 96, 87 overall, $1.20M expiring, 24 pts/27 GP)
recommendations.summary: Offer Koltsov, St. Jacques and our third-round pick to Phoenix for Mike Sillinger.
recommendations.rationale: PHX at 24 points with 9 expiring and $55.41M payroll must shed salary. Sillinger at FACE 96 and 87 overall is a playoff-ready centre who wins every draw; net payroll saving $0.70M. We give three players who produced nothing (combined 0 pts this season).

recommendations.proposed: Vasicek (CAR, C, 25, 84 overall, FACE 80, POTE 87, $0.40M expiring, 37 pts/37 GP)
recommendations.summary: If Sillinger is unavailable, offer Koltsov plus our third-round pick to Carolina for Vasicek.
recommendations.rationale: CAR cannot re-sign him; bottom of standings with 14 expiring deals. Vasicek at 25 with POTE 87 and 37 points is a young top-six centre who raises FACE from 75 to 80 and saves $0.70M. His FACE 80 still loses to elite playoff centres but he is a long-term piece unlike a rental.

recommendations.summary: Close task #2 (Luongo/DiPietro goalie trade window monitoring) — Luongo is on our roster at 95, the window was fulfilled last season, and the GM closed goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19.
recommendations.rationale: The task was to find a 90+ goalie; we hold Luongo at 95 overall, $1.60M, 1 year left. The successor concern is his July 2006 renewal, which is tracked separately.

recommendations.summary: Luongo enters July 2006 as a restricted free agent at 95 overall; he must be re-signed on a 5–6 year deal or traded before that summer.
recommendations.rationale: Contract shows 1 year at $1.60M remaining. His backup is Ouellet at 81 base. Losing Luongo in free agency would undo the entire January 2005 goalie acquisition.

recommendations.slot: right wing, third or fourth line
recommendations.summary: Dress Gaborik and put him on the third or fourth line; his 0.47 rate and 22.6 MPG when playing exceed Alexeev's 0.43 on 10.6 MPG and he's sitting out 43% of games.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik produces at a higher rate than any young forward already in the lineup and gets top-line minutes when dressed. Scratching him while Upshall (0.24) and Spezza (0.21) dress on the fourth line wastes his season at 23.

recommendations.summary: Chlup, Nash, Chistov and Klesla are earning every shift and no adjustment is needed for the core young group.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup 24 pts in 30 GP, Nash 18 in 30, Chistov 21 in 30, Klesla 12 in 30 at 25.9 MPG. All four are producing at or above what their role demands.

recommendations.summary: Drop Alexeev to the scratch or fourth line; 0.36 pts/g in 23 games is below the 0.45 threshold set on November 17th.
recommendations.rationale: His rate fell from 0.55 last season to 0.36 on 10.8 MPG. More ice is not fixing the production gap. Brendl at 3.6 MPG needs a real look if Alexeev is stalling.

recommendations.summary: Chistov has made himself a top-six winger at 0.66 pts/g on 20.2 MPG over 30 games at age 22. Treat him as one.
recommendations.rationale: He went from 6 MPG in the first sample to 20.2 MPG with real production. He is no longer a depth forward and the lines should reflect that.

recommendations.summary: Spezza and Upshall are both in the collapse pattern at 22 with under 6 MPG and sub-0.21 rates. Offseason camp audition or stop dressing.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza 0.21 pts/g on 5.6 MPG over 24 games, Upshall 0.20 on 5.8 over 21. Neither is producing at their current role. This is the third or fourth season of the same pattern.

recommendations.summary: St. Jacques has zero points in 12 games on 11.8 MPG. With Safronov (0.47, 21.2 MPG) and Hainsey (0.37, 20.9 MPG) outperforming him, he is first out at third-pairing D.
recommendations.rationale: 12 games and zero points at 25 on meaningful minutes. He is not holding a regular spot.

recommendations.summary: No change to the D minutes load. Jackman (24.7 MPG) and Klesla (25.4) have come down from 41 and 42 in October. The concentration problem is fixed.
recommendations.rationale: Safronov, Hainsey, Stahle and Fischer are absorbing the volume. Endurance risk from the October note has passed.

recommendations.summary: No ice-time changes. The room has recovered on the back of recent wins; most players sit at 97 with positive trends.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo (82, full 60 MPG) and Spacek (76, scratched) are the only outliers below 90, and neither is fixable by giving more or fewer minutes. Richards at 11.5 MPG and 84 is below his band but has declined to a third-line role over three seasons; his morale is rising on its own.

recommendations.summary: No changes to even-strength lines or power play units.
recommendations.rationale: L1 is a scoring line with speed (93 mean) and legitimate checking (75 mean). L2 balances offence and defence with Chlup's 79 faceoffs at centre. L3 is a second skill line built around Richards' 92 playmaking, and I have already recommended the shuffle once. P1 and P2 both carry speed above 87 and scoring above 83.

recommendations.summary: Put Tucker on the second penalty kill in place of Spezza or Upshall to raise K2's checking mean from 71 toward 76.
recommendations.rationale: K2's checking mean is 71 and toughness mean is 63, with Spezza and Upshall as the two weakest skaters carrying PK duty. Tucker is at 80 checking, our designated checking forward per the GM's January order, and is currently scratched. He belongs on the ice for kills.

recommendations.summary: The second PK unit is thin because our designated checking forwards (Tucker 80, Roberts 83) are scratched while depth players carry the kills.
recommendations.rationale: We have four forwards over 80 checking (Jackman 91, Roberts 83, Nash 81, Tucker 80) but only two are dressed. The roster has the depth; the lineup does not use it. This is a deployment problem, not a roster problem.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo. No fatigue flag showing, 95 OVR against a 2.30-goal offence.
recommendations.rationale: ATL scores 63 in 26 games. Luongo has no tired icon per the standing order. There is no reason to sit him.

recommendations.summary: No line changes for Atlanta. Our first line and first pair already match up correctly against their only dangerous unit.
recommendations.rationale: ATL's top line has Kovalchuk (86) and Heatley (85) behind a 70 OVR centre. Sundin at 92 with FACE 94 wins draws all night. Our second line (Chlup 87) faces their second line centre at 68. The gap is 19 points of OVR on every line. Their PP converts at 6.4% (7/110), so there is no shorthanded danger to structure against.

recommendations.summary: Trade Klesla at the deadline while his 87 OVR and rising 0.40 rate make the card attractive.
recommendations.rationale: Rate recovered from 0.29 in late November to 0.40 over 30 games. Expiring at $0.90M. Every game his value is more visible to a buyer and less useful to us next year.

recommendations.summary: Colaiacovo is the first defenceman to move at season's end: 0 goals and 0.12 pts/g in 25 games at $1.40M x 4.
recommendations.rationale: Confirmed over 25 games. The rate has not improved with volume. At 76 OVR and four years remaining the only question is whether a trade partner takes the contract.

recommendations.summary: Jackman stays. 0.67 pts/g in 30 games at $0.70M x 2 is well above the 0.55 sell trigger.
recommendations.rationale: Rate has been stable from 25 to 30 games. No reason to revisit the sell decision.

recommendations.summary: Dress Gaborik on the first line immediately; 98 speed and 92 playmaking on the bench is the biggest internal fix available.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik is 92 overall with the highest speed grade on the roster and second-highest playmaking grade. He is in no unit at 23 years old with 17 games of 0.47 pts/g production.

recommendations.summary: Build the fourth line from Koltsov (SPEE 92), Fischer (SPEE 89, CHKG 82) and Upshall (CHKG 80), all currently unlined.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach's fourth line totals 12 MPG against teams icing 15-minute units. Fischer and Koltsov are 'not lined' despite carrying 80+ grades in speed and checking. This gives the line real minutes and real roles.

recommendations.summary: Put Roberts (CHKG 86) or Tucker (CHKG 83) on K2 to raise the 71 checking mean; both are unlined.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach flags K2 at 71 checking with Klesla at 26 MPG doing double duty. Roberts at 39 with 98 durability is suited to short PK shifts; Tucker at 30 with 83 CHKG is the same fix with less remaining career.

recommendations.summary: Line Wallin (FACE 83) at third-line centre for faceoff duty; he is the only active player besides Sundin drawing above 80.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto have exactly two players at 80+ faceoffs: Sundin 90 and Wallin 83. Wallin is 'not lined'. Richards at 70 and Chlup at 75 are both below the 80 threshold the role demands.

recommendations.summary: No toughness acquisition needed; displayed TOUG has 11 players at 80+ as of December 4, and all prior targets remain closed.
recommendations.rationale: The base-grade picture (zero at 80+ TOUG) is a development concern, not a roster gap. The Dec 4 finding confirmed displayed toughness is adequate, and the GM closed Hartnell, Kurka and Jovanovski as targets.

recommendations.summary: Move Gaborik by March 2006 at any price above a fourth-round pick; his value is collapsing with every scratched game and $11.90M for four more years is the largest dead-money block on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: 8 pts in 17 GP at $11.90M, 13.2% of payroll. Mid-contract renegotiation is impossible. Even a below-market return clears $47.60M of committed salary through July 2010.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Luongo to a 5-6 year extension in July 2006; he expires at 26, POTE 97, on a $1.60M salary and walks for nothing otherwise.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo (26, POTE 97, 94 overall) and Chlup (19, POTE 95, 20 pts/28 GP) both expire July 2006. Lock Luongo first; Ouellet behind him is 81 base and also expiring.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Chlup to a 5-6 year extension in July 2006, same window as Luongo; he is 19 with POTE 95 and 20 points in 28 games on a $2.34M deal.
recommendations.rationale: At 19 he is the cheapest centre with that production in the league. Letting him hit the market after a breakout season at age 20 costs a first-round pick or a top prospect to match.

recommendations.summary: Begin the process of extending Richards two years early in July 2007 to break the 2009 cluster of eleven contracts worth $37.40M.
recommendations.rationale: Richards is the first name off the 2009 list ($6.70M, age 27 in 2007, POTE 88). Extending him early staggers the largest financial cliff in the dynasty.

recommendations.summary: Tucker at $1.30M expiring with 0 GP is the last movable chip at the deadline; his standing order as a tradeable asset remains open.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker (30, $1.30M, 1yr, 0 GP scratched) has zero role value and expiry value as a depth addition for a contender. The GM confirmed in March 2005 he was a chip; that status has not changed.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Luongo on a 5-year deal in July 2006; this is the single most important contract decision the club faces.
recommendations.rationale: He is at 95 overall, 91 base, 26 years old, and only 1 year remains. Without a new deal he walks and the backup is Ouellet at 81 base.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Chlup on a 5-year deal in July 2006 if the GM believes he is a top-six centre.
recommendations.rationale: He is 19, already holding a regular roster spot, and at $2.34M expiring. Locking five years now avoids a bidding war at 21 and pushes his expiry past the 2009 cluster.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Klesla on a 4- or 5-year deal in July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: He is 23, carries 26 MPG and double duty on PK units, and costs only $0.90M. This is exactly the cheap-young-playing profile the roster needs, and a long deal breaks the 2009 renewal cluster.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Ouellet on a 2-year deal as backup unless a 90+ goalie is acquired; decide by late February.
recommendations.rationale: The GM's standing order is that Ouellet alone is not enough as backup. At 24, $0.90M and 81 base he fills the role cheaply, and two years is the right term for a non-star.

recommendations.summary: Move Mogilny at the March deadline for a pick or a young player; do not renew at 36 and $5.50M.
recommendations.rationale: The coach does not mention him in the current report, which says he is not driving the lineup. His $5.50M is the single largest payroll item on the expiring list and the over-80 expiring mechanic should recover at least a pick.

recommendations.summary: Trade Tucker at the deadline in a package targeting a young top-six winger or centre; he qualifies for the over-80 expiring mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: He is 30, $1.30M expiring, and carries CHKG 81. The coach flags no functional fourth line and Tucker's skill set belongs elsewhere in the lineup we will actually run next season.

recommendations.summary: Trade Spezza at the deadline for a later-round pick unless the coach commits him to 10+ MPG before February.
recommendations.rationale: The coach reports 4 MPG and morale at 79, a negative spiral costing 2 points on every grade. At 22 and $1.00M he has trade value for a rebuilding club; he does not have development value sitting on the bench on a contender.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Koltsov on a 3-year deal if he holds a regular role by February; otherwise trade him at the deadline alongside Tucker.
recommendations.rationale: He is 24, $1.10M, and not flagged by the coach. Cheap young depth worth keeping if he plays, worth trading if he sits.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign St. Jacques on a 2-year deal if he earns a role; otherwise trade at the deadline for a late pick.
recommendations.rationale: He is 25, $0.80M, and not mentioned by the coach. If his ice time is minimal by February, he is a chip. If he earns minutes, renew cheap.

recommendations.summary: No trade negotiations open before late February; this is a December planning exercise.
recommendations.rationale: The GM's standing order from January 2005 holds: negotiations open in late February. We have 98 days. Targets are identified but talks wait.

recommendations.summary: Offer Tucker plus R1 to Atlanta for Heatley at the March deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Heatley is 91 overall_base at 22 on a $1.60M expiring deal for a 22-point club with league-lowest payroll ($40.34M) and six expiring players. He cannot be re-signed. He fills our top-six scoring gap directly.

recommendations.summary: If Atlanta refuses Heatley, pivot to Kovalchuk at 89 overall_base on the same expiring profile.
recommendations.rationale: Same club, same contract situation, age 22, 89 overall_base. Atlanta cannot re-sign both and likely cannot re-sign either. A club that sells one elite expiring 22-year-old will sell the second.

recommendations.summary: Offer Klesla plus R1 to Vancouver for Jovanovski.
recommendations.rationale: Only player in the league above 90 on both TOUG (93) and CHKG (94). 89 overall_base, $2.30M expiring, age 29. VAN at 30 points with 13 expiring and $46.36M payroll cannot re-sign him. Fills our penalty-kill and shutdown gap in one move.

recommendations.summary: Track Ottawa through January; if they fall below 20 points, inquire on Havlat or Hossa.
recommendations.rationale: Havlat has 26 pts/25 GP at 90 displayed, Hossa has 23 pts/25 GP at 89 overall_base. Both fill the top-six scoring gap. OTT at 24 pts with only 4 expiring is not yet selling, but a January collapse opens the door.

recommendations.summary: PHI at 28 points with 9 expiring is a sell profile; inquire on Lang if he is among the expiring.
recommendations.rationale: PHI have 9 expiring deals and only 28 points at $55.67M payroll with $23.50M profit. Their sell probability is high by February. Specific targets need confirmation once the January roster settles.

recommendations.summary: Offer Tucker alone for Savard; no draft pick needed.
recommendations.rationale: FACE 87, 79 overall_base, 19 pts/22 GP, $1.00M expiring, age 28. Closes our faceoff deficit (Richards at 70 FACE is the problem) at zero draft cost. ATL will not re-sign him on a $40.34M payroll.

recommendations.summary: Offer Koltsov plus R3 for Vasicek; cheaper than Savard and two years younger.
recommendations.rationale: 82 overall_base, FACE 80, 18 pts/22 GP, $0.40M expiring, age 25. CAR at 33 points with 14 expiring and $63.79M payroll must shed salary. Net saving of $0.70M versus Koltsov.

recommendations.summary: Offer Alexeev plus R2 for Hartnell as a developmental toughness piece.
recommendations.rationale: TOUG 91, CHKG 92, POTE 95, age 23, $1.10M expiring. BUF at 26 points with 5 expiring will not re-sign. Not a gap-fill (we have 11 players at 80+ displayed toughness) but a cheap upgrade to the fourth line.

recommendations.proposed: Dump to a bottom-feeding club (LA or CHI)
recommendations.summary: Explore a salary dump of Gaborik's $11.90M for a late pick plus a body before the March deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Scratched, 8 pts/17 GP, $11.90M = 13.2% of payroll. The Coach won't dress him. LA at 20 pts with $15.21M profit and 6 expiring could absorb him for development. Even a zero-return move frees the largest single obligation on the books for the Luongo renewal.

recommendations.summary: No trade needed for penalty-kill checking; Roberts (86 CHKG) and Tucker (83 CHKG) are on the roster and unlined.
recommendations.rationale: The coverage phase confirmed the checking depth exists; the problem is deployment. The Coach should line Roberts for PK minutes rather than requiring a trade.

recommendations.summary: Offer Tucker plus our first-round pick to Atlanta for Heatley; their 22-point rebuild cannot re-sign him and needs picks.
recommendations.rationale: Atlanta at 22 points with $40.34M league-lowest payroll and six expiring deals cannot retain Heatley at 91 base. A first-rounder plus a veteran body (Tucker, 92 CHKG) is a fair price for a rental. We gain a 22-year-old with a 91 base who directly fills the top-six winger hole the Gaborik scratch created. Net payroll +$0.30M.

recommendations.summary: Offer Koltsov plus our third-round pick to Atlanta for Savard; his FACE 87 closes the center faceoff gap at $1.00M.
recommendations.rationale: Savard is expiring on a club that will not re-sign him. Koltsov at 24 with ACCE 96 and POTE 94 is unused (0 GP this season) and better suited to a rebuilding club than one that already has Chlup, Richards, and Wallin at center. Third-rounder is a modest cost for a player producing 19 points in 22 games at FACE 87. Net payroll -$0.10M.

recommendations.proposed: Ed Jovanovski (VAN, 89 base, 29, TOUG 93, CHKG 94, $2.30M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Offer Klesla plus our second-round pick to Vancouver for Jovanovski; their 13 expiring deals mean he walks for nothing.
recommendations.rationale: Vancouver at 30 points with 13 expiring and $46.36M payroll must shed. Jovanovski at 29 is a rental they lose for nothing. Klesla at 23 with POTE 97 and speed 88 is a player they can keep or flip for a pick (expiring, potentially above 80). This is the shutdown-D answer the Coach's K2 at 71 checking mean demands. Net payroll +$1.40M, manageable against $36.12M profit.

recommendations.summary: If no deal lands before March, the roster already contains the answers: line Gaborik, run Koltsov-Fischer-Abid as the fourth line, deploy Roberts and Tucker on the PK.
recommendations.rationale: The coverage phase confirms these are deployment gaps, not personnel gaps. Gaborik at 92 overall with 98 speed is the top-six winger we lack, already on the roster. Koltsov (92 speed), Fischer (89 speed, 82 CHKG), and Abid (90 INJU) are three unused players who total 3.7 MPG between them.

recommendations.summary: Close the goalie trade-window monitoring task; Luongo is on the roster and the window is eight months past.
recommendations.rationale: The GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19. Luongo is at 95 overall with 1 year and $1.60M left. The live issue is his July 2006 renewal, not availability. DiPietro is not on the Islanders' roster and NYI at 33 points are not selling.

recommendations.summary: Luongo's 1-year contract ($1.60M, 95 overall) requires a 5-6 year extension in July 2006 or he walks.
recommendations.rationale: With 1 year remaining at $1.60M on a 95-overall goalie, this is the single most urgent contract on the roster. Without it the backup is Ouellet at 81 base.

recommendations.summary: Dress Gaborik over Upshall on the fourth line; his 0.47 pts/g at 22.6 MPG doubles Upshall's 0.21 at 5.5.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik has the best rate of the three RW options and gets elite minutes when he plays. Upshall at 0.21 pts/g and morale 82 is the same collapse pattern for a second straight season.

recommendations.summary: Scratch Gardener permanently; 0 points in 19 games at 3.2 MPG is not development.
recommendations.rationale: Already recommended December 8th and the GM took it, but he is still dressed. Zero production over 19 games confirms the young-forward collapse pattern.

recommendations.summary: Give Spacek a decision: dress him at 8+ MPG or stop carrying him entirely. Morale 76 is in the two-point tax band.
recommendations.rationale: He is 20 with POTE 91 and 0.50 pts/g in 6 games, but 5.8 MPG and morale 76 mean the underuse is now actively costing him on-ice quality.

recommendations.summary: Leave Spezza as is; 4.8 MPG on the fourth line is no worse than scratching him, and his season is already a write-off for development.
recommendations.rationale: Second consecutive season at 0.18-0.21 pts/g with no grade movement. The development window has passed; the only real decision is an offseason role reset, not a mid-season change.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev has fallen below the 0.45 pts/g threshold at 21 games (now 0.35). His dressing recommendation weakens; reassess at 25 games as a final window.
recommendations.rationale: Rate fell from 0.40 at 15 games to 0.35 at 21 on 10.9 MPG. He is 23 and declining on steady ice. The development case is closing.

recommendations.summary: Flag Jackman's rate at 0.59 pts/g (sell trigger 0.55). If he drops below 0.55 in the next assessment he goes back on the sell list.
recommendations.rationale: Nov 13th he was 0.88 over 16 games. Now 0.59 over 28. The hot start is regressing. Four points below the trigger.

recommendations.summary: Spezza, Upshall and Gardener are confirmed write-offs this season. All three must get a real camp audition next offseason or stop being dressed.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza 0.18 pts/g on 4.8 MPG over 22 games. Upshall 0.17 on 4.9 over 19. Gardener 0 points in 19 on 2.5 MPG. All confirm the minutes-collapse pattern. No in-season fix exists.

recommendations.summary: Chlup at 0.70 pts/g on 21.5 MPG at 19, Nash at 0.56 on 15.6 MPG at 21, and Chistov at 0.59 on 20.5 MPG at 22 are all developing on track. No change.
recommendations.rationale: Three young players earning top-six minutes through production. The development pipeline is working where talent exists.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker and put him on K2 in place of the weakest checking forward on the unit.
recommendations.rationale: K2 carries 72 mean checking and 64 toughness, eight points below the functional floor for a kill unit. Tucker at 81 checking is the only available upgrade and directly addresses the gap.

recommendations.summary: Put Tucker on L3 as the forward checker to raise its mean checking from 71 toward 74.
recommendations.rationale: L3 has 71 checking and 63 toughness, too soft to match opposing second lines. Tucker's 81 checking and 81 role-grade give the line physical presence without disrupting Richards' playmaking role.

recommendations.summary: We need a third player above 80 checking on the active roster; Jackman and Nash are the only two we have.
recommendations.rationale: The full 31-man roster holds Jackman at 92, Nash at 82, Tucker at 81, and Roberts at 84. With Tucker and Roberts scratched we run one checker per two lines, which makes K2 permanently fragile. This is a roster problem the lineup cannot solve.

recommendations.slot: first and second lines, both power plays
recommendations.summary: L1, L2, P1 and P2 are correctly built. Leave them alone.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has scoring (90 mean), speed (94) and clutch (73 with Sundin at 99). L2 is balanced with Nash anchoring at 82 checking. Both PPs have a faceoff taker and speed. No structural flaw to fix.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes for Philadelphia; every auto-paired matchup favours Toronto.
recommendations.rationale: We are 17-7-0 vs their 10-11-2, 2-0-0 in the season series, and our centre beats theirs on every line (Sundin 92 vs Handzus 79, Chlup 87 vs Roenick 84, Richards 87 vs Primeau 79). The D pair slot order is already correct; swapping D2 and D3 would put St. Jacques (66) against Roenick, which is worse.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon before confirming per the standing order.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 95 OVR faces Esche at 74. PHI averages 2.80 goals a game and Esche's 74 is beatable. If Luongo shows the tired icon, Ouellet takes it.

recommendations.summary: Monitor Jackman's rate daily; at 0.61 he is 0.06 from the 0.55 sell trigger. If he crosses before the deadline, move him while 86 OVR is still on the card.
recommendations.rationale: Zero points in the last three games, rate dropped from 0.68 to 0.61 in one week. If the decline continues, the 86 grade and $0.70M salary are the last attractive features and a buyer will stop calling once the rate shows on the screen.

recommendations.summary: Priority sell candidate at season end: 0.12 pts/g, 76 OVR, $1.40M x 4. Most expensive dead weight on the blue line.
recommendations.rationale: Zero points in his last three games, now 3 in 25. Four years of $1.40M for a 76 is a cap problem that compounds. He is already not dressed.

recommendations.summary: Still in the sell window: 87 OVR, $0.90M expiring, 0.36 rate unchanged since November. Move before the grade drops.
recommendations.rationale: Rate holding at 0.36, not recovering above 0.40 or falling below 0.30. The card value is the OVR grade and it will not stay at 87 forever.

recommendations.summary: Insert Fischer (82 CHKG, 89 SPEE, 92 INJU) onto L4 to raise that unit's checking mean from 70 toward 78.
recommendations.rationale: Coach already flagged Fischer for Tuesday; he's the only 80+ checker available who isn't a trade chip or a top-pair D.

recommendations.summary: Dress Wallin (83 FACE) on L3 or L4 to give the lineup a second 80+ faceoff draw-taker alongside Sundin (90).
recommendations.rationale: Only Sundin clears 80 FACE among lined players. Wallin sits unlined at 83 and costs nothing.

recommendations.summary: Bell remains the only external player who closes the faceoff depth gap (88 FACE per Nov 26 reading) at $0.90M expiring with no draft cost beyond Tucker + St. Jacques + R3.
recommendations.rationale: Wallin at 83 fixes one line; Bell at 88 fixes faceoff coverage at the level the Coach wants and adds 82 TOUG as a bonus. The GM has not closed this target.

recommendations.summary: Coach's verdict stands: Spezza (POTE 99, 0.21 pts/g on 4.6 MPG in 19 GP) needs 12+ minutes or stops being dressed; the roster lacks a centre who is both young and capable enough to absorb a real role without him.
recommendations.rationale: Richards (85 PASS, 90 ENDU) holds the slot; no internal alternative exists who isn't already playing. If Spezza isn't ready by February, he's trade bait for the Heatley package.

recommendations.summary: No toughness acquisition; GM closed this on December 4 based on displayed grades.
recommendations.rationale: Standing order accepted. The shipped-grade gap (0 at 80+ TOUG) is noted but not actionable per the GM's ruling.

recommendations.summary: Trade Gaborik before the March deadline; his $11.90M/year through 2010 is the single largest structural threat to every renewal summer ahead.
recommendations.rationale: At 23 with POTE 90 and 8 pts/17 GP he still has trade value, but it decays each undressed month. Mid-contract renegotiation is impossible. If he is still here in March he becomes a fire-sale piece, and if he is still here in July he is $47.60M of dead money through 2010.

recommendations.summary: Lock Chlup, Luongo and Spezza on 5-6 year deals in July 2006 before any other renewal business; these three are the franchise spine.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup is 19 with POTE 95 and 20 points in 27 GP at $2.34M. Luongo is 26 with POTE 97 at $1.60M and the backup is Tellqvist at POTE 91. Spezza is 22 with POTE 99 on $1.00M. All three expire simultaneously in July 2006 and all three are irreplaceable. Even doubling their combined salary from $4.94M to $10M is affordable against $35.56M profit.

recommendations.summary: Extend Richards, Chistov and Nash one year early in July 2007 to pull them out of the $37.40M cluster of eleven contracts expiring together in 2009.
recommendations.rationale: Eleven players on four-year deals worth $37.40M all come up in July 2009 simultaneously. Richards (25, POTE 88, $6.70M), Chistov (22, POTE 95, $5.00M), and Nash (21, POTE 95, $3.90M) are certain keeps whose early extension costs one year of escalation but prevents a renewal summer where you must re-sign eleven men at once.

recommendations.summary: Move Mogilny (36, $5.50M expiring, 16 pts/27 GP) at the deadline for a mid-round pick plus a cheap young player.
recommendations.rationale: He is the roster's largest single salary, 36 years old, and expiring. Rental value is highest in February and March; he walks for zero in July.

recommendations.summary: Tucker ($1.30M expiring, 30) funds the deadline acquisition the coach needs: a checker above 80 on both toughness and checking.
recommendations.rationale: Already designated a chip by the GM on March 19 2005. Hartnell has TOUG 91/CHKG 92/POTE 95 at 23; Savard has FACE 87 at 28. Both are expiring on non-contenders.

recommendations.summary: Koltsov ($1.10M expiring, 24, below coach's 0.45 pts/g threshold) packages with St. Jacques or a 4th for Savard's FACE 87.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 16 points with second-lowest payroll cannot re-sign Savard. They get a cheap wing and depth D; we get the L3 faceoff fix.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Chlup (19, 82 base, FACE 80, $2.34M) on 5-6 years at first contract opportunity.
recommendations.rationale: He is a 19-year-old franchise center whose entry contract expires this season. Stars on 5-6 years; missing this is the worst mistake available to us.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Luongo (26, $1.60M) on 5 years.
recommendations.rationale: GM closed the goalie file on March 19 2005: 'Goalies are solved. Done.' Renew and do not revisit.

recommendations.summary: Renew Spezza (22, POTE 99, $1.00M) on 5 years in the summer, contingent on him receiving 12+ MPG before February.
recommendations.rationale: Coach says 4.6 MPG in 19 games at POTE 99 is wasted development. If he gets the role and performs, lock him. If still scratching, become a development trader.

recommendations.summary: Renew Ouellet (24, $0.90M, 8 GP) on 2 years as Luongo's backup.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is gone. Ouellet is the only playoff backup. Cheap and adequate.

recommendations.proposed: Klesla as chip or Klesla as keeper — decision at February
recommendations.summary: Decide Klesla's future (23, D, POTE 97, $0.90M expiring) by late February: renew as long-term defenseman or trade as the best defense chip we own.
recommendations.rationale: GM protected Eminger and McCabe specifically on Feb 19 2005; Klesla was not named. His POTE 97 makes him the only piece that can fetch a top-pairing defender. Keeping him as a 3rd-pairing 23-year-old wastes his value.

recommendations.summary: Let St. Jacques (25, D, $0.80M, 0 pts/9 GP) walk in July or renew at $0.70M for one year as pure depth.
recommendations.rationale: No production, minimal ice time, replaceable. Include him in a deadline package if it helps close a deal; otherwise irrelevant.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Heatley (ATL) as the primary deadline target; 91 base, 22 years old, $1.10M expiring, 23 pts in 25 GP on the league's lowest-payroll club at 20 points.
recommendations.rationale: Fills the Gaborik RW slot at a ninth the salary. ATL hold Heatley, Kovalchuk and Savard on expiring deals at a combined $3.20M and cannot re-sign all three at $40.34M payroll and 20 points. They are the most motivated seller in the league.

recommendations.summary: Alternative ATL target if Heatley is not available; 89 base, 22, $1.10M expiring, 27 pts in 25 GP leads the club.
recommendations.rationale: Same ATL seller logic. 27 points in 25 games at SPEE 99 is the highest scorer on any expiring deal in the league. If ATL will deal both, take Heatley because RW is the broken slot; take Kovalchuk if ATL prices Heatley beyond what we can offer.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Savard (ATL) to close the faceoff gap; FACE 87 with 21 pts in 25 GP at $1.00M expiring. Tucker alone is a plausible package.
recommendations.rationale: Only Sundin (FACE 90) clears 80 among lined players. Wallin at FACE 83 closes the internal gap but 87 is a real upgrade for a playoff series. ATL at 20 points with 6 expiring must move him. Tucker is the GM's declared chip and is 30 with 83 CHKG, an expiring asset of similar value.

recommendations.summary: Monitor Havlat (OTT) through January; 87 base at $0.90M expiring with 25 pts in 24 GP is the best value on the board if OTT drifts.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 23 points in 23 games with $59.27M payroll and $20.23M profit are not yet a seller. But his salary at renewal triples and they carry only 4 expiring. Ask in February; if OTT falls below .450 they may prefer picks to a $3-4M commitment to a 23-year-old.

recommendations.summary: Track Bouwmeester (FLA, 22, 81 base, POTE 96, 33.0 MPG, $1.20M expiring) as the July target if FLA sell.
recommendations.rationale: Franchise-D profile at 22 with 33 minutes a night. FLA at 27 points and $57.33M payroll are not desperate sellers now, but 5 expiring and other youth on the back end could push them to move him. Monitor their record through February.

recommendations.summary: Drury (BUF, 25, 89 base, FACE 81, 23 pts in 25 GP, $2.00M expiring) fills faceoff and scoring simultaneously; ask in February if BUF fall below .450.
recommendations.rationale: Unique profile: 89 base scorer with 81 FACE at age 25. BUF at 24 points with 5 expiring are not yet clear sellers, making this less likely than the ATL targets. Worth an inquiry because no other player in the league combines faceoffs above 80 with base above 85.

recommendations.summary: Keep Hartnell (BUF, 23, CHKG 90, POTE 95, $1.10M expiring) on the board as insurance if Fischer's internal fix does not hold by February.
recommendations.rationale: Coverage phase says Fischer (82 CHKG) closes L4 internally. Hartnell at CHKG 90 and POTE 95 is the upgrade if Fischer struggles or is injured. 9 pts in 25 GP at 18.1 MPG is below-average production for a 23-year-old but the checking grades are the reason to watch, not the scoring.

recommendations.summary: Doan falls off the target board: CHKG fell from 91 to 85, displayed overall is 79, production is 14 pts in 20 GP, and $2.40M does not match the return.
recommendations.rationale: October note had him at 86 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 87 base as a top target. The November decay finding shows his grades have slipped. PHX at 19 points with 9 expiring are a clear seller, but the price-to-production ratio is no longer compelling when Heatley and Kovalchuk are at $1.10M each.

recommendations.proposed: Dany Heatley (ATL, RW, 22, 91 base, $1.10M expiring, 23 pts/25 GP)
recommendations.summary: Offer Tucker plus the first-round pick for Heatley; he fills the RW slot at a ninth of Gaborik's salary and is re-signable in July as a franchise piece.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 20 points with $40.34M payroll (league lowest) and six expiring deals cannot re-sign Heatley, Kovalchuk, and Savard. Tucker gives them a body for 30 games or a rental asset to flip, and the R1 is the future value a rebuilding GM prices highest. Net payroll saves $0.20M. Acceptance uncertain: ATL may want a younger player than Tucker alongside the pick.

recommendations.proposed: Martin Savard (ATL, C, 28, 79 base, FACE 87, $1.00M expiring, 21 pts/25 GP)
recommendations.summary: Offer Koltsov plus St. Jacques for Savard at zero draft cost; he gives a second 80+ faceoff man and 21 points without spending Tucker or a pick.
recommendations.rationale: Savard's FACE 87 and 21 points make him a legitimate 2C, not a specialist. Koltsov ($1.10M, 0 GP, expiring) and St. Jacques ($0.80M, 0 GP, expiring) give ATL two expiring bodies to use or release, no commitment past June. Net payroll saves $0.90M. ATL may want a late pick as sweetener. Faceoffs are solvable internally with Wallin (FACE 83) so this is insurance, not necessity.

recommendations.proposed: Ilya Kovalchuk (ATL, LW, 22, 89 base, $1.10M expiring, 27 pts/25 GP)
