recommendations.rationale: Jovanovski at 29, 89 base, 93 TOUG, 94 CHKG, $2.30M expiring. VAN carry 13 expiring and the league-lowest payroll at $46.36M. Klesla is 23, $0.90M — exactly the youth a selling club rebuilds with.

recommendations.summary: Test Mogilny's trade value in February to trigger the over-80 expiring pick-recovery mechanic before he walks at zero return.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny is 36, $5.50M, expiring. The December 2004 package that included him never executed. At 36 each month costs him value; if his overall is above 80 the mechanic works. If below, he is a July salary-dump loss either way.

recommendations.summary: Lock Chlup on 5-6 years the first week of July. 19 years old, 1.25 pts/g at 23.5 MPG, $2.34M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: He is the best player on the roster and the one every club will try to sign away in July. Stars get 5-6 year deals per the manual; yearly renewals ratchet his demands.

recommendations.summary: Lock Luongo on 5-6 years the same week as Chlup. 26, $1.60M expiring, 90+ base.
recommendations.rationale: GM confirmed Luongo as the future number one on 2005-03-19. Goalies walk easily if unmonitored. Renew first if possible because the backup (Tellqvist) is a clear step down.

recommendations.summary: Decide Spezza's status by mid-November: dress him at L3C or move him before his value evaporates.
recommendations.rationale: Coach's five-game clock has expired. POTE 99, morale 88, $1.00M expiring. If undressed through November, his trade value drops toward zero and we lose a top-potential asset for nothing. GM must force the decision.

recommendations.summary: No salary dumping is needed at 5-1-0. Keep the rotation and let revenue cover the payroll.
recommendations.rationale: The GM's Oct 16 question answered: at first place with 76 games left, keeping $1-2M depth players costs nothing we need back. The only payroll events are Mogilny ($5.50M walking) and the contracts we renew. There is no cap.

recommendations.current: Spezza (C, 22, POTE 99, $1.00M expiring) + Koltsov (LW, 24, POTE 94, $1.10M expiring) + 1st-round pick (TOR)
recommendations.summary: Send Spezza, Koltsov and our first-rounder to Atlanta for Dany Heatley. Both incoming players are 0-GP healthy scratches whose trade value decays every week on the bench.
recommendations.rationale: ATL are 1-3-0 with 2 points and hold both Heatley (91 base) and Kovalchuk (89 base) on expiring deals they cannot both re-sign. Heatley is the older asset and the one they will move. A POTE 99 center, a POTE 94 winger, and a first-rounder for a player they lose for free in July is a rebuild package they should accept. Salary: ATL gain $2.10M and shed $1.10M (net +$1.00M against $17.79M profit, manageable). TOR shed $2.10M and add $1.10M (net -$1.00M). Both incoming TOR players have zero games and zero role; Spezza's coach deadline expired at 5 GP.

recommendations.current: Abid (LW, 25, POTE 94, $1.30M x4, INJU 90, TOUG 80) + 2nd-round pick (TOR)
recommendations.proposed: Stuart (D, 25, 87 base, 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG, POTE 91, $1.80M expiring) from SJ
recommendations.summary: Package Abid and our second-rounder to San Jose for Brad Stuart. He is a 25-year-old top-four defenseman with real toughness who fixes the gap for years, not one season.
recommendations.rationale: SJ carry $66.24M payroll (highest among the four seller targets) against 13,558 attendance and hold 13+ expiring contracts. They are shedding salary. Abid at 25, POTE 94, INJU 90, TOUG 80 is a similar physical profile to Stuart but without the NHL track record. San Jose get a cheap POTE 94 asset plus a second-rounder for a player they will lose at expiry for nothing. TOR net +$0.50M in salary but gain 87 base and 89 CHKG on a player eight years younger than Roberts.

recommendations.current: St. Jacques (D, 25, $0.80M expiring, CHKG 84) + Tucker (LW, 30, $1.30M expiring, CHKG 92, TOUG 88) + 3rd-round pick (TOR)
recommendations.proposed: Bell (LW, 25, 80 base, 88 TOUG, 82 FACE, $0.90M expiring) from CHI
recommendations.summary: Send Tucker, St. Jacques and our third-rounder to Chicago for Mark Bell. He closes the TOUG gap (88) and the faceoff gap (82) in one player, and we shed $1.20M in salary.
recommendations.rationale: CHI are 1-1-1, 3 points in 3 games, with 13 expiring contracts and $23.35M profit. They are not contending. Bell at 80 base is a rental for them too. Two checking wings (CHKG 84 and 92) plus a third-rounder for an expiring 80-base winger is fair value: Chicago get depth for now and a pick for later. Tucker is the GM's designated chip from March 19. St. Jacques has zero games and is expiring. Net salary: TOR -$1.20M. Bell must be re-signed in July to retain him beyond this season.

recommendations.summary: If none of these three land before the deadline, do not force a fourth package. Dress Spezza at fourth-line centre and Alexeev on the wing, develop toughness through Nash and Jackman, and reassess the market in February with fresher data and picks that have aged past the ten-game trade lock.
recommendations.rationale: The 1st-round pick is our only high-value asset; spending it on a marginal fit is worse than holding it for February when ATL, VAN and SJ have a full record to sell from. The internal fix (lining McCabe, Tucker, Wallin) addresses the checking and faceoff thinness without any move.

recommendations.summary: Lock Luongo on a 5-6 year deal in July 2006 before he tests the market on a $1.60M expiring deal at age 26 with a 97 overall.
recommendations.rationale: He is 97 overall, 26, and carries only 1 year at $1.60M. Every contender in the league would trade for him. The renewal window is the single highest-priority contract on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Move Chlup to first-line centre; 8 points in 6 games at 19 is a first-line rate.
recommendations.rationale: 1.33 pts/g on 19.8 MPG at age 19 is outperforming the current first-line setup where Gaborik has 1 point in 5 games. Chlup belongs on the top line.

recommendations.summary: Spezza and Eminger have zero games; the GM needs to tell me whether they are part of the plan or not.
recommendations.rationale: Two players with the highest potential grade on the roster, 22 and 21, both healthy, both scratched every game. No development is happening for them and I have no explanation in front of me for why.

recommendations.summary: Spacek, Gardener and Upshall stay on the fourth line despite morale at 76.
recommendations.rationale: Their current grades put them on the fourth line and their minutes reflect that. Spacek and Upshall each have 3 points in 6 games on 5.8 MPG, which is reasonable production at that role. Morale will recover with wins.

recommendations.summary: Move Chlup to first-line centre; he is already getting 22.6 MPG and 1.40 pts/g at 19, the slot should match the role.
recommendations.rationale: GM has given Chlup first-line minutes but not the first-line slot. 1.40 pts/g over 6 games at age 19 on 22.6 MPG is the best production-to-age ratio on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Spacek, Upshall and Gardener have collapsed to under 4 MPG; either give them a real role or stop dressing them so they can play elsewhere.
recommendations.rationale: Spacek fell from 17.0 to 3.6 MPG, Upshall from 16.0 to 3.8, Gardener from 16.0 to 2.2. At 20-22 with POTE above 85 all three, benching them without a path back wastes their development window.

recommendations.summary: Fischer's emergence at 0.80 pts/g on 21.8 MPG is the D-load redistribution working; leave the pairing order alone.
recommendations.rationale: Jackman dropped from 41.0 to 25.2 MPG and Klesla from 42.0 to 23.6. Fischer, Kaberle, Colaiacovo and Stahle absorbed the load. The October 13 endurance concern is being addressed by the current allocation.

recommendations.summary: Move Richards up to the second line to bring his minutes toward 17 MPG; his morale at 78 on 11.8 MPG is the lowest among dressed players and costs two points off every grade in the 70s band.
recommendations.rationale: Richards is a 25-year-old centre with prior first-line experience getting only 11.8 MPG on the third line. His morale dropped 13 points and has held at 78 across multiple saves, indicating a sustained minutes deficit rather than a results dip. Against a quality opponent like Boston, putting him alongside Chlup and Chistov raises both his minutes and our second-line quality.

recommendations.summary: Leave the fourth line (Upshall, Spacek, Gardener) at 76 morale despite low minutes; this is the GM's development rotation and their production (3 points in 6 games each) justifies the plan.
recommendations.rationale: All three are at 76, the floor of the 70s band where morale costs two points off grades. Upshall and Spacek are producing at 0.50 pts/g on minimal ice. The GM's standing order prioritizes development minutes for young players in games we can manage, and these three are exactly that. Revisit if any drops below 72.

recommendations.summary: Unit compositions are correct given the roster; the checking shortage is a depth problem, not an arrangement one.
recommendations.rationale: L3 at checking mean 76 (Roberts 84, Nash 82) is our best shutdown unit and belongs there. K1 with Jackman (92) is the right use of our only elite checking defender. K2 at mean 71 is thin but no better personnel exists on the roster to swap in without breaking L1 or K1.

recommendations.summary: We need a second defence pair with 80+ checking to staff K2 without relying on a scratched McCabe.
recommendations.rationale: K2 checking mean is 71; Klesla (86) and Spacek (84) carry it while Kaberle and Upshall drag it down. McCabe at 83 checking and 83 stamina is the only rostered D who could raise it, and he is currently a scratch. If McCabe stays scratched, K2 will concede high-danger chances all season.

recommendations.summary: Play the same lines. Auto-pairing puts our depth against their thinness on L3 and L4, and our L1 handles Thornton without shuffling.
recommendations.rationale: TOR L3 (Richards 86, Nash 85, Roberts 85) vs BOS L3 (Vernarsky 74, Zamuner 72, McInnis 71) is a ten-point gap. Luongo at 97 vs Raycroft at 85 is the single biggest talent edge in the building. We are 5-1-0 at 1.67 GA/game; they are 2-1-1 at 2.75. No matchup adjustment improves on what the slot order already gives us.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming per January 19 order.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 97 OVR is 12 points ahead of Raycroft at 85 and has the edge on every displayed grade. His morale is 91, no fatigue flag visible in the brief. Confirm on screen before puck drop per the standing order.

recommendations.summary: Trade Jackman now while his 0.83 pts/g rate is still above his 0.48 career average; the window is narrowing as he regresses.
recommendations.rationale: His rate was 1.00 at 4 games, now 0.83 at 6. Each game brings him closer to the career mean a buyer won't pay for. At $0.70M x 2 years he's the cheapest 27-MPG defenceman available.

recommendations.summary: No move on Klesla yet; he's the second sell candidate if Jackman goes, but the blue line can't lose both top-pair minutes in one window.
recommendations.rationale: 26.7 MPG, 87 OVR, age 23, expiring at $0.90M. His value peaks now but he's needed. Re-evaluate after Jackman is dealt.

recommendations.summary: No change to the D pairing structure for BOS; the minute spread has improved to 46% top-pair concentration from 56% at game 4.
recommendations.rationale: Endurance concern from October 13 is easing. Fischer at 19.8 MPG and Kaberle at 19.5 are absorbing their share properly.

recommendations.summary: Line McCabe (86 CHKG, 94 ENDU, 30) into a regular defensive role; he is rostered, unlined, and directly answers the Coach's checking complaint.
recommendations.rationale: McCabe is 86 CHKG and 94 ENDU and in no unit. The Coach's standing flag is 'no forward who combines 75+ checking with enough skill to hold a third-line role' — McCabe is the answer already on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker (83 CHKG, 30, $1.30M) as the nightly checking presence the roster lacks below the top two lines.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker carries 83 CHKG and is unlined. The Coach flagged this gap in April and it persists. He is the internal floor for the checking void.

recommendations.summary: Give Wallin (83 FACE, 25) a regular centre spot on the third line to fix the faceoff void outside Sundin.
recommendations.rationale: Wallin is the only player on the roster above 80 FACE besides Sundin (90). He is currently unlined. Every other centre reads 75 or below on the draw.

recommendations.slot: fourth line wing or power play
recommendations.summary: Dress Koltsov (92 SPEE, 24) on the fourth line or a power-play unit; he is rostered, unlined, and the third-fastest skater on the club.
recommendations.rationale: Koltsov at 92 speed and 24 is the best unused forward on the roster. He costs nothing to deploy and adds a speed dimension the bottom six currently lack.

recommendations.summary: Bell (CHI, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, 24) is the only player in the league closing toughness, checking, and faceoff gaps simultaneously; maintain as primary February target.
recommendations.rationale: Toughness gap (0 at 80+ displayed) is unfixable internally. Bell is 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE at 24 on a cheap deal. CHI remain motivated sellers at 73+ points with many expirings. Package cost remains Tucker plus 4th-rounder as sweeteners, which is insufficient alone — need a larger chip.

recommendations.summary: Scoring depth at 80+ (11 forwards) and speed depth (25 at 80+) mean no acquisition is needed in those areas this season.
recommendations.rationale: Eleven players read 80+ in scoring, twelve in stamina, nine in clutch. The roster is top-heavy on skill and bottom-heavy on grit; only the grit side requires external help.

recommendations.summary: Lock Chlup on a 5-6 year deal the first week of July 2006; his $2.34M one-year contract expires before his second full season.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup is 19, POTE 95, producing 6 points in 5 games as first-line centre. He is the franchise center and he is expiring. If he takes a step this season his asking price triples. The existing memory already flags this as simultaneous with Luongo.

recommendations.summary: Lock Luongo on a 5-6 year deal the same week as Chlup in July 2006; his $1.60M contract expires with Tellqvist (91 POTE) as the clear step down behind him.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 26, 97 POTE, 3 wins in 3 starts is the franchise goalie. Tellqvist at 91 POTE is not an adequate backup for a Cup window. Losing Luongo mid-summer would force a trade from a position of weakness.

recommendations.summary: Trade Klesla plus the R2 pick to Vancouver for Jovanovski at the February 2006 deadline; Klesla is expiring at $0.90M regardless.
recommendations.rationale: Jovanovski at 89 base, 93 TOUG, 94 CHKG fills the toughness gap since April. VAN have 13 expiring contracts and the league's lowest payroll ($46.36M), so they want a 23-year-old POTE 97 D. Klesla costs nothing to move because he walks in July.

recommendations.summary: If Gaborik's production stays below 0.40 pts/g after 10 games, make him available at the February deadline before his fourth more year of $11.90M poisons every future extension.
recommendations.rationale: He has 1 point in 4 games on $11.90M (13% of payroll). The Coach already demanded a roster-or-trade decision by mid-October. Every game he plays below replacement level lowers his trade value further; the existing note says it evaporates by January.

recommendations.summary: Do not add long-term salary before the July 2006 renewal window; profit of $33.95M is comfortable but the 2009 cluster of $37.40M across 11 players will require headroom.
recommendations.rationale: The $89.94M payroll against $47.76M ticket revenue is covered by TV, prestige and playoff bonuses producing $33.95M profit. Adding another $5-6M long-term now (e.g. Iginla re-sign) before the Chlup/Luongo extensions are set reduces flexibility for the renewal queue that arrives in nine months.

recommendations.summary: Move Mogilny at the deadline (late February negotiations) for a first-round pick or high-potential young player; he is 36, $5.50M, and the over-80 expiring mechanic guarantees pick value even without a team needing him.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny is the highest-paid player on a $89.94M payroll at 36 years old with 3 points in 5 games. No future version of this roster includes him at this cost. The deadline is 152 days away; open talks in late February per the GM's standing order.

recommendations.summary: Trade Tucker at the deadline if he remains unlined; 30 years old, 79 base, POTE 80, was already a chip last March and carries no developmental case.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker is rostered but unlined per the Oct 16 Coach report. At 30 with capped potential and $1.30M, his only remaining value is as a salary-matching piece or the over-80 pick mechanic. If still unlined in February, he goes.

recommendations.summary: Spezza's contract fate depends entirely on whether he plays before the Coach's deadline: if undressed past five games, trade him in February; if he produces, renew 5 years.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza is 22, POTE 98, 73 base, $1.00M expiring, and has played 0 games in two consecutive seasons. The Coach demands a decision in five games. His trade value as a 98-potential 22-year-old is real even at 73 base; it evaporates if he stays a healthy scratch through February.

recommendations.summary: Lock Luongo on 5-6 years immediately upon contract expiry; he is 26, 91 base, POTE 98, at $1.60M and the clear number one.
recommendations.rationale: Three starts this season, 179 minutes. POTE 98 at 26 means he is still improving. His current $1.60M will not survive free agency. Same week as Chlup per the July 2006 renewal plan.

recommendations.summary: Lock Chlup on 5-6 years at renewal; 19 years old, 82 base, POTE 96, 6 points in 5 games at first-line centre, currently $2.34M.
recommendations.rationale: He is the franchise centre at 19 and already producing at 1.2 points per game. His salary will rise at renewal; term matters more than the figure. Renew the same week as Luongo.

recommendations.summary: Lock Klesla on 5-6 years at renewal; 23 years old, 78 base, POTE 98, $0.90M, already playing 27 minutes per game.
recommendations.rationale: The gap between his 78 base and his 98 potential is the largest on the roster. His current $0.90M is absurd for a top-pairing 23-year-old. Lock him before the gap closes and his price doubles.

recommendations.summary: Renew Koltsov on 3 years; 24, 68 base, POTE 95, $1.10M. Three years tests the potential without overcommitting at his current 68 overall.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 95 at 24 is a late developer's profile. At 68 base he is still a fourth-liner. Three years at a modest raise is the right risk if he does not break through quickly.

recommendations.summary: Keep Ouellet as depth goalie through the season; reassess at renewal whether he stays as Luongo's backup or becomes trade capital. 24, 81 base, POTE 98, $0.90M.
recommendations.rationale: The GM's standing order from Jan 15 2005 was to develop young goalies. Ouellet at 24 with POTE 98 fits that profile. With Luongo locked long-term, Ouellet is insurance or a component in a future goalie package.

recommendations.summary: Offer St. Jacques a 2-year deal at $0.80M or release; at 25 with 66 base overall, the POTE 95 has not translated into NHL-quality grades.
recommendations.rationale: 66 overall at 25 means this player has not developed despite the high potential reading. A cheap two-year deal tests whether the 95 potential has any path to 75+ overall. If not, release.

recommendations.summary: The ATL binary (Heatley 89 base / Kovalchuk at 91 base, both 25, both expiring) is the February deadline priority; either one solves the Coach's toughness gap and the scoring bridge simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: ATL have 2 points and 9 expiring contracts; they cannot re-sign both. The one who moves solves both the zero-80-toughness-forward gap and the scoring void left by Mogilny's departure. Fund with Mogilny's pick value and possibly Tucker.

recommendations.summary: Do not open any trade negotiations before late February. The deadline is 152 days away; per the GM's standing order, January and most of February are for watching, not calling.
recommendations.rationale: GM's Jan 15 2005 position: trade negotiations should not open until late February. This season follows the same calendar.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Jovanovski in February for Klesla plus R2; he closes the D-side checking depth gap and VAN are the league's most motivated sellers at 10 expiring and $46.36M payroll.
recommendations.rationale: VAN carry 10 expiring contracts from 30 rostered, the lowest payroll in the league, and are rebuilding. Klesla (23, POTE 97, $0.90M expiring) is the currency that costs nothing we want to keep. Confirmed October 12 and the structural picture is unchanged.

recommendations.proposed: Bell (CHI, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, $900K, 2 years left)
recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell in February for Colaiacovo plus R2 or Klesla plus R2; he is the only forward in the league who closes the 80+ toughness gap on a controllable 2-year deal at $900K.
recommendations.rationale: CHI carry 10 expiring contracts out of 30 at $50.12M payroll, making them a structural seller. Bell at 24 with 2 years left and $900K salary is the cheapest long-term answer to the toughness gap the Coach has flagged since April. The January veto was about faceoff logic for a wing; the toughness argument stands.

recommendations.proposed: Heatley or Kovalchuk (ATL, whichever is traded)
recommendations.summary: Track the ATL binary through January; whichever winger ATL does not re-sign becomes our primary February scoring target because both carry 82+ TOUG and 89-91 base.
recommendations.rationale: ATL have 9 expiring contracts, $39.13M payroll (second lowest), and at 1-2-0 cannot re-sign both Heatley (91 base, 24) and Kovalchuk (89 base, 21). The one who moves solves the scoring bridge and toughness gaps simultaneously.

recommendations.summary: Target Cammalleri as a July 2006 UFA signing; LA carry 12 expiring contracts and cannot retain him, and at 22 with POTE 98 he is the highest-upside available forward.
recommendations.rationale: LA have 12 expiring out of 31 rostered at $50.80M payroll. Cammalleri produced 60 points in 61 games last season and is expiring. This is a July target, not a February one, because LA will likely hold him to the deadline rather than trade an asset they are losing.

recommendations.summary: Avery is the cheapest 3-gaps-closed option at $400K on a 2-year deal; pursue only if McCabe and Tucker lined internally fail to address the checking gap by late January.
recommendations.rationale: His production (6 pts/57 GP last season) means he fills a role, not a line. LA are sellers at 12 expiring. The internal fix (McCabe 86 CHKG, Tucker 83 CHKG lined) should come first; Avery is the insurance policy.

recommendations.summary: Answer to the GM's October 16 question: keep all good players and rotate them; our $33.95M profit means the constraint is development minutes, not payroll.
recommendations.rationale: Dumping salary now takes ice time from Chlup, Nash, Jackman, Stahle, and the July 2009 replacements never grow into roles. The only exception is Gaborik: if he hasn't crossed 0.40 pts/g by mid-February, his $11.90M is the one salary that poisons the entire future.

recommendations.summary: Package Klesla plus our second-round pick to Vancouver for Jovanovski before the February 2006 deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Klesla (23, POTE 97, $0.90M) expires in July so we lose him for nothing if we do not convert him. VAN carry 10 expiring on the league's lowest payroll at $46.36M and need young D; Jovanovski (29, 89 base, 93 TOUG, 94 CHKG, $2.30M expiring) closes the checking gap the Coach has flagged since April in one move. Net payroll increase to us is $1.40M against $33.95M profit.

recommendations.summary: Package Colaiacovo plus our second-round pick to Chicago for Bell, targeting February 2006.
recommendations.rationale: Colaiacovo (22, POTE 99, $1.40M, 4 years) is stalled per the Coach's May write-off at 0.39 pts/g. CHI carry 10 expiring at $50.12M payroll and want cheap long-term upside. Bell (24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, $900K, 2 years left) is the only league-wide player whose TOUG cracks 80 displayed even with form drag. We save $500K net. Risk: GM may view Colaiacovo as defensive core alongside Eminger and McCabe.

recommendations.summary: Prepare Koltsov plus Tucker plus our second-round pick as the package for whichever of Heatley or Kovalchuk Atlanta lists before the February 2006 deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Koltsov (24, POTE 94, $1.10M, expiring, 0 GP) and Tucker (30, POTE 79, $1.30M, expiring, 0 GP) are unlined and walk in July regardless. ATL at 1-2-0 with 9 expiring on $39.13M cannot re-sign both stars; the one who moves needs a destination that gives ATL salary relief and a pick. Heatley (91 base, 24) or Kovalchuk (89 base, 21) both carry 82+ TOUG, closing toughness and scoring simultaneously. This resolves no earlier than January when ATL's re-signing decision comes.

recommendations.summary: Goalie trade monitoring task #2 is complete; Luongo is here. No action until July 2006 renewal.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo acquired at 97 overall on $1.60M with 1 year left. The GM closed all goalie monitoring March 19, 2005. The next decision is a 5-6 year extension in July 2006, same week as Chlup.

recommendations.summary: Dress Spezza and give him fourth-line minutes; at POTE 99, morale 88 and zero games in five, we are wasting a top-potential asset.
recommendations.rationale: Last season he finished at 4.8 MPG and now he is not even playing. At 22 with the highest scouting number on the roster, his morale is already the lowest of any young player. Either he earns a role or we need to have a harder conversation about his place.

recommendations.summary: Put Alexeev in the lineup over a fourth-line winger; he scored 2 points in 1 game this season and outproduced both L4 wingers last year.
recommendations.rationale: Alexeev at 0.55 pts/g last season and 2 points in 1 game now outproduces Spacek and Upshall (0.60 pts/g each) at 23 with POTE 94. The rate-to-role mismatch flagged in April persists.

recommendations.summary: Eminger at zero games and $2.20M x 4 needs a role or needs to be moved; scratching him entirely helps nobody.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 but 0.36 pts/g last season. At 21, sitting him costs development on a player locked to a long deal. Either find him a third-pair role or flag him to the GM as a trade candidate before the value drops further.

recommendations.summary: No change for Chlup at 19; 20 MPG and 1.20 pts/g means he is where he belongs.
recommendations.rationale: 6 points in 5 games on the second line at 20 MPG. He has earned every minute he is getting.

recommendations.summary: Move Chlup to first-line centre permanently; 23.5 MPG and 1.25 pts/g at 19 is the best forward on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: He went 0.62 to 0.88 to 1.25 across three seasons on rising minutes (11.0 to 18.2 to 23.5). This is no longer development; he is the best centre available.

recommendations.summary: Gardener, Spacek and Upshall need a clear decision: give them 12+ MPG each or stop dressing them.
recommendations.rationale: All three went from 16-17 MPG in the opener to 1.5-3.5 MPG over the next four games. One game then the press box builds nothing. The pattern is repeating from last season for Spacek and Upshall specifically.

recommendations.summary: Spezza (22, POTE 99) and Eminger (21) have played zero games. The GM needs to decide their roster status.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza sat out last season and sits again. Eminger was flagged for trade in March and hasn't played since. Neither benefits from being dressed but not used.

recommendations.summary: Fischer, Nash, Klesla, Stahle and Sundin are all trending up or holding. Leave them alone.
recommendations.rationale: Fischer went from 10 to 21 MPG with 1.00 pts/g at 25. Nash at 19.5 MPG and 0.75 pts/g is holding. Klesla normalized to 23.2 MPG. Stahle doubled his minutes to 14.2 and is scoring. Sundin at 34 is at 1.25 pts/g on 19.8 MPG. No intervention needed.

recommendations.summary: No morale action needed. The entire roster sits at 88-100, no player is below their minutes band enough to be slipping, and the D-minute concentration that worried me in early October has eased.
recommendations.rationale: All 19 dressed skaters carry morale at 91. Scratched players range 88-100. Richards at 12.4 MPG is the furthest below his calibre band but at 0.8 pts/g and morale holding at 91, there is no case to force a change before results or a second look in two weeks.

recommendations.summary: Keep all lines as they are. Every auto-pairing favors us and no slot reorder improves a single matchup.
recommendations.rationale: MTL's top D is Markov at CHKG 64/TOUG 50 drawn by our first line via auto-pairing. Their PP is 1-for-13. Their centres lose every faceoff draw to ours. The talent gap is large enough that the only risk is undiscipline.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming per January 19 order.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 97 is the clear starter against a 2.00 GF/game team. MTL's one path to a win is Theodore out-duelling us; we give him the best shot-stopper to match.

recommendations.summary: Sell Jackman at the deadline or early summer while his 1.00 pts/g rate is fresh on the scoresheet.
recommendations.rationale: 5 points in 5 games at $0.70M x 2 is peak trade value. His career rate is 0.48 and regression is coming.

recommendations.summary: Move McCabe on $3.00M x 3 — undressed, declining at 0.48 recent rate, and blocking no one.
recommendations.rationale: 84 OVR on paper but he doesn't dress. Recent production (0.48) and age (30) say the asset is eroding.

recommendations.summary: Keep Colaiacovo dressed for now; zero in five is a small sample and no internal replacement exists.
recommendations.rationale: 0 points in 5 games at 13 MPG is poor, but Hainsey and Safronov are lower-rated and the minute spread needs six bodies.

recommendations.summary: Line McCabe on a defence pair; his 86 CHKG and 94 ENDU are wasted on the press box and are the single largest internal fix for the checking gap.
recommendations.rationale: McCabe is not in any unit despite being the club's second-best checker at 86 CHKG and having the best endurance on the blue line at 94 ENDU. The coach's L3 checking mean of 68 and L4 mean of 72 cannot be fixed at forward without a trade, but a third pairing with McCabe frees Fischer and Jackman to take checking roles higher up.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker nightly as the fourth-line checking wing; his 83 CHKG is the only forward-grade checker outside Fischer and Upshall.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker at 83 CHKG is not lined despite being the club's third-best forward checker. He is 30 with a POTE of 79, so this is not development — it is filling the role the coach says is missing. His 70 TOUG does not close the toughness gap but it does close the checking gap.

recommendations.summary: Line Wallin at a bottom-six centre slot; his 83 FACE is the club's second-best draw and he is currently undressed.
recommendations.rationale: The coach flagged L4 faceoff mean at 52 in May and nothing has changed. Sundin (90) is the only other faceoff man above 83. Wallin is on the roster and not in any unit. Giving L3 or L4 a 75–83 faceoff range across four centres is a real improvement over the current low-70s.

recommendations.summary: Dress Gaborik or move him by February; at 92 scoring and 98 speed with POTE 90 he is the club's best young scorer and he has 0 GP in 4 games.
recommendations.rationale: The May 2005 structural void flagged that no under-30 is positioned to absorb Mogilny (94, 36), Sundin (92, 34), and Roberts (88, 39). Gaborik is 23 and the most obvious candidate, but every undressed week erodes his trade value toward the January threshold already flagged. The coach must pick one: develop or deal.

recommendations.summary: Toughness at 80+ cannot be fixed internally; Bell (88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, 24, POTE 81) or Avery (83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 93 FACE, 25, $400K, 2 years) are the only targets closing all three gaps.
recommendations.rationale: Zero Toronto players carry TOUG above 75. The coach's L3 checking mean of 68 and L4 mean of 72 will not improve without an 80+ TOUG/CHKG forward. Bell is the higher ceiling; Avery is the cheaper entry at $400K. Both require a package worth more than Tucker plus a 4th, per the March 30 valuation.

recommendations.summary: Goalies are covered: Luongo (94 GSH_, 0.50 GAA, 0.983 SV) and Ouellet (86 GSH_, 2.50 GAA, 0.898 SV) are a 1-2 with depth behind them.
recommendations.rationale: GM closed all goalie monitoring on March 19. Luongo is 26 and Ouellet is 24; both carry 1 year left. No action until renewal window.

recommendations.summary: Resolve Gaborik this week: dress him or move him before January when his game count kills his value.
recommendations.rationale: He is 23 with POTE 90 on a $11.90M salary and sitting on the bench. Three games played, one point. Every additional scratch lowers his trade value.

recommendations.summary: Build the July 2006 renewal list now: Luongo, Chlup, Spezza, Klesla are all one-year deals expiring the same month.
recommendations.rationale: Nine players worth $15.44M expire in 2006. The four core young pieces — Luongo ($1.60M, POTE 97), Chlup ($2.34M, POTE 95), Spezza ($1.00M, POTE 99), Klesla ($0.90M, POTE 97) — need 5-6 year extensions. Four simultaneous renewals is a logistics problem that needs a plan by February.

recommendations.summary: Iginla (CGY, 93 base, 1.92 pts/g, $6.50M expiring) remains the July 2006 priority to replace the Mogilny/Sundin scoring decline.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny (36, POTE 55) walks after this season. No under-25 forward on this roster carries the scoring profile to replace him without a leap. Iginla closes the gap at $6.50M, which the $35.05M profit absorbs.

recommendations.summary: Payroll at $89.94M with $35.05M profit leaves room for the Iginla-class acquisition and four renewals without cutting elsewhere.
recommendations.rationale: No money move is needed before the Iginla deal and the Luongo/Chlup renewals are agreed. Cutting McCabe ($3.00M, POTE 78) or Fischer ($3.70M, POTE 90) before those are settled would weaken the roster to solve a problem that does not yet exist.

recommendations.summary: Lock Luongo on 5-6 years the first week of July, before any other renewal.
recommendations.rationale: 26 years old, 90+ base, $1.60M expiring. Franchise goalie on a cheap deal; losing him is a rebuild.

recommendations.summary: Lock Chlup on 5-6 years the same week as Luongo.
recommendations.rationale: 19 years old, assigned L1C by the Coach, $2.34M expiring July 2006. Second-highest value piece we must not lose.

recommendations.summary: Lock Klesla on 5-6 years; do not package him for Jovanovski or any rental D.
recommendations.rationale: 23, POTE 98, 78 base, $900K. Giving up POTE 98 at 23 for a 29-year-old expiring defenseman is a short-term rental that guts the long-term core.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Ouellet on 2 years at current salary as the backup goalie.
recommendations.rationale: 24, POTE 98, 81 base, $900M. Best cheap backup available; the GM's Feb 2005 objection was about being sole playoff backup, which Luongo solves.

recommendations.summary: Package Tucker and St. Jacques to Buffalo for Begin at the deadline if contending.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker 30/$1.30M is a designated chip; St. Jacques 25/$800K is the second piece. Begin (BUF, 87 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 86 FACE, 27, $936K expiring) fills the L4 checking and faceoff gap.

recommendations.summary: Do not re-sign Mogilny at 36 and $5.50M; ride him as a rental or dump by the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: 37 next season, $5.50M is the largest contract on the roster. The over-80 expiring mechanic may yield a pick if he is not needed by March.

recommendations.summary: Dress Spezza at L3C within 2 games or he becomes a March chip alongside Tucker.
recommendations.rationale: 73 overall, POTE 98, age 22, morale 88 (lowest on roster). 0 GP in 3 games. Value decays with every scratched game at this price.

recommendations.summary: Decide Eminger within 5 games: dress him or trade him by the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 at 21 is the highest upside on the roster. If scratched past 8 total games his development case dies per the Coach and he becomes a chip whose value drops with every undressed game.

recommendations.summary: If Gaborik is still a healthy scratch in January, open trade discussions immediately; his $11.90M salary means he cannot simply be released.
recommendations.rationale: 23, POTE 90, $11.90M/year, benched. Not expiring so the pick mechanic does not apply. His trade value drops with every game he does not play.

recommendations.summary: No deadline action until late February; revisit buyer/seller status then.
recommendations.rationale: 154 days to the deadline, 4 games played. The GM's standing order from January 2005 is that negotiations open late February, not mid-October.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Heatley (ATL, RW, 91 base, TOUG 82, CHKG 88, 24, $1.10M expiring) as the primary February target; ATL cannot keep both him and Kovalchuk.
recommendations.rationale: First player in the league to clear toughness 80 with elite scoring (91 base, 4pts in 2GP, 2.00 ppg pace). ATL at 9 expiring and $8.37M expiring payroll must choose between him and Kovalchuk; whichever stays, the other moves. Package: R1 plus a young forward.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Kovalchuk (ATL, LW, 89 base, TOUG 85, 99 SPEE, 22, $1.10M expiring) as the alternate if ATL retains Heatley.
recommendations.rationale: Same binary as Heatley at ATL. Higher TOUG (85 vs 82), younger (22 vs 24), and 99 SPEE with 5pts in 2GP (2.50 ppg). If ATL keeps the older scorer, Kovalchuk is the better long-term fit. Same price tag applies.

recommendations.summary: Bertuzzi (VAN, RW, 94 base, TOUG 85, CHKG 89, 30, $2.60M expiring) is the fallback if ATL holds both stars — a one-year fix with no development upside.
recommendations.rationale: 94 base with 85 TOUG and 89 CHKG closes all three front-office gaps tonight. POTE 58 at 30 means this is purely a competitive window addition. VAN at 10 expiring, $7.50M expiring payroll, lowest total payroll in league, rebuilding around Sedins — Bertuzzi is expiring surplus.

recommendations.summary: Iginla (CGY, RW, 93 base, 1.92 ppg, 27, $6.50M expiring) remains the best pure scoring bridge if toughness is solved internally.
recommendations.rationale: 93 base at 27 with 1.92 pts/g replaces Mogilny's production without requiring Chlup or Nash to jump levels. Does not solve toughness. CGY at 4 pts, 9 expiring, $22.83M profit — they will listen if the return includes an R1 and a young player.

recommendations.summary: Jovanovski (VAN, D, 89 base, TOUG 93, CHKG 94, 29, $2.30M expiring, 30.3 MPG) is the February D-side toughness target.
recommendations.rationale: Already flagged October 12 as the top defensive trade target. 93 TOUG and 94 CHKG on a blueliner is unique on the market. VAN at $46.36M payroll (lowest in league) with 10 expiring are structurally motivated sellers. Package: Klesla plus 2nd-round pick.

recommendations.summary: Aulin (LA, C, 71 base, FACE 85, POTE 95, 23, $900K expiring) is the cheapest long-term faceoff solution; acquire for a late pick.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 95 at 23 with 85 FACE is a projection worth $900K and a 4th-rounder. LA at 12 expiring with $21.73M in expiring payroll (most in league) will deal depth for picks. Does not solve toughness — this is the L3C answer, not the physical answer.

recommendations.summary: Bell (CHI, LW, ~80 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, 24, 2 years left) remains the three-gap answer but is locked through 2006-07 — February trade target, not July.
recommendations.rationale: Not expiring this season (contract_years shows 1 additional year). Currently producing 3pts in 2GP at 19 MPG for CHI. CHI at 10 expiring with $19.70M expiring payroll are sellers, but Bell isn't among them. Must approach in February, not July.

recommendations.summary: Zhitnik (BUF, D, 85 base, TOUG 82, CHKG 86, 33, $3.50M expiring) is a playoff-rental option at the deadline but not a long-term fit.
recommendations.rationale: 33 years old with POTE 66 and $3.50M salary makes this purely a deadline rental. BUF at 9 expiring and $13.78M expiring payroll might deal a rental Dman. Lower priority than Jovanovski because of age and cost.

recommendations.summary: Walker (VAN, D, 71 base, TOUG 94, CHKG 92, 25, $500K expiring) is the cheapest toughness available — a depth blueliner at 94 TOUG.
recommendations.rationale: 94 TOUG and 92 CHKG at $500K is absurd value for a checking pair. 71 base means he's not a top-pair player, but he gives a third defensive pair real physicality. VAN at 10 expiring, lowest payroll, will deal him for a late-round pick or nothing.

recommendations.summary: Reinstate Eminger to a defensive pair; he is the highest-ceiling D on the roster and has played zero games.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 at age 21, GM confirmed he is a keeper in January. Four games without him is four games of development lost on a player we chose to retain.

recommendations.summary: Reinstate Spezza to a forward line; he has played zero games at 22 with POTE 99.
recommendations.rationale: Last season's collapse is done. Fresh start means a real audition, not another year on the bench.

recommendations.summary: Give Alexeev a regular spot on the fourth line; he is 2 for 1 when he plays but only appeared in 1 of 4 games.
recommendations.rationale: Same mismatch flagged in April: outproduces dressed wingers, gets scratch duty. At 23 this needs resolving before it becomes a morale problem.

recommendations.summary: Cap Klesla at 24-25 MPG by rolling Stahle and Colaiacovo in more; 28.5 MPG at 23 mirrors the pattern that broke Jackman last season.
recommendations.rationale: Already at 28.5 MPG after 4 games. My October 13 finding flagged exactly this concentration risk. Four games is early but the load trajectory needs to bend now, not in December.

recommendations.current: Chlup, Nash, Chistov, Spacek, Stahle, Colaiacovo, Upshall
recommendations.summary: No change for the young players already in sensible roles: Chlup at 20 MPG, Nash at 20 MPG producing 1.0 pts/g, Chistov at 1.0 pts/g on the third line.
recommendations.rationale: These seven are getting games proportional to their grade and contributing. Leaving them alone is the right call.

recommendations.summary: Spezza has played 0 games in two consecutive seasons. Decide his future now: give him real minutes or make him available before his trade value evaporates further.
recommendations.rationale: 0 GP across 4 games at age 22 with POTE 99. The 'next camp' lever from March failed. A second season of zero ice at a high-potential age means he will either be wasted or leave for nothing.

recommendations.summary: Spacek (3.7 MPG), Gardener (1.7 MPG) and Upshall (4.0 MPG) are all at ages 20-22 getting under 5 minutes. Either give them a real shift allocation or stop dressing them.
recommendations.rationale: Development requires games. Three players aged 20-22 at combined 9.4 MPG with zero production means we are using roster spots to warm benches.

recommendations.summary: Nash at 1.00 pts/g on 20.7 MPG at 21 has crossed from prospect to top-six winger. Factor his raised value into any trade discussion.
recommendations.rationale: Last season flagged him as declining at 0.43 rate. He has doubled both his rate and his minutes this year. His trade value moved materially in four games.

recommendations.summary: Gaborik at 23 is playing 16 MPG with 0.33 pts/g. Give him room to climb toward 18-20 if his production holds through ten games.
recommendations.rationale: First meaningful ice since I started tracking him. At 23 with 16 MPG and some production he is heading the right direction but needs more of the game to confirm.

recommendations.summary: No ice-time changes needed; the room is stable at 90-91 with no downward movement.
recommendations.rationale: Every dressed player sits at 91 morale unchanged, minutes broadly match calibre bands, and Spezza at 88 is a known GM rotation choice that has not deteriorated further.

recommendations.summary: L3 checking stays at 68 mean because no forward on this roster with 75+ checking is available to slot in.
recommendations.rationale: The only forwards above 75 checking are Jackman (92), Roberts (86), Nash (82) and McCabe (83, scratched). All four are already placed or unavailable. This is a roster gap, not a lineup problem.

recommendations.summary: Keep K2 as is; the load concern on Kaberle and Klesla is managed by in-game usage, not by reshuffling the menu.
recommendations.rationale: Kaberle carries 91 stamina which is the best among our defencemen. K2 mean of 72 checking is adequate for a second kill. Restructuring breaks chemistry for a problem that in-game management handles better.

recommendations.summary: We still have no forward who combines 75+ checking with enough skill to hold a third-line role. The gap persists since April and limits every line below the top two.
recommendations.rationale: Role inventory shows checking above 75 belongs only to Jackman (92), Roberts (86), Nash (82), McCabe (83). All four are locked into L1 or scratched. L3 mean checking is 68 and L4 is 72. The fix requires acquiring a checking forward; no rearrangement solves it.

recommendations.summary: D minutes remain concentrated on Jackman and Klesla; monitoring continues, no menu change yet at 4 games in.
recommendations.rationale: At the 4-5 game mark early-season load concentration is normal. If the ratio holds past ten games their endurance will crater by December. The lever is spreading minutes to Kaberle, Fischer and Stahle in game, not a lineup reshuffle.

recommendations.summary: Start Ouellet; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming per January 19 order.
recommendations.rationale: Ouellet is 86 OVR but carries ENDU 64. PHX have scored 4 in 3 games so the risk of a relief is low if he tires mid-game.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes for PHX. All four lines are appropriate against their roster.
recommendations.rationale: PHX top defenceman reads 75, their offence is 1.33 GF per game, and their PP is 1-for-12. Our lines already match well; nothing needs restructuring.

recommendations.summary: Ride second and third forward lines more than usual tonight to spread D minutes to Stahle/Colaiacovo and Fischer/Kaberle.
recommendations.rationale: Klesla and Jackman are at 28.5 and 28.0 MPG after 4 games. PHX's third line reads 75/72 and will not punish a third pair. This is the cheapest night to feed those minutes down.

recommendations.summary: Move Jackman now while his 1.00 pts/g start inflates his return; at $0.70M x 2 and 24, this window is the peak of his trade value.
recommendations.rationale: 4 points in 4 games after a 0.48 pts/g season. Cheap, young, top-pair minutes at 28 MPG. His rate will regress; the return won't be this good in December.

recommendations.summary: McCabe is a healthy scratch at $3.00M x 3 and 84 OVR. Explore any return; he is not coming back into this lineup.
recommendations.rationale: Not dressed in 4 games while two 76-OVR defencemen play 12 MPG each. His recent career rate is 0.48. Dead cap if we can't move him.

recommendations.summary: Dress McCabe on the third line or third pair to raise L3 checking from 68 to above 80; he is at 86 CHKG and currently in no unit.
recommendations.rationale: Six players carry CHKG 80+ but the coach deploys none of them on L3 or L4. McCabe at 86 CHKG, 94 ENDU, age 30 is the best available and is dressed but unlined. Tucker at 83 CHKG is the alternative.

recommendations.summary: Dress Wallin at fourth-line centre; at 83 FACE he is the only man besides Sundin who wins draws and he is currently in no unit.
recommendations.rationale: L4 faceoff mean is 52 per the coach's May report. Wallin is 25, carries 83 FACE and 80+ speed, and is rostered but unlined. This eliminates the need to chase Avery or Bell for faceoff duty.

recommendations.summary: Toughness remains the one gap no internal move solves; the best TOUG on the roster is 75 and the team needs 80+. Bell at 88 TOUG, 24, $0.90M expiring is still the cheapest fix if the GM accepts him purely for TOUG and not faceoffs.
recommendations.rationale: Zero players at TOUG 80+. The coach flags L3/L4 cannot handle an opponent's bottom six. Tucker at 83 CHKG/70 TOUG is the internal floor but he is unlined and his TOUG is the problem, not the answer. Bell at 88 TOUG is the only identified player who fixes this without a first-round pick.

recommendations.summary: The scoring group averages 33.8 years old across the top three (Mogilny 36, Sundin 34, Roberts 39); the structural void behind them is the defining roster problem for 2006-07 and cannot be solved by a single trade.
recommendations.rationale: From the May 2005 finding: no player under 30 is positioned to absorb 426 combined points. Gaborik at 23 is the closest but is a healthy scratch. The July Iginla target and any young winger acquisition from now to June 2006 serve this problem.

recommendations.summary: Resolve Gaborik before the end of October: dress him on a real line or begin trade talks now while game count preserves value.
recommendations.rationale: $11.90M dead on a healthy scratch is 13.2% of payroll. Coach's deadline was mid-October and it is October 15. If undressed by January, the value drops per the standing note.

recommendations.summary: July 2006: lock Chlup and Luongo on 5-6 year deals the same week; Chlup first.
recommendations.rationale: Both expire July 2006 on expiring deals ($2.34M and $1.60M). POTE 95 and 97 respectively, ages 20 and 27. The entire forward and goalie foundation walks if one is neglected.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Begin for the L4 at February 2006; he fixes the checking gap AND removes a roster spot, unlocking 1-2 high-POTE players for top-nine minutes.
recommendations.rationale: Begin (87 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 86 FACE, $936K expiring) addresses the Coach's role-gap AND the development bottleneck. Package already built: Tucker plus St. Jacques. BUF have $19.07M profit and 6 expiring.

recommendations.summary: Lock Chlup on 5-6 years immediately when he hits the market in July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: He is 19, earning $2.34M, playing L1C at 25+ MPG. At that age and role the next 5 years are the ones that matter. No mid-contract renegotiation is possible, so the plan is to be first in line in July with a long offer.

recommendations.summary: Lock Luongo on 5-6 years in July 2006, same week as Chlup.
recommendations.rationale: He is 26, $1.60M, and the confirmed #1 goalie. The GM closed the goalie-trade question on 2005-03-19 with Belfour and Luongo as the two 90+ goalies for the run. The long-term plan runs through Luongo.

recommendations.proposed: Tucker + St. Jacques to Buffalo for Begin
recommendations.summary: Pursue the Tucker + St. Jacques to Buffalo package for Begin when negotiations open late February.
recommendations.rationale: Coach flags the checking-middle-six gap (L3 mean 68 CHKG, L4 mean 72). Begin carries 95 CHKG, 87 TOUG, 86 FACE at 27 on an expiring $936K. Buffalo have 6 expiring contracts and $19.07M profit, making a rebuild sell logical for them.

recommendations.summary: Renew Klesla on 3-5 years in July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: He is 23 at $0.90M carrying top-pairing minutes against tough opponents. The coach explicitly asked to protect his ENDU 63 against depth forward groups, which means he trusts him in tough minutes. Lock the cheap young D.

recommendations.summary: Renew Spezza only if he plays top-nine minutes by February; otherwise convert him to a trade chip at the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 at 22 but zero games in three and morale at 88, the lowest on the roster. The coach demands a roster decision within 5 games. A player with that potential who cannot dress is not a roster asset; he is trade value.

recommendations.summary: Let Mogilny walk in July if he has not been traded by the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: 36 years old, $5.50M, no development case. Moving him at the deadline recovers a pick via the over-80 mechanic; letting him walk saves the same $5.50M but loses the pick. Trade preferred, release acceptable.

recommendations.summary: No deadline action before late February per the GM's standing order; use the interim to track Spezza, Eminger, and Koltsov.
recommendations.rationale: 155 days to March 19 with 3 games played. The buyer/seller determination comes from the standings in February, not from today's record.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Begin at L4C for checking (95 CHKG), faceoffs (86 FACE) and toughness (87 TOUG) on an expiring $936K deal; Buffalo at 4 points with 6 expiring are sellers.
recommendations.rationale: L3 checking mean 68 and L4 mean 72 per Coach's report; Begin at 95 CHKG and 86 FACE fixes both simultaneously and frees Tucker or McCabe from the lineup for a high-POTE prospect.

recommendations.summary: Target Cole (ANA, 84 base, 95 CHKG, 86 TOUG, $600K expiring) for L3 left wing; Anaheim at 2 points with 11 expiring deals must shed salary.
recommendations.rationale: L3 checking gap at 68 mean needs a CHKG 90+ body; Cole fills it at $600K from the league's most desperate seller class.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Jovanovski (VAN, 89 base, 93 TOUG, 94 CHKG, 29, $2.30M expiring) with Klesla plus 2nd-round pick; Vancouver at 2 points with 13 expiring are the most motivated seller.
recommendations.rationale: No TOR defenceman exceeds 85 TOUG; Jovanovski gives the top pairing the physical presence McCabe cannot provide, and Klesla (POTE 97) cannot dress on this roster depth.

recommendations.summary: Target Morrow (DAL, 88 base, 87 TOUG, 89 CHKG, POTE 85, 26, $1.30M expiring) as the premium middle-six option; Dallas at 4 points with 11 expiring but $26.69M profit makes them reluctant.
recommendations.rationale: Superior to Begin and Cole in overall (88 vs 73 and 84) and in POTE (85 vs 63 and 74), but Dallas's profit means acceptance requires more than a late pick.

recommendations.summary: Monitor Lecavalier (TB, 90 base, 83 CHKG, 73 TOUG, POTE 85, 25, $2.60M expiring); Tampa at 0-0-0 with $18.31M profit and 6 expiring deals could become a February seller if they start poorly.
recommendations.rationale: A 25-year-old 90-overall centre on $2.60M expiring from a non-contender is the single highest-value rental in the league; Toronto holds three first-through-third rounders and high-POTE undressed players (Eminger, Chistov) Tampa could want.

recommendations.summary: Track Hartnell (NSH, 79 base, 87 TOUG, 88 CHKG, POTE 94, 23, $1.10M expiring); he fills the physical gap and has the ceiling to keep beyond February.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 94 at 23 with 87 TOUG and 88 CHKG means this is a keeper, not a rental; Nashville at $22.35M profit makes acceptance uncertain but the fit is permanent.

recommendations.summary: Avery (LA, 79 base, 93 FACE, 88 CHKG, 83 TOUG, $400K, 1 year) is the cheapest single player closing all three gaps; LA at 4 points with 6 expiring are motivated.
recommendations.rationale: His 0.11 pts/g production last season is the risk, but at $400K the floor is a faceoff specialist who can kill penalties; LA's desperation makes acceptance more likely than for any comparable target.

recommendations.summary: Bell (CHI, 80 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82, POTE 81, 25, $900K expiring) at L3 or L4 wing fills checking and toughness from a 3-point seller with 8 expiring deals.
recommendations.rationale: January veto was about faceoffs at centre; as a LW his TOUG 88 and CHKG 86 raise the L3/L4 means without the centre-position problem. Chicago at 3 points with 8 expiring must shed contracts.

recommendations.summary: The Coach's mid-October dress-or-trade deadline is today; Gaborik at $11.90M undressed is the single largest waste on the roster and his trade value drops with every undressed week.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 90 at 23 on $11.90M is tradeable only if the market still values his youth and potential over his current zero-game streak; waiting past November guarantees a worse return.

recommendations.current: Tucker (LW, 30, $1.30M expiring, 92 CHKG, 88 TOUG, 0 GP) + St. Jacques (D, 25, $0.80M expiring, POTE 94, 84 CHKG, 80 TOUG, 0 GP)
recommendations.proposed: Begin (C, BUF, 27, $936K expiring, 73 base, 95 CHKG, 87 TOUG, 86 FACE)
recommendations.summary: Offer Tucker plus St. Jacques to Buffalo for Begin; both our pieces are undressed and expiring, so we shed $2.10M and add $936K while filling the L4 checking-and-faceoff void the Coach has flagged since May.
recommendations.rationale: BUF at 4 points with $17.67M profit and 6 expiring are building through youth; they get a veteran checking wing and a 25-year-old POTE 94 defenseman at zero long-term cost. Acceptance uncertain but the fit is clean on both sides.

recommendations.current: Klesla (D, 23, $0.90M expiring, POTE 97, SPEE 88, AGIL 87, 3 GP 0 pts) + 2nd-round pick
recommendations.proposed: Jovanovski (D, VAN, 29, $2.30M expiring, 89 base, 93 TOUG, 94 CHKG)
recommendations.summary: Offer Klesla plus our 2nd-round pick to Vancouver for Jovanovski; he is the only defenseman in the league at 90+ base with 90+ TOUG and 90+ CHKG on an expiring deal from a structural seller.
recommendations.rationale: VAN at 2 points with 13 expiring and $46.36M payroll (league-lowest) must shed; Klesla at 23 with POTE 97 matches their rebuild timeline and the R2 gives them another lottery ticket. We absorb $1.40M net for July but gain the toughness nobody on our blue line carries.

recommendations.current: Brendl (RW, 24, $0.80M, 2 years remaining, POTE 93, SPEE 88, SHPW 87, 1 GP 1 pt)
recommendations.proposed: Avery (C, LA, 25, $400K, 1 year, 79 base, 93 FACE, 88 CHKG, 83 TOUG)
recommendations.summary: Offer Brendl to LA for Avery; at $400K with 93 FACE he kills the L4 faceoff problem permanently and costs almost nothing, while Brendl's POTE 93 and speed fit LA's youth timeline.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 4 points with 6 expiring and Avery producing 6 points in 57 games last season have no reason to keep him; Brendl at 24 with SPEE 88 and a shot gives them a cheap speed prospect. This stacks with Begin if both land, giving L3C and L4C faceoff wins above 85.

recommendations.summary: Luongo's 1-year deal expires July 2006; lock him on 5-6 years the same week Chlup's deal comes up, Luongo first.
recommendations.rationale: He is 97 overall at 26 on $1.60M with 1 year left. Tellqvist behind him is a clear step down. No mid-contract renegotiation is possible in this game, so the window is the week his contract expires.

recommendations.summary: Dress Spezza and slot him at third-line centre; 0 games in 3 at POTE 99 and morale 88 is the lowest on the roster and heading the wrong direction.
recommendations.rationale: Last season his minutes fell from 9.1 to 4.8 MPG and produced 0.32 pts/g. This season he isn't even in the lineup. At 22 with the club's highest POTE he needs a real role or this becomes two wasted years.

recommendations.summary: Eminger is completely out of the picture at 21 with POTE 99; decide within 5 games whether he's a player we develop or a piece we move.
recommendations.rationale: 0 GP in 3 games at $2.20M x 4. Last season 0.36 pts/g on 15.8 MPG. If the coaching staff (me) doesn't need him, the GM needs to know now so the trade window doesn't close on another dead year.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev's rate-to-role mismatch continues: 2 points in 1 game on 6 MPG while Upshall gets 9.3 MPG with 1 point. Watching for 3 more games before pushing.
recommendations.rationale: Same pattern as last season when he outproduced dressed wingers from the scratch list. One game is too small to force a change but the direction is consistent.

recommendations.summary: Chlup, Nash, Chistov, Spacek, Gardener, Stahle, Colaiacovo, Upshall and Klesla are all getting ice appropriate to their role. No intervention needed for them.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup 20.0 MPG, Nash 18.0, Chistov 12.3, the fourth-liners at 9.3. Everyone is where their game says they should be.

recommendations.summary: Keep Chlup at 25+ MPG on the first line; his role is finally where it should be.
recommendations.rationale: Minutes tripled from 6.0 to 27.0 MPG at 19 with 1 point in 2 games. This is the first-line role the April finding called for and it is working. Do not pull him back.

recommendations.summary: Spacek's minutes collapsed again (17.0 to 5.5 MPG, zero points); if this holds past five games, the case for dressing him next season needs a fresh argument.
recommendations.rationale: This is the same pattern that killed his February last season (12+ to 8.1 MPG). Three separate minute collapses with no grade movement suggests he cannot hold a top-nine role without deliberate minutes allocation.

recommendations.summary: Third consecutive season where Upshall's minutes collapse within weeks (now 16.0 to 6.0 MPG). Either he gets a deliberate 12+ MPG role or the development case is dead.
recommendations.rationale: 13.4 to 4.9 last season, now 16.0 to 6.0 this October. No grade movement either time. The game is not punishing him; he is not holding ice. The GM needs to decide if he is a project or a roster piece.

recommendations.summary: No change to D minutes; the load redistribution (Jackman 41→22, Klesla 42→22, four others up) is the fix the October 13 finding called for.
recommendations.rationale: Jackman maintained 1.00 pts/g at 22 MPG, confirming the March diagnosis that his production was load-driven. Let the rotation settle.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev still at 1 GP despite outscoring dressed wingers; the rate-to-role mismatch is now two seasons old and unresolved.
recommendations.rationale: GP unchanged from 1. The April finding flagged him at 0.55 pts/g against Chistov and Upshall at 0.29. Chistov is now at 0.50 on 15.5 MPG so that comparison has closed, but Upshall at 0.00 on 6.0 MPG remains below him.

recommendations.summary: No morale-driven minutes change before NYR; the room is at 88-100 with 3 games played.
recommendations.rationale: Lowest morale is Spezza at 88 (0 GP, development scratch). Every dressed player is at 91. Jackman and Klesla at 28.7 MPG carry an endurance risk by December but show no morale cost at 3 games.

recommendations.summary: No line changes needed for the Rangers game — current composition is the best arrangement available.
recommendations.rationale: L1 and L2 are well-sorted with skill, checking, and speed. L3 and L4 are soft defensively but no player outside those lines has checking above 75 to swap in.

recommendations.summary: We still lack a checking middle-six forward. L3 checking mean 68, L4 mean 72; neither can handle an opponent's bottom six without pulling L1 or L2.
recommendations.rationale: The role inventory confirms no forward outside L1–L2 checks above 75. This has been flagged since April and remains the primary structural deficiency. A trade or call-up of an 80+ checking forward is the only fix.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo at NYR; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming per the January 19 order.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo has been the recent starter and carries the workload. Standing order requires checking the fatigue icon before every start decision.

recommendations.summary: Start Ouellet; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming per January 19 order.
recommendations.rationale: Ouellet is 86 OVR versus Tellqvist at 73. NYR's top two lines are skilled enough to punish the drop in quality at 73. No fatigue icon flagged in the brief but must confirm visually.

recommendations.summary: No lineup change for NYR. The forward lines and D pairs match up correctly through auto-pairing.
recommendations.rationale: Our L1/L2 at 87/87 team OVR match their L1/L2 at 88/90. Their L3/L4 (OVR 77/74 average) is soft, especially with Purinton out. The auto-pairing gives our L1 Jackman/Klesla against Leetch/Jonsson and our L2 Fischer/Kaberle against Malakhov/Poti, which are both favorable.

recommendations.summary: Lean on Fischer/Kaberle for more of the game to protect Klesla's endurance (ENDU 63) against NYR's deep forward group.
recommendations.rationale: Klesla is ENDU 63 and already carrying 34.5 MPG per the Oct 13 finding. Against four lines that can score, he must not play 35+ minutes. Fischer/Kaberle handle their second pair (Malakhov 81, Poti 84) and should absorb their middle minutes.

recommendations.summary: Klesla's sell timeline moves from offseason to this season's trade deadline — he is 24, OVR 87, and expiring at $0.90M, the most tradeable he will ever be.
recommendations.rationale: 0 points in 3 games confirms the production ceiling. But OVR at 87 with one year left at $0.90M is peak trade value. After July he is a UFA loss.

recommendations.summary: Jackman's 1.00 pts/g through 3 games is a watch item, not a sell trigger. $0.70M x 2 gives us time to see if it holds to 10 games.
recommendations.rationale: Last season 0.48 pts/g; three games at 1.00 is noise at this sample size. His value as the cheapest top-pair D rises if this persists — we would sell higher later.

recommendations.summary: Toughness is the one role zero players cover above 80; Bell (88 TOUG, 82 FACE, 24) or Avery (83 TOUG, 93 FACE, 25) are the only fixes and both remain targets for February.
recommendations.rationale: Jackman at 75 is the roster best. The Coach's K2 checking mean of 72 and L4 toughness mean of 57 confirm no internal solution. Bell is confirmed available from CHI's 10 expiring; Avery's LA situation (13 expiring) was confirmed in January.

recommendations.summary: Dress McCabe (86 CHKG, 94 ENDU, 30) onto the second pair or penalty kill; he is rostered at 86 checking and currently plays no role.
recommendations.rationale: Six players at 80+ checking is thin, and two of them (McCabe, Tucker) are not lined. McCabe at 30 with 94 endurance can eat 18+ minutes without fatigue penalty.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker (83 CHKG, 30) as a nightly checker on the fourth pair or PK; he is rostered and currently in no unit.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker at 83 CHKG is the fourth-best checker on the roster and the only internal option that moves the K2 mean without a trade. Standing order from March says he is a trade chip, but until a deal materializes he is free depth.

recommendations.summary: Dress Wallin (83 FACE, 25) to take fourth-line draws; he is the only internal player above 80 on faceoffs outside Sundin.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach quantified L4 faceoff at 52 in April. Wallin at 83 is the only roster option who improves it without a trade. He is currently not lined.

recommendations.summary: Give Abid (86 overall, 25) real fourth-line minutes; he is rostered, healthy, and in no unit while carrying a higher overall than several lined players.
recommendations.rationale: Abid at 86 is the same overall as Tucker and above Upshall (80). He adds scoring depth to a line that currently has none above 75. The standing order from January keeps him as a toughness target for trades, but he is also free roster depth today.

recommendations.summary: Speed (25 at 80+), stamina (12 at 80+), and clutch (9 at 80+) are all well covered; no action needed in those areas.
recommendations.rationale: The brief shows no structural weakness in speed, stamina, or hero beyond the age of the top names, which is a July problem (Iginla target) not an October one.

recommendations.summary: Lock Luongo and Chlup on 5-6 year deals in July 2006 before they hit the market.
recommendations.rationale: Both expire this summer ($1.60M and $2.34M). Luongo is the franchise goalie at 26 with POTE 97; Chlup is the first-line centre at 19 with POTE 95. Tellingqvist behind Luongo is a step down (POTE 91, $1.20M on 6 years). Missing either is unrecoverable.

recommendations.summary: Iginla closes the scoring void left by Mogilny and Sundin aging out, and his $6.50M salary fits between Gaborik's $11.90M and the rest of the core.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny walks in July 2006 (expiring). Sundin will be 38 when his deal ends in 2009. No player under 30 currently on the roster is producing at 0.80+ pts/g. Iginla at 93 base with POTE 85 is the one acquisition that solves both the scoring gap and the toughness ceiling simultaneously.

recommendations.summary: No payroll action needed this season; $34.08M profit leaves room to absorb Iginla's $6.50M without cutting elsewhere.
recommendations.rationale: Payroll is $89.94M against revenue of $44.58M but profit stands at $34.08M (TV, prestige, and other income exceed the gap). There is no cap. The binding constraint is not this year's bill but the July 2009 cluster, and adding Iginla in July 2006 actually helps by giving the young core a bridge player through 2009.

recommendations.summary: Lock Chlup on a 5-6 year extension the same week Luongo renews, July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup is 19, base 82, 0.88 pts/g at L1C on a $2.34M expiring deal. He is the future first-line centre and must not be exposed to a bidding war.

recommendations.summary: Renew Luongo on 5-6 years the same week as Chlup, Luongo first.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 26, base 91, $1.60M expiring. Tellqvist behind him is base 77. Payroll is $89.94M with $34.08M profit; the only risk is letting him hit the market.

recommendations.summary: Target Jovanovski from VAN at the deadline with Klesla plus a 2nd-round pick.
recommendations.rationale: Jovanovski is 29, base 89, 93 TOUG, 94 CHKG, $2.30M expiring. VAN carry 13 expiring contracts on $46.36M payroll (lowest in league) and cannot retain him.

recommendations.summary: Package Tucker plus St. Jacques to Buffalo for Begin if we miss the top 8.
recommendations.rationale: Begin at 27, base 73, 87 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 86 FACE, $936K expiring fills the L4 checking and faceoff gap the Coach quantified. BUF have $19.07M profit and 6 expiring.

recommendations.summary: Let Mogilny walk in July. Do not re-sign at any length.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny is 36, $5.50M, base 90 on an expiring deal. At $5.50M and 37 next year there is no re-signing that does not eat the Chlup and Luongo renewals.

recommendations.summary: Let Koltsov walk. No renewal, no trade deadline urgency.
recommendations.rationale: Koltsov is 24, base 68, $1.10M. He is below the 80 threshold so the pick mechanic does not apply and carries minimal trade value.

recommendations.summary: Reassess Spezza's trade value in February based on whether he gets dressed before then.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza at 22, base 73, POTE 99, zero games this season. If the Coach dresses him and he shows something, he stays. If he is still a healthy scratch by late February, trade him while POTE holds value.

recommendations.summary: Keep Ouellet through the playoffs as backup; let him walk after if Luongo signs.
recommendations.rationale: Ouellet at 24, overall 86, base 81, $0.90M. He is the playoff backup the GM kept for insurance. Once Luongo is locked on 5-6 years, Ouellet has no role behind Tellqvist on 6 years.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell (CHI, 25, $900K, 1 year) at the February deadline: TOUG 86, CHKG 84, FACE 92, SPEE 95 closes all three structural gaps simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Bell is 84 overall at $900K with 8 other CHI players expiring and $21.76M profit. No other player in the league closes toughness, checking and faceoffs at his age and price simultaneously.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Komisarek (MTL, D, 23, $1.10M, 1 year) at February: TOUG 82, CHKG 89, SPEE 95, POTE 92 is the best young defenseman on a sell team.
recommendations.rationale: MTL at 1 point with 8 expiring and $17.76M profit cannot retain him. He closes the toughness gap on defense while giving speed no current TOR defenseman has (SPEE 95 vs Kaberle's 88). At 23 with POTE 92 the one-year rental has upside beyond its term.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Kovalchuk (ATL, LW, 22, $1.10M, 1 year, 89 base, SPEE 99, TOUG 84) as the scoring-bridge target replacing the now-dead Iginla plan.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 0 points with 6 expiring cannot retain both him and Heatley. At 22 with 89 base and 99 speed he is the only player who absorbs Mogilny's 426-point bridge without requiring Chlup or Nash to jump 0.20 pts/g. His TOUG 84 would also be Toronto's best on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Heatley (ATL, RW, 24, $1.10M, 1 year, 91 base, TOUG 81, CHKG 87, SPEE 97) as the RW scoring fix Mogilny's expiry leaves open.
recommendations.rationale: Same sell logic as Kovalchuk. At 24 with 91 base and 81 TOUG he clears the current roster's best toughness (Jackman 75) while filling the RW void. ATL cannot keep both stars; pick one.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Hartnell (NSH, LW, 23, $1.10M, TOUG 92, CHKG 93, SPEE 96, POTE 95) if his contract status confirms he is available.
recommendations.rationale: Highest grade-per-dollar package in the league: 92/93/96 at age 23 on $1.10M. The uncertainty is his contract_years showing 0 rather than 1; if genuinely expiring, he is the single best toughness addition available. NSH at 2 OT losses with 4 expiring may not sell.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Jovanovski (VAN, D, 29, $2.30M, 1 year, 89 base, TOUG 91, CHKG 92) as the immediate playoff-ready toughness upgrade on defense.
recommendations.rationale: VAN at $46.36M payroll (league-lowest) with 13 expiring contracts are the most motivated sellers. He is 8 years older than Komisarek with a set ceiling, but 89 base with 91/92 is elite tonight. The October 12 note confirmed him as top target; data validates.

recommendations.summary: Begin (BUF, C, 27, $935K, 1 year, TOUG 82, CHKG 90, FACE 79) is the cheap backup if Bell is unavailable, but his grades have dropped from October 12 readings.
recommendations.rationale: TOUG now 82 (was 87), CHKG 90 (was 95), FACE 79 (was 86). Still adequate for L4 checking but the faceoff decline makes him strictly inferior to Bell at nearly the same price. Keep as fallback only.

recommendations.summary: Avery (LA, C, 25, $400K, 1 year, FACE 90, CHKG 80, TOUG 75) is the cheapest faceoff fix but no longer closes the toughness gap.
recommendations.rationale: His TOUG fell from 83 in January to 75. He is now a faceoff specialist, not a three-gap target. At $400K he is the cheapest roster addition available for L4 draws, but the primary gap (toughness) remains open with him.

recommendations.summary: Reid (STL, RW, 24, $600K, 1 year, FACE 86, SPEE 99, POTE 94, TOUG 50) offers speed and faceoffs at a bargain price if STL shed salary.
recommendations.rationale: STL carry $69.76M payroll (2nd-highest in league) with $18.89M profit. His TOUG 50 means he does not fix toughness, but 99 speed plus 86 faceoffs plus POTE 94 at $600K is high ceiling per dollar.

recommendations.slot: first or second line left wing
recommendations.summary: Forsberg (COL, LW, 32, $9.90M, 1 year, 97 base) is the highest-rated player on a sell team; COL at 0 points with $68.11M payroll and 7 expiring are desperate.
recommendations.rationale: At 97 base and 95 speed he is transcendent for 15 playoff games. But $9.90M at age 32 is one month of rental at a cost that equals Toronto's entire surplus profit ($34.08M) minus a third. Only pursue if the club reaches the deadline in position to make a cup run.

recommendations.current: Upshall (22, $1.50M, POTE 99) + Koltsov (24, $1.10M, POTE 94) + TOR R2 2006
recommendations.proposed: Heatley (ATL, 24, 91 base, TOUG 81, CHKG 87, SPEE 97, $1.10M, 1 year)
recommendations.summary: Acquire Heatley from ATL for Upshall + Koltsov + R2; he closes the scoring void and is the first TOR player above 80 TOUG.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 0-2 with 6 expiring and $17.95M profit are in full rebuild mode; two POTE 94+ players under 25 plus a pick is their exact currency. TOR saves $1.50M payroll and gains a 91-base winger at $1.10M. Heatley's TOUG 81 plus Bell's TOUG 86 (if Proposal 2 lands) plus Tucker's 88 solves the toughness gap entirely.

recommendations.proposed: Bell (CHI, 25, 80 base, TOUG 86, CHKG 84, FACE 92, SPEE 95, $900K, 1 year)
recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell from CHI for Lundmark + R3; he simultaneously closes toughness (86), checking (84), and faceoffs (92) for $900K.
recommendations.rationale: CHI at 2 points with 8 expiring and $21.76M profit are rebuilding. Lundmark at 24 with POTE 97 is a developable speed project. Bell replaces the Oct 12 Begin package: strictly superior at TOUG (86 vs 82), FACE (92 vs 79), age (25 vs 27), and speed. Payroll effect +$100K.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Jovanovski from VAN for Klesla + R2; third priority, only if Heatley deal does not consume the R2 or if defense breaks down by February.
recommendations.rationale: VAN at $46.36M payroll (league lowest) with 13 expiring are the most motivated sellers. Jovanovski at 89 base with 91/92 toughness-checking is playoff-ready tonight. However, Bell + Heatley + Tucker already give four players at 80+ TOUG, making this supplementary. If R2 goes to ATL, drop this target.

recommendations.summary: Goalie trade monitoring task #2 is complete; Luongo is on the roster at 97 and the GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo arrived at 91 base last season, now reads 97 at 26 with 1 year at $1.60M. GM standing order 2005-03-19: 'Close all goalie monitoring.' No reopen signal exists.

recommendations.summary: Move Chlup from third line to first line centre.
recommendations.rationale: 59 points at 19 last season, currently at 17 MPG on the third line. He has been on L3 since April despite repeated recommendations to promote him.

recommendations.summary: Increase Gaborik's ice time if he is healthy; 8 MPG on the second line is too little at 23.
recommendations.rationale: 1 game played, 8.0 MPG, 1 point. POTE 90 at age 23 warrants 12+ minutes on a top-six wing.

recommendations.current: Spacek, Stahle, Colaiacovo, Upshall, Gardener, Nash, Chistov
recommendations.summary: No change for the rest of the young group after 2 games.
recommendations.rationale: All dressed with minutes appropriate to their age and role. Two-game sample does not support intervention.

recommendations.summary: No morale action needed; all dressed players at 91 after two wins.
recommendations.rationale: Everyone sits above the 90 threshold where morale gives +1 to grades. Richards at 11.5 MPG is the only light-usage case worth monitoring but at 91 after two games there is nothing to adjust.

recommendations.summary: We have no forward outside L1-L2 who checks above 75. L3 (mean 69) and L4 (mean 71) cannot play a shutdown role in any arrangement. We need a middle-six forward with checking 80+ and toughness 70+.
