recommendations.rationale: Role inventory shows only Nash 81 and Roberts 85 among forwards above 80 checking, both already deployed on L1/L2. Koltsov is scratched, McCabe is scratched, Wallin 87 faceoffs is scratched. The gap flagged in April persists into October and no line change fixes it.

recommendations.summary: The current unit composition is the best available with this roster. Moving Nash to L3 drops L2's checking to the same level L3 currently sits at, and no other swap improves either unit.
recommendations.rationale: L1 and L2 are properly built. L3 and L4 are soft because the roster has no checkers to put there, not because the wrong players are assigned. Power plays are well-stocked on both units.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming per January 19 order.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is at OVR 97. PIT scored 0 in their only game; this is not a night that demands a rest day for the starter.

recommendations.summary: Run the same lines. We win every positional matchup by at least 5 points of OVR and all four faceoffs.
recommendations.rationale: PIT's strongest forward is Lemieux at 85 against Sundin at 92. Their weakest D is Melichar at 63 against Gaborik at 99. No adjustment creates an advantage we do not already have.

recommendations.summary: No sell-list change after 2 games. Jackman, Klesla, McCabe and Eminger verdicts from last season carry forward unchanged.
recommendations.rationale: Two games is not enough to revise a full-season read. Jackman is at 1.00 pts/g but on a 2-game sample; Klesla is at 0.00 on 34.5 MPG which reinforces rather than revises the sell verdict. McCabe and Eminger are healthy scratches, consistent with prior calls.

recommendations.summary: Jackman and Klesla are eating 56% of all D minutes (33.0 and 34.5 MPG). Endurance will collapse by December at this rate. The four remaining D need to absorb more.
recommendations.rationale: Six D players dressed share 120 D-minutes per game. Pair 1 is getting 67.5 of them while the remaining four split 52.5 between them at ~13 MPG each. No one should be at 34 MPG for 82 games.

recommendations.proposed: Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81)
recommendations.summary: Bell remains the only league-wide player closing toughness, checking, and faceoffs simultaneously; the zero-at-80+ TOUG count is unchanged since spring and the season has started without him.
recommendations.rationale: No Toronto player reaches 80 TOUG. Bell's 88/86/82 in toughness, checking, and faceoffs is the single acquisition that fixes all three gaps the Coach quantified in April.

recommendations.summary: Dress Wallin (83 FACE, 25) at fourth-line centre; he is on the roster unlined and is the best draw-taker after Sundin.
recommendations.rationale: The L4 faceoff mean was 52 in April with the best available at 55. Wallin at 83 nearly doubles that. He is not a checker, but he solves the draw half of the fourth-line problem at zero cost.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker (83 CHKG, 30, 70 TOUG, $1.30M) nightly as the internal checking band-aid until an external toughness solution arrives.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker is the second-best checker on the roster at 83 and is currently unlined. He does not fix toughness but he adds the physical presence the Coach says is missing from the bottom six.

recommendations.summary: Dress Koltsov (92 SPEE, 24) to add a speed element the bottom six currently lacks; he is on the roster in no unit.
recommendations.rationale: Four players at 92+ speed are already lined (Gaborik, Afinogenov, Mogilny, Koltsov is the fifth unlined). Adding him to a bottom unit gives transition speed the Coach's system appears to reward.

recommendations.summary: The Iginla target remains the only single acquisition closing both the scoring bridge void and the toughness gap; CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him at his salary.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny (36), Sundin (34), and Roberts (39) carry 426 combined points with no under-30 inheritor. Iginla at 27 with TOUG 85 is both the scoring replacement and the toughness piece. The July window has not produced him.

recommendations.summary: Goalies are set; Luongo is arrived, Ouellet and Tellqvist provide cheap depth, and no action is needed this season.
recommendations.rationale: The March 19 standing order closed goalie monitoring. Luongo's 94/94 glove-stick grades at 26 with one year remaining is the answer the January rebuild sought.

recommendations.summary: Lock Luongo on a 5-6 year deal at July 2006 renewal; he is 26, POTE 97, and on a one-year contract at $1.60M.
recommendations.rationale: Losing the franchise goalie to UFA at 26 with POTE 97 while holding Tellqvist and Ouellet as options is a structural failure. He must be the first call in the renewal window.

recommendations.summary: Lock Chlup on a 5-6 year deal at July 2006; he is 19, POTE 95, assigned first-line centre, and carries $2.34M on one year.
recommendations.rationale: If he produces anywhere near his POTE this season, his July 2006 asking price triples. The Coach has already made him L1C; the renewal secures that investment.

recommendations.summary: Move Tucker ($1.30M, 30, POTE 79, 1 year) to a non-playoff team by the March 2006 deadline or accept losing him for nothing.
recommendations.rationale: He was the GM's designated chip in March 2005 and remains undressed. At POTE 79 and one year left, his value only decreases.

recommendations.summary: Release Roberts at July 2006; he is 39, POTE 52, $4.90M, with one year left that buys nothing.
recommendations.rationale: His playoff-mentor function has been served. One year of $4.90M at POTE 52 and age 40 is a wasted roster slot and salary line.

recommendations.summary: Accept the Sundin contract as immovable for now; $8.40M through 2009 at age 34 cannot be traded and will be dead weight by 2008.
recommendations.rationale: No club takes a 34-year-old at $8.40M with POTE 60. The loss is sunk; plan production without assuming he stays at current levels past 2007.

recommendations.summary: Lock Chlup (19, 82 base, $2.34M expiring) on a 5-6 year deal immediately at contract expiry.
recommendations.rationale: He scored 59 points at 16.9 MPG as a 19-year-old L1C. His price doubles by 20. This is the franchise centre contract.

recommendations.summary: Lock Luongo (26, 91 base, $1.60M expiring) on a 5-6 year deal immediately at contract expiry.
recommendations.rationale: He is the established number-one goalie entering his prime. No contending team lets a 91-base goalie hit the market.

recommendations.summary: Explore trading Mogilny (36, 90 base, $5.50M expiring) at the March 2006 deadline for a draft pick via the over-80 mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach flagged him for step-down in May 2005. At 36 and $5.50M he is not returning. 90 base qualifies him for pick-recovery; letting him walk in July loses that capital.

recommendations.summary: Move Klesla (23, $0.90M expiring) before the March 2006 deadline; the Coach put him on the sell list on May 31, 2005.
recommendations.rationale: Not re-signing per the Coach. Trading him for a pick or a prospect beats losing him to free agency in July.

recommendations.summary: Move Tucker (30, $1.30M expiring) at the March 2006 deadline; he was a designated chip in March 2005 and was never traded.
recommendations.rationale: Second season as an expiring asset at 30. Either converts to a pick or young player before the deadline or walks for nothing in July.

recommendations.summary: Conditional: if Spezza (22, POTE 99, $1.00M) does not earn top-nine minutes at camp, trade him at the March 2006 deadline before his POTE value decays further.
recommendations.rationale: Coach demanded on May 11 that Spezza either earn real minutes or stop dressing. 46 games at 6.7 MPG last season is the record. Reassess at camp, decide by February.

recommendations.proposed: 2-year extension at similar salary if he earns a regular role
recommendations.summary: Assess Koltsov (24, $1.10M) at camp; renew on 2 years if he contributes, otherwise let walk.
recommendations.rationale: At 24 and $1.10M he is cheap depth. A 2-year deal locks affordable roster depth without a long commitment.

recommendations.summary: Renew Ouellet (24, $0.90M) on 2 years as cheap goalie depth or let him walk if Tellqvist is ready.
recommendations.rationale: With Luongo locked long-term, the backup role is insurance. $0.90M is the cheapest insurance available. Letting him walk risks a playoff-injury scramble.

recommendations.summary: Let St. Jacques (25, $0.80M) walk in July 2006 unless injuries in the stretch make him useful.
recommendations.rationale: Depth defenceman at $0.80M. Replaceable on the free-agent market at similar cost. Not worth a renewal commitment.

recommendations.summary: No buy-or-sell posture in October. Reassess deadline stance in late January when 40+ games of data exist.
recommendations.rationale: 17 of 1230 games played, TOR has 81 remaining. The deadline is 158 days away. Toronto holds an R1, an extra R1 from Ottawa, and an R2 in the 2006 draft, so capital exists for either posture.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Jovanovski (VAN, D, 29, 89 base, TOUG 93, CHKG 94, $2.30M expiring) as the top trade target this season — he closes the toughness void and the defence cliff simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: VAN carry 13 expiring contracts, $46.36M payroll (lowest in the league), and are in rebuild mode. He is 89 overall with 93 TOUG and 94 CHKG, the highest-toughness player on any motivated seller. At 29 and expiring, VAN must get something now or lose him for nothing in July. Price will be substantial given his grade.

recommendations.summary: Target Ott (DAL, LW, 23, 72 base, POTE 97, TOUG 83, CHKG 84, $800K expiring) — the cheapest high-POTE player who closes the toughness gap while developing.
recommendations.rationale: DAL have 11 expiring contracts and cannot re-sign all of them. Ott at $800K with POTE 97 and real checking grades (83 TOUG, 84 CHKG) is exactly the manual's shape: young, cheap, high upside, on a seller. He plays bottom-six minutes today but his grades say he grows into a top-nine role.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Begin (BUF, C, 27, 73 base, TOUG 87, CHKG 95, FACE 86, $936K expiring) to fix the L4 checking-and-faceoff gap the Coach has flagged since April.
recommendations.rationale: No internal option combines TOUG 80+ with FACE 80+. Jackman tops out at 75 TOUG, Tucker at 70. Begin at 87 TOUG, 95 CHKG and 86 FACE is the single best fit for the L4 centre the Coach demands. BUF with 6 expiring and $19.07M profit are moderate sellers; a pick or depth player should suffice.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Hartnell (NSH, LW, 23, 79 base, POTE 94, TOUG 87, CHKG 88, $1.10M expiring) — elite toughness grades at 23 on a cheap expiring deal.
recommendations.rationale: NSH have only 4 expiring contracts and $21.70M profit, making them less motivated than VAN or DAL. But at 79 base with 87 TOUG, 88 CHKG and POTE 94 on $1.10M, he is the second-best young tough forward on the market after Ott. Worth a conversation if NSH listen.

recommendations.summary: Target Malec (CAR, D, 23, 73 base, POTE 97, TOUG 82, CHKG 84, $700K expiring) as the Colaiacovo replacement at the defence-development slot.
recommendations.rationale: CAR have 14 expiring contracts, the most in the league, and $19.73M profit — they must shed. At $700K with POTE 97 and toughness grades that matter (82 TOUG, 84 CHKG), he is the cheapest high-upside D available. Colaiacovo's May write-off makes this slot urgent.

recommendations.summary: Avery (LA, C, 25, 79 base, TOUG 83, CHKG 88, FACE 93, $400K, 1 year) closes all three forward gaps at the lowest price on the board, but his 6 pts in 57 GP last season is a production concern.
recommendations.rationale: LA have 6 expiring and $19.13M profit. Avery at $400K is the cheapest player in the league with 80+ TOUG, 80+ CHKG and 80+ FACE. His production was poor but the grades drive game play. He is the low-risk alternative if Begin or Conroy price out.

recommendations.summary: Wanvig (PHX, RW, 24, 74 base, POTE 94, TOUG 86, CHKG 87, $600K expiring) is a third young tough forward on a 9-expiring seller at $600K.
recommendations.rationale: PHX are 0-1-0 with 9 expiring contracts. At $600K with POTE 94 and elite toughness grades, he is a cheap developmental asset. Lower POTE than Ott or Hartnell but still 90+ and the toughness grades are comparable.

recommendations.summary: Sutton (ATL, D, 27, 78 base, TOUG 94, CHKG 90, $1.34M, 3 years) is the second-best tough D available, younger than Jovanovski but on a 3-year deal making him harder to extract.
recommendations.rationale: ATL are 0-1-0 with $17.95M profit and the second-lowest payroll at $39.32M. At 27 with 94 TOUG and 90 CHKG on $1.34M he is a bargain, but the 3 years remaining means ATL are less forced to move him than an expiring player. Pursue if Jovanovski's price is out of reach.

recommendations.summary: Conroy (CGY, C, 34, 85 base, FACE 94, CHKG 80, $2.00M expiring) remains the March deadline rental centre if we are in the race.
recommendations.rationale: CGY have 9 expiring and $22.95M profit. Already flagged in prior notes. A pure rental — not a keeper at 34 — but the best faceoff draw-taker available at a reasonable price. Only act in late February or March per the GM's standing order on timing.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker (83 CHKG), McCabe (86 CHKG), Abid (86 OVR) and Koltsov (92 SPEE) before the trade market opens — they cost nothing and give a checking-and-speed core on the bottom two lines.
recommendations.rationale: All four are rostered and unrined. Together they provide checking (Tucker, McCabe), physicality (Abid) and speed (Koltsov) that partially bridge the L4 gap while a trade is worked. The Coach should try them before the GM spends draft capital.

recommendations.summary: Lock Luongo on 5-6 years at season end (July 2006). He is 26, 91 base, POTE 97, $1.60M on 1 year. Losing him is the worst single outcome available to this club.
recommendations.rationale: The trajectory phase flagged this as the single most urgent renewal. Luongo and Chlup both expire July 2006 and must be addressed the same week. Luongo first because his replacement (Tellqvist, POTE 91) is a clear step down.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Jovanovski (89 base, 93 TOUG, 94 CHKG, $2.30M expiring, 29) from Vancouver for Klesla ($0.90M, POTE 97, SPEE 88, AGIL 87, 23) plus a second-round pick.
recommendations.rationale: VAN carry 13 expiring on $46.36M payroll (lowest in league) and are rebuilding. Jovanovski walks in July for nothing. Klesla at POTE 97 is exactly the youth asset a rebuilding team collects. We close the 80+ TOUG void (zero today) and the defence-depth gap simultaneously. Net payroll +$1.40M. Jovanovski is expiring so this is a 2005-06 rental; re-sign in July if he works or get a playoff run from him.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Begin (87 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 86 FACE, $936K, 1 year, 27) from Buffalo for Tucker ($1.30M, CHKG 92, TOUG 88, 30) plus St. Jacques ($0.80M, POTE 94, CHKG 84, TOUG 80, 25).
recommendations.rationale: Coach has flagged the L4 checking-and-drawing gap since April 2005 (checking mean 61, toughness mean 57, faceoffs 50). Begin closes all three axes. BUF have 6 expiring and $19.07M profit; Begin walks in July for nothing. Two players for one expiring centre is a fair package. Tucker is the March 2005 chip, never moved. St. Jacques is expiring and not lined. Net payroll -$1.16M. No pick required.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Avery (93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, 1 year, 25) from LA for Koltsov ($1.10M, POTE 94, ACCE 96, AGIL 92, 24) plus a third-round pick.
recommendations.rationale: Prior negotiation history (March 2005) confirmed LA wants a young POTE 94 asset, not a veteran checker. Koltsov at 24, POTE 94, ACCE 96 fills that demand exactly. LA have 6 expiring. Avery's 6 points in 57 games is ugly but his grades (93 FACE, 88 CHKG) are what the game plays up. $400K is below the pick's table price. Net payroll -$700K. Conflicts with Proposal 2 only if both are pursued (Begin and Avery both play L4 centre; only one needed).

recommendations.summary: Goalie monitoring task is closed; Luongo is on the roster at 97 and DiPietro remains at NYI on an expiring deal.
recommendations.rationale: The GM closed all goalie trade monitoring on 2005-03-19 after Luongo was acquired. Luongo is 97 overall at $1.60M with 1 year left. DiPietro at NYI is 88 on an expiring deal with 0 years left. No change since the file closed.

recommendations.summary: Dress Spezza and give him fourth-line minutes starting this game; POTE 99 at 22 with zero games last season and zero now is wasting a year.
recommendations.rationale: His minutes collapsed from 9.1 to 4.8 last season with no injury, suggesting a system-fit problem. The only way to diagnose it is playing him at all. He needs to be in the lineup and on the ice.

recommendations.summary: Dress Eminger; at 21 with POTE 99 and a 4-year contract he cannot be a healthy scratch or we waste his development year.
recommendations.rationale: The GM confirmed in May he is locked at $2.20M x 4 and not expiring. If he is not traded he must play or we burn a roster spot on a player getting no development.

recommendations.summary: Move Chlup to first-line centre; 6 MPG on the third line after scoring 59 points at 18 MPG last year is a step backward.
recommendations.rationale: Last season Chlup went 0.62 to 0.88 pts/g while minutes doubled from 11 to 18.2. He proved he can handle first-line minutes. Game one of a new season is the right time to put him back there.

recommendations.summary: At 23 with POTE 90 and healthy scratches, Gaborik's development window is closing; decide whether he is a roster piece or a trade chip this week.
recommendations.rationale: He is dressed but not playing. At 23 the development argument runs out. Either put him in the lineup or move him before his value erodes further.

recommendations.summary: No change to ice time today. The room is at 91 average and rising with the win.
recommendations.rationale: Only one game played. Chlup at 6 MPG against a calibre that expects 17 and Richards at 13 against a band of 20 are the two deficits to watch, but neither man's morale has moved yet. If Chlup is still at 6 MPG after three games his morale will start to drop.

recommendations.summary: K2 checking mean of 72 cannot be improved with available players; this is a roster gap, not a lineup problem.
recommendations.rationale: Only four players on the roster check above 80 (Jackman 91, Roberts 85, McCabe 82 scratched, Nash 81). Two PK units need six-plus bodies at 75+ checking. McCabe is scratched for development and Ottawa at 0-1 does not trigger the all-out framework. We need a checking forward in the 78-85 range who isn't Jackman or Roberts.

recommendations.summary: Lines stand as-is for a home game against a 0-1 Ottawa club.
recommendations.rationale: Ottawa is not a quality opponent requiring veteran deployment. Chemistry from camp is worth preserving, and the lines are producing at their assigned roles. No matchup reason to shuffle.

recommendations.summary: Chlup stays on L3. I am withdrawing my repeated first-line recommendation.
recommendations.rationale: He produced 0.88 pts/g on 18.2 MPG at 19 on that line last season. Per the GM's own evaluation philosophy, a kid producing on his current minutes has found his role. The development framework says give him time there.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming per January 19 order.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 97 OVR against a Lalime-led offence that scored 1 goal in their opener. The 7-point goalie gap is the easiest edge we hold tonight.

recommendations.summary: Keep all four lines as set; the auto-pairing gives us favourable matchups on three of four lines.
recommendations.rationale: Our L1 (Sundin 92, Roberts 87) handles their L1 (White 82, Alfredsson 91). Our L2 (Richards 89, Gaborik 99) crushes their L2 (Fisher 82, Hossa 86). Our L3 (Chlup 87) faces Ulmer at 70. The only line where they have any claim is their top winger group, and Roberts' TOUG 91 against Alfredsson's TOUG 69 plus Klesla's SPEE 99 against Havlat covers it.

recommendations.summary: Move Kaberle and Fischer to the first defensive pair slots; drop Klesla and Jackman to pair 2.
recommendations.rationale: Kaberle (85 OVR) got 11 MPG and Fischer (84 OVR) got 10 while Klesla and Jackman (both on sell lists) took 42 and 41. The top pair should be our best players, not our expendable ones.

recommendations.summary: Klesla is now $0.90M x 1 (expiring). The sell window is this season, not next offseason.
recommendations.rationale: Two declining seasons (0.38, 0.36 pts/g), age 23, one year left. If he gets 40+ MPG on a losing club his trade value erodes toward zero by deadline.

recommendations.summary: McCabe stays on the sell list. Already not dressed, confirming the evaluation.
recommendations.rationale: 30 years old, $3.00M x 3, final season rate 0.76 but recent window 0.48. The scratch status means even the current coaching staff (me) doesn't see him fitting.

recommendations.summary: Line Gaborik on the first or second wing before camp; he carries 92 scoring, 92 playmaking, 98 speed, and 90 clutch at 23 and is currently not in any unit.
recommendations.rationale: He is the highest-rated skater on the roster and the only player under 26 with 90+ grades across four categories. The coach already flags him as the best weapon against quality opponents.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Iginla (27, 93 base, TOUG 85, 140 pts/73 GP, $6.50M expiring) in July; he closes the toughness void and the scoring bridge simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Zero players on the roster carry TOUG 80+ and the scoring core is Mogilny (36), Sundin (34), Roberts (39). CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him.

recommendations.summary: Acquire a faceoff-winning center: Bell (24, 82 FACE, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG) or Avery (25, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K). The L4 mean is 52 FACE with no internal fix.
recommendations.rationale: The coach stated on May 5 that no bench player closes this. Sundin at 90 is the only 80+ FACE center and he is 34. Bell and Avery are the only two league-wide solutions.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Luongo (26, 94/94 glove-stick, 0.889 SV) to a 5-year deal at the end of 2005-06 when his 1-year contract expires at $1.60M.
recommendations.rationale: He enters his prime at 27 next season. A star goalie on a one-year deal is the highest-risk contract on the roster. Per the star-contract rule, 5-6 years prevents demand escalation.

recommendations.summary: After Tucker departs as a trade chip and Roberts ages out, the roster drops from 6 to roughly 3 checkers at 80+; monitor whether Fischer (82, 24) and McCabe (86, 29) are sufficient or whether a depth checker is needed.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker (83 CHKG, 30) is a March 19 chip. Roberts (86 CHKG) is 39 with an expiring deal. Upshall (80 CHKG) is in the camp-audition group. The checking depth shrinks this summer without an external addition.

recommendations.summary: Speed, stamina, and clutch coverage are adequate; 24 players at 80+ speed and 14 at 80+ stamina need no intervention.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik at 98, Afinogenov at 96, Mogilny at 94, Dvorak at 93, Koltsov at 92 provide more speed than any coach can use. Kaberle at 97 ENDU and McCabe at 94 anchor the stamina corps.

recommendations.summary: Extend Luongo on 5-6 years this summer; he is 26, POTE 97, one year at $1.60M, and he is the only goalie who can carry a playoff run.
recommendations.rationale: If he hits UFA July 2006, the replacement plan is Ouellet at 13 career games and Tellqvist at 11. No trade or free-agent market at $1.60M replaces a 91-base goalie. The extension costs at most $3-4M/year and is the cheapest insurance on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Lock Chlup on 5-6 years this summer at or near his current $2.34M; he is 19, POTE 95, 59 points in 71 games, and the Coach has named him first-line centre.
recommendations.rationale: He is the only player positioned to absorb Mogilny's 84 points within two seasons. One year at $2.34M means July 2006 UFA with a 95-POTE centre entering the market. The cost to prevent that is negligible compared to losing him.

recommendations.summary: Extend Klesla on 4-5 years at a modest raise from $0.90M; he is 23, POTE 97, played all 82 games.
recommendations.rationale: At $0.90M with one year remaining he is the cheapest over-80-POTE asset in the league. Extending him removes one name from the July 2006 list and locks a top-four blueliner at pennies.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Iginla (CGY, 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, $6.50M expiring) in July to fill Mogilny's seat and the structural toughness ceiling simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny at 36 with one year left produces 84 points; no player under 30 on the roster scored more than 66. Iginla at 27 with 140 points in 73 games closes that gap without requiring Chlup or Nash to make a leap. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring contracts and $14.43M profit cannot retain him.

recommendations.summary: If Spezza cannot be given top-six minutes for 2005-06, trade him this summer while POTE 99 holds market value; do not let him walk in July 2006 on a $1.00M deal.
recommendations.rationale: 15 points in 46 games at 6.7 MPG is a wasted year at the highest potential grade on the roster. Coach independently demanded this on May 11. One year at $1.00M means he is a UFA in 14 months with no trade return.

recommendations.summary: No action on Sundin's $8.40M for four years; factor the contract into every acquisition decision but do not attempt a trade that cannot recover value.
recommendations.rationale: At 34 with four years remaining at the league's highest salary, no club will take him without a substantial draft-pick package the GM is unwilling to spend. The money is sunk; the decision is how to score around him cheaply, which the Iginla target addresses.

recommendations.summary: Renew Luongo on 5-6 years before July; he is 26, 91 base, $1.60M, and the only goalie whose loss would be unrecoverable.
recommendations.rationale: The GM's standing order keeps Luongo as a 90+ starter. Belfour may retire; if Luongo also walks we are starting a 23-year-old in the playoffs. Lock him long-term now.

recommendations.summary: Renew Chlup on 5-6 years; he is 19, assigned first-line centre by the Coach, and the franchise centre.
recommendations.rationale: Coach assigned him L1C before preseason on 2005-05-25. At $2.34M with one year left, the cost of losing him is a rebuild at centre for the next decade.

recommendations.summary: Hold Spezza's renewal decision until September camp: renew 5-6 years if he wins top-nine minutes, trade in October if he does not.
recommendations.rationale: Coach on 2005-05-31: 'top-six minutes audition at camp or he should be dealt; 6.7 MPG and 0.33 pts/g at POTE 99 is a year wasted.' POTE 99 at 21 is tradeable value that decays if he plays another year at 6 minutes.

recommendations.summary: Do not renew Mogilny; he is 36, $5.50M, and the Iginla target replaces his production and toughness in one move.
recommendations.rationale: The April 12 target note identifies Iginla (27, 93 base, 140 pts, $6.50M expiring) as the RW priority. Mogilny's $5.50M at 36 buys a declining season; Iginla's $6.50M at 27 buys a decade.

recommendations.summary: Do not renew Tucker; he is 30, $1.30M, and the GM designated him a trade chip on 2005-03-19.
recommendations.rationale: He was flagged expendable before the deadline, not moved, and has no role in the Coach's development plan for 2005-06.

recommendations.summary: Renew Ouellet 2-3 years at $0.90M; he is 23 and the only backup goalie if Belfour retires.
recommendations.rationale: The GM's Feb 19 order required a capable backup for the playoffs, naming Ouellet. If Belfour walks in July, Ouellet is the only other option. Cheap depth at a critical position.

recommendations.summary: Renew Klesla 2-3 years; he is 23 at $0.90M on the blueline.
recommendations.rationale: Young, cheap, at a position where depth is needed. No reason to release and re-acquire later at higher cost.

recommendations.summary: Renew St. Jacques 2-3 years; he is 24 at $0.80M, the cheapest blueliner on the expiring list.
recommendations.rationale: At $0.80M he is the lowest-cost option for a third pair or call-up. Releasing a 24-year-old defenceman to save $0.80M is not worth it.

recommendations.summary: Release Koltsov if he does not make the roster at September camp; he is 24 at $1.10M with no development flag.
recommendations.rationale: Not in the Coach's camp audition group, not flagged for development, and $1.10M for a player without a role is money better spent elsewhere.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla (CGY, 27, 93 base, $6.50M expiring) in July as the Mogilny replacement; his departure funds the signing.
recommendations.rationale: The April 12 note identifies him as the top RW target closing both the scoring void and the toughness ceiling. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him.

recommendations.current: Spezza (21, POTE 99, $1.00M expiring) + Koltsov (24, POTE 94, $1.10M expiring) + TOR 4th-round pick
recommendations.proposed: Bell (24, CHI, 82 base, 92 FACE, 86 TOUG, 84 CHKG, $900K expiring)
recommendations.summary: Trade Spezza, Koltsov, and the 4th-rounder to Chicago for Bell to close both the toughness and faceoff gaps simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Coach quantified L4 checking mean 61 and toughness mean 57 with no internal fix. Bell at 92 FACE and 86 TOUG solves both at $900K. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring want young players with upside; Spezza at POTE 99 and Koltsov at ACCE 96 serve that rebuild. Coach has already said Spezza should be dealt if top-six minutes don't appear. We net-save $1.20M in payroll.

recommendations.proposed: Stuart (25, SJ, 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91, ~4 years control)
recommendations.summary: Trade Colaiacovo and the OTT 1st-rounder to San Jose for Stuart to replace Roberts on the second pair with eight years of control.
recommendations.rationale: Coach flagged Colaiacovo as a write-off on May 15 (31 GP, 17.9 MPG, 0.39 pts/g). Stuart closes the Roberts replacement gap at 87 base with POTE 91 and eight years remaining. SJ at 72 points with 13 expiring on $45.39M need to rebuild and would value a POTE 99 defenceman at 22 plus a 1st rounder. Less certain than Bell because SJ may want to build around Stuart.

recommendations.summary: If Bell falls through, trade Tucker to LA for Avery as a cheap faceoff solution at $400K.
recommendations.rationale: Avery at 93 FACE closes the faceoff gap the Coach quantified at 52-mean on L4. He is a partial toughness answer (83 TOUG, not 86 like Bell). LA at 79 points with 14 expiring have roster clutter and might shed even a $400K player for Tucker plus salary relief. Acceptance uncertain given LA's improved position versus the 48-point team from February.

recommendations.proposed: Cammalleri (22, LA, POTE 98, 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M UFA)
recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri off the LA UFA pool in July at $1.10M to begin building the post-Mogilny scoring core.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 79 points with 14 expiring cannot retain both Cammalleri and Frolov. At 22 with POTE 98 and 60 points in 61 games, he is the highest-value player hitting free agency. The scoring bridge from Mogilny (84 pts, 36) and Roberts (81 pts, 39) to a successor under 30 has no internal answer; Cammalleri is the closest external one at $1.10M.

recommendations.proposed: Luongo on a 5-6 year extension at season's end
recommendations.summary: Renew Luongo on a 5-6 year deal at season's end; losing him in July 2006 leaves only Ouellet and Tellqvist.
recommendations.rationale: The trajectory phase called this the renewal emergency: Luongo at 26 with 91 base and POTE 97 carries one year at $1.60M. No other player under 30 can absorb 45 starts. Lock him at the same time as Chlup (also 1-year, POTE 95, L1C per Coach) and Klesla (1-year, POTE 97, 82 GP).

recommendations.proposed: Chlup on a 5-6 year extension at season's end
recommendations.summary: Renew Chlup on 5-6 years simultaneously with Luongo; he is 19 with POTE 95, 59 points in 71 games, and carries the Coach's L1C assignment.
recommendations.rationale: Coach named Chlup L1C on May 25. At 19 with 59 points in 71 games and POTE 95, losing him in 14 months reopens centre in a thin market. His $2.34M is already above the market rate for his age; a 5-6 year extension locks it.

recommendations.summary: Give Gardener a full camp audition next season; zero games at POTE 98 and age 20 is a wasted asset.
recommendations.rationale: Gardener has 0 GP, 0 MPG, POTE 98. No other young player on the roster has been kept out entirely. He needs real game action to know if he belongs.

recommendations.summary: Give Stahle a real look at camp; 4 games all year with POTE 96 at 21 is abandonment, not development.
recommendations.rationale: Stahle got 17.8 MPG in his 4 games but zero points. The staff clearly saw something top-pair in his role but never built on it. Camp is the reset.

recommendations.summary: Pencil Colaiacovo for top-pair minutes next season with Eminger expiring and Klesla on the sell list.
recommendations.rationale: Colaiacovo at 31 GP but 17.9 MPG when in, POTE 99, age 22. He's already playing top-pair minutes when he's dressed — he just hasn't been dressed consistently.

recommendations.summary: Camp decides Spezza: 46 games at 6.7 MPG is not developing anyone. Either he earns real minutes or stop dressing him.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza POTE 99, age 21, morale 88 (lowest on the youth group), 6.7 MPG and 0.32 pts/g. The pattern of games without minutes hasn't produced growth.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev at 0.55 pts/g outproduces Chistov and Upshall (both 0.29) who hold L3/L4 spots; he deserves a dressed role next season.
recommendations.rationale: Alexeev 30 points in 55 games at 8.3 MPG while Chistov and Upshall get 13.1 and 7.9 MPG respectively for identical production rates. The mismatch has been flagged since April.

recommendations.summary: Assign Chlup to first-line centre at camp; 59 points and 16.9 MPG at 19 confirms he belongs there permanently.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup 87% share, 71 GP, 59 points, POTE 95, morale 100. He has outperformed every other centre on the roster and the role change has been recommended since April with no action.

recommendations.summary: Set Chlup at first-line centre before camp begins.
recommendations.rationale: 0.88 pts/g on 18.2 MPG at 19 with minutes still rising. His rate improved 42% purely from harder usage with no grade movement -- he outperforms his card. This has been recommended four times and never set.

recommendations.summary: Give Spacek, Upshall and Spezza a real audition at camp or stop dressing them next season.
recommendations.rationale: All three saw minutes collapse to under 5 MPG with no grade movement. Spacek 16.0 to 5.2, Upshall 13.4 to 4.8, Spezza 9.1 to 4.6. The year is a write-off for each; camp is the only lever.

recommendations.summary: Begin planning for Mogilny and Roberts to step down from top-nine roles within 1-2 seasons.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny 1.62 to 0.83 at 36 on 19.1 MPG. Roberts 1.29 to 0.86 at 39 on 21.4 MPG. Both still produce but the slope is steep and the minutes load is heavy for their age. Chlup and Gaborik can absorb the role.

recommendations.summary: No change to Gaborik's role; his 1.12 pts/g on 21.2 MPG over 58 games is elite production at 23.
recommendations.rationale: The 1.42 early rate was a hot start regressing to mean, not a decline. Minutes are still rising.

recommendations.summary: No morale changes needed. Every dressed player is at 100 and trending up.
recommendations.rationale: The winning streak has everyone happy. Upshall and Spacek at 94 are the only dressed players below 100, both rising, both on minutes appropriate to their depth-tier calibre. No line adjustment addresses anything tonight.

recommendations.summary: Dress Wallin in place of Upshall on the fourth line against Dallas.
recommendations.rationale: L4 faceoff mean is 53 with best 59. Wallin wins draws at 88. Upshall is at 4.9 MPG and 0.29 pts/g so we lose no offense; we gain 29 points of faceoff capability against a quality opponent.

recommendations.summary: Leave L1, L2, and L3 as they are for Dallas.
recommendations.rationale: L1 checking mean 80 and L2 scoring mean 87 are the right shapes for the top two matchups. L3 speed 92 and playmaking 85 give us transition offence against their third pair. The auto-pairing puts Jackman/Fischer on their top line and McCabe/Kaberle on their second, which is correct.

recommendations.summary: PK units are correctly built; no adjustment.
recommendations.rationale: K1 has checking 80 and stamina 89 with Sundin's 95 faceoffs. K2 has checking mean 84, the best of any unit. Both have what a kill needs.

recommendations.summary: We still lack a fourth-line centre who both checks and wins draws. Wallin patches the faceoff hole but is not a checker.
recommendations.rationale: L4 checking mean is 72, best 87, but the faceoff best on that line (even with Wallin) tops out at 88 versus opponents' centers. A true shutdown centre with 80+ checking and 55%+ draws would close this permanently.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming per January 19 order.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo reads 97 OVR. Last call on May 31 was taken with no game between saves, so he should be rested. Turco at 95 means we need our best in net.

recommendations.summary: Leave all lines as-is. The auto-pairing puts our second and third lines against DAL pairs rated 68 and 67, and we lead the season series 5-1-1.
recommendations.rationale: DAL's PP is 10.8%, their bottom six is Messier at 44 and Gilmour at 41, and our defensive matchups at L2 and L3 are lopsided in our favour. Nothing to fix.

recommendations.summary: Sell Klesla this offseason before he walks as an unrestricted free agent at 24 with 1 year remaining.
recommendations.rationale: Final season rate 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG, second consecutive decline. Contract is 1 year at $0.90M — if we wait, we get nothing.

recommendations.summary: Sell Jackman this offseason at $0.70M x 2 for top-pair minutes cheap; his rate dropped to 0.46 on 29.6 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: Final season at 0.46 pts/g on 80 games. The cheap salary and high minutes make him attractive to a contender. One year less control than when first flagged; move before the pool narrows.

recommendations.summary: Sell McCabe while he still carries a 0.76 season line; his true current rate is closer to 0.50.
recommendations.rationale: Season rate 0.76 masks a 58-game window of 0.48. At 29, 3 years, $3.00M, every month of delay lowers the return.

recommendations.summary: No urgency on Eminger — he is not expiring. Contract is $2.20M x 4, not the short deal I misread in March.
recommendations.rationale: 0.36 pts/g on 15.5 MPG at 21 is poor but he is locked up. Correcting my March 30 note which called him expiring.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Avery (LA, C, 25, 93 FACE, 88 CHKG, 83 TOUG, $400K, 2y) to close the faceoff, checking, and toughness gaps on L4 simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: The coach needs a centre at FACE 80+, CHKG 85+, TOUG 80+ on the bottom six. No Toronto player meets even one of those thresholds at centre. Avery is the only player in the league meeting all three, and at $400K with 2 years left he fits the timeline. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring deals are motivated sellers.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81) to close the toughness and checking void on the forward group.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto has zero players at TOUG 80+. Bell at 88 is the highest available. His ENDU 71 requires short shifts but at 24 with POTE 81 the upside justifies it. CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring deals and $29.46M profit are sellers. Faceoffs do not apply because Bell plays wing.

recommendations.summary: Line Gaborik (23, 92 overall, SPEE 98) at camp; he carries the second-highest speed grade on the roster and is in no unit.
recommendations.rationale: A 92-overall 23-year-old sitting in no unit is either a system-fit problem or a waste of the best internal scoring bridge after Mogilny. The coach's system-fit review must resolve him.

recommendations.summary: Line Koltsov (24, SPEE 92) at camp or move him; he is the third-fastest player on the roster and plays no unit.
recommendations.rationale: Two players with 90+ speed sitting idle while the team has a 4th-line gap is a utilisation failure. If he cannot make top-nine, his speed trades for the depth Toronto lacks elsewhere.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring) in July as the answer to the scoring bridge Mogilny (36) leaves behind.
recommendations.rationale: No player under 30 on this roster produces at Mogilny/Sundin/Roberts rates. Iginla closes both the scoring void and the toughness ceiling (85 TOUG) in one move. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring deals cannot retain him. The salary is the problem to solve in negotiation.

recommendations.summary: Goalie coverage is adequate per the GM's March 19 order; Luongo (26) and Belfour (40) cover the present, Ouellet (23) and Tellqvist (25) the future.
recommendations.rationale: GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19. The depth is two 90+ options now and two developmental options at 23 and 25. I do not revisit.

recommendations.summary: Sign Gaborik to a 6-year deal this July; 99 points at 23 on $1.10M is the single most valuable renewal on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: His contract expires with the 13-player cluster. At 99 points in 82 games, POTE 90, age 23, he is the best player the club owns and the cheapest star in the league. A bidding war in July risks losing the franchise's offensive engine.

recommendations.summary: Sign Richards to a 5-6 year deal alongside Gaborik; 66 points at 25 on $1.00M cannot walk in the same summer.
recommendations.rationale: He and Gaborik together carry 165 points at $2.10M combined. Both expire simultaneously. Losing either creates a top-six hole that no internal replacement fills next season.

recommendations.summary: Sign Eminger (21, POTE 99, $1.20M) and Nash (20, POTE 95, $1.20M) to 5-6 year deals; both expire this July and are decade-long building blocks.
recommendations.rationale: Eminger has 23 points in 64 games at 21 with potential of 99. Nash scored 39 points at 20. Both are cheap now and will not be after a strong 2005-06 season. The GM has protected them from trade; lock them from free agency.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla (CGY, 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, TOUG 85) as a UFA or sign-and-trade this July; he is 27 and closes both the Mogilny scoring void and the toughness ceiling simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: The 30-33 age bracket has exactly one player (Tucker, 3 GP). Iginla fills it at 27 while producing more than Mogilny (84 pts) or Sundin (91 pts) individually. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him.

recommendations.summary: Move Tucker (30, $1.30M, 2 years, 1 GP) this off-season; he occupies the empty 30-33 bracket without contributing.
recommendations.rationale: One game played, one point, $1.30M per year. He is the only player between 26 and 33, which makes him either trade bait for a contender needing depth or a release. The GM already flagged him as a chip on March 19.

recommendations.summary: When Chlup's deal becomes renegotiable, extend to 6 years immediately; 59 points at 19 with POTE 95 makes him the franchise centre for the next decade.
recommendations.rationale: He is on 2 years at $2.34M, coming up in July 2006. His rate of 0.83 pts/g at 19 with potential of 95 means the second contract is the one that matters. Signing him to 6 years then locks the centre position through age 27.

recommendations.summary: Sundin stays. 5 years at $8.40M is expensive but he is 34 with 91 points and POTE 60 means his grade will not collapse suddenly.
recommendations.rationale: The contract runs through 2009-10 when he will be 39. The $8.40M is the most expensive on the roster, but profit at $55.69M absorbs it easily, and his production this season (91 pts) shows no decline yet. Moving a 34-year-old with 5 years and no market is not feasible.

recommendations.summary: Sign Gaborik to a 5-6 year deal immediately when free agency opens.
recommendations.rationale: 23, 91 base, POTE 90, 67 pts/45 GP, currently $1.10M. The highest-value player on the expiring list and the one a bidding war would hurt most.

recommendations.summary: Sign Eminger to a 5-6 year deal alongside Gaborik.
recommendations.rationale: 21, POTE 99, GM's January 19 veto on trading him stands. Lock before camp so the 2005-06 build has two untouchable young D.

recommendations.summary: Sign Kaberle on 5-6 years at $1.90M.
recommendations.rationale: 27, prime-age defenceman, named in the December 2004 staggered-lock plan. Eight years of window remain.

recommendations.summary: Sign Nash to 5-6 years before the system-fit review concludes.
recommendations.rationale: 20, $1.20M, in the Coach's system-fit review but that is a coaching question. Lock him before a camp performance or a poor preseason changes his asking price.

recommendations.summary: Sign Richards on 3-4 years, not 5-6, pending the Coach's system-fit review.
recommendations.rationale: 25, 70 FACE, 85 PASS, $1.00M. The Coach collapsed his rate on flat minutes and is reviewing his fit. A shorter term preserves the option to reprice if he stalls.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk at $2.70M. Do not offer renewal.
recommendations.rationale: 39 years old, part of the 426-point aging core the Coach flagged. No development left, and the $2.70M is the best contribution he can still make to this roster.

recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour a one-year reduced-salary deal after the playoffs; if declined, let him go.
recommendations.rationale: 40, $6.50M expiring, GM expected him to decline a reduced offer. Luongo is the number one. Do not carry a 40-year-old past this contract.

recommendations.summary: Sign Abid to a 2-3 year deal at or near $0.40M.
recommendations.rationale: 25, TOUG 80, CHKG 80, 0.70 pts/g on 11.5 MPG. Cheapest toughness on the market. Insurance if the Bell acquisition fails.

recommendations.summary: Sign Tellqvist on 2-3 years as Luongo's backup.
recommendations.rationale: 25, GM's January 15 order: stays, high-90s potential, give him time. $0.80M saves no money but holds the position.

recommendations.summary: Trade Chistov (22, POTE 95) to Chicago for Bell (24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 82 FACE) in July.
recommendations.rationale: Coach named Chistov tradeable on May 5 and the fourth-line faceoff mean of 52 is unsolved without Bell or Avery. CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring are motivated sellers.

recommendations.summary: Do not offer Alexeev a contract before camp; decide after his top-nine audition.
recommendations.rationale: Coach's May 29 order: top-nine audition or stop carrying him. A $1.10M deal signed before camp removes the incentive.

recommendations.summary: Do not offer Upshall a contract before camp; decide after his audition.
recommendations.rationale: Same Coach instruction as Alexeev, May 29. 21, $1.20M expiring, camp-audition-or-cut. Sign 2-3 years only if he makes the roster.

recommendations.summary: Offer Colaiacovo a 2-year prove-it deal, or trade his POTE 99 in July if camp confirms the write-off.
recommendations.rationale: Coach wrote him off May 15: 31 games, 17.9 MPG, 0.39 pts/g despite POTE 99. A 5-6 year commitment is off the table; a trade preserves the 99's market value.

recommendations.summary: At the June 8 rookie draft, use the fourth-round pick on a goalie if a high-potential one is available.
recommendations.rationale: GM's January 22 standing order to scout for goalie drafts. Toronto holds no pick above the fourth round; a fourth-rounder on a goalie is the cheapest path to depth behind Luongo and Tellqvist.

recommendations.summary: Sign Iginla as a free agent in July: 94 overall, 128 points/76 GP, 87 TOUG, 27 years old, contract_years = 0 from a 70-point club with 10 expiring deals.
recommendations.rationale: Closes the Mogilny/Sundin/Roberts scoring void (426 combined points, no successor under 30) and raises the team's toughness ceiling from 75 to 87 simultaneously. CGY at $14.38M profit and 70 points cannot retain him against a competitive offer.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Kovalchuk: 90 overall, 138 points/79 GP, age 22, 78 TOUG, POTE 85, $1.10M expiring from a club with 11 expiring deals who cannot retain both him and Heatley.
recommendations.rationale: 138 points at 22 for $1.10M is the best production-to-cost ratio in the league. ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring must choose between Kovalchuk and Heatley; whichever they keep, the other becomes available as a UFA in July.

recommendations.summary: Sign or trade for Havlat: 89 overall, 103 points/82 GP, age 24, POTE 85, $900K, contract_years = 1 from a 77-point club with 11 expiring deals.
recommendations.rationale: Under $1M for a 24-year-old with 103 points is the cheapest high-end scoring available. OTT cannot retain 11 expiring players at $42.80M payroll with 77 points. His TOUG 68 does not close physical gaps but his production bridges the scoring cliff.

recommendations.summary: Sign Gagne as a free agent now: 86 overall, 108 points/82 GP, age 25, POTE 80, $2.40M, contract_years = 0. PHI at $66.73M payroll and $2.12M profit are the most financially desperate club in the league.
recommendations.rationale: PHI must shed salary; Gagne at $2.40M on a $66.73M payroll with barely $2M profit is a priority cut. 108 points at 25 from a club that cannot afford him is a straight UFA signing opportunity.

recommendations.summary: Sign Marleau as a free agent: 88 overall, 98 points/71 GP, age 25, POTE 82, $1.60M, contract_years = 0. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring deals cannot retain him.
recommendations.rationale: A 25-year-old center with 88 overall and 98 points at $1.60M. He is the Sundin successor the trajectory phase identified as missing. Already a free agent; requires only a competitive offer.

recommendations.summary: Sign Brewer as a free agent: 87 overall, 82 TOUG, 93 CHKG, POTE 83, age 26, 61 points/82 GP, $2.00M, contract_years = 0. SJ at 76 points cannot retain 13 expiring players.
recommendations.rationale: Best available defenceman closing the toughness gap now that Chara is off the table per the GM's Feb 19 order. 82 TOUG clears the 80 threshold; 93 CHKG clears the coach's 85 bar. Already a free agent.

recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri: 83 overall, 60 points/61 GP, age 22, POTE 97, $1.10M, contract_years = 1. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring deals will likely prioritize Frolov over him.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 97 is the highest available forward ceiling outside our own roster. 60 points in 61 games at 22 says he is close now. LA cannot retain all 14 expiring players; Frolov (POTE 95, same position) likely takes priority.

recommendations.summary: Explore a trade for Holik: 81 overall, FACE 94, 86 TOUG, 92 CHKG, 86 points/82 GP, age 34, $9.00M, contract_years = 3. NYR at $78.14M payroll with $0 profit must shed salary.
recommendations.rationale: The only player in the league at 94 FACE and 86 TOUG simultaneously; he closes the faceoff and toughness gaps at centre in one body. But 34 years old and $9M with 3 years left means this is a two-year bridge, not a long-term fix. NYR's financial desperation is the angle.

recommendations.summary: Trade for Conroy: 85 overall, FACE 94, 102 points/82 GP, age 33, $2.00M, contract_years = 1. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring deals are motivated sellers.
recommendations.rationale: 94 FACE closes the L4C faceoff gap and 102 points is top-six production from a centre. At $2.00M he costs a fifth of Holik. But 33 and expiring means a rental unless he signs a re-signing cheaply. A one-year fix on the way to developing Chlup or Spezza.

recommendations.summary: Sign Heatley if ATL keeps Kovalchuk: 88 overall, 131 points/79 GP, age 24, POTE 85, $1.10M, contract_years = 1. Mirror target to Kovalchuk.
recommendations.rationale: 131 points at 24 for $1.10M. ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring cannot retain both him and Kovalchuk. Whichever ATL keeps, the other becomes available. Pursue the one they let go.

recommendations.summary: Explore a trade for Stuart: 87 overall, POTE 91, 80 TOUG, 91 CHKG, age 25, $1.80M, contract_years = 1. Higher ceiling than Brewer at the same club.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 91 with 80 TOUG and 91 CHKG at 25 gives the best long-term defensive profile available. But SJ will fight to re-sign a POTE 91 blueliner at $1.80M; probability is lower than Brewer who is already a free agent.

recommendations.summary: The coverage phase's claim that no forward on this roster has 80+ TOUG is wrong: Abid is at 94 TOUG, 80 CHKG, 81 overall, 66 points/82 GP, $400K. The coach's May 29 instruction to give him 16+ MPG is the correct fix, not a new acquisition.
recommendations.rationale: Abid at 94 TOUG clears the 80 threshold the coach set. The gap is one additional 80+ forward, not zero. An acquisition above Abid (Bell at 88 TOUG, Primeau at 91 TOUG) adds depth, not the first body. The priority acquisitions (Iginla, Kovalchuk, Heatley) add toughness as a byproduct of their scoring.

recommendations.current: Upshall (TOR, 21, RW, POTE 99, CHKG 87, $1.20M, 1yr) + St. Jacques (TOR, 24, D, POTE 94, $0.80M, 2yr, 1 GP)
recommendations.proposed: Heatley (ATL, 24, RW, 88 base, 131 pts/79 GP, POTE 85, $1.10M, 1yr)
recommendations.summary: Trade Upshall and St. Jacques to Atlanta for Dany Heatley; ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring deals cannot re-sign both him and Kovalchuk.
recommendations.rationale: We get 131 points from a 24-year-old at $1.10M for two players producing 20 combined points. Toronto nets $900K savings; ATL adds $900K against a payroll shedding 14 contracts. Coach flagged Upshall as audition-or-cut; trading while POTE 99 holds is better than releasing. Acceptance uncertain — AI valuation of POTE 99 against POTE 85 is not known.

recommendations.current: Koltsov (TOR, 24, LW, POTE 94, ACCE 96, AGIL 92, $1.10M, 2yr, 19 pts/38 GP, no unit)
recommendations.proposed: Avery (LA, 25, C, 77 base, 9 pts/82 GP, FACE 93, CHKG 88, TOUG 83, $400K, 2yr)
recommendations.summary: Swap Koltsov to Los Angeles for Scott Avery; he is the only player at 93 FACE, 88 CHKG and 83 TOUG simultaneously at centre, closing all three coach-demanded gaps in one body.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 79 points with 14 expiring cannot use a 9-point checking centre; Koltsov's ACCE 96 and POTE 94 are what a rebuild hoards. We save $700K in payroll. Koltsov is in no unit and Gaborik at 99 points is the primary scoring bridge, so the cost is manageable.

recommendations.current: Colaiacovo (TOR, 22, D, POTE 99, $1.10M, 1yr, 12 pts/31 GP) + 4th-round pick
recommendations.proposed: Havlat (OTT, 24, LW, 89 base, 103 pts/82 GP, POTE 85, $900K, 1yr)
recommendations.summary: Trade Colaiacovo and the 4th-rounder to Ottawa for Michael Havlat; OTT at 77 points with 11 expiring deals cannot retain him.
recommendations.rationale: Coach called Colaiacovo a development write-off on May 15: 0.39 pts/g in 31 games at 17.9 MPG. He is a trade piece by the Coach's own assessment. We get 103 points at 24 for $900K, saving $200K. POTE 99 against 103 points is the hardest ask of the three; acceptance is least certain.

recommendations.proposed: Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 94 overall, 128 pts/76 GP, 87 TOUG, POTE 80, $6.50M, contract_years = 0)
recommendations.summary: Sign Jarome Iginla as a free agent; he closes the 426-point veteran scoring void and the toughness ceiling simultaneously with no trade required.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 70 points with $14.38M profit cannot match a competitive offer. Our $55.69M profit funds a 5-6 year deal at $7-8M without touching the roster. No other single move fills both the 30-33 age void and the scoring bridge in one body.

recommendations.proposed: Gagne (PHI, LW, 25, 86 overall, 108 pts/82 GP, POTE 80, $2.40M, contract_years = 0)
recommendations.summary: Sign Simon Gagne as a free agent; 108 points at 25 for $2.40M is the cheapest 100-point forward in the league.
recommendations.rationale: PHI at $66.73M payroll with $2.12M profit are the most financially distressed club and must shed salary. A second top-six left winger pairs directly with Gaborik at right wing and adds depth the current roster lacks.

recommendations.summary: Goalie trade window task is closed; Luongo is on the roster at 94 and the GM shut all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19.
recommendations.rationale: The original ask was to track Luongo availability and DiPietro development as a path to a high-90s backup. Luongo is here. The GM closed the task explicitly on 2005-03-19.

recommendations.summary: Give Alexeev a top-six look at camp next season; his 0.55 pts/g in 55 games exceeds Chistov and Upshall who hold those roles.
recommendations.rationale: Alexeev produced at double the rate of Chistov (0.29) and Upshall (0.29) while getting only 8.3 MPG. The mismatch is confirmed over a full half-season.

recommendations.summary: Stahle needs a full camp audition next September; 4 games at 21 with POTE 96 is not a development plan.
recommendations.rationale: He got 17.8 MPG in his 4 appearances, proving he was considered ready, then was abandoned. The club owes him a real look before deciding his future.

recommendations.summary: Spezza needs a top-six minutes audition at camp or he should be dealt; 6.7 MPG and 0.33 pts/g at POTE 99 is a year wasted.
recommendations.rationale: His minutes collapsed from 9.1 to 4.8 MPG during the season. The season is a write-off. Camp is the only lever left.

recommendations.summary: Chlup, Nash, Spacek, Eminger, Chistov, Upshall, and Klesla all got games in line with their production this year.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup 71 GP/16.9 MPG/0.83 pts/g earned it. Nash and Spacek are on tracks that need offseason review, not a mid-season correction. Chistov and Upshall produced at rates consistent with their minutes.

recommendations.summary: Assign Chlup to first-line centre at the start of next camp, before any preseason games.
recommendations.rationale: 0.88 pts/g on 18.2 MPG at 19, up from 0.62 on 11.0. Minutes doubled and rate rose. He is the only young player who grew into a bigger load this season.

recommendations.summary: Move McCabe to the sell list for the offseason trade window.
recommendations.rationale: Season final is 0.48 pts/g on 21.5 MPG across 82 games, well below the 0.60 threshold. At 29 with 4 years and $3.00M the return on a declining defenceman exceeds his on-ice value.

recommendations.summary: Koltsov's trade value is dropping fast — 1.10 to 0.29 pts/g across the window. Move him before his numbers make him undressable.
recommendations.rationale: GM wants him as a trading chip and he is, but 0.29 on 9.9 MPG at 24 is a depreciating asset. A return is available now; by next season it may not be.

recommendations.summary: Kaberle is trending up (0.54 to 0.62 pts/g on minutes rising from 19.4 to 21.5). No change needed; he is in his prime.
recommendations.rationale: Both rate and minutes rose simultaneously at 27. The GM's January call to make him untouchable is confirmed by the trend.

recommendations.summary: Give Chistov a bigger role next season. He doubled minutes from 9.5 to 14.0 MPG while holding his rate at 0.30 at age 22.
recommendations.rationale: Earning ice time without losing production is the development signal we want from a 22-year-old. He has earned trust.

recommendations.summary: Every dressed player is at 100 morale; no ice-time adjustments are warranted.
recommendations.rationale: All 18 skaters and both goalies in the lineup read 100, the ceiling. Spezza at 88 is the only player below 90, is trending up (+3), and is scratched for this game. Nothing to fix.

recommendations.summary: Dress Gaborik against Dallas; he is the highest-rated skater on the roster and this is a quality opponent where the 'go all out' principle applies.
recommendations.rationale: Dallas is 42-24. Gaborik is 98 scoring, 99 playmaking, 99 speed, 99 clutch. The Jan 15 standing order says maximize quality against top opponents. His grade is the ceiling for this club.

recommendations.summary: The roster holds no faceoff winner below L3. Best on L4 is 55; we need a centre who wins draws and plays 12-14 minutes.
recommendations.rationale: Faceoff winners available: Sundin 91, Chlup 80, Roberts 76, Richards 75. All four are on L1-L3. The fourth line's 52 mean means we lose zone time every draw. This persists across arrangements.

recommendations.summary: K2 is the strongest checking unit (84 mean, Jackman 90) and correctly built for shutdown duty.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup developing PK alongside Jackman (90 checking) and McCabe (85) is the right growth path at 19. Tucker in his checking role holds it together.

recommendations.summary: No line changes for Dallas. The auto-pairing already puts our best D pair on Modano and gives our L2 and L3 their softest opponents.
recommendations.rationale: DAL D pair 1 is Boucher 75/Zubov 83 (matched to our L1), pair 2 is Matvichuk 73/Berenweig 68 (matched to our L2), pair 3 is 65/65 (matched to our L3). Defensively, Modano 88 gets Fischer 85/Jackman 86 whose CHKG 92 and SPEE 94 match his game. Season series is 5-1-1 with 20 goals on 7 games; these lines produced that.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming per January 19 order.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo OVR 94, morale 100. DAL's last 10 is LLLWWLWOWW at 2.00 GF per game; he is the man for a quality opponent even at 10.8% PP.

recommendations.summary: Sell McCabe this offseason at 29, $3.00M x 4, 0.76 season rate with 0.48 recent window.
recommendations.rationale: Full season confirms 0.76 pts/g but the back half is 0.48. At 29 with four years remaining the return on a declining defenceman exceeds keeping him.

recommendations.summary: Trade Jackman this offseason. 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG at $0.70M x 3 is pure trade bait.
recommendations.rationale: Season rate ticked down from 0.48 in March to 0.46 over 80 games. His value is the cheap top-pair minutes package a contender will pay for.

recommendations.summary: Sell Klesla. 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG, second declining season in a row.
recommendations.rationale: Confirmed second consecutive decline: 0.38 at 22, 0.37 at 23. $0.90M x 2 is the exit window before he drops below useful trade value.

recommendations.summary: Move Eminger before July. 0.36 pts/g on 15.5 MPG at $1.20M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Season rate slid from 0.38 in March to 0.36 final. Expiring contract means the last window for any return closes with free agency.

recommendations.summary: Iginla (CGY, 27, 93 base, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring) is the only single acquisition closing the scoring void, the toughness ceiling, and the scoring bridge simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Zero Toronto players at 80+ toughness; Mogilny (36) and Sundin (34) carry 426 combined points with no under-30 replacement. Iginla at 140 points in 73 GP with TOUG 85 closes all three. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring deals cannot retain him.

recommendations.summary: Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE) is the cheapest player closing both the toughness and faceoff voids, and CHI are motivated sellers at 73 points with $29.46M profit.
recommendations.rationale: Only Sundin (90) draws above 80 at faceoffs, and zero players check above 75 in TOUG. Bell solves both in one body. ENDU 71 means short shifts initially but he is 24 with POTE 81.

recommendations.summary: Avery (LA, C, 25, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2 years left) is the cheapest option closing all three gaps simultaneously at a fraction of Bell's asking price.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 48 points with 13 expiring deals are selling. Avery's $400K over two years is below every other option. His FACE 93 alone fixes the L4 draw problem (currently 52 mean) without a roster rotation.

recommendations.summary: Gaborik (23, 92 scoring, 98 speed) is on the roster but in no unit; deploying him adds a young 90+ scorer without any trade cost.
recommendations.rationale: The scoring role reads 10 at 80+ but three are 34+. Gaborik is the highest-speed player on the roster (98) with 92 scoring and 90 clutch. If he cracks a top-nine role, the external scoring need softens and trade packages can focus on toughness/faceoffs instead.

recommendations.summary: Koltsov (24, 92 speed) is unlined; deploying him provides speed depth that frees Fischer (89 speed, 82 CHKG) for a checking role or a trade.
recommendations.rationale: 21 players at 80+ speed means surplus exists only if the coach uses it. Koltsov in the lineup lets Fischer shift to the L3/L4 checking role where his 82 CHKG matters, or becomes tradeable without weakening speed.

recommendations.summary: Stuart (SJ, D, 25, 87 base, 89 CHKG, POTE 91) replaces Roberts (39) with eight years of development; SJ at 72 points with 13 expiring may not deal him but the fit is exact.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts at 39 carries 86 CHKG and 90 clutch; his decline creates a top-four D hole by 2007. Stuart at 25 with POTE 91 and 89 CHKG is the only identified replacement. Acceptance uncertain at 72 points.

recommendations.summary: Goalies are solved: Luongo (26, 2y) plus Ouellet (23, 2y) is the post-Belfour pair; no acquisition needed before next summer.
recommendations.rationale: GM closed goalie monitoring on March 19. Ouellet's INTE 69 and ENDU 60 are thin but he is 23 with two years of development left, and Luongo at 92 overall with 45 GP is a confirmed number one.

recommendations.summary: Offer 5-6 year extension deals to these five first in July; they are 20-27, carry POTE 90-99, and $21.30M of Toronto contracts expire simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik scored 99 points on $1.10M, Richards 66 on $1.00M, Nash 39 at age 20, Eminger POTE 99 at 21, Kaberle 44 points at 27. Payroll at $60.04M against $53.43M profit easily absorbs raises. Losing two or more of these in one summer guts the core.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla with a player package this July; Toronto owns no pick better than a 4th-rounder so the return must come from the Coach's system-fit casualties.
recommendations.rationale: Iginla at 93 base, 140 points, age 27, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring closes both the Mogilny scoring void and the toughness ceiling. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him.

recommendations.summary: Do not renew Belfour ($6.50M, age 40) or Roberts ($2.70M, age 39); saves $9.20M and both are replaced.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo (91 base, 26, 2 years left) and Ouellet (POTE 97, 23, 2 years) cover the goalie position. Roberts at 39 with POTE 52 has no succession path. The $9.20M freed helps fund the young-core raises.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik on 5-6 years before July; he is 23, POTE 90, $1.10M expiring, and the only under-30 player with the scoring profile to bridge Mogilny/Sundin/Roberts.
recommendations.rationale: The January urgency was directionally right — his contract simply could not be touched mid-term. Now it is expiring and re-signing is the mechanism. No other player under 30 on this roster carries his speed and shot combination.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger on 5-6 years; 21, POTE 99, $1.20M expiring, GM-protected core piece whose ceiling is set high.
recommendations.rationale: GM explicitly protected Eminger from trade in January. POTE 99 at 21 means his best hockey is four or five years away. Lock him now while the salary is $1.20M.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle on 3-4 years; he is 27, $1.90M expiring, and in his prime as a top-pairing blueliner.
recommendations.rationale: A 27-year-old defenseman with real minutes is expensive on the open market. Three or four years locks the prime without over-committing to a player who is not a franchise pillar.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards on 3-4 years after camp if the system-fit review clears him; 25, $1.00M, 70 FACE, 85 PASS.
recommendations.rationale: At $1.00M and 25, he is cheap for a middle-six centre. Renew after the Coach's review resolves, not before.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Abid on 2 years at $0.40M; his TOUG 80 and CHKG 80 give the bottom six its checking element at near-rookie cost.
recommendations.rationale: Coach wants him at 16+ MPG and his rate held at 0.70 while minutes dropped. At $0.40M this is the cheapest rosterable toughness Toronto has.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Tellqvist on 2-3 years; 25, POTE high-90s, $0.80M. GM standing order is to let him develop.
recommendations.rationale: He saves no money by leaving and his development path is behind Luongo. Two or three years keeps the prospect alive without blocking.

recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour one year at reduced salary; at 40 and $6.50M he likely declines, and that is an acceptable outcome with Luongo at 94 on 2 years.
recommendations.rationale: GM said he stays if he accepts reduced. Luongo (94 displayed, 91 base, $1.60M, 2 years) plus Tellqvist is a sufficient goalie group for a contender. The $6.50M is better deployed on a scorer.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts go at 39 and $2.70M; his production is not replaceable at his cost, and the Stuart trade target fills the same defensive role three years younger.
recommendations.rationale: 39 years old on $2.70M expiring. The scoring bridge void requires investment in youth, not retention of veterans whose ceiling is behind them.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, $6.50M expiring) as a July UFA or trade; he closes the scoring bridge and adds TOUG 85 simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him. This is the single acquisition that solves the structural void the Coach and I have both flagged.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81) as a UFA or trade; his FACE 82 is the only league-wide answer to L4's mean of 52.
recommendations.rationale: Coach has quantified the gap twice. Bell is 24, cheap to acquire from a selling club, and closes both the faceoff and checking deficits the lineup has carried all season.

recommendations.summary: Auto-draft the single 5th-round pick on June 8; no package capital exists beyond it.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto owns no pick better than a 5th rounder. The draft adds a body at best; it does not solve the roster gaps.

recommendations.summary: Do not renew Chistov, Colaiacovo, Upshall, or Alexeev before camp; their expiring deals are the audition the Coach demanded.
recommendations.rationale: All four sit in the Coach's 'make it or stop dressing us' group. Committing salary before they prove it wastes money that the Iginla or Bell acquisitions need.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Iginla from CGY via Nash-based package: 93 base, 85 TOUG, 128 pts/76 GP, age 27, $6.50M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: He closes the scoring void (Mogilny 36, Sundin 34, Roberts 39 roll off), the toughness ceiling (zero Toronto forwards at 80+ TOUG), and the scoring bridge (27 years old, prime ahead). CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him. Nash (20, POTE 96, 90 TOUG) is the package piece CGY's rebuild would want.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell from CHI: 80 base, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 82 FACE, age 24, $900K with 2 years left.
recommendations.rationale: He is the only player in the league closing toughness (95 TOUG vs Toronto's zero at 80+), faceoffs (82 vs L4 mean of 52), and checking (93) simultaneously. At 24 with 2 years left he is a keeper, not a rental. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit are rebuilding but profitable, which makes them selective sellers. Package requires a young player they value.

recommendations.summary: Pursue whichever ATL scorer becomes available in July: Kovalchuk 138 pts/79 GP age 22, or Heatley 131 pts/79 GP age 24, both $1.10M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring cannot re-sign both. If they miss the playoffs one walks in July. At $1.10M on a 130-point player this is the cheapest scoring in the league. Neither closes toughness or faceoffs, but either solves the scoring bridge if Iginla falls through.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Komisarek from MTL: 77 base, 85 TOUG, 92 CHKG, POTE 92, age 23, $1.10M expiring, 82 pts/82 GP.
recommendations.rationale: He closes the defence-side toughness gap (85 TOUG, 92 CHKG; Toronto has no defender above 87 CHKG besides Jackman and McCabe who stay), replaces Roberts' physical presence, and at POTE 92 age 23 has the highest development ceiling of any available blueliner. MTL at 66 points with 15 expiring are the league's worst team and must sell.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Cammalleri in July UFA if LA cannot retain him: age 22, POTE 98, 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Highest potential ceiling on the market after Iginla. At POTE 98 age 22 on $1.10M, if LA cannot keep both him and Frolov (14 expiring at 79 points), he tests the market. He does not close toughness or faceoffs but his ceiling makes him worth roster space.

recommendations.summary: Backup plan if Bell trade fails: Avery at $400K, 2 years left, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, age 25.
recommendations.rationale: Closes toughness at bargain cost but POTE 71 and 9 points in 82 games mean he will never be more than a checker. Only worth pursuing if Bell is unavailable and the GM needs a cheap fourth-line body. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring are motivated sellers.

recommendations.summary: Request Sulku as part of an Iginla package: age 21, 84 TOUG, POTE 90, $943K expiring from CGY.
recommendations.rationale: If we're already at the table with CGY for Iginla, Sulku is 21 with 84 TOUG and POTE 90 on an expiring $943K deal. He's not ready for top-nine (5 pts in 40 GP) but provides depth toughness and potential. Could also be a piece CGY requests in the reverse direction.

recommendations.summary: Do not pursue Thornton (BOS): 94 base but BOS at 97 points will not sell a 25-year-old centre.
recommendations.rationale: BOS at 97 points with only $43.97M profit have no reason to move their young centre. The POTE of 74 alongside 59 games (injury-shortened) and the prior 76-vs-94 discrepancy note make his true value uncertain. No package Toronto can construct without picks gets BOS to say yes.

recommendations.summary: Package Nash (20, POTE 95, TOUG 88), Tucker (30, CHKG 92) and the 4th-rounder to Calgary for Iginla (27, 93 base, 85 TOUG, 128 pts in 76 GP, $6.50M expiring).
recommendations.rationale: Iginla closes the 426-point scoring bridge, the zero-toughness-at-80 ceiling, and the age-void simultaneously. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain his salary; Nash at POTE 95 with 88 TOUG at 20 is a rebuild centerpiece. Net payroll cost is +$4.00M, trivial against $53.43M profit.

recommendations.summary: Send Chistov (22, POTE 95, SPEE 89, expiring) and Upshall (21, POTE 99, CHKG 87, expiring) to Chicago for Bell (24, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 82 FACE, 80 base, $900K, 2 years left).
recommendations.rationale: Both are Coach-flagged surplus: Chistov explicitly tradeable per May 5, Upshall in the camp-audition-or-cut group. Bell uniquely solves toughness and faceoffs at once. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit gain two POTE 95+ speed prospects; Bell's 28 pts in 80 GP and ENDU 71 make him expendable in their rebuild. Net payroll saving $1.40M for us.

recommendations.summary: Koltsov (24, POTE 94, ACCE 96, 19 pts in 38 GP, $1.10M, 2 years) to LA for Avery (25, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, POTE 71, 2 years).
recommendations.rationale: Speed has 21 players at 80+ and Koltsov played only 38 games. Avery provides 83 TOUG and 88 CHKG in 82 games at $400K, solving L4 checking. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring gain a POTE 94 prospect. Risk: trading POTE 94 for POTE 71 is bad long-term value; only pursue if Iginla and Bell both fail.

recommendations.summary: Owed item #2 is complete and closed; no further monitoring required.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo (94, 26, $1.60M, 2 years) is on our roster. GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19. The task this item described no longer exists.

recommendations.summary: Assign Chlup to first-line centre at the start of next camp, before any preseason games.
recommendations.rationale: 59 points in 71 games at 19, 0.83 pts/g on 16.9 MPG. He outscored every other centre and earned the role months ago. The GM has not moved him all season; camp assignment is the last chance before next year locks.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza a real camp competition for a top-nine forward spot next preseason rather than a depth role.
recommendations.rationale: 46 games, 6.7 MPG, 0.33 pts/g. He never got a sustained stretch to show what his scouting number means. Camp is the only lever left for this year's wasted development.

recommendations.summary: Give Alexeev a top-nine audition at camp; if he does not make it, stop carrying him.
recommendations.rationale: 30 points in 55 games (0.55 pts/g) outproduced Chistov and Upshall who both played 68 games. The mismatch was never resolved during the season.

recommendations.summary: Stahle gets a camp look at the blue line or he stops being dressed.
recommendations.rationale: 4 games, 0 points. The blue-line depth blocked him all year but a fourth year on the roster with no look is a wasted asset.

recommendations.summary: No change for Nash. His role and minutes are appropriate for a 20-year-old at 0.57 pts/g.
recommendations.rationale: 39 points in 69 games on 13.1 MPG. His mid-season rate dip is flagged for offseason review but his usage was fair.

recommendations.summary: Assign Chlup to first-line centre for next season before camp begins.
recommendations.rationale: 0.88 pts/g on 18.2 MPG at 19 with both rate and minutes climbing. He outproduced every TOR centre this season.

recommendations.summary: Give Abid 16+ MPG next season; his rate held at 0.70 while minutes dropped from 20.1 to 11.5.
recommendations.rationale: A 0.70 winger on 82 games getting 11 minutes is a wasted asset. His production didn't decline, his role did.

recommendations.summary: System-fit review for Afinogenov, Richards, and Nash before camp. All three collapsed their scoring rate on flat minutes.
recommendations.rationale: Afinogenov 1.17 to 0.73 on 16.8 MPG, Richards 1.08 to 0.71 on 16.9 MPG, Nash 0.83 to 0.42 on 13 MPG. No injuries, no minutes cut. The pattern is identical across all three and points at how I'm using them, not them.

recommendations.summary: Spacek, Spezza, and Upshall all need a real camp audition next season or they should stop being dressed.
