recommendations.rationale: Spacek 0.28 pts/g on 5.2 MPG, Spezza 0.24 on 4.6 MPG, Upshall 0.27 on 4.8 MPG. All buried, all declining, all at 19-21. The season gave no reason to keep dressing them without a role change.

recommendations.summary: Klesla is a sell this offseason. Two consecutive declining seasons confirm it.
recommendations.rationale: 0.50 to 0.31 pts/g on flat 15 MPG. Second year of decline at 23. His value is highest now before the slide continues.

recommendations.summary: Jackman must be sold. The 30 MPG load has destroyed his production.
recommendations.rationale: 0.65 to 0.39 pts/g on 29.4 MPG. Confirmed collapse across the full season. His value is the cheapest top-pair minutes; that doesn't last.

recommendations.summary: McCabe goes back on the sell list. The hot start is fully gone.
recommendations.rationale: Season final is 0.48 pts/g. The recent-window 0.48 confirms the early 1.42 was a hot streak. At 29, four years, $3.00M the return beats keeping him.

recommendations.summary: No lineup change for morale. Spezza at 88 is the only sub-92 reading, it is rising (+3), and the GM's maximize-quality order against Dallas keeps the current lineup correct.
recommendations.rationale: Every other player is at 92 or above and most are at 100 with positive momentum. The room does not need intervention.

recommendations.summary: L1 is the best unit we ice and needs no adjustment.
recommendations.rationale: Checking mean 79, scoring 88/95, speed 91/95, faceoffs anchored by Sundin at 91. This is the line that should match their top unit.

recommendations.summary: L4 faceoff mean of 52 is a roster gap, not an arrangement problem. No forward on this roster outside L1-L2 wins draws above 80.
recommendations.rationale: Abid at 87 checking and 72 toughness is the only identity player. Nobody else on the bench can win a faceoff or check above 80 for this line. This needs a trade, not a lines change.

recommendations.summary: K2 at 84 mean checking is the highest of any unit and the correct identity kill.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker at 94 checking displayed, McCabe at 85, Jackman at 90. Well-constructed checking kill that needs no change.

recommendations.summary: Fourth-line checking and faceoff depth remain unsolved: no forward outside L1-L2 checks above 85 or wins a faceoff above 80, and L4's mean faceoff of 52 will be punished by competent centres.
recommendations.rationale: The entire forward checking inventory tops out at 85 (Roberts, McCabe, Fischer — all D-men in the audit). Tucker at 94 is the only forward checker and he is on L3. A bottom-six centre who wins draws and checks 80+ is the missing piece.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming.
recommendations.rationale: OVR 94 vs Turco at 94. No reason to sit him at home against a 42-24-7 team. Standing order from January 19: verify the streak cell is not showing a tired goalie icon before locking it in.

recommendations.summary: No lineup change for Dallas.
recommendations.rationale: Auto-pairing sends Fischer/Jackman (92 CHKG each) against Modano's line, which is the right match. Our second and third lines face 65-73 OVR defensemen, which is already the easiest assignment the lineup can draw. The season series is 4-1-1 and we are at home with 133 points. Nothing to fix.

recommendations.summary: Trade Eminger before July; after that he leaves for nothing.
recommendations.rationale: 0.36 pts/g in 64 games, expiring $1.20M, 21 years old. The regular-season deadline passed and he is still here. Two months remain before he is a UFA loss.

recommendations.summary: Sell McCabe this offseason while his trade value still supports a return.
recommendations.rationale: 0.76 season rate but 0.48 recent window at age 29 on $3.00M x 4 years. Every week of holding him costs return value.

recommendations.summary: Sell Jackman; his 30 MPG at $0.70M is worth more to a club that needs top-pair volume.
recommendations.rationale: 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG. Cheap and durable but his production does not justify top-pair minutes in our system.

recommendations.summary: Sell Klesla; two consecutive declining seasons mean his upside is gone.
recommendations.rationale: 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG at 23, down from 0.38 at 22. $0.90M x 2 years of no-growth asset.

recommendations.slot: bottom-six LW or C with toughness
recommendations.summary: Toughness (0 at 80+) and faceoffs (1 at 80+) are structural gaps no internal move closes; Bell and Avery remain the only targets.
recommendations.rationale: Best TOUG on roster is 75 (Jackman); only Sundin at 90 draws above 80. Coach quantified L4 faceoff mean at 52 on 2005-05-05 and stated no bench player fixes it.

recommendations.summary: Iginla at 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, 27, $6.50M expiring is the only player closing the Mogilny/Sundin/Roberts scoring void without requiring a young player to jump.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny 36, Sundin 34, Roberts 39 carry 426 combined points; no player under 30 is positioned to absorb that. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him.

recommendations.summary: Checking at 6 players above 80 is thin but adequate if Tucker is dressed; no additional D-side checking acquisition is required before the Iginla target takes priority.
recommendations.rationale: Jackman 87 CHKG (24), McCabe 86 CHKG (29), Tucker 83 (30), Fischer 82 (24), Upshall 80 (21), Roberts 86 (39). Five viable beyond Roberts. Depth is present.

recommendations.summary: Stuart at 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, 25, POTE 91 replaces Roberts's 39-year-old body with eight years of runway; pursue in July after the Iginla package.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts is 86 CHKG and 88 scoring at 39. Durability 98 cannot overcome the age curve indefinitely. SJ at 72 points with 13 expiring on $45.39M cannot retain all of them, though at 72 they may resist dealing a POTE 91 blueliner.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik on a 5-6 year deal before any other renewal or acquisition.
recommendations.rationale: 99 points at 23 on $1.10M expiring. POTE 90. The highest-scoring player on expiring money and the cheapest top-six salary on the roster. If he walks in July, 99 points vanish with no internal replacement.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards on a 5-6 year deal, second priority after Gaborik.
recommendations.rationale: 66 points at 25 on $1.00M expiring, POTE 88. The oldest non-expiring core player is 25 (Afinogenov), so Richards is the bridge between the veterans and the under-22 group.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash on a 5-6 year deal.
recommendations.rationale: 39 points in 69 games at age 20, POTE 95, expiring at $1.20M. Locking Nash at 20 means the left wing position is covered through age 25-26, which is his prime.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger on a 5-6 year deal.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 at 21, 23 points in 64 games, expiring at $1.20M. Highest potential rating on the roster. The GM vetoed trading him in January on exactly this reasoning.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle on a 3-4 year deal.
recommendations.rationale: 44 points in 74 games at 27, POTE 75. Past his development window but the most productive blueliner on this roster. Three or four years is the right term for a player at his age.

recommendations.summary: The age curve at 23 and under is sound: 13 players, eight with POTE 95+ in the lineup.
recommendations.rationale: The manual targets six high-potential players and three-to-four playing every night. This roster has eight lined at POTE 95+. The depth is not the problem; the bridge above 23 and below 34 is.

recommendations.summary: Sign Gaborik to a 5-6 year extension immediately at the start of free agency.
recommendations.rationale: Age 23, POTE 90, $1.10M expiring. The cheapest high-ceiling asset we have; any bidding war prices us out of the extension window.

recommendations.summary: Sign Kaberle to a 5-6 year extension before July.
recommendations.rationale: Age 27, $1.90M expiring. The blueline anchor; losing him starts a rebuild on defence while Eminger and Colaiacovo are still developing.

recommendations.summary: Sign Richards to a 5 year extension at $1.00M or slightly above.
recommendations.rationale: Age 25, 70 FACE, 85 PASS. The Coach's fourth-line faceoff void is quantified at a 61 checking mean; Richards at third line is the internal solution.

recommendations.summary: Sign Eminger to a 5 year extension at approximately $1.20M.
recommendations.rationale: Age 21, POTE 99, $1.20M expiring. GM vetoed trading him in January; he is the long-term top-pair defenceman.

recommendations.summary: Sign Nash to a 5 year extension despite the Coach's system-fit review.
recommendations.rationale: Age 20, $1.20M expiring. The Coach's concern is fit and confidence, not talent; he is two years younger than Gaborik and the cost to re-sign rises every year we wait.

recommendations.summary: Renew Tellqvist for two years at $0.80M.
recommendations.rationale: Age 25, high-90s POTE per the GM. Two years lets him develop as the future starter without a long commitment at $0.80M.

recommendations.proposed: Belfour (2 year, reduced salary) or release
recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour two years at reduced salary; if he refuses, let him walk and hand the net to Luongo with Tellqvist as backup.
recommendations.rationale: Age 40, $6.50M expiring. The GM's Jan 15 order is to offer reduced pay and accept if he walks; his retirement risk makes a longer deal dangerous.

recommendations.summary: Release Roberts or offer two years at a significant pay cut (below $1.50M).
recommendations.rationale: Age 39, $2.70M expiring, one third of the 426-point old guard. At 39 there is no development path and the money funds a Bell or Cammalleri package.

recommendations.summary: Renew Colaiacovo for one year only as a camp audition; if he does not earn a role by November, trade him.
recommendations.rationale: Coach flagged him as a development write-off on 2005-05-15 after 31 games at 0.39 pts/g on 17.9 MPG. A one-year deal keeps the option without committing past this year.

recommendations.summary: Renew Chistov for two years at $1.10M as depth; the Coach has already moved Alexeev ahead of him.
recommendations.rationale: Age 22, POTE 95, $1.10M. GM's March 19 order protects him from trade. Two years at a flat salary preserves the option to use him as a package piece next summer if Alexeev takes the spot permanently.

recommendations.summary: Renew Upshall for one year at camp terms; his roster spot is conditional on camp performance per the Coach.
recommendations.rationale: Age 21, $1.20M, named in the camp audition group on 2005-05-11. One year keeps the option without blocking Alexeev.

recommendations.summary: Renew Alexeev for one year; the Coach projects him ahead of Chistov and Upshall at camp.
recommendations.rationale: Age 23, $1.10M, in the camp audition group. One year proves whether the Coach's faith is justified before committing.

recommendations.summary: Renew Abid for one year at $0.40M; he is the cheapest toughness on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: Age 25, TOUG 80, CHKG 80, $0.40M. No reason not to keep him at that salary.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla in July via a player-for-player trade; he closes the 426-point scoring void from one position.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny is 36, Sundin 34, Roberts 39. No player under 30 is positioned to absorb their production. Iginla at 93 base and 27 fills the void and arrives at the same $6.50M Belfour would cost.

recommendations.proposed: Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82)
recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell to close both the toughness gap (mean 57) and the faceoff gap (mean 50) on the fourth line simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach quantified both voids on 2005-04-09 and states no bench player fixes them. Bell is the only league-wide player who closes both. CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring are motivated sellers.

recommendations.summary: Sign Iginla as a UFA in July: 128 pts/76 GP, TOUG 85, SPEE 98, 27, $6.50M, from CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Closes the 256-point scoring cliff and raises the toughness ceiling from 75 to 85 simultaneously. CGY at $14.43M profit with 10 expiring contracts cannot retain him at that salary.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell from CHI: TOUG 95, CHKG 93, FACE 87, POTE 82, 24, $900K, 2 years remaining. Trade Spezza plus a D prospect or Colaiacovo plus the 4th-rounder.
recommendations.rationale: The only player in the league who raises toughness above 80 AND faceoffs above 87 AND checking above 90 in a single acquisition. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit are motivated sellers.

recommendations.summary: Sign Kovalchuk if he reaches the market: 138 pts/79 GP at 22, SPEE 99, $1.10M expiring from ATL (84 pts, 11 expiring).
recommendations.rationale: Best production-to-age-to-cost ratio in the league. ATL cannot retain both him and Heatley on expiring rookie deals. At 22 with POTE 84 he is three years from peak.

recommendations.summary: Sign Thornton if BOS lets him walk: 83 pts/59 GP at 25, TOUG 80, CHKG 81, FACE 78, $4.00M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: A top-two centre who adds toughness to the scoring group and pushes Richards to 2C. BOS at 97 points with 13 expiring must make cuts, though their $34.32M profit makes retention more likely than with other clubs.

recommendations.summary: Sign Gagne as a UFA: 108 pts/82 GP, 25, SPEE 96, $2.40M from PHI at $66.73M payroll with only $2.14M profit and 13 expiring.
recommendations.rationale: PHI's financial position forces them to shed salary. Gagne is 108 points at 25 for $2.40M, the second-best scoring-per-dollar in this pool after Kovalchuk.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Stuart from SJ: 87 base, TOUG 74, CHKG 83, POTE 92, SPEE 94, 25, $1.80M expiring. Replaces Roberts.
recommendations.rationale: SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring cannot keep him and Marleau both. Stuart brings speed and potential to a blueline that loses Roberts at 39. POTE 92 at 25 means five more years of development.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Komisarek from MTL: TOUG 85, CHKG 92, POTE 92, 23, $1.10M, 82 pts/82 GP at D. MTL at 66 points (worst in league) with 15 expiring.
recommendations.rationale: TOUG 85 and CHKG 92 at D would make him the toughest blueliner on the roster by 10 points. MTL are selling everything at 66 points and cannot retain him.

recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri as a UFA: 60 pts/61 GP at 22, POTE 98, $1.10M expiring from LA (79 pts, 14 expiring).
recommendations.rationale: Highest potential on any available player at POTE 98. Already producing 60 points in 61 games at 22. LA cannot retain him and Frolov on expiring deals at $52.43M payroll.

recommendations.summary: Sign Belanger as a UFA: FACE 96, CHKG 77, TOUG 73, 27, $700K from LA (79 pts, 14 expiring).
recommendations.rationale: The cheapest faceoff solution in the league at $700K. FACE 96 gives the third line a draw-taker capable of handling any opponent's checks without burning Bell or Avery's minutes.

recommendations.summary: Sign Conroy as a rental UFA: FACE 95, 102 pts/82 GP, 33, $2.00M from CGY (70 pts, 10 expiring). Two-year deal maximum.
recommendations.rationale: Bridge piece at centre while Chlup develops. 95 FACE and 102 points give the second line production and draws immediately. At 33 he is a two-year solution, not a long-term answer.

recommendations.current: Spezza (21, C, POTE 99, $1.00M, 2 yr) + Chistov (22, LW, POTE 95, $1.10M, exp) + Tucker (30, LW, POTE 79, $1.30M, 2 yr) + 4th-round pick
recommendations.proposed: Iginla (27, RW, 93 base, 128 pts/76 GP, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Offer Spezza + Chistov + Tucker + 4th-rounder to Calgary for Iginla; they shed $6.50M on a $45.93M payroll with 10 expiring and get a franchise centre in Spezza (POTE 99, 21, 2 years of control) plus two more assets to develop or flip.
recommendations.rationale: CGY finished 70 points with $14.43M profit and cannot retain Iginla plus nine other expiring contracts. Spezza gives them a 21-year-old centre with the highest POTE we hold; Chistov is a speed winger (SPEE 89, ACCE 88) on expiring they can extend cheaply or flip; Tucker adds CHKG 92 for the present. We gain the 128-point scorer who closes the 426-point Mogilny/Sundin/Roberts void and raises team toughness from 75 to 85 in one move. Net payroll +$1.90M, absorbed by $51.14M profit.

recommendations.current: Upshall (21, RW, POTE 99, $1.20M, exp, CHKG 87) + Tucker (30, LW, POTE 79, $1.30M, 2 yr, CHKG 92/TOUG 88)
recommendations.proposed: Bell (24, LW, TOUG 95, CHKG 93, FACE 87, POTE 82, $900K, 2 years remaining)
recommendations.summary: Offer Upshall + Tucker to Chicago for Bell; they shed a role player for a POTE 99 prospect with CHKG 87 plus a physical veteran, and the $1.60M net payroll increase is irrelevant against $31.73M profit.
recommendations.rationale: Bell closes toughness (95), checking (93), and faceoffs (87) simultaneously — the three gaps the coach has quantified since April with no internal fix. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring have no reason to protect POTE 81 when they can get a POTE 99 winger and a CHKG 92 veteran. Upshall's CHKG 87 fits a physical identity; Tucker adds one more season of checking. We net -$1.60M payroll and gain the only player on the sheet above 80 in all three categories.

recommendations.current: Colaiacovo (22, D, POTE 99, $1.10M, exp) + Upshall (21, RW, POTE 99, $1.20M, exp) + 4th-round pick
recommendations.proposed: Komisarek (23, D, 82 base, TOUG 85, CHKG 92, POTE 92, 82 pts/82 GP, $1.10M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Offer Colaiacovo + Upshall + 4th-rounder to Montreal for Komisarek; at 66 points with 15 expiring they must stockpile youth and they will not re-sign him at $1.10M against 15 other deals.
recommendations.rationale: Komisarek at 82 points from the blueline at 23 with TOUG 85 and CHKG 92 is the Roberts replacement the blueline needs, and MTL at 66 points (league worst) with 15 expiring contracts cannot keep him. Two POTE 99 players plus a pick is exactly the currency a 66-point rebuilding team craves. Colaiacovo specifically is the coach's flagged development write-off. Payroll unchanged ($2.30M both ways).

recommendations.summary: Task #2 is closed: Luongo is acquired (94, 26, 2 years), and the GM explicitly ordered all goalie monitoring stopped on 2005-03-19.
recommendations.rationale: The January 19 task was to track Luongo and DiPietro for a goalie trade window. Luongo arrived at 91 base in February and now reads 94; the GM closed the topic twice (Feb 19 'Goalies are solved. Done.' and Mar 19 'Close all goalie monitoring'). No further work exists.

recommendations.summary: Stahle must get a real camp audition next season. 4 games in 82 with POTE 96 is a development failure I own.
recommendations.rationale: He averaged 17.8 MPG in his 4 games, which shows he can handle top-pair minutes. The club made zero attempt to build him into a rotation piece.

recommendations.summary: Spezza needs a real camp audition or he stops being dressed. POTE 99 at 21 on 6.7 MPG is not a plan.
recommendations.rationale: His minutes collapsed from 9.1 to 4.8 MPG between February and March and his rate dropped with them. 46 games at 0.32 pts/g.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev's 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG while scratched is unresolved since April. He is 23 and needs a real decision: play him or stop dressing him.
recommendations.rationale: He outproduces dressed wingers Chistov and Upshall (0.29 each) by nearly double on less than half their ice time.

recommendations.summary: Nash's rate halved from 0.83 to 0.43 with flat minutes and no injury. Flag for offseason system-fit review alongside Afinogenov and Richards.
recommendations.rationale: 39 points in 69 games at 13.1 MPG. The role did not change, the production did.

recommendations.summary: Assign Chlup to first-line centre before camp begins.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup went 0.62 to 0.88 pts/g while minutes rose from 11.0 to 18.2 over 71 games at 19. He outproduces Richards (0.71) and carries a rising trajectory. Richards at 0.71 on flat minutes belongs in the second-line spot for now.

recommendations.summary: McCabe is the top defensive trade candidate this offseason: 0.48 pts/g at 29 on a declining trend.
recommendations.rationale: Season settled at 0.48 over 82 games, down from an early 1.42 pace. At 29 with 4 years and $3.00M his return on a declining rate is worth more than keeping him.

recommendations.summary: Jackman is the second defensive sell: 0.39 pts/g on 29.4 MPG at 24, confirming the load is killing his production.
recommendations.rationale: Dropped from 0.65 to 0.39 while carrying 29.4 MPG over 80 games. His value is the cheapest top-pair minutes in the league at $0.70M x 3. Best return comes this offseason.

recommendations.summary: Klesla is the third defensive sell: 0.31 pts/g at 23 on a second consecutive declining season.
recommendations.rationale: Went 0.50 to 0.31 on flat 14.9 MPG over 82 games. Two straight down years at age 23 is not a blip.

recommendations.summary: Eminger's contract expired and he must be moved or re-signed before he walks as a UFA.
recommendations.rationale: Flat at 0.37 pts/g on 15.9 MPG, age 21. No growth, no decline. His contract is done and he provides nothing without a new deal or a trade.

recommendations.summary: Roberts at 39 played 21.4 MPG and his rate fell from 1.29 to 0.86. Plan next season around reduced minutes or his departure.
recommendations.rationale: The 4.9 MPG jump from 16.5 to 21.4 at age 39, combined with a 33% rate drop, is an unsustainable combination. Sundin (34, 21.7 MPG) and Mogilny (36, 19.1 MPG) show the same pattern. These three veterans are aging fast.

recommendations.summary: Spezza (4.6 MPG, 0.24 pts/g), Spacek (5.2 MPG, 0.28 pts/g) and Upshall (4.8 MPG, 0.27 pts/g) all need real camp auditions next fall or should stop being dressed.
recommendations.rationale: All three 21-year-olds lost two-thirds of their minutes and their scoring rate collapsed simultaneously. Spacek is below the 8 MPG floor I set in March. Camp assignment is the only lever left this season.

recommendations.summary: Koltsov's trade value is dropping fast — 1.10 to 0.29 pts/g on flat minutes — and we should move him early this offseason if we move him at all.
recommendations.rationale: GM holds him as a chip (standing order 2005-01-15). At 24 with 9.9 MPG and 0.29 over 38 games, his value is bleeding. Early offseason is the best window.

recommendations.summary: Gaborik's rate dip from 1.42 to 1.12 is explained by his 2.4 MPG increase. He stays the top winger.
recommendations.rationale: 1.12 pts/g on 21.2 MPG over 82 games at 23 is an elite line. No action needed.

recommendations.summary: Room is healthy; no player needs a minutes adjustment before Dallas.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza at 88 is the only sub-90 and he is scratched by GM design, recovering (+3). Everyone else is 94 or above with minutes matching their band.

recommendations.summary: L4 stays as-is; faceoff mean 52 with best 55 is a roster gap, not an arrangement problem.
recommendations.rationale: No available forward wins draws outside L1-L2. Spacek, Abid and Upshall are the only bodies. The April 13 checking-gap finding still holds.

recommendations.summary: Chlup stays on PK2 despite the development cost; no replacement exists with checking above 75 outside L1-L2 forwards already assigned.
recommendations.rationale: Pulling him saves defensive-zone reps for a 19-year-old at 0.88 pts/g, but Jackman 90, Roberts 85, McCabe 85 and Fischer 85 are all already committed to PK units. The checking-forward gap forces his hand.

recommendations.summary: Keep the lines as they are for Dallas.
recommendations.rationale: Dallas has three defensive pairs aged 32, 34, 32, 27, 27, 35 with agility ratings of 62, 80, 70, 70, 58, 65. Our auto-paired lines put Nash (92 speed), Chistov (99 speed) and Afinogenov (93 speed) directly onto that blue line. The season series is 3-1-1. No adjustment improves a matchup already in our favor.

recommendations.summary: Sell list unchanged since May 2nd: McCabe, Jackman, Klesla, Eminger. Fischer and Kaberle stay.
recommendations.rationale: Jackman's rate crept from 0.48 to 0.46 (80 GP), Eminger's from 0.38 to 0.36 (64 GP). Both confirm existing sell calls. McCabe and Klesla are season-complete and unchanged. No new candidates emerged.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik on a 6-year deal in July 2005 before any other renewal.
recommendations.rationale: 99 points at 23 years old with POTE 90 on a $1.10M salary. He is the highest-rated forward on the roster and the single most expensive loss if he walks to a competing offer.

recommendations.summary: Lock Richards, Nash and Eminger on 5-6 year deals in the same July window as Gaborik.
recommendations.rationale: Richards (66 pts/80 GP, 25), Nash (39 pts/69 GP, 20, POTE 95), Eminger (POTE 99, 21) are the next tier of the core. Combined with Gaborik they are 227 points from four players aged 20-25. Losing any one forces a rebuild that the draft capital cannot fund.

recommendations.summary: Sign Iginla as a UFA in July if CGY does not re-sign him.
recommendations.rationale: 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, 27 years old, TOUG 85, $6.50M. Closes the Mogilny scoring void (84 pts at 36, declining to 0.79 pts/g) and the RW gap simultaneously. Against $48.88M profit, $6.50M is noise. No draft pick or player needed.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle on a 4-year deal, not 5-6, to stagger the next renewal wave.
recommendations.rationale: Kaberle (27, 44 pts/74 GP, $1.90M) is solid but POTE 75 caps him. Four years puts his renewal in 2009, one summer after the 2007 wave, splitting the load. A six-year deal at 27 creates a 33-year-old on a large contract with limited upside.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Abid on a 2-3 year deal; he is 66 points on $0.40M with POTE 94 and must not walk.
recommendations.rationale: 82 GP, 66 pts, 25 years old, POTE 94, earning $0.40M. He is the cheapest production on the roster. Even a 3-year deal at $1.50M is a bargain. If he hits UFA, every physical winger in the league will bid for him.

recommendations.summary: If Chistov is displaced by Alexeev per the Coach, trade him this summer for a player who fills the faceoff and checking void rather than losing him for nothing.
recommendations.rationale: Coach states Alexeev displaces Chistov (2005-05-05). Chistov is 22, POTE 95, $1.10M expiring. Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, 82 FACE, 88 TOUG, POTE 81) is the only league-wide solution to the 4C role-gap but CHI wants more than one forward. Chistov plus another piece may bridge the gap.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik on 5-6 years at the first renewal window in July; he is the single most important re-signing on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: Age 23, POTE 90, $1.10M expiring. The mid-contract renegotiation the GM corrected as impossible in January is now moot; July is the first and only window. Losing him leaves the scoring bridge void with no young answer.

recommendations.summary: Lock Kaberle on 5-6 years; he is 27, a core defenseman, and $1.90M is a reasonable cost for a prime-year blueliner.
recommendations.rationale: Age 27, $1.90M expiring. The GM has never questioned keeping him. Same renewal window as Gaborik; sign both in the first week of free agency.

recommendations.summary: Lock Eminger on 5-6 years; POTE 99 at 21 is the highest-potential defenseman the club owns.
recommendations.rationale: Age 21, POTE 99, $1.20M expiring. The GM vetoed trading him on January 19, confirming the long-term plan. Star-length deal while the contract is still $1.20M.

recommendations.summary: Lock Richards on 5-6 years; he is 25 and the Coach's designated first-line centre next season.
recommendations.rationale: Age 25, $1.00M expiring, 70 FACE, 85 PASS. The system-fit review flagged his rate decline but at 25 with that profile he is a starter, not a prospect. Coach's May 25 report assigns him L1C.

recommendations.summary: Renew Tellqvist on 3-4 years as the developmental backup behind Luongo.
recommendations.rationale: Age 25, $0.80M expiring, POTE high 90s. The GM's January standing order is to give him time. He saves no money over Belfour but provides a long-term backup at a fraction of the cost.

recommendations.summary: Renew Abid on 2-3 years; at $0.40M with TOUG 80 and CHKG 80 he is the cheapest answer to the Coach's fourth-line gap.
recommendations.rationale: Coach quantified the L4 gap: checking mean 61, toughness mean 57, faceoffs 50. Abid closes toughness and checking at the lowest salary on the roster. Renewing him makes Bell a luxury rather than a necessity.

recommendations.summary: Plan for Belfour to walk after the playoffs; offer a reduced deal at renewal, but budget on him declining at age 40.
recommendations.rationale: Age 40, $6.50M expiring. The GM's January note: 'I would offer him a reduced contract at renewal but he probably won't accept.' Luongo is the starter at 91 base. His $6.50M freed is what makes the Iginla signing possible.

recommendations.summary: Release Roberts; at 39 and $2.70M he is end-of-career salary that should fund the Iginla pursuit.
recommendations.rationale: Age 39, $2.70M expiring. The scoring bridge memory names him among the 426-point veterans whose production has no young replacement. At 39, there is no next year. Letting him go frees $2.70M for the RW acquisition.

recommendations.summary: Sign Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, $6.50M expiring) as the July priority; Belfour and Roberts leaving frees $9.20M which covers his salary.
recommendations.rationale: He closes the Mogilny scoring void and the structural toughness gap simultaneously. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring contracts cannot retain him. This is the play the entire summer is built around.

recommendations.summary: Hold all five camp auditions (Nash, Chistov, Upshall, Alexeev, Colaiacovo) on 2-year deals only if they earn a roster spot; otherwise treat as July trade chips.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach's May 25 report names Alexeev replacing Chistov or Upshall, flags Colaiacovo's development stall, and puts Nash in a system-fit review. None are signed yet. Camp decides their futures.

recommendations.summary: Rest Sundin, Mogilny, and other veterans in the four remaining games; seeding is locked at 1st with 19 points on 2nd place.
recommendations.rationale: TOR is 133 points, 19 clear of New Jersey at 114. No seeding incentive remains. Preserve health for the playoffs and raise ticket prices toward 75 for round one per the manual.

recommendations.current: Chistov (LW, 22, $1.10M expiring, POTE 95) + Abid (LW, 25, $0.40M expiring, 66 pts/82 GP, POTE 94)
recommendations.proposed: Bell (LW, 24, $900K, 2 years, 80 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81)
recommendations.summary: Trade Chistov and Abid to Chicago for Bell, who closes both the toughness void (zero TOR players at 80+) and the faceoff gap (next best at 75) in one move.
recommendations.rationale: Bell is the only league-wide player at 80+ base carrying 85+ TOUG, 85+ CHKG and 80+ FACE simultaneously. CHI at 73 points with $29.46M profit are rebuilding and would value POTE 95 at 22 over POTE 81 at 24. Abid's 66 points at $400K gives them cheap production while they develop. We save $600K net.

recommendations.current: Koltsov (LW, 24, $1.10M, 2 years, POTE 94, ACCE 96, 19 pts/38 GP)
recommendations.summary: Trade Koltsov to LA for Avery, who at FACE 93 gives the fourth line its first legitimate faceoff center at $400K.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 48 points in full rebuild prefers POTE 94 speed at 24 over a 79-base center with limited upside. This is the exact package identified on March 19 as LA's stated preference. We save $700K net and gain a player the Coach has flagged as one of two league-wide solutions to the L4 faceoff problem.

recommendations.summary: Sign Iginla as a UFA in July; CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring cannot retain him.
recommendations.rationale: His contract shows contract_years = 0, making him a free agent. At 93 base, 27 years old, 140 points in 73 games, and TOUG 85, he bridges the Mogilny scoring void and becomes our first player above 85 toughness. Our $48.88M profit makes $6.50M routine. CGY's $14.43M profit cannot cover his renewal alongside 9 other expiring players.

recommendations.summary: Hold Tucker and the 4th rounder as sweeteners; neither adds enough to a package for Bell or Avery to justify spending them on these targets.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker at 30 with POTE 79 and 1 point in 3 games is worth approximately a 74-76 base player. None of the three targets fall in that range. Holding both preserves flexibility for a larger package or a contingency if Bell and Iginla both fail.

recommendations.summary: Close goalie monitoring task #2 permanently — Luongo is on the roster and the GM closed the window on March 19.
recommendations.rationale: The task was scoped to a trade window that no longer exists. Luongo is our starter at 94 overall on a $1.60M deal with 2 years left. Belfour's expiring contract is a renewal question, not a trade-window question.

recommendations.summary: Move Chlup to first-line centre for next season before camp begins.
recommendations.rationale: 59 points in 71 games at 16.9 MPG and POTE 95 at age 19. He has outgrown the second line and the pattern will repeat if the lineup is set without him on top.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev replaces Chistov or Upshall on a forward line next season.
recommendations.rationale: Alexeev scored 30 points in 55 games (0.55 pts/g) against Chistov at 20 in 68 (0.29) and Upshall at 20 in 68 (0.29). He outproduces both dressed wingers but remains a scratch.

recommendations.summary: Give Colaiacovo a defined defensive pair role next season or his development stalls again.
recommendations.rationale: 31 games at 17.9 MPG but only 12 points. When he plays he gets real minutes, but 38% share at 22 with POTE 99 means the rotation is capping his growth.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza a real audition at camp next season or stop dressing him.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 at 21 with 46 games at 6.7 MPG and 15 points. Another year in this pattern wastes him. The camp assignment is the only remaining lever.

recommendations.summary: No change needed for Stahle; he is not being wronged.
recommendations.rationale: 4 games, 0 points, POTE 96. No evidence of readiness. He should compete in camp but has no claim to games he has not earned.

recommendations.summary: Klesla has played every game at 14.8 MPG; his problem is production, not opportunity.
recommendations.rationale: 82 games, 30 points (0.37 pts/g), second consecutive declining season. He got the chance. The rate is the issue.

recommendations.summary: Assign Chlup to first-line centre at camp. 0.88 pts/g on 18.2 MPG at 19, the only young player whose rate and minutes both rose.
recommendations.rationale: I have recommended this twice and neither was taken. With 4 games left this is now a camp decision. Every other player 23 or under declined in rate, minutes, or both. Chlup went the other way.

recommendations.summary: McCabe goes on the sell list for offseason. Final season rate 0.48 pts/g on 21.5 MPG at 29.
recommendations.rationale: 1.42 to 0.48 across the two windows confirms the early-season pace was the anomaly. 4 years and $3.00M on a declining 0.48-rate defenceman — the trade return exceeds the keeping value.

recommendations.summary: Jackman goes on the sell list. 0.39 pts/g on 29.4 MPG at 24.
recommendations.rationale: Rate collapsed from 0.65 while minutes held at 29-30. At 24 the direction is wrong for his age. Either the load breaks him or it does not; next year at $0.70M x 3 the trade return is worth more than gambling on a fix.

recommendations.summary: Klesla goes on the sell list. 0.31 pts/g on 14.9 MPG, second consecutive year of decline at 23.
recommendations.rationale: 0.50 to 0.31 on flat minutes with no injury. At 23 the expected direction is up and it went the other way two years running.

recommendations.summary: System-fit review for Afinogenov, Richards, and Nash in the offseason. All three held flat minutes while their rates collapsed.
recommendations.rationale: Afinogenov 1.17 to 0.73, Richards 1.08 to 0.71, Nash 0.83 to 0.42. None injured, none lost ice. The role did not change, the production did. Offseason review before pencilling any of them as top-six.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes for Dallas. The season trends are final; these are offseason decisions.
recommendations.rationale: Four games left. Nothing in these trends changes tonight's lines.

recommendations.summary: No morale action needed. Every dressed player is at 100; the two scratched players (Spezza 88, Alexeev 92) are stable and that is the development rotation, not a lines problem.
recommendations.rationale: Active roster all at 100 morale after the recent wins. Spezza and Alexeev have held at 88 and 92 for many saves without further decline, consistent with being healthy scratches rather than neglected players.

recommendations.summary: We have no fourth-line centre who can win a faceoff or check above 87; this is a trade/offseason need, not a lines fix.
recommendations.rationale: L4 faceoff mean is 52 with a best of 55, and checking best is 87. The roster's top four faceoff men (Sundin 91, Chlup 80, Roberts 76, Richards 75) are already on L1-L3. No rearrangement creates a fourth-line centre.

recommendations.summary: L1-L3, P1-P2, K1-K2 are all correctly composed for their roles.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has checking (79 mean, Jackman 90) and draws (Sundin 91). K2 outchecks K1 (84 vs 79 mean) which is correct: K1 handles draws and top forwards, K2 handles the physical kill. Both PP units have scoring (P1 88, P2 87 mean) and speed.

recommendations.summary: Chlup's 80 faceoffs are the best we have after Sundin and he is 19. Accept the 59 line mean on L2 draws; he improves with reps.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup at 80 faceoffs is the second-best on the roster and rising. The L2 faceoff gap (mean 59) exists because Nash and Afinogenov are wingers; there is no alternative centre to slot in.

recommendations.summary: Keep all lines as they are; our L1 (Sundin/Roberts/Mogilny) is the correct answer to Modano and our depth D dominates their bottom pairs.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin FACE 91 beats Modano FACE 81 on draws. Roberts CHKG 88 is our best available forward checker to shadow him. Their D outside Zubov (83) reads 75, 73, 68, 65, 65; our PP at 32.3% will punish that all night. No structural adjustment needed.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming.
recommendations.rationale: OVR 94 and the starter on quality nights. Turco on the other side also reads 94, so we need our best fresh. The fatigue-icon protocol applies.

recommendations.summary: Extend Kaberle before his $1.90M x 1 contract expires in July; losing an OVR-84 defenceman at 27 for nothing is the biggest risk on this blue line.
recommendations.rationale: Kaberle finished at 44 points in 74 games (0.60 pts/g) with OVR 84 at age 27. His contract has 1 year left per the sheet and that year is ending. The GM called him a star and a keeper on January 15.

recommendations.summary: McCabe stays on the sell list at 0.76 season rate but 0.48 recent window, age 29, $3.00M x 4.
recommendations.rationale: Final season rate confirmed at 62 points in 82 games. The 58-game recent window was 0.48, meaning his true level is a 0.50-rate third-pair defenceman on a top-pair salary and four years remaining.

recommendations.summary: Sell Jackman this offseason. 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG at $0.70M x 3 is tradeable value to any club needing cheap top-pair minutes.
recommendations.rationale: Final: 37 points in 80 games. His production does not justify a top-pair role but his cap hit and minutes make him a useful piece for a contender.

recommendations.summary: Sell Klesla. 0.37 pts/g for a second straight season at 23 on 14.8 MPG, $0.90M x 2 remaining.
recommendations.rationale: 0.38 last year, 0.37 this year, flat minutes. He is not developing upward. The 2 remaining cheap years are worth more as a return than as benching depth.

recommendations.summary: Move Eminger before July. 0.36 pts/g, 64 games, $1.20M expiring, age 21. After free agency opens his value drops to nothing.
recommendations.rationale: Confirmed slide from 0.44 (Feb) to 0.36 final. At 21 with an expiring deal he has a trade window that closes in six weeks.

recommendations.summary: Fischer stays. 41 points in 77 games, OVR 85 at 24, locked at $3.70M x 4. GM's call and the numbers support it.
recommendations.rationale: GM rejected trading Fischer on January 15 as emphatically as he rejected trading Svehla. His two-way game and age justify it.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bell as the primary July target; he is the only player in the league closing both the toughness void (88 TOUG) and the faceoff void (82 FACE) simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto has zero players at 80+ TOUG and one at 80+ FACE (Sundin, 34). Bell at 24 with POTE 81 and two years on $0.90M is the cheapest solution to both gaps. CHI are at 73 points with 10 expiring deals and $29.46M profit.

recommendations.summary: Avery is the backup option if Bell is unavailable: 93 FACE and 83 TOUG at $400K with two years left.
recommendations.rationale: Avery closes the faceoff gap harder than Bell (93 vs 82) but is weaker on toughness (83 vs 88) and has a lower ceiling. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring deals are motivated sellers. Cheaper by $500K.

recommendations.summary: Stuart at 87 base with 89 CHKG and POTE 91 is the Roberts replacement at defence.
recommendations.rationale: Jackman at 24 (87 CHKG) is the only young blueliner with top-pair traits. Roberts at 39 is 86 CHKG but cannot be counted on beyond 2006. SJ at 72 points with 13 expiring deals on $45.39M cannot retain everyone, but at 72 points they may hold a POTE 91 defenceman.

recommendations.summary: Richards at 70 FACE on L4 is the best internal option; the gap beyond that is acquisition-only.
recommendations.rationale: The GM took this assignment three times this season. Richards at 70 FACE and 85 PASS is above the L4 mean of 52. No other Toronto centre exceeds 75 FACE. The structural fix is Bell or Avery, not another lineup slide.

recommendations.summary: Goalies are covered: Luongo (26, 2y), Belfour (40, 1y), Ouellet (23, 2y), Tellqvist (25, 1y).
recommendations.rationale: The GM closed all goalie monitoring on March 19. Luongo is the franchise goalie at 26 with two years left. Belfour at 1.93 GAA and 0.931 SV carries the playoff run. No role gap exists.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik on 6 years in July; 99 points at 23 on $1.10M is the most valuable expiring asset on the roster and the one loss the club cannot survive.
recommendations.rationale: He is the second franchise pillar after Chlup's development confirms it. A 99-point season at 23 will draw league interest; losing him restarts the rebuild after a 133-point year.

recommendations.summary: Lock Richards on 6 years; 66 points at 25 on $1.00M with POTE 88 is the cheapest franchise-quality center available in this league.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach already assigned him L3C. At 25 he is entering his prime on a $1.00M expiring deal. Losing him to a bidding war costs a top-nine center and a faceoff solution simultaneously.

recommendations.summary: Lock Nash on 6 years; 39 points at age 20 with POTE 95 is the highest-upside forward outside Gaborik and the natural L1W replacement for Mogilny.
recommendations.rationale: He is two years from prime production and will command a real salary by then. Locking him now at $1.20M-adjacent numbers is the cheapest protection available.

recommendations.summary: Lock Eminger on 5 years; POTE 99 at 21 with 23 points is the highest-ceiling defenseman on the roster and the only blueliner who can carry a top-pairing future.
recommendations.rationale: GM protected Eminger from being dealt at the deadline specifically for his upside. An expiring deal on a POTE 99 defenseman is the worst possible contract to let lapse.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla in July with a package built around Klesla plus Chistov or Koltsov; at 27 and 93 base he replaces the Mogilny/Sundin/Roberts production in one move.
recommendations.rationale: The three expiring veterans produced 256 points this season. No internal player under 30 can absorb that without a 0.20 pts/g jump. Iginla did 1.92 pts/g at 27. CGY cannot retain him with 10 expiring deals and a 70-point season.

recommendations.summary: Let Belfour walk in July at 40 and $6.50M expiring; his playoff-purpose purpose is served and Luongo plus Ouellet cover the future.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is 26, POTE 97, 2 years left. Ouellet is 23, POTE 97, 2 years. Belfour's $6.50M buys nothing the club cannot get from its own goalie depth.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk at 39 and $2.70M expiring; 81 points at POTE 52 is a final season, not a foundation.
recommendations.rationale: His overall will decline from here. The toughness void he filled is better solved by Bell or Avery acquisition than by re-signing a 40-year-old.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik on 5-6 years the first day renewals open. He cannot reach the market at 1.12 pts/g, age 23, POTE 90.
recommendations.rationale: His $1.10M expiring deal is the cheapest franchise-player contract in the league. Every contender will bid him up in July. No leverage argument justifies delay.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle on 5-6 years at or near $1.90M before his value rises past what Toronto can match.
recommendations.rationale: 27 years old, top-pairing D, expiring at a below-market salary. He enters his prime and his next renewal will be expensive.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger on 5-6 years at $1.20M or slightly above.
recommendations.rationale: 21, POTE 99, GM vetoed trading him in January because his ceiling is the reason to hold him. Expiring deals for players that young are the ones you lock immediately.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards on 5-6 years at $1.00M. He is a top-six centre at a third-line salary and his contract is expiring.
recommendations.rationale: 25, 70 FACE, 85 PASS, Coach assigned him third-line centre for next season. If he walks the faceoff gap widens further.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash on 5-6 years at $1.20M regardless of the system-fit review outcome.
recommendations.rationale: 20 years old with an expiring deal. The fit question determines his line, not his long-term value to the club. Lock youth at youth prices.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Tellqvist on 2-3 years at $0.80M.
recommendations.rationale: GM standing order from 2005-01-15: give him time to develop, POTE high 90s. Shorter term keeps the next renewal flexible while he proves himself behind Luongo.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Abid on 2 years at $0.40M.
recommendations.rationale: Cheapest toughness on the roster. No reason for a longer deal but no reason to lose him either.

recommendations.summary: Let Belfour walk in July. Do not offer a new deal; at 40 and $6.50M he will not accept less.
recommendations.rationale: GM's January position was 'offer reduced salary, he probably won't accept.' Luongo at 91 is the number one for the next four years. Belfour's value was as a playoff insurance policy and that window closes with the season.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk. At 39 and $2.70M there is no role that justifies renewal.
recommendations.rationale: His production is part of the 426-point bridge that needs replacing. The money goes to Iginla or Bell.

recommendations.summary: Trade Chistov this summer before his contract expires. He is displaced by Alexeev, the Coach stated so on May 5.
recommendations.rationale: 22, POTE 95, SPEE 89, ACCE 88, $1.10M expiring. If not re-signed he walks for nothing. The Coach confirmed Alexeev outproduces him (0.55 vs 0.29 pts/g). His value as a piece funds the toughness target.

recommendations.summary: Hold Colaiacovo through September camp. If he shows top-four ability, renew on 2-3 years. If not, trade before a second year of zero development.
recommendations.rationale: 31 games at 17.9 MPG and 0.39 pts/g is a rotation player, not a prospect. Camp is the test. Expiring at $1.10M so the decision cannot wait past summer.

recommendations.summary: Same as Colaiacovo: one camp audition, then renew or trade. 0.29 pts/g on 7.9 MPG with POTE 99 must produce an answer by September.
recommendations.rationale: Coach's May 21 report: 'either a system-fit problem or a bust, and camp is where you find out which.' $1.20M expiring, same urgency.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Iginla as the Mogilny replacement. 93 base, 140 pts in 73 games, $6.50M expiring from a 70-point club.
recommendations.rationale: The 426-point scoring bridge has no internal successor under 30. Iginla closes it outright and adds TOUG 85 to a roster whose fourth-line checking mean is 61. CGY at 70 points with $14.43M profit cannot retain him.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell to close the faceoff gap (52/55 on L4) and the toughness gap (checking 61, toughness 57) simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Only league-wide player at 82+ base with 88 TOUG and 82 FACE. CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring and $29.46M profit are motivated sellers. Fund with Chistov plus Tucker plus the 4th-rounder.

recommendations.summary: No action available. Mogilny has 2 years at $5.50M left and cannot be moved or bought out.
recommendations.rationale: He declined to 0.79 pts/g at 36. The $11M remaining is a sunk cost of the 2003 acquisition. No in-game mechanism removes it.

recommendations.summary: At the June 8 rookie draft, prioritize goaltending depth per the GM's January 22 standing order. Otherwise best player available.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto owns no pick better than a fourth-rounder. This is a depth draft. Goaltending is the position where a fourth-rounder can become a career backup with high potential.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Jarome Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, 128 pts/76 GP, 87 TOUG, $6.50M expiring) as the July RW priority.
recommendations.rationale: Replaces Mogilny's RW production and carries 87 TOUG which partially addresses the toughness void. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Martin Havlat (OTT, LW, 24, 87 base, 103 pts/82 GP, POTE 85, $900K expiring) as the LW complement to Nash and Gaborik.
recommendations.rationale: 103 points at $900K from a 77-point Ottawa club with 11 expiring deals and $32.36M profit. POTE 85 at 24 means five-plus better seasons ahead. Does not compete with Iginla for the RW slot.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Mark Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 80 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, $900K, 2 years left) to close the toughness and faceoff voids.
recommendations.rationale: The only league-wide player above 80 on all three missing grades. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit is rebuilding. Two years left means he is not a rental.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Brad Stuart (SJ, D, 25, 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91, $1.80M expiring) to replace Roberts and pair with Jackman.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 91 at 25 gives eight development years. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring cannot retain Stuart, Brewer, McLaren, and Mironov simultaneously.

recommendations.summary: If Stuart is unavailable, acquire Eric Brewer (SJ, D, 26, 88 base, 93 CHKG, 82 TOUG, POTE 83, $2.00M expiring, 61 pts/82 GP).
recommendations.rationale: Higher CHKG than Stuart (93 vs 89) and more points (61 vs 52). Lower POTE but one year older means less development runway. Same seller situation.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Dany Heatley (ATL, RW, 24, 91 base, 131 pts/79 GP, POTE 85, $1.10M expiring) if ATL retains Kovalchuk.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring cannot re-sign both Kovalchuk (138 pts) and Heatley (131 pts). Whichever they keep, the other moves. Heatley as RW fills the Mogilny slot at 91 base and $1.10M.

recommendations.summary: Consider Chris Drury (BUF, LW, 28, 89 base, 99 pts/82 GP, POTE 80, $2.00M expiring) as LW depth behind Nash and Havlat.
recommendations.rationale: BUF at 84 points with 10 expiring and $24.30M profit. 89 base at 28 with POTE 80 means two or three more 90-point seasons. Stronger than Daze (POTE 77, age 29).

recommendations.summary: Daze (CHI, LW, 29, 89 base, 127 pts/82 GP, POTE 77, $3.00M expiring) is a one-year rental option if no young LW materializes.
recommendations.rationale: Highest production on any expiring LW after Kovalchuk. POTE 77 at 29 means his peak is now. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit will deal him. A stopgap, not a fix.

recommendations.summary: Sign Mike Cammalleri (LA, RW, 22, 79 base, POTE 97, 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M UFA) in July as developmental RW depth.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 97 at 22 for $1.10M as an unrestricted free agent. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring will not re-sign both him and Frolov. Cheapest high-ceiling player available.

recommendations.summary: Sean Avery (LA, C, 25, 79 base, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, POTE 70, $400K, 2 years) is the cheapest faceoff and toughness solution if Bell falls through.
recommendations.rationale: Produces only 9 points in 82 games which is below any roster requirement, but his 93 FACE and 83 TOUG at $400K make him useful on L4 specifically. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring will deal him.

recommendations.summary: Patrick Marleau (SJ, C, 25, 89 base, 98 pts/71 GP, POTE 82, $1.60M expiring) gives Toronto the deepest centre corps in the league alongside Chlup and Richards.
recommendations.rationale: SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring must shed salary. Marleau's 98 points at $1.60M is the highest production-to-cost ratio available. Uncertainty: SJ may prioritize retaining him for one more year.

recommendations.current: Upshall (RW, 21, $1.20M expiring, POTE 99) + Koltsov (LW, 24, $1.10M, 2 yrs, POTE 94)
recommendations.proposed: Bell (LW, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, $900K, 2 yrs, POTE 81)
recommendations.summary: Trade Upshall and Koltsov to Chicago for Bell, closing both the toughness and faceoff gaps in one move.
recommendations.rationale: Bell is the only player in the league above 80 on both TOUG (88) and FACE (82). CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring deals and $29.46M profit are rebuilding and get two POTE 94+ wingers under 25 for Bell at POTE 81. We save $1.40M in net salary. Acceptance uncertain but the hockey logic is clean for both sides.

recommendations.current: Chistov (LW, 22, $1.10M expiring, POTE 95) + Colaiacovo (D, 22, $1.10M expiring, POTE 99) + Tucker (LW, 30, $1.30M, 2 yrs, POTE 79) + 4th round pick
recommendations.proposed: Havlat (LW, 24, 87 base, 103 pts/82 GP, POTE 85, $900K expiring)
recommendations.summary: Trade Chistov, Colaiacovo, Tucker and the 4th rounder to Ottawa for Havlat at 103 points and $900K.
recommendations.rationale: Havlat is the cheapest 87-base, 100-point player on the market and fills the LW slot beside Nash. OTT at 77 points with 11 expiring deals and $32.36M profit face aggregate raises that may force one departure. Chistov (POTE 95) and Colaiacovo (POTE 99) are both 22 and real prospects for a mid-table club. We save $2.60M. Acceptance uncertain: Ottawa may simply re-sign Havlat.

recommendations.proposed: Stuart (D, 25, 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91, $1.80M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Trade Klesla to San Jose for Stuart, replacing Roberts at 39 with a 25-year-old POTE 91 blueliner.
recommendations.rationale: SJ at $45.39M payroll with 13 expiring deals and $20.74M profit must shed blueliners. Klesla replaces Stuart at lower salary ($900K vs $1.80M), younger age (23 vs 25), and higher POTE (97 vs 91), so SJ saves $900K and gets a better long-term asset. We give our best young defenseman; the GM may veto this on principle.

recommendations.summary: If Bell does not come, sign Avery as a UFA for 93 FACE and 83 TOUG at $400K.
recommendations.rationale: Avery is the cheapest faceoff-plus-toughness combo available without a trade. His 9 points in 82 games cap him at a bottom-six role but his 93 FACE fixes the L4 draw problem the Coach quantified at 52 mean.

recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri as a UFA in July for the cheapest high-POTE offensive depth available.
recommendations.rationale: Cammalleri at 22, POTE 97, 60 points in 61 games on $1.10M is the highest-value UFA on the market. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring deals cannot retain both him and Frolov.

recommendations.summary: Goalie monitoring task #2 is closed. Luongo (94, 2 years, $1.60M) is the confirmed starter; DiPietro at 79 base is not a target; Belfour renewal is a summer decision, not a trade-window question.
recommendations.rationale: GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19. Luongo arrived and performed at 94. DiPietro at 79 base, 21 GP, 0.865 SV% is not ready and is worse than Tellqvist's POTE trajectory. No action needed.

recommendations.summary: Move Chlup to first-line centre now. 0.88 pts/g on 18.2 MPG at 19 with minutes rising is a player outgrowing his role.
recommendations.rationale: His rate went from 0.62 to 0.88 while minutes nearly doubled. He is producing on the second line and deserves the first.

recommendations.summary: Koltsov's trade value has collapsed to near-zero. 0.29 pts/g across 38 games at 24 with flat minutes. Any return now is better than waiting.
recommendations.rationale: Rate fell from 1.10 to 0.29. Minutes flat at 9.9. He is not a chip anymore; he is a spare winger with no role fit.

recommendations.summary: Sell Jackman this offseason at $0.70M x 3. 0.39 pts/g on 29.4 MPG across 80 games confirms the load is killing him.
recommendations.rationale: Season rate held below 0.50. His value is the cheapest top-pair minutes in the league; that value shrinks every month he plays 30 minutes at 0.39.

recommendations.summary: Plan to cut Sundin, Mogilny and Roberts to 15-17 MPG at camp. All three are declining with age but still getting 19-22 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin 0.97 at 34 on 21.7 MPG, Mogilny 0.83 at 36 on 19.1, Roberts 0.86 at 39 on 21.4. Production is still there but the minutes need to come down to protect them and create space for Chlup and Gaborik.

recommendations.summary: Abid needs 15+ MPG next season or he should be moved. He is at 11.5 MPG and falling, with production dropping from 0.84 to 0.70 alongside the minutes.
recommendations.rationale: Rate and minutes are falling together, which means the role is suppressing him. At 25 this is a player wasting in a bottom-six role.

recommendations.summary: No morale-driven line or minutes changes needed for Dallas.
recommendations.rationale: Every dressed player is at 100. The four below 100 (Spezza 88, Alexeev 92, Spacek 94, Upshall 94) are all trending upward on wins. Spezza and Alexeev are scratches; their minutes are an offseason conversation, not a pre-game adjustment.

recommendations.slot: first through third lines, both power plays, both penalty kills
recommendations.summary: L1-L3, P1-P2, K1-K2 are correctly profiled for their roles; no composition change before Dallas.
recommendations.rationale: Each unit carries the attribute profile its job demands. Tucker at 94 checking anchors L3, Chlup at 80 faceoffs and Kaberle at 85 stamina anchor L2, K2 checking mean of 84 is the highest on the roster.

recommendations.summary: L4 faceoff mean is 52 with nobody above 55; acquire a centre who wins draws and plays a 200-foot game.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin (91), Chlup (80) and Richards (75) are the only centres with faceoff grades above 55 and all three are needed on L1-L3. No rearrangement fixes this.

recommendations.summary: No lineup change for Dallas; the auto-pairing already places our skill lines against their soft second and third defensive pairs (OVR 65-73).
recommendations.rationale: DAL's D2 (Matvichuk 73, Berenzweig 68) and D3 (Descoteaux 65, Richards 65) face our L2 (Chlup 86, Nash 83 with SHPW 98, Afinogenov 86 with DEKG 98) and L3 (Richards 87, Chistov 82). Their fourth line features Gilmour at 41 and Messier at 44 against our Abid/Spacek/Upshall. We are deeper at every position.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is OVR 94 with 100 morale, matching Turco's 94. Standing order: verify no tired icon on screen.

recommendations.summary: Sell McCabe this offseason: final season 0.76 pts/g but recent 58-game window is 0.48, age 29, 4 years, $3.00M.
recommendations.rationale: His 0.76 season total is carried by a hot start. The May 2nd sell call stands on locked numbers now. At 29 with $3.00M he is worth more to a playoff club than to us.

recommendations.summary: Sell Jackman at $0.70M x 3: 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG is a buy-low opportunity for a contender.
recommendations.rationale: OVR 86 at 0.70M is the cheapest top-pair minutes in the league. He is declining but any playoff team needs a third-pair guy with his ice-time absorption.

recommendations.summary: Sell Klesla: 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG is a second consecutive decline (0.38 at 22, 0.37 at 23).
recommendations.rationale: The trend is flat-to-down with no path to improvement. $0.90M x 2 is movable salary.

recommendations.summary: Move Eminger before July: 0.36 pts/g final, $1.20M expiring, or he walks as a UFA.
recommendations.rationale: Already flagged March 30th as a deadline. The season-final number confirms the slide. After July we get zero return.

recommendations.summary: Kaberle's contract is expiring now: 0.59 pts/g, OVR 84, $1.90M x 1. The GM called him a keeper and a star. Renew or trade before he walks.
recommendations.rationale: A keeper-quality defenceman at 0.59 pts/g who can walk in July is either re-signed or sold. That decision cannot wait until camp.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, 81 POTE, $0.90M, 2 years) in July; he is the only league-wide player closing toughness, checking and faceoffs at once.
recommendations.rationale: Zero Toronto players at TOUG 80+; best is Jackman 75. L4 faceoff mean is 52 with best 55. Bell at 24 with 2 years left and $0.90M fits the young-core timeline and the coach's quantified gaps.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring) as the July scoring-bridge acquisition.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny (36), Sundin (34) and Roberts (38) carry 426 combined points with no under-30 player positioned to absorb that production. Iginla at 93 base with TOUG 85 closes scoring and partial toughness. CGY at 70 points with $14.43M profit cannot retain him.

recommendations.summary: If Bell falls through, pursue Avery (LA, C, 25, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2 years) as the single-gap faceoff fix.
recommendations.rationale: The coach quantified L4 faceoff mean at 52 with best 55. Avery at 93 FACE closes that one hole at $400K. His TOUG 83 and CHKG 88 also raise the fourth-line floor. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring are sellers.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker nightly as the fifth checker at 83 CHKG; his 30-year-old body and POTE 79 cap him as a depth body, not a top-four regular.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker at 83 CHKG and 70 TOUG is the fourth-best checker on the roster and the coach already named him as the internal toughness fallback. The GM listed Tucker and the 4th-rounder as the only trade chips, but those are sweeteners for a larger package (Bell or Iginla), not standalone deals.

recommendations.summary: Run the coach's system-fit review on Afinogenov (25, 90 scoring, 96 speed) before finalising next season's top six; if he fits, he is the internal bridge for Mogilny's minutes.
recommendations.rationale: Afinogenov at 90 scoring and 96 speed is the youngest high-grade scorer on the roster. The coach flagged a system-fit review alongside Richards and Nash on 2005-05-17. His 95 INJU means he can carry the load.

recommendations.summary: Checking depth (6 at 80+, four of them 29 or under) does not require an acquisition; Jackman 87, McCabe 86, Fischer 82 and Tucker 83 cover four lines plus the penalty kill.
recommendations.rationale: The age curve is right: Jackman 24, McCabe 29, Fischer 24, Upshall 21. Only Roberts at 38 and Tucker at 30 are in decline. One departure from this group makes it thin, but acquiring a seventh checker in July would crowd the players the coach is developing.

recommendations.summary: Renew Gaborik first in July on a 5-6 year deal at $5-6M; he produced 99 points at $1.10M and is the single largest production asset on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik at 23 with 99 pts in 82 GP and POTE 90 is the club's only confirmed 90+ point scorer with any longevity. His contract expires July 2005. A bidding war with no cap means he could command more, but locking 5-6 years now protects against losing him for nothing.

recommendations.summary: Renew Richards second on a 5-year deal; 66 points in 80 GP at 25 for $1.00M is a second-line centre at a fourth-line price.
recommendations.rationale: Richards is the bridge player between the aging top six and the young core. At 25 with 66 pts and POTE 88, he's entering prime. Losing him forces Chlup (19) or Spacek (19) into a top-nine role with no proven NHL centre.

recommendations.summary: Renew Nash ($1.20M), Eminger ($1.20M) and Abid ($0.40M) on 5-year deals immediately after Gaborik and Richards; all three are under 26 with POTE 94+ and expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Nash (20, 39 pts, POTE 95), Eminger (21, POTE 99), Abid (25, 66 pts, POTE 94) are the core the entire rebuild was built to acquire. If the GM splits renewals across two summers by letting depth walk, these three must be in the first group.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Iginla (CGY, 27, 93 base, 1.92 pts/g, $6.50M expiring) in July; he closes the scoring void that Mogilny (84 pts, age 36) and Roberts (81 pts, walking) leave behind.
recommendations.rationale: No under-30 Toronto player averages over 0.83 pts/g. Iginla at 1.92 pts/g with TOUG 85 at age 27 is the only league-wide player who simultaneously replaces Mogilny's production and raises the toughness ceiling. CGY at 70 pts with $14.43M profit cannot retain him.

recommendations.summary: Trade Tucker ($1.30M, 2 years, 1 point in 3 GP, POTE 79) in July for a 5th-round pick as a sweetener attached to a larger package; he has no role on the projected roster.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker is the only chip the GM has authorized. At 30 with POTE 79 he has no future but his contract is short and cheap enough to be a salary-matching piece. The GM authorized him and the 4th-rounder as the only moving parts on 2005-03-19.

recommendations.summary: Trade Roberts (38, 92 base, 81 pts, $2.70M expiring) to a contender for a draft pick using the over-80 expiring mechanic; do not release him.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts produced 81 points at 38 and is above 80 base with an expiring contract, which qualifies for the pick-recovery mechanic. Releasing him wastes the only remaining pick-recovery asset after Belfour was closed. His age means no return beyond a low pick is realistic, but that is better than nothing with no first or second rounders on hand.

recommendations.summary: Renew Chlup (2yrs left), Klesla (2yrs) and Jackman (3yrs) in 2006 to split the renewal burden; none should be allowed into an unrestricted July 2005.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup at 19 with 59 pts and POTE 95 is the franchise centre of the next decade. His contract has 2 years left, so renewal falls in 2006, which splits the cluster across two summers as the guide recommends. Klesla (23, 30 pts, POTE 97, 2yrs) and Jackman (24, 37 pts, POTE 89, 3yrs) are the same logic.

recommendations.summary: The trade deadline of 2005-03-19 passed 63 days ago; no deadline action remains.
recommendations.rationale: The GM's 2005-03-19 standing order closed all deadline tasks. Only Tucker and the 4th-rounder were chips and the deadline window is closed.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik on 6 years before any other contract action in the summer.
recommendations.rationale: Age 23, 91 base, 67 pts/45 GP, POTE 90, $1.10M expiring. He is the highest-rated player on the expiring list and the RW scoring void makes him untouchable.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash on 6 years.
recommendations.rationale: Age 20 at $1.20M expiring. Youngest player on the list; a 6-year deal keeps his next renewal after the Kaberle/Richards 5-year deals expire.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger on 6 years.
recommendations.rationale: Age 21, POTE 99, $1.20M expiring. The GM protected him explicitly on 2005-02-19. Six years separates his expiry from the 5-year Kaberle and Richards deals.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle on 5 years.
recommendations.rationale: Age 27, $1.90M expiring, the core right-shot defenseman. Five years puts his next renewal one year ahead of the 6-year deals.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards on 5 years.
recommendations.rationale: Age 25, 70 FACE, 85 PASS, $1.00M expiring. Coach and analyst both assign him L3C. Five years staggers against the 6-year deals.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Abid on 2-3 years.
recommendations.rationale: Age 25, TOUG 80, CHKG 80, $0.40M expiring. Coach demands 18+ MPG next season. Cheap enough to renew immediately on a short deal.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Alexeev on 2-3 years after camp confirms a third-line wing role.
recommendations.rationale: Age 23, $1.10M expiring, 0.55 pts/g outproducing both dressed wingers. Coach assigns him L3W. Renew only if camp confirms the role; otherwise he becomes trade depth.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Tellqvist on 2-3 years as backup goalie depth.
recommendations.rationale: Age 25, $0.80M expiring, POTE high 90s. GM's January standing order was to give him time to develop. Short deal preserves the option to move him if a better backup arrives.

recommendations.summary: Do not re-sign Roberts; let his $2.70M deal expire at age 38.
recommendations.rationale: Age 38, $2.70M. The manual caps veterans at 2 years, but releasing frees salary for Iginla or Bell. Stuart (SJ, 25, POTE 91) was identified as the replacement in March.

recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour a reduced-salary 1-year deal; expect him to decline; plan for his $6.50M to fund an Iginla signing.
recommendations.rationale: Age 40, $6.50M expiring. GM's February standing order was to offer reduced and accept the likely decline. Luongo (91 base, 2 years left) and Tellqvist cover goalies.

recommendations.summary: Colaiacovo gets a full camp audition; if he cannot secure top-four minutes, trade him while POTE 99 holds value.
recommendations.rationale: Age 22, POTE 99, $1.10M expiring, but 31 games at 17.9 MPG and 0.39 pts/g this season. Coach called him a write-off on 2005-05-15. If he fails camp, the over-80-expiring mechanic converts him to a draft pick.

recommendations.summary: Trade Chistov this summer if Alexeev holds the third-line wing; do not let POTE 95 walk for nothing.
recommendations.rationale: Age 22, POTE 95, SPEE 89, ACCE 88, $1.10M expiring. Coach stated on 2005-05-05 that Alexeev displaces him. He is available as a trade piece per the Coach's own word.

recommendations.summary: Upshall faces the same camp audition as Spezza and Spacek; if he does not earn a top-nine role, do not renew.
recommendations.rationale: Age 21, $1.20M expiring. Coach named him in the camp audition group on 2005-05-11 with no guaranteed role.

recommendations.summary: Sign Iginla as a free agent in July; he is the RW replacement for Mogilny and the toughness fix the Coach quantified.
recommendations.rationale: Age 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him. His salary matches Belfour's outgoing $6.50M.

recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri as a free agent in July at $1.10M; highest POTE available at the lowest cost.
recommendations.rationale: Age 22, POTE 98, 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M expiring. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring cannot retain both him and Frolov.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell from Chicago to close both the toughness ceiling (mean 57) and the L4 faceoff void (mean 52) in one player.
recommendations.rationale: Age 24, 82 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82, ENDU 71, POTE 81. CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring and $29.46M profit are motivated sellers. ENDU 71 means short shifts initially.

recommendations.summary: At the 2005-06-08 rookie draft, use the fourth-rounder on a goalie if scouting flags one; auto-draft is adequate at current scouting level.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto own no pick better than a fourth-rounder. GM's 2005-01-22 standing order is to scout for goalies in the draft. Late-pick goalies are cheap insurance behind Tellqvist.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla (CGY) as the July priority — he closes the scoring bridge void and the toughness ceiling simultaneously at 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot justify retaining a 27-year-old at $6.50M with no playoff path. This closes the two hardest gaps on the roster in one acquisition.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bell (CHI) as the toughness/faceoff/checking solution — 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, on a cheap deal.
recommendations.rationale: The only player in the league who closes all three structural gaps simultaneously. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring are not contending and have $31.73M profit suggesting they are liquidating rather than competing.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Theodore (MTL) at 91 base, 28 years old, POTE 87, $5.50M expiring — the exact profile the Jan 15 order set for the post-Belfour backup role.
recommendations.rationale: MTL are the worst team in the league at 66 points with 15 expiring contracts. After Belfour leaves at 40 we have Luongo plus Ouellet (80 GSH_) and Tellqvist (80 GSH_). Theodore is the only high-90s goalie on a non-contender.

recommendations.summary: Target Kovalchuk (ATL, 21, 89 base, 104 pts/61 GP, expiring) if ATL retains Heatley rather than him — elite scoring at the cheapest payroll in the league cannot keep both.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at $36.79M payroll (league floor) with 11 expiring contracts face a binary. Whichever they keep, the other enters the pool. Kovalchuk's ceiling is higher at 21; Heatley's floor is better at 24.

recommendations.summary: Target Heatley (ATL, 24, 91 base, 96 pts/58 GP, expiring) if ATL retains Kovalchuk rather than him — proven scorer, two years older than Kovalchuk but a higher current grade.
recommendations.rationale: Same binary logic as Kovalchuk. Heatley at 91 base has the higher floor; Kovalchuk has the higher ceiling. Whichever ATL sheds is the one we pursue.

recommendations.summary: Probe Stuart (SJ, 25, 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91) as the Roberts replacement — he adds toughness on the back end and has eight years of runway.
recommendations.rationale: SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring must shed contracts, but at 76 points they are not desperate and may hold a POTE 91 blueliner. Worth a probe in July but lower probability than Theodore or the ATL wings.

recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri (LA UFA) at 22, POTE 98, 60 pts/61 GP on $1.10M — zero trade assets required, pure free agency, and the cheapest high-potential production available.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 79 points with 14 expiring on $52.43M payroll cannot retain everyone. At $1.10M and 22 with POTE 98 he is the highest-upside UFA signing available at negligible cost.

recommendations.summary: Hold Daze (CHI, 29, 89 base, 127 pts/82 GP, $3.00M expiring) as the fallback if Iginla signs elsewhere — same production tier at less than half the salary, but only 29 so he's a bridge not a destination.
recommendations.rationale: CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring are moving talent. Daze delivers Iginla-level production at $3.00M versus $6.50M but with no runway beyond age 32. He's the answer if Iginla goes to a contender.

recommendations.proposed: Bell (24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, $900K/2yr) from CHI
recommendations.summary: Send Chistov, Tucker and the 4th to Chicago for Bell; he closes toughness, checking and faceoffs in one move at $900K.
recommendations.rationale: Bell is the only league-wide player at 80+ on all three gap grades simultaneously. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring are collecting young ceiling over established floor; Chistov's POTE 95 exceeds Bell's POTE 81. We net $2.60M in savings. Requires GM to release Chistov beyond the March 19 Tucker-only authorization.

recommendations.proposed: Cammalleri (22, POTE 98, 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M expiring) as UFA
recommendations.summary: If neither trade lands, sign Cammalleri off the UFA market in July; no trade asset leaves our books.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 79 points with 14 expiring cannot retain everyone. At 22 with POTE 98 and 60 points in 61 games on $1.10M, he is the highest-value UFA available and costs nothing in trade assets. He does not close toughness or faceoffs but adds scoring depth to bridge the Mogilny decline.

recommendations.summary: Goalie monitoring task (#2) is complete and closed per the GM's 2005-03-19 standing order; Luongo developed from 91 to 94 base and is locked for two more years at $1.60M.
recommendations.rationale: The GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19 after confirming both Luongo (94, 26, 2yr, $1.60M) and Belfour (93, 40, expiring) for the playoff run. Luongo's base rose from 91 at acquisition to 94 by season end, validating the original POTE-based acquisition logic. No further monitoring is warranted without a new GM directive.

recommendations.summary: Assign Chlup to first-line centre for next season. 59 points in 71 games at 19 belongs on the top line.
recommendations.rationale: 59 points on 16.9 MPG at age 19. This recommendation has been filed repeatedly since April and not taken. Camp assignment is the last lever before the season locks in.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza a top-six audition at camp next September. 6.7 MPG and 15 points on POTE 99 is the biggest development waste on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99, 46 games, 6.7 MPG, 15 points. The season is a write-off. If he cannot earn a top-six role in camp, stop carrying him on the active roster.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev at 0.55 pts/g outproduces dressed wingers Chistov and Upshall at 0.29. Either dress him in a lineup spot next year or move him while he still has trade value at 23.
recommendations.rationale: 30 points in 55 games on 8.3 MPG while Chistov (0.29 pts/g, 13.1 MPG) and Upshall (0.29 pts/g, 7.9 MPG) dress ahead of him. Flagged since April, unresolved.

recommendations.summary: Give Colaiacovo a defined top-four pairing role next season. 17.9 MPG when he plays but only 31 of 82 games means he is stuck in a rotation, not developing.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99, 12 points in 31 games at 17.9 MPG. The GM's deliberate rotation for younger players has cost him 51 games of development. Next year needs a fixed role.
