recommendations.summary: Decide Stahle's role before camp: trade chip or bottom-pair candidate. 4 games at 21 gives no basis for either call but carrying him another year without one is waste.
recommendations.rationale: 4 GP, 17.8 MPG in those 4 games, POTE 96, 0 points. No path on this blue line. Needs a decision.

recommendations.summary: Upshall gets one honest camp audition. 0.29 pts/g on 7.9 MPG with POTE 99 is either a system-fit problem or a bust, and camp is where you find out which.
recommendations.rationale: 20 points in 68 games, 7.9 MPG. Same offseason decision as Spezza but a season later. If camp shows nothing, stop dressing him.

recommendations.summary: No change for Spacek. 7.6 MPG and 0.34 pts/g is fourth-line production on fourth-line minutes, which is appropriate at 19.
recommendations.rationale: 17 points in 50 games at 7.6 MPG, POTE 91. He is getting what his role provides. No mismatch to fix.

recommendations.summary: Assign Chlup to first-line centre for next season now, not at camp.
recommendations.rationale: 0.88 pts/g on 18.2 MPG at 19 over 71 games. The evidence has been there since April and the assignment keeps slipping.

recommendations.summary: Decide Abid's offseason: first-line minutes or trade. Do not leave him at 11 MPG again.
recommendations.rationale: Minutes collapsed 20.1 to 11.5 MPG while rate dropped 1.09 to 0.70. At 25 with a full 82-game season he is a quality winger being wasted, and his trade value erodes with another buried year.

recommendations.summary: Give Chistov a real roster spot next season based on his late-season minutes bump.
recommendations.rationale: Minutes went 9.5 to 14.0 at age 22 and his rate held at 0.30. He earned more with what he got.

recommendations.summary: Run a system-fit review for Nash, Afinogenov and Richards before assigning lines for next season. Three players, flat minutes, halved rates.
recommendations.rationale: Nash 0.83→0.42 on 13 flat MPG, Afinogenov 1.17→0.73 on 17 flat MPG, Richards 1.08→0.71 on 17 flat MPG. Same pattern across three players points at the system, not the players.

recommendations.summary: Gaborik at 1.12 pts/g on 21.2 MPG at 23 is the second franchise pillar. Build the offense around him and Chlup next season.
recommendations.rationale: His recent rate of 1.12 is elite for a 23-year-old and his minutes are still climbing. The early-season 1.42 was a hot start, not the true rate.

recommendations.summary: No change to Kaberle's role. He is 27 and improving, not declining.
recommendations.rationale: 0.54→0.62 pts/g at 27 on minutes up from 19.4 to 21.5. He is the keeper the GM already identified, and the trend confirms it.

recommendations.summary: The room is right — every player is at 88+ and trending up 3 to 5 points since last save. No ice-time intervention needed.
recommendations.rationale: Lowest morale is Spezza at 88 and rising +3. No player is materially under or over his expected minutes band with morale slipping in response.

recommendations.summary: L1 through L4, P1, P2, K1 and K2 are all built correctly for their roles; no arrangement change is warranted.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has checking 79 and skill 88/85 in balance. K2 has checking mean 84 and is a legitimate shutdown unit. L2 is correctly a scoring line with Chlup handling draws at 80. Nothing in the composition is wrong.

recommendations.summary: We have no bottom-six centre who can win faceoffs; the fourth line draws at 52/55 and there is no fix within the current roster.
recommendations.rationale: Our four best faceoff men (Sundin 91, Chlup 80, Roberts 76, Richards 75) are all locked into L1-L3. L4 has Spacek, Abid and Upshall, none listed among the top faceoff men. This is the same gap flagged April 13 and remains unsolved.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 94 OVR is the only answer to Turco at 94. Standing order: verify no tired icon before confirming.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes for Dallas.
recommendations.rationale: DAL's first line is dangerous but we are 2-0-0 against them outscoring 8-3. Their bottom four defenders average 67 OVR and our depth is the advantage. Tucker (CHKG 90, TOUG 86) already matches Arnott (TOUG 88). Their PP at 10.8% does not test our PK. No rearrangement improves this.

recommendations.summary: Finalize McCabe as a sell: 0.76 pts/g over 82 games but 0.48 over his last 58, $3.00M x 4 is dead cap for a declining 29-year-old.
recommendations.rationale: Season numbers are locked. The recent-window collapse confirms the early-season pace was the anomaly.

recommendations.summary: Sell Jackman in the offseason: 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG at $0.70M x 3 is the cheapest top-pair workload in the league and any club pays for it.
recommendations.rationale: Confirmed at 80 games. His value is the minutes and the price, not the production.

recommendations.summary: Sell Klesla: 0.37 pts/g over 82 games is his second consecutive declining season at 23. He will not recover on this roster.
recommendations.rationale: 0.38 at 22, 0.37 at 23 on flat minutes. The trend is unambiguous.

recommendations.summary: Move Eminger before free agency in July or lose him for zero return: 0.36 pts/g, 77 OVR, $1.20M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Contract expires in 1 year. After July he is gone and we get nothing.

recommendations.summary: Flag Kaberle's expiring contract: 0.59 pts/g in 74 games, 84 OVR, age 27, $1.90M x 1 year left. Extend or risk losing a top-pair defenceman for nothing.
recommendations.rationale: GM named him a keeper in January. His production supports that. Without an extension he is a UFA after next season.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bell as the July priority: he is the only league-wide player closing both the toughness void (0 at 80+ shipped TOUG) and the faceoff void (1 at 80+, age 34).
recommendations.rationale: Bell is 24, shipped TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82, POTE 81. CHI had 73 points and $29.46M profit, making them motivated sellers. ENDU 71 means short shifts initially but his ceiling covers the gap for years.

recommendations.summary: Keep Avery as the budget alternative to Bell: FACE 93, TOUG 83, CHKG 88, $0.40M with 2 years left, age 25.
recommendations.rationale: LA had 48 points with 13 expiring deals. Avery closes the same three gaps as Bell at a fraction of the cost, with a lower ceiling. If Bell's price is too high, Avery is the fallback that still moves the needle.

recommendations.summary: Iginla remains the July priority for the RW seat that Mogilny (36, 0.79 pts/g) cannot hold next season.
recommendations.rationale: Iginla is 27, 93 base, 140 points in 73 GP, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him. He closes the Mogilny scoring void and raises the toughness ceiling simultaneously.

recommendations.summary: Chlup's POTE 96 and shipped FACE 75 at age 19 make him the designated successor to Sundin at faceoffs and centre; give him top-nine minutes at camp.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin is the only Toronto player above 80 FACE and he is 34 with INJU 57. Chlup's displayed overall is 86 with 80 FACE right now. He is the only player on the roster whose trajectory points toward filling that role without an external acquisition.

recommendations.summary: Flag Koltsov to the Coach: at 24 with 92 speed and unlined, he is free depth against the durability problem (Gaborik 52 INJU, Richards 53, Sundin 57).
recommendations.rationale: The Coach should explain why Koltsov sits unlined. If he is healthy, his speed grade places him among the top six skaters on the roster and he costs nothing to dress.

recommendations.summary: Goalies need no action this offseason: Luongo (26, 2y, $1.60M) at 94/94/89/85 is the future, Belfour (40, expiring) is a renewal or retirement question the GM has stated he will handle.
recommendations.rationale: Ouellet (23, 2y, $0.90M) provides backup depth. The GM closed goalie trade monitoring on 2005-03-19 and that decision stands. The only open item is Belfour's contract decision, which is the GM's call, not a role gap.

recommendations.summary: Renew Gaborik on a 5-6 year deal before any other July negotiation begins; he is the only player already producing at 1+ pts/g and his $1.10M deal expires in one year.
recommendations.rationale: 99 points at 23 with POTE 90 and one year remaining. If he walks the core has no first-line scorer. His current salary is 1.8% of payroll; even a $5M renewal is 8.3%.

recommendations.summary: Renew Richards on a 5-year deal immediately after Gaborik; he is 66 points on $1.00M and his market value will be $3-4M on the open market.
recommendations.rationale: At 25 with POTE 88 and 66 points, he is the cheapest top-nine centre available to any other club. Losing him for nothing would cost the equivalent of a mid-80 acquisition.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla in July; he closes the 2-year scoring gap between Roberts/Mogilny declining and Chlup/Nash maturing, and CGY cannot retain him on $6.50M.
recommendations.rationale: 93 base, 140 points in 73 GP, TOUG 85, age 27. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring contracts and $14.43M profit have no retention path. He solves both the Mogilny scoring void and the fourth-line toughness ceiling simultaneously.

recommendations.summary: Move Tucker (30, 1 pt, 3 GP, $1.30M, 2yrs) plus the 4th-rounder for a mid-70s depth player with at least one pick back; do not accept a package without a draft asset.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto owns no pick better than a 4th-rounder. The farm produced this roster via the draft; without accumulating picks the development cycle cannot restart. Tucker is a pure chip the GM has already identified.

recommendations.summary: Renew Eminger, Nash and Kaberle on 5-year deals after Gaborik and Richards; three high-POTE pieces (99, 95, 75) on one-year deals at $4.30M combined is the biggest uninsured risk on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: Eminger at POTE 99 and Nash at POTE 95 cannot be replaced if they test the market. Kaberle at 27 with 44 points fills the top-four D slot that opens if Fischer stalls. Their combined $4.30M is the cheapest insurance available.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik on 5-6 years at the top of the re-signing window before any other renewal is discussed.
recommendations.rationale: 23 years old, 91 base, POTE 90, $1.10M expiring. Every other club sees him the moment the window opens.

recommendations.summary: Lock Eminger on 5-6 years; his POTE 99 at 21 with $1.20M expiring makes him the highest-value renewal after Gaborik.
recommendations.rationale: GM vetoed trading him in January specifically for his potential. His ceiling is not set and he is the youngest blueliner with real upside.

recommendations.summary: Lock Kaberle on 5-6 years at 27, $1.90M.
recommendations.rationale: Prime-age defenceman whose contract expires alongside the whole core; staggering starts here.

recommendations.summary: Lock Richards on 5-6 years at 25, $1.00M.
recommendations.rationale: Second-best centre on the roster at his second-best contract years; the Coach already slotted him at L3C.

recommendations.summary: Lock Nash on 5-6 years at 20, $1.20M.
recommendations.rationale: The future first-line left wing; one of the four young core players the December staggered-locks plan identified for long deals.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Tellqvist on 3 years as development backup behind Luongo.
recommendations.rationale: GM standing order from January: potential in the high 90s, give him time. At $0.80M the cost is negligible.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Abid on 2 years at $0.40M.
recommendations.rationale: TOUG 80, CHKG 80 at $0.40M is the cheapest physicality on the roster; Coach wants 18+ MPG next season.

recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour one year at a reduced salary (~$3.00M); if he declines, let him walk.
recommendations.rationale: 40 years old at $6.50M. GM said in January he'd offer reduced and Belfour probably won't accept. Luongo is the future #1.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk at 38, $2.70M. Do not offer renewal.
recommendations.rationale: Coach flagged system-fit concerns. At 38 he is the oldest of the three veterans carrying the scoring void and his production is declining.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Alexeev on 2-3 years only if he earns a top-nine role at camp.
recommendations.rationale: Coach says his 0.55 pts/g outproduces both dressed wingers while he sits scratched. Give him the audition; if it clicks, renew; if not, he is trade material.

recommendations.summary: Conditional: renew Colaiacovo on 2-3 years only if he secures 60+ game workload at camp; otherwise he becomes a trade chip.
recommendations.rationale: Coach flagged him as potential development write-off at 31 games, 17.9 MPG. If he cannot earn a role, his value is as a package piece for a Bell or Stuart target.

recommendations.summary: Move Chistov in the summer if he does not make the top nine; his POTE 95 and SPEE 89 have trade value even without Luongo's demand for R1.
recommendations.rationale: Coach explicitly stated Chistov is displaced by Alexeev. At 22 with POTE 95 he is worth more in a package than on the fourth line.

recommendations.proposed: Jarome Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, TOUG 87, 140 pts/73 GP, $6.50M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Acquire Iginla from CGY as the July priority; closes the Mogilny RW void and brings toughness in one move.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring contracts and $14.43M profit must rebuild; Iginla's $6.50M on a non-contender is a trade signal. Chistov plus Colaiacovo plus the 4th-rounder is the opening package.

recommendations.proposed: Dany Heatley (ATL, RW, 24, 91 base, 131 pts/79 GP, $1.10M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Pursue Heatley as the fallback if Iginla fails; ATL must move one of him or Kovalchuk before he walks for nothing.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring holds two 90+ point players on $1.10M deals and can only re-sign one. Heatley at 91 base, age 24, POTE 85 fills the RW seat with five years of development remaining.

recommendations.proposed: Mark Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 80 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82, $900K, 2 years)
recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell to close both the toughness and faceoff gaps in one trade; he is the only league-wide player doing both.
recommendations.rationale: CHI at 78 points with $31.73M profit and 10 expiring contracts is rebuilding. Bell at $900K is not their urgent dump, so acceptance requires a real package: a 2nd-rounder or a young defenceman.

recommendations.proposed: Craig Conroy (CGY, C, 33, 85 base, FACE 94, 102 pts/82 GP, $2.00M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Acquire Conroy as a two-year bridge at centre while Chlup matures; his FACE 94 and 102 points solve the scoring void and the draw problem at once.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 70 points rebuilding will not extend a 33-year-old at $2.00M. Tucker plus a 3rd-rounder is the opening price. He is not a solution after 2007 but covers the gap between Mogilny's decline and Chlup's arrival.

recommendations.proposed: Mike Cammalleri (LA, RW, 22, POTE 97, 79 base, 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri in July as a UFA; POTE 97 at age 22 on a $1.10M expiring deal is the best development value in the market.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 79 points with 14 expiring contracts cannot retain him alongside Frolov (POTE 95), Allison ($6.70M), Deadmarsh ($2.80M), Svehla ($3.60M), and Cechmanek ($3.30M). No trade needed; just sign before LA re-signs him.

recommendations.proposed: Eric Belanger (LA, C, 27, FACE 97, 82 base, $700K expiring)
recommendations.summary: Sign Belanger in July as the cheapest faceoff fix; FACE 97 at $700K raises the L4 draw from 52 to elite.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 79 points is a seller, but Belanger's $700K makes him non-urgent to move. As a UFA he is free. His 14 pts/64 GP confirms he is a checker only; the entire case is the FACE 97 grade.

recommendations.proposed: Steve Begin (BUF, C, 26, FACE 86, TOUG 87, CHKG 95, $936K, 2 years)
recommendations.summary: Monitor Begin in July; his 86/87/95 FACE/TOUG/CHKG triple at age 26 on $936K is the best defensive-centre profile in the league if he is playable.
recommendations.rationale: No GP or points appear in the season data, which is a red flag. BUF at 84 points with $24.30M profit are not motivated sellers. Worth a call only if his availability confirms.

recommendations.proposed: Heatley (ATL, RW, 24, 91 base, 131 pts/79 GP, $1.10M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Offer Chistov plus the 4th-rounder to Atlanta for Heatley; ATL keeps Kovalchuk and must move Heatley or lose him free.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 84 points holds Heatley and Kovalchuk on identical $1.10M expiring deals. They keep the 22-year-old. Chistov at 22/POTE 95/89 speed is their rebuild profile. Net payroll change zero. Acceptance uncertain: ATL has $43.29M profit and might try to re-sign both.

recommendations.proposed: Conroy (CGY, C, 33, 78 base, FACE 94, 102 pts/82 GP, $2.00M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Offer Tucker to Calgary for Conroy; CGY dumps a 33-year-old's salary, we get FACE 94 and 102 points as a two-year bridge while Chlup develops.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring cannot keep Conroy at $2.00M. Tucker's $1.30M over 2 years is cheap checking depth for their young roster. Payroll rises $700K, trivial against $46.70M profit. Acceptance uncertain: CGY may demand a young player, not a 30-year-old who played 3 games.

recommendations.current: Chistov (TOR, LW, 22, POTE 95, $1.10M expiring) + Tucker (TOR, LW, 30, $1.30M) + 4th-round pick
recommendations.proposed: Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, $6.50M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Test whether CGY will deal Iginla for our full capital; they cannot retain him at $6.50M on a 70-point team.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 70 points, $14.43M profit, 10 expiring contracts must shed $6.50M salary. Chistov gives them a POTE 95 core piece. Tucker fills a roster slot. The 4th is marginal. Likely fails because CGY wants a first-rounder for their franchise scorer, but the structural logic (cannot retain, must rebuild) is airtight.

recommendations.summary: Goalie monitoring task #2 is delivered and closed — Luongo is on the roster at 94, DiPietro (.871 SV%, 63 GP at 22) does not represent an upgrade, and the GM's March 19 order ended the search.
recommendations.rationale: The GM closed all goalie trade monitoring on 2005-03-19. Luongo at 94/26/$1.60M/2yr and Belfour at 93/40/$6.50M/1yr give two 90+ goalies for the playoffs. DiPietro's .871 save pct in 63 starts at 22 is solid volume for a young backup but not a Luongo-grade number.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bell (CHI, 24, 88 TOUG, 82 FACE, POTE 81) as the single acquisition closing toughness and faceoffs simultaneously; Avery (LA, 25, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, $400K) is the cheaper alternative.
recommendations.rationale: Zero players at 80+ TOUG and only Sundin at 80+ FACE on the entire roster. The coach confirmed no internal fix exists. Bell also gives 86 CHKG which provides checking depth once Tucker departs as a chip.

recommendations.summary: Line Gaborik top-six next season; at 92 overall with 98 SPEE he is the speed the roster has in abundance but is not using.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik appears in no unit per the role coverage. He is the only player under 30 at 90+ scoring grade and the bridge away from Mogilny and Sundin runs through him. Sitting him wastes the one young asset that already plays at NHL level.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza a genuine 15+ MPG camp audition; the coach, the analyst and March all independently flagged that 6.7 MPG wasted a POTE 99.
recommendations.rationale: Coach's May 15 report demands the same thing independently. POTE 99 at 6.7 MPG is the costliest non-decision on the roster. If he cannot make the top nine, trade while the scouting number holds value.

recommendations.summary: Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, $6.50M expiring) remains the July priority for the scoring bridge; CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny (36), Sundin (34) and Roberts (38) carry 426 combined points with no successor under 30 lined. Iginla closes both the scoring void and the toughness ceiling (TOUG 85) simultaneously.

recommendations.summary: Restore Abid to 18+ MPG in camp; his minutes fell from 20.1 to 11.5 and his production followed.
recommendations.rationale: Coach explicitly flagged the minutes collapse on May 15. Abid at 86 scoring grade and 90 durability is a top-nine forward by attributes; 11.5 MPG is the cost of hiding him.

recommendations.summary: Goalies are solved per the March 19 standing order: Luongo 26 with 2 years, Belfour for the playoffs, Ouellet as backup at 23 with 2 years.
recommendations.rationale: GM closed all goalie monitoring on March 19. No action required.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik on a 5-6 year deal immediately at season end; 99 points at 23 on $1.10M expiring is the most valuable contract on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: He scored 99 points in 82 games at age 23 with POTE 90. His contract expires July 2005. A 5-year deal locks a point-per-game winger through age 28 at whatever number the market sets, and no mid-contract extension was possible during the season.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards on a 5-6 year deal immediately; 66 points at 25 on $1.00M expiring is the second-most urgent renewal.
recommendations.rationale: 66 points, 80 games, age 25, POTE 88. His contract expires in July and he is the best faceoff centre on the roster. A 5-year deal at $3-4M still buys five prime years of a second-line centre cheap.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash on a 5-6 year deal this summer; 39 points at age 20 with POTE 95 on a $1.20M expiring deal is the roster's cheapest elite upside.
recommendations.rationale: Nash turned 20 this season and scored 39 points. POTE 95 with the scoring already arriving. Without a long deal he walks into free agency at his peak development window.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger on a 5-6 year deal this summer; POTE 99 at age 21 with 23 points on $1.20M expiring locks the franchise defenceman.
recommendations.rationale: GM protected Eminger specifically on 2005-02-19 as the highest-potential blueliner. POTE 99, age 21, expiring. If he walks the defence has no top-pairing replacement.

recommendations.summary: The Sundin contract is a 5-year liability at age 39 but cannot be moved or bought out; the $46.70M profit absorbs it.
recommendations.rationale: No buyout mechanic exists in this game. His production will decline toward 30-40 points on $8.40M but revenue is $119M. The deal is ugly but unaffordable is not the same as unplayable, and there is no action to take.

recommendations.summary: Sign Gaborik to a 5-6 year extension immediately when contracts open; he is 91 base, 23, POTE 90, and the best player on the expiring list.
recommendations.rationale: At 23 with 91 base and POTE 90 he is the team's most valuable asset. Letting him hit open market risks a bidding war the GM cannot fund without releasing Belfour's $6.50M.

recommendations.summary: Sign Richards to a 5-6 year extension; at 82 base, 25, $1.00M he is prime-age and underpriced.
recommendations.rationale: He is three years from his physical prime, already carries third-line centre minutes, and $1.00M is less than replacement-level cost. Lock him in the same window as Gaborik.

recommendations.summary: Sign Kaberle to a 5-year deal; at 84 base and 27 he is fully formed with five productive years ahead.
recommendations.rationale: Star-length contract per the manual. He is the only defenceman on the roster at prime age and 84+ base.

recommendations.summary: Sign Eminger to a 5-6 year deal at 21 with POTE 99 before his value rises.
recommendations.rationale: The GM killed a trade for Eminger on January 19 because his development runway outweighed certainty. That logic applies more strongly at 21 than it did at 20.

recommendations.summary: Sign Abid on a 2-3 year deal; TOUG 80, CHKG 80 at $0.40M is the cheapest toughness on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach wants him at 18+ MPG and says no bench player fixes the checking and toughness gap. At 25 and half a million there is no reason to test the market without him.

recommendations.summary: Renew Tellqvist on a 2-year deal at approximately $0.80M; GM's standing order keeps him for development.
recommendations.rationale: GM stated January 15 that Tellqvist stays and gets time to develop. He saves no money but provides goalie depth behind Luongo and Ouellet.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk at 38, 87 base, $2.70M; do not offer renewal.
recommendations.rationale: Coach plans for his decline; 0.86 pts/g at 38 confirms it. His $2.70M funds a Bell or Stuart acquisition.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Mark Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 80 base, $0.90M, 2 years left) to close the L4 faceoff gap at 52.
recommendations.rationale: Coach quantified the L4 mean at 52 with best 55 and says no bench player fixes it. Bell at 82 FACE, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG is the only league-wide solution.

recommendations.summary: Trade Chistov (78 base, 22, POTE 95) in July rather than renewing him for a displaced fourth-line role.
recommendations.rationale: Coach explicitly stated on May 5 that Alexeev displaces him and flagged him as available in a Bell package. POTE 95 at 22 carries trade value even at 78 base.

recommendations.summary: Run camp auditions for Nash (20, 77 base), Alexeev (23, 76 base), Upshall (21, 78 base), and Colaiacovo (22, 72 base) before making renewal or release decisions.
recommendations.rationale: Coach named this group on May 11. Nash and Alexeev earn a roster spot with production; Upshall and Colaiacovo are most likely released if camp says no.

recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour a reduced one-year deal; if he declines, the playoff backup is Ouellet at 81 base and $0.90M with two years left.
recommendations.rationale: GM's March 19 order keeps Belfour for the playoffs, but his contract expires in July. GM predicted he probably won't accept a reduced salary. Ouellet is the fallback.

recommendations.summary: Sign Iginla as a July UFA: 93 base, 128 pts, 85 TOUG, 27 years old, $6.50M expiring from 70-point CGY.
recommendations.rationale: He is the only player who closes the RW scoring void (Mogilny 0.83 at 36), raises toughness from 75 to 85, and fills the 30-33 age band simultaneously. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him.

recommendations.summary: Sign Havlat as a July UFA: 87 base, 103 pts, POTE 86, 24 years old, $900K expiring from 77-point OTT.
recommendations.rationale: At $900K he is the best value contract among available players. He adds a second point-per-game winger behind Gaborik and partially offsets Sundin's decline at centre. OTT at 77 points with 11 expiring deals have no reason to retain him.

recommendations.summary: Monitor Thornton's renewal with BOS through June; if unresolved, sign him at 94 base, $4.00M, 25 years old.
recommendations.rationale: He is expiring at 94 base with 83 pts in 59 games, but BOS at 97 points will try to re-sign. If he hits the market he is the best centre available and the only player who replaces Sundin's production at a quarter of his salary.

recommendations.summary: Trade for Bell (CHI, 80 base, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, $900K, 2 years) to close the toughness and faceoff voids.
recommendations.rationale: No rostered player reaches 80 TOUG and the L4 faceoff mean is 52. Bell at $900K with 2 years left is the only player closing both gaps. CHI at 78 points with $31.73M profit are profitable but not contending; a mid-round pick plus depth should suffice.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Heatley via trade only if Iginla is lost: 91 base, 131 pts, POTE 84, $1.10M, age 24, 1 year left on deal.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 84 points with $25.99M profit have financial room to re-sign, making them a reluctant seller. He requires a trade package rather than a UFA signing, and our only pick is a 4th-rounder. Secondary to Iginla on every axis except pure production.

recommendations.summary: Sign Daze as a July UFA if Iginla is lost: 89 base, 127 pts, 29 years old, $3.00M expiring from 78-point CHI.
recommendations.rationale: 127 points at $3.00M is the highest production available per dollar. He is a one-year fix, not a bridge, at age 29 with POTE 78. If Iginla signs, Daze is unnecessary; if Iginla goes elsewhere, Daze is the best fallback.

recommendations.summary: Sign Sturm as a July UFA: 85 base, 81 pts, age 26, $1.00M expiring from 82-point PHI.
recommendations.rationale: PHI's $66.73M payroll against $2.14M profit is the worst financial profile among non-playoff clubs, making them potential forced sellers. At $1.00M and age 26 with POTE 76, he is a low-cost LW addition behind Gaborik and Havlat.

recommendations.proposed: Jarome Iginla, Martin Havlat, Marco Sturm
recommendations.summary: Do not pursue Avery despite his $400K and 94 FACE; his 9 pts in 82 GP and 79 base make him a faceoff specialist without the scoring underneath.
recommendations.rationale: Bell at the same cost closes toughness and faceoffs with more upside. Avery's production is the worst of any available player on a multi-year deal; the grade profile is misleading.

recommendations.proposed: Jarome Iginla, Martin Havlat, Marco Sturm
recommendations.summary: Do not pursue Bertuzzi (94 base, 128 pts, $2.6M, age 30, POTE 58) despite the absurd value; POTE 58 means his ceiling is set and he becomes another Sundin by 2009.
recommendations.rationale: VAN at 99 points won't trade him mid-season and his contract has 1 year left, so he isn't even a July UFA. The POTE 58 at age 30 is the same profile as Sundin five years ago, which is exactly the problem this summer is supposed to solve.

recommendations.proposed: Jarome Iginla, Martin Havlat, Marco Sturm
recommendations.summary: Add Cammalleri (LA, 22, POTE 98, $1.10M expiring) as a camp audition if the July budget allows.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 79 points with 14 expiring deals cannot retain all of them. POTE 98 at 22 and $1.10M is the highest-upside depth signing available. He won't make the team in camp but the cost is a rounding error and the upside is a top-nine winger in two years.

recommendations.summary: Trade Chistov and the 4th-rounder to Chicago for Bell ($900K, 2 years left, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE).
recommendations.rationale: Bell is the only player in the league who closes both the toughness void (zero players at 80+ TOUG on our roster) and the faceoff gap (L4 mean 52, quantified by the coach on May 5). Chistov is displaced by Alexeev per the coach and walks for nothing in July if not traded. CHI at 78 points with $31.73M profit are rebuilding and Bell's 28 pts in 80 GP caps his offensive value in their system.

recommendations.summary: Trade Colaiacovo and Koltsov to San Jose for Stuart (87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91, age 25).
recommendations.rationale: Roberts (88 base, 38, expiring) is a write-off; Stuart replaces him with eight years of development remaining. Colaiacovo is a coach-flagged write-off (31 GP, 0.39 pts/g, 17.9 MPG) and Koltsov's ACCE 96 is surplus behind Gaborik at 98 SPEE. SJ at 72 points with 13 expiring deals on $45.39M payroll are shedding salary, but at 72 points they may not deal a POTE 91 blueliner. Stuart's salary is not visible so the payroll effect is incomplete. Acceptance uncertain.

recommendations.summary: If Ottawa trades Havlat before free agency, swap Upshall ($1.20M expiring, POTE 99, CHKG 87) for Havlat ($900K expiring, 103 pts, 87 base).
recommendations.rationale: Havlat replaces Sundin's 0.97 pts/g at $900K against Sundin's $8.40M. Upshall is the second player the coach says Alexeev displaces (Chistov going to CHI for Bell). OTT at 77 points with 11 expiring deals are thinning. If Havlat simply walks, sign him as a UFA instead and keep Upshall as depth.

recommendations.summary: Sign Iginla as a UFA at $6.50M if CGY lets him walk in July.
recommendations.rationale: Iginla at 93 base, 128 pts in 76 GP, age 27, TOUG 85 closes the RW scoring void left by Mogilny (0.83 at 36), raises the toughness floor by 10 points, and fills the 30-33 age band where only Tucker (3 GP) currently sits. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring deals and $14.43M profit have no reason to retain him.

recommendations.summary: Close the Luongo/DiPietro monitoring task; it is complete.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is on the roster at 94 overall with 2 years at $1.60M. The GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19. No open window exists.

recommendations.summary: Give Alexeev a third-line wing role at camp; his 0.55 pts/g has outproduced both dressed wingers all season while he sits scratched.
recommendations.rationale: Alexeev 0.55 pts/g vs Chistov 0.29 and Upshall 0.29. The mismatch was flagged in April and nothing changed. At 23 with POTE 94 he has earned a top-nine look or his production goes to waste again.

recommendations.summary: Target 60+ games for Colaiacovo next season; 31 games at 17.9 MPG is the workload of a starter in a backup's schedule.
recommendations.rationale: At 22 with POTE 99, his 17.9 MPG shows the staff trusts him in short bursts. He needs reps to convert that into a full season. With Eminger expiring and Klesla a sell candidate, the logjam clears on its own.

recommendations.summary: Spezza gets a real top-nine audition at camp; if he cannot hold it there, stop dressing him next season.
recommendations.rationale: 0.33 pts/g on 6.7 MPG at 21 with POTE 99. The season is done for development purposes. Camp is the last lever before he turns 22 with no first-team contribution.

recommendations.summary: Same camp audition as Spezza: top-nine on merit or stop dressing him.
recommendations.rationale: 0.29 pts/g on 7.9 MPG at 21. POTE 99 means nothing if it never converts to more than fourth-line production.

recommendations.summary: Chlup keeps his second-line role untouched; 0.83 pts/g on 16.9 MPG at 19 is what earned minutes look like.
recommendations.rationale: No intervention needed. He is exactly where his production says he should be.

recommendations.summary: Assign Chlup to first-line centre before camp begins.
recommendations.rationale: 0.88 pts/g on 18.2 MPG at 19, with his rate rising as his load rose. He has outperformed every centre on this roster over the full season.

recommendations.summary: McCabe stays on the sell list; his final season rate is 0.48 pts/g.
recommendations.rationale: Season finished at 0.48 pts/g on 21.5 MPG at age 29, well below the 0.60 threshold. His early-season 1.42 pace was a 24-game anomaly.

recommendations.summary: Give Abid 18+ MPG next season.
recommendations.rationale: 0.70 pts/g on 11.5 MPG. His minutes were cut from 20.1 mid-season while his rate held. He is a quality winger on penalty-killer minutes.

recommendations.summary: Run a system-fit review for Afinogenov, Richards and Nash before finalising next season's top six.
recommendations.rationale: Afinogenov 1.17→0.73, Richards 1.08→0.71, Nash 0.83→0.42. All three at flat minutes with no injuries, all at ages where the expected direction is up.

recommendations.summary: Spacek, Spezza and Upshall need a real camp audition or stop dressing them.
recommendations.rationale: Spacek finished 5.2 MPG and 0.28 pts/g, Spezza 4.6 and 0.24, Upshall 4.8 and 0.27. None has a meaningful role.

recommendations.summary: No morale action needed for Washington; the room is at 94 or above across the board and trending up.
recommendations.rationale: Lowest morale is Spezza at 88 (up 5), a development scratch the GM placed intentionally. All dressed players sit at 94 or 100. The results are carrying the room and one game remains.

recommendations.summary: If Gaborik is healthy, dress him on the first line for this game and move one winger down to the second.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik holds the roster's best marks in scoring (98), playmaking (99), speed (99), and clutch (99). Against a 39-26 opponent on the last night we go all out per the GM's standing order, and leaving the best player in four categories out contradicts that.

recommendations.summary: L1 through L3 and both PP units are correctly constructed. No rearrangement improves them for this opponent.
recommendations.rationale: L1 checking mean 79 with Sundin at 91 draws; L2 has Chlup at 80 and speed mean 87; L3 gets Richards at 75 draws and 97 clutch. PP1 scoring mean 88, PP2 speed mean 91. These units suit their jobs.

recommendations.summary: We have no fourth-line centre who wins draws. Best available is 55, mean across L4 is 52.
recommendations.rationale: This is the same gap flagged in April. No player currently on the roster provides faceoff coverage for a checking line. Only a trade or a camp signing fills it.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 94 OVR with morale 100. Kolzig is 87 but Luongo is the clear starter against a team scoring 2.80 per game in their last 10.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes for WSH. Every forward line and defensive pairing already mismatches in our favor.
recommendations.rationale: Our D pair 1 (Fischer CHKG 92, Jackman CHKG 92) faces Jagr and that is correct. Our second and third lines face 74 and 66 OVR units. Their 284 PP chances allowed this season means our 32.3 percent PP gets extra looks. No reordering of D pairs or forward line swaps improves these matchups.

recommendations.summary: McCabe stays on the sell list. Final season 62 pts in 82 GP (0.76 pts/g) masks a 0.48 back half.
recommendations.rationale: At 29 with 4 years and $3.00M, the second-half decline is the real read. His value is the full-season optics, and those fade next year.

recommendations.summary: Jackman is a sell at $0.70M x 3. Final: 37 pts in 80 GP, 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: His 29.6 MPG is the asset; the production rate does not justify keeping those minutes on our roster. Cheapest top-pair value in the league for the right buyer.

recommendations.summary: Klesla is a sell. Two consecutive declining seasons (0.38, 0.36, now 0.37 pts/g) on flat 15 MPG at age 23.
recommendations.rationale: He is not improving. At $0.90M x 2 there is still return available before he becomes a low-value depth piece.

recommendations.summary: Eminger must move before July. 23 pts in 64 GP, 0.36 pts/g, $1.20M expiring at 21.
recommendations.rationale: The slide from 0.44 to 0.36 is locked. After free agency he is a zero return.

recommendations.summary: Renew Kaberle urgently. 44 pts in 74 GP, 0.59 pts/g, OVR 84, age 27, $1.90M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: He is the best offensive defenceman on the roster and walks after this season. If we lose him and sell McCabe and Jackman we have no top pair.

recommendations.summary: Move Chlup to first-line centre for next season; his 75 FACE gives L1 a competent draw-taker and frees Sundin from faceoff duty at age 34.
recommendations.rationale: Coach's May 13 recommendation. Chlup's 75 FACE on L1 lifts the team's faceoff distribution without requiring an external acquisition. Richards at 70 FACE slides to L3 as the next-best draw-taker.

recommendations.summary: Put Richards at third-line centre for next season; his 70 FACE and 85 PASS give L3 both the draw and the playmaking the line currently lacks.
recommendations.rationale: Coach flagged L4 faceoff mean at 52 on April 9. Richards to L3 raises that line to 70. Tucker at 67 FACE on L4 is the residual gap that cannot be fixed internally.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev replaces Upshall on the fourth line; 0.55 pts/g versus 0.29 at comparable ice time.
recommendations.rationale: Coach's May 13 report explicitly names Alexeev over Upshall on production. Upshall's 80 CHKG is the only contribution that Alexeev does not match.

recommendations.summary: Bell at 88 TOUG and 86 CHKG is the only league-wide player closing both the toughness and L4 faceoff gaps simultaneously; CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring are motivated sellers.
recommendations.rationale: Zero Toronto players at 80+ toughness. Tucker at 83 CHKG but 70 TOUG raises L4 checking from 61 to approximately 68 but leaves toughness untouched. Bell closes both at 24 years old with POTE 81.

recommendations.summary: Iginla at 93 base, 27, 140 points, expiring, replaces Mogilny's declining 0.79 pts/g and the Roberts vacancy simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny 36 declining, Roberts 38 expiring and $5.10M. The club loses approximately 70 points of top-six production if both fall or leave. Iginla's 140 points at $6.50M from a 70-point CGY club with $14.43M profit is the only target that closes the scoring bridge and toughness ceiling together.

recommendations.summary: Stuart at 87 base, 25, POTE 91, 89 CHKG and 80 TOUG replaces Roberts' expiring $5.10M deal with eight years of development.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts at 38 with durability 98 is irreplaceable for next season's playoff run but his contract expires at $5.10M. Stuart closes toughness (80), checking (89) and durability simultaneously at 25. SJ at 72 points with 13 expiring may not deal POTE 91.

recommendations.summary: Speed (21 players at 80+) and stamina (11 at 80+) are overcovered; no action needed and no reason to trade from these groups.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik 98, Afinogenov 96, Mogilny 94, Koltsov 92, Fischer 89 at speed. Kaberle 97, McCabe 94, Sundin 92 at endurance. Neither role constrains the lineup.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik ($1.10M, 99 pts, 23), Richards ($1.00M, 66 pts, 25), Nash ($1.20M, 39 pts, 20), Eminger ($1.20M, POTE 99, 21) and Chlup ($2.34M, 59 pts, 19) on 5-6 year deals in July 2005.
recommendations.rationale: These five are the window. Eleven contracts worth $12.10M expire in the same summer they are all at breakout value. If any two walk simultaneously the core collapses.

recommendations.summary: Replace Mogilny (36, 0.79 pts/g decline, $5.50M) with Iginla (27, 140 pts/73 GP, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring at CGY) in July.
recommendations.rationale: Same salary slot, nine years younger, closes the toughness void the Coach quantified at mean 57. Mogilny is a negative asset by July 2006.

recommendations.summary: Attempt to trade Belfour (92 base, expiring, $6.50M) or Roberts (81 base, 81 pts, expiring, $2.70M) for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic before July.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto owns only a 4th-rounder. The guide notes that any player above 80 the club will not re-sign can be traded for a pick. Either recovery converts a zero-pick club into one with ammunition for summer packages.

recommendations.summary: Sundin's $8.40M x 5 years cannot be moved mid-contract; the plan is Chlup taking his minutes as production fades, not a trade.
recommendations.rationale: Contract runs to age 38. No renegotiation possible per game mechanics. Chlup at 19 with POTE 95 and 59 pts in 71 GP is the succession plan and needs top-nine minutes now.

recommendations.summary: Offer Gaborik a 5-6 year deal on day 1 of free agency; he is 91 base at 23 with 87 points and $1.10M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: He is the single highest-value renewal on the roster. The March 21 priority list puts him first. At $1.10M he is well below market for a 91-base RW; a bidding war in July is the main risk.

recommendations.summary: Offer Richards a 5-6 year deal alongside Gaborik; 64 points at 25, $1.00M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Priority 2 on the March 21 list. Together Gaborik and Richards are $2.10M in combined salary for a 151-point core; locking both removes the two biggest renewal risks in the same week.

recommendations.summary: Offer Nash a 5-6 year deal; he is 20, $1.20M expiring, and part of the young core the GM refused to trade in January.
recommendations.rationale: The March 21 list puts Nash and Eminger as priorities 3-4. At 20 with a market rate far above $1.20M, a 5-6 year lock is the cheapest way to keep him.

recommendations.summary: Offer Eminger a 5-6 year deal; he is 21, POTE 99, $1.20M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: GM vetoed the Chara trade in January specifically because Eminger at 21 with POTE 99 is worth more to the timeline. Locking him on 5-6 years secures the blueline for five seasons at below-market cost.

recommendations.summary: Offer Kaberle a 5-year deal; he is 27, $1.90M expiring, and the oldest of the five core renewals.
recommendations.rationale: His prime is now rather than ahead. Five years covers his best remaining hockey; beyond that the money stretches past his decline. The December 2004 staggered-lock plan named him for 5-6 years.

recommendations.summary: Offer Abid a 2-3 year deal at or near $0.40M; he carries 66 points on 13.8 MPG at 25.
recommendations.rationale: The coach wants him at 16-18 MPG next season. At $0.40M he is the cheapest impact forward on the roster and the easiest renewal to execute.

recommendations.summary: Offer Tellqvist a 2-year deal at $0.80M; the GM's standing order is to keep and develop him.
recommendations.rationale: GM instruction from January 15: Tellqvist stays, give him time to develop. Two years is the right length to let that play out without overcommitting.

recommendations.summary: Offer Chistov a 2-year deal at $1.10M; he is 22 with POTE 95, SPEE 89 and remains depth even if Alexeev passes him on the depth chart.
recommendations.rationale: The manual's target shape calls for hoarding young talent. A 22-year-old with POTE 95 at $1.10M as a healthy scratch is better than a trade that returns a 74-76 depth player. His trade value holds on the bench.

recommendations.summary: Offer Colaiacovo a 2-year deal; let camp decide whether he makes the roster.
recommendations.rationale: 22 years old, POTE 99, but only 31 games and 0.39 pts/g. The coach wants a real camp audition. A 2-year deal at $1.10M gives that without a long-term commitment either way.

recommendations.summary: Offer Alexeev a 2-year deal; he outproduces Chistov and Upshall at 0.55 pts/g but is in the camp audition group.
recommendations.rationale: The coach wants him dressed and his production rate is the best of the three audition forwards. A 2-year deal at $1.10M is the right price for a 23-year-old still proving himself.

recommendations.summary: Let Upshall go; he is 21, 0.29 pts/g, and Alexeev and Chistov cover his spot at the same price with higher ceilings.
recommendations.rationale: The coach names him as the one the development group should displace. At 0.29 pts/g against Chistov at 0.55 and Alexeev at 0.55, there is no case for using a roster spot or a renewal slot on him.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts go; he is 38 at $2.70M and the March 21 renewal plan lists him as a walk.
recommendations.rationale: No renewal case at 38. His departure opens $2.70M that helps fund an Iginla-type acquisition.

recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour a reduced-salary deal; plan for him to decline or retire, freeing $6.50M.
recommendations.rationale: GM standing order: offer a reduced contract, he probably will not accept. Budget for the $6.50M walking. At 40 the retirement risk is real. Luongo at 91 base with 2 years left becomes the clear number one.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla (CGY, 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, $6.50M expiring) as the top July acquisition target.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny has fallen to 0.79 pts/g at 36 and Roberts is walking. Iginla closes the RW scoring void and the toughness ceiling (TOUG 85) in one signing. The Belfour and Roberts money ($9.20M combined) covers his salary.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82) to fill the L4 faceoff and toughness void.
recommendations.rationale: The coach has flagged the L4 gap since April with checking mean 61, toughness mean 57, faceoffs 50. Bell is the only league-wide player closing both simultaneously. Chicago at 73 points with 10 expiring are motivated sellers.

recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri (LA, 22, POTE 98, 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M expiring) if LA cannot retain him alongside Frolov.
recommendations.rationale: A 22-year-old with POTE 98 at $1.10M is the highest-value UFA available. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring cannot keep both him and Frolov.

recommendations.summary: Decide before July whether to trade Spezza (21, POTE 99, 0.33 pts/g at 6.7 MPG, morale 88) or give him top-nine minutes.
recommendations.rationale: The coach has flagged this seven times. His trade value peaks while POTE 99 holds credibility. If he stays at 6.7 MPG the asset erodes further. This is the one non-expiring decision the GM must make before free agency opens.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Stuart (25, 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, 90 INJU, POTE 91, $1.80M expiring, 52 pts/77 GP) from SJ via a Roberts-inclusive package.
recommendations.rationale: Closes defense toughness (no roster D above 75 TOUG), checking distribution, and durability (only 4 roster players above 80 INJU) simultaneously. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring and $20.74M profit is a motivated seller. Roberts at 81 base and $5.10M expiring is the over-80 mechanic piece that funds the gap.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell (24, 80 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, $900K, 2 years) from CHI with Tucker, a recovered pick, and Chistov.
recommendations.rationale: Bell is the only player in the league closing toughness (88), checking (86), and faceoffs (82) at once. Coach quantified L4 TOUG mean at 57 on April 9; no internal arrangement exceeds 73. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit are sellers. Coach flagged Chistov as tradeable on May 5.

recommendations.summary: Sign Belanger (27, 82 base, FACE 97, CHKG 83, TOUG 79, $700K, expiring) as a July UFA.
recommendations.rationale: FACE 97 is the best draw in the league and his 14 points in 64 GP is bottom-six production, which is what L4 requires. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring will not re-sign him. No trade needed, no assets spent, no draft capital required.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Bouwmeester (21, 81 base, POTE 95, 27 pts/79 GP, $1.20M expiring) from FLA with Tucker plus the 4th-rounder as the base offer.
recommendations.rationale: FLA has 19 expiring contracts (league-high), $51.07M payroll, and only $13.64M profit. They cannot retain a POTE 95 blueliner. At 21 with 79 games already played, this is a franchise defenseman arriving early. Need his TOUG and CHKG to confirm physical fit before committing a second asset.

recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri (22, 79 base, POTE 97, 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M expiring) as a July UFA to fill the scoring bridge.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny at 36 and 0.79 pts/g plus Roberts at 38 and expiring creates a roughly 70-point top-six void. Cammalleri at 60 points in 61 games with POTE 97 at age 22 is the cheapest scoring bridge available. LA cannot retain both him and Frolov (POTE 95, 55 pts/62 GP). Competition risk is real.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Sutton (27, 78 base, CHKG 90, TOUG 94, INJU 87, $1.34M, 4 years left) from ATL for Tucker plus the 4th-rounder.
recommendations.rationale: TOUG 94 and CHKG 90 on four locked years at $1.34M is the cheapest toughness available. The toughness void (no roster player above 75) needs an immediate external fix. ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring and $25.99M profit are borderline sellers who might prefer roster flexibility over a 27-year-old.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla (27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring) from CGY but only with a Chistov-or-Spezza-inclusive package plus the over-80 mechanic pick.
recommendations.rationale: Same salary slot as Mogilny ($6.50M), nine years younger, 140 points versus 0.79 pts/g, and TOUG 85 raises the team ceiling. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit must sell. The package requires a POTE 95+ young player because Tucker plus the 4th is nowhere near 93-base value. The GM must decide if the window justifies moving a prospect.

recommendations.proposed: Trade Roberts and/or Belfour via over-80 expiring mechanic for draft picks
recommendations.summary: Move Roberts (81 base, $5.10M expiring) and/or Belfour (92 base, $6.50M expiring) after the playoffs for a draft pick each via the over-80 mechanic, creating the ammunition every package above requires.
recommendations.rationale: We hold one 4th-rounder. The guide's over-80 expiring mechanic converts two players we are losing anyway into picks that fund the Bell, Stuart, and Bouwmeester packages. Roberts at 81 and Belfour at 92 both clear the threshold. This is the prerequisite step that makes every other target addressable.

recommendations.summary: Monitor Hartnell (23, 79 base, POTE 94, TOUG 87, 25 pts/82 GP, $1.10M expiring) as a secondary toughness target if Bell or Sutton are unavailable.
recommendations.rationale: TOUG 87 with POTE 94 at 23 fills the toughness gap with upside. But NSH at 101 points is a playoff team, so they are not a July seller unless they re-sign him and trade from strength. Lower priority than Bell (cheaper, 2 years locked, from a confirmed seller).

recommendations.summary: Offer Tucker + Chistov + 4th-rounder to Chicago for Mark Bell; closes the L4 toughness (70 to 88) and faceoff (67 to 82) gaps in one move and saves $1.50M/year.
recommendations.rationale: Bell at 24, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, $900K with two years left is the only league-wide player closing both quantified L4 gaps simultaneously. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring deals and $31.73M profit are triaging their roster; Tucker gives them a 92 CHKG checker immediately and Chistov at 22/POTE 95/SPEE 89 is a speed prospect for their future. Coach flagged Chistov tradeable on May 5.

recommendations.summary: Offer Mogilny + Spezza + Upshall + 4th-rounder to Calgary for Iginla; replaces 0.79 pts/g at 36 with 1.92 pts/g at 27, closes the scoring bridge and the RW toughness ceiling in one swap.
recommendations.rationale: Iginla at 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring from CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring deals is the single highest-value target available. CGY rebuilding gets Spezza at 21/POTE 99 (franchise-center prospect) and Upshall at 21/POTE 99/87 CHKG; Mogilny can be released. Net saving $1.20M/year. Coach flagged Spezza trade-or-develop on May 11.

recommendations.summary: Offer Roberts + Koltsov + 4th-rounder to San Jose for Brad Stuart; replaces a 38-year-old expiring blueliner with a 25-year-old at 87 base/POTE 91 who closes durability, checking, and toughness gaps on the blue line simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Stuart at 25, 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91, $1.80M expiring, 52 pts/77 GP. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring deals and $20.74M profit cannot re-sign everyone. Roberts gives them INJU 98 and 82 GP at 38; Koltsov at 24/POTE 94/ACCE 96 is a skill winger surplus to our lineup. The risk is SJ at 76 points may keep Stuart.

recommendations.summary: If Bell does not come, sign Eric Belanger as a UFA at $700K; his FACE 97 and CHKG 83 close the faceoff gap at one-third Bell's cost with no players surrendered.
recommendations.rationale: Belanger at 82 base, FACE 97 (league best), CHKG 83, TOUG 79, $700K expiring from LA at 79 points with 14 expiring deals. No trade capital required. The risk is competition from every contender needing a draw-taker. He does not close the toughness gap (79 vs Bell's 88) but raises the L4 mean from 57 to approximately 70.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev at 0.55 pts/g outproduces Chistov (0.29) and Upshall (0.29); he needs top-nine minutes next season or we're wasting him.
recommendations.rationale: Alexeev finished at 30 points in 55 games on 8.3 MPG. Chistov and Upshall combined for 40 points in 136 games on more minutes. The rate gap is 1.9x and unresolved since April.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza a genuine 15+ MPG audition at camp next season; POTE 99 with 6.7 MPG this year wasted the only asset that mattered.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza finished 15 points in 46 games on 6.7 MPG (0.33 pts/g). His season is gone; camp assignment is the only lever left before next year.

recommendations.summary: Spacek at 0.34 pts/g on 7.6 MPG and Upshall at 0.29 on 7.9 MPG are earning their fourth-line minutes at age 19 and 21 respectively.
recommendations.rationale: Both are within the 7 MPG band a depth player expects. Their rates match their role. No gap to close.

recommendations.summary: Assign Chlup to first-line centre for next season before camp begins.
recommendations.rationale: 0.88 pts/g on 18.2 MPG at 19, both rate and minutes rising. He is ready for the top job now.

recommendations.summary: Give Abid back 18+ MPG in camp. His minutes fell from 20.1 to 11.5 and his rate followed.
recommendations.rationale: 0.70 pts/g on 11.5 MPG at 25 in his prime. The minutes loss caused the rate decline, not the other way around.

recommendations.summary: Trade Klesla this offseason. Two consecutive declining seasons confirm it.
recommendations.rationale: 0.50 at 22 to 0.31 at 23 on flat 15 MPG. His value is higher now than next year when the trend is locked in.

recommendations.summary: Trade Jackman this offseason at $0.70M x 3. His 30 MPG is killing his production.
recommendations.rationale: 0.65 to 0.39 pts/g while carrying 29.4 MPG at 24. He is the cheapest top-pair minutes in the league and his value is the minutes, not the points.

recommendations.summary: Plan for Sundin (0.97 at 34), Mogilny (0.83 at 36) and Roberts (0.86 at 38) to decline further. Do not build next season assuming they hold.
recommendations.rationale: All three saw rate drops on rising minutes, the classic aging pattern. One season more and each is a lower-tier contributor.

recommendations.summary: No change to Fischer's role, but watch his trend. 0.63 to 0.50 on rising minutes.
recommendations.rationale: The GM has him protected and the absolute numbers are still fine. If next season mirrors this window's end rate he drifts to a top-four role.

recommendations.summary: No morale-driven ice-time changes needed; the room is healthy with everyone at 94 or above and trending up.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza is lowest at 88 but rising (+3) after a recent win. Alexeev, Spacek and Upshall are all in the low 90s recovering from brief dips. Every player on L1-L4 is at 100. The recent win lifted morale across the board by 5 to 9 points.

recommendations.summary: We need a bottom-six centre who wins faceoffs; the L4 mean of 52 is the worst unit on the roster by a wide margin.
recommendations.rationale: L4 faceoff mean 52, best 55. No centre on the roster outside Sundin (91), Chlup (80), Roberts (76), and Richards (75) wins draws. This gap persists regardless of how lines are assembled.

recommendations.summary: No line changes for Washington. The units are built correctly and this game is meaningless for the standings.
recommendations.rationale: We are eliminated at 33-34-14. K2's checking mean of 84 is the team's strongest defensive unit and K1's 79 is adequate with Roberts 85 and Fischer 85 as the best checking forwards available. No rearrangement improves tonight.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming.
recommendations.rationale: OVR 94 vs Kolzig at 87. WSH is on an 8-game heater scoring 2.90/g; we need our best netminder.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes for WSH. The auto-pairings give us favorable matchups on every line.
recommendations.rationale: Our P1 D (Fischer/Jackman, both CHKG 92) gets Jagr's line. Our P2 D (Kaberle/McCabe, both 84) gets their 69-70 second pair. We win all four faceoff circles. Their 12.3% PP means no special kill unit needed beyond what is already set.

recommendations.summary: Sell McCabe this offseason: 29, 4 years at $3.00M, recent-window rate 0.48.
recommendations.rationale: Full season reads 0.76 but his last 58 games are 0.48. The hot start is gone. At 29 with 4 years left on $3M, a declining defenceman's trade value now exceeds his remaining contribution.

recommendations.summary: Sell Jackman this offseason: 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG at $0.70M x 3.
recommendations.rationale: His season rate confirmed at 0.46 on 80 games (was 0.48 on 73 in March). His market value is the volume of top-pair minutes at the cheapest price in the league.

recommendations.summary: Sell Klesla this offseason: two consecutive declines, 0.37 at 23.
recommendations.rationale: 0.38 at 22, 0.37 at 23, flat 15 MPG both years. No development signal. $0.90M x 2 remaining.

recommendations.summary: Sell Eminger urgently this offseason: contract expires, rate fell again to 0.36.
recommendations.rationale: Rate slid from 0.44 to 0.38 to 0.36 across three reads this season. His contract expires after this year — no move means no return.

recommendations.summary: Open a renewal conversation with Kaberle: contract expires, GM has named him a keeper.
recommendations.rationale: 0.60 pts/g on 20.8 MPG at 27. One year left on $1.90M. If the GM wants him, the renewal needs to happen before his value moves.

recommendations.summary: Dress Alexeev for Washington; he at 0.55 pts/g outproduces Chistov and Upshall at 0.29 who are both in the lineup.
recommendations.rationale: 30 points in 55 games beats both dressed wingers by nearly double the rate. He's 23, morale 92, POTE 94. On a maximize-quality night his production is the argument.

recommendations.summary: Flag Spezza for offseason: morale 88 is the lowest in the young group, and the season is a development write-off at 6.7 MPG and 0.33 pts/g.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 at 21 with minutes that collapsed from 9.1 to 4.8. Nothing changes now, but the GM needs to know camp assignment is the only lever left.

recommendations.summary: Flag Colaiacovo for offseason: 31 games is not a development pattern for a 22-year-old with POTE 99 getting 17.9 MPG when he plays.
recommendations.rationale: Either he's a regular next year or he isn't. In-and-out at 38% share stunts growth even when the minutes he does get are good.

recommendations.summary: Move Chlup to first-line centre for next season before camp.
recommendations.rationale: 0.88 pts/g at 19 on 18.2 MPG, up from 0.62 on 11.0. He is the only young player whose rate and minutes both rose.

recommendations.summary: Put McCabe back on the sell list for offseason.
recommendations.rationale: Back-half rate of 0.48 pts/g across 58 games at age 29. My March call to clear him was built on the 0.76 season average; the direction inside it is down.

recommendations.summary: No changes before Saturday's game against WSH.
recommendations.rationale: This is a development-trends phase, not a matchup phase. Lines and goalies are set for the game already.

recommendations.summary: We need a young forward who can take minutes off Sundin, Roberts and Mogilny next season.
recommendations.rationale: All three got more ice as the season wore on while their rates fell. Sundin 16.9 to 21.7 MPG at 34, Roberts 16.5 to 21.4 at 38, Mogilny 16.9 to 19.1 at 36.

recommendations.summary: Schedule an offseason system-fit review covering Nash, Afinogenov and Richards together.
recommendations.rationale: All three lost 40-50% of their rate with flat or near-flat minutes and no injury. Nash 0.83 to 0.42, Afinogenov 1.17 to 0.73, Richards 1.08 to 0.71. Three separate players, same pattern.

recommendations.summary: The room is healthy: nearly all at 100 or 94, and trending up with recent wins. No morale-driven line change needed.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza is lowest at 88 but gained 3 last save and is recovering from a long scratch stretch. Every other skater is at 94+. The recent positive swings across the roster confirm the team's results are lifting morale naturally.

recommendations.slot: left wing, third or fourth line
recommendations.summary: Give Abid 16-18 MPG next season; his 66 points on 13.8 MPG at age 25 is a rate-to-minutes mismatch that will eventually cost morale.
recommendations.rationale: Abid's morale reads 100 today so there is no tonight fix. His production rate (0.80 pts/g over 82 games) is a top-six winger's output on fourth-line minutes. The finding from March 16 flagged this as a risk window before his morale breaks.

recommendations.summary: Top three lines are well-constructed for the personnel available; no rearrangement improves them.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has Sundin's faceoffs (87) and Mogilny's scoring (90). L2 has Chlup producing 0.88 pts/g despite the faceoff weakness (mean 57). L3 has Richards' clutch (93) and stamina (95) plus Chistov's speed (94). Breaking any of these costs chemistry for no grade improvement.

recommendations.summary: We need a bottom-six centre who wins faceoffs (70+) and checks (75+). No arrangement of this roster fills the L4 draw requirement.
recommendations.rationale: L4 faceoff mean is 50, best 51. Our only faceoff winners above 70 are Sundin 87, Chlup 76, Roberts 72, Richards 71, all already placed on L1-L3. This gap was flagged April 13 and remains open.

recommendations.summary: If Upshall is not being scratched for a stated development reason, Alexeev takes his spot: 0.55 pts/g versus 0.29.
recommendations.rationale: Alexeev outproduces both Upshall (0.29) and Chistov (0.29) yet does not dress. His production-to-role mismatch has been unresolved since April 23. If the GM has a development-space reason for Upshall specifically, I accept it.

recommendations.summary: Keep all lines as-is for WSH.
recommendations.rationale: Auto-pairing puts Fischer and Jackman (both CHKG 88) against Jagr's first line via the P1-to-L1 link, and Roberts (CHKG 84, TOUG 86) is already on L1. The D-pair slot order correctly assigns our best checkers to their best player. WSH PP is 12.3% so there is no sheltering priority that overrides this.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at OVR 92 is the right answer against Kolzig at OVR 87. Standing order from Jan 19: confirm no tired-goalie icon before locking the start.

recommendations.summary: McCabe on the sell list: final season 0.76 pts/g over 82 games but 0.48 over the last 58. At 29 with $3.00M x 4, the recent window is the real read.
recommendations.rationale: Season locked at 62 points in 82 games. My May 2 finding identified the 0.48 recent window; the season finishing confirms the early hot start has fully bled off. Four years of $3.00M on a declining defenceman is more valuable as a trade chip now.

recommendations.summary: Jackman confirmed sell: 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG at $0.70M x 3. Cheapest top-pair minutes in the league.
recommendations.rationale: Final: 37 points in 80 games. Already flagged March 23; season confirms the number. His value to another club (top-pair minutes at a bargain rate) exceeds his value here.

recommendations.summary: Klesla confirmed sell: 0.37 pts/g, second consecutive declining season, $0.90M x 2 remaining.
recommendations.rationale: Final: 30 points in 82 games on 14.8 MPG. Confirmed March 23; the season locked it. Two years and $0.90M is return he can still command.

recommendations.summary: Fischer stays. 0.53 pts/g at 24 with 4 years and $3.70M. GM keeper.
recommendations.rationale: 41 points in 77 games on 22.4 MPG. GM rejected him as a trade candidate on January 15th and called him very very good. No change.

recommendations.summary: Kaberle stays but his expiring contract needs the GM's attention: 0.60 pts/g at 27, $1.90M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: 44 points in 74 games on 20.8 MPG. GM called him a star on January 15th. The number justifies a raise; the decision is the GM's to make.

recommendations.summary: Colaiacovo needs a real camp audition: only 31 games, 0.39 pts/g, age 22, expiring.
recommendations.rationale: 12 points in 31 games on 17.9 MPG. Not dressed recently. If camp doesn't give him a genuine shot he follows Eminger out the door for nothing.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell as the primary summer target: he closes the toughness gap (88 TOUG), the checking depth (86 CHKG), and the faceoff void (82 FACE) in one move at age 24.
recommendations.rationale: Zero Toronto players carry 80+ TOUG. Bell is the only league-wide player who raises toughness, checking, and faceoffs simultaneously while still being young enough to develop (POTE 81). Chicago at 73 points with 10 expiring and $29.46M profit are motivated sellers.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla in July as the RW replacement for Mogilny: 93 base, 140 points in 73 games, 85 TOUG, closes both the scoring void and raises the team toughness ceiling.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny at 36 fell to 0.79 pts/g and is expiring. Iginla is the only player who replaces that production AND carries 85 TOUG, which would be the first 80+ toughness grade on the roster. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him.

recommendations.summary: Explore Stuart as the Roberts replacement: 25 years old, 87 base, 89 CHKG, POTE 91, eight development years remaining.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts at 38 and 98 durability is expiring. Stuart at 25 with POTE 91 is the best available blueliner for this timeline. San Jose at 72 points with 13 expiring on $45.39M cannot retain all of them, though at 72 points they may not sell a POTE 91 defenceman.

recommendations.summary: The GM's January directive to fetch a high-90s goalie from a rebuilding club remains unfulfilled. After Belfour and Tellqvist expire, Ouellet at 23 is the only backup on contract.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour (40, $6.50M, 1y) and Tellqvist (25, $0.80M, 1y, 0.880 SV) both expire. That leaves Luongo (26, 2y) and Ouellet (23, 2y) with one 13-game sample. The GM set this goal on 2005-01-15 and it has not been closed.

recommendations.summary: Coach's Chlup-to-L1C assignment gives the top line a 75 FACE centre, but L3 and L4 still average below 70 without an acquisition.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup at 75 FACE and 70 TOUG is the best internal drafter after Sundin (90). This raises L1C from whatever was there but does not solve L3C or L4C. The internal ceiling on faceoffs is 75.

recommendations.summary: Coach demands Alexeev be dressed or traded. He outproduces wingers ahead of him. This is a roster decision for the GM: keep him for camp or include him in a package.
recommendations.rationale: Coach flagged this explicitly on 2005-05-11: 'outproduces the wingers dressed ahead of him and needs a resolution.' The Chistov memory notes he displaces Chistov or Upshall. Alexeev's trade value or his roster spot needs a decision before camp.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign these five on 5-6 year deals in July before any other negotiation; they are 13 of the $21.30M expiring cluster and the core of the next three seasons.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik scored 99 points at $1.10M, Richards 66 at $1.00M, Nash 39 at $1.20M with POTE 95, Eminger POTE 99 at $1.20M, Kaberle 44 points at $1.90M. All expire the same summer. The manual's contract-clustering warning applies directly; lock the stars first, split the rest across 2-3 year deals.

recommendations.summary: Let Belfour ($6.50M) and Roberts ($2.70M) expire in July; the $9.20M freed funds a top target like Iginla at $6.50M without raising net payroll.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 40 with POTE 50, Roberts is 38 with POTE 52. Luongo (91 base, 26, POTE 97) is the starter. The GM confirmed Belfour stays if he accepts reduced salary but did not expect acceptance. Freeing $9.20M against a $44.48M profit gives clean headroom for a $6.50M addition.

recommendations.proposed: any package with a contending club
recommendations.summary: Shop Fischer ($3.70M, 4 years left, 24, declining from 0.63 to 0.41 pts/g) in July while he still carries four years of team control and residual value.
recommendations.rationale: Fischer's production has dropped 35 percent and his salary is 15th-highest on the roster at $3.70M. His trade value falls every year until the deal expires in 2008-09 when he is 28. No buyer identified yet; this is a flag for the GM's summer planning, not an immediate action.

recommendations.summary: Do not protect the 24-29 group as untouchable if it gets a package closer to Iginla or Bell; the POTE pipeline below them is deep enough to absorb one or two departures.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto carries 13 players at 23 or under with six at POTE 95+. Upshall (POTE 99, 21), Chistov (POTE 95, 22), Alexeev (POTE 94, 23) are depth today but could be package fillers in July without damaging the three-year outlook. The missing draft picks mean players are the only currency.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik to five or six years at the top of market as the first action of free agency.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base ovr, age 23, POTE 90, $1.10M current salary. He is the most valuable player on the roster and the cheapest long-term contract available.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards to five or six years as the second renewal.
recommendations.rationale: Age 25, 64 points, $1.00M. Centre depth is scarce; losing him after Gaborik would gut the top two lines.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle to five or six years.
recommendations.rationale: Age 27, $1.90M, at his prime. The power play runs through him. Losing him at 27 would be losing him at his best.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash to five or six years immediately.
recommendations.rationale: Age 20, $1.20M. Locking a 20-year-old now is the cheapest insurance the roster has. The staggered-lock plan from December 2004 calls for this.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger to five or six years.
recommendations.rationale: Age 21, POTE 99, $1.20M. The GM correctly refused to trade him in January. This is a franchise defenceman on a rookie-scale deal.

recommendations.summary: Renew Chistov on four or five years only if he earns a middle-six role in camp.
recommendations.rationale: Age 22, POTE 95, $1.10M. Coach's order is a middle-six audition based on 0.30 pts/g held flat on a 47% minutes increase. If he holds it, lock him; if not, he walks.

recommendations.summary: Renew Colaiacovo on three years after camp, conditional on development.
recommendations.rationale: Age 22, $1.10M. Needs a season of real top-four minutes before the club commits five years.

recommendations.summary: If Alexeev earns the top-nine roster spot in camp, renew on three years. If not, move him this summer for a pick before he signs elsewhere for nothing.
recommendations.rationale: Age 23, $1.10M. Coach states he outproduces wingers ahead of him. The over-80-for-a-pick mechanic does not apply (his grade is below 80), so value recovery requires a trade, not a pick dump.

recommendations.summary: Let Upshall go if he fails the camp audition; renew on two years only if he makes the top nine.
recommendations.rationale: Age 21, $1.20M. Named in the coach's camp audition list alongside Spezza and Alexeev. Carrying a $1.20M player who cannot hold top-nine minutes is the kind of payroll the depth plan does not need.

recommendations.summary: Renew Abid on two years.
recommendations.rationale: Age 25, TOUG 80, CHKG 80, $0.40M. The cheapest toughness on the roster and the only player addressing the structural gap the coach has flagged four times since April.

recommendations.summary: Renew Tellqvist on two years as backup.
recommendations.rationale: Age 25, $0.80M. GM standing order: give him time to develop. Two years is consistent with that.

recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour two years at approximately $3.50M. If he refuses, he walks.
recommendations.rationale: Age 40, $6.50M current. GM standing order: 'Belfour stays if he wants to stay at reduced salary.' Manual says older players get two years. Luongo at 91 is the future number one regardless.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk. Do not re-sign at age 38 on $2.70M.
recommendations.rationale: Age 38, $2.70M. The renewal priority note of 21 March lists him among those who walk. At 38 the next step is down, not up.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla in free agency as the RW scoring solution for Mogilny's decline.
recommendations.rationale: CGY, age 27, 93 base, 140 points in 73 GP, $6.50M expiring. Mogilny fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g. CGY at 70 points with $14.43M profit cannot retain him.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bell in free agency to close the faceoff and toughness gap on the fourth line.
recommendations.rationale: CHI, age 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE. The only league-wide player closing both gaps simultaneously. CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring and $29.46M profit are motivated sellers.

recommendations.summary: No trades between now and the end of the regular season. The deadline passed and the GM's standing order is that everyone except Tucker and the 4th-rounder stays.
recommendations.rationale: Five games remain including playoffs. The roster is set. The only remaining chips (Tucker, 4th-rounder) are for offseason use.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla as the July priority; he fills the RW void left by Mogilny and the structural toughness gap (TOUG 85) in one acquisition.
recommendations.rationale: 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring from CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring. Closes two of three structural gaps simultaneously. Requires a major young-player package since we hold only a 4th-rounder.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Theodore from MTL as the playoff-ready backup and competition for Luongo.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base, 66 GP at 60.2 MPG, $5.50M expiring from MTL at 66 points with 15 expiring in full teardown. Satisfies the Jan 15 standing order for a high-90s goalie from a non-contender. Eliminates the Ouellet-as-backup problem.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bell from CHI as the cheapest acquisition closing both the faceoff gap and the toughness ceiling.
recommendations.rationale: 82 base, TOUG 95, CHKG 93, FACE 87, $900K, 2 years left. Production is 28 pts/80 GP on 17.8 MPG. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring are not desperate but not retainers either. Acceptance uncertain given CHI profitability.

recommendations.summary: Fund Iginla with a package centred on Koltsov (POTE 94, 19 pts/38 GP) plus Tucker, since no picks exist.
recommendations.rationale: Iginla at 93 base cannot be acquired for Tucker plus a 4th (worth ~74-76 base). Koltsov at 22 with POTE 94 is the only unprotected young asset with trade appeal to CGY. Upshall (POTE 99) is an alternative if Koltsov is retained for development.

recommendations.summary: If Iginla reaches UFA rather than being traded, sign him at $6.50M; the freed Belfour and Roberts money covers it.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour ($6.50M) and Roberts ($2.70M) expiring frees $9.20M. Iginla at $6.50M fits inside that with $2.70M to spare for Gaborik and Richards raises. No trade cost, but risk of losing him to another club.

recommendations.summary: If Havlat reaches UFA, sign him immediately at or near $900K; 103 pts/82 GP at that salary is unmatched value.
recommendations.rationale: 88 base, 103 pts/82 GP, $900K expiring from OTT at 77 points with 11 expiring. Does not fill a structural gap (FACE 51, TOUG 66) but provides elite top-six scoring at the lowest salary on the market.
