recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri off the UFA market if available; POTE 98 at 22 for $1.10M is the highest-value development signing possible.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 79 points with 14 expiring and $52.43M payroll cannot retain him and Frolov. 60 pts/61 GP at 22 with POTE 98. No trade cost; pure July signing.

recommendations.summary: Do not pursue Conroy at 31 and expiring; he blocks Richards (24, 66 pts, $1.00M) and Chlup (moving to L1C per the Coach) from the minutes they need.
recommendations.rationale: Conroy is excellent (102 pts/82 GP, FACE 95) but at 31 with one year left he is a two-year rental that displaces two developing centres under team control. The faceoff gap is better solved by Bell (24, 2 years, 87 FACE) or internal development at Richards and Chlup.

recommendations.summary: Drop Reid from the target list; his TOUG 50 and CHKG 50 create a new gap while filling the faceoff one, and STL at 86 points are not sellers.
recommendations.rationale: FACE 84 and 58 pts/73 GP are real, but TOUG 50 and CHKG 50 mean he adds zero physicality to the bottom six. STL at 86 points with only 8 expiring have no pressure to deal a 23-year-old with 58 points.

recommendations.summary: Trade Chistov to LA for Sean Avery: fills toughness (83) and faceoff (94) gaps simultaneously at $400K, saving $700K net.
recommendations.rationale: Avery at 77 overall/79 base carries TOUG 83, CHKG 88, FACE 94 in stored grades — the only player at a price we can reach who closes both structural gaps. LA holds Belanger (FACE 96), Allison (FACE 89), Stumpel (FACE 88) already; Avery is their fourth centre. Chistov at 22, POTE 95, SPEE 89 fits a 79-point team's youth pipeline. Acceptance uncertain: LA may prefer a proven 77-overall player over an unproven POTE 95 winger.

recommendations.summary: Trade Upshall, Tucker and our 4th-rounder to MTL for Komisarek, replacing departing Roberts with a 22-year-old POTE 92 blueliner at $1.10M.
recommendations.rationale: Komisarek at 82 overall/77 base carries TOUG 85, CHKG 92, POTE 92. Roberts (38, $2.70M, TOUG 73, CHKG 86, expiring) is walking; Komisarek is 16 years younger, 12 TOUG better and $1.60M cheaper. MTL at 66 points with 15 expiring deals, prestige 399 and Hainsey (21, POTE 98) already at D holds Komisarek as surplus. The value gap is real — MTL may want a higher pick we don't have. Acceptance uncertain.

recommendations.summary: Trade Alexeev and Tucker to CHI for Mark Bell if LA passes on Avery: Bell's stored TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82 fill all three gaps at $900K.
recommendations.rationale: Bell at 82 overall/80 base is CHI's 5th winger behind Daze, Fleury, Sullivan, Calder. Fleury ($4.30M, 0 years) and Sullivan ($3.00M, 1 year) are expiring at RW; Alexeev at 23, POTE 94, 30 pts/55 GP is a young replacement. CHI adds $1.50M net against $31.73M profit — trivial. Risk: CHI has no financial pressure and Bell is a genuine checking winger. Conflicts with Komisarek package on Tucker; pursue one or the other.

recommendations.summary: Sign Iginla as a UFA in July: 93 base, TOUG 85, 140 pts/73 GP at 27, on a 0-year deal from a 70-point team with $14.43M profit.
recommendations.rationale: Iginla closes the Mogilny RW void and the structural toughness ceiling in one signing. CGY cannot re-sign him at $6.50M while rebuilding. Belfour and Roberts walking frees $9.20M; Iginla fits inside that space. No trade package needed if he reaches the market.

recommendations.summary: Sign Havlat as a UFA: 88 base, 103 pts/82 GP at 23, $900K, from OTT with 11 expiring and $32.36M profit.
recommendations.rationale: The highest points-per-dollar in the league. Does not fill toughness or faceoff gaps but at 23 with POTE unlisted and a $900K base salary he is the best available scoring if Iginla goes elsewhere or we sign both.

recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri as a UFA: 79 base, POTE 98, 60 pts/61 GP at 22, $1.10M, from LA with 14 expiring and $52.43M payroll.
recommendations.rationale: LA at $52.43M payroll with 14 expiring deals cannot retain both Cammalleri and Frolov (POTE 96). A POTE 98 winger at 22 on $1.10M is the highest-upside free agent available and costs almost nothing to sign.

recommendations.summary: Assign Chlup to first-line centre for next season before camp begins.
recommendations.rationale: 0.83 pts/g at 19 on 16.9 MPG over 71 games with morale at 100. He has earned the top centre slot and is the centrepiece of the next two seasons.

recommendations.summary: Spezza needs a top-nine role next season or we should trade him while he still has value.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 at 21 but down to 6.7 MPG and 0.33 pts/g with morale at 88, the lowest of our young group. A season at fourth-line minutes is wasting his development window.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev outproduces the wingers dressed ahead of him and needs a resolution: dress him or trade him.
recommendations.rationale: 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG versus Chistov at 0.29 on 13.1 MPG and Upshall at 0.29 on 7.9 MPG. At 23 he is past the development-rotation stage.

recommendations.summary: No change for Spacek; his role is appropriate for a 19-year-old fourth-line centre.
recommendations.rationale: 7.6 MPG on 50 games, 0.34 pts/g, morale 93. He is learning at the right level. No reason to push minutes he cannot yet sustain.

recommendations.summary: Give Chistov a middle-six audition in camp next fall based on his 0.30 pts/g held flat on a 47% minutes increase.
recommendations.rationale: He went 9.5 to 14.0 MPG with rate unchanged at 0.29-0.30. That is a player growing into more responsibility without losing efficiency.

recommendations.summary: Next camp is the audition for Spezza, Upshall, Spacek and Alexeev; if they cannot hold top-nine minutes there, stop dressing them.
recommendations.rationale: All four saw minutes collapse below 6 MPG with declining rates this season. They are 19-23 with unrealized potential but are not getting chances or taking them in games.

recommendations.summary: McCabe goes on the sell list at season's end; final rate 0.48 pts/g on 21.5 MPG at age 29 confirms the decline.
recommendations.rationale: His 1.42 early-season pace on 24 games was a hot start that bled off across the remaining 58. The season rate is 0.48 and the trend is down.

recommendations.summary: Klesla is a confirmed sell at season's end; second consecutive declining season (0.50 to 0.31 pts/g) at age 23.
recommendations.rationale: Flat minutes at 14.9 MPG with rate halved means the game passed him by a year early. His value is highest now before another decline.

recommendations.summary: No change; Chlup's 0.62 to 0.88 pts/g on doubling minutes confirms he belongs on the first line.
recommendations.rationale: He improved his rate while absorbing a larger role. That is the trend you build around.

recommendations.summary: All eight units are correctly built for their intended role; no composition change is warranted.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has checking and faceoffs, L2 has scoring, L3 has speed and clutch, L4 is the bottom-six filler the roster supports, PK1 and PK2 are properly differentiated (checking mean 75 vs 80), and both PPs have a shooter and a playmaker.

recommendations.summary: The roster holds only four players with faceoff ability above 70 (Sundin, Chlup, Roberts, Richards), leaving L3 and L4 unable to win a defensive draw.
recommendations.rationale: L4 faceoff mean is 50 with a best of 51; no reshuffle fixes this because Richards at 71 is the only remaining option and moving him strips L3 of its clutch and stamina engine (both 95+).

recommendations.summary: Keep the current lines as set; every unit already outmatches its WSH counterpart.
recommendations.rationale: Our L1 (89/88/86) faces their L1 (84/75/74) with Roberts already providing CHKG 84 against Jagr's CHKG 50. Our L2 and L3 are 10+ OVR points better than their L2 and L3. No re-shuffle improves the matchup.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is 92 OVR against a WSH team with no player above 84. Ouellet at 80 is not needed tonight.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Jarome Iginla as the July priority: 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, TOUG 85, expiring from CGY who cannot retain him.
recommendations.rationale: Closes the RW scoring void left by Mogilny's decline (0.79 pts/g at 36) and the structural toughness gap (zero players above 80) simultaneously. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring contracts and $14.43M profit are forced sellers.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bell from Chicago: 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, closes toughness and faceoff gaps in one acquisition.
recommendations.rationale: The only league-wide player addressing both the zero-toughness gap and the one-faceoff-man gap at once. CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring deals and $29.46M profit are motivated sellers. ENDU 71 requires short shifts initially.

recommendations.summary: Avery from LA is the cheaper alternative to Bell: 25, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2 years left.
recommendations.rationale: Closes faceoffs and toughness at a fraction of Bell's cost. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring are sellers. If both deals land, Avery takes L3C for draws and Bell plays LW on the checking line.

recommendations.summary: No internal fix exists for the toughness gap; the best rostered TOUG is Jackman at 75.
recommendations.rationale: Zero players carry 80+ TOUG in stored grades. This was confirmed structural on March 19 after the Feb 24 contradiction was resolved. Only external acquisition closes it.

recommendations.summary: No internal fix exists for the faceoff gap; Chlup at 75 is the best after Sundin and he is needed at first centre.
recommendations.rationale: Coach quantified L4 faceoff mean at 51 with best 55 and confirmed no bench player fixes it. The only solutions are Bell (82) or Avery (93), both external.

recommendations.summary: Roberts' departure in July thins checking from six to five above 80; Eminger at 21 with POTE 99 must fill that role.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts (86 CHKG, 38) walks. Eminger carries 75 ENDU and is the next blueliner up the depth chart. His development from here determines whether checking is adequate next season.

recommendations.current: Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, Kaberle (1-year deals)
recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger and Kaberle on 5-6 year deals in July before the cluster explodes; together they are 281 points and $6.60M at current rates.
recommendations.rationale: 13 contracts worth $21.30M expire simultaneously. These five produce the most at the cheapest cost; losing any two resets the timeline by two years. No cap means money is not the constraint; negotiation bandwidth is.

recommendations.summary: Extend Chlup before a 2005-06 breakout erases his rookie-window price; at 19 with 59 points and POTE 95 he is the cheapest first-line centre available.
recommendations.rationale: Two years remain so he misses the July cluster, but his asking price at renewal in 2007 will double if he produces another 60-point season. The GM's Luongo signing worked because it came before the price moved.

recommendations.proposed: Move for a draft pick or young depth before his contract becomes unsellable
recommendations.summary: Explore a summer trade for Mogilny: 36 with 2 years at $5.50M and declining from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g; any pick or prospect recovered is better than riding him to 38 and losing him for nothing.
recommendations.rationale: The over-80 expiring mechanic applies at the end of his deal in 2007, but by then he will be 38 and no team will want him. A 2005-06 trade window still has value because 84 points is still production.

recommendations.summary: Raise ticket prices to approximately 75 for the first playoff round before the postseason begins.
recommendations.rationale: We are the 1st seed in the East at 133 points. The guide's curve is 75/80/90/100 by round. This is the one action needed before the playoffs start.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik on a 5-6 year deal at the top of the renewal list, immediately at the start of free agency.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base, 1.12 pts/g on 21.2 MPG, age 23, currently $1.10M. He is the first-line winger per the coach. A 5-6 year lock prevents a July bidding war on a player whose salary will multiply.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards on a 5 year deal, second priority behind Gaborik.
recommendations.rationale: 25, 64 pts, $1.00M, best faceoff drafter on the roster at 70. Five years staggers him against the Gaborik/Nash/Eminger cluster and keeps centre depth controlled.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash on a 5-6 year deal.
recommendations.rationale: Age 20, currently $1.20M. Lock him now before his next renewal sees a market adjustment. Five years keeps the young core staggered against the depth group.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger on a 5-6 year deal.
recommendations.rationale: 21, POTE 99, $1.20M. The GM protected him from the Chara package because his development is open. A 5-6 year lock at his current cheap salary is the highest-value contract on the roster going forward.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle on a 5 year deal.
recommendations.rationale: 27, $1.90M. Prime age for a defenceman. Five years is the right length — long enough to hold him through his best seasons without overcommitting into his 30s.

recommendations.summary: Let Belfour walk in July. Do not attempt to re-sign at a reduced salary.
recommendations.rationale: Age 40, $6.50M. The GM assessed in January that Belfour probably will not accept a reduced deal. Luongo at 91 base and Tellqvist with high-90s potential cover the positions. $6.50M freed funds a replacement scorer or blueliner.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk in July.
recommendations.rationale: Age 38, $2.70M, LW. The March 21 renewal order already identified him as a walk. At 38 his production cannot justify $2.70M on any line that is not first.

recommendations.summary: Move Chistov in the summer as part of a package for Bell (CHI) rather than renewing him to a fourth-line role he will not accept.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 95 at 22 carries real value. The coach says his 0.30 pts/g on 14.0 MPG earns fourth-line minutes. Bell at 82 base with 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE closes the coach's quantified L4 gap (mean 51 faceoff, 57 toughness). Chistov is the named trade component per the May 5 note.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Colaiacovo, Alexeev, Upshall, Abid, and Tellqvist on 3-year deals to stagger against the 5-6 year core cluster.
recommendations.rationale: Colaiacovo 22/$1.10M, Alexeev 23/$1.10M (0.48 pts/g on 6.0 MPG outproduces Chistov on half the ice), Upshall 21/$1.20M, Abid 25/$0.40M (TOUG 80, CHKG 80), Tellqvist 25/$0.80M (POTE high 90s). Three years expires them in 2008 while the core cluster runs to 2010-11, avoiding a second simultaneous renewal.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla (CGY, 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring) in July as the primary replacement for the Mogilny RW void and the toughness ceiling.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 70 points with $14.43M profit cannot retain him. His $6.50M exactly matches the Belfour savings. He closes both the scoring gap (0.79 pts/g from Mogilny last season) and the structural toughness deficit (zero Toronto players at 80+ TOUG).

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81) via the Chistov package as the only league-wide player who closes both the toughness and faceoff voids simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: The coach quantified L4 faceoff at 51 and checking at 61 with no internal fix. Bell is at 82 FACE, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG. CHI at 73 points with $29.46M profit are motivated sellers.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla from CGY as the single acquisition that closes both the RW scoring void and the structural toughness ceiling; Belfour as salary match plus one young player if the GM releases him at renewal.
recommendations.rationale: 94 overall, 128 pts/76 GP, TOUG 85, age 27, $6.50M expiring. CGY at 70 pts with 10 expiring and prestige 446 cannot build around him. Only player in the league closing two gaps simultaneously.

recommendations.summary: Target Heatley from ATL via Chistov plus Tucker plus the 4th rounder; ATL cannot retain both him and Kovalchuk at $1.10M each.
recommendations.rationale: 88 overall, 131 pts/79 GP, age 24, $1.10M expiring, POTE 84. ATL at 84 pts with 11 expiring deals must choose one star. Chistov (22, POTE 95) gives them the future piece they need.

recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri as a July UFA for $3.50-4.00M over five years; no trade package required, only a contract offer.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 98, 60 pts/61 GP, age 22, $1.10M expiring from LA at 79 pts with 14 expiring deals. LA cannot retain him. We have $42.23M in profit to fund the deal.

recommendations.summary: Offer Stahle (21, POTE 96) plus the 4th to CHI for Bell, who closes toughness (95), checking (93), and faceoffs (87) in one 24-year-old at $900K.
recommendations.rationale: Bell is 82 overall, 28 pts/80 GP, POTE 82, 2 years remaining. CHI at 78 pts with 10 expiring deals (Daze, Sullivan, Zhamnov all expiring) are rebuilding their forward group. Acceptance uncertain because CHI is profitable at $31.73M and does not need to sell.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Stuart from SJ for the July window; 87 overall, POTE 92, age 25, $1.80M expiring, replaces Roberts with eight years of runway.
recommendations.rationale: SJ at 76 pts has 13 expiring deals on $45.39M payroll and cannot keep all of them. Stuart's CHKG 83 and TOUG 74 exceed any current Toronto blueliner. Offer a young player plus an over-80 expiring mechanic pick.

recommendations.summary: Monitor Drury as a BUF expiring (86 overall, FACE 85, 99 pts, $2.00M, age 24, POTE 81); first-round price without picks makes this a stretch but he is the best faceoff-scoring forward on the market.
recommendations.rationale: BUF at 84 pts with 10 expiring deals are retooling. Drury's FACE 85 and 99 points at age 24 make him worth a significant package, but we hold only one 4th-rounder. Pursue only if a multi-club package or an over-80 expiring piece unlocks.

recommendations.summary: Add Conroy (FACE 95, 102 pts/82 GP, $2.00M expiring) to a CGY package for Iginla or separately; he is 31 and a rental but at 1.24 ppg he covers the faceoff gap immediately.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 70 pts with 10 expiring deals are motivated sellers. Conroy's FACE 95 is the second-highest on the sheet. If we already negotiate with CGY, fold him into the same call.

recommendations.summary: If ATL retains Heatley rather than trading him, Kovalchuk (90 overall, 138 pts/79 GP, age 21, $1.10M expiring) becomes available on the same mechanism; same package applies.
recommendations.rationale: ATL cannot keep both stars at $1.10M. Kovalchuk is LW not RW but at 1.75 ppg he plays any side. Lower probability because ATL likely keeps the younger one (Kovalchuk 21 vs Heatley 24).

recommendations.summary: Monitor Roenick from PHI as a financial-distress sale candidate; PHI has $66.73M payroll against $2.14M profit, but 3 years at $7.50M makes him hard to move.
recommendations.rationale: 89 overall, CHKG 90, FACE 82, 99 pts/82 GP, age 29. Fills checking, faceoffs, and scoring in one man. PHI's $2.14M profit makes them the most financially pressured club in the league, but 3 years remaining and $7.50M salary make this a long shot.

recommendations.summary: Goalie market is closed per GM's March 19 order. Theodore (MTL, 91, $5.50M expiring) and Nabokov (SJ, 90, $3.60M expiring) are available but not pursued.
recommendations.rationale: GM explicitly closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19. Luongo and Belfour are the playoff tandem. Do not reopen unless GM changes the order.

recommendations.summary: Trade Chistov + Tucker + 4th to ATL for Heatley; closes the RW scoring void with a 131-point, 24-year-old on an expiring deal.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring cannot keep both Heatley and Kovalchuk. They trade Heatley or lose him free. Chistov (POTE 95, age 22, same position) plus Tucker (CHKG 92, physical) plus a pick is three assets for one player they'd otherwise lose for nothing. We shed $2.40M, add $1.10M, then re-sign Heatley at roughly $4.50M x 5 against $42.23M profit.

recommendations.summary: Trade Koltsov + 4th to CHI for Bell; closes toughness and faceoff gaps simultaneously with a 24-year-old on a $900K deal.
recommendations.rationale: Bell at TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82 is the only league-wide player filling both structural voids. CHI at 78 points rebuilding may value Koltsov's POTE 94 and ACCE 96 over Bell's POTE 81 depth role. But CHI has $31.73M profit and no salary pressure, so they can simply keep Bell. Acceptance uncertain.

recommendations.summary: Trade Stahle + 4th to CGY for Conroy as a one-year faceoff rental; use only if the Bell deal fails.
recommendations.rationale: Conroy at FACE 95, 102 points, age 31, $2.00M expiring. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit want salary relief and get Stahle (POTE 96, age 21, 3 years of control) saving them $1.03M net. Coach flagged Stahle as needing games or a move. Conroy is a rental that buys one season for Chlup and Spacek to develop.

recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri as a free agent in July on a 5-year deal at $3.50-4.00M; no pick or player required.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 79 points with 14 expiring on $52.43M payroll cannot retain him. He is 22 with POTE 98 and 60 points in 61 games. Execute regardless of trade outcomes.

recommendations.summary: Task #2 (DiPietro/Luongo monitoring) is closed: Luongo was acquired at 93/26/$1.60M/2yr, and the GM terminated all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19.
recommendations.rationale: The original objective — acquire a high-90s goalie from a non-contender — was fulfilled. The GM explicitly closed this function on March 19. No further action required.

recommendations.summary: Play Alexeev over Chistov for the final 5 games to test him at 12+ MPG before offseason decisions.
recommendations.rationale: Alexeev produces 0.55 pts/g vs Chistov's 0.29 and Upshall's 0.29. He needs a sustained sample at higher ice time to make the offseason case either way.

recommendations.summary: Assign Chlup to first-line centre for next season before camp.
recommendations.rationale: 0.83 pts/g in 71 games at age 19 with morale 99. He has earned the first line and the decision should be made now, not carried into camp undecided.

recommendations.summary: Stahle at 4 GP all season at 21 with POTE 96 needs games or needs to be moved; raise with GM for offseason planning.
recommendations.rationale: Four games in a full season means he is fifth defenceman on a team that plays four. At 21 with the third-highest POTE on the blue line that is wasted time unless a trade puts him in a top-pair role.

recommendations.summary: Assign Chlup as first-line centre for 2005-06 based on 0.88 pts/g on 18.2 MPG at age 19.
recommendations.rationale: He is the only young player improving on both rate and load. The trend has held since December.

recommendations.summary: Gaborik at 1.12 pts/g over 58 games on 21.2 MPG at 23 is a permanent first-line winger.
recommendations.rationale: His late-season rate is elite. He and Chlup are the young core; they should play together next year.

recommendations.summary: Chistov's 14.0 MPG produced 0.30 pts/g; reduce to fourth-line minutes or scratch next season.
recommendations.rationale: He was given the ice to develop and gave back nothing. His rate is flat while his minutes nearly doubled.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev at 0.48 pts/g on 6.0 MPG outproduces Chistov by 0.18 on half the ice; promote his role next season.
recommendations.rationale: The rate-to-role mismatch flagged in April persists. He is 23 and producing at a second-line rate on fourth-line minutes.

recommendations.summary: Spezza's season is over at 0.24 pts/g on 4.6 MPG; evaluate at camp next autumn with real minutes.
recommendations.rationale: His minutes fell from 9.1 to 4.6 with his rate dropping simultaneously. POTE 99 but no path to development in the current role.

recommendations.summary: Sell McCabe this offseason at $3.00M x 4; his late-season rate of 0.48 confirms the early 1.42 was a hot start.
recommendations.rationale: Season rate 0.76 over 82 games, late window 0.48. At 29 the asset value exceeds the hockey value.

recommendations.summary: No change. Kaberle is trending up at 0.54→0.62 on 19.4→21.5 MPG; he is the only veteran improving.
recommendations.rationale: He is 27 and still climbing. Leave him as the top-pair anchor and build the defensive core around him.

recommendations.summary: No morale-driven ice-time changes. The room averages 92 and is trending up on recent wins; every dressed player sits at or near his expected minutes band.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza at 88 is the only name below 92 and he is climbing (+3), not falling. With 5 games left and no vacancy for him in the lineup, there is nothing to fix this week.

recommendations.summary: Play Gaborik on the first line against Washington unless he is injured — he is 97 scoring, 99 speed, 98 clutch and this is a maximize-quality night.
recommendations.rationale: The standing order says go all out against quality opponents. Gaborik is the highest-rated skater on the roster. If scratched for development, override it tonight. If scratched for injury, no change.

recommendations.summary: L4 faceoff mean of 51 is bad but moving Richards there breaks L3's checking unit; accept the weakness one more game.
recommendations.rationale: L4 checking mean 72 is adequate. The faceoff deficit is a roster gap, not an arrangement problem — no centre above 73 is available to shift down without cost.

recommendations.summary: We have no centre outside Sundin (89) and Chlup (78) who wins draws and checks above 75. L4 faceoff mean 51 cannot be fixed by arrangement.
recommendations.rationale: Top faceoffs: Sundin 89, Chlup 78, Roberts 74, Richards 73. Top checking: Jackman 88, Roberts 83, McCabe 83, Fischer 83 — all defensemen or already committed. The intersection of 'wins draws' and 'checks' is empty outside L1-L2.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; his fatigue icon is clear.
recommendations.rationale: No goalie-tired flag showing. OVR 93 with GSH_ 97 and GSL_ 97. Kolzig at 87 is solid but our PP at 32.3% is the weapon tonight.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes for Washington.
recommendations.rationale: Auto-pairing already puts Fischer/Jackman (both CHKG 90, SPEE 92) on with our first line, which is the line the GM matches against Jagr. Kaberle is in per standing order. The D pair slot order is correct.

recommendations.summary: McCabe on the sell list: 0.48 pts/g over the last 58 games at 29 with 3 years and $3.00M remaining.
recommendations.rationale: Season rate 0.76 (62 pts/82 GP) is inflated by a hot start. Recent window confirms the decline. Offseason is the window.

recommendations.summary: Sell Jackman: 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG at $0.70M. His minutes are his trade value.
recommendations.rationale: Final season confirms 0.46 across 80 GP. At that price a contender pays for 30 MPG of top-pair minutes regardless of scoring.

recommendations.summary: Sell Klesla: 0.37 pts/g at 23 is a second declining season with no upward movement.
recommendations.rationale: 30 points in 82 games on flat 14.8 MPG. Two consecutive years below 0.40 means the development is not coming.

recommendations.summary: Move Eminger before July or lose him for nothing: 0.36 pts/g on an expiring deal.
recommendations.rationale: 23 points in 64 GP at $1.20M expiring. After free agency begins he is a UFA and the return is zero.

recommendations.slot: checking wing or center, any tier
recommendations.summary: Acquire Avery or Bell in July to close the zero-TOUG-80 and one-FACE-80 gaps simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Zero Toronto players carry 80+ stored TOUG; highest is Jackman at 75. Only Sundin is 80+ at FACE (90) and he is 34. Avery closes TOUG (83), CHKG (88), FACE (93) at $400K with 2 years left. Bell closes TOUG (88), CHKG (86), FACE (82) at 24 with POTE 81. No internal roster combination fixes either gap.

recommendations.summary: Target Iginla or Heatley in July to replace Mogilny's scoring production before the decline completes.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g by March 2005 at age 36. Iginla is 27 with 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, TOUG 85 and $6.50M expiring from a 70-point CGY side with 10 expiring deals. Heatley is 91 base. Either closes the scoring void; Iginla also raises the toughness ceiling to 85.

recommendations.summary: Press the Coach to give Koltsov a top-nine audition next camp; at 92 SPEE and 92 overall, he is the cheapest depth upgrade available.
recommendations.rationale: Koltsov reads 92 overall at age 24 with SPEE 92 and is in no line unit. Chistov at 0.29 pts/g on 13.1 MPG is the man the Coach already flagged for displacement. Koltsov's speed grade makes him the natural next candidate.

recommendations.summary: Do not slide any existing player onto L4 for faceoffs; the best internal option (Richards, 70 FACE) is still below the 80 threshold and wastes his 85 PAS playmaking.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach confirmed L4 faceoff mean is 52 with best 55. Richards at 70 would raise it to roughly 63, still non-competitive. The prior recommendation to slide him was taken on 2005-03-16 but he scored 0 and played 0. The only fix is external acquisition.

recommendations.summary: Renew Gaborik on 5-6 years in July; 99 points at 23 on an expiring $1.10M deal is the single most valuable contract situation on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: Without him the 133-point core dissolves simultaneously. At even $5M/year he is affordable against $114.69M revenue.

recommendations.summary: Renew Richards on 5-6 years; 66 points at 25 on $1.00M expiring, and no replacement second-centre exists on the market at that level.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto holds no pick better than a 4th-rounder, so losing Richards forces a player-for-player trade from a position of weakness.

recommendations.summary: Renew Nash (20, POTE 95, $1.20M) and Eminger (21, POTE 99, $1.20M) on 5-6 years in July.
recommendations.rationale: Both are foundational young players on expiring rookie-window deals. Their current salaries are below 15% of what their production and potential command.

recommendations.summary: Renew Kaberle on 4-5 years; 27, ascending from 0.54 to 0.62 pts/g on 21.5 MPG, expiring at $1.90M.
recommendations.rationale: The only established defender still improving. At 4-5 years he ages off the contract at 31-32, keeping money flexible for Eminger's next extension.

recommendations.summary: Extend Chlup to 5-6 years before his sophomore season; 19, 59 points, POTE 95 on $2.34M with two years left.
recommendations.rationale: His price doubles after a 70-point sophomore year. Locking him now at $3-4M is the cheapest star contract on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Use Belfour (92 base, expiring) and Roberts (expiring) for pick recovery via the over-80 mechanic in July rather than losing them for nothing.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto holds one 4th-rounder. Generating even two first-rounders restores draft capital for the next rebuild cycle.

recommendations.summary: Move Chistov (22, POTE 95) in July for a depth player or pick; Coach confirms Alexeev displaces him for top-nine minutes.
recommendations.rationale: Chistov produced 0.29 pts/g on 13.1 MPG. His POTE keeps his trade value alive even after a weak season.

recommendations.summary: No deadline moves needed; the club is at 133 points and the entire trajectory question is resolved in July through renewals.
recommendations.rationale: The playoff roster is set (GM confirmed Belfour and Luongo as the two goalies). Only Tucker and the 4th-rounder remain as trade chips.

recommendations.summary: Renew Gaborik on 5-6 years immediately in July before he hits free agency at $1.10M.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base, POTE 90, age 23, $1.10M expiring. The March 21 plan lists him as the top renewal priority; losing him to a bidding war opens a hole no other roster move fills.

recommendations.summary: Renew Richards on 5-6 years in July.
recommendations.rationale: Age 25, 64 points, $1.00M expiring. Second priority per the March 21 order. A centre at that production and price does not reappear.

recommendations.summary: Renew Nash on 5-6 years.
recommendations.rationale: Age 20, $1.20M expiring. Lock the cheapest impact forward the club will ever hold before his numbers rise his asking price.

recommendations.summary: Renew Eminger on 5-6 years.
recommendations.rationale: Age 21, POTE 99, $1.20M expiring. Highest potential grade on the roster. The GM vetoed selling him in January; the same logic applies to letting him leave.

recommendations.summary: Renew Kaberle on 4-5 years with a raise from $1.90M.
recommendations.rationale: Age 27, 0.62 pts/g on 21.5 MPG and ascending per the coach's May 5 report. Entering his prime; the cost rises every season you wait.

recommendations.summary: Renew Colaiacovo on 3-5 years at or near $1.10M.
recommendations.rationale: Age 22, carried 17.9 MPG across 31 games. The coach wants a full-season audition; keep him cheap while he earns a longer deal.

recommendations.summary: Renew Alexeev on 3-5 years at $1.10M.
recommendations.rationale: Age 23, 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG, outproducing Chistov and Upshall per the coach. Lock him at the current rate before his usage rises his price.

recommendations.summary: Renew Upshall on 2-3 years at $1.20M.
recommendations.rationale: Age 21, 0.29 pts/g on 7.9 MPG, below his ice share but cheap and young. Depth on a short deal keeps the roster shape without a long commitment.

recommendations.summary: Renew Abid on 2-3 years at $0.40M.
recommendations.rationale: Age 25, $0.40M is the cheapest contract on the roster. He carries TOUG 80 and CHKG 80, the only 80-grade physical presence available internally.

recommendations.summary: Renew Tellqvist on 3-5 years at $0.80M.
recommendations.rationale: Age 25, POTE in the high 90s per the January standing order. Give him time to develop at a cost lower than any other goalie on the market.

recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour reduced terms at renewal; if he declines, let him walk.
recommendations.rationale: Age 40, $6.50M, expiring. The GM's February note flagged retirement risk. Luongo at 91 base plus Tellqvist cover the position without paying a 40-year-old starter-level money.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk in July.
recommendations.rationale: Age 38, $2.70M. The March 30 note names Stuart (SJ, 25, 87 base, POTE 91) as the replacement target. Do not pay $2.70M for a 38-year-old.

recommendations.summary: Package Chistov for Bell (CHI) in July to close both the toughness and faceoff gaps.
recommendations.rationale: Chistov at 22 with POTE 95 is expendable per the coach's May 5 report (Alexeev displaces him). Bell at 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 82 FACE is the only league-wide player closing both L4 gaps the coach quantified (mean 52 FACE, mean 57 TOUG). CHI at 73 points and $29.46M profit are motivated sellers.

recommendations.summary: Auto-draft on June 8 with the only pick available, a 4th-rounder.
recommendations.rationale: Scouting is not upgraded, so auto-draft is adequate. The 4th-rounder pick is confirmed still owned (round 4, not traded). Draft for depth.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla from CGY in July: 93 base, TOUG 87, 128 pts/76 GP, age 27, $6.50M expiring. Closes scoring and toughness in one move.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him. He is the only player who closes both structural gaps simultaneously. Salary is 11% of revenue.

recommendations.summary: Monitor Thornton from BOS: 94 base, TOUG 89, age 25, $4.00M expiring, 83 pts/59 GP. Closes toughness and scoring at centre.
recommendations.rationale: BOS at 97 points but 13 expiring deals; if they retool he is the piece they cannot retain. Half Iginla's salary at the same grade level.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Brad Stuart from SJ: 87 base, TOUG 80, CHKG 89, POTE 91, age 25, $1.80M expiring, 52 pts/77 GP. Only defence-side toughness answer.
recommendations.rationale: SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring on $45.39M payroll cannot retain all of them. At 25 with POTE 91 and 52 points he is the best available D with both grades and production.

recommendations.summary: Heatley as the scoring fallback if Iginla or Thornton is unattainable: 91 base, 131 pts/79 GP, age 24, $1.10M expiring from ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Best points-per-dollar on the list at $1.10M. TOUG 75 does not close the toughness gap but 131 points at 24 replaces Mogilny entirely.

recommendations.summary: Bell from CHI closes toughness and faceoffs in one $900K package: TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82, age 24, two years left. Cheapest gap-filler on the list.
recommendations.rationale: CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit are motivated sellers. Two years on the deal means we own him through 2007 without renewal risk.

recommendations.summary: Bouwmeester at 21, POTE 95, CHKG 87, 81 base, $1.20M expiring from FLA at 76 points with 19 expiring. Highest-upside defenceman available.
recommendations.rationale: Already at 2629 minutes (33 MPG) at 21. FLA has 19 expiring contracts and cannot keep all of them. A 21-year-old with POTE 95 and 33 MPG is a franchise blueliner if developed.

recommendations.summary: Havlat at 87 base, 103 pts/82 GP, age 24, $900K expiring from OTT at 77 points with 11 expiring. Best production-per-dollar scorer available.
recommendations.rationale: 103 points at $900K is the cheapest volume scoring in the league. TOUG 68 means he does not close toughness but fills the second-line scoring void behind a new top-line addition.

recommendations.summary: Komisarek at 77 base, POTE 91, TOUG 76, age 23, $1.10M expiring, 82 pts/82 GP from MTL at 66 points with 15 expiring. Production D with a climbing ceiling.
recommendations.rationale: 82 points from a 23-year-old defenceman with 2496 minutes proves he already carries a top-pair role. MTL at 66 points with 15 expiring are in full rebuild and must deal him.

recommendations.summary: Avery at $400K with two years left closes faceoffs (93 FACE) and toughness (83 TOUG) at the lowest salary on the list. A depth piece, not a top-six answer.
recommendations.rationale: Production is 9 pts/82 GP which limits him to bottom-six usage, but FACE 93 and TOUG 83 are the exact grades the Coach flagged as missing. $400K salary means no opportunity cost.

recommendations.summary: Marleau as a July UFA target if SJ cannot re-sign him: 89 base, 98 pts/71 GP, age 25, $1.60M expiring. Our $114.69M revenue makes him a realistic UFA signing.
recommendations.rationale: SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring cannot retain both him and Brad Stuart. If he reaches UFA, we can outbid anyone. But pursue via trade first to avoid overpaying.

recommendations.summary: Drury at 89 base, FACE 84, 99 pts/82 GP, age 28, $2.00M expiring from BUF at 84 points with 10 expiring. Best scoring-plus-faceoffs package on the list.
recommendations.rationale: 99 points and 84 FACE in one player at $2.00M. TOUG 79 falls one point short of the toughness threshold but is the closest on a scorer. One year older than Heatley, Gagne or Havlat.

recommendations.summary: Briere at 83 base, FACE 83, 95 pts/82 GP, age 27, $1.50M expiring from BUF. Cheaper UFA alternative to Drury with similar production.
recommendations.rationale: Same club as Drury, same seller window. TOUG 65 does not close the toughness gap but 95 points and 83 FACE at $1.50M is strong value for a centre.

recommendations.summary: Package Belfour ($6.50M expiring), Roberts ($2.70M expiring), Chistov (22, POTE 95, expiring) and the 4th-rounder to Calgary for Iginla (93, TOUG 87, 128 pts/76 GP, age 27, $6.50M expiring).
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring deals and $14.43M profit cannot re-sign Iginla and will lose him for nothing otherwise. Belfour at 92 base gives them a bridge goalie, Roberts 81 points of veteran offence, and Chistov a POTE 95 prospect. All three are walk-aways or Coach-displaced, so the cost to our core is zero.

recommendations.summary: Send Upshall (21, POTE 99, $1.20M expiring) plus the 4th-rounder to Chicago for Bell (82 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82, 24, $900K, two years left).
recommendations.rationale: CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit are motivated sellers. Bell is the only league-wide player closing both the toughness ceiling (88 vs our stored max of 75) and the L4 faceoff gap (82 vs our mean of 52) in one body, at $900K with two years already locked. Upshall is Coach-displaced at 0.29 pts/g on 7.9 MPG.

recommendations.summary: Trade Koltsov (24, POTE 94, ACCE 96, $1.10M, two years) to LA for Avery (79 base, FACE 93, TOUG 83, CHKG 88, 25, $400K, two years left).
recommendations.rationale: LA at 79 points with 14 expiring deals cannot retain everyone. Avery's 9 points in 82 games is the lowest production of any forward in the brief, making his roster spot more valuable than his contribution. Koltsov at POTE 94 and ACCE 96 is a direct youth upgrade at LA. No pick required; compatible with either of the other two proposals.

recommendations.summary: Task #2 is delivered and closed. Luongo is on the roster at 93/26/$1.60M/2yr; GM closed all goalie monitoring on March 19.
recommendations.rationale: The January task was to find a high-90s goalie from a non-contender. Luongo arrived during the season, Belfour was kept for the playoff, and the GM's March 19 standing order explicitly ended the monitoring. Nothing to report forward.

recommendations.summary: Move Chlup to first-line centre for next season. He scored 59 points on 16.9 MPG at 19, the best production-to-minutes ratio on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: Prior finding chlup-franchise-centre established this in April. Two recommendations on April 28 and May 2 were not taken. His rate (0.83) dwarfs the current first-line centre.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev earns third-line minutes over Upshall next season. 0.55 pts/g in 55 games versus Upshall's 0.29 in 68.
recommendations.rationale: Alexeev outproduces Upshall and Chistov by nearly double. The mismatch has been flagged since April 23 and remains unresolved. Upshall's rate does not support a roster spot over a higher producer.

recommendations.summary: Colaiacovo and Spezza need a clear camp audition next September: earn a top-nine forward or top-three D role, or be told plainly they are not ready.
recommendations.rationale: Colaiacovo: 31 GP at 22 with 99 potential and 17.9 MPG when playing. Spezza: 99 potential but 6.7 MPG and 0.33 pts/g. Neither has been given a real shot or a real answer this year.

recommendations.summary: Spacek, Nash, Chistov and Klesla are all getting appropriate games for their level. No change in their development track needed from what I see.
recommendations.rationale: Spacek: 50 GP at 19, 7.6 MPG, appropriate depth minutes. Nash: 69 GP at 20, 13.1 MPG, 0.57 rate, earning second-line games. Chistov: 68 GP, 13.1 MPG, third-line winger at 22, reasonable. Klesla: 82 GP at 23, on the sell list for trajectory, not development.

recommendations.summary: McCabe goes back on the sell list for the offseason: 0.48 pts/g on 21.5 MPG across 82 games at age 29.
recommendations.rationale: His early-season 1.42 pace has bled off entirely. The final season rate is well below the 0.60 threshold. At 29 with $3.00M and 4 years remaining, the trade return on a declining 0.48-rate defenseman exceeds keeping him.

recommendations.summary: Assign Chlup to the first-line centre slot for next season. 0.88 pts/g on 18.2 MPG at 19 is confirmed.
recommendations.rationale: His rate rose while his minutes doubled, the clearest evidence a player can give that he earned the bigger role. Fifth recommendation this season; the data has not contradicted it once.

recommendations.summary: Spacek needs a real training-camp audition next season or we stop dressing him. 0.28 pts/g on 5.2 MPG at age 19 is no longer a role.
recommendations.rationale: His minutes collapsed from 16.0 to 5.2 and his rate from 0.55 to 0.28. No stored grade movement. The season gave us nothing to build on; next camp is the only lever.

recommendations.summary: Spezza needs a real training-camp audition next season or we stop dressing him. 0.24 pts/g on 4.6 MPG at 21 with POTE 99.
recommendations.rationale: Same pattern as Spacek: minutes halved, rate halved, no stored grade movement. We carry a 99-potential center at 4.6 minutes a night and get 0.24 per game. Next camp decides whether that continues.

recommendations.summary: Upshall gets the same camp-or-cut decision. 0.27 pts/g on 4.8 MPG at 21.
recommendations.rationale: Minutes dropped from 13.4 to 4.8 with a slight rate decline. No stored grade movement. Same offseason audition as Spacek and Spezza.

recommendations.summary: Abid's situation has worsened: 11.5 MPG and 0.70 pts/g down from 20.1 and 1.09. He needs 18+ MPG next season or becomes a trade candidate.
recommendations.rationale: My March 16 note set the 18 MPG floor. He received less, and the rate decline accelerated. This is the pattern that produces a morale spiral and a worthless asset.

recommendations.summary: Expand the offseason system-fit review to Nash alongside Afinogenov and Richards. All three had rates halved on flat minutes at ages 20, 25 and 25.
recommendations.rationale: Three forwards aged 20 to 25 with stable ice and collapsed scoring rates point at a systemic issue rather than individual decline. Nash at 0.83 to 0.42 on flat 13 MPG fits the pattern exactly.

recommendations.summary: No change for Kaberle. His trend line (0.54 to 0.62 pts/g on rising minutes) confirms the GM's read that he is our star defenseman.
recommendations.rationale: The only defenseman on the roster whose production and load are both climbing. He is the blue-line anchor for next season and beyond.

recommendations.summary: No ice-time changes needed tonight. The room averages 92 with a floor of 88.
recommendations.rationale: Every player at 91 or above except Spezza at 88 (flat, season write-off, camp is the lever). Abid, Richards and Afinogenov are minutes-under their band but their morale is 100 and 98 respectively and trending up. No active morale risk requires a line move before WSH.

recommendations.summary: All eight units are logically constructed; no composition change is warranted.
recommendations.rationale: L1-L3 each have their required role covered (skill up top, two-way in the middle, Tucker as the third-line enforcer). P1 and P2 are well-split between shooting and speed. K1/K2 split correctly between skating and hitting.

recommendations.summary: L4 faceoff mean is 51 with a best of 53; no player on the roster outside L1-L3 can win draws on the fourth line.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin 89, Chlup 78, Roberts 74, Richards 73 are the only faceoff men worth naming, and all are already on L1-L3. A fourth-line centre at 55% would fix the defensive-zone draw problem without touching chemistry.

recommendations.summary: Roster toughness ceiling is 76 (Jackman); we cannot build any unit that deters through physicality.
recommendations.rationale: The four forwards and D who play 20+ minutes carry toughness of 71-76 at best. No one on the roster exceeds 76. This is a design consequence of a skill-first roster and only an offseason acquisition changes it.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming.
recommendations.rationale: OVR 93, morale 100, ENDU 77 — no signs of fatigue. WSH's Kolzig is 87 and we need the edge we have in net.

recommendations.summary: No lineup change for WSH; the current slot order already puts our best units against Jagr's line and Gonchar's pair.
recommendations.rationale: Auto-pairing gives us L1 (Roberts/Sundin/Mogilny, OVR 87/90/89) against their L1 (Lang/Jagr/Dupuis, OVR 75/84/74) and pair 1 (Fischer/Jackman, OVR 84/85) against their pair 1 (Gonchar/Witt, OVR 78/73). Every matchup is ours by at least 5 points of overall.

recommendations.summary: McCabe stays on the sell list: full season is 0.76 pts/g but his recent 58-game window is 0.48, meaning the number is inflated by a hot start that is gone. At 29 with 4 years at $3.00M, shop him this offseason.
recommendations.rationale: 62 points in 82 games looks fine on the surface but the trend is unmistakably down. A 0.50-rate defenceman on a 4-year $12M commitment is a liability, not an asset.

recommendations.summary: Jackman stays on the sell list: 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG across 80 games at $0.70M. His value is the cheapest top-pair minutes in the league, but the production does not justify keeping him.
recommendations.rationale: 0.46 is third-pair offence. Someone else will pay for 30 MPG at $700k. Sell and reinvest.

recommendations.summary: Klesla stays on the sell list: 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG, second straight year declining. His trade value is his age (23) and cheapness ($0.90M x 2), not his play.
recommendations.rationale: Season locked at 82 games. Two consecutive declining years at low volume. Move him while he still has youth on his card.

recommendations.summary: Eminger must be moved before July: 0.36 pts/g on 15.5 MPG, down from 0.38 in March, $1.20M expiring. After free agency he is a zero-asset loss.
recommendations.rationale: The slide continued for a full month. Deadline is past but any offseason offer beats losing him for nothing.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell to close the zero-to-80 TOUG gap and the L4 faceoff gap simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Zero players at 80+ TOUG; Bell at 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE at 24 with POTE 81 is the only tracked target closing both gaps. CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring deals and $29.46M profit are motivated sellers.

recommendations.summary: Sign a top-six RW in July to replace Mogilny's production after he departs at 36.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny fell to 0.79 pts/g and is 36; once he leaves the top scoring group has only Gaborik 92 as an elite winger. Heatley at 91 base or Doan fills the void with years remaining.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Stuart to pair with Jackman on the top defence pair with physicality and eight years of development.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts walks, leaving Jackman 87 CHKG and McCabe 86 CHKG as the top pair with zero TOUG 80+. Stuart at 25 with 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91 adds toughness and youth. SJ at 72 points may not deal him.

recommendations.summary: If Bell is unavailable, Avery at $400K with 93 FACE and 83 TOUG closes both gaps at minimal cost.
recommendations.rationale: Avery's 93 FACE is the single best draw-taker available anywhere; at $400K with 2 years left he costs almost nothing. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring deals want youth, so the package likely needs Koltsov.

recommendations.summary: Promote Alexeev to top-nine minutes next season, displacing Chistov or Upshall.
recommendations.rationale: Alexeev produces 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG while Chistov gives 0.29 on 13.1 and Upshall 0.29 on 7.9. The coach flagged this today; pure usage correction.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza a real camp competition with top-six looks next season; his 0.33 pts/g on 6.7 MPG across 46 GP was a write-off.
recommendations.rationale: The coach flagged Spezza six times by late March asking for a stay-or-go decision. At 21 with POTE 99 he still has upside but needs real minutes to prove it before his trade value erodes.

recommendations.summary: Checking depth is adequate: six at 80+ (Jackman 87, McCabe 86, Tucker 83, Fischer 82, Upshall 80) after Roberts leaves.
recommendations.rationale: Five 80+ checkers remain even without Roberts. The issue is toughness and faceoffs, not shot-blocking or stick-checking volume.

recommendations.summary: Lock all five on 5-6 year deals this July before any team can approach them as UFAs.
recommendations.rationale: 13 contracts worth $21.30M expire in July 2005. These five are the team's identity: Gaborik 99 pts at 91 base, Richards 66 pts, Nash POTE 95, Eminger POTE 99, Kaberle ascending at 0.62 pts/g. If they walk, the roster collapses in one summer.

recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour (92 base, $6.50M, expiring) for a draft pick via the over-80 mechanic before July.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is the starter with 2 years left. Belfour at 40 will retire or walk. At 92 base he qualifies for the over-80 expiring pick mechanic. This recovers draft capital Toronto does not otherwise have.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Iginla in July to replace Mogilny at similar salary while his production is still at 93 base.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny's production fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g at 36; Iginla at 27 carries 93 base, 140 pts, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring cannot retain him. Mogilny and Roberts walk $8.20M combined; Iginla replaces the production without raising payroll.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Iginla (CGY, 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, 85 TOUG, $6.50M expiring) as the July priority to replace Mogilny's scoring and close the toughness gap simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: He is the only player in the league closing both the RW scoring void (93 base, 140 pts) and the structural toughness ceiling (85 TOUG) in one move. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him. The $6.50M replaces Mogilny's $5.50M and Roberts' $2.70M rolling off.

recommendations.summary: Sign or trade for Cammalleri (LA, 22, 79 base, POTE 97, 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M expiring) as the highest-value forward available this summer.
recommendations.rationale: 60 points in 61 games at age 22 with POTE 97 on $1.10M is the cheapest high-upside winger in the league. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring cannot retain him. At 79 base the over-80 mechanic may not apply, so July UFA signing is the likely path.

recommendations.summary: Trade for Bell (CHI, 24, 80 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, $900K, 2 years) to close toughness and faceoff gaps on a re-signable deal.
recommendations.rationale: He is the only player with 80+ TOUG and 80+ FACE simultaneously on a deal with 2 years left at $900K. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit are the most motivated seller. The L4 faceoff mean of 52 and zero 80+ TOUG players on the roster make this an external-only fix.

recommendations.summary: Trade for Avery (LA, 25, 79 base, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2 years) as the budget alternative to Bell for toughness and faceoffs.
recommendations.rationale: 93 FACE and 83 TOUG at $400K closes both structural gaps at half Bell's cost. His 0.11 pts/g production means he slots on the fourth line, which is exactly where the 52-mean faceoff gap sits. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring will deal him for minimal return.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Stuart (SJ, 25, 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91) as the physical top-pair partner after Roberts walks.
recommendations.rationale: Zero current Toronto defencemen carry 80+ TOUG. Stuart is the only tracked blueliner closing that gap while being 25 with POTE 91. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring face retention pressure, but 76 points means they are not desperate enough for a cheap deal.

recommendations.summary: Sign Reid (STL, 23, 77 base, 80 FACE, POTE 94, $600K expiring) as a July UFA if Bell and Avery are unavailable.
recommendations.rationale: 80 FACE at age 23 with POTE 94 on $600K is the floor price for the faceoff gap. STL at 86 points are not sellers, so the over-80 pick mechanic does not apply and this is a UFA path only. Below Bell and Avery on the priority list because his base is lower.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Heatley (ATL, 24, 91 base) as the elite winger if ATL releases him in favour of Kovalchuk; requires trading Mogilny as the over-80 expiring return.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring cannot retain both Heatley (91 base) and Kovalchuk (89 base, 104 pts). If ATL moves Heatley, the over-80 mechanic means they accept an over-80 expiring player like Mogilny (94 base, $5.50M) for the trade. This is the Iginla alternative if CGY hold firm.

recommendations.summary: Trade Mogilny (94 base, $5.50M expiring) using the over-80 mechanic to recover a draft pick before he walks in July.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny's production fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g and he is not in the renewal plan. At 94 base and expiring, the over-80 mechanic converts him into a pick — Toronto's only current pick is a 4th-rounder. That recovered pick funds the Bell or Avery trade package.

recommendations.current: Mogilny (RW, 36, 94 base, $5.50M, 2 yrs) + Koltsov (LW, 24, POTE 94, ACCE 96, $1.10M, 2 yrs) + 4th-rounder
recommendations.summary: Send Mogilny, Koltsov and the 4th to Calgary for Jarome Iginla.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 70 pts with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot re-sign Iginla at $6.50M while restructuring; Mogilny's 94 base and 84 points give them one more year of production, Koltsov is a 24-year-old POTE 94 project with two years of control, and the net salary change for CGY is +$0.20M on a $14.43M profit. For Toronto, this replaces Mogilny's declining 0.79 pts/g second-half with Iginla's 140 points and closes the RW scoring void and toughness gap simultaneously at net-zero payroll in year one.

recommendations.current: Chistov (LW, 22, POTE 95, SPEE 89, ACCE 88, $1.10M, 1 yr) + Tucker (LW, 30, 88 TOUG, 92 CHKG, $1.30M, 2 yrs)
recommendations.proposed: Bell (LW, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, $900K, 2 yrs)
recommendations.summary: Send Chistov and Tucker to Chicago for Bell.
recommendations.rationale: CHI at 78 pts with 10 expiring deals and $31.73M profit are stockpiling youth; Chistov's POTE 95 on a cheap one-year audition plus Tucker's 88 TOUG/92 CHKG for two years at $1.30M is a reasonable asking price for a player they'd never re-sign long-term. Bell solves both the toughness void (zero current TOR players at 80+ TOUG) and the faceoff void (L4 mean 52) at $900K with two years of control. The coach already displaced Chistov with Alexeev, so no internal plan is lost.

recommendations.proposed: Draft pick (2nd or 3th round via over-80 expiring mechanic)
recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour to a non-contender for a draft pick using the over-80 expiring mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour at 92 base and expiring qualifies for the over-80 pick mechanic. The GM's March 21 renewal order has Belfour walking; trading him recovers a pick instead of losing $6.50M of value for nothing. Per the GM's March 4 standing order, send him to a non-playoff team. This pick becomes the funding for a Heatley or Stuart package if Proposal 1 fails. Acceptance is uncertain because the mechanic's pick value by team is not known.

recommendations.current: Upshall (RW, 21, POTE 99, CHKG 87, $1.20M, 1 yr) + Alexeev (RW, 23, POTE 94, BALA 90, SPEE 89, $1.10M, 1 yr)
recommendations.summary: If Bell falls through, send Upshall and Alexeev to LA for Avery as the budget toughness/faceoff fix.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 79 pts with 14 expiring deals and $52.43M payroll will deal Avery ($400K) for almost any package. Upshall's POTE 99 and Alexeev's POTE 94 give LA two cheap youth evaluations for one season. The cost is high relative to return: two POTE 94+ wings for one year in exchange for a 0.11 pts/g centre. This is the fallback if Bell's price rises or CHI asks for more. Both players walk in July 2006 if LA doesn't re-sign them.

recommendations.summary: Goalie monitoring task is complete; Luongo is on the roster at 94 and the GM closed this on 2005-03-19.
recommendations.rationale: The January request was to track Luongo's availability from Florida and DiPietro's development as a fallback. Florida traded Luongo; he is now our starter at 94 overall with 2 years left. The GM explicitly retired this task twice.

recommendations.summary: Give Alexeev top-nine minutes next season; his 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG outproduces Chistov and Upshall who both sit at 0.29 on more ice.
recommendations.rationale: At 23 with 55 games, Alexeev's rate is nearly double both players currently ahead of him. His production-to-ice-time mismatch is the clearest on the roster and persists across the full season.

recommendations.summary: Colaiacovo needs a full-season audition next year; 31 games at 17.9 MPG proves he can carry minutes but not volume.
recommendations.rationale: At 22, his MPG when dressed (17.9) is higher than Klesla's 14.8, so the staff already trusts his shifts. The missing piece is games, not quality. Only 31 appearances is too few to judge a defenceman this young.

recommendations.summary: Spezza needs a real camp competition next year with top-six looks; his season (46 GP, 6.7 MPG, 0.33 pts/g) was a write-off.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 at 21 with only 46 games and collapsing minutes means the system never gave him a chance. Next camp is the only remaining lever this season can't fix.

recommendations.summary: Chistov (0.29 pts/g on 13.1 MPG) and Upshall (0.29 on 7.9) are both producing below what their ice earns; Alexeev should displace one of them next season.
recommendations.rationale: Both hold top-nine minutes while matching Alexeev's rate on double or more the ice. Their roles are not supported by production and the mismatch persists for the full 68-game sample.

recommendations.summary: Build the offseason plan around Kaberle as the one ascending defender: 0.54 to 0.62 pts/g on 21.5 MPG at age 27.
recommendations.rationale: He is the only established player whose rate and load both rose through this window. The GM called him a keeper; this trend says he is the top-pair anchor for the next three seasons.

recommendations.summary: Place McCabe back on the sell list at season's end with his full-season 0.48 confirmed.
recommendations.rationale: The 1.42 December rate was a 24-game hot start; 82 games at 0.48 is his real number. At 29 with $3.00M and 4 years remaining, the asset value of his contract exceeds his on-ice contribution.

recommendations.summary: Klesla stays on the sell list: 0.31 pts/g over 82 games is his second consecutive decline.
recommendations.rationale: 0.38 at 22, 0.31 at 23 on flat 15 MPG. The trend is unambiguous and he has 2 years at $0.90M left to move.

recommendations.summary: No action on Gaborik despite the 1.42 to 1.12 drop; 1.12 over 82 games at 23 is on-track production.
recommendations.rationale: The 1.42 was 24 games. Full-season rate with a rising load from 18.8 to 21.2 MPG is what you expect from a young star settling in.

recommendations.summary: Sundin at 0.97 on 21.7 MPG at 34 is normal decline; begin planning around his departure over the next two seasons.
recommendations.rationale: His rate dropped from 1.46 but he is still the second-best centre on the roster. No emergency, but the Chlup-first plan means his minutes should be redistributed within two years.

recommendations.summary: No morale-driven lineup change for Washington; the room is at 98 average with every player trending up or stable.
recommendations.rationale: Lowest morale on the roster is Spezza at 88 (up 3), scratched by design. All dressed players are 95-100. No player is under his minutes band with slipping morale.

recommendations.summary: L4 faceoff mean is 52 with a best of 55; no one outside L1-L3 can win a draw. This is a roster gap requiring a checking centre with 65+ faceoffs.
recommendations.rationale: The four faceoff men on the roster are Sundin (91), Chlup (80), Roberts (76), Richards (75) — all already on L1-L3 and PK. Moving any one to L4 weakens those lines. Abid's 72 toughness is the only role contribution on L4. Unchanged since April 13.

recommendations.summary: All four even-strength lines and all four special-teams units are correctly composed for their purpose. No rearrangement is needed tonight.
recommendations.rationale: L1 checks (Jackman 90, Fischer 85) and scores (Sundin 93, Mogilny 94). K2 is the best checking unit on the roster at mean 84. P2 has Mogilny's 94 speed as the weapon. The only deficiency is the L4 faceoff problem, which is a roster issue not a lines issue.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming.
recommendations.rationale: OVR 94, morale 100, ENDU 73. Far above Ouellet at 82. Check fatigue icon per standing order from January 19.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes for Washington. The auto-pairing already puts Fischer and Jackman on Jagr, and our top two lines (Sundin 91, Mogilny 90, Chlup 86, Afinogenov 86) are far too skilled for their soft D pairs (Gonchar 78, Yonkman 70, Pilar 69).
recommendations.rationale: We lead the series 3-1-0 (20-10 goals), we are 59-13-5, and our current lines are already maximum quality. No benched player improves us. Washington's 8-game win streak is a hot run against weaker opposition; their top player (Jagr, 84) is matched by our second-best D.

recommendations.summary: Sell McCabe this offseason: 0.48 rate over his last 58 games at 29 and $3.00M for 4 more years.
recommendations.rationale: Season rate 0.76 is inflated by a hot start. Recent window 0.48 on 22.1 MPG at age 29 means the decline is real. Four years of $3.00M on a declining 0.50-rate D man is a burden.

recommendations.summary: Sell Jackman this offseason: 29.6 MPG at $0.70M x 3 is tradeable to any club needing top-pair minutes cheap.
recommendations.rationale: Final rate 0.46 on 80 games. His value to a buyer is 30 MPG at $700K, which is the best minutes-per-dollar package on our blue line.

recommendations.summary: Sell Klesla this offseason: second consecutive declining season (0.38 to 0.37) on flat minutes.
recommendations.rationale: 82 GP, 30 pts, 0.37 rate at 14.8 MPG. Age 23 with two straight years going backwards. $0.90M x 2 is cheap enough to attract a suitor.

recommendations.summary: Sell Eminger before July 1: his contract expires and if he walks we get nothing for a 21-year-old 77 OVR.
recommendations.rationale: 64 GP, 0.36 rate on 15.5 MPG, age 21, $1.20M expiring. Most urgent of the sell list because the window closes with no deadline trade protection.

recommendations.summary: Hold Colaiacovo for camp; his $1.10M expiring deal and 0.39 rate in 31 games make him depth, not a sell priority.
recommendations.rationale: If Eminger, Klesla and McCabe all move we need a 7th/8th D. See him in camp before deciding.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bell at any offseason window; he is the only league-wide player closing toughness, checking, and faceoffs simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Zero Toronto players carry 80+ TOUG. Sundin at 90 is the only 80+ faceoff man and he is 34. Bell brings 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE at 24 with POTE 81, from a 73-point CHI club with 10 expiring deals.

recommendations.summary: Keep Avery as the cheaper alternative to Bell: 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG at $400K with two years left.
recommendations.rationale: LA finished at 48 points with 13 expiring deals. Avery closes the faceoff gap (team high 70 without Sundin) and the toughness gap in one body at a fraction of Bell's asking price.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Stuart to replace Roberts; checking drops from 6 to 5 at 80+ the day Roberts walks.
recommendations.rationale: Stuart is 25 with 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91. SJ finished at 72 points with 13 expiring on $45.39M and cannot retain all of them, though at 72 points they may not deal a POTE 91 blueliner.

recommendations.summary: Iginla supersedes Heatley as the RW priority: 93 base, 140 pts in 73 GP, 85 TOUG, expiring from a 70-point club.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny declined to 0.79 pts/g at 36. CGY finished at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit and cannot retain him. Iginla also raises the structural toughness ceiling that Bell alone cannot fix.

recommendations.summary: The backup spot is a hole: Ouellet's grades (INTE 69, ENDU 60) say he cannot carry a playoff series as Belfour's successor.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour (40, expiring) walks. Ouellet at 23 posted 4-4 in 13 games with GAA 2.41 but his grades are well below starter-level. Tellqvist (25, expiring, GAA 3.39) is not the answer either.

recommendations.summary: Give Alexeev the camp audition the coach flagged; his 0.48-0.55 pts/g outproduces Chistov (0.29) and Upshall (0.29) who dressed ahead of him all year.
recommendations.rationale: Alexeev at 0.48 pts/g on 6 MPG is the most productive fourth-line option the club has and is not being used. Chistov at 0.29 on 14 MPG is the worst rate among regulars.

recommendations.summary: Speed and stamina are the deepest roles on the roster: 21 players at 80+ speed, 11 at 80+ stamina. No action needed.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik 98, Afinogenov 96, Koltsov 92, Fischer 89, Sundin 89 on speed. Kaberle 97, McCabe 94, Sundin 92 on stamina. These roles are covered for multiple seasons.

recommendations.summary: Sign Gaborik to a 5-6 year deal at season end before any other club can offer long term.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base, 99 points, age 23, POTE 90, $1.10M expiring. He is the foundation of the next five years and there is no pick to replace him.

recommendations.summary: Sign Richards to a 5-6 year deal at season end.
recommendations.rationale: 66 points, age 25, POTE 88, $1.00M expiring. He is a top-six centre entering his prime and the second-highest priority after Gaborik.

recommendations.summary: Sign Nash to a 5-6 year deal at season end.
recommendations.rationale: 39 points, age 20, POTE 95, $1.20M expiring. Lock him before his price rises with production.

recommendations.summary: Sign Eminger to a 4-year deal, not 5 or 6, to buy one more year of proof.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 is the highest on the roster but 23 points in 64 games at age 21 has not yet justified a 6-year commitment. Four years keeps control through 25 without overpaying for upside that may not convert.

recommendations.summary: Renew Upshall, Colaiacovo, Alexeev, Chistov and Abid on 2-year deals to split the renewal cluster across two summers.
recommendations.rationale: Five two-year deals come up in 2007 instead of thirteen in 2005. This avoids the manual's warning about simultaneous expirations and preserves payroll flexibility in the interim.

recommendations.summary: Let Belfour walk in July. Do not re-sign at $6.50M.
recommendations.rationale: Age 40, scratched, POTE 50, $6.50M. Luongo at 91 base and 26 is the starter. Belfour frees $6.50M that can fund the Iginla signing.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk in July. Do not re-sign at $2.70M.
recommendations.rationale: Age 38, POTE 52, 81 points but no room to grow. $2.70M buys two years of a 40-year-old. The money is better spent on a player with years left.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Iginla in July via trade for Belfour plus a roster player, or sign if he reaches UFA.
recommendations.rationale: 93 base, 140 points in 73 GP, TOUG 85, age 27, $6.50M expiring. Closes the RW void and the toughness gap simultaneously. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring cannot retain him.

recommendations.summary: Accept Sundin's $8.40M five-year deal as sunk cost and build around him for two more seasons.
recommendations.rationale: No trade market exists for a 34-year-old with five years at $8.40M. He will decline but the contract is signed. The move is to maximize his remaining production by adding Iginla alongside him now, not later.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik on a 5-6 year deal immediately at season end before free agency.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base, 23, 87 points, $1.10M expiring. He is the best player on the roster and the cheapest. A bidding war in July costs multiples.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards on a 5-year deal.
recommendations.rationale: 25, 64 points, $1.00M expiring. Second priority after Gaborik. A centre at 25 with 64 points is the rarest commodity in the league.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash on a 5-year deal.
recommendations.rationale: 20 years old, $1.20M expiring. Lock him while he is rookie-cheap.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger on a 5-year deal.
recommendations.rationale: 21, POTE 99, $1.20M expiring. GM standing order from Jan 19 keeps him; the renewal is the logical execution of that.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle on a 3-4 year deal, not 5-6.
recommendations.rationale: 27, $1.90M expiring. At 31-32 a 5-year extension becomes a trade anchor. Three or four years balances value and exit.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Tellqvist on a 3-year deal.
recommendations.rationale: 25, $0.80M, POTE high 90s. GM standing order from Jan 15 says keep him and give him time.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Abid on a 2-year deal at his current salary.
recommendations.rationale: 25, $0.40M, TOUG 80, CHKG 80. The cheapest toughness on the roster and impossible to replace at that price.

recommendations.summary: Let Belfour walk at season end. Do not re-sign at any salary.
recommendations.rationale: 40 years old, $6.50M. GM standing order from March 19 confirmed keeping him only through the playoffs. $6.50M for a 40-year-old goalie is $6.50M that cannot go toward Iginla.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk at season end.
recommendations.rationale: 38, $2.70M expiring. GM standing order from March 21 renewal priority list: Belfour and Roberts walk.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla from Calgary using the Islanders' first-round pick as the centrepiece.
recommendations.rationale: 93 base, 27, 140 points in 73 GP, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring cannot retain him. The NYI R1 now in Toronto's hands makes a package Iginla-calibre, which was impossible in January.

recommendations.summary: Monitor Cammalleri as a UFA value signing at 22 with POTE 98 on a $1.10M expiring deal.
recommendations.rationale: 60 points in 61 games, LA at 79 points with 14 expiring. If he clears waivers or walks, sign on a 3-year deal at his current salary.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bell from Chicago to close the fourth-line toughness gap the Coach quantified.
recommendations.rationale: 24, 82 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82. Coach flagged checking mean 61 and toughness mean 57 on L4; Bell is the only league-wide player closing both. CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring and $29.46M profit are motivated sellers.

recommendations.summary: Camp auditions in July decide renew-or-release for all four expiring prospects at $1.10-1.20M each.
recommendations.rationale: Upshall POTE 99 at 0.29 pts/g, Alexeev 0.48 on 6.0 MPG, Chistov 0.29 on 14.0, Colaiacovo 0.39 on 17.9 across 31 games. None have earned a roster spot; four slots and $4.50M is not worth carrying on flat numbers.

recommendations.summary: Sign or trade for Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, 128 pts/76 GP, 87 TOUG, $6.50M expiring) as the July priority — he closes RW scoring and toughness in one body.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain a $6.50M winger. His 87 TOUG raises the team ceiling from 75 (Jackman) to 87. Payroll frees $9.20M from Belfour and Roberts, making the $6.50M possible.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Brewer (SJ, D, 26, 88 base, 61 pts/82 GP, 82 TOUG, 93 CHKG, $2.00M expiring) as Roberts' replacement.
recommendations.rationale: His 82 TOUG and 61 points exceed what Roberts provided at a lower cost ($2.00M vs $2.70M) with twelve years of remaining career. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring deals have too many D to retain all of them.

recommendations.summary: Target Lalime (OTT, G, 30, 92 base, GAA 3.09, $1.90M expiring) as the playoff-ready backup Luongo needs.
recommendations.rationale: Ouellet reads INTE 69 and ENDU 60 — not a playoff backup. Lalime is 92 base at $1.90M, a third of Belfour's cost. OTT at 77 points with $32.36M profit and 11 expiring are the most motivated sellers in the league.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Havlat (OTT, LW, 24, 87 base, 103 pts/82 GP, $900K expiring, POTE 85) — 103 points at $900K from the same selling club as Lalime.
recommendations.rationale: Same club as Lalime (OTT, 77 pts, 11 expiring) which allows a double-dip package. At $900K he provides top-six scoring at rookie-scale money. His 68 TOUG means he adds scoring, not toughness.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Heatley (ATL, RW, 24, 91 base, 131 pts/79 GP, $1.10M expiring) as the fallback if Iginla is unattainable.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring cannot re-sign both Heatley and Kovalchuk at $1.10M each. If they keep Kovalchuk, Heatley at 91 base and 131 points is the best RW available. His 75 TOUG is below target but 20 points above the current team mean.

recommendations.summary: Monitor Kovalchuk (ATL, LW, 22, 89 base, 138 pts/79 GP, $1.10M expiring, POTE 85) — highest production on any expiring deal in the league.
recommendations.rationale: 138 points at 22 years old for $1.10M is the single best player-for-money ratio available. ATL's binary with Heatley means only one stays. He plays LW not RW, so he does not directly fill Mogilny's slot, but 138 points reshapes any line.

recommendations.summary: If SJ keeps Brewer, pivot to Stuart (SJ, D, 25, 87 base, 52 pts/77 GP, 80 TOUG, POTE 91, $1.80M expiring).
recommendations.rationale: Two years younger than Brewer with 10 more potential points. His 80 TOUG hits the team's new floor. Same club situation as Brewer — SJ at 76 points cannot keep both.

recommendations.summary: Explore Gagne (PHI, LW, 25, 86 base, 108 pts/82 GP, $2.40M expiring) as PHI needs to shed from their $66.73M payroll with only $2.14M profit.
recommendations.rationale: PHI's financial distress makes them the most pressure-seller among 80+ point clubs. His 58 TOUG adds nothing to the toughness problem but 108 points at 25 is elite production at moderate cost.

recommendations.summary: Sign Belanger (LA, C, 27, 82 base, 97 FACE, $700K expiring) as pure faceoff insurance for Sundin at 34.
recommendations.rationale: 97 FACE is the highest in the league and $700K is the cost of a depth player. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring are sellers. His 14 points in 64 games means he is a specialist, not a top-nine forward.

recommendations.summary: Monitor Thornton (BOS, C, 25, 94 base, 83 pts/59 GP, 89 TOUG, 90 CHKG, $4.00M expiring) but do not build around him.
recommendations.rationale: He closes scoring, toughness, and checking simultaneously but BOS at 97 points with $34.32M profit are a contender with no incentive to sell. January readings also conflicted on his base (76 vs 94). Pursue only as an opportunistic call.

recommendations.summary: Scout Komisarek (MTL, D, 23, 77 base, POTE 91, $1.10M expiring) from the worst team in the league, but verify the anomalous 82 GP/82 points reading before building a case.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 91 at age 23 with $1.10M expiring from a 66-point club with 15 expiring deals makes him available. The points figure is anomalous for a 77-base defenseman and requires verification before valuation.

recommendations.proposed: Brewer (SJ, D, 26, 88 base, 93 CHKG, 82 TOUG, 61 pts/82 GP, $2.00M, expiring)
recommendations.summary: Trade Upshall to San Jose for Eric Brewer to replace Roberts on the blue line and raise team checking from 75 to 93.
