recommendations.rationale: SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring deals and $20.74M profit have too many defensemen to retain all of them. A 21-year-old with POTE 99 and CHKG 87 at $1.20M gives them a player they can extend cheaply and build a top-nine role around. We get a proven 88-base blueliner in his prime.

recommendations.summary: Trade Ouellet to Ottawa for Dominik Lalime to secure a 92-base playoff backup alongside Luongo.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 77 points with 11 expiring deals and $32.36M profit are the league's most motivated sellers. Ouellet at POTE 97 and age 23 is a franchise-project goalie they need for the crease. Saves them $1.00M net. Our current backup options (Ouellet at INTE 69, ENDU 60; Tellqvist at GAA 3.39) cannot hold a playoff series.

recommendations.current: Spezza (C, 21, POTE 99, $1.00M, 2 years) + Tucker (LW, 30, $1.30M, 2 years) + 4th-round pick
recommendations.proposed: Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, 128 pts/76 GP, 87 TOUG, $6.50M, expiring)
recommendations.summary: Trade Spezza, Tucker, and the 4th-rounder to Calgary for Jarome Iginla to close the RW scoring void and the structural toughness gap simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring deals and $14.43M profit cannot retain a $6.50M winger. A POTE 99 center at 21 with two years of control at $1.00M is the cornerstone of any rebuild. Mogilny fell to 0.79 pts/g at 36; without this move the RW slot has no credible replacement. Payroll impact net of Belfour/Roberts departures is negative $5.00M for us. Acceptance is uncertain because Calgary's AI may prefer a single high-potential piece over a package.

recommendations.summary: Item #2 is delivered and closed: Luongo is on our roster at 94, DiPietro monitoring is moot, and the GM's March 19 order formally ended the goalie trade window.
recommendations.rationale: The task existed to monitor a target we have now acquired. Luongo reads 94 overall at 26 with 2 years at $1.60M. The GM closed all goalie trade monitoring on 2005-03-19.

recommendations.slot: right wing on a lower line
recommendations.summary: Put Alexeev in tonight's lineup at right wing, benching Upshall.
recommendations.rationale: Alexeev produces 0.55 pts/g over 55 games versus Upshall's 0.29 over 68, yet sits scratched. PIT at 24-34 is a development game per the GM's standing order, and this is the last chance to evaluate Alexeev before offseason.

recommendations.summary: No other lineup changes tonight.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup, Nash, Gaborik, Klesla and Eminger are all dressed and producing in proportion to their roles. Spacek at 19 on 7.6 MPG is at the correct depth band for his first pro year. The season is over for development purposes beyond tonight's one look.

recommendations.summary: Assign Chlup to first-line centre permanently for next season.
recommendations.rationale: 0.62 to 0.88 pts/g while minutes doubled from 11.0 to 18.2. He thrived under increased load at 19, which is the rarest outcome for a teenager.

recommendations.summary: Sell McCabe this offseason at $3.00M x 4 before his rate drops further.
recommendations.rationale: Recent 58-game window at 0.48 pts/g on 21.5 MPG. Season rate 0.76 is carried by a hot 24-game start that has fully bled off. At 29 his value erodes each month.

recommendations.summary: Give Spacek a real first-camp audition at centre. If he cannot hold 10 MPG on merit, stop dressing him.
recommendations.rationale: 0.55 to 0.28 pts/g on minutes that fell from 16.0 to 5.2. He had a role and lost it without a grade or injury explaining why. At 19 the only lever left is a clean run in preseason.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza a real first-camp audition. Same test as Spacek: earn 10+ MPG or stop dressing.
recommendations.rationale: 0.43 to 0.24 pts/g on 9.1 to 4.6 MPG at age 21. High potential is meaningless if he never gets ice to show it.

recommendations.summary: Kaberle is trending up at 27 and stays as the top-pair quarterback. No change.
recommendations.rationale: 0.54 to 0.62 pts/g on 19.4 to 21.5 MPG. The only TOR skater whose rate and minutes both rose in this window.

recommendations.summary: Klesla stays on the sell list for the offseason.
recommendations.rationale: 0.50 to 0.31 pts/g on flat 14.9 MPG. Second consecutive declining season at 23 with $0.90M x 2 remaining.

recommendations.summary: The room is happy. Morale averages 92 with the dressed lineup all at 98 or 100. No minutes adjustment needed tonight.
recommendations.rationale: Abid's production-to-minutes gap (0.80 pts/g on 13.8 MPG) is the only structural concern but his morale is 100 and rising. Spezza at 88 is the GM's development choice, not a morale fix. Everyone else sits within their expected band.

recommendations.summary: We need a centre with faceoff above 60 who can anchor the fourth line; no one on this roster or in the scratches fills it.
recommendations.rationale: L4 faceoff mean is 51, best 54. The entire roster's faceoff depth is four deep (Sundin 90, Chlup 79, Roberts 75, Richards 74) and all four are already on L1-L3 handling draws. No swap fixes L4 without breaking another unit.

recommendations.summary: Give L4 fewer shifts tonight; every draw they take is a likely possession loss at 51 mean.
recommendations.rationale: L4 faceoff best is 54 against Pittsburgh. Until the roster gap is filled, limiting their exposure to defensive-zone starts is the smallest available mitigation.

recommendations.summary: Lines 1-3 and both PK/PP units are correctly built; no swap improves the roster given current personnel.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has elite scoring and checking alongside Sundin's draws. L2's job is offence and it has it. L3 is the best checking unit (Tucker at 93 best, Richards clutch 96). PK division between K1 (draws) and K2 (checking) is correct. Both PPs score at 86 mean.

recommendations.summary: Play the same lines we have been running. No matchup adjustment needed.
recommendations.rationale: TOR is 133 pts vs PIT's 85, we lead the season series 7-2-1, and their PP converts at 11.6%. There is no unit on their side that requires a special assignment against us.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 94 OVR with 100 morale. Their goalie Hedberg is 87, a downgrade we should exploit all night.

recommendations.summary: Sell list unchanged from May 2: McCabe (0.48 recent), Jackman (0.46 season), Klesla (0.37 season), Eminger (0.36 season, expiring). Fischer and Kaberle are keepers per GM.
recommendations.rationale: Final season numbers confirm every call. Jackman dipped marginally from 0.48 to 0.46, Eminger from 0.38 to 0.36. No new information changes any recommendation.

recommendations.summary: Toughness is the only structurally missing role: zero players at 80+, ceiling is Jackman 75. Only an acquisition closes it.
recommendations.rationale: Bell (CHI, 88 TOUG, 24, POTE 81) and Avery (LA, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 93 FACE, $400K) are the only league-wide players who reset this. Avery closes toughness, checking, and faceoffs simultaneously at 25 and $400K on two years.

recommendations.summary: Faceoffs are a one-man role: Sundin 90 is the only forward above 80, with Chlup next at 75.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts at 75 is expiring. After him the ceiling is Chlup at 75. Avery at 93 FACE or Bell at 82 are the only targets who fix this. No internal player at 25 or younger draws above 75.

recommendations.summary: Gaborik is listed as unlined at 92 overall and 98 speed; confirm he enters the playoff lineup.
recommendations.rationale: The role coverage shows him at 92 and 'not lined.' He is 23, $1.10M, and the first July renewal priority. If he is still unlined he is the largest single internal gap on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Avery at 25, $400K, two years, closes toughness (83), checking (88), and faceoffs (93) in one move.
recommendations.rationale: He is the cheapest player closing all three structural gaps simultaneously. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring deals remain motivated sellers. His $400K salary makes him nearly free relative to Bell at $900K or Iginla at $6.50M.

recommendations.summary: Belfour (40, $6.50M, 1y) walks after this season; the GM's January order to fetch a high-90s goalie from a non-contender is still open.
recommendations.rationale: Post-Belfour depth is Ouellet (23, 2y, 911 SV%) or Tellqvist (25, 1y, 880 SV%). Neither is a credible number-two for a contending club. Luongo (26, 2y) needs a real backup by October.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik, Richards, Nash and Eminger on 5-6 year deals before any other July move, in that order of urgency.
recommendations.rationale: These four are the core of the next five seasons. Gaborik (99 pts/82 GP at 23) and Richards (66 pts/80 GP at 25) are proven; Nash (POTE 95 at 20) and Eminger (POTE 99 at 21) are the future. All four are on 1-year deals expiring simultaneously. Losing any of them without compensation guts the roster.

recommendations.summary: Trade Mogilny this summer while his 84-point season still fetches value, before the decline becomes obvious.
recommendations.rationale: He is 36, $5.50M for two more years ($11M remaining), and his rate dropped from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g during this season. In twelve months he may be worth a 4th-rounder; now he can fetch a mid-round pick plus a young player. A contender needing a depth RW for a playoff push is the target.

recommendations.summary: Ride Sundin's five-year deal; do not attempt to move it.
recommendations.rationale: He is 34 with 91 points in 82 games and $8.40M locked for five years. No club would take on $8.40M to a 35+ year-old without Toronto feeding them young players they want to keep. The deal is productive for 2-3 more years and untradeable after that; accept the back-end risk and move on.

recommendations.summary: Sign Abid to a 3-4 year extension; at $0.40M he is a 66-point player at $400K and will not stay there.
recommendations.rationale: Abid scored 66 points in 82 games at age 25 on $0.40M. His POTE is 94. Any club will offer him at least $1M in free agency. Locking him at $1.00-1.50M on term is the cheapest value on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Renew Gaborik on 6 years as the first July call.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base, POTE 90, 87 points, $1.10M expiring, age 23. He is a star and the game rewards 5-6 year locks on stars to avoid ratcheting demands.

recommendations.summary: Renew Richards on 5-6 years as the second July call.
recommendations.rationale: 25 years old, 64 points, $1.00M expiring. Franchise centre opposite Sundin. If Gaborik stays and Richards doesn't, you kept the wing and lost the centre.

recommendations.summary: Renew Kaberle on 5 years.
recommendations.rationale: 27, $1.90M, top-pairing D. Least replaceable at his grade this summer. Five years fits the veteran profile.

recommendations.summary: Renew Nash on 6 years.
recommendations.rationale: Age 20, $1.20M. Cheapest long-term lock on the roster. Early commitment on rookies is the guide's recommendation.

recommendations.summary: Renew Eminger on 6 years.
recommendations.rationale: 21, POTE 99, $1.20M. The GM protected him from deadline packages specifically because his development window is the longest on the blue line.

recommendations.summary: Renew Colaiacovo on 5 years.
recommendations.rationale: 22, $1.10M, young D the Coach is still evaluating. Five years is right if he's in the next-camp plans; the POTE profile supports holding him.

recommendations.summary: Renew Alexeev on 3 years at middle-six depth.
recommendations.rationale: 23, 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG — the Coach's own numbers put him above Chistov and Upshall at 0.29 each. He earns the roster spot the Coach flagged.

recommendations.summary: Let Chistov walk in July rather than renew.
recommendations.rationale: 0.29 pts/g at 22, $1.10M, outproduced by Alexeev who is the same age. Coach flagged him as the weakest of the three 21-23 year-olds on the bottom six.

recommendations.summary: Renew Upshall on 2 years at reduced salary, or let him walk alongside Chistov.
recommendations.rationale: 21, 0.29 pts/g, $1.20M. A year younger than Chistov so tradeable as a sweetener, but depth is thin if both go. Decide by July roster size.

recommendations.summary: Renew Abid on 2 years.
recommendations.rationale: 25, 80 TOUG, 80 CHKG, $0.40M. The cheapest toughness on the roster. Coach's gap is structural with zero forwards above 85 TOUG outside Roberts.

recommendations.summary: Belfour walks in July. Do not pursue a renewal.
recommendations.rationale: 40, $6.50M. GM's March 19 standing order closed all goalie trade tasks and set the playoff goalie plan. Belfour and Roberts walk per the March 21 renewal order.

recommendations.summary: Roberts walks in July.
recommendations.rationale: 38, $2.70M. His physical presence must be replaced — Stuart (SJ, 87 base, 89 CHKG, POTE 91, expiring) is the closest target.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla in July as the RW replacement for Mogilny's decline.
recommendations.rationale: 93 base, 140 pts in 73 GP, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring, age 27. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring cannot retain him. Closes the scoring void and the toughness ceiling simultaneously.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bell as the fourth-line toughness and faceoff fix.
recommendations.rationale: CHI LW, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE. Only league-wide player closing both the checking and faceoff voids the Coach quantified on April 9.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Stuart to replace Roberts on the blue line.
recommendations.rationale: SJ D, 25, 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91, expiring. San Jose at 72 points with 13 expiring cannot retain all of them.

recommendations.summary: The March 19 deadline passed with no trades executed. No action available.
recommendations.rationale: The GM's February standing orders protected the defensive core (Eminger, McCabe), and the only remaining chips (Tucker, 4th-rounder) were insufficient to close any target. This was the correct outcome for a team at 133 points.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Thornton (BOS, 94 base, 89 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 79 FACE, $4.00M expiring) as the single move that closes toughness, checking, faceoffs, and scoring simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: BOS at 97 points with 13 expiring contracts may not re-sign him and will seek value over losing him to UFA for nothing. No other available player combines 94 base, elite toughness, and elite checking at age 25.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla (CGY, 93 base, 87 TOUG, 81 CHKG, 128 pts/76 GP, $6.50M expiring) to close the Mogilny scoring void and the structural toughness ceiling in one move.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him. 87 TOUG raises the roster ceiling from 75 to 87. Mogilny at $5.50M is the salary-matching piece.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Lalime (OTT, 92 base, $1.90M, expiring) as the cheapest 90+ goalie from a non-contender, fitting the Jan 15 standing order.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 77 points with 11 expiring and $32.36M profit will not re-sign him. At $1.90M he costs $3.60M less than Theodore while carrying a higher base (92 vs 91). POTE 80 means he is what he is: a 92.

recommendations.summary: Theodore (MTL, 91 base, POTE 88, $5.50M, expiring) is the higher-ceiling goalie option if Lalime is unobtainable or if we want more development upside.
recommendations.rationale: MTL at 66 points with 15 expiring are the most motivated sellers in the league. POTE 88 exceeds Lalime's 80, meaning more remaining growth. Costs $3.60M more per season.

recommendations.summary: If Iginla does not land, pursue Heatley (ATL, 91 base, 131 pts/79 GP, $1.10M, 1 year) as the best scoring-for-salary target available.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring face a binary with Kovalchuk at the same salary. Whichever they keep, the other becomes available. Heatley at 75 TOUG does not close the toughness gap but his 131 points at $1.10M is unmatched value.

recommendations.summary: Kovalchuk (ATL, 89 base, 138 pts/79 GP, $1.10M, 1 year) is available if ATL extends Heatley instead. Highest point total on any likely seller.
recommendations.rationale: 138 points in 79 games at age 22 for $1.10M. TOUG 78 sits below the 80 gap threshold but his production fills the LW wing at a fraction of Iginla's cost.

recommendations.summary: Gagne (PHI, 86 base, 108 pts/82 GP, $2.40M, expiring) is a July UFA signing target; PHI at $2.14M profit cannot re-sign him.
recommendations.rationale: 1.32 pts/g at 25 for $2.40M on the open market. Does not close toughness (58 TOUG) but fills a scoring wing cheaply if neither ATL target materializes.

recommendations.summary: Bell (CHI, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, $900K, 2 years) raises the toughness ceiling for a fraction of any large-package cost if the big fish don't land.
recommendations.rationale: CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit are motivated sellers. The March 30 note identifies him as the only league-wide player closing toughness and faceoffs together. His data fell below today's query cutoffs but the standing read holds.

recommendations.summary: Avery (LA, 79 base, 93 FACE, 88 CHKG, 83 TOUG, $400K, 2 years) is the cheapest player raising the toughness ceiling, but at 9 points in 82 games he contributes nothing offensively.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 79 points with 14 expiring are motivated sellers. At $400K the risk is negligible, but Bell at $900K is the better option if CHI accepts a package. Avery is the fallback if neither Thornton, Iginla, nor Bell can be acquired.

recommendations.summary: Trade Mogilny (36, $5.50M, 2 years remaining) this summer while his 84-point season still carries paper value; he is the salary-matching piece for Iginla or Thornton.
recommendations.rationale: His production fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g during the season. $11.00M total remaining for a declining 37-year-old. No team wants him after one more decline. He must leave before the window closes.

recommendations.summary: Decide by next camp whether Spezza gets top-six minutes or becomes trade bait; at 21, POTE 99, and never above 0.33 pts/g, his value peaks while the potential grade is credible.
recommendations.rationale: The coach flagged this six times by March and again April 30. The March 23 note says his trade value is highest while the potential grade is believed. Another dead season without real minutes kills it.

recommendations.summary: Trade Mogilny and Alexeev to Calgary for Iginla; converts a $5.50M declining asset into the 93-base RW who closes the toughness ceiling and the scoring void simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain Iginla and losing him to UFA yields nothing. Mogilny still projects 30-40 points for one year and Alexeev at POTE 94 gives them a young piece. Toronto net minus $100K on payroll.

recommendations.summary: Trade Afinogenov and the 4th-rounder to Boston for Thornton; the single player who resets toughness, checking, and faceoffs in one transaction.
recommendations.rationale: BOS at 97 points with 13 expiring must move Thornton or lose him. Afinogenov at 25 with POTE 95 and a 4-year deal is a controllable top-nine winger. Toronto net minus $500K. Acceptance uncertain because BOS may want more for a 94-base center.

recommendations.summary: Trade Koltsov to Chicago for Bell; resets the toughness ceiling from 75 to 88 and closes the faceoff gap at $900K with two years of control.
recommendations.rationale: CHI at 78 points, 10 expiring, and $31.73M profit are in full teardown and would prefer POTE 94 at 24 over POTE 81 at 24. Bell's grades already exceed our entire roster at TOUG and CHKG. Net minus $200K.

recommendations.summary: Goalie monitoring task (#2) is closed per GM's 2005-03-19 standing order; Luongo at 94 is on the roster and the trade window is past.
recommendations.rationale: The GM closed all goalie monitoring on March 19. Luongo (94 overall, $1.60M, 2 years) and Belfour (93) are both on the roster. The task expired before the deadline and was superseded by the decision to keep both through the playoffs.

recommendations.summary: Assign Chlup to the first-line centre slot for next season based on his 0.83 pts/g at 19 on 16.9 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: 59 points in 71 games is the best rate on the roster outside Gaborik. He has earned the top centre job permanently.

recommendations.summary: Give Alexeev a top-nine audition in camp next season; his 0.55 pts/g outproduces Chistov (0.29) and Upshall (0.29) who dressed ahead of him all year.
recommendations.rationale: 30 points in 55 games on 8.3 MPG is a rate that deserves a real look at top-nine minutes. He has not been given them.

recommendations.summary: Spezza's season is done at 0.33 pts/g on 6.7 MPG; decide at camp whether he is a project or a release.
recommendations.rationale: 46 games, collapsed minutes in the back half, POTE 99 not translating. The only lever left is a real preseason audition.

recommendations.summary: Upshall's season is done at 0.29 pts/g on 7.9 MPG with POTE 99; same offseason audition-or-release decision as Spezza.
recommendations.rationale: 68 games dressed but never earned more than 8 minutes a night. POTE 99 has not produced.

recommendations.summary: Colaiacovo earned a roster audition in camp at 0.39 pts/g on 17.9 MPG across 31 games; he has not yet earned a permanent top-four spot.
recommendations.rationale: When given top-pair minutes he held them at a reasonable rate with POTE 99. Needs a full preseason to convert that into a job.

recommendations.summary: Spacek at 19 earned his fourth-line role at 0.34 pts/g on 7.6 MPG; he is a depth player and his year is settled.
recommendations.rationale: 50 games on the fourth line at 19 is a reasonable season for a rookie with POTE 91. No argument for more ice.

recommendations.summary: Ouellet at 23 with 13 starts is adequate backup development behind Luongo; no change needed.
recommendations.rationale: 16% share at 40.2 MPG in 13 starts is the right role for a third goalie learning the pro game.

recommendations.summary: McCabe goes back on the sell list: 0.48 pts/g over 58 games is well below the 0.60 threshold.
recommendations.rationale: His 1.42 hot start inflated the season rate long enough to keep him off the list in March. The recent window has collapsed to 0.48 at age 29 with 4 years and $3.00M. The re-evaluation we set for season's end is now complete.

recommendations.summary: Flag both for offseason system-fit review: rate collapses at ages 25 with flat minutes.
recommendations.rationale: Afinogenov dropped 1.17 to 0.73 pts/g, Richards 1.08 to 0.71, both at 25 where the expected direction is up or flat. Neither lost ice time. Something in the system or role isn't fitting them.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev at 0.48 pts/g deserves more than 6.0 MPG; Chistov at 0.30 on 14.0 does not.
recommendations.rationale: Alexeev outproduces Chistov by 0.18 pts/g while receiving 8 fewer minutes a night. The gap has persisted since April 23 and no line arrangement from the bench fixes it.

recommendations.summary: Both need a real camp audition next offseason; their minutes have collapsed to under 5 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: Spacek at 5.2 MPG and 0.28 pts/g, Spezza at 4.6 MPG and 0.24. Neither develops on that schedule. The season is a write-off; next camp is the only lever.

recommendations.summary: Kaberle's trend confirms he should carry the top pair next season without adjustment.
recommendations.rationale: 0.54 to 0.62 pts/g on rising minutes (19.4 to 21.5 MPG) at age 27. He is ascending into his prime and the best trend on this blueline.

recommendations.summary: No morale-driven minutes change needed for the final two games; the room is at 98-100 across the board.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza is the lowest at 88 and climbing +3, but his situation is structural (collapsed minutes since March, 6.7 MPG, 0.33 pts/g) and not fixable in two games. Abid's minutes-to-production mismatch (13.8 MPG, 0.80 pts/g) is not causing morale damage while wins flow. No player is in trouble.

recommendations.summary: L4 faceoffs at 52 mean and 55 best is a roster gap; no available forward can fix it by moving him in.
recommendations.rationale: The four best faceoff men (Sundin 91, Chlup 80, Roberts 76, Richards 75) are all on L1-L3. Spacek, Abid and Upshall win draws at 52-55. No rearrangement of the current roster gives L4 a faceoff presence.

recommendations.summary: No unit reassignment needed for Pittsburgh.
recommendations.rationale: L1 provides scoring, L2 has Chlup for draws, L3 can check via Tucker at 94 or run via Chistov at 98 speed. P1 and P2 both carry 87+ scoring mean. The units fit their roles against a 24-34 opponent that will take penalties.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; fatigue icon is clear.
recommendations.rationale: q74 shows no goalie_tired flag and no streak icon. He's fresh and this is a free game before the playoffs.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes for PIT.
recommendations.rationale: 7-2-0 in the series against a 24-34-11 club with the top record locked. Breaking chemistry one game before the playoffs costs more than a development spot gains. Lemieux's 1.60 pts/g is managed by our existing depth; his first line reads 88 OVR against our 91 and 86.

recommendations.summary: Move Eminger this offseason before July 1 free agency; even a late-round pick beats losing him for nothing.
recommendations.rationale: 0.36 pts/g on 15.5 MPG across 64 games at age 21, $1.20M x 1 year expiring. After July he is a UFA loss.

recommendations.summary: Sell Jackman offseason; his 29.6 MPG on $0.70M x 3 is the cheapest top-pair volume in the league and another club will pay for it.
recommendations.rationale: 80 GP, 0.46 pts/g, 37 points on the league's heaviest D load. His production cannot support the minutes he takes.

recommendations.summary: Klesla goes this offseason too; two declining seasons on 14.8 MPG at $0.90M x 2 is a bench-grade output at a regular price.
recommendations.rationale: 0.37 pts/g confirmed over 82 games, down from 0.38 last year. No path up at 23 on this role.

recommendations.proposed: Bell (CHI, LW/C, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81)
recommendations.summary: Bell closes both the toughness void (zero TOR players at 80+ TOUG) and the fourth-line faceoff gap (only Sundin at 90 exceeds 80) in one player at age 24.
recommendations.rationale: Chicago at 73 points with 10 expiring and $29.46M profit are motivated sellers per the March 30 note. ENDU 71 means short shifts initially, which suits a bottom-six role. Tucker and the 4th-rounder are too small to reach him alone; need a larger package or to combine with another chip.

recommendations.proposed: Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, $6.50M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Iginla fills the Mogilny succession void and raises the team toughness ceiling simultaneously with his 85 TOUG.
recommendations.rationale: Calgary at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him per the April 12 note. His 85 TOUG partially addresses the structural toughness gap on the wing side, though Bell remains better on the centre side.

recommendations.proposed: Stuart (SJ, D, 25, 87 base, 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG, POTE 91)
recommendations.summary: Stuart replaces Roberts on the top pair and is the only blueliner on the target list with 80+ TOUG, adding toughness to the defensive side.
recommendations.rationale: San Jose at 72 points with 13 expiring on $45.39M cannot retain all of them, but at 72 points they may not deal a POTE 91 defenceman per the March 30 note. The deal is harder to land than Bell or Iginla.

recommendations.summary: Goalies are solved per the March 19 standing order; Belfour and Luongo carry the playoffs, Ouellet backs up next season.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour at 32-5, 1.93 GAA and 0.931 SV is the playoff starter. Luongo at 26 with 2 years left is the long-term answer. No further goalie action before July.

recommendations.summary: The fourth-line toughness and faceoff gap has no internal fix; the highest TOUG on the roster is 75 and the highest FACE outside Sundin is 75 (Chlup, who moves to 1C).
recommendations.rationale: The coach confirmed on April 28 that no bench player fixes the checking-61, toughness-57 fourth line. This is confirmed as structural on March 19 (zero players at 80+ TOUG). Acquisition is the only path.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, and Upshall on 5-6 year deals the first week of July 2005; their combined current salary is $5.70M and even tripling costs less than 10% of revenue.
recommendations.rationale: All five expire simultaneously in July 2005. Their combined POTE averages 94. If they walk, the window closes and the 2006 cluster becomes impossible to manage. Priority order: Gaborik first (99 pts at 23), Richards second (66 pts at 24), then Nash, Eminger, Upshall.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Abid on a 2-year deal at approximately $0.80M rather than a 5-year lock; he is a trade chip at 25 with POTE 94 and $0.40M carries more value as currency than as a locked asset.
recommendations.rationale: Abid at $0.40M and POTE 94 is the cheapest trade bait on the roster. A 2-year renewal keeps him as deadline currency for 2006-07 while the Bell target requires a package, and a 2-year deal keeps his price credible to other clubs.

recommendations.summary: Let Belfour ($6.50M) and Roberts ($2.70M) walk at contract expiry; together they free $9.20M and their roles are filled by Luongo/Ouellet and the youth movement on the wing.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 40 and scratched. Roberts is 38 with POTE 52. Both are expiring one-year deals. Mogilny walks in 2006 at $5.50M. These three free $14.70M for Iginla-class RW acquisition and a fourth-line centre.

recommendations.proposed: Bell (CHI, LW/C, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 82 FACE, POTE 81)
recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell this summer or a comparable 4C who wins draws; the coach has flagged the faceoff void every report since March and no roster player fixes it.
recommendations.rationale: Bell at 82 base, 88 TOUG, 82 FACE, age 24 closes the coach's structural gap. CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring contracts and $29.46M profit are motivated sellers. His $1.00M-plus salary fits the freed veteran payroll.

recommendations.summary: Sundin at 34, $8.40M, 5 years left is the roster's longest liability but he is producing (91 pts) and cannot be moved before 2006 at the earliest; no action needed this summer.
recommendations.rationale: His contract runs through age 39 with POTE 60, so the ceiling is set. At 91 points he still earns the minutes. The question resolves itself when Chlup's development either displaces him or makes the cost-per-minute ratio untenable in 2007.

recommendations.summary: Offer Gaborik a five- or six-year extension on the first day of free agency; he is the most valuable expiring asset on the roster at 91 base, POTE 90, age 23, $1.10M.
recommendations.rationale: At 23 with 91 base and POTE 90 he is the cheapest elite player on the expiring list. Losing him to a first-day competing offer would undo the season.

recommendations.summary: Offer Richards a five-year deal; at 24, $1.00M and 0.71 pts/g he is cheap to lock even with the coach's production concern.
recommendations.rationale: The decline from 1.08 to 0.71 pts/g makes him a bargain, not a risk. Five years gives either the old Richards back or a tradeable cheap asset through age 29.

recommendations.summary: Offer Nash a five- or six-year extension at age 20; he is the longest-runway forward on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: Nash is 20 at $1.20M. A six-year deal runs him through age 26, which is the entire development window.

recommendations.summary: Offer Eminger a five- or six-year deal at 21 with POTE 99; the GM has protected him all season and he is the defensive foundation.
recommendations.rationale: The GM's Feb 19 standing order protects Eminger and McCabe from being deadline currency. POTE 99 at 21 is the highest potential on the blue line.

recommendations.summary: Offer Kaberle a five-year deal at 27; prime-age defenceman at $1.90M, lock him through age 32.
recommendations.rationale: Five years keeps him off the market at 32 and staggers him against the 2026 renewal cluster.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk at 38, $2.70M; the GM decided this on March 21 and no offer should be made.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts is the second-oldest player on the expiring list and $2.70M at 38 buys nothing the young defence cannot.

recommendations.summary: Renew the five depth players on two- or three-year deals; Upshall (21) and Chistov (22) take three, the rest two.
recommendations.rationale: Together they cost $5.90M and carry the bottom six. Abid at $0.40M is the cheapest 80-TOUG player available.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla as the top free-agency target; at 93 base and 140 points in 73 games he closes the RW scoring void Mogilny leaves behind.
recommendations.rationale: Calgary at 70 points with 10 expiring deals cannot retain $6.50M at age 27. He is the highest-value player on the open market.

recommendations.summary: No summer action on Mogilny; he is not expiring and at 36 his role shrinks naturally if Iginla lands.
recommendations.rationale: His production fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g but he still carries veteran minutes and a first-wing shift if needed.

recommendations.summary: Sign or trade for Iginla in July: 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, TOUG 85, age 27, $6.50M expiring from 70-point CGY with 10 expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Closes the RW scoring void left by Mogilny (0.79 pts/g at 36) and the structural toughness gap (85 TOUG vs zero on our roster) simultaneously. CGY cannot retain him on an expiring $6.50M deal with $14.43M profit at 70 points.

recommendations.summary: Trade for Bell in summer: 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, age 24, POTE 81, $900K from CHI at 78 points with $31.73M profit.
recommendations.rationale: The only player in the league who closes both toughness (zero rostered at 80+) and fourth-line faceoffs (coach flagged April 28) with development runway. CHI are the most motivated sellers with 10 expiring and the highest profit margin.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Stuart in summer: 87 base, TOUG 80, POTE 92, age 25, 59 pts/82 GP, $1.80M expiring from SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Fills Roberts' void (38, walking) and adds 80+ TOUG to the blue line where Roberts was the only player above 80. SJ at $45.39M payroll with 13 expiring cannot retain all of them.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Komisarek cheaply: 77 base, TOUG 85, CHKG 92, POTE 92, age 23, $1.10M expiring from MTL at 66 points with 15 expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Cheapest high-ceiling blueliner available. MTL are the worst team in the league with the most expiring contracts and $21.59M profit, making them the most likely to accept any offer. His POTE 92 at 23 mirrors Eminger's development arc.

recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri as UFA in July: 79 base, POTE 98, age 22, 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M expiring from LA at 79 points with 14 expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Highest-value UFA per the April 7 note. LA cannot retain both him ($1.10M) and Frolov ($1.10M, POTE 96) at 79 points. At POTE 98 and age 22, he is a potential top-pair wing for three years.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Heatley if Iginla goes elsewhere: 91 base, 131 pts/79 GP, age 24, POTE 84, $1.10M expiring from ATL at 84 points.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring face a binary: keep Kovalchuk (89 base, 138 pts, age 22) or Heatley. If they keep Kovalchuk, Heatley walks at $1.10M and is the best proven RW scorer available.

recommendations.summary: Trade for Avery as a cheap fourth-line specialist: 79 base, 94 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, age 25, $400K, 2 years left from LA.
recommendations.rationale: Closes faceoff and toughness gaps at $400K with 2 years of control. His 5 pts in 82 GP confirms he is a checker only, but at this price the risk is nil. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring will deal him.

recommendations.summary: Sign Reid as UFA: 77 base, POTE 94, SPEE 99, FACE 80, age 24, 70 pts/76 GP, $600K expiring from STL at 86 points.
recommendations.rationale: Speed and faceoffs in one package at $600K. POTE 94 at 24 with 70 points this season means he could grow into a top-nine wing. STL at 86 points with only 8 expiring are less motivated but at this price any offer is hard to refuse.

recommendations.summary: Sign Belanger as UFA if Avery falls through: 82 base, FACE 96, age 27, 19 pts/73 GP, $700K expiring from LA at 79 points.
recommendations.rationale: Pure faceoff centre at $700K. The coach's April 28 flag demands someone who wins draws on the fourth line; Belanger at 96 FACE is the best in the pool. Zero toughness contribution though, so he is a complement not a solution.

recommendations.summary: Offer CGY: Spezza (21, POTE 99, $1.00M) + Koltsov (24, POTE 94, $1.10M) + our only 4th-rounder for Iginla (27, 93 base, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring).
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain a $6.50M expiring star. They shed $4.40M net and receive two players under 25 with POTE 99 and 94 under team control for two years. Spezza's value is highest now while POTE 99 remains credible; the coach has flagged his stagnation six times. Iginla closes the RW scoring void (140 pts vs Mogilny's 84 and declining) and raises the team toughness ceiling from 75 to 85 in one move.

recommendations.summary: Offer CHI: Colaiacovo (22, D, POTE 99, $1.10M, 12pts/31GP) for Bell (24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, $900K).
recommendations.rationale: Bell is the only league-wide player closing both the toughness void (88 TOUG where our best is Jackman at 75) and the faceoff void (82 FACE where Sundin at 90 is 34) simultaneously. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit are the most motivated sellers per the March 30 finding. Colaiacovo is surplus at D (31 games, 12 points, behind Jackman, McCabe, Klesla, Eminger) and carries the highest POTE grade we can give without selling the core. No pick needed if the Iginla deal claims the 4th.

recommendations.summary: Offer SJ: Abid (25, 66pts/82GP, POTE 94, $0.40M, 1yr) + Tucker (30, $1.30M, 2yr) for Stuart (25, 87 base, 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG, POTE 91, $1.80M expiring).
recommendations.rationale: Roberts at 38 walks and leaves a hole at 87 base on the top pair with zero TOUG 80 on any blueliner. Stuart fills both gaps in one move and is two years older than Jackman. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring on $45.39M payroll cannot keep all of them, but at 76 they are not tanking and the March 30 note explicitly flagged they may hold a POTE 91 D. Abid gives them 66 points at $0.40M; the coach's April 28 lineup does not include him. Tucker adds veteran depth for two years.

recommendations.summary: If no trade lands, sign Cammalleri (22, POTE 98, 60pts/61GP, $1.10M) as a UFA in July.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 79 points with 14 expiring cannot retain both him and Frolov. At $1.10M and POTE 98 he is the highest-value UFA available. This is a floor guarantee, not a ceiling replacement for the Iginla or Bell targets.

recommendations.summary: Goalie monitoring task (#2) is complete and closed per GM order of 2005-03-19; Luongo is on the roster at 94 with two years left.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo was acquired and placed on the roster. The GM closed all goalie monitoring on March 19. The February trade window this job served has passed. No further monitoring is warranted or requested.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza real games or stop dressing him next camp. The half-measure is hurting him.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99, morale 88 (lowest of the young group), 46 games at 56% share on 6.7 MPG and 0.33 pts/g. He went from 9.1 to 4.8 MPG in his recent window. At 21 he needs either a consistent role or a clear signal he's not in the plan.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev produces at 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG and is scratched while Chistov and Upshall (both 0.29) dress ahead of him. This mismatch needs resolving next season.
recommendations.rationale: He outproduces two dressed wingers by nearly double at 55 games and 67% share. At 23 with POTE 94 he's old enough to contribute now, not just develop. The offseason decision is whether he's a winger in the plan or not.

recommendations.summary: Chlup is getting the games and minutes his production has earned. No change needed.
recommendations.rationale: 71 games at 87% share, 16.9 MPG, 59 points at 0.83 pts/g on the second line at 19, morale 98. Everything is where it should be.

recommendations.summary: Decide next camp whether Colaiacovo needs 60+ games to develop or whether the rotation is enough.
recommendations.rationale: 31 games at 38% share but 17.9 MPG and 0.39 pts/g when in. At POTE 99 and 22, a 38% season is either fine for development or a stagnation risk. The quality of minutes when he plays is good; the volume is the question.

recommendations.summary: Sell McCabe this offseason. 0.48 pts/g across 82 games at 29 on $3.00M x 4 puts him well below the 0.60 sell threshold.
recommendations.rationale: His 1.42 early pace was a 24-game anomaly. The full-season 0.48 confirms he is past peak. His remaining value is the cheap years relative to what he was.

recommendations.summary: Assign Chlup to the first line for next season. 0.88 pts/g at 19 on 18.2 MPG earns it.
recommendations.rationale: This recommendation was not taken in April. The end-of-season data confirms it: he went from 0.62 to 0.88 while minutes nearly doubled. He has earned the top job.

recommendations.summary: Afinogenov needs an offseason system-fit review. 1.17→0.73 pts/g on flat minutes at 25 is a decline where the direction should be up.
recommendations.rationale: No role change, no minutes change, rate down 37%. Same category as Richards. Determine before camp whether the system or the player is the problem.

recommendations.summary: All three 21-year-olds need a real camp audition next season. Their season rates collapsed simultaneously when minutes were cut.
recommendations.rationale: Spacek 0.55→0.28, Spezza 0.43→0.24, Upshall 0.33→0.27, all with minutes gutted. The pattern is systemic. Either give them real ice in camp or stop dressing them.

recommendations.summary: No change. Kaberle at 0.62 pts/g on rising minutes is the one defenceman improving.
recommendations.rationale: 0.54→0.62 on 19.4→21.5 MPG. He handles load. The GM already named him a keeper; the data confirms it.

recommendations.summary: No morale intervention needed for Pittsburgh; every dressed player is at 98 or above and Spezza at 88 is trending up.
recommendations.rationale: Lowest morale on the roster is Spezza at 88 (one-point grade penalty, not a crisis). Everyone in the lineup sits 98-100. Upshall and Spacek at 91 are both improving. Nothing to fix tonight.

recommendations.summary: No lineup change tonight; all units are built from players who suit their roles.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has the faceoff anchor (Sundin 91) and the scorer (Mogilny 94). L2 has Chlup at 80 draws. K2 at checking mean 84 is the correct grinding unit versus K1's transition game. PP1 carries three 90+ playmakers. Nothing to fix for a 24-34 Pittsburgh club.

recommendations.summary: We have no forward with checking above 85 outside Roberts, so we can only field one heavy kill unit.
recommendations.rationale: Role inventory: Jackman 90 (D), Roberts 85, McCabe 85, Fischer 85. Among forwards only Roberts clears 85. L4 faceoff mean is 52 with best 55. A true third-pair shutdown line does not exist on this roster in any arrangement. Offseason trade target: a two-way centre with checking 85+ and faceoffs 52%+.

recommendations.summary: Run the standard lines. Our auto-pairing puts Fischer/Jackman against Lemieux and our depth dwarfs theirs at every position.
recommendations.rationale: We are 7-1-0 against PIT this season (32-19 goals). Their PP is 11.6% (32/276). Their top line is Lemieux at 39 with OVR 88 but CHKG 66 and TOUG 61. Fischer and Jackman at CHKG 92 each handle him. No tactical mismatch exists in any direction.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at OVR 94 and morale 100 against a 2.20 GF/game team. Per the GM's standing order, verify no tired icon before confirming.

recommendations.summary: Sell Jackman this offseason; 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG at $0.70M x 3 is the cheapest top-pair minutes available to any buyer.
recommendations.rationale: Final season rate locked at 0.46 pts/g across 80 games on the highest minutes load in the league. His only value is the contract.

recommendations.summary: Sell Klesla this offseason; 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG is two consecutive declining seasons with no recovery signal.
recommendations.rationale: Age 23, $0.90M x 2. Production slid from 0.38 to 0.37 with flat minutes. No path to improvement visible.

recommendations.summary: Move Eminger before July 1 or lose him for nothing; 0.36 pts/g on 64 GP at age 21 with an expiring deal.
recommendations.rationale: Rate locked at 0.36. Contract expires. After July he is a UFA loss.

recommendations.summary: The toughness and faceoff gaps are structural (0 at 80+ TOUG, 1 at 80+ FACE) and can only be closed by acquiring Bell or Avery this summer.
recommendations.rationale: Bell at 88 TOUG / 86 CHKG / 82 FACE closes both gaps in one player at age 24. Avery at 93 FACE / 83 TOUG / 88 CHKG at $400K is cheaper but at 25 his POTE is lower. Neither fix is available from the current roster.

recommendations.summary: Mogilny's departure removes the best scorer (94 SHPW) and the top shot-power player from the roster; a top-6 wing must be acquired in July.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny (36, 94 SHPW, 0.83 pts/g) is leaving with no internal replacement above 92 SHPW. Iginla (CGY, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, TOUG 85) closes scoring and toughness simultaneously per the April 12 note.

recommendations.summary: Roberts leaves with 86 CHKG and 98 INJU; Stuart at 87 base and 89 CHKG replaces both the checking and durability with eight years of runway.
recommendations.rationale: After Roberts, only Jackman 87 and McCabe 86 remain above 80 CHKG on defence. Stuart (SJ, 25, POTE 91) at 89 CHKG / 80 TOUG fills the slot with youth. SJ's 13 expiring contracts make them a possible seller.

recommendations.summary: Speed (21 at 80+), stamina (11 at 80+), playmaking (10 at 80+ post-Mogilny) and clutch (7 at 80+ post-exits) are all adequately covered; no action needed on these axes.
recommendations.rationale: These four roles have depth even after Mogilny and Roberts depart. The club's problem is not breadth but the specific holes at toughness and faceoffs.

recommendations.summary: Chlup at FACE 75 and age 19 is the best internal faceoff option after Sundin; his development as a draw-taker should be tracked but cannot close the gap this season.
recommendations.rationale: The coach already moved Chlup to the first line for scoring (0.83 pts/g at 19). His 75 FACE is the next-best on the roster but 15 points below Sundin. He could develop toward 80+ over two seasons but is not a fix now.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik to a 5-6 year deal on July 1 — 99 points at 23 on $1.10M is the most undervalued contract in the league and the single most urgent move this summer.
recommendations.rationale: He will command $4-6M on a new deal. A 5-year lock at $3-4M saves millions over his career and eliminates any bidding risk.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards to a 5-6 year deal — 66 points at 24 on $1.00M, the cheapest centre production in the league.
recommendations.rationale: He is the second-oldest player in the young core at 24 and the second-cheapest. His price triples the moment he tests the market.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash to a 5-6 year deal — 39 points at age 20 with POTE 95 is a franchise winger who will cost $4M+ in a year.
recommendations.rationale: The manual says lock stars on 5-6 years immediately. Nash at 20 with that potential and that salary is the definition of a rookie-window lock.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger to a 5-6 year deal — 21 years old, POTE 99, $1.20M. Lock him before he proves it and the price rises.
recommendations.rationale: He had 23 points in 64 games as a rookie at 21. His potential is the highest on the roster. The cost of a lock now versus a market deal later is enormous.

recommendations.summary: Extend Chlup from 2 remaining years to 5-6 total — 59 points at 19, POTE 95, $2.34M. Do this in July alongside the expiring deals.
recommendations.rationale: He is in the 2006 cluster. Extending now splits the renewal load across two summers and captures his pre-breakout price.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle to a 3-4 year deal — 44 points at 27 on $1.90M is fair value but not a franchise long-term piece.
recommendations.rationale: Colaiacovo (POTE 99, 22) and Stahle (POTE 96, 21) need runway. Three years covers the transition. Five years risks being locked to a declining blueliner.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Abid to a 3-4 year deal — 66 points in 82 games on $0.40M is the cheapest production on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: He fills the toughness void the Coach flagged and costs nothing. Release him only if you can find his replacement for free, which you cannot.

recommendations.summary: Release Upshall — 20 points in 68 games at 21 with POTE 99 is a stalled prospect whose potential has not converted over two full seasons of top-nine ice.
recommendations.rationale: Same POTE as Nash and Eminger but 39 and 23 points respectively versus 20. The development has stalled; the coach flagged it explicitly.

recommendations.summary: Extend Luongo to 4-5 years in July — 91 base at 26, $1.60M, the franchise goalie. Do not let him reach the market at 28.
recommendations.rationale: He is in the 2006 cluster. Extending now avoids a bidding war in two years and locks the position that the Jan 15 mandate was designed to solve.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla in July — 93 base, 140 points in 73 GP, TOUG 85, age 27, $6.50M expiring from a 70-point Calgary club with $14.43M profit.
recommendations.rationale: He closes the Mogilny scoring void and the structural toughness ceiling in one signing. The payroll ($35.74M profit) easily absorbs him.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik on 5-6 years as the first July transaction; he is 91 base at 23 on $1.10M and will be untouchable once his market opens.
recommendations.rationale: 87 points in 82 games at age 23 with only $1.10M owed. Every club needs a 91-rated RW; letting him reach the open market risks losing him for nothing.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards on 5-6 years immediately after Gaborik; he is 24 with 64 points on $1.00M and centres are the scarcest position on the market.
recommendations.rationale: The March 21 renewal priority order puts him second. At 24 he is entering his prime and the club has no replacement at any price.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash on 5-6 years in July before his production rises and his asking price follows.
recommendations.rationale: He is 20 on $1.20M with no trade demand. The 2004-12-17 staggered-locks plan already flags him for 5-6 years.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger on 5-6 years; POTE 99 at 21 on $1.20M is the cheapest long-term defence piece the club will have.
recommendations.rationale: The GM protected Eminger over Chara in January specifically because of his upside. Lock him before a breakout year triples his cost.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle on 2-3 years; 27, 85 base, $1.90M is solid but his ceiling is set and star length is wasted.
recommendations.rationale: He is productive but at 27 the 5-6 year rule does not apply. Shorter deal keeps flexibility if Stuart or another young D arrives.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Abid on 2-3 years; 80 TOUG and 80 CHKG at $0.40M fills the structural toughness gap the Coach flagged at 57 mean.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach wants him in the top six. At 0.70 pts/g he earns it, and $0.40M is the cheapest quality roster player on the club.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Alexeev on 2 years; 0.55 pts/g is nearly double Chistov and Upshall, and the Coach explicitly prefers him.
recommendations.rationale: He is 23 on $1.10M and the Coach flagged dressing him over both Chistov and Upshall. Two years lets the club see if the rate holds.

recommendations.summary: Let Belfour walk; he is 40, $6.50M, and the GM already established he will not accept a reduced deal.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 94 base on $1.60M with 2 years left is the answer. Ouellet at 82 base on $900K and Tellqvist provide depth. The $6.50M freed funds the young-core locks.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk at 38; 0.86 pts/g is finished production and $2.70M is better spent elsewhere.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach's own report says 'plan the wings around Mogilny and Roberts exiting.' At 38 with a two-year deal still on the books, he is a rental the GM chose not to renew last year.

recommendations.summary: Do not renew Upshall; POTE 99 on 0.29 pts/g across 8 MPG over two seasons is a stalled prospect, not a future contributor.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach issued an ultimatum: top-nine in camp or he drops from the dressing list. The club should not pay $1.20M+ for a third-year player who has never earned above 8 minutes a night.

recommendations.summary: Do not renew Chistov; Alexeev outproduces him (0.55 vs 0.29 pts/g) at the same age and the Coach prefers him.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach explicitly says dress Alexeev over Chistov. Paying both at $1.10M is redundant when one is outscoring the other nearly 2-to-1.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla in July via trade or free agency; 93 base at 27 with TOUG 85 closes the Mogilny scoring void and the toughness ceiling simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Calgary are 26-43-8 at 70 points with $14.43M profit and cannot retain him. He is the highest-value player available anywhere in the 2005 summer.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bell from Chicago; 82 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE at 24 is the only league-wide player closing both toughness and faceoff gaps simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Chicago are 25-36-14, 78 points, $31.73M profit and are motivated sellers. Tucker at 80 base and $1.30M plus the 4th-rounder is the starting package.

recommendations.summary: Monitor Cammalleri as a UFA signing; POTE 98 at 22 on $1.10M expiring from a 79-point club that cannot retain him and Frolov.
recommendations.rationale: LA have $52.43M payroll at 79 points. If he clears, he is the highest-potential player on the open market and costs one roster spot.

recommendations.summary: No moves during the playoffs. Tucker stays available as the only chip if a rival-weakness package emerges, but the GM's March 19 order locks the roster.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto are 1st in the East at 133 points with Belfour and Luongo at 90+ in net. The job now is winning the Cup, not reshaping.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, SHPW 99, TOUG 85, 128 pts/82 GP, $6.50M expiring) via July trade or UFA signing.
recommendations.rationale: He closes the Mogilny scoring void (SHPW 99 vs 94) and raises the toughness ceiling from 75 to 85 in one move. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit must sell.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Havlat (OTT, LW, 24, 87 base, SHPW 95, 103 pts/82 GP, $900K expiring) at UFA.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 77 points with 11 expiring cannot retain him. He is the cheapest top-six scorer on the board and plays either wing, giving lineup flexibility alongside Iginla or Gaborik.

recommendations.summary: Sign Belanger (LA, C, 27, 82 base, FACE 96, $700K expiring) at UFA.
recommendations.rationale: He is the only player in the league with FACE above 95 under age 30. The Coach flagged no fifth centre who wins faceoffs on April 26; Belanger at 96 draws solves it for $700K. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring will not re-sign him.

recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri (LA, LW/C, 22, POTE 98, 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M expiring) at UFA.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 79 points cannot retain both him and Frolov. At 22 with POTE 98 on a rookie deal he is the highest-ceiling available player. Development risk is real but the price is minimal.

recommendations.slot: centre or left wing, top six
recommendations.summary: Sign Marleau (SJ, C/LW, 25, 89 base, 98 pts, $1.60M expiring) at UFA.
recommendations.rationale: SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring cannot keep him. He is arrived, not a project, and fills a top-six spot at a below-market salary. Competition in free agency is the risk.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Heatley (ATL, RW, 24, 91 base, SHPW 95, 131 pts/79 GP, $1.10M expiring) only if ATL re-signs Kovalchuk over him.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring must choose between Kovalchuk (22, 138 pts) and Heatley (24, 131 pts). The younger player is the logical keep, making Heatley available. He is conditional, so Havlat is the primary fallback.

recommendations.slot: right wing or left wing, second line
recommendations.summary: Acquire Deadmarsh (LA, RW, 29, 89 base, TOUG 82, SHPW 93, $2.80M, one year left) via summer trade with LA.
recommendations.rationale: He adds toughness (82) and scoring (SHPW 93) simultaneously. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring will deal him rather than lose him in 2006. Age 29 means three useful years, not five.

recommendations.summary: Acquire McLaren (SJ, D, 27, 82 base, TOUG 89, CHKG 93, $2.20M, one year left) via summer trade with SJ.
recommendations.rationale: TOUG 89 and CHKG 93 make him the toughest available blueliner from a seller. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring on $45.39M payroll are shedding. He is not a PP quarterback but he is the physical presence our D has never had.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Barnaby (NYR, LW, 31, 82 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 89, $1.50M, one year left) via summer trade.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach's fourth-line toughness mean is 57. Barnaby at 88 TOUG and 89 CHKG is the only player on the board who moves that number by double digits. NYR at 84 points with $0.00 profit are distressed sellers.

recommendations.summary: Attempt a summer trade for Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82, $900K, two years left) using Tucker plus a Belfour-mechanic pick.
recommendations.rationale: He closes toughness, checking, and faceoffs in one player at age 24 on a $900K deal. CHI at 78 points with $31.73M profit are not desperate, so acceptance is uncertain. The package is the constraint, not the fit.

recommendations.proposed: Havlat (LW/RW, 24, 87 base, SHPW 95, 103 pts/82 GP, $900K, expiring)
recommendations.summary: Trade Tucker and the 4th-rounder to Ottawa for Havlat, then re-sign him to a 4-5 year deal at $3-4M in July.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 77 points with 11 expiring contracts cannot retain Havlat; Tucker's 92 CHKG gives them a bottom-six checker and the 4th is a lottery ticket for a full rebuild. We replace Mogilny's 84 pts/78 GP with 103 pts/82 GP at $400K less payroll and gain ten years of development runway.

recommendations.current: Tucker (LW, 30, $1.30M, 2 yrs, CHKG 92, TOUG 88) + Koltsov (LW, 24, POTE 94, ACCE 96, AGIL 92, $1.10M, 2 yrs)
recommendations.proposed: Bell (LW, 24, 82 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82, $900K, 2 yrs)
recommendations.summary: If the GM releases Koltsov, trade him and Tucker to Chicago for Bell to close toughness and faceoffs simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Bell is the only league-wide player with TOUG 88, CHKG 86, and FACE 82 at age 24 on $900K. CHI at 78 points with $31.73M profit have no forced move, so acceptance is uncertain. This requires Koltsov at POTE 94 as the centerpiece or CHI has no reason to move a 24-year-old with two years left.

recommendations.proposed: Belanger (C, 27, 82 base, FACE 96, $700K, expiring from LA)
recommendations.summary: Sign Belanger as a UFA in July for FACE 96 at $700K — the cheapest gap-closer in the league.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach flagged 'no fifth centre who wins faceoffs' on April 26; L4's best draw is at 55. Belanger at FACE 96 on $700K solves this without any trade asset. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring cannot retain all of them. This is the fallback if no trade lands.

recommendations.proposed: Cammalleri (LW/RW, 22, POTE 98, 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M, expiring from LA)
recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri as a UFA in July — 22 years old, POTE 98, rookie salary, LA cannot retain both him and Frolov.
recommendations.rationale: Highest-ceiling player on the free agent board at a cost that barely moves payroll. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring must choose between him and Frolov; Frolov's higher floor likely wins. Risk is development failure, but at $1.10M the downside is one year of a roster spot.

recommendations.summary: Goalie trade monitoring task is formally closed per the GM's March 19 order; Luongo is on the roster at 94 with 2 years left, DiPietro is eliminated at 79 base.
recommendations.rationale: The GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19. Luongo arrived at 94/$1.60M/2yrs. DiPietro reads 79 base at 52 GP, well below the 90+ threshold set January 15. No open question remains.

recommendations.summary: Dress Alexeev and take Chistov's spot for the remaining 4 games.
recommendations.rationale: Alexeev is 0.55 pts/g in 55 games versus Chistov's 0.29 in 68. At 0-34 PIT these are the games to test whether he can hold a regular role.

recommendations.summary: No further changes for Spezza, Stahle, or Colaiacovo — their cases are for camp, not these 4 games.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza (0.33 pts/g, 6.7 MPG), Stahle (0 points in 4 GP), and Colaiacovo (0.39 in 31 GP) do not clear the bar over current roster players in a four-game window.

recommendations.summary: Spacek at 19, 7.6 MPG, 0.34 pts/g on the fourth line is a fair development pace. Leave him.
recommendations.rationale: Age-appropriate minutes and role for a 19-year-old. No mismatch in either direction.

recommendations.summary: Assign Chlup to the first-line centre slot for next season based on his 0.88 pts/g at 19 on 18.2 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: His rate rose 42 percent while minutes nearly doubled, the opposite of what happens to most 19-year-olds under increased load. He is the team's best forward under 25.

recommendations.summary: McCabe goes back on the sell list: 0.48 pts/g over 82 games is well below the 0.60 threshold set March 30.
recommendations.rationale: His early-season 1.42 pace over 24 games was the anomaly, not the norm. At 29 with 4 years and $3.00M he is expensive for a third-pairing defenceman.

recommendations.summary: Klesla is a confirmed sell after two consecutive declining seasons: 0.31 at 23, down from 0.38 at 22, on flat 15 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: Two years of decline with no role change rules out a system-fit excuse. His $0.90M x 2 is recoverable only while he is still young enough to trade as a project.

recommendations.summary: Flag Richards for an offseason system-fit review: 1.08 to 0.71 pts/g on flat minutes at age 24.
recommendations.rationale: At 24 the expected direction is up. A 34 percent rate drop with no change in role or minutes is unexplained and must be diagnosed before camp.

recommendations.summary: Spacek had a lost season (0.28 pts/g, 5.2 MPG at 19). Camp assignment is the only lever left.
recommendations.rationale: His minutes collapsed from 16.0 to 5.2 and his rate halved. No in-season move can fix this; it is an offseason audition or stop dressing.

recommendations.summary: Kaberle is trending up at 27 (0.54 to 0.62 pts/g on rising minutes). Protect him; no change needed.
recommendations.rationale: More load and a better rate simultaneously is the signature of a defenceman entering his prime. The GM's January call to keep him was right.

recommendations.summary: No morale intervention needed tonight. The room is at 98-100 across the board and everything is trending up.
recommendations.rationale: Every dressed player is at 98 or 100 with positive movement. The only sub-90 man is Spezza at 88 (up 3) on 6.7 MPG, and he is a scratch with rising morale. No minutes adjustment improves this room before Pittsburgh.

recommendations.summary: All units are correctly composed for tonight. Leave the lines as they are.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has checking (83 mean) plus elite offense. L3 has Nash at 94 checking and Chistov at 98 speed. L4's faceoff weakness (52 mean) is tolerable against a 24-34 opponent. K1 keeps Sundin's 91 faceoff for draw wins on the kill.

recommendations.summary: We need a centre who wins faceoffs on the fourth line; the roster has nobody.
recommendations.rationale: L4 faceoff mean is 52, best 55. The only centres on the roster who win draws are Sundin (91), Chlup (80), and Richards (75), all needed on top lines. No lineup change fixes this.

recommendations.summary: Move Mogilny to first-line right wing, Chistov to second-line right wing, Upshall to third-line right wing. Fourth line becomes three-man.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik is out until June. Mogilny at 90 OVR is the only winger who can handle Lemieux's first line (PASS 99, PUCK 95, DEKG 98) alongside Sundin and Roberts. Chistov at 82 bumps to second, Upshall at 79 to third.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo. His fatigue icon is clear.
recommendations.rationale: Query q73 shows no streak icon on Luongo. At 94 OVR with 99 glove he handles a 2.20 goals-per-game opponent without concern.

recommendations.summary: Leave D pair slot order as is: Fischer/Jackman first, Kaberle/McCabe second, Eminger/Klesla third.
recommendations.rationale: Fischer/Jackman (CHKG 92, SPEE 94) on pair 1 are already matched against Lemieux's first line. PIT's second and third lines (Eastwood 69, Holzinger 76) are below our second and third pairs.

recommendations.summary: Sell Jackman this offseason. Final line is 37 points in 80 on 29.6 MPG, 0.46 pts/g, $0.70M x 3.
recommendations.rationale: Second straight season below 0.50 with the highest minutes load on the roster. His value to a buyer is top-pair minutes at a bargain rate.

recommendations.summary: Sell Klesla. 30 points in 82, 0.37 pts/g, second consecutive decline, $0.90M x 2.
recommendations.rationale: Rate fell from 0.38 to 0.37 with no change in role. Two more years on the contract means we can get something back now.

recommendations.summary: Trade Eminger before July. 23 points in 64, 0.36 pts/g, $1.20M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: After July he is a UFA loss at zero return. At 21 he has trade value to a rebuild.

recommendations.summary: Kaberle's contract expires this summer. Renewal is the priority on this blue line.
recommendations.rationale: 44 points in 74 on 20.8 MPG at 27. GM named him a star and a keeper. Losing him in UFA would gut the top pair alongside McCabe's contract years.

recommendations.proposed: Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, $0.90M, 2 years)
recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell from Chicago to close the toughness, checking and faceoff gaps simultaneously; he is the only player in the league who fills all three.
recommendations.rationale: Zero Toronto players carry 80+ TOUG on stored grades; only Sundin (34) exceeds 80 FACE. Bell at 24 with 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG and 82 FACE is the single-player fix. CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring deals and $29.46M profit are motivated sellers.

recommendations.proposed: Avery (LA, C, 25, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2 years)
recommendations.summary: If Bell is out of reach, pursue Avery as the cheaper alternative closing all three structural gaps at $400K salary.
recommendations.rationale: Avery's 93 FACE is 11 points above Bell's 82, and his $400K over two years is half the cost. The trade-off is no scoring upside and weaker skating. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring deals are the most motivated sellers in the league.

recommendations.slot: fourth-line forward or healthy scratch rotation
recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker nightly; at 83 CHKG he is the fourth 80+ checker available and he is currently in no unit.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker's 83 CHKG is the same tier as Fischer (82) and above Upshall (80). After Roberts (86 CHKG, age 38) walks at season's end, Tucker becomes the third-best checker on the roster. The coach's own fourth-line checking mean of 61 says he needs one more body at 80+.

recommendations.proposed: Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla in July; at 93 base with TOUG 85 he closes the RW scoring void left by Mogilny's decline and raises the toughness ceiling by 10 points over the current best.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g at age 36. Iginla at 27 with 140 points in 73 games and TOUG 85 is the only player who replaces the production and the physicality in one move. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring contracts and $14.43M profit cannot retain him.

recommendations.summary: Speed (21 at 80+) and stamina (11 at 80+) are covered; no acquisition needed in either area.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik 98, Afinogenov 96, Mogilny 94, Koltsov 92 at the top of speed. Kaberle 97, McCabe 94, Sundin 92 on stamina. These are the deepest roles on the roster and require no move.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger and Kaberle on 5-6 year deals this July before any of them hits free agency.
recommendations.rationale: All five expire in the same July 2005 cluster worth $21.30M. Gaborik scored 99 points on $1.10M, Richards 66 on $1.00M, Nash 39 on $1.20M with POTE 95, Eminger is 21 with POTE 99, Kaberle is 27 on $1.90M. If these walk, the core disintegrates in one summer.

recommendations.summary: Extend Chlup from his 2-year deal to 5-6 years before his rookie-window price of $2.34M disappears after a full top-nine season.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup is 19 with POTE 95, rising from 0.62 to 0.88 pts/g as minutes doubled from 11.0 to 18.2. The coach confirmed him as first-line centre for 2005-06. A 2-year deal means he hits the market at 21 coming off a breakout season.

recommendations.proposed: Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, $6.50M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Sign Iginla as a July UFA to close both the Mogilny scoring void and the structural toughness ceiling in one move.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny fell to 0.79 pts/g at 36 and has 2 years left at $5.50M. Iginla at 27 delivers 1.92 pts/g with TOUG 85, entering his prime. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him. Toronto's $35.74M profit covers a $6.50M-$7M salary.

recommendations.proposed: Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81)
recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell from Chicago to close the toughness (mean 57) and faceoff (50%) voids the coach quantified.
recommendations.rationale: No Toronto player carries 80+ TOUG in stored grades. Bell closes both gaps at 24 with POTE 81. Chicago at 73 points with 10 expiring contracts and $29.46M profit are motivated sellers. Toronto holds only a 4th-round pick, so the package needs a young body — Koltsov or Alexeev (both POTE 94, scratched, 1-2 years remaining).

recommendations.summary: The age curve and payroll structure are sound; the 30-33 gap and the 55.5% payroll-to-revenue ratio leave room for the moves above without financial strain.
recommendations.rationale: Payroll $60.04M against $108.20M revenue with $35.74M profit. After locking the young core and adding Iginla at $6.50M, payroll rises to roughly $75-80M, still under 75% of revenue. The shape — 13 players at 23 or under, 12 in 24-29 — matches the manual's target.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik on a 5-6 year deal the moment free agency opens.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base, age 23, POTE 90, currently at $1.10M. A 5-6 year lock is cheaper than a July bidding war.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards on a 5-6 year deal immediately after Gaborik.
recommendations.rationale: 24 years old, $1.00M expiring. Core centre of the future; same lock logic as Gaborik.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash on 5-6 years.
recommendations.rationale: Age 20, $1.20M expiring. GM protected him from selling on Feb 19; he is a foundation piece.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger on 5-6 years.
recommendations.rationale: Age 21, POTE 99, $1.20M expiring. GM vetoed selling him on Jan 19 and Feb 19; he is the defensive future.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle on 2-3 years.
recommendations.rationale: Age 27, $1.90M. Still a productive top-pair D but the salary and age say shorter term; saves against the 2007-08 cluster.

recommendations.summary: Let Belfour walk in July. No trade window remains.
recommendations.rationale: Age 40, $6.50M. GM closed the trade question on March 19. Frees $6.50M for summer targets.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk in July.
recommendations.rationale: Age 38, $2.70M. GM confirmed he walks on March 21. Stuart (SJ, 87 base, POTE 91) is the summer replacement.

recommendations.summary: Do not re-sign Upshall.
recommendations.rationale: Age 21, 0.29 pts/g, $1.20M. Coach flagged him on April 23 for camp-or-cut and his production does not justify the salary.

recommendations.summary: Do not re-sign Chistov.
recommendations.rationale: Age 22, 0.29 pts/g, $1.10M. Outproduced by Alexeev (0.55) who is on the same salary; one fringe winger is enough.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Colaiacovo on 3-5 years at $1.10M or below.
recommendations.rationale: Age 22, D, cheap depth. Keeps the defensive prospect pool intact without meaningful payroll cost.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Tellqvist on 3-5 years.
recommendations.rationale: GM ordered on Jan 15: potential high 90s, give him time. $0.80M salary. Backup behind Luongo and Belfour's replacement.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Abid on 2-3 years.
recommendations.rationale: $0.40M, age 25, the cheapest 80 TOUG / 80 CHKG player on the roster. Keep for playoff depth.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bell (CHI) in free agency: closes toughness AND faceoff gaps simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, age 24, POTE 81. The coach quantified the fourth-line gap at TOUG 57 mean, FACE 50. Bell fixes both. CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring are motivated sellers if a trade is possible in the offseason.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Stuart (SJ) as Roberts' replacement: 87 base, POTE 91, age 25.
recommendations.rationale: SJ at 72 points with 13 expiring on $45.39M cannot retain all of them. Stuart at 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG gives eight years of elite-pair defence at the position Roberts leaves.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Cammalleri (LA) in free agency: highest-ceiling UFA at POTE 98, age 22.
recommendations.rationale: 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M expiring. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring cannot retain both him and Frolov. If he signs elsewhere, the scoring void Mogilny leaves is unfilled.

recommendations.summary: If Iginla hits the market (CGY, 27, 93 base, TOUG 85), pursue aggressively over Heatley or Doan.
recommendations.rationale: Closes both the RW scoring void (Mogilny at 0.79 pts/g in decline) and the structural toughness ceiling (85 TOUG on a 93-base player). CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Alexeev only if he accepts 2 years at $1.10M or below; otherwise let go.
recommendations.rationale: Age 23, 0.55 pts/g, best of the three fringe wingers but still below roster standard. Two years hedges the upside without blocking a Bell or Cammalleri signing.

recommendations.summary: Make Iginla the July signing priority: he closes the RW scoring void and the toughness ceiling together.
recommendations.rationale: 27, 93 base, 140 points in 73 games (1.92 pts/g), TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring. Calgary finished 70 points with 10 expiring deals and $14.43M profit and cannot retain him.

recommendations.summary: Primary target: the only league player closing faceoffs, checking and toughness in one body.
recommendations.rationale: 24, 80 base, showing 93 CHKG, 95 TOUG, 87 FACE, $0.90M with two years, 28 points in 80 games. Chicago at 78 points with 10 expiring deals and $31.73M profit are motivated sellers; Koltsov is the chip.

recommendations.summary: Add Stuart to replace Roberts' checking minutes on the back end.
recommendations.rationale: 25, 87 base, SPEE 94, CHKG 83, 52 points in 77 games at 30.8 minutes, $1.80M with one year left. San Jose at 76 points with 13 expiring deals and $20.74M profit cannot keep all of them. TOUG 74 falls short of the 80 toughness line, so this is a core add not the toughness fix.

recommendations.summary: Cheap faceoff floor if Bell cannot be had.
recommendations.rationale: 30, 74 base, FACE 87, CHKG 82, $0.40M and expiring, 4 points in 66 games at 8.7 minutes. A specialist draw-taker for the fourth line at no acquisition cost beyond a July deal.

recommendations.summary: Depth checking centre only, not a top target.
recommendations.rationale: 26, 73 base, FACE 81, CHKG 92, TOUG 84, $0.94M with two years. ENDU 50 means he cannot hold a shift, so he is a spare body until that recovers.

recommendations.current: Koltsov (LW, 24, POTE 94, $1.10M, 2 yrs) + Tucker (LW, 30, CHKG 92, TOUG 88, $1.30M, 2 yrs)
recommendations.proposed: Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, $0.90M, 2 yrs)
recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell from Chicago for Koltsov plus Tucker, closing faceoffs, checking and toughness in one move and saving $1.50M against the July cliff.
recommendations.rationale: Bell is the only league player covering FACE 82, CHKG 86 and TOUG 88 simultaneously at age 24. Chicago at 78 points with 10 expiring deals and $31.73M profit prefer Koltsov's POTE 94 over Bell's POTE 81 for their rebuild window. Koltsov is scratched behind Chlup, Richards, Spacek and Alexeev at centre.

recommendations.current: Alexeev (RW, 23, POTE 94, $1.10M, 1 yr) + Colaiacovo (D, 22, POTE 99, $1.10M, 1 yr)
recommendations.proposed: Stuart (SJ, D, 25, 87 base, POTE 91, SPEE 94, CHKG 83, 52 pts/77 GP, $1.80M, 1 yr)
recommendations.summary: Acquire Stuart from San Jose for Alexeev and Colaiacovo, replacing Roberts' 30.8-minute checking minutes with eight years of runway, contingent on Iginla signing first.
recommendations.rationale: Stuart at 87 base and POTE 91 fills the Roberts void at age 25 with SPEE 94 and 52 points in 77 games. San Jose at 76 points with 13 expiring deals on $45.39M cannot retain all of them. Alexeev becomes surplus if Iginla signs at RW; trading him before then guts a position the coach already flagged as thin.

recommendations.summary: If Bell does not land, sign Nichol as a UFA faceoff specialist for the fourth line at $0.40M with no acquisition cost.
recommendations.rationale: Nichol's 87 FACE and 82 CHKG at $0.40M is the cheapest faceoff solution on the board. He is 30 with no development upside, so he is a stopgap, not a plan, but he closes the coach's 60 FACE threshold at zero draft-pick cost.

recommendations.proposed: Roberts (38, ~82 base, $2.70M expiring) traded to a non-contender for a draft pick
