recommendations.summary: Use the over-80 expiring mechanic on Roberts to generate a draft pick before he walks, since Toronto holds only a fourth-rounder.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts at approximately 82 base with INJU 98 and TOUG 92 is above 80 and expiring, and the renewal order says he walks. The guide states any over-80 player not being re-signed can be traded for a pick. This is the only source of pick capital available this summer.

recommendations.summary: Retire owed item #2 — Luongo is on the roster at 94, DiPietro is eliminated at 79, and the GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19.
recommendations.rationale: The task's premise (a goalie trade window still open in February) expired when Luongo arrived. The GM explicitly closed the topic twice: first on 2005-02-19 ('Goalies are solved. Done.') and again on 2005-03-19 ('Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks.').

recommendations.summary: Move Chlup to the first line immediately — 0.83 pts/g at 19 on 16.9 MPG earns Gaborik's linemate slot, not second-line minutes.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup's 59 points in 71 games trails only Gaborik's 99 in 82 on the roster. Gaborik gets 20.5 MPG on L1; Chlup gets 16.9 on L2. At 19 with morale 98 and POTE 95, he has outgrown the second line.

recommendations.summary: Dress Alexeev over Chistov or Upshall for the remaining games — his 0.55 pts/g is nearly double their 0.29.
recommendations.rationale: Alexeev has 30 points in 55 games, outproducing both dressed wingers he'd replace. His morale is 92 but sitting this long with this rate is the kind of thing that drops it. The remaining games cost nothing to use him.

recommendations.summary: Spezza gets a top-nine audition in camp or stops being a roster project — POTE 99 wasted on 6.7 MPG and 0.33 pts/g.
recommendations.rationale: Highest scouting number on the club, lowest young-player morale at 88, season rate collapsed to 0.33. The regular-season minutes are gone; camp is the last lever before his next contract year starts.

recommendations.summary: Stahle needs a camp audition — POTE 96 and four games in 82 means the club has never evaluated him.
recommendations.rationale: Four appearances is no sample at all. The club is carrying a high-potential defenceman it hasn't looked at.

recommendations.summary: Upshall either earns a real top-nine role in camp or drops from the dressing list — 0.29 pts/g on 7.9 MPG with POTE 99 is a stalled prospect.
recommendations.rationale: Minutes fell from 13.4 to 7.9 across the season while his grade held flat. He's dressed but invisible. Camp or out.

recommendations.summary: McCabe goes back on the sell list. His 58-game recent rate is 0.09 pts/g.
recommendations.rationale: The first 24 games (34 points) masked a collapse. Remaining 58 games produced approximately 5 points on 21.5 MPG. At 29 with 4 years and $3.00M his contract is a liability, not an asset.

recommendations.summary: Chlup keeps the first line permanently. No offseason change.
recommendations.rationale: 0.62 to 0.88 pts/g while minutes rose from 11.0 to 18.2 at age 19. He absorbed a bigger role and got better.

recommendations.summary: Abid needs top-six minutes next season. He produced 0.70 pts/g on 11.5 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: His rate held while minutes were cut from 20.1 to 11.5 across the season. He is 25 and wasting his best years on the fourth line.

recommendations.summary: Spezza and Spacek both need a real training camp audition next season or stop dressing them.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza: 0.24 pts/g on 4.6 MPG. Spacek: 0.28 pts/g on 5.2 MPG. Neither got meaningful games at ages 19-21 with high potential.

recommendations.summary: Plan the wings around Mogilny and Roberts exiting. Mogilny finished 0.83 at 36, Roberts 0.86 at 38.
recommendations.rationale: Both declined as age predicts and will decline further next year. The roster needs two younger wings ready to step in.

recommendations.summary: The room is healthy; every dressed player is at 91 or above and the team's results are carrying morale. No line change needed tonight.
recommendations.rationale: 28 of 30 rostered players sit at 95+. Spezza at 88 is the only man below 90 and he has recovered +5 recently, but he is a healthy scratch with no minutes lever available to me. No pre-game adjustment improves this.

recommendations.summary: Swap Jackman and Kaberle between K1 and K2 so the first kill has our two best checkers together.
recommendations.rationale: K1 checking mean is 79 while K2 is 84; that's backwards. Jackman at 90 checking alongside Roberts (85) and Fischer (85) lifts K1 to roughly 83-84, and K2 keeps McCabe at 85 to anchor.

recommendations.summary: Kaberle to K2 as part of the K1/K2 checking swap.
recommendations.rationale: K2 retains McCabe at 85 checking so it stays competitive even with Kaberle in for Jackman.

recommendations.summary: We have no fifth centre who wins faceoffs. L4's best draw man is at 55, meaning fourth-line shifts consistently start with the puck against us.
recommendations.rationale: Faceoff leaders are Sundin 91, Chlup 80, Roberts 76, Richards 75. Those four are on L1-L3. The fifth centre on L4 maxes at 55. Against a team with a real fourth-line pivot this is a structural mismatch every game.

recommendations.summary: L1 through L3 forwards, both power plays, and the even-strength D pairs are correctly built.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has 83 checking with 92/99 best scoring. L2 trades checking for Mogilny/Afinogenov's 94/92 scoring and is designed as an offensive unit. L3 has Richards at 97 clutch. P1 and P2 both have 87+ scoring and playmaking. No rearrangement improves any of these.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is OVR 94 with morale 100. PIT is a bottom-half team; no reason to roll the backup.

recommendations.summary: No line changes for Pittsburgh.
recommendations.rationale: We are 5-1-0 against them this season (24-14 goals). Their only player above 80 OVR is Lemieux at 88, and our first line auto-pairs against him. Their top D pair reads 77/76 against our first pair at 85/86. Every line is a mismatch in our favour.

recommendations.summary: Sell Jackman this offseason while $0.70M x 3 still attracts suitors; his rate has dropped to 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: Now at 80 GP and 37 points the season rate is 0.46, worse than the 0.48 I flagged March 23. Cheap contract is the only remaining value and every game erodes it further.

recommendations.summary: Sell Klesla this offseason at $0.90M x 2; season locked at 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG, second straight decline.
recommendations.rationale: 82 GP, 30 points. Two consecutive declining seasons confirm this is his ceiling. No development case remains at 23.

recommendations.summary: Move Eminger before July when his contract expires; rate has slid to 0.36 pts/g and four scoreless games since March 30 confirm the slide.
recommendations.rationale: 64 GP, 23 points, $1.2M expiring. Deadline passed so offseason is the last window. After July he walks for nothing.

recommendations.summary: McCabe stays. Season complete at 82 GP, 62 pts, 0.76 pts/g on 22.1 MPG. Case closed.
recommendations.rationale: Clears the 0.60 sell threshold with room. At 29 with 4 years remaining he anchors the top pair. No further re-evaluation needed.

recommendations.summary: Bell remains the single best solution to the toughness and faceoff gaps: 88 TOUG, 82 FACE, 86 CHKG, 24 years old, 82 base.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto has zero players at 80+ TOUG and one at 80+ FACE (Sundin 90). Bell closes both. CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring and $29.46M profit are motivated sellers. ENDU 71 means short shifts initially.

recommendations.summary: Avery at 83 TOUG, 93 FACE, $400K, 2 years left is the cheapest closing of the faceoff gap; his toughness is below Bell's but his draw-winning is elite.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 48 points with 13 expiring deals are motivated sellers. Avery's 93 FACE solves lines 3-4 faceoffs completely. His 83 TOUG is above any current Toronto player but below Bell's 88. If both Bell and Avery are reachable, take Bell; if Bell is too expensive, Avery fills the faceoff void at $400K.

recommendations.summary: Iginla at 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, age 27, closing both the Mogilny scoring void and the structural toughness ceiling (TOUG 85) simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny fell to 0.79 pts/g at 36. Roberts is 38 and expiring. Iginla's TOUG 85 would also raise the club's best stored toughness from 75 to 85, partially addressing the gap without a second acquisition. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him at $6.50M.

recommendations.summary: After Belfour (40, expiring) walks, the backup is Ouellet at INTE 69 and REBC 75 or Tellqvist at REBC 64. Neither is a viable number-two for a contender.
recommendations.rationale: The Jan 15 standing order to fetch a really good goalie from a non-contender remains open. Luongo's GAA 2.67 and SV 0.889 suggest he needs rest; playing 82 games at 26 is a workload risk. The target is a 90+ GSH_/GSL_ goalie from a team under 80 points.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker for remaining games if healthy; his 83 CHKG is the club's fourth-best and he is the only unlined checker.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker (30, 83 CHKG, 70 TOUG, POTE 79, $1.30M) is not in any unit. He is a trade chip per the March 19 standing order, but if he is healthy and not traded, he adds a body to the checking group during the playoffs. His value as a playoff body may exceed his value as a 4th-round-adjacent chip.

recommendations.summary: Speed, playmaking, stamina, and clutch are all covered with 9-21 players at 80+ each. No action required on these roles.
recommendations.rationale: 21 players at 80+ SPEE, 11 at 80+ PASS, 11 at 80+ ENDU, 9 at 80+ HERO. These roles have depth and young bodies behind them. The construction problem is toughness, faceoffs, and top-six scoring replacement, not these.

recommendations.summary: Sign Gaborik to a 5-6 year deal at $3-4M in July 2005; he is the highest-value contract on the roster at 99 points on $1.10M.
recommendations.rationale: 99 pts in 82 GP at age 23 with POTE 90. If he reaches the market he commands $5-7M. This is the single most urgent renewal; losing him removes 30+ points from the first wing.

recommendations.summary: Sign Nash to a 5-6 year deal in July 2005 at 20 years old with POTE 95.
recommendations.rationale: 39 points at age 20 on $1.20M. One more season at 50 points makes him a $4-5M player. Lock the rookie price now.

recommendations.summary: Sign Eminger to a 5-6 year deal in July 2005; at 21 with POTE 99 his price resets the moment he has two full top-pairing seasons.
recommendations.rationale: 23 points in 64 GP at 21 on $1.20M with POTE 99, the highest on the roster. The coach and GM both protected him as a foundation piece.

recommendations.summary: Sign Abid to a 3-4 year deal in July 2005 before his $400K salary resets to $2-3M at renewal.
recommendations.rationale: 66 points in 82 GP, POTE 94, the only forward with 80+ TOUG and CHKG in stored grades. At $400K he is the cheapest player on the roster. Renewal will cost at least $2M regardless; get the term done.

recommendations.summary: Sign Richards to a 4-5 year deal at $2-3M; his 0.71 pts/g decline makes his asking price lower than his 66-point season suggests.
recommendations.rationale: 66 points on $1.00M at 24 with POTE 88. The coach flagged the decline from 1.08 to 0.71 pts/g as a system-fit issue. Lock him before he bounces back and demands more, or before people write him off and we lose trade value.

recommendations.summary: Extend Chlup to a 5-6 year deal before his $2.34M rookie price resets after another 60-point season.
recommendations.rationale: 19 years old, 59 points in 71 GP, POTE 95, two years left at $2.34M. One more season at this rate makes him a $5M+ player. The extension window is now or never.

recommendations.summary: Sign Kaberle to a 3-4 year deal at $3-4M; he is 27, proven, and will not improve further.
recommendations.rationale: 44 points in 74 GP at 27 on $1.90M with POTE 75. A top-pairing right defenseman whose value is stable. Two years is enough to avoid paying for decline years.

recommendations.summary: Sundin ($8.40M, 5 years) and Fischer ($3.70M, 4 years) are locked in and cannot be renegotiated mid-contract; plan around them.
recommendations.rationale: Together they commit $12.10M through 2008-09 with declining production. No action is possible this summer. Fischer becomes trade-bait in summer 2008 when his low production makes him cheap for a contender.

recommendations.summary: Sign Gaborik to a 6-year deal the day free agency opens. He is the first name on the renewal list.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base, 131 points in 82 games, age 23, $1.10M expiring. Star on a star-length deal. Every other renewal waits behind him.

recommendations.summary: Sign Richards on 5 years.
recommendations.rationale: 82 base, 66 points, age 24, $1.00M expiring. His rate dipped to 0.83 but the coach expects it to rise at 24. Second priority behind Gaborik.

recommendations.summary: Sign Eminger on 6 years.
recommendations.rationale: 76 base, POTE 99, age 21, $1.20M expiring. The GM vetoed trading him in January specifically because his ceiling outlasts the current roster window.

recommendations.summary: Sign Upshall on 6 years.
recommendations.rationale: 78 base, POTE 99, age 21, 47 points in 55 games (0.85/g), $1.20M expiring. His season rate confirms the development is real.

recommendations.summary: Sign Nash on 5 years.
recommendations.rationale: 77 base, age 20, 39 points in 69 games, $1.20M expiring. Behind Upshall's rate but two years younger. Lock the youth.

recommendations.summary: Sign Alexeev on 5 years.
recommendations.rationale: 76 base, POTE 94, age 23, 30 points in 55 games, $1.10M expiring. Development is on schedule and the price is $1.10M.

recommendations.summary: Sign Chistov on 5 years.
recommendations.rationale: 78 base, age 22, 20 points, $1.10M expiring. Minutes rose from 9.5 to 14.0 and the rate held, per the coach. He earned a look; give him a contract.

recommendations.summary: Sign Kaberle on 2 years at a modest raise.
recommendations.rationale: 84 base, age 27, 44 points, $1.90M expiring. Solid top-four D but not a franchise anchor. Two years keeps the money reasonable and avoids a fifth-year anchor.

recommendations.summary: Sign Abid on 2 years.
recommendations.rationale: 79 base, 80 TOUG, 80 CHKG, 66 points, $0.40M expiring. He is the only roster player addressing the coach's checking-wing gap, and the price is absurd.

recommendations.summary: Sign Tellqvist on 3 years at $0.80M or less.
recommendations.rationale: 77 base, age 25, potential in high 90s per the GM's standing order. Luongo is the starter; Tellqvist provides the third body at minimal cost.

recommendations.summary: Let Belfour walk in July. Do not renew.
recommendations.rationale: Age 40, $6.50M, expiring. The GM confirmed this on March 21. He carries the playoff run; the money is freed in July. One off-season attempt at the over-80 pick mechanic is free but not expected to land.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk in July.
recommendations.rationale: Age 38, $2.70M, 21.4 MPG load flagged by the coach as unsustainable. He produced 88 points but the injury risk and age curve say this is the last year. $2.70M funds a replacement.

recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri (LA, 22, POTE 98) in July as an unrestricted free agent.
recommendations.rationale: 60 points in 61 games, $1.10M expiring. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring cannot retain both him and Frolov. Cheapest high-upside forward available.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, POTE 81) in July.
recommendations.rationale: The coach explicitly states no forward outside L1-L2 checks above 80. Bell is the only league-wide player closing both the toughness and faceoff gaps. CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring and $29.46M profit are motivated sellers.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Stuart (SJ, D, 25, 87 base, 89 CHKG, POTE 91) to replace Roberts.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts walks at 38. Stuart at 25 with eight years of development replaces the minutes at a lower cost. SJ at 72 points with 13 expiring on $45.39M payroll may deal him if the return works.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, 140 points) if CGY cannot retain him.
recommendations.rationale: He closes the Mogilny scoring void and the structural toughness ceiling simultaneously. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him at $6.50M. This requires the Belfour+Roberts money freed ($9.20M).

recommendations.summary: Keep Mogilny for his two remaining years at $5.50M. Do not attempt to trade him.
recommendations.rationale: 94 points in 82 games (1.15/g) at age 36 is still first-line production. His POTE is 55 so he will decline, but his contract expires in 2007 and the problem solves itself. He is not expiring, so no trade mechanic improves his value.

recommendations.summary: Keep Tucker at 2 years and $1.30M as fourth-line depth, or attempt a salary-dump in July.
recommendations.rationale: 79 base, POTE 79, age 30, 8 points in 40 games. Below 80 so the pick mechanic does not apply. No urgency — he costs $1.30M and fills a body on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Sign Scatchard (NYI, C, 29, 85 base, 85 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 84 FACE, $1.40M expiring) as the checking centre who wins draws for lines 3-4.
recommendations.rationale: Only player in the league closing toughness, checking AND faceoffs simultaneously on an expiring deal. NYI at 84 pts with 13 expiring and $12.46M profit cannot retain all 13.

recommendations.summary: Sign Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, 140pts/73GP, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring) as the Mogilny replacement on the top wing.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 70 points with $14.43M profit and 10 expiring cannot retain a $6.50M RW. Closes the scoring void and lifts the team-wide toughness ceiling by 10 points in one move.

recommendations.summary: Sign Lalime (OTT, G, 30, 92 base, $1.90M expiring) as Luongo's playoff-calibre backup after Belfour walks.
recommendations.rationale: 92 base matches the Jan 15 standing order for a high-90s goalie. OTT at 77 pts with 11 expiring on $42.80M payroll are selling. Nabokov (SJ, 90 base, POTE 90, $3.60M) is the alternative.

recommendations.summary: Sign Barnaby (NYR, LW, 32, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 53pts/78GP, $1.50M expiring) for toughness with production.
recommendations.rationale: NYR at $78.14M payroll with zero profit are shedding salary by any means. 88 TOUG is the highest on any expiring player with 50+ points. Solves the structural toughness gap cheaply.

recommendations.summary: Sign Belanger (LA, C, 27, 82 base, 97 FACE, 79 TOUG, 83 CHKG, $700K expiring) as faceoff insurance if Scatchard is taken.
recommendations.rationale: 97 FACE is the best in the league. LA at 79 pts with 14 expiring on $52.43M are selling. At $700K he costs nothing and gives L3-4 a 90+ draw-taker.

recommendations.summary: Sign Bouwmeester (FLA, D, 21, 81 base, POTE 95, 27pts/79GP, 33.3 MPG, $1.20M expiring) as the long-term top-pairing defenceman.
recommendations.rationale: Already playing 33 MPG at 21 with 81 base. FLA at 76 pts with 19 expiring and $13.64M profit cannot retain 19 players. Replaces Roberts within two years.

recommendations.summary: Sign Vandermeer (PHI, D, 25, 76 base, POTE 91, 86 TOUG, 84 CHKG, $400K expiring) as a cheap tough blueliner.
recommendations.rationale: PHI at 82 pts with 13 expiring and only $2.14M profit are selling. 86 TOUG/84 CHKG gives the third pair toughness the club currently has zero of. $400K is nothing.

recommendations.summary: Sign Havlat (OTT, LW, 24, 87 base, 103pts/82GP, $900K expiring) as a second top-six winger if Iginla goes elsewhere.
recommendations.rationale: 87 base at 24 with 103 points on $900K is the best value on the market. OTT at 77 pts selling everything. TOUG 68 is a weakness but his production replaces Mogilny at half the salary.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Heatley (ATL, RW, 24, 91 base, 131pts/79GP, TOUG 75, $1.10M expiring) as the fallback if ATL re-signs Kovalchuk and lets him walk.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 84 pts with 11 expiring cannot retain both Kovalchuk (138pts) and Heatley (131pts). Whichever walks is available. Heatley at 91 base and 24 is the RW target if Iginla signs elsewhere.

recommendations.summary: Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 80 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, $900K, 2 years remaining) remains the best long-term fit but requires a trade we cannot currently fund.
recommendations.rationale: Two years left means UFA July 2006. Tucker plus the 4th is worth a 74-76 player per the March 30 assessment. Only viable if the GM releases a protected player into the package.

recommendations.summary: If Lalime signs elsewhere, pursue Nabokov (SJ, G, 29, 90 base, POTE 90, GAA 2.66, SV 0.872, $3.60M expiring).
recommendations.rationale: Best actual numbers of any expiring goalie (2.66 GAA, 0.872 SV). SJ at 76 pts with 13 expiring on $45.39M cannot retain all of them. $3.60M is affordable within our $31.56M profit.

recommendations.summary: Orpik (PIT, D, 24, 70 base, POTE 97, 84 TOUG, 87 CHKG, $1.10M expiring) as development defence depth if the back end thins.
recommendations.rationale: 70 base is low but POTE 97 with 84 TOUG/87 CHKG at 24 is a real project. PIT at 85 pts with 14 expiring. Worth a look if Vandermeer is taken.

recommendations.summary: Send Koltsov to LA for Avery; closes toughness and faceoff gaps at $400K salary, dropping our cost by $700K per year.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 48 points with 14 expiring on $52.43M payroll needs POTE 94 youth for their rebuild. The coach calls Koltsov a trading chip (0.28 pts/g). Avery is the only 2-year player who clears both 80+ TOUG and 80+ FACE simultaneously. Package confirmed viable on April 19.

recommendations.proposed: Bell (C/LW, 24, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, $2.00M est., 2yr, 82 base)
recommendations.summary: Package Koltsov plus Tucker plus the 4th-rounder to CHI for Bell; the single best player closing toughness, checking, and faceoffs at age 24.
recommendations.rationale: CHI at 73 points with $29.46M profit and 10 expiring deals are sellers. Bell's POTE 81 is 13 points below Koltsov's POTE 94 at the same age; CHI gets a higher-ceiling swap plus a pick and a veteran depth piece. Acceptance uncertain because Bell's proven 82 base may outweigh Koltsov's unproven 19 points in their valuation.

recommendations.proposed: Scatchard (C, 29, 85 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 84 FACE, $1.40M, NYI UFA)
recommendations.summary: If both trade proposals fail, sign Scatchard as a UFA on July 1; he solves the same gaps with no trade capital required.
recommendations.rationale: NYI at 84 points with 13 expiring deals and $12.46M profit cannot retain him. At 26 points in 78 games on 10.9 MPG he is a third-and-fourth-line centre exactly where the coach's gap lives. No package needed, no Koltsov surrendered.

recommendations.summary: Goalie monitoring task is closed; Luongo (94, 26, $1.60M, 2 yrs) and Belfour (93, 40, $6.50M, 1 yr) are the playoff pair as ordered.
recommendations.rationale: The February window this task served is past, Luongo arrived, and the GM's 2005-03-19 order formally closed all goalie monitoring.

recommendations.summary: Reinstate Spezza for the remaining 6 games, starting Sunday against Pittsburgh.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99, 6.7 MPG in 46 games, morale 88 (lowest among young players). Pittsburgh is 24-34 and this is a development-priority night. Even 2-3 games of real ice starts the camp momentum the March finding called for.

recommendations.summary: Give Stahle a look in the final 6 games against a bad Pittsburgh club.
recommendations.rationale: 4 games all season at age 20 with POTE 96. Morale is 99 but he is accumulating zero experience. Six games left and one of them is against a 24-34 team.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev at 0.55 pts/g outproduces dressed wingers Chistov (0.29) and Upshall (0.29) but has been scratched since late in the season.
recommendations.rationale: 30 points in 55 games, POTE 94, morale 92. He is being benched in favour of players producing at half his rate. Flag for the GM to consider reinstating him over one of the two.

recommendations.summary: Chlup stays on line two through the final 6 games.
recommendations.rationale: 59 points in 71 games, 16.9 MPG, morale 98. He is earning everything he is getting and the trajectory is the best on the roster.

recommendations.current: Nash, Klesla, Eminger, Chistov, Upshall, Spacek, Ouellet, Colaiacovo, Gaborik
recommendations.summary: No change for any other young player. Each is getting ice time consistent with his current production level.
recommendations.rationale: Nash 13.1 MPG on line 3, Klesla 14.8 MPG on pair 3, Eminger 15.5 MPG on pair 3, Chistov 13.1 MPG on line 3, Upshall 7.9 MPG on line 4, Spacek 7.6 MPG on line 4, Gaborik 20.5 MPG on line 1, Ouellet 13 starts as backup, Colaiacovo at GM's deliberate rotation pace.

recommendations.summary: Chlup confirmed as first-line centre for 2005-06. He kept production rising (0.62→0.88) as minutes doubled (11.0→18.2).
recommendations.rationale: The only young player ascending. His rate held under doubling load at 19, which is the profile of a permanent top-six centre.

recommendations.summary: Sell Jackman this summer at $0.70M x 3. His season confirmed at 0.39 pts/g on 29.4 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: Third straight activation confirming the collapse from 0.65 to 0.39. The load is killing his production and at 24 the expected direction is up.

recommendations.summary: Sell Klesla at $0.90M x 2. Third declining season locked at 0.31 pts/g over 82 games.
recommendations.rationale: 0.38→0.36→0.31 across three seasons with minutes flat at 15 MPG. The trend is unambiguous.

recommendations.summary: Trade Eminger before free agency. 0.37 on 15.9 MPG, $1.2M expiring in July.
recommendations.rationale: Confirmed slide across the season. Any return beats a UFA loss. Deadline passed, offseason is the last window.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza, Spacek and Upshall a real camp audition next September or stop dressing them.
recommendations.rationale: All three collapsed to under 5 MPG and under 0.30 pts/g. No development can be judged on 4 minutes a night.

recommendations.summary: No change to Fischer. His rate dipped (0.63→0.50) but minutes rose (20.8→22.9), which dilutes rate without signaling decline.
recommendations.rationale: At 24 with increased defensive-zone load the GM's keeper call stands. The rate drop is explained by the role change, not by regression.

recommendations.summary: The room is healthy. Every player is at 88 or above, nearly all at 100, and every trend is flat or positive. No minutes adjustment is warranted.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza at 88 is the lowest and rising; Upshall and Spacek at 91 are in their expected depth band and climbing; the core is all at 98-100. The team's results are lifting the group and no individual is under-ice for his calibre in a way that's creating friction.

recommendations.summary: We need a bottom-six centre who wins faceoffs above 60; nobody on the roster can fill that role.
recommendations.rationale: L4 faceoff mean is 52 with a best of 55. The four best draw men on the roster (Sundin 91, Chlup 80, Roberts 76, Richards 75) are all slotted on L1-L3. This is a composition gap no arrangement fixes.

recommendations.summary: All four even-strength lines and both power-play units are built for their roles; no composition change tonight.
recommendations.rationale: L1 is elite scoring with a checking spine (mean 83). L2 is a scoring line with adequate defence (Chlup faceoffs 80). L3 checks well (mean 75, best of four). L4 faceoff gap is a roster problem, not a lines problem. PIT is 24-34-15; the development framework applies and young guys are already in the top six.

recommendations.summary: Keep L3's shifts short and give L4 more reps to cover the stamina gap.
recommendations.rationale: L3 stamina mean 63 (best: Richards 87). Nash, Chistov, Eminger, and Klesla all sit well below that. Shorter shifts preserve their checking effectiveness; L4 can handle the minutes against a 24-34 opponent.

recommendations.summary: Play the same lines. The auto-pairing already puts Fischer/Jackman on Lemieux's line, Sundin wins the dot 91 to 68, and their blue line has no one above 77.
recommendations.rationale: PIT's PP is 11.6% (32/276), their best D pair reads 76/77, and Lemieux at 39 with CHKG 66 gets matched against two 92-checking defencemen by the existing slot order. Every structural advantage favours us without intervention.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is OVR 94 with morale 100 and no injury. PIT shoots 2.5 goals per game. He should handle this.

recommendations.summary: Sell Jackman this offseason at $0.70M x 3; his final season is 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: Two full seasons below 0.50 on top-pair minutes. His contract makes him the cheapest top-pair D available; his value erodes further each month.

recommendations.summary: Sell Klesla this offseason at $0.90M x 2; final season 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: Two consecutive declining seasons at 22 and 23. No trajectory toward top-four production. Best return available while contract is cheap.

recommendations.summary: Trade Eminger before July; final season 0.36 pts/g on 15.5 MPG, $1.20M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Rate fell again from the 0.38 noted in March. After July he is a UFA with zero return. Any deal is better than nothing.

recommendations.summary: Bell (CHI, 24, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81) is the only player in the league closing the toughness, checking, and faceoff gaps simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Zero Toronto players carry 80+ toughness in stored grades. Bell provides 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, and 82 FACE at age 24. CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring deals are motivated sellers.

recommendations.summary: Avery (LA, 25, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2 years) is the budget alternative if Bell's price is prohibitive.
recommendations.rationale: Cheapest player in the league closing all three structural gaps at once. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring deals. His ENDU is lower than Bell's but he is on a cheaper deal with two years of control.

recommendations.summary: Stuart (SJ, 25, 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91) replaces Roberts' checking and durability at age 25 with eight years of development remaining.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts at 86 CHKG and 98 durability is expiring at 38. Stuart closes the checking and durability voids that open when Roberts walks, and at 25 pairs with Jackman for the long term. SJ at 72 points may resist.

recommendations.summary: Line Tucker (83 CHKG) on the fourth line to give a fourth 80+ forward checker; costs nothing and requires no trade.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker is at 83 CHKG, not lined, and is the only rostered forward above 82 checking outside Fischer. His 70 TOUG does not fix the toughness gap but improves the checking profile of the bottom six.

recommendations.summary: Faceoff coverage collapses after this season: Sundin (34, 90 FACE) is expiring and the next-best on the roster is 75. This is a July priority alongside the toughness target.
recommendations.rationale: One player at 90 FACE at 34 with one year left. Bell or Avery both carry 82+ FACE and would solve this simultaneously with the toughness gap.

recommendations.summary: Sign Gaborik to a 5-year deal immediately in July before the market opens.
recommendations.rationale: 99 points at 23 on $1.10M with one year left. POTE 90, age 23, entering prime. If he walks, the club loses its top forward and the identity of the core.

recommendations.summary: Sign Richards to a 5-year deal in the same July window as Gaborik.
recommendations.rationale: 66 points, 24 years old, $1.00M, one year left. POTE 88. A second full 80-game season says he is arrived. No reason to risk a bidding war.

recommendations.summary: Sign Nash on a 5-year deal at rookie-window pricing this July.
recommendations.rationale: 39 points at age 20, POTE 95, $1.20M, one year left. Cheapest long-term lock available. Locks left wing through 2010.

recommendations.summary: Sign Eminger to a 5-year deal immediately in July.
recommendations.rationale: 21 years old, POTE 99, 23 points in 64 games, $1.20M with one year left. The defense cornerstone. One year of exposure on a POTE 99 blueliner is unacceptable.

recommendations.summary: Sign Kaberle to a 4-year deal in July.
recommendations.rationale: 44 points at 27, POTE 75, one year at $1.90M. Entering prime but ceiling is set. Four years buys the floor without overcommitting to a declining ceiling.

recommendations.summary: Sign Abid to a 3-year deal before July opens.
recommendations.rationale: 66 points, 82 games, $0.40M, POTE 94, age 25. The lowest-paid player on the roster produced 66 points. Any open-market exposure loses him. Three years at a modest raise locks the bottom six.

recommendations.summary: Sign Iginla as a free agent in July if he clears from CGY.
recommendations.rationale: RW, 27, 93 base, 140 pts in 73 GP, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring. Closes Mogilny's scoring void and the toughness gap simultaneously. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring cannot retain him.

recommendations.summary: Plan Sundin's exit for July 2006, not now; he is still producing 91 points at 34.
recommendations.rationale: $8.40M for five more years means he is 39 at the tail end. By 2006-07 he will decline rapidly. The bridge-age gap (only Tucker at 30) needs filling with a young piece acquired while Sundin still carries trade value.

recommendations.proposed: Acquire a first-rounder via player trades in 2005-06
recommendations.summary: The only pick held is a fourth-rounder; the club must manufacture draft capital through player moves over the coming season.
recommendations.rationale: No picks beyond a fourth. Every future restock depends on players. Sundin at 35 with one year remaining is the only asset with enough value to fetch a first from a contender.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik to a 5-6 year deal immediately after the season ends; he is 91 base at 23 with POTE 90 on $1.10M and every contender will chase him.
recommendations.rationale: The March 21 priority order puts him first. At 87 points and 91 base, losing him to free agency creates an RW scoring hole with no internal replacement and no affordable external one.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards to a 5-6 year deal; he is 24 with 64 points on $1.00M.
recommendations.rationale: Coach flagged a production drop but the system-fit question is a coaching problem, not a roster one. A 24-year-old centre at $1.00M is not walkable.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle to a 5-6 year deal at 27 on $1.90M.
recommendations.rationale: He is in his prime and the top puck-mover on the blue line. The December staggered-lock plan includes him.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash to a 5-6 year deal; he is 20 on $1.20M.
recommendations.rationale: At 20, production drops are development noise. Lock him before he prices himself into the next tier.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger to a 5-6 year deal; he is 21 on $1.20M with POTE 99.
recommendations.rationale: GM vetoed trading him in January specifically because of his potential. Lock that potential before the market does.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Colaiacovo to a 3-5 year deal; he is 22 on $1.10M.
recommendations.rationale: At 22 his starter status is not yet settled. Three years buys a look; five is a risk if development stalls.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Chistov, Upshall and Alexeev on 2-3 year deals; they are 22, 21 and 23 respectively on roughly $1.10M each.
recommendations.rationale: These are depth players whose next 60 games determine if they are regulars. Shorter deals preserve flexibility.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Abid to a 2-year deal at base TOUG 80 and CHKG 80 on $0.40M.
recommendations.rationale: He is the cheapest toughness on the roster. At $0.40M there is no reason to let him walk.

recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour one reduced contract (around $3M on 1-2 years); if he refuses, let him walk.
recommendations.rationale: He is 40 on $6.50M. Luongo is 91 base and two years younger by 15. The March 21 plan says Belfour walks. $6.50M is not a backup goalie salary.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk; he is 38 on $2.70M.
recommendations.rationale: GM's March 21 standing order is explicit. At 38 there is no return on a $2.70M investment.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE) in July as the primary toughness acquisition.
recommendations.rationale: Coach's April 15 report confirms zero forwards outside L1-L2 check above 75. Bell closes both toughness and faceoff gaps. CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring are motivated sellers.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, $6.50M expiring) in July if he hits free agency; he replaces Mogilny's production and adds TOUG 85.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g at 36. Iginla at 140 points over 73 games closes the RW void and the toughness ceiling simultaneously.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza 15+ minutes in the remaining 7 games; if he cannot produce above 0.33 pts/g in this window, his trade value peaks now with POTE 99 still credible.
recommendations.rationale: The coach has flagged him six times. Seven games at 15 MPG is a genuine sample. The summer renewal decision for Spezza follows from it.

recommendations.summary: Give Upshall 15+ minutes in the remaining 7 games to determine his contract length this summer.
recommendations.rationale: He is 21 and expiring. These seven games decide whether he gets two years or three.

recommendations.summary: Dress Spacek for any fourth-line opening in the remaining 7 games.
recommendations.rationale: Coach requested this on April 15. Free games against weak opponents are the only pre-playoff window to evaluate him.

recommendations.summary: Offer Spezza and the fourth-rounder to Calgary for Iginla, the 93-base 27-year-old RW on an expiring $6.50M deal.
recommendations.rationale: Iginla's 140 points in 73 games close the RW void Mogilny (36, 0.79 pts/g late) leaves, and TOUG 85 beats every current forward. CGY finished 70 points with 10 expiring deals and cannot retain a $6.50M star; a POTE 99 centre at $1.00M plus a pick is a rebuild return. Acceptance uncertain.

recommendations.summary: Offer Klesla and the fourth-rounder to Chicago for Bell, the only player closing the toughness, checking and faceoff gaps in one body.
recommendations.rationale: Bell at 24 carries 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG and 82 FACE where the roster tops out at Jackman's 75 and one draw-taker in a 34-year-old Sundin. CHI finished 78 points with 10 expiring deals and $31.73M profit, the most motivated seller; they take youth, and Klesla is 23 at POTE 97 on $0.90M. Acceptance uncertain.

recommendations.summary: Offer Colaiacovo and Tucker to San Jose for Stuart as the Roberts replacement on defence.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts (38, expiring) takes 86 CHKG and 98 durability with him; Stuart at 25 gives 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG and POTE 91. SJ finished 72 points with 13 expiring deals on $45.39M and cannot keep them all. Ranked third because SJ may refuse to move a POTE 91 blueliner. Acceptance uncertain.

recommendations.summary: Retire the goalie trade window monitoring task; Luongo is acquired, DiPietro is eliminated, and the GM closed the window on March 19.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo (94, 26, $1.60M, 2 yrs) is on the roster. DiPietro reads 79 base after 52 GP, well below the high-90s threshold. The GM's 2005-03-19 order explicitly closed all goalie monitoring. The task has no remaining purpose.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle tonight against PIT and give him 15+ minutes.
recommendations.rationale: 4 GP in 82 games at age 20 with POTE 96 is the most obvious waste on the roster. He logged 17.8 MPG in the 4 games he played, so the trust is there when he is in. PIT at 24-34 is a game we can afford to use for development.

recommendations.summary: Move Spezza up from the fourth line to get minutes against PIT.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 at 21, 6.7 MPG on the fourth line, morale 88 is the lowest of any young player. Against a 24-34 team this is a development night. He needs to see second- or third-line minutes to have any chance in camp.

recommendations.summary: Reinstate Spacek for remaining games.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 91 at 19, 7.6 MPG season rate, currently scratched. The March bump to 12+ MPG did not hold. With PIT coming in at 24-34 and the season nearly done, these are the last chances to give him a real look.

recommendations.summary: Dress Colaiacovo against PIT and give him top-four minutes.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 at 22, only 31 GP but 17.9 MPG when he plays. He is a fifth defenceman in a good lineup. A weak opponent is the only time to test him without the cost of a loss.

recommendations.summary: Leave Chlup where he is.
recommendations.rationale: 59 points in 71 games on 16.9 MPG at age 19. He is playing 87% of games and getting real minutes. No development concern.

recommendations.summary: McCabe goes on the sell list. Final rate 0.48 pts/g on 21.5 MPG across 82 games, below the 0.60 threshold.
recommendations.rationale: The March 30 conditional said if the final rate held below 0.60 he goes back on. It is 0.48. At 29 with $3.0M x 4 years, his value is highest now before the next decline shows.

recommendations.summary: Abid's per-60 rate is 3.65 on 11.5 MPG. He needs 15+ minutes next season to be properly used.
recommendations.rationale: His minutes dropped from 20.1 to 11.5 while his per-game rate stayed reasonable. At 25 he is still improving and his per-60 is elite for a winger his age.

recommendations.proposed: Offseason system-fit review before next camp
recommendations.summary: Richards dropped from 1.08 to 0.71 pts/g at age 24 on flat minutes. The expected direction is up. Review the system fit before June ends.
recommendations.rationale: At 24, 16 MPG and 0.71 pts/g is below what the age curve says he should produce. Either the system is suppressing him or he is not a first-line centre. Either way, decide before camp.

recommendations.current: Chistov on the third or fourth line
recommendations.proposed: Give Chistov a top-nine audition next camp
recommendations.summary: Chistov at 22 saw minutes rise from 9.5 to 14.0 MPG and his rate held at 0.30. He earned more ice and should get a real look.
recommendations.rationale: He is the only young forward whose minutes went up this season without production dropping. At 0.30 the rate is modest, but the trajectory is correct and the sample is now 68 games.

recommendations.proposed: Real camp auditions or stop dressing
recommendations.summary: Spezza at 0.24 on 4.6 MPG and Upshall at 0.27 on 4.8 MPG both collapsed. Give them a genuine preseason battle or drop them from the rotation.
recommendations.rationale: Both at 21, both lost their minutes and their rates simultaneously. Dressing them at 5 MPG next season achieves nothing for their development or the team.

recommendations.proposed: Reduce Roberts below 18 MPG next season
recommendations.summary: Roberts at 38 carried 21.4 MPG this season. That load is unsustainable at his age and raises his injury risk.
recommendations.rationale: His rate declined from 1.29 to 0.86 as expected for a 38-year-old, but the minutes went UP from 16.5 to 21.4. Cut the load, keep the leadership.

recommendations.summary: Room is healthy; lowest morale is Spezza at 88, already addressed as an offseason camp assignment.
recommendations.rationale: All dressed players at 91+, trending up with wins. The two below 90 (Spezza 88, Spacek 89) are scratched or fourth-line by GM design for development; no in-season line change moves them.

recommendations.summary: No line composition changes; L1-L3, P1, P2, K1, and K2 all suit their roles.
recommendations.rationale: L1 checks 83 mean and scores 89 mean. K2 has the highest checking mean on any unit at 84. P1 has Gaborik at 99 scoring and Sundin at 92 playmaking. Each unit's personnel matches its job.

recommendations.summary: We need a checking centre who wins draws for lines 3-4; no forward outside L1-L2 checks above 80.
recommendations.rationale: L4 checking mean is 65, toughness 59, faceoffs 53. Our four best checkers (Jackman 90, Roberts 85, McCabe 85, Fischer 85) are all deployed on PK and top-six minutes. No available forward fills a shutdown-centre role.

recommendations.summary: Keep the fourth line as-is; these are 20-21 year-olds whose stamina (51 mean) and checking (65 mean) are development problems, not arrangement problems.
recommendations.rationale: No swap fixes L4 because no better personnel exists. The stamina at 51 and faceoffs at 53 will come with age and conditioning. Moving Abid down would trade a 0.84 pts/g winger off L3 for a marginal checking gain on L4.

recommendations.summary: Keep all lines as set. The auto-pairing already puts our best D against their best line and the gap is too wide to need adjustment.
recommendations.rationale: TOR is 4-0-0 vs PIT with 20 goals to 9. PIT's top D pair is OVR 77/76, third pair is 67/70. Fischer and Jackman at CHKG 92 on pair one against Lemieux (CHKG 66) is already the ideal match. Slot order needs no shuffle.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo if his fatigue icon is clear on screen.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is 94 OVR, morale 100. PIT's last 10 shows 2.6 goals per game against a 1.70 GA club. No reason to roll back to Tellqvist at 75.

recommendations.proposed: Upshall (shift to LW) or scratch Koltsov and give fourth-line minutes to Spezza/Upshall
recommendations.summary: If the GM wants development tonight, scratch Koltsov (0.28 pts/g, trading chip) and give Upshall or Spezza the extra fourth-line reps. This is a development choice, not a matchup need.
recommendations.rationale: Per the GM's framework, development applies in games we can afford. PIT at 24-34-11 is one. Spezza is at 72 OVR and 88 morale with collapsed minutes; Upshall at 79 and 91. Koltsov's value is as a chip, not a player.

recommendations.summary: Trade Eminger before free agency in July — his contract expires and he is sliding to 0.36 pts/g.
recommendations.rationale: 23 points in 64 games on 15.5 MPG at age 21. $1.20M expiring. After July he is a UFA loss. Any return beats zero.

recommendations.summary: Sell Jackman this offseason — 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG, $0.70M x 3 years is the cheapest top-pair minutes available to any club.
recommendations.rationale: Rate has declined from 0.48 at 73 GP to 0.46 at 80 GP. The load is suppressing his production and his role would need to change to fix it, which we cannot do without trading him.

recommendations.summary: Sell Klesla this offseason — two consecutive declining seasons, final rate 0.37 pts/g.
recommendations.rationale: 0.38 at 22, 0.37 at 23, on flat 14.8 MPG. No growth signal. $0.90M x 2 years is tradeable depth that other clubs will take for a bottom-pair or prospect.

recommendations.summary: Renew Kaberle before he hits free agency at $1.90M — he is the GM's stated keeper.
recommendations.rationale: 0.59 pts/g on 20.8 MPG at age 27. GM called him 'a star defenseman' on 2005-01-15. Losing him for nothing would be unacceptable.

recommendations.summary: Bell is the primary acquisition target: 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE at 24 closes both the toughness (0 at 80+) and faceoff (1 at 80+) gaps simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Zero Toronto players carry 80+ TOUG in stored grades and only Sundin (90) is 80+ FACE. Bell at 24 with POTE 81 is the only league-wide player addressing both. CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring are motivated sellers.

recommendations.summary: Avery at $400K with 93 FACE and 83 TOUG is the budget alternative to Bell, closing faceoffs outright and touching toughness.
recommendations.rationale: Lower ceiling than Bell (83 vs 88 TOUG) but 93 FACE makes him the best draw-taker available by a wide margin. At $400K with 2 years left, he costs almost nothing to retain.

recommendations.summary: Stuart (87 base, 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 25, POTE 91) replaces Roberts' expiring checking and durability with eight years of runway.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts (38) walks in July taking 86 CHKG and 98 INJU. Stuart at 25 is the only young blueliner with both 80+ TOUG and 80+ CHKG identified as a realistic target. SJ at 72 points with 13 expiring may not deal him.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker for the remaining games; his 83 CHKG is the only unlined 80+ checking grade available.
recommendations.rationale: He is rostered, unlined, 30, POTE 79, $1.30M. He will not be kept long-term but 3-4 games of 83 CHKG costs nothing and gives the fourth line a real checker for the playoff seed.

recommendations.summary: Dress Spacek against NYI and remaining weak opponents; his 84 playmaking is untested in any NHL context.
recommendations.rationale: Coach already flagged this on April 14. 19 years old, 84 P, unlined. Three games is the entire audition window before July camp.

recommendations.summary: Scoring (10 at 80+) and speed (21 at 80+) are covered and do not need external help before the remaining gaps are closed.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik 92 at 23, Sundin 92 at 34, Afinogenov 90 at 25 give three 90+ scorers under 35. The problem is not the top of the roster but the bottom: toughness and faceoffs.

recommendations.current: Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, Colaiacovo, Chistov
recommendations.summary: Re-sign the six young core players on 5-6 year deals immediately in July, staggering terms to prevent a second cluster: Gaborik 6, Nash 6, Richards 5, Eminger 5, Colaiacovo 5, Chistov 5.
recommendations.rationale: All six carry POTE 90+ and contracts expiring this July at a combined $6.80M. If they walk, the window closes. Staggering 5 and 6 year terms splits the next renewal between July 2010 and July 2011.

recommendations.summary: Sign Kaberle (27, 44 pts, POTE 75, $1.90M) to a 3-4 year deal rather than 5-6, because his potential ceiling is near and locking him long wastes cap space that the next cluster will need.
recommendations.rationale: At POTE 75 his grade has roughly 5 points of upside left. A 3-year deal keeps him through age 30 and returns him to the market when the 2008 cluster (Afinogenov, Fischer, McCabe) also needs money.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Abid (25, 66 points, POTE 94, $0.40M) on a 2-year deal before he leaves for free; he is the cheapest 66-point producer on the roster and his POTE suggests more upside at $0.40M than the market will offer him.
recommendations.rationale: He played all 82 games scoring 66 points at $0.40M. No other player on the roster delivers that ratio. Losing him costs a bottom-six scoring line.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla as a UFA signing in July; he closes the RW scoring void (Mogilny fell to 0.79 pts/g at 36) and the structural toughness gap (TOUG 85) in one move.
recommendations.rationale: Iginla is 27, 93 base, 140 points in 73 GP, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring. CGY at 70 points cannot retain him. No draft pick is required for a UFA signing. Payroll headroom accommodates $6.50M against $29.51M profit.

recommendations.summary: Sundin stays at $8.40M for five more years; there is no mid-contract trade mechanism and his 91 points this season justify the money through age 37 even if the grade declines.
recommendations.rationale: The contract is locked. The only question was whether to trade him at the deadline and the answer was no because he is the centre that makes the top line work and his points this season (91) exceed anything the club could get back.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik on six years the day re-signing opens; 91 base, 87 pts, $1.10M.
recommendations.rationale: He is the highest-base, highest-production player on the expiring list by a full tier. Delay risks a bidding war at renewal.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards on five or six years; 24, 64 pts, $1.00M.
recommendations.rationale: Best young centre in the league at that salary. His production-to-cost ratio is what makes the roster profitable.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle on five years; 27, D, $1.90M, prime age.
recommendations.rationale: Only established top-pairing blueliner we hold long-term. At 27 his ceiling is set and he is arriving.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash on six years; 20, LW, $1.20M.
recommendations.rationale: Future first-line left wing at the lowest possible price for a player his age. Lock him before his rate rises.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger on five years; 21, D, $1.20M, POTE 99.
recommendations.rationale: GM locked him in on February 19. Eight years of development remaining.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Chistov on two or three years; 21, LW, $1.10M, 0.30 pts/g rising minutes.
recommendations.rationale: Coach flagged positive development: rate held while minutes rose 50%. Middle-six audition at camp first.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Colaiacovo on two or three years; 22, D, $1.10M.
recommendations.rationale: Defensive depth at youth pricing. Pair with Eminger's development arc.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Abid on two years at $0.60M; 25, 80 TOUG, 80 CHKG, $0.40M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Only rostered player closing the structural toughness gap. Coach says fourth-line checking mean is 61, toughness 57.

recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour a reduced-salary renewal; if he declines, let him walk and save $6.50M.
recommendations.rationale: GM's standing order: offer reduced salary, he probably won't accept. Luongo plus Tellqvist covers the position.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk; 38, LW, $2.70M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: March 21 renewal order already states Roberts walks. His role is filled by Nash and the youth movement.

recommendations.summary: Let Upshall walk unless camp shows 0.35+ pts/g; 21, 0.28 pts/g on 5.2 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: Coach declared his season dead on April 14. No bench role fixed the problem all year.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, $6.50M expiring) as the primary July RW target.
recommendations.rationale: Closes the Mogilny scoring void and the structural toughness ceiling (TOUG 85) simultaneously. CGY at 70 points cannot retain him.

recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri (LA, 22, C, POTE 98, 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M expiring) as a July UFA if he hits the market.
recommendations.rationale: Highest-value UFA in the pool by potential-to-cost ratio. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring cannot retain both him and Frolov.

recommendations.summary: Sign Langenbrunner (PHI, RW, 89 base, $2.10M expiring) as a secondary UFA target.
recommendations.rationale: 89 base at $2.10M is a better value than Elias at 90 for $4.90M. Fills a top-six wing slot at half the cost.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza a genuine first-line camp audition in 2005-06; if he fails a seventh time, trade while POTE 99 is credible.
recommendations.rationale: Never exceeded 0.33 pts/g in any season at 5 MPG. His trade value is highest now and decays every year he stalls.

recommendations.current: Roberts (38, D, 88 base, 92 TOUG, 98 INJU, 81 pts/82 GP, $2.70M, expiring)
recommendations.summary: Trade Roberts to a playoff contender for a draft pick using the over-80 expiring mechanic before he walks in July.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts is 88 overall and expiring. The guide confirms 80+ players you will not re-sign can be traded for a pick. A contender at defence-thin positions gets an 88-overall blueliner with 98 INJU for one playoff run at $2.70M; we recover a pick that funds the Bell or Stuart pursuit.

recommendations.current: Koltsov (23, LW, POTE 94, ACCE 96, AGIL 92, 2 yrs, $1.10M)
recommendations.proposed: Avery (25, C, 79 base, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 93 FACE, $400K, 2 yrs)
recommendations.summary: Trade Koltsov to LA for Avery to close the faceoff and checking voids at a net saving of $700K.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 79 points with 14 expiring deals need young upside; Koltsov at 23 with POTE 94 and ACCE 96 is a developable asset for them. Avery at 93 FACE and 88 CHKG is the single best faceoff-toughness forward available at $400K, and LA's profit position makes them salary-shedders on their older depth.

recommendations.current: Tucker (30, LW, 2 yrs, $1.30M, CHKG 92, TOUG 88) plus 4th-round pick plus one pick recovered from Roberts deal
recommendations.proposed: Bell (24, LW, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, $900K, 2 yrs)
recommendations.summary: If the Roberts-for-a-pick deal lands, add that pick to Tucker and our fourth to pursue Bell from Chicago.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker plus the fourth alone scores around 74-76 base against Bell's 82. An additional recovered pick narrows the gap. CHI at 78 points with $31.73M profit are not desperate but Bell at POTE 81 is good-not-franchise, and Tucker's 92 CHKG fills their fourth-line checking need immediately. Acceptance remains uncertain because Bell is cheap and young.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza 15+ MPG for the remaining three games against weak opponents.
recommendations.rationale: 46 games at 6.7 MPG on the fourth line is not development. POTE 99, morale 88, and the GM's standing order says develop in games we can afford. NYI is 30-38.

recommendations.summary: Give Upshall 15+ MPG for the remaining three games against weak opponents.
recommendations.rationale: 68 games at 7.9 MPG is dressed but not developed. Same logic as Spezza: POTE 99, weak opponents left, development window.

recommendations.summary: Dress Spacek for the remaining games if a fourth-line spot opens up.
recommendations.rationale: Scratched at 19 with POTE 91 and morale 89. 50 games at 7.6 MPG. Dressing him costs nothing against a 30-38 team and keeps his morale stable heading into camp.

recommendations.summary: No change to Chlup's role. He is getting everything earned.
recommendations.rationale: 71 games, 16.9 MPG, 59 points at 19, morale 98. The usage is right.

recommendations.summary: Spacek and Spezza need a defined role at next camp or stop dressing them; both collapsed to under 5 MPG with rates below 0.30.
recommendations.rationale: Spacek 0.55→0.28 pts/g on 16.0→5.2 MPG at 19, Spezza 0.43→0.24 on 9.1→4.6 at 21. Both seasons are gone; camp assignment is the only lever left.

recommendations.summary: McCabe (0.48 pts/g, 82 GP, $3.00M), Jackman (0.39 on 29.4 MPG, $0.70M), and Klesla (0.31, $0.90M) are sell candidates this offseason.
recommendations.rationale: McCabe final rate 0.48 is below the 0.60 threshold set March 30. Jackman 0.39 on 30 MPG across 80 games. Klesla is two consecutive declining seasons. All three have value only in trade; Jackman's is the cheapest top-pair minutes in the league.

recommendations.summary: Eminger's contract expires in July; trade him before free agency or lose him for nothing.
recommendations.rationale: 0.37 pts/g on 15.9 MPG at 21 with $1.2M expiring. His value is eroding; after July he is a UFA loss.

recommendations.summary: Review the system fit for Richards and Nash in the offseason; both at 20 and 24 saw production drop sharply with no role or minutes change.
recommendations.rationale: Richards 1.08→0.71 on 16.9→15.8 MPG. Nash 0.83→0.42 on 12.9→13.2 MPG. Neither got less ice; both scored less. Two first-line-calibre players declining simultaneously without an obvious cause points at system fit.

recommendations.summary: Leave Chlup where he is. 0.62→0.88 pts/g on minutes doubling from 11.0 to 18.2 is the best trend on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: No grade moved on the card, meaning the production gain is pure confidence and usage. He belongs on the first line permanently.

recommendations.summary: No morale intervention needed; the room is at 88+ across the board with most players at 98-100.
recommendations.rationale: Lowest morale on the roster is Spezza at 88 and it is recovering (+3 recently). Abid's 13.8 MPG against 0.80 pts/g production is a next-camp structure issue with 3 games left, not a pre-game adjustment.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes for NYI. Every unit is assembled from the best available personnel for its role, and NYI's bottom six won't exploit the fourth-line checking gap.
recommendations.rationale: L1-L3 have proper role fit. L4 (checking 62, toughness 57) is structurally weak but against a 30-38 opponent this is not a matchup liability. Breaking chemistry tonight gains nothing.

recommendations.summary: We still have no forward outside L1-L2 who checks above 75. This is a roster acquisition target for the offseason.
recommendations.rationale: Checking inventory tops out at Jackman 87, Roberts 82, McCabe 82, Fischer 82 — all already assigned. Abid 70 is the best available checker on L3 and below. A shutdown middle-six forward who checks 80+ would fix the fourth-line problem permanently.

recommendations.summary: Play normal lines. NYI at 30-38-4 is a development-affordable opponent and the young guys are already in the lineup.
recommendations.rationale: We're 133 pts to their 84, 5-2-1 in the series. Spezza, Koltsov and Upshall are already on the fourth line; Chlup is on the second. Nothing to change.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is OVR 92, morale 100. DiPietro's REBC 62 is exploitable with our HERO-heavy top line. No reason to rest Luongo against a 30-win team.

recommendations.summary: Confirm Jackman as a summer sell: 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG at $0.70M x 3 is a minutes-absorber, not a producer.
recommendations.rationale: His rate has dropped from 0.48 (March 23, 73 GP) to 0.46 (80 GP). The load is confirmed. His value is the cheap top-pair minutes, not offense. Sell before the rate drops further.

recommendations.summary: Kaberle's contract is in its final year. The GM needs to decide on an extension before July or risk losing him as a UFA.
recommendations.rationale: 82 OVR, 0.60 pts/g on 20.8 MPG at age 27. GM called him a star and a keeper on Jan 15. At 1 year remaining the renewal is urgent.

recommendations.summary: McCabe confirmed at 0.76 pts/g on 82 games. Cleared the sell threshold. Stays.
recommendations.rationale: Final season rate 0.76 on 22.1 MPG at 29 with 4 years and $3.00M. He anchors the top pair alongside Fischer.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell in July: 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE at 24 years old closes both structural gaps simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Zero Toronto forwards carry 80+ toughness; only Sundin at 90 FACE carries 80+ faceoffs. Bell is the single player in the league who fixes both. CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring deals and $29.46M profit are motivated sellers.

recommendations.summary: If Bell is unobtainable, pivot to Avery: 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG at $400K with 2 years left.
recommendations.rationale: Avery is the cheapest path to all three gaps (faceoffs, toughness, checking) and at 25 with 2 years he is not a rental. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring deals are the most motivated sellers in the league.

recommendations.summary: Replace Roberts at the blue line with Stuart: 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, 87 base, 25, POTE 91.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts at 38 with an expiring deal is the anchor of the checking group (86 CHKG, 73 TOUG). When he walks, checking depth drops to five at 80+ with Tucker and Upshall as the only replacements. Stuart carries eight years of runway.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Iginla in July to fill the RW void Mogilny leaves at 36: 93 base, 140 points in 73 games, 27 years old.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny fell to 0.79 pts/g in the second half. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him. He closes both the scoring void and the structural toughness ceiling (85 TOUG) on one wing.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker for checking depth at 83 CHKG until an external acquisition arrives.
recommendations.rationale: He is the only rostered player above 80 CHKG who is not lined. At 30 with POTE 79 he is not a long-term piece, but he gives a seventh 80+ checker for the playoffs without cost.

recommendations.summary: Sign Colaiacovo to 5-6 years in July at whatever his renewal demands; at 22 with POTE 99 and $1.10M current salary, no future price is as low.
recommendations.rationale: 31 GP, 12 pts, POTE 99, age 22, expiring. If he walks the club has no first-rounder to replace a future top-pair blueliner.

recommendations.summary: Explore trading Fischer this summer while POTE 90 still gives him value; $3.70M for 4 years against 0.41 pts/g is dead money that only gets worse.
recommendations.rationale: Production halved over two seasons at 24. Four years means no relief before 2009. Moving him now, even at a salary dump, frees the most structurally damaging contract on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle on 2 years at approximately $2.50M; his POTE 75 and age 27 say the price rises but the ceiling does not.
recommendations.rationale: 44 pts in 74 GP at 27 is useful second-pair minutes but not a long-term asset. Two years splits his renewal away from the 13-player July cluster and keeps defence depth without locking five years of rising cost.

recommendations.summary: Renew Gaborik on a 5-6 year deal before any other renewal on the list.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base at 23, $1.10M expiring, 87 points last season. A 5-6 year lock is the single most important renewal; losing him to a bidding war at age 23 is the worst outcome on this list.

recommendations.summary: Renew Richards on a 5-6 year deal, second on the priority list.
recommendations.rationale: 24 years old, 64 points, 70 FACE (best draw-taker on the roster), $1.00M expiring. Lock the second-center position for 5+ years.

recommendations.summary: Renew Nash on a 5-6 year deal despite low production this season.
recommendations.rationale: Age 20, $1.20M expiring, 0.42 pts/g on 13.2 MPG. The age makes this a development contract, not a production contract. Renew before he improves and the price rises.

recommendations.summary: Renew Eminger on a 5-6 year deal.
recommendations.rationale: 21, POTE 99, $1.20M expiring. The GM's February 19 order is that the defensive core stays. This is the highest-potential defenseman on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Renew Kaberle on 4-5 years, not 5-6.
recommendations.rationale: 27, $1.90M expiring, starting-pairing defenseman. A deal through age 31-32 protects against the decline tail. Shorter than the young core's terms.

recommendations.summary: Renew Colaiacovo on 2 years, conditional on the camp audition.
recommendations.rationale: 22, $1.10M expiring. The coach wants full minutes in the remaining games. Give him the 4-game audition now, then decide at camp whether 2 years is enough or he earns a longer look.

recommendations.summary: Renew Chistov on 2-3 years.
recommendations.rationale: 21, $1.10M expiring. Cheap, young, not yet proven. A short deal preserves flexibility while he develops.

recommendations.summary: Renew Alexeev on 2 years if season production supports it; otherwise let go.
recommendations.rationale: 23, $1.10M expiring. At this age and salary the downside of a short renewal is small, but if his points-per-game is below 0.30 the roster spot is better used on an UFA signing or a young body from a trade.

recommendations.summary: Renew Tellqvist on 3-4 years.
recommendations.rationale: 25, POTE high 90s, $0.80M expiring. Cheapest goalie insurance in the league. The GM's January order: give him time to develop.

recommendations.summary: Renew Abid on 2 years.
recommendations.rationale: 25, TOUG 80, CHKG 80, $0.40M expiring. The cheapest toughness on the roster and the coach's checking gap keeps him relevant.

recommendations.summary: Do not renew Belfour; let him walk in July.
recommendations.rationale: 39, $6.50M expiring. He will not accept a reduced deal at this age. $6.50M for a 40-year-old is the number that ends the conversation. Luongo at 91 base and Tellqvist cover the crease.

recommendations.summary: Do not renew Roberts; let him walk in July.
recommendations.rationale: 38, $2.70M expiring. The March 21 renewal order flagged his departure. The toughness gap is better solved by Bell or a younger body.

recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri if available on the UFA market; POTE 98 at $1.10M is the best value in the pool.
recommendations.rationale: LA, 22, POTE 98, 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M expiring. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring cannot retain both him and Frolov.

recommendations.summary: Dress Colaiacovo and give him full minutes in all 4 remaining games before the camp audition.
recommendations.rationale: Coach flagged on April 13. NYI is 30-38, the remaining opponents are weak. Seeding is locked at 133 points. These are the only live development minutes before September.

recommendations.summary: Auto-draft the 4th-rounder on June 8 unless scouting reports suggest a goalie worth selecting.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto owns no pick better than a 4th. The manual says auto-draft is adequate without upgraded scouting. The January 22 standing order to target goalies in the draft applies where a prospect is available.

recommendations.summary: July priority: sign or acquire Iginla (93 base, 27, 140pts/73GP, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring) to replace Mogilny at RW and partially close the toughness ceiling.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 70 pts with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him. He closes both the RW scoring void and the structural toughness problem simultaneously. His TOUG 85 is the highest among any top scorer available.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell (82 base, 24, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, $900K, 2y) — the Coach's exact request for a forward who checks 75+ and wins draws.
recommendations.rationale: CHI at 78 pts with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit are motivated sellers. Bell is the only league-wide player closing toughness, checking, and faceoffs simultaneously on a re-signable deal. Price exceeds Tucker-plus-4th; may require the over-80 pick mechanic via Roberts.

recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri as UFA: 22, POTE 98, 60pts/61GP, $1.10M expiring. LA at 79 pts with 14 expiring on $52.43M cannot retain him.
recommendations.rationale: Highest potential-to-cost ratio in the July class. No trade capital needed, only cap-space equivalent in our payroll. LA must prioritize Frolov or other pieces over him.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Stuart (87 base, 25, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91) to replace Roberts on the blue line with eight years of runway.
recommendations.rationale: SJ at 76 pts with 13 expiring are in sell mode. Stuart's 80 TOUG is the only available defenceman closing the toughness gap on D. Acceptance uncertain — SJ are not tanking and may hold a POTE 91 blueliner.

recommendations.summary: If Iginla stays at CGY, pivot to Marleau (89 base, 25, 98pts, $1.60M expiring) as the RW/LW scoring target from SJ's rebuild.
recommendations.rationale: Same club as Stuart, same sell mode. 98 points at 25 on $1.60M is the second-best production-to-cost in the market after Iginla himself.

recommendations.summary: If ATL retains Kovalchuk and Heatley hits UFA, he is the fallback RW target: 91 base, 24, 96pts/58GP, expiring.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 84 pts with 11 expiring on $36.79M payroll face the binary. Kovalchuk (21, 104pts) is more likely retained at his age. Heatley then reaches the market.

recommendations.summary: Sign Reid (77 base, 23, FACE 80, POTE 94, $600K expiring) as bottom-six centre for faceoff depth without spending the 4th-rounder.
recommendations.rationale: STL at 86 pts with only 8 expiring are not desperate, but at $600K expiring he hits UFA automatically. FACE 80 at 23 with POTE 94 is the cheapest faceoff depth available anywhere.

recommendations.summary: If Belfour retires this summer, Theodore (91 base, 28, $5.50M expiring) becomes the backup target: MTL at 66 pts with 15 expiring cannot retain him.
recommendations.rationale: The GM closed goalie monitoring March 19 with Luongo and Belfour. Theodore only re-enters if Belfour does not return. Flagging now so we are ready if the scenario triggers.

recommendations.summary: Daze (89 base, 127pts/82GP, $3.00M expiring) carries the highest production on any expiring deal. If 26-28, he supersedes Heatley as the RW target.
recommendations.rationale: CHI at 78 pts with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit are sellers. Age remains unverified — his DOB could not be confirmed in prior attempts. If over 30, his $3.00M for 2-3 years is a rental that blocks a younger solution.

recommendations.current: Koltsov ($1.10M, 23, LW, POTE 94, 19 pts in 38 GP, 2y)
recommendations.summary: Trade Koltsov to LA for Avery; he closes toughness, checking, and faceoffs simultaneously — the Coach's exact request in one player.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 79 points with 14 expiring contracts and $52.43M payroll are restructuring and a 23-year-old at POTE 94 and $1.10M is the kind of cheap upside they accumulate. We save $700K and gain a proven 25-year-old who fixes three gaps. Acceptance uncertain; Koltsov's POTE is high but he has not yet produced.

recommendations.proposed: Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, $900K, 2y)
recommendations.summary: Trade Tucker plus the 4th-rounder to Chicago for Bell; he is the best available player who closes both toughness and faceoff gaps at age 24.
recommendations.rationale: CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit are motivated sellers. We save $400K. The package sits below Bell's assessed value (my estimate 74-76 vs his 82), so Chicago may decline, but their financial position and sell-mode may override that. Acceptance genuinely uncertain.

recommendations.proposed: Fleury (RW, 89 base, 93 TOUG, 77 CHKG, 71 FACE, 44 pts in 60 GP, $4.30M expiring)
recommendations.summary: If Fleury reaches UFA, consider a two-year deal at $3.5-4.0M as a partial toughness fix, but only if the RW scoring plan (Iginla/Heatley) has not consumed the money.
recommendations.rationale: 89 TOUG closes the Coach's toughness request outright, but 71 FACE and 77 CHKG only barely qualify. The $4.30M he earned last year competes with Cammalleri (POTE 98, age 22) and Iginla (93 base). Lower priority than either.

recommendations.summary: Goalie monitoring task (#2) is closed; Luongo (92, 26, 2 yrs) and Belfour (91, 39, expiring) stay for the playoffs per your 2005-03-19 order.
recommendations.rationale: GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19. DiPietro eliminated at 79 base on 2005-03-14. Luongo acquired and on roster. Nothing left to monitor.

recommendations.summary: Dress Spacek for the remaining games against NYI and other weak opponents.
recommendations.rationale: Spacek is 19, 0.34 pts/g on 7.6 MPG across 50 games, and has been scratched. With four games left against weak opposition (NYI at 30-38 tonight), this is the last cheap window to give him real games before offseason decisions.

recommendations.summary: Dress Alexeev for the remaining games against weak opponents.
recommendations.rationale: Alexeev is at 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG when he played (30 points, 55 games) and has been out of the lineup for 27 games. At 23 he is close to a roster decision and deserves a fair look in low-stakes games before offseason choices.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza a genuine first-line camp audition next season or stop dressing him.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza has POTE 99 at 21 and has been given 6.7 MPG on the fourth line all season (46 GP, 0.33 pts/g). The season is gone, but the only lever left is a serious camp assignment next year where he earns his minutes rather than collecting scraps.

recommendations.summary: No change for Chlup, Gaborik, Nash, or any dressed player whose role matches his production.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup (0.83 pts/g, 16.9 MPG), Gaborik (1.21 pts/g, 20.5 MPG), and Nash (0.57 pts/g, 13.1 MPG) are all in roles that match what they have earned this season. Their minutes and lines are correct.

recommendations.summary: McCabe goes back on the sell list; his final season rate is 0.48 pts/g across 82 games, not the 0.76 I previously reported.
recommendations.rationale: He scored 0.09 pts/g in his last 58 games after a 1.42 pace through 24. At 29 with 4 years and $3.00M, a D at 0.48 is a sell while the contract still has term and the name still carries value.

recommendations.summary: Give Chistov a middle-six audition at camp; his rate held at 0.30 while minutes rose 50% from 9.5 to 14.0.
recommendations.rationale: At 21, holding production under increased load is the correct development pattern. He has earned the look.

recommendations.summary: No action needed on Kaberle; at 0.62 pts/g on 21.5 MPG and rising, he is the blue-line anchor for next season.
recommendations.rationale: The only D on the roster going the right direction. Build the pair structure around him next year.

recommendations.summary: Spacek's season is confirmed dead at 0.28 pts/g on 5.2 MPG. Offseason audition or stop dressing, same decision tree as Spezza and Upshall.
recommendations.rationale: The March bump never stuck. His season rate fell from 0.55 to 0.28 with minutes cut by two thirds.

recommendations.summary: No ice-time changes needed; lowest morale is 88 (Spezza) and it is not declining.
recommendations.rationale: The room sits at 98-100 across the core. Spezza at 88 is below his 10-MPG band on 6.7 MPG but the number is flat, not sliding. Spacek at 89 and Upshall at 91 are stable scratched/depth players within their bands. No intervention required.

recommendations.summary: Keep the fourth line as-is tonight; NYI is a develop-them night, not a maximize night.
recommendations.rationale: L4 checking mean 62 and toughness mean 57 confirm the roster gap, but against a 30-38 opponent the development priority applies per the standing principle. No one on the roster can fix the checking deficiency at any slot.

recommendations.summary: No line or pair changes for NYI. Current configuration handles them comfortably.
recommendations.rationale: 5-1-1 season series against a 30-38-4 club. Fischer/Jackman's 89/89 checking shuts down Yashin (64 CHKG) on their first line; McCabe's 84 CHKG handles Peca's puck battles on their second. Swapping pair slots to better isolate Peca gains little against a team we've beaten six times and risks disrupting chemistry late in the season.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 92 OVR and morale 100, facing a team generating 2.00 GF/game. No fatigue icon visible in the lineup sheet tonight.

recommendations.summary: Sell Jackman this offseason at $0.70M x 3; his final season is 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: 37 points in 80 games confirms the decline. His value is the cheap minutes he eats for a contender, not his production.

recommendations.summary: Sell Klesla this offseason; second consecutive declining season locks the call at 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG.
