recommendations.rationale: 0.38 at age 22, 0.37 at 23 on flat minutes. $0.90M x 2 still has tradeable value.

recommendations.summary: Move Eminger before July 1 or lose him for nothing; 0.36 pts/g at age 21 with an expiring deal.
recommendations.rationale: 64 games, 23 points, $1.20M expiring. Any return beats zero in free agency.

recommendations.summary: Line Afinogenov immediately; he is 90 scoring, 96 speed, 25 years old and in no unit.
recommendations.rationale: Afinogenov carries 90 overall scoring, 96 speed, 87 playmaking, and 95 durability at age 25. He is on the roster but not lined. The coach's scoring depth is 10 at 80+ without him; leaving him scratched wastes the second-best speed rating on the club.

recommendations.summary: Toughness gap is structural at zero players 80+ TOUG; Bell remains the only known fix closing toughness, checking, and faceoffs simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Jackman 75 is the best stored TOUG on the roster. Bell at 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE is the single league-wide player closing all three voids. The coach confirmed the fourth-line gap at 61 checking mean and 57 toughness mean on April 9 and stated no bench player fixes it.

recommendations.summary: Faceoff depth is one man (Sundin 90 FACE at 34); Chlup at 75 is the only successor and is 19. Any acquisition of a faceoff-capable centre (Bell 82, Avery 93) addresses this directly.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin is 34 and the only Toronto player at 80+ FACE. Chlup is 75 at 19 and the coach names him first-line centre next season, meaning he inherits faceoff duty without a proven backup. The gap has no internal fix inside two seasons.

recommendations.summary: Hold Tucker as a chip only if the return replaces his 83 CHKG; trading him drops checking depth to 5 at 80+ without addressing the toughness gap.
recommendations.rationale: Standing order (March 19) designates Tucker and the 4th-rounder as the only chips. Tucker's 83 CHKG is the third-highest on the roster. If traded for a 74-76 base player (per Tucker-fourth-cannot-reach-targets), checking drops to five 80+ men and toughness stays at zero.

recommendations.summary: After Roberts walks, durability drops to 3 players at 80+ (Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92, Abid 90); no internal replacement exists for his 98 DUR / 88 CHKG at the top pair.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts at 38 with an expiring contract is the 98 durability and 88 checking anchor. McCabe at 86 CHKG and 75 DUR is the next man, a significant drop on both axes. The Stuart target (89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91 at 25) is the only known replacement addressing both the checking and durability loss.

recommendations.summary: Lock all five on 5-6 year deals at the start of July; they are collectively at $7.70M now and will demand $20-25M combined if they hit free agency with a year of top-nine experience on their resumes.
recommendations.rationale: Thirteen contracts totaling $21.30M expire simultaneously. These five are the core and their current salaries ($1.00-1.90M) are the cheapest they will ever be. The $29.51M profit absorbs any raise they command.

recommendations.summary: Open a trade window for Sundin (34, $8.40M, 5 years, 91 pts) during the summer of 2006 or the 2006-07 deadline; his value at 36 is lower than at 35 and the 5 remaining years shrink every season.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin's POTE 60 means he will not improve further. At 34 he is maximally valuable. By 37 he is $8.40M on a bottom-six player. Converting him into a 25-28 year old with 3+ years left accelerates the window while Luongo, Gaborik, Richards, and Chlup are still ascending.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla (93 base, 27, 140 pts/73 GP, $6.50M expiring) as a July UFA signing; he replaces Mogilny (36, declining, $5.50M dead money) and closes the toughness ceiling simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny cannot be traded at 36 on a 2-year $5.50M deal. His $5.50M is sunk cost for two seasons. Iginla at 27 with TOUG 85 is both the scoring replacement and the structural fix the Coach has flagged since February.

recommendations.summary: Extend Luongo (26, 91 base, POTE 97, $1.60M, 2 years) to a 5-year deal before the 2006-07 season; his value doubles after one more 40-win campaign.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at $1.60M for a 97-POTE starter is the cheapest elite asset on the roster. Two years left means he hits UFA at 28 in his prime. Lock him before that window closes.

recommendations.summary: Do not panic about the $21.30M expiring cluster; the $29.51M profit absorbs every raise the core demands and there is no salary cap to breach.
recommendations.rationale: Revenue is $101.97M against $60.04M payroll. Even after locking the core at a combined +$15M raise, payroll lands near $75M and profit stays above $24M. The constraint is not money, it is time to negotiate before free agency.

recommendations.summary: Renew Gaborik on 6 years at a significant raise as the first deal of the summer.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base, 87 points, POTE 90, age 23, $1.10M expiring. He is the team's asset and cannot be re-signed mid-contract; July is the only window.

recommendations.summary: Renew Richards on 5 years after completing the system-fit review.
recommendations.rationale: 64 points, age 24, POTE 99, $1.00M expiring. The coach's decline flag (1.08 to 0.71 pts/g) needs explanation but does not change the renewal case at his age and grade.

recommendations.summary: Renew Kaberle on 5 years.
recommendations.rationale: Age 27, $1.90M expiring, top-pairing defenceman at his prime age. No alternative available at comparable cost.

recommendations.summary: Renew Eminger on 5-6 years before his value moves to the open market.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99, age 21, $1.20M expiring. GM protected him from trade in January; the same logic protects him from losing him in July.

recommendations.summary: Renew Nash on 5-6 years after the coach's system-fit review explains the rate decline.
recommendations.rationale: Age 20, $1.20M expiring, but production halved from 0.83 to 0.42 pts/g on identical minutes. Renew, but not before the review.

recommendations.summary: Renew Colaiacovo on 3 years, not 5-6.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 at 22, but only 31 games. Three years to age 25 gives the sample needed before a star-length commitment.

recommendations.summary: Renew Chistov on 2 years as a depth forward.
recommendations.rationale: Age 21, $1.10M expiring. Young, cheap, fills a roster slot. No reason to release.

recommendations.summary: Renew Alexeev on 2 years as a depth forward.
recommendations.rationale: Age 23, 0.55 pts/g in 55 games, $1.10M expiring. Coach wants more minutes for him; he is a bottom-six producer.

recommendations.summary: Renew Upshall on 2 years as a depth forward.
recommendations.rationale: Age 21, $1.20M expiring. Same logic as Chistov and Alexeev: cheap youth fills the roster.

recommendations.summary: Renew Abid on 2 years. $0.40M for TOUG 80 and CHKG 80 is unrepeatable.
recommendations.rationale: Age 25, $0.40M expiring. The cheapest physical presence on any roster in the league.

recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour 2 years at half his salary; accept his decline and proceed with Luongo as the confirmed number one.
recommendations.rationale: Age 39, $6.50M expiring. The GM's own January read was that he would not accept a reduced deal. Walking him frees $6.50M for the July market.

recommendations.summary: Do not offer Roberts a renewal. He walks in July.
recommendations.rationale: Age 38, $2.70M expiring. No development or role case at his age and cost.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla as the top July signing: closes both the RW scoring void and the toughness ceiling in one move.
recommendations.rationale: 93 base, 140 points in 73 games, TOUG 85, age 27, $6.50M expiring from a 70-point Calgary club that cannot retain him. Mogilny fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g at 36.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Cammalleri as the second July signing: cheapest high-ceiling forward available.
recommendations.rationale: Age 22, POTE 98, 60 points in 61 games, $1.10M expiring. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring contracts cannot retain him.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bell as the third July signing: the only league-wide player closing toughness and faceoffs simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, age 24. The coach quantified the fourth-line toughness gap at mean 57; Bell at 88 is the answer.

recommendations.summary: No further trade activity is possible before the summer; focus all effort on the renewal queue and July market.
recommendations.rationale: The deadline passed 25 days ago on March 19. The GM closed all active trade monitoring on that date. Tucker and the 4th rounder remain available as summer sweeteners if a larger package requires them.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bell from CHI in July; he is 24, 80 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, $900K with 2 years left.
recommendations.rationale: Only player in the league closing toughness, checking, and faceoff gaps simultaneously on a re-signable deal. CHI at 78 points with $31.73M profit and 10 expiring are the most motivated sellers in the league.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Heatley from ATL in July or as UFA; 91 base, 131 pts/79 GP, age 24, POTE 85, $1.10M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Replaces Mogilny (36, dead money) with the best RW scorer on the market. ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring cannot retain both him and Kovalchuk. Whichever ATL keeps, the other is available.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Stuart from SJ in July; 87 base, POTE 91, 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG, age 25, $1.80M expiring, 52 pts/77 GP.
recommendations.rationale: Replaces Roberts (88 CHKG, 98 durability, walks at 38) and closes the zero-80-TOUG gap at defense. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring and $20.74M profit cannot retain all 13.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Komisarek from MTL in July; 77 base, POTE 91, age 23, $1.10M expiring, 82 GP and 82 pts.
recommendations.rationale: 82 points from a 77-base blueliner at 23 is the most extreme production-to-grade ratio in the league. MTL at 66 points with 15 expiring are the biggest sellers. If POTE 91 is credible, he becomes a top-pair D within two seasons.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bouwmeester from FLA in July or as UFA; 81 base, POTE 95, age 21, $1.20M expiring, 27 pts/79 GP.
recommendations.rationale: Best young defenseman available. FLA at 76 points with 19 expiring deals (most in the league) and $13.64M profit cannot retain him. POTE 95 at 21 on $1.20M is the cheapest long-term blue-line fix in the league.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Nabokov from SJ in July; 90 base, POTE 90, age 29, GAA 2.66 in 69 GP, $3.60M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Fits the January 15 standing order for a high-90s goalie from a non-contender. Cheaper than Theodore ($3.60M vs $5.50M) with four more potential points and a lower GAA. SJ at 76 with 13 expiring cannot retain all of them.

recommendations.summary: Alternate goalie target: Theodore from MTL, 91 base, POTE 88, age 28, GAA 3.29, $5.50M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: MTL at 66 points with 15 expiring and $21.59M profit will move him. Higher base than Nabokov (91 vs 90) but $1.90M more expensive and four fewer potential points. Pursue only if Nabokov stays at SJ.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Doan from PHX in July if Heatley stays; 87 base, 88 TOUG, 93 CHKG, age 28, POTE 79, $2.40M expiring, 62 pts/82 GP.
recommendations.rationale: Closes RW scoring AND toughness in one acquisition. Harder to get than Heatley because PHX at 93 points are in the race. A fallback for the RW vacancy that also addresses the structural toughness gap.

recommendations.summary: Target Belanger from LA as a UFA signing; 82 base, 97 FACE, 79 TOUG, 83 CHKG, age 27, $700K expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin is 34 with POTE 60 and five years at $8.40M. Belanger gives a 97 FACE and 83 CHKG second-line center for $700K. LA at 79 with 14 expiring will let him walk. Not a Bell substitute but a complement.

recommendations.summary: Secondary target: Drury from BUF, 89 base, 99 pts/82 GP, age 28, POTE 80, $2.00M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Elite scoring winger at 28 without a toughness component. BUF at 84 with 10 expiring and $24.30M profit may sell. Fill one gap (scoring depth) where Heatley fills two (scoring + youth trajectory).

recommendations.summary: Probe Havlat from OTT; 87 base, 103 pts/82 GP, age 23, POTE 85, $900K expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Young LW scorer at 23 on $900K. OTT at 77 points with $32.36M profit are financially motivated but at 77 points with a 1-0 playoff run they may retain him. Worth a low-cost probe given the contract.

recommendations.summary: Depth target: Scatchard from NYI, 85 base, 85 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 84 FACE, age 29, $1.40M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: The best two-way center on the expiring market with genuine toughness (85 TOUG, 89 CHKG). NYI at 84 with 13 expiring may deal. At 29 with POTE unlisted his ceiling is set, but he closes the fourth-line checking gap immediately.

recommendations.summary: Daze is 29 with POTE 77 — he does not supersede Heatley as the RW target despite 127 points.
recommendations.rationale: The April 7 note set the test at 26-28. He is 29 with POTE 77 on $3.00M expiring from CHI. At that age and potential his ceiling is set and the cost is 2.7x Heatley. Heatley retains RW priority.

recommendations.current: Colaiacovo (D, 22, POTE 99, $1.10M expiring, 31 GP, 12 pts) + Tucker (LW, 30, $1.30M, 2 yrs left, CHKG 92, TOUG 88, 3 GP, 1 pt) + 4th round pick
recommendations.proposed: Bell (LW, 24, 82 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82, POTE 81, $1.10M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Offer Chicago Colaiacovo plus Tucker plus the 4th rounder for Bell. Closes all three structural gaps (toughness, checking, faceoffs) simultaneously.

A POTE 99 defenceman at 22 on $1.10M is a franchise prospect for a rebuilding club; Tucker adds 92 CHKG depth for two years at low cost; the 4th is free upside. Toronto shed $1.30M in net salary and close the only gap no internal player addresses. Colaiacovo finished eighth in our defensive depth chart with 31 GP and cannot displace Eminger, Klesla, Jackman, McCabe, or Kaberle. Acceptance uncertain: Chicago may value Bell's playoff contribution over a prospect-only rebuild.

recommendations.current: Alexeev (RW, 23, POTE 94, $1.10M expiring, 55 GP, 30 pts, BALA 90, SPEE 89) + Tucker (LW, 30, $1.30M, 2 yrs left, CHKG 92, TOUG 88) + 4th round pick
recommendations.summary: Offer Atlanta Alexeev plus Tucker plus the 4th rounder for Heatley. Replaces Mogilny (0.79 pts/g at 36, POTE 55, $5.50M, 2 years remaining, untradeable) with the best young RW available.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring deals cannot retain both Heatley and Kovalchuk (21, 89 base, 138 pts). They keep Kovalchuk; Heatley moves. Alexeev at POTE 94 with 90 BALA and 89 SPEE gives ATL a winger to develop alongside Kovalchuk; Tucker (92 CHKG) is the checking partner their top line needs. They shed $1.10M and gain $2.40M incoming, but with 11 contracts walking their payroll has enormous flexibility. Toronto's payroll change is zero net (shed $2.40M, gain $1.10M, Mogilny remains stuck). Acceptance uncertain: 131 points may command more than a POTE 94 prospect.

recommendations.current: Tucker (LW, 30, $1.30M, 2 yrs left, CHKG 92) + 4th round pick + 1 late-round pick (converted from Roberts via over-80 expiring mechanic)
recommendations.summary: If Bell and Heatley are unavailable, target Bouwmeester from Florida. FLA at 76 points with 19 expiring contracts (most in the league) cannot retain him.
recommendations.rationale: Bouwmeester at 21 with POTE 95 on $1.20M is the best young defenceman available and four years younger than Stuart at $600K cheaper. FLA's 19 expiring deals make them the league's biggest seller. Tucker gives them a checking winger for the bottom six; the two late picks help their rebuild. Toronto lose our only designated chip but gain a POTE 95 blueliner who could anchor the left side for five years. Acceptance uncertain: FLA at 76 points may retain him for one more season.

recommendations.current: Roberts (LW, 38, 81 base, CHKG 88, INJU 98, HERO 90, 82 pts/82 GP, $2.70M expiring)
recommendations.proposed: 1 draft pick (round 4 or 5, via over-80 expiring mechanic)
recommendations.summary: Before the season ends, convert Roberts to a draft pick rather than losing him for nothing in July. He is walking per the renewal plan.
recommendations.rationale: Any player above 80 base who will not be re-signed can be traded for a pick via the over-80 mechanic. Roberts at 81 base with 82 points and 98 durability is a playoff-relevant checking wing any contender would take at $2.70M for one year. Converting him yields a pick that strengthens Proposal 3 or adds to draft capital. Execute this in June before he clears.

recommendations.summary: Mogilny carries 2 years at $5.50M at age 36 with POTE 55. No club accepts this contract. Ride him out as a 13th forward or healthy scratch.
recommendations.rationale: The over-80 mechanic does not apply because he is not expiring. A 36-year-old with POTE 55 and two years of $5.50M has zero trade value. The salary is sunk cost. Plan around him: dress him only when the top twelve cannot play.

recommendations.summary: Goalie monitoring task is closed — Luongo (92, 26, $1.60M, 2yr) is on the roster, DiPietro eliminated at 79 base, and the GM explicitly shut down all goalie trade tasks on March 19.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo arrived from Florida via the Aebischer + R1 package confirmed 2005-01-25. DiPietro reads 79 base at 52 GP, 11 points below threshold. The GM's March 19 order closes all goalie monitoring.

recommendations.summary: If any games remain against weak opposition, dress Colaiacovo and give him full minutes.
recommendations.rationale: 31 games at 17.9 MPG on a POTE 99 defenceman at 22 is too thin a sample. The GM's standing order says development applies against beatable opponents. NYI at 30-38 qualifies.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza a real first-camp audition next September at centre with top-nine minutes, or remove him from the development plan.
recommendations.rationale: Two seasons, POTE 99, age 21, 6.7 MPG this year down from 9.1 last window. He has not had a single extended run at NHL pace. If the club wants that potential to become something, it needs 15+ MPG in camp or the roster spot is being wasted.

recommendations.summary: Same as Spezza: real camp audition or stop dressing him.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99, age 21, 68 games dressed but 7.9 MPG. He is technically on the roster but not developing. Two POTE 99s at 21 in the same organisation both stuck on the fourth line is a structural problem with how we use the bottom six.

recommendations.summary: Stahle needs a genuine camp audition or he should be exposed. Four games in two seasons proves nothing.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 96 at 20, 4 GP this year, 17.8 MPG in those 4 games when he did play suggests the coaching staff liked what they saw briefly. That's either a reason to play him or evidence the plan is incoherent.

recommendations.summary: Chlup, Gaborik, and Nash got the games they earned. No intervention needed on their development paths.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup 71 GP at 16.9 MPG and 0.83 pts/g, Gaborik 82 GP at 20.5 MPG and 1.21 pts/g, Nash 69 GP at 13.1 MPG. The opportunity was there. Their next step is production growth, which is a system question not an ice-time question.

recommendations.summary: McCabe returns to the sell list: 0.48 pts/g over 58 second-window games on 21.5 MPG, below the 0.60 threshold.
recommendations.rationale: December rate of 1.42 over 24 games was the outlier. 58 games at 0.48 at age 29 with $3.00M x 4 is a sell before the contract becomes an anchor.

recommendations.summary: Klesla confirmed sell: third consecutive declining season, 0.31 pts/g at 23 on flat 14.9 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: No development visible across three seasons. At 23 the trend is unambiguous and $0.90M x 2 is expiring leverage that erodes each month.

recommendations.summary: Jackman confirmed sell: 0.39 pts/g on 29.4 MPG at 24. His value is top-pair minutes at $0.70M, not his production.
recommendations.rationale: The load-production gap is structural and unfixable within his current role. Move him while another club still pays for the minutes.

recommendations.summary: Spezza's season is a write-off at 4.6 MPG and 0.24 pts/g. Offseason camp audition is the only lever.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 with no opportunity. Either he earns a real role at camp or we stop dressing him and the development stalls permanently.

recommendations.summary: Upshall same situation as Spezza: 4.8 MPG, 0.27 pts/g. Camp decides whether he's roster-relevant.
recommendations.rationale: Minutes collapsed from 13.4 to 4.8 with no grade movement. At 21 this is either a role problem or a coaching decision to make at camp.

recommendations.summary: Spacek at 5.2 MPG and 0.28 pts/g is the same offseason camp decision as Spezza and Upshall.
recommendations.rationale: The March bump to 12+ MPG clearly did not hold. He's at 5.2 now. Camp audition or stop dressing.

recommendations.summary: Nash needs an offseason system-fit review: 0.42 pts/g on flat 13.2 MPG at age 20.
recommendations.rationale: Role unchanged, production halved. At 20 the expected direction is up, so either the system doesn't suit him or his form needs time. Review before next camp.

recommendations.summary: Richards needs an offseason system-fit review: 0.71 pts/g at 24 on minutes flat around 16.
recommendations.rationale: No role change explains the drop from 1.08 to 0.71. At 24 this is unexpected. Before pencilling him as first-line centre next year, determine if the system is wrong for him.

recommendations.summary: Leave all lines as they are for NYI; the room is healthy with the lowest active morale at 88 (Spezza).
recommendations.rationale: Average morale across the roster is above 95 with only Spezza below 90 at 88. With 4 games remaining there is no minutes adjustment that fixes his situation without breaking a working fourth line for a meaningless window.

recommendations.proposed: a depth forward with 75+ checking and ideally a faceoff number above 60
recommendations.summary: We need one more forward who checks 75+ and wins draws — nobody on this roster fits that role outside our top-six.
recommendations.rationale: L4 has checking mean 62, toughness mean 57, faceoff mean 51. The four best checkers (Jackman 87, Roberts 82, McCabe 82, Fischer 82) are all on L1-L2. No arrangement of existing personnel builds a checking fourth line.

recommendations.summary: Lines 1-3, P1, P2, K1 and K2 are correctly constructed. Leave them alone for NYI.
recommendations.rationale: Each top-three line has its role covered: L1 two-way skill, L2 veteran support around Chlup, L3 Klesla's 91 checking plus Richards' 94 clutch. PP units have shooters and quarterbacks. K1/K2 ordering justified by Sundin's 88 faceoffs.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo; check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 92 OVR against a 2.00 GF/G opponent is the obvious start. Standing order: verify no tired icon before locking.

recommendations.summary: No line changes. Roll the standard four lines unchanged.
recommendations.rationale: TOR leads the season series 5-1-1 (21-12 in goals) and outscores NYI by 1.60 per game across the board. Every forward line has a quality edge. The auto-pairing puts Fischer/Jackman against Hamrlik/Niinimaa (both 83/81) and our top pair handles that; the third pair against their 70/71 bottom unit is a mismatch in our favour.

recommendations.summary: Defenceman sell list confirmed at season's end: Jackman (0.46 pts/g, 29.6 MPG), Klesla (0.37 pts/g, 14.8 MPG), Eminger (0.36 pts/g, expiring July). No change from last delivery.
recommendations.rationale: Final season rates confirm all three calls. Jackman slipped 0.48 to 0.46 over his last 7 games, Klesla holds at 0.37 for a second straight decline, Eminger continues sliding with his contract expiring. McCabe (0.76), Kaberle (0.59), Fischer (0.53) confirmed as the core three.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker on the fourth line for the playoffs; his 83 CHKG is the only unused forward checking grade above 80.
recommendations.rationale: The coach's fourth-line checking mean is 61 and no bench forward exceeds 82. Tucker at 83 CHKG and 30 is the single internal piece that lifts that line's defensive capability. His 70 TOUG does not fix toughness but the checking upgrade is real.

recommendations.proposed: Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE)
recommendations.summary: Bell remains the only league-wide player who closes all three forward-side gaps simultaneously; pursue in July when CHI's 10 expiring contracts force them to move him.
recommendations.rationale: Zero Toronto forwards carry 80+ TOUG and only Sundin clears 80 at FACE. Bell at 88/86/82 across toughness/checking/faceoffs at age 24 with POTE 81 is the sole fix. ENDU 71 means short shifts initially but the grades are structural, not form.

recommendations.proposed: Stuart (SJ, D, 25, 87 base, 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG, POTE 91)
recommendations.summary: Stuart replaces Roberts at 38 with eight years of development remaining and the only available defenceman carrying both 80+ TOUG and 89 CHKG.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts (86 CHKG, 98 DUR) walks this summer. Jackman (87 CHKG) and McCabe (86 CHKG) are the remaining 80+ checkers but neither has above 75 TOUG. Stuart at 87 base with 80 TOUG and POTE 91 is the only target that maintains the checking and adds toughness at 25.

recommendations.summary: Mogilny at 36 declining to 0.79 pts/g confirms the RW scoring crisis; Heatley or Doan are the July priority for that position.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny's 94 base cannot hide 0.79 pts/g at 36. The club needs a 25-year-old RW with scoring ability. Gaborik covers one wing; the other has no internal successor above 80 base.

recommendations.summary: Scoring, speed, playmaking, stamina, and clutch are all covered with multiple 80+ players; no action needed in those roles.
recommendations.rationale: 21 players at 80+ speed, 10 at 80+ scoring, 11 at 80+ stamina, 9 at 80+ clutch. The roster is deep where the gaps are not.

recommendations.summary: Extend Chlup to 5-6 years this July at his current price range before his contract expires in 2006 and his asking price doubles.
recommendations.rationale: He is 19 with POTE 95 and 59 points. If he reaches 70+ points next season, a renewal costs $5-6M. Locking him now saves $2-3M a year for five seasons. His two-year deal expires in July 2006 alongside Luongo and Klesla, creating a second mass-renewal window.

recommendations.current: Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, Kaberle (all 1yr, $6.40M combined)
recommendations.summary: Sign the five one-year core players to 5-6 year deals in July 2005; their combined production (297 points) is the roster's offensive base and they will walk simultaneously without contracts.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik (99 pts at $1.10M), Richards (66 pts at $1.00M), Nash (39 pts), Eminger (POTE 99), Kaberle (44 pts) are all expiring. Their current salaries total $6.40M; market-rate renewals will cost $20-25M. With $29.51M profit, the payroll absorbs this if Belfour ($6.50M) and Roberts ($2.70M) walk.

recommendations.summary: Extend Luongo to 5-6 years in the same July window as the core forwards to avoid facing his renewal alongside Chlup in July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: He is 26 with POTE 97 at $1.60M. If he improves to 93+ base, his market value jumps. Extending him now at $3-4M spreads the renewal cost across years rather than hitting all at once in 2006 with Chlup and Klesla.

recommendations.summary: Do not re-sign Belfour or Roberts; their $9.20M combined is the payroll headroom that funds the core extensions.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 39 with POTE 50. Roberts is 38 with POTE 52. Both are declining. Luongo (26, POTE 97) is the number-one goalie and Ouellet (23, POTE 97) provides backup. Freeing $9.20M directly funds two of the core extensions.

recommendations.summary: Mogilny's contract runs through 2006-07 and cannot be renegotiated; absorb the cost and plan to not re-sign at 38.
recommendations.rationale: At 0.79 pts/g by March and declining, he produces 30-35 points next season for $5.50M. No mid-contract renegotiation is possible and no team wants a 37-year-old with a year left on a big deal. This is sunk cost for one more season.

recommendations.summary: Sign Gaborik to a 5-6 year extension in July before any bidding war.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base overall, 87 points, POTE 90, age 23, $1.10M expiring. He is the team's top producer and the single biggest walk risk.

recommendations.summary: Sign Richards to a 5-6 year extension in July.
recommendations.rationale: 64 points at 24 on $1.00M. Second-longest-tenured centre on the roster and the cheapest top-nine C in the league.

recommendations.summary: Sign Eminger to a 5-6 year extension in July.
recommendations.rationale: Age 21, POTE 99, $1.20M expiring. GM vetoed trading him in January because his ceiling exceeds Chara's; same logic locks him long.

recommendations.summary: Sign Nash to a 5-6 year extension in July.
recommendations.rationale: Age 20, $1.20M. His scoring halved without a role change, which is a system-fit question the coach flagged, not a talent loss. Option value at that price is enormous.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle on 2-3 years, not 5-6.
recommendations.rationale: Age 27, $1.90M. His ceiling is set; a long deal at his price blocks payroll for the younger defencemen (Eminger, Colaiacovo).

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Tellqvist on 2-3 years as backup and trade asset.
recommendations.rationale: Age 25, POTE high 90s per GM's January note, $0.80M. Luongo is the starter; Tellqvist is insurance and the goalie-potential the GM wants on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Abid on 1-2 years. At $0.40M with TOUG 80 and CHKG 80 he is the cheapest 4th-line toughness available.
recommendations.rationale: The coach's gap is toughness mean 57 and checking mean 61 on L4. Abid at TOUG 80, CHKG 80 for four hundred thousand fills half that gap at the lowest possible cost.

recommendations.summary: Let Belfour walk at expiry. He walks in July; the GM confirmed this on March 19.
recommendations.rationale: Age 39, $6.50M. Luongo is the starter at 91 base with 2 years left. Belfour was kept solely as playoff insurance and now departs, freeing $6.50M.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk at expiry.
recommendations.rationale: Age 38, $2.70M. Named for walking in the March 21 renewal priority. The D-core moves to Eminger, Kaberle, Colaiacovo and one summer acquisition.

recommendations.summary: Do not renew Upshall ($1.20M) until camp determines whether he can earn a dressable role.
recommendations.rationale: Coach's March 9 report: 'needs a genuine camp audition next season or he stops being dressable.' At 21 with $1.20M, the club should not commit without a role.

recommendations.summary: Target Bell (CHI, age 24, 82 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82, POTE 81) as a summer trade to fix the fourth-line checking and faceoff gap.
recommendations.rationale: Coach's gap: checking mean 61, toughness 57, faceoffs 50. Bell closes both halves simultaneously. Chicago are 73 points with ten expiring deals and $29.46M profit; they are sellers this summer.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Heatley or Doan in July to replace Mogilny's decline at top-six RW.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g at 36. The RW scoring void is confirmed and locks the July priority. Neither Heatley nor Doan will be cheap; the $9.20M freed by Belfour and Roberts funds the deal.

recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri (LA, age 22, POTE 98, 60 pts, $1.10M expiring) as a UFA if LA cannot retain him.
recommendations.rationale: LA are 79 points with 14 expiring contracts and cannot keep both him and Frolov. POTE 98 at 60 points and $1.10M is the highest-value UFA on the market.

recommendations.summary: At the June 8 draft, use the fourth-rounder on the best available goalie with high POTE per the GM's standing instruction.
recommendations.rationale: No pick better than a fourth-rounder. GM's January 22 order: scout for goalies in the draft. A high-POTE project behind Tellqvist costs nothing and builds the position for 2007.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Iginla as a July UFA signing; 93 base, TOUG 85, 140 pts/73 GP, $6.50M expiring from CGY at 70 points.
recommendations.rationale: He closes the RW scoring crisis (Mogilny at 0.79 pts/g) and the structural toughness ceiling (our roster max is 75) in one signing. CGY is a 70-point rebuild with 10 expiring deals; Belfour and Roberts walking frees $9.20M against his $6.50M ask.

recommendations.summary: Trade for Bell in July; TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82, 82 base, age 24, $900K with 2 years left from CHI at 78 points.
recommendations.rationale: He is the only league-wide player closing the Coach's exact specification (checks above 75, draws above 55%). Chicago at 78 points with $31.73M profit and 10 expiring are structurally motivated to rebuild but will demand a real package since they are profitable.

recommendations.summary: Target Stuart as a July UFA; 87 base, CHKG 83, POTE 92, $1.80M expiring, 30.8 MPG, age 25 from SJ at 76 points.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts is 38 and walking. Stuart at 25 with POTE 92 and 30.8 minutes a night is the only available D at his production level from a seller. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring cannot retain all 13.

recommendations.slot: right wing (top-six, fallback if Iginla unavailable)
recommendations.summary: Pursue Heatley via UFA or over-80 pick mechanic from ATL; 91 base, 96 pts/58 GP, age 24, expiring.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 84 points with $36.79M payroll (league lowest) and 11 expiring cannot retain both him and Kovalchuk. Kovalchuk at $1.10M is the cheaper keeper, making Heatley the likely one to leave.

recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri in July UFA; 79 base, POTE 98, 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M expiring, age 22 from LA at 79 points.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 79 points with 14 expiring on $52.43M payroll cannot retain all 14. Cammalleri at POTE 98 and 60 points for $1.10M is the highest-value depth addition available.

recommendations.slot: defence or top-six (from SJ, priority lower than Stuart)
recommendations.summary: Marleau (89 base, 98 pts, $1.60M, 25) is available from SJ but deprioritize below Stuart since Iginla fills the RW role.
recommendations.rationale: If SJ cannot keep both Stuart and Marleau, take Stuart. Iginla fills top-six RW; Marleau is redundant unless Iginla signs elsewhere.

recommendations.proposed: Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, $900K, 2 yrs, TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82)
recommendations.summary: Offer Tucker and the 4th-rounder to Chicago for Bell; this is the only single-move package that closes the Coach's fourth-line specification.
recommendations.rationale: Bell is the only player in the league clearing TOUG 75 and FACE 82 simultaneously. Chicago at 78 points with 10 expiring and POTE 81 on Bell have no retention argument. Payroll saves $400K. Acceptance uncertain because the value gap between 82 base and 79-POTE-30-year-old is real.

recommendations.current: Belfour (39, $6.50M expiring) and Roberts (38, $2.70M expiring) traded via the over-80 pick mechanic
recommendations.proposed: One or two draft picks of unknown round; then package those plus the 4th for Stuart (SJ, D, 25, 87 base, POTE 92, $1.80M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour and Roberts before July via the over-80 mechanic to generate picks, then offer the resulting pick plus the 4th to San Jose for Stuart.
recommendations.rationale: SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring on $45.39M cannot retain Stuart. The over-80 mechanic converts non-re-signing 80+ players into draft picks per the guide. If those picks are second or third round, SJ may deal; if they are fourths, the package is too thin. Must be sequenced before any Stuart conversation.

recommendations.current: Picks generated from Belfour/Roberts mechanic + 4th-rounder + possibly Tucker (if Bell deal not pursued)
recommendations.proposed: Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, $6.50M expiring, 140 pts/73 GP, TOUG 85, CHKG 79)
recommendations.summary: If the over-80 mechanic yields two or more mid-round picks, attempt to package them for Iginla from a Calgary club in full rebuild with 10 expiring and no re-signing path.
recommendations.rationale: Calgary at 70 points with $14.43M profit is in full rebuild and will not pay $6.50M+ to retain a 27-year-old with POTE 81. He either walks for nothing in July or trades for assets. We need first- or second-round capital to compete, which only the over-80 mechanic can generate. If he clears UFA, sign him at reduced salary using our 625 prestige and $29.51M profit.

recommendations.proposed: Heatley (ATL, RW, 24, 91 base, POTE 87, $1.10M expiring) via the over-80 mechanic if ATL shops him for our 4th
recommendations.summary: If ATL uses the over-80 pick mechanic on Heatley, offer our 4th-rounder directly for him; this closes RW scoring but not the fourth-line gap.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at $36.79M (lowest in the league) with 11 expiring cannot retain both Heatley and Kovalchuk. If they choose Kovalchuk at $1.10M and shop Heatley via the mechanic, our single 4th is the currency. This conflicts with the Bell proposal since both need the 4th; choose one.

recommendations.summary: Goalie monitoring task is complete and formally closed by the GM on 2005-03-19; no further action needed.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is on the roster at 92 overall with 2 years left at $1.60M. DiPietro eliminated at 79 base after 52 GP. GM closed all goalie trade tasks March 19.

recommendations.summary: Reinstate Colaiacovo for the remaining five games; he has POTE 99 at 22 and played only 31 games all season.
recommendations.rationale: When he played he averaged 17.9 MPG — the coaches already trust him at top-pair minutes. Benching him for veterans against weak opponents wastes the development window that remains.

recommendations.slot: fourth-line left wing or extra forward
recommendations.summary: Reinstate Spacek for the remaining five games as a development audition.
recommendations.rationale: At 19 with POTE 91 he played only 50 games at 7.6 MPG and is now scratched. Five games of live action beats five as a healthy scratch.

recommendations.slot: third or fourth line right wing
recommendations.summary: Reinstate Alexeev for the remaining five games; he produced 0.55 pts/g in 55 games and is scratched.
recommendations.rationale: 30 points in 55 games at age 23 earned him more than 8.3 MPG and a scratch. These are free games against a 30-38 team.

recommendations.summary: No change. Chlup at 19 is the success story: 59 points on 16.9 MPG, second line, production up under increased load.
recommendations.rationale: He has earned his role and is performing in it. No development concern.

recommendations.summary: No change. Gaborik at 99 points on 20.5 MPG in 82 games is where he belongs.
recommendations.rationale: First-line minutes, first-line production. The development is complete; he is a finished player.

recommendations.summary: Chlup is a first-line centre next season; his production rose from 0.62 to 0.88 under doubled minutes at 19.
recommendations.rationale: At 19, most players decline under a jump from 11 to 18 MPG. He went the other direction. Treat him as the franchise centre going into camp.

recommendations.summary: Spacek needs a real camp audition or stop dressing him; 0.28 pts/g on 5.2 MPG at 19 is not a development path.
recommendations.rationale: His rate fell from 0.55 to 0.28 and minutes from 16.0 to 5.2 with no grade movement. He is buried and the season confirmed it.

recommendations.summary: Run a system-fit review on Richards before the offseason; 1.08 to 0.71 pts/g at 24 on flat minutes is a decline that needs explanation.
recommendations.rationale: At 24 the expected direction is up. A 35% drop with no role change and minutes that dipped from 16.9 to 15.8 suggests the system is not drawing out his strengths.

recommendations.summary: Nash's rate halved from 0.83 to 0.42 on identical minutes at 20; flag for offseason system-fit review.
recommendations.rationale: Minutes flat at 12.9 to 13.2, so it is not a usage problem. The production just stopped. Needs a conversation about role and confidence.

recommendations.summary: Kaberle is improving at 27 (0.54 to 0.62, minutes up from 19.4 to 21.5); he stays as the top-pair anchor and gets more, not less.
recommendations.rationale: The only defenceman on the roster trending upward. The GM's January call on him was right.

recommendations.summary: Jackman's season is locked at 0.39 pts/g recent on 29.4 MPG; he goes in the offseason before his price drops further.
recommendations.rationale: Confirmed collapse from 0.65 to 0.39 with the heaviest D load on the roster. At 24 with 3 years at $0.70M his value is the minutes, not the points.

recommendations.summary: Eminger is flat at 0.35 to 0.37, age 21, expiring. He must be moved before July or we lose him for nothing.
recommendations.rationale: No improvement, no decline, just stalled. Expiring contract means the window is now.

recommendations.summary: No morale intervention for the final stretch; the room is 98-100 and climbing.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza at 88 and Spacek at 89 are the only players below 92, both trending +3 to +5. With 5 games left no line change fixes their minutes, and their morale is recovering on its own from the team's results.

recommendations.summary: No composition changes needed. All units are built from players who suit their roles.
recommendations.rationale: L1-L4 means align with their functions (scoring, two-way, defensive, development). P1 and P2 have proper shooter-and-setup constructions. K1 is a possession kill, K2 a grinding kill, both correct for their personnel. Known gaps (L4 faceoffs, no enforcer) are roster-level and already flagged.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo if his fatigue icon is clear; Tellqvist if tired.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 92 OVR and morale 100 against their 2.20 goals per game. Standing order: check fatigue icon on screen before confirming.

recommendations.summary: Keep all lines as they are for NYI.
recommendations.rationale: TOR leads the season series 4-1-1, outscored them 18-11. Their PP is 8.3%, their bottom six averages 73 OVR. Our current alignment puts Fischer/Jackman on Yashin and gives Eminger the softest assignment on their roster. No rearrangement improves any matchup.

recommendations.summary: Sell Jackman this offseason. Final season: 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG at $0.70M x 3.
recommendations.rationale: Rate dropped from 0.48 to 0.46 across the final seven games. No path to growth at this load and this contract.

recommendations.summary: Sell Klesla. Final season: 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG at $0.90M x 2, second consecutive decline.
recommendations.rationale: 0.38 at 22, 0.37 at 23. The trend is established across two full seasons.

recommendations.summary: Move Eminger before July. 0.36 pts/g, expiring $1.20M.
recommendations.rationale: Rate fell again (was 0.38 in February). UFA loss is the alternative to any return.

recommendations.summary: Trade or release Colaiacovo. 0.39 pts/g in 31 games, $1.10M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Scratched all season, low sample, low rate, expiring. No case to keep him over younger depth.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell in July: 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, 24 years old, from a seller with 10 expiring deals.
recommendations.rationale: Zero Toronto players carry 80+ TOUG. Bell is the only league-wide option closing toughness AND faceoffs simultaneously. CHI at 73 points with $29.46M profit are motivated sellers.

recommendations.summary: Avery at $400K with 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 25 years old, two years left is the cheapest player closing all three gaps simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: If Bell is unaffordable, Avery is the fallback. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring deals cannot retain him. He is cheaper than Bell by an order of magnitude on salary.

recommendations.summary: The RW scoring slot is vacant after Mogilny walks; Heatley (91 base, expiring) or Doan are the July acquisition priority.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g at 36. His minutes rose to 19.3 with no production gain. The RW side needs a 25-year-old who can produce at 0.8+ pts/g.

recommendations.summary: Stuart at 25 with 87 base, 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG and POTE 91 replaces Roberts with eight years of runway.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts is 38 and walking. The post-Roberts D core is Kaberle, McCabe, Eminger, Jackman. Stuart slots between McCabe and Jackman and adds the toughness the blueline lacks.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker on the fourth unit for next season; his 83 CHKG is the best internal checking available after Roberts leaves.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker is not lined. At 83 CHKG he is the third-best checker on the roster after Jackman and McCabe. Without him the fourth line checking mean drops further.

recommendations.summary: Speed (21 at 80+) and stamina (11 at 80+) are covered. No roster move needed.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik 98, Afinogenov 96, Koltsov 92, and 18 others above 80 SPEE. Kaberle 97 ENDU and 10 others above 80. These roles are not gaps.

recommendations.summary: Offer Gaborik and Richards 5-6 year deals first, before any other renewal conversation, to split the $21.30M cluster across two summers.
recommendations.rationale: 13 contracts worth $21.30M expire simultaneously. Gaborik (99 pts, 91 base, 23, $1.10M) and Richards (66 pts, 24, $1.00M) are the two whose production-to-salary ratio makes them most valuable and most at risk in a bidding war. Locking them early reduces the July 2005 negotiation queue from 13 to 11 and sets the template for Nash, Eminger, and Chlup to follow.

recommendations.proposed: Chlup on 5-6 years, Nash on 5-6 years, Eminger on 5-6 years
recommendations.summary: Renew Chlup (19, POTE 95, 59 pts), Nash (20, POTE 95, 39 pts) and Eminger (21, POTE 99) on 5-6 year deals to move them out of the July 2006 cluster.
recommendations.rationale: All three carry one year left at $1.20-2.34M. Their POTE ratings (95, 95, 99) mean their next-season price will jump. A 5-6 year deal now captures them at a young-player rate and spreads the renewal burden across two summers instead of three consecutive walls.

recommendations.summary: Accept Mogilny's two remaining years at $5.50M as sunk cost; do not force a trade that gives away value to shed salary the club can absorb at $25.38M profit.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny is 36 with 0.79 pts/g and two years locked. The over-80 expiring mechanic does not apply until 2007. Moving him now requires a team to accept a declining 36-year-old on $5.50M with a year of term, which means accepting a bad return. At $25.38M profit the payroll absorbs it.

recommendations.summary: No action on Sundin; his five-year deal runs to age 39 and the club should plan for his production decline from 2007-08 onward rather than attempt an impossible trade.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin is 34, $8.40M, 91 points, with 5 years left. He cannot be renegotiated mid-contract and no team will absorb four years of $8.40M at a declining age. The roster is already built around Gaborik and Richards at 23-24, which is the correct response to a Sundin deal that expires when he is 39.

recommendations.summary: Sign Gaborik to a 5-6 year extension at the top of his price range before any other renewal conversation happens.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base overall, 23 years old, 87 points this season, $1.10M expiring. The highest-value player on the expiring list and the one most likely to receive an offer sheet.

recommendations.summary: Sign Richards to a 5-6 year extension after Gaborik.
recommendations.rationale: 64 points at 24, $1.00M expiring. A second centre locked long-term prevents a market correction when the club needs him alongside Gaborik and Nash.

recommendations.summary: Sign Kaberle to a 5-year deal at $4-5M.
recommendations.rationale: 27, $1.90M expiring. He is the top-pairing blueliner until Eminger arrives, and at 27 his market value peaks now. A 5-year deal at a raise anchors the blue line through 2010.

recommendations.summary: Sign Eminger to a 5-6 year extension at a modest raise.
recommendations.rationale: 21, POTE 99, $1.20M expiring. The GM himself blocked trading him in January because his ceiling is the highest on the roster. Lock him long before his potential is reflected in his price.

recommendations.summary: Sign Nash to a 5-6 year deal despite the system-fit flag; address the role in camp, not in the contract.
recommendations.rationale: 20 years old, $1.20M expiring. His rate halved but at 20 that is a usage issue, not a value one. Losing him at his current salary is not an option.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Abid on a 2-3 year deal at current or slightly above current salary.
recommendations.rationale: 80 TOUG and 80 CHKG at $0.40M is the cheapest toughness available. The coach's gap calls for 75+ checking and 55+ faceoffs; Abid fills the first and not the second, but at 40 cents there is no reason to release him.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Colaiacovo on a 3-year deal.
recommendations.rationale: 22, $1.10M expiring. Young depth that could develop into top-four minutes. At his salary there is no reason to risk losing him.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Tellqvist on a 2-3 year deal as the backup behind Luongo.
recommendations.rationale: 25, high-90s potential, $0.80M expiring. The January standing order says give him time to develop. Two more years of NHL exposure is the right window before deciding if he is a starter or career backup.

recommendations.summary: Do not renew Belfour. Offer two years at a reduced figure, accept that he will likely decline, and move on.
recommendations.rationale: 39, $6.50M expiring. The GM kept him for the playoffs on March 19 and that was correct. After the run, the salary and age make him an asset the club cannot carry.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk. Do not offer.
recommendations.rationale: 38, $2.70M expiring. Confirmed walk per the GM's March 21 order.

recommendations.summary: Do not renew Upshall. Release him after the season.
recommendations.rationale: 21, $1.20M expiring. The coach's report says without a genuine camp audition he stops being dressable. He has not earned another shot at this price.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Cammalleri (LA, 22, POTE 98, 60 pts, $1.10M expiring) in July free agency after the core is locked.
recommendations.rationale: He fixes the right-wing scoring crisis Mogilny's decline confirmed in March. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring contracts cannot retain everyone. Sign him after Gaborik is locked, not before.

recommendations.summary: At the June 8 draft, select the best available goalie.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour walks, Tellqvist is unproven. The January standing order says draft goalies well. Even a fourth-rounder can become a quality backup with three years in the minors.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Heatley as a UFA signing in July; he fills the RW scoring hole Mogilny leaves at 24 years old on whatever deal he demands.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base, 131 pts/79 GP, $1.10M expiring from ATL at 84 points. ATL cannot retain both him and Kovalchuk at market rate. Direct replacement for Mogilny's RW role at half the age.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Kovalchuk as UFA if ATL retains Heatley; 138 points at 22 on $1.10M is the highest production-per-dollar available.
recommendations.rationale: Born April 1983, age 22, 89 base, POTE 85, 138 pts/79 GP, $1.10M expiring from ATL at 84 points. The binary with Heatley means one of them will be free.

recommendations.summary: Trade for Bell in July; he is the only player in the league closing toughness, checking, and faceoffs simultaneously on a young deal.
recommendations.rationale: 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, 28 pts/80 GP, 17.8 MPG, $900K, 2 years left, POTE 81, age 24. CHI at 78 points with $31.73M profit and 10 expiring are rebuilding and have no reason to keep a checking LW while stockpiling elsewhere.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Stuart as UFA or trade target in July; he replaces Roberts with 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG and eight years of development left.
recommendations.rationale: 87 base, 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG, POTE 91, 52 pts/77 GP, 30.8 MPG, $1.80M expiring from SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring on $45.39M payroll. SJ cannot retain all of them.

recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri as UFA if salary space allows; 22 years old with POTE 97 and 60 pts/61 GP on a $1.10M deal is the highest-upside forward on the market.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 79 points with 14 expiring cannot retain Cammalleri, Frolov, and Belanger simultaneously. At 22 with POTE 97, even if he only becomes a second-liner he is worth the deal.

recommendations.summary: Sign Theodore as Luongo's backup in July; 91 base at 28 fills the high-90s goalie order from January.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base, 3.29 GAA, .856 SV in 66 starts, $5.50M expiring from MTL at 66 points with 15 expiring. Belfour walks; Theodore gives a true 1A/1B tandem. MTL is rebuilding and has no reason to keep a 28-year-old on their timeline.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Havlat as fallback if both ATL forwards sign elsewhere; 24 years old, 103 pts/82 GP, $900K expiring from OTT at 77 points.
recommendations.rationale: 87 base, POTE 85, 103 pts/82 GP, $900K expiring. OTT at 77 points with 11 expiring and $32.39M profit are financially capable but not obligated to retain him.

recommendations.summary: Sign Belanger as the faceoff specialist if Bell is unavailable; 97 FACE at $700K solves the draws problem but not toughness.
recommendations.rationale: 97 FACE, 83 CHKG, 79 TOUG, $700K expiring from LA at 79 points. He does not close the 80+ TOUG gap alone, so he is a complement to Bell, not a replacement.

recommendations.summary: Consider Bouwmeester as UFA only if Stuart falls through; at 21 with POTE 95 and 33.3 MPG he is already a number-one defenceman.
recommendations.rationale: 81 base, POTE 95, 27 pts/79 GP, 33.3 MPG, $1.20M expiring from FLA at 76 points with 19 expiring. Lower current grade than Stuart but three years younger and higher ceiling. We already have Eminger (POTE 99, 21) developing, so adding Bouwmeester may be redundant in three years.

recommendations.summary: Consider Frolov as the LA package partner if we pursue Cammalleri; 22, POTE 95, 55 pts/62 GP, $1.10M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Same LA sell window as Cammalleri. A double acquisition fills both top-six wing spots for five years at $2.20M combined. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring cannot retain both plus Belanger.

recommendations.summary: Drop Daze from the target list; age is confirmed at 29, which eliminates him from the youth-core timeline.
recommendations.rationale: Born July 1975, confirmed age 29. At 29 with POTE 77 and $3.00M expiring, he is a one-year rental. The earlier low-confidence note flagged age as the disqualifier, and it is now confirmed. Heatley at 24 supersedes him permanently.

recommendations.current: Klesla (D, 23, POTE 97, $0.90M, 2 yrs, 30 pts/82 GP) + 4th-round pick
recommendations.proposed: Bell (LW, 24, POTE 81, $900K, 2 yrs, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE)
recommendations.summary: Trade Klesla and the 4th-rounder to Chicago for Bell to close the toughness, checking, and faceoff gaps in one move at $900K.
recommendations.rationale: Bell's 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, and 82 FACE close all three fourth-line gaps the Coach flagged (team means: 57, 61, 50). CHI at 78 points with $31.73M profit are rebuilding and Klesla at POTE 97 with 82 games played and SPEE 88 fills their defensive priority. Payroll is neutral. Acceptance uncertain — Klesla is a POTE 97 blueliner and CHI may demand more than a fourth-rounder alongside him.

recommendations.proposed: Avery (C, 25, POTE 79, $400K, 2 yrs, 93 FACE, 88 CHKG, 83 TOUG)
recommendations.summary: Trade Koltsov to Los Angeles for Avery to add a 93 FACE centre and the first forward above 80 TOUG the roster has ever carried.
recommendations.rationale: Avery's 93 FACE and 88 CHKG solve the faceoff void after Sundin and the checking gap simultaneously. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring contracts cannot retain Cammalleri and Avery at centre; Koltsov at POTE 94 and ACCE 96 gives them a young asset. LA adds $700K net against $45M+ payroll shedding. Acceptance uncertain — LA may keep Avery as cheap depth.

recommendations.proposed: Heatley (ATL, 91 base, RW, 131 pts/79 GP, expiring), Stuart (SJ, 87 base, D, POTE 91, expiring), Theodore (MTL, 91 base, G, expiring), Cammalleri (LA, 79 base, C/LW, POTE 98, 60 pts/61 GP, expiring)
recommendations.summary: Sign the four highest-value expiring UFAs in July to replace Mogilny, Roberts, Belfour, and add top-six depth; no trade packages required.
recommendations.rationale: All four are expiring and hit the market simultaneously in July. Heatley (131 pts at 24 on $1.10M) replaces Mogilny (84 pts, 36, $5.50M). Stuart (87 base, POTE 91, 52 pts at 25) replaces Roberts. Theodore (91 base, .856 SV, 66 starts) replaces Belfour. Cammalleri (POTE 98, 60 pts/61 GP at 22) adds a second top-six option. Belfour ($6.50M) and Roberts ($2.70M) expiring frees $9.20M to absorb these signings.

recommendations.summary: Goalie monitoring task #2 is complete and closed per the GM's 2005-03-19 standing order; no further reporting needed.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo (92, 26, $1.60M, 2 yrs) is on the roster and confirmed as a playoff goalie alongside Belfour (91). DiPietro eliminated at 79 base versus the 90+ threshold on 2005-03-14. GM closed all goalie monitoring explicitly on 2005-03-19.

recommendations.summary: Give Alexeev the fourth-line right wing spot for the final game over Upshall.
recommendations.rationale: Alexeev produces 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG; Upshall manages 0.29 pts/g on 7.9 MPG from the same line. NYI at 30-38 is a game where development takes priority per the standing order.

recommendations.summary: Spezza and Upshall both need a genuine camp assignment next season or they stop being dressable players.
recommendations.rationale: Two players at POTE 99, age 21, getting under 8 MPG and producing under 0.35 pts/g. The scouting report says something the opportunity isn't allowing them to prove or disprove.

recommendations.summary: Chlup's spot on the second line is permanent; no further development conversation needed.
recommendations.rationale: 0.83 pts/g at 19 on 16.9 MPG with morale 98. He has earned the role and it is producing.

recommendations.summary: Chlup is confirmed as a permanent top-nine centre going into next season; give him a top-six role in camp.
recommendations.rationale: 0.62 to 0.88 pts/g on minutes up from 11.0 to 18.2 across 58 games at age 19. He outperformed his increased load.

recommendations.summary: Spezza, Spacek, and Upshall all need a genuine camp audition next season; if they do not earn minutes in camp, stop dressing them.
recommendations.rationale: All three went from double-digit MPG to under 5.2 MPG and their rates collapsed simultaneously. Their minutes were taken by others who held the ice and produced.

recommendations.summary: Koltsov is worth whatever a club will give; do not wait for a price that is coming.
recommendations.rationale: Full season 0.43 pts/g on 38 games, recent window 0.29. No club in the league will see a 1.10 pace from October when his last 28 games produced 8 points.

recommendations.summary: Nash needs a system-fit review in the offseason like Richards; at 20 he halved his rate with no role change.
recommendations.rationale: 0.83 to 0.42 pts/g on flat 13 MPG. The role was consistent; the production was not. Something about how he is being used is not working.

recommendations.summary: Kaberle is the one defenceman trending up. 0.54 to 0.62 on increased minutes at 27. Secure him this offseason before his contract situation forces a conversation.
recommendations.rationale: He is the only TOR defenceman whose production went up with more ice time. At 27 he is entering or in his prime.

recommendations.summary: No ice-time or lineup change needed for morale purposes. The room averages 92 and nobody is trending toward trouble in the final six games.
recommendations.rationale: Lowest morale on the roster is Spezza at 88, flat for weeks. Six games remain. The development fixes for Spezza and Spacek are offseason camp assignments, not bench adjustments at this point.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes for NYI. They are 30-38, not a quality opponent requiring the all-out framework, and the current units are functional against this level.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has scoring 85/playmaking 83/speed 88 means. L4's checking 61 and faceoffs 51 are structural gaps that no arrangement fixes, and NYI won't exploit them the way a playoff team would. Leave chemistry intact with 6 games left.

recommendations.summary: Fourth line checking mean 61, toughness mean 57, faceoffs 50 with 51 best. No bench player fixes this. Offseason solution needed: at least one forward who checks above 75 and wins draws above 55.
recommendations.rationale: The L4 faceoff void was noted in March (mean 51, best 54). No new player has appeared. Koltsov is a collapsed trading chip, Spezza and Upshall are at 4.8 and 4.9 MPG. This is a roster problem, not a lineup problem.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes for NYI. The talent gap is too wide to need adjustment and development is already baked into the current construction.
recommendations.rationale: TOR is 133 pts vs NYI 84, 3.70/1.70 GF/GA vs 2.30/2.30, and 3-1-1 in the season series. Young players (Chlup, Nash, Klesla, Eminger, Spezza) are already in top-six and top-four roles. Sundin's FACE 87 neutralizes Yashin's FACE 70 on every draw.

recommendations.summary: Sell Jackman this offseason; 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG is a load problem no role fix will solve at $0.70M.
recommendations.rationale: Final season: 37 pts in 80 GP at 29.6 MPG. Rate fell from 0.48 to 0.46 as he finished the schedule. His market value is cheap top-pair minutes; hold him and that erodes.

recommendations.summary: Sell Klesla this offseason; 0.37 pts/g is his second straight declining year at 23.
recommendations.rationale: 30 pts in 82 GP on 14.8 MPG. Declined from 0.38 last year. No trajectory, flat minutes, two years and $0.90M remaining.

recommendations.summary: Move Eminger before July; 0.36 pts/g at 21 on an expiring $1.2M deal he walks for nothing otherwise.
recommendations.rationale: 23 pts in 64 GP. Contract expires this summer. Any return is better than losing a 21-year-old defenceman for zero.

recommendations.summary: Bell is the only league-wide player closing both the toughness (0 at 80+) and checking-forward (only 2 remaining after Roberts walks) gaps in one acquisition.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto carries zero players above 80 TOUG in stored grades; after Roberts departs only Fischer (82) and Upshall (80) remain as 80+ checking forwards. Bell is 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 24 years old, and CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring and $29.46M profit are motivated sellers. His 82 FACE is a bonus but not the primary reason per the GM's Jan 25 ruling.

recommendations.summary: Mogilny's confirmed decline and Roberts' departure strip the scoring group; Heatley at 91 base or Doan must arrive in July to maintain three scoring lines.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g at 36 with minutes rising to 19.3. Roberts walks at 38. The RW slot loses two of its best scorers simultaneously. Neither Heatley nor Doan fits Tucker-plus-4th pricing, so this requires a larger package or free-agency window.

recommendations.summary: The faceoff gap (one player at 90, next best at 75) is a centre problem that adding a wing cannot fix; Chlup at 19 with POTE 99 and 75 FACE is the two-year internal solution.
recommendations.rationale: GM ruled on Jan 25 that the faceoff argument for Bell is invalid because both are wings. Chlup is at 0.87 pts/g on 18.3 MPG at age 19 and climbing; the development track closes this without spending currency.

recommendations.summary: No action needed for the current playoff run; the team is at 133 points and the structural gaps have not prevented dominance.
recommendations.rationale: At 59-13-5 the toughness deficit has not been exposed to a fatal degree in 82 games. The gaps matter for 2005-06, not for tonight. The GM's March 19 order holds: keep everyone, trade only Tucker and the 4th.

recommendations.summary: Offer Gaborik a 5-6 year deal at July expiration; he is 23 with 99 points on $1.10M and every other club knows it.
recommendations.rationale: 99 pts at age 23 on an expiring $1.10M contract. A 5-year deal at even $3.00M through age 28 is the highest-value transaction available this summer. The GM confirmed 13 contracts worth $21.30M hit one summer; Gaborik is the most dangerous one to leave open.

recommendations.summary: Lock Richards on 5-6 years at July expiration; 66 points at 24 on $1.00M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Second in production behind Gaborik, same age window, same contract structure. A centre with 88 POTE at 24 costs far more on the open market than a 5-year extension at modest increase.

recommendations.summary: Renew Nash (20, POTE 95) and Eminger (21, POTE 99) on 5-6 year deals this July to lock the third wave.
recommendations.rationale: Both on expiring $1.20M deals. Nash has 39 pts in 69 games at 20; Eminger has 23 in 64 at 21 with POTE 99. Their replacement cost will be multiples of any extension Toronto offers now.

recommendations.summary: Plan Chlup's July 2006 renewal as the next priority; at 19, POTE 95, and 59 pts he will price himself out of $2.34M before he turns 22.
recommendations.rationale: 2-year contract expires July 2006. He is climbing (0.87 pts/g per coach). By next July he will be 21 with a full season as a top-six centre and his asking price will have tripled. The 2006 cluster ($15.44M) is manageable because Mogilny walks, creating the room.

recommendations.summary: Accept the Sundin $8.40M x 5 years as sunk cost; he is 34 and producing 91 points, and no mid-contract move exists.
recommendations.rationale: He is locked through age 39 at POTE 60. The money will constrain July 2007 and 2008 renewals but there is no mechanism to move it. The correct answer is to budget around it rather than pretend it can be reduced.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik to 5-6 years at July opening, before any other renewal.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base, 87 pts, age 23, $1.10M expiring. Highest-value renewal in the league. A bidding war in July with 87-point wingers scarce is the worst outcome.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards to 5 years immediately after Gaborik.
recommendations.rationale: 24 years old, 64 pts, centres the second line, $1.00M expiring. Four years from his prime and a top-six centre at that price does not come again.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash to 4-5 years after Richards.
recommendations.rationale: Age 20, $1.20M expiring, a core piece the coach dresses every night. Locking him splits the 13-contract July cluster.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger to 4-5 years after Nash.
recommendations.rationale: Age 21, $1.20M, POTE 99 per GM's Feb 19 veto. He is the future top-pairing defenceman and must not hit the open market.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle to 3 years.
recommendations.rationale: 27, $1.90M expiring. Good but commands top-pair salary; three years preserves flexibility for the UFA market while retaining the current top pairing.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Tellqvist to 2 years as Luongo's backup.
recommendations.rationale: GM standing order: POTE high 90s, give him time. $0.80M expiring, two years at roughly $0.90M keeps the goalie situation stable.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Colaiacovo to 2-3 years.
recommendations.rationale: 22, $1.10M, depth defenceman. Two years lets him prove he earns a third before locking longer.

recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour a reduced two-year deal around $3.00M; accept if he walks.
recommendations.rationale: 39, $6.50M expiring. GM expects refusal. Luongo and Tellqvist cover next season. $3.50M+ saved funds the UFA market.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk in July.
recommendations.rationale: 38, $2.70M. GM confirmed he walks. His 84 CHKG role is replaceable at half the price.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Gagne in UFA free agency as the primary RW target.
recommendations.rationale: 25, 86 base, 94 pts, expiring from a distressed PHI club. More likely to sign here than Marleau given Toronto's win record.

recommendations.summary: Offer Marleau a max attempt in July; expect him to re-sign or demand a trade package.
recommendations.rationale: 25, 89 base, 98 pts, expiring from SJ at 72 points. The biggest UFA available. If Toronto cannot outbid SJ's offer, accept it and take Gagne.

recommendations.summary: Give Chlup top-nine minutes in the final seven games so he arrives in October with NHL seasoning.
recommendations.rationale: 19 years old, 0.87 pts/g on 18.3 MPG and climbing per coach's March 30 report. Seven games of real experience changes next camp.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle and give him shifts in the remaining seven games.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 96 at 20 with four games all season per the coach. Seven more games at 8-10 MPG is a development season instead of a non-event.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Heatley as a July UFA signing or trade target from ATL; he fills the RW scoring void Mogilny's departure creates.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base, 131 pts in 79 GP, 24 years old, $1.10M expiring from ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring contracts. A 5-year deal at $3.50-4.00M is affordable against $25.38M profit and his competitive profile favors Toronto as the league's best team.

recommendations.summary: Trade for Bell from Chicago; he is the only player in the league closing the zero-80-TOUG structural gap in a single body at age 24.
recommendations.rationale: 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, 24, $900K with 2 years left. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit wants young assets; Colaiacovo (POTE 99, 21, $1.10M) is the package centerpiece if the GM cannot re-sign all three of Nash, Eminger, and Colaiacovo.

recommendations.summary: Sign Cammalleri as a July UFA; at 22 with POTE 98 and 60 points on $1.10M expiring from LA, he is the highest-value available player.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 79 points with 14 expiring cannot retain both him and Frolov. Zero trade assets required — only salary. A 5-year deal at $2.50M locks a top-six RW through age 27.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Stuart via UFA signing; 87 base with 80 TOUG and 89 CHKG gives the blue line the physical identity no current Toronto blueliner carries.
recommendations.rationale: SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring cannot retain all of them. At 25 with POTE 91 he still has development runway. UFA route avoids spending a young asset, which neutralizes the Jan 19 Eminger-over-Stuart logic. Target salary $2.50-3.00M on 5 years.

recommendations.summary: Fallback D target if Stuart is unavailable; 82 base with 47 points in 82 GP at 31 MPG from same seller club.
recommendations.rationale: Same SJ seller logic as Stuart. Lower grade (82 vs 87) and higher cost ($2.20M vs $1.80M). Only pursue if Stuart re-signs or his price escalates beyond $3.00M.

recommendations.summary: Investigate Daze (CHI, 89 base, 127 pts in 82 GP, $3.00M expiring) before finalizing the RW target; his age is unconfirmed and determines whether he supersedes Heatley.
recommendations.rationale: 127 points at 89 base is the highest production on any expiring deal in the league. If age is 26-28 he is superior to Heatley; if 30+ the trajectory math reverses. Must verify before July.

recommendations.current: Colaiacovo (D, 22, POTE 99, $1.10M expiring) + Tucker (LW, 30, CHKG 92, TOUG 88, $1.30M, 2yr) + 4th-round pick
recommendations.proposed: Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, $900K, 2yr)
recommendations.summary: Offer CHI Colaiacovo plus Tucker plus the 4th-rounder for Bell; this is the only route to close the toughness gap since Bell has two years remaining.
recommendations.rationale: CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit are rebuilding and want high-POTE young assets; Colaiacovo is POTE 99 at 22. Bell is expiring risk for TOR below Nash and Eminger on the renewal list, so trading him now guarantees a return rather than losing him for nothing.

recommendations.proposed: Heatley (ATL, RW, 24, 91 base, 131 pts/79 GP, expiring UFA, target $3.50-4.00M on 5 years)
recommendations.summary: Sign Heatley as a UFA in July; ATL holds both him and Kovalchuk on expiring deals and their rebuild favors the younger, cheaper Kovalchuk.
recommendations.rationale: Heatley's 91 base and 131 points replace Mogilny's declining 84-point season at age 24 with seven years of prime remaining; no trade asset is required since he is expiring.

recommendations.proposed: Stuart (SJ, D, 25, 87 base, 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG, POTE 91, expiring UFA, target $2.50-3.00M on 5 years)
recommendations.summary: Sign Stuart as a UFA in July; SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring on $45.39M cannot retain him, and his 89 CHKG and 80 TOUG give the blue line a physical identity.
recommendations.rationale: Stuart at 25 with POTE 91 still has eight years of development left, unlike the 38-year-old Roberts he replaces; his 52 points in 77 games at 30 MPG confirms he plays the minutes Toronto needs from a top-pair blueliner.

recommendations.summary: Do not trade Upshall or Koltsov for Heatley or Stuart unless a competing club signs them first and eliminates the UFA route.
recommendations.rationale: Upshall (POTE 99) and Koltsov (POTE 94) are 21 and 23 with no arrival timeline; trading either for a player we can sign in July is overpaying. Hold them as insurance only.

recommendations.summary: Goalie monitoring task is complete: Luongo is on the roster at 92, DiPietro eliminated at 79 base, and the GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo arrived in February at 92 base / $1.60M / 2 years. DiPietro confirmed at 79 base over 52 GP by March 14. GM's standing order from March 19 closes this file.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza a top-nine roster spot and real camp minutes next season; 6.7 MPG at POTE 99 was a failure of this staff.
recommendations.rationale: 46 GP, 6.7 MPG, 0.33 pts/g at age 21 with POTE 99. He never got a genuine chance this year.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev earns a top-nine audition in camp; 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG says he was underused all year.
recommendations.rationale: 30 points in 55 games on 8.3 MPG at age 23. He was outproducing top-nine regulars and was scratched late.

recommendations.summary: Stahle needs a real camp audition with 15+ MPG games or we drop him from prospect plans.
recommendations.rationale: 4 GP all season at POTE 96. We cannot judge a 20-year-old on four shifts.

recommendations.summary: Chlup belongs in the top nine and earned it; no adjustment needed.
recommendations.rationale: 59 pts, 16.9 MPG, 0.83 pts/g on the second line at 19. He exceeded expectations under increased load.

recommendations.summary: Plan Chlup as a top-six centre next season; his rate and load both increased at 19, which means the current role is too small for him.
recommendations.rationale: 0.88 pts/g on 18.2 MPG in 58 games since December, up from 0.62 on 11.0 MPG in the first 13. Both went up at an age where increased load normally suppresses rate.

recommendations.summary: Flag Richards for offseason system-fit review; at 24 his rate dropped 34% with no change in role or minutes.
recommendations.rationale: 1.08→0.71 pts/g on 16.9→15.8 MPG across 80 games. At 24 the expected direction is up. Same pattern as Afinogenov at 25.

recommendations.summary: Flag Afinogenov for the same offseason review as Richards; prime age, flat role, 38% rate decline.
recommendations.rationale: 1.17→0.73 pts/g on flat 16.6 MPG in 67 games. At 25 this should not be happening.

recommendations.summary: McCabe goes back on the sell list for the offseason; his season rate is confirmed below 0.60.
recommendations.rationale: 1.42→0.48 pts/g across 82 games at 29. The March 30 threshold (0.60) is clearly breached. He was never recovered.

recommendations.summary: Abid's minutes-to-production mismatch worsened: rate down 36% AND minutes down 43%. Offseason decision needed on whether to restore his ice time or trade him.
recommendations.rationale: 1.09→0.70 pts/g on 20.1→11.5 MPG in 82 games at age 25. Both the role and the production are moving the wrong way simultaneously.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes needed in the final five games; Spezza, Upshall and Spacek's development windows are closed for this season and veterans are aging on expected curves.
recommendations.rationale: The last five games will not change any of these trajectories. Preserve what's working (Chlup's minutes, Kaberle's load) and let the offseason sort the rest.

recommendations.summary: The room is fine. Morale at 96-99 across all dressed players, winning streak has lifted the whole group. Only Spezza at 86 is low and that is an offseason problem.
recommendations.rationale: Team average morale is well above 90. The only sub-90 reading is Spezza at 86 on 6.7 MPG at 21, already flagged as a season write-off on March 25. No minute changes help him in the final 7 games. The GM's standing order to prioritize development in games we can afford means Afinogenov stays scratched and Spezza stays on the 4th line.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo, checking his fatigue icon on screen before confirming.
recommendations.rationale: 92 OVR against a 2.60 GF/G club at home. Standing order requires checking the fatigue icon; Tellqvist at 73 is the only alternative.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes for NYI. The current arrangement covers their threats and gives the young guys safe minutes on L3 and L4.
recommendations.rationale: TOR 133 pts vs NYI 84 pts. Our L1 (Gaborik 95) dominates their L1 (Yashin 83). L4 faces a 72/77/67 fourth line, ideal development context. No defensive pair change needed since their third and fourth lines are their weakest units.

recommendations.summary: Sell Jackman this offseason at $0.70M x 3; season locked at 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG across 80 games.
recommendations.rationale: Below 0.50 for the full season as predicted. His value is the price and the minutes, not the production. Any club needing a top-pair body at 700k sees 80 GP.

recommendations.summary: Sell Klesla this offseason at $0.90M x 2; second consecutive declining season locked at 0.37 pts/g.
recommendations.rationale: 0.38 at 22, 0.37 at 23, flat 15 MPG. No growth signal after two years. $0.90M x 2 is a cheap depth pair for someone else.

recommendations.summary: Move Eminger before July 1 or lose him for nothing; 0.36 pts/g on 15.5 MPG at 21, $1.20M expiring.
