recommendations.rationale: Season locked at 0.36 rate across 64 games. Expiring contract means summer is the last window for any return.

recommendations.summary: Confirm whether the Koltsov-for-Avery package is still live; he is the only available player who closes both the toughness and faceoff voids in one move.
recommendations.rationale: Zero Toronto players carry 80+ TOUG and only Sundin (90) sits above 80 FACE. Avery is 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG at $400K with 2 years. No internal lineup change closes either gap.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker for the final three games to add a 92 CHKG body to the bottom six before the season ends and the chip decision is made.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker is on the roster with 83 CHKG in the checking column and 92 in his raw CHKG grade, but sits in no unit. Three games is the last chance to evaluate whether he helps or whether the chip is more valuable on the shelf.

recommendations.summary: Do not move Richards to L4 for faceoffs; he is 70 FACE and the fourth-line stamina mean of 55 means he burns out there.
recommendations.rationale: Richards at 70 FACE lifts the L4 mean from 51 to roughly 57, which is still below the 80 threshold the role demands. It also removes an 85 PASS and 90 ENDU from L3, where he is functioning. The fix is external, not a shuffle.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik, Richards, Nash and Eminger on 5-6 year deals in July 2005 at the top of the renewal priority.
recommendations.rationale: All four are expiring at a combined $4.50M with market value of $14M-$18M. The club owns no draft pick better than a 4th rounder, so losing any one of them is unrecoverable. Gaborik at 87 base, 95 pts, age 23 is the most urgent single signing.

recommendations.summary: Let Belfour ($6.50M), Roberts ($2.70M) and Tellqvist ($0.80M) walk in July, freeing $10.00M for the young-core renewals.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 39 with POTE 50, Roberts is 38 with POTE 52, Tellqvist is the third goalie behind Luongo (97 POTE). None develops. Together they represent 47% of the expiring cluster's salary and contribute nothing to the next three seasons.

recommendations.summary: Trade Koltsov ($1.10M, 2 years, POTE 94, 18 pts in 35 GP) for a third or fourth rounder before his value drops further.
recommendations.rationale: He has two years of control but is producing 0.51 pts/g on the fourth line with the coach flagging him as surplus. The club owns zero picks better than a 4th. At 23 with POTE 94 he still has trade value a buyer would pay for; waiting until 2006 makes him a rental worth only a 5th.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik to a 6-year deal on the first day of July free agency.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base overall at 23 with 87 points and a $1.10M expiring contract. He is the cheapest elite scorer in the league and leaving him to a bidding war is unacceptable.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards to a 5-year deal immediately after Gaborik.
recommendations.rationale: 64 points at 24, 73 FACE, $1.00M expiring. The only centre between first and fourth line worth long-term minutes.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger to a 5-year deal.
recommendations.rationale: 21 years old with POTE 99 at $1.20M. GM's own standing order from Jan 19 makes him the defense cornerstone on this timeline.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle to a 4-year deal.
recommendations.rationale: 27 years old, entering his prime at top-pairing minutes, $1.90M. Four years staggers his next renewal off the Eminger/Colaiacovo cluster.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash to a 4-year deal after the camp audition determines his line role.
recommendations.rationale: 20 years old, $1.20M. The rate halved from 0.83 to 0.38 per the coach, but age and cap hit justify keeping him even at 3LWF. Four rather than five preserves a re-evaluation point.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Colaiacovo to a 3-year deal.
recommendations.rationale: 22, $1.10M, third-pairing defense. Losing him leaves three NHL-ready blueliners.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Chistov to a 2-year deal and revisit his trade value in July.
recommendations.rationale: 21, $1.10M. The LA/Avery package was never executed and the deadline has closed. Keep him cheap; trade him later if a third party accepts youth over a pick.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Abid to a 2-year deal on the first day of July free agency.
recommendations.rationale: $0.40M for 80 TOUG and 80 CHKG is the cheapest toughness available. Only a structural toughness fix this club has ever found.

recommendations.summary: Offer Alexeev a 2-year deal at or below $1.10M; let him walk if his ask rises meaningfully.
recommendations.rationale: 23, $1.10M, depth wing. Renewal priority falls below the young core, and at 23 his asking price may jump.

recommendations.summary: Let Belfour walk in July. Offer a 1-year reduced-salary bridge and accept the likely refusal.
recommendations.rationale: GM's March 21 renewal order lists him as walking. At 39 and $6.50M, the only deal he'll sign is one he doesn't want.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk in July.
recommendations.rationale: GM's March 21 order. 38 years old, $2.70M, no future top-nine role.

recommendations.summary: Let camp decide Upshall's future; do not renew unless he earns top-nine minutes.
recommendations.rationale: Coach reports MPG collapsed from 13.4 to 4.9 and rate fell from 0.33 to 0.29. $1.20M is too expensive for a fourth-liner at 21.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bell in July as the primary toughness acquisition; he is the only available player with 88 TOUG and 86 CHKG who can play top six.
recommendations.rationale: The coverage phase confirmed zero rostered players at 80+ TOUG in stored grades. Bell at 88/86/82 is the single league-wide player closing both structural voids. CHI at 73 points, $29.46M profit, 10 expiring — motivated sellers. POTE 81 at 24. ENDU 71 is the only weakness.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Stuart in July as the Roberts replacement; 87 base, 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG, POTE 91 at 25.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts walks in July at $2.70M. Stuart at 87/80/89 replaces him and adds the toughness our blue line currently lacks. SJ at 72 points with 13 expiring cannot re-sign 13 players on $45.39M payroll. $20.63M profit means they have no reason to hold onto an expiring rental.

recommendations.summary: Heatley remains the July wing priority at 91 base with 81 CHKG, the only high scorer who is not a defensive liability.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny finished (0.79 pts/g at 36) and Roberts walking removes two 80+ scorers. ATL at 82 points with 11 expiring and $36.79M payroll cannot retain both Heatley (91 base, 96 pts/58 GP) and Kovalchuk (89 base, 104 pts/61 GP). Whoever ATL keeps, the other is available.

recommendations.summary: If the L4 faceoff mean stays at 51 after Bell arrives at wing, add Avery at 93 FACE and $400K as the specialist fix.
recommendations.rationale: Bell plays wing so the faceoff gap at L4 centre persists. Avery at 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG closes it at $400K with 2 years left. But 6 pts in 57 GP and ENDU 50 mean he plays 9 minutes and contributes nothing else. Only pursue if the L4 faceoff problem persists after other moves.

recommendations.summary: Kovalchuk is the fallback if ATL keeps Heatley; 89 base, 104 pts/61 GP, 21, TOUG 78 just below the 80 threshold.
recommendations.rationale: The Feb 28 binary determines which ATL wing is available. Kovalchuk has higher production and youth (21 vs 24) but Heatley's 81 CHKG is closer to the toughness profile we need. TOUG 78 is below our threshold by 2 points.

recommendations.summary: Do not pursue Barnaby (NYR), Frolov (LA), Cammalleri (LA), or Samsonov (BOS) this summer.
recommendations.rationale: Barnaby: POTE 58 and ENDU 67 mean he is finished and cannot play a regular shift. Frolov/Cammalleri: 77-79 base development projects that do not help a current Cup window. Samsonov: TOUG 55 does not address the structural void and BOS at 93 points are not sellers.

recommendations.summary: Trade Koltsov to LA for Avery to close the L4 faceoff and toughness voids simultaneously; requires GM to unlock Koltsov from the March 19 lockdown.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 48 points with 10 expiring deals wants high-ceiling youth; Koltsov's POTE 94 and 96 ACCE are exactly what a rebuilding club hoards. Avery fills the only structural gaps on our roster (zero forwards above 80 TOUG, L4 faceoff mean of 51) on $400K for two years.

recommendations.proposed: Marleau (SJ, 25, 89 base, 98 pts) or Gagne (PHI, 25, 86 base, 94 pts) via UFA
recommendations.summary: Use the $9.20M freed by Belfour and Roberts to sign Marleau or Gagne on a 5-year deal at $2.50M-$3.50M instead of pursuing a trade.
recommendations.rationale: Both are 25, both expiring from clubs that cannot re-sign them (SJ at 72 with 13 expiring on $45.39M, PHI at 63 with financial distress). No prospect leaves and no pick is spent. Acceptance depends on whether other clubs with more draft capital outbid us.

recommendations.summary: Do not trade Tucker and the 4th-rounder; neither package reaches any target worth having.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker (30, POTE 79, $1.30M, 3 GP) plus a 4th-rounder is worth approximately a 74-76 base depth player. None of our targets (Bell 82, Stuart 87, Heatley 91) are in that range. The assets are better held as a summer sweetener to pair with a larger package if the Avery deal requires one.

recommendations.summary: Close the goalie monitoring task — Luongo is on the roster at 94 overall, DiPietro is permanently eliminated at 79 base.
recommendations.rationale: GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19. Both monitoring subjects are resolved: Luongo acquired (94 ovr, 25, 2 yrs, $1.60M), DiPietro fails the high-90s threshold by 15 points.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza top-nine minutes in at least one of MIN or OTT, or accept the year is dead and plan his camp assignment now.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 at 21, 6.7 MPG fourth line, morale 86. Raised five times since January with no movement. Season is a write-off; the only remaining in-season lever is real minutes in a beatable game.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle and give him ice in MIN or OTT. Four games at POTE 96 at age 20 is not a development season.
recommendations.rationale: Three games left. If he doesn't play before season's end he has had no genuine NHL audition at 20 and the decision defers entirely to September camp.

recommendations.summary: No change to Chlup's assignment.
recommendations.rationale: 56 points in 68 games at 16.9 MPG on the second line at age 19. Exactly where he belongs.

recommendations.summary: No change to Gaborik.
recommendations.rationale: 95 points, 100% games played, 20.5 MPG top line at 23. Fully earned.

recommendations.summary: Flag Chlup for a top-six centre role next season. He is at 0.87 pts/g on 18.3 MPG at 19 and climbing.
recommendations.rationale: His rate rose while his minutes nearly doubled (11.0 to 18.3 MPG). At 19, players normally fall under increased load. He did the opposite. He has outgrown the bottom six.

recommendations.summary: Re-evaluate McCabe for the sell list this offseason. His recent 55-game window is 0.45 pts/g on 21.7 MPG at 29.
recommendations.rationale: I took him off the sell list March 4 at 0.83 over 66 games, but that sample was carried by a 24-game hot start at 1.42. The recent window is the real reading, and 0.45 at 29 on 21.7 MPG is bottom-pair production at top-pair minutes.

recommendations.summary: Confirm Jackman on the sell list. Season rate is now 0.41 on 29.5 MPG at 24.
recommendations.rationale: Down from 0.65 in the first 23 games. I flagged this in March at 0.48 and 0.65; it has slipped further. At 0.41 on 30 MPG his value erodes every week he stays.

recommendations.summary: The Koltsov trading chip is dead. He is at 0.28 pts/g across 35 games.
recommendations.rationale: My March 11 note flagged the collapse from 1.10 to 0.28. Now at 35 games and 0.28 season rate, no club will offer meaningful return. GM's decision to keep him as a chip has cost what value he had.

recommendations.summary: Spacek, Spezza and Upshall all need a binary offseason decision: real camp audition or stop dressing them. All three are at or below 5 MPG and 0.28 pts/g.
recommendations.rationale: Spacek 0.28/5.2 MPG, Spezza 0.27/4.5 MPG, Upshall 0.27/4.8 MPG. I raised this three times for Spacek and Spezza with no movement. Another season of spot minutes at this age wastes all three.

recommendations.summary: Abid's minutes have fallen again, now 11.5 MPG at 0.74 pts/g. He needs 15+ MPG or becomes a trade candidate this summer.
recommendations.rationale: Raised March 16 at 12.6 MPG. Now 11.5 and still dropping. At 25 his development window is closing. A winger producing 0.74 should see 15 MPG minimum.

recommendations.summary: Room is at 96+ everywhere except Spezza (86) and Upshall (89), both structurally underused and unrecoverable in 3 remaining games.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza at 6.7 MPG and Upshall at 8.0 MPG are both in the 80s band costing -1 grade. No arrangement of the next three games moves their season average enough to recover. The fix is offseason role assignment, not in-game minutes.

recommendations.summary: No composition change before New Jersey; every unit matches its role.
recommendations.rationale: K2 checks at 84 mean and K1 at 78, both with a 75+ draw man; P1 has Gaborik at 98 scoring and P2 has Mogilny at 94, so no unit is missing a role it needs.

recommendations.summary: We have one checking forward above 80 (Roberts, 84); a three-forward shutdown line is impossible from this roster.
recommendations.rationale: Of the top four checkers, Jackman 90, McCabe 84 and Fischer 84 are defencemen; only Roberts 84 is a forward. Any checking-line plan at 80+ needs a forward the club does not have.

recommendations.summary: Move Abid from fourth-line left wing to second-line left wing to replace the injured Afinogenov.
recommendations.rationale: Afinogenov is out until April 15. Abid at 80 OVR with 86 checking gives us a two-way winger who can handle Elias (86 OVR, 98 AGGR on his line partner Madden) without opening a hole on the second pair of Kaberle/McCabe.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour if his fatigue icon is clear on screen; Aebischer if tired.
recommendations.rationale: Brodeur at 92 OVR is the best goalie we face this month. We cannot hand him Ouellet at 82 on the road. Standing order: check the fatigue icon before confirming.

recommendations.summary: No change to lines 1 and 3.
recommendations.rationale: We lead the season series 3-0 with 19 goals for and 2 against. Line 1 auto-pairs against their top line (Gomez/Friesen/Langenbrunner) and our 97 OVR right wing against their 78-rated defenceman Kubina is a matchup we do not want to disturb.

recommendations.summary: Trade Eminger before his contract expires; his season rate has fallen from 0.44 to 0.38 and he will leave for nothing as a UFA.
recommendations.rationale: 23 points in 61 games on 15.8 MPG, age 21, $1.20M x 1 expiring. Was 0.44 in February, now 0.38 — the slide continued all month. An expiring asset with a declining rate must be moved for something.

recommendations.summary: Sell list unchanged: Jackman (0.48 at 29.7 MPG, $0.70M x 3), Klesla (0.38 at 14.9 MPG, $0.90M x 2), Eminger (0.38 at 15.8 MPG, $1.20M x 1 expiring), Colaiacovo (0.39 at 17.9 MPG, $1.10M x 1 expiring). Keep: McCabe, Kaberle, Fischer.
recommendations.rationale: Season is 79 of 82 games. Rates are locked. Eminger moved slightly (0.44 to 0.38) but was already on the list. No new injuries or grade shifts.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker on the fourth line for the final 6 games and the playoffs; his 83 CHKG is the fifth-best checker on the roster and he's currently not lined.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker is rostered but in no unit. With Roberts expiring and checking dropping to four next year, the playoff roster needs a fifth body who can kill penalties. He's 83 CHKG, not a toughness answer, but he's a checking answer the coach isn't using.

recommendations.summary: Line Koltsov (23, 92 speed, not lined) for the final 6 games to evaluate whether he earns a roster spot next season.
recommendations.rationale: 92 speed is top-four roster talent sitting idle. With Mogilny departing and a RW solution needed, seeing whether Koltsov can fill a scoring wing role in NHL minutes costs nothing and informs the Heatley-or-Doan decision.

recommendations.summary: Avery (LA, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2y) is the only known single player who closes both structural gaps (toughness zero, faceoffs one). July priority if the Koltsov-package is rejected.
recommendations.rationale: Zero TOR players carry 80+ TOUG and only Sundin clears 80 FACE. No internal fix exists for either. Avery closes both at $400K with two years left. LA at 48 points are sellers. The March 19 note pivoted the offer to Koltsov; if LA rejects that, Avery at 25 with a cheap contract is the target.

recommendations.summary: Speed, playmaking, clutch and stamina are covered (21, 11, 9, 11 at 80+ respectively). No roster move needed in these areas.
recommendations.rationale: Twenty-one skaters at 80+ speed including Gaborik 98 and Afinogenov 96 means this gap cannot arise. Eleven at 80+ playmaking from Sundin through Richards gives three lines of creation. These roles need no fix.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik to 5-6 years this July as the top renewal priority. 91 base, 91 pts at 23, currently $1.10M.
recommendations.rationale: He is the most productive player on the roster and the cheapest star by a wide margin. A 5-6 year deal protects four prime years at a pre-breakout price that will not repeat.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards to 5-6 years this July, second priority. 64 pts at 24 on $1.00M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: He is the successor to Sundin at centre. At 24 with 64 points he will command $4M+ on the open market; locking him now saves years of that cost.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash to 5-6 years this July. 20 years old, 35 pts, POTE 95, $1.20M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: He is the cheapest player with star potential on the roster. At 20 with POTE 95, his next two seasons determine whether he is a $1M player or a $6M player. Lock the price now.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger to 5-6 years this July. 21, POTE 99, $1.20M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: GM protected Eminger as a core piece on Feb 19. His ceiling is the highest on the blueline. A 5-6 year deal keeps him through his prime at a young-player price.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle to 3-4 years. 27, 41 pts, $1.90M expiring, entering prime per the coach.
recommendations.rationale: He is a year or two from decline so 5-6 years risks paying for a version that will not exist. 3-4 years covers the prime window and his renewal lands alongside the depth group in 2008-09, splitting the cluster.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Abid to 3-4 years. 25, 66 pts, $0.40M expiring, POTE 94.
recommendations.rationale: He went from a bargain contract to 66 points. The raise will be steep but he is still cheaper than what a 66-point winger costs elsewhere. 3-4 years rather than 5-6 because his base is 78, not 90+.

recommendations.summary: Put Chistov, Colaiacovo, Alexeev, Upshall, and Tellqvist on 2-3 year deals to split the renewal burden away from July 2006.
recommendations.rationale: The 2-year group (Chlup, Luongo, Koltsov, Spezza, Ouellet, Klesla) already comes up in 2006. Adding depth renewals to the same summer creates a second cluster. Two or three year deals push these five to 2007-08.

recommendations.summary: Let Belfour walk or move him for a pick before July. $6.50M expiring, 39 years old, 92 base.
recommendations.rationale: GM decided March 19 to keep him for the playoffs. After the playoffs the decision is simple: he is 39, CON 50, and his $6.50M is the single largest payroll item. Luongo at 91 base and $1.60M is the number one.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk. 38, $2.70M expiring, 77 pts but POTE 52.
recommendations.rationale: His production is real but so is his age. At 38 he is one season from the bottom six. $2.70M that frees up pays for the Gaborik raise.

recommendations.summary: Fischer stays. Four years at $3.70M is an anchor but he is 24 and cannot be moved mid-contract.
recommendations.rationale: His production fell to 0.41 pts/g but the contract runs to 2009. No mid-deal renegotiation is possible. The only move is at expiration or via trade in a future window when another club takes on the term.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik on 5–6 years the day free agency opens. He is the single most important contract of the summer.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base, 23, 87 points, $1.10M expiring. The cheapest top-15 overall in the league walks in July if we let a bidding war start.

recommendations.summary: Lock Richards on 5–6 years immediately after Gaborik.
recommendations.rationale: 82 base, 24, 64 points, $1.00M expiring. Same shape as Gaborik: young, productive, and about to be repriced.

recommendations.summary: Lock Kaberle on 5–6 years as the top-pair quarterback.
recommendations.rationale: 84 base, 27, rising from 0.54 to 0.63 pts/g with minutes climbing to 21.9. Entering his prime and the coach named him next year's top-pair QB.

recommendations.summary: Lock Eminger on 5 years. The GM protected him all season on the POTE 99 argument; follow through.
recommendations.rationale: 76 base, 21, $1.20M. The January order kept him over Chara specifically because his development curve was open. A two-year deal signals we don't believe that.

recommendations.summary: Lock Nash on 5 years.
recommendations.rationale: 77 base, 20, $1.20M. Youngest forward on the roster, first-line minutes, and every comparable age-20 LW is cheaper now than at 22.

recommendations.summary: Renew Abid on 2 years. Cheap toughness the roster has no replacement for.
recommendations.rationale: 79 base, 25, $0.40M, 80 CHKG and 80 TOUG. The coach wants 17+ MPG for him next year; a 2-year deal at a modest bump keeps that optionality without a long commitment.

recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour two years at $3.5–4.0M. If he declines, let him walk and bank $6.50M.
recommendations.rationale: 92 base, 39, $6.50M. GM's own standing order says he probably won't accept a reduced deal. If he walks, that $6.50M funds a Heatley or Doan package.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk. No renewal offer.
recommendations.rationale: 87 base, 38, $2.70M. The March 21 renewal order already set this. Saves $2.70M for next year's young core bumps.

recommendations.summary: Try to trade Upshall for a late-round pick or depth piece; otherwise let him walk.
recommendations.rationale: 78 base, 21, $1.20M, 0.30 pts/g, minutes collapsed from 13.4 to 5.1 MPG. Coach flagged it as a wasted year. At 78 base the over-80 pick mechanic does not apply, so a straight trade or a walk.

recommendations.summary: Renew Chistov on 2–3 years at bottom-six money.
recommendations.rationale: 78 base, 21, $1.10M. Young enough to improve, cheap enough to keep for bottom-six depth without a long commitment.

recommendations.summary: Let Colaiacovo test the market. Re-sign only at $900K or below.
recommendations.rationale: 72 base, 22, $1.10M. Thin for a second-pairing D, and we have Jackman at 80 base on 3 years plus Stahle at 70 base with POTE 96 behind him.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Heatley in July — 91 base, 120 pts/71 GP, 24, expiring from ATL who cannot keep both him and Kovalchuk.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 81 pts with 11 expiring must choose between Kovalchuk (130 pts) and Heatley (120 pts). Heatley fills the exact RW hole Mogilny leaves. Toronto's $24.39M profit absorbs a $5-6M raise. No trade asset needed if ATL lets him walk to UFA.

recommendations.summary: Test Iginla as the higher-ceiling RW alternative — 93 base, 112 pts/69 GP, 27, $6.50M expiring from 60-pt CGY who must sell.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 60 pts with $45.93M payroll and only $12.21M profit cannot retain Iginla's $6.50M. He walks in July for nothing unless traded. At 93 base he is the best RW in the league but the salary strains the renewal budget alongside Gaborik and Richards.

recommendations.summary: Sign Gagne as UFA in July if PHI cannot re-sign — 86 base, 98 pts/74 GP, 25, UFA from a club at $3.38M profit.
recommendations.rationale: PHI at 71 pts with $66.73M payroll and $3.38M profit cannot re-sign 13 expiring players. Gagne at $2.40M UFA requires no trade assets. He plays LW but at 86 base and 98 points he upgrades the top nine regardless of side.

recommendations.summary: Target Marleau as UFA fallback — 89 base, 98 pts/71 GP, 25, expiring from 68-pt SJ.
recommendations.rationale: SJ at 68 pts with 13 expiring and $19.95M profit may try to re-sign at $1.60M. If they can't, he's UFA. A center who can play RW at 89 base and 98 points provides positional flexibility that Heatley doesn't.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell for toughness, checking, and faceoffs — 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, 24 years old, $900K, 2 years left from 69-pt CHI.
recommendations.rationale: Bell is the only player closing all three structural gaps on a re-signable deal. CHI at 69 pts with $28.03M profit are profitable but rebuilding with 10 expiring. Proposed price from Jan 25: R2 plus Colaiacovo. He is not a rental; 2 years means Toronto controls his prime.

recommendations.summary: Cheaper toughness/faceoff alternative — 83 TOUG, 94 FACE, $400K, 2 years from 71-pt LA with 14 expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Avery closes the same two gaps as Bell at half the salary but produces 0.12 pts/g (9 pts in 75 GP). He is a role player with elite grades, not a top-nine option. LA at 71 pts with 14 expiring are willing sellers. Backup option if Bell is unavailable.

recommendations.summary: Acquire the LA pair for long-term top-six depth — both 22, POTE 98/96, 52 and 50 pts/54 and 55 GP, $1.10M expiring each.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 71 pts with 14 expiring cannot re-sign both stars on development contracts. Acquiring both fills two top-six wing spots for five years on cheap deals. The risk is development stalls (Isbister precedent) but 50+ points at 22 with 95+ POTE is the strongest development case available.

recommendations.summary: Low-probability elite target — 89 base, 112 pts/64 GP, 26, $1.90M expiring, but BOS at 91 pts likely keeps him.
recommendations.rationale: BOS at 91 pts with $27.92M profit and 13 expiring can afford Samsonov. Only available if BOS decides to sell, which their record doesn't suggest. Listed as a fallback if Heatley and Gagne both fall through.

recommendations.proposed: Heatley (ATL, RW, 24, 91 base, 120 pts/71 GP, $1.10M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Trade Tucker and the 4th-rounder for Heatley to replace Mogilny at right wing in July.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 81 points with 11 expiring keeps Kovalchuk (89 base, 130 pts) and loses Heatley for nothing unless traded. Tucker's 92 CHKG on 2 years at $1.30M gives ATL something physical; the 4th is marginal. Toronto fills the RW crisis the March 23 note locked.

recommendations.current: Koltsov (23, POTE 94, 96 ACCE, $1.10M, 2 years, not lined)
recommendations.proposed: Avery (LA, C, 25, 83 TOUG, 94 FACE, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2 years)
recommendations.summary: Trade Koltsov for Avery to close both the toughness and faceoff gaps simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Zero Toronto players carry 80+ TOUG; only Sundin clears 80 FACE. Avery covers both at $400K for 2 years. LA at 71 points with 14 expiring gets a POTE 94 winger with 96 ACCE to replace a 0.12 ppg fourth-liner. Koltsov has no line assignment and 18 points in 35 games.

recommendations.proposed: Late-round draft pick (via over-80 pick mechanic)
recommendations.summary: Dump Mogilny for a late-round pick using the over-80 expiring mechanic to clear $5.50M and add draft capital.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny's stored grades (ACCU 95, PASS 94, AGIL 95) still clear 80 overall. We do not intend to re-sign a 36-year-old at 0.79 pts/g. The mechanic trades 80+ players the club won't keep for a pick. A contender needing top-nine hands for 2 years takes the salary. Acceptance uncertain at 0.79 ppg.

recommendations.summary: Spezza must earn a top-nine role in camp next season; he cannot return to the fourth line at POTE 99 with 7 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: 40 games at 7.0 MPG on L4, 15 points, age 21, morale 89. Raised five times with no movement. The role is the problem, not the player.

recommendations.summary: Decide Stahle's future this offseason: top-pair audition in camp or trade him for a forward asset. Another year at 4 GP is worthless.
recommendations.rationale: 4 games all season at 20, POTE 96, morale 99. When he did play he held 17.8 MPG. The development investment is getting zero return.

recommendations.summary: No development-driven changes to tonight's lines. CAR is a quality opponent and the standing order is maximize.
recommendations.rationale: Against a 27-23 club we go all out. The development items above are offseason work.

recommendations.summary: Spezza needs a real top-six role at training camp or we stop dressing him; 4.8 MPG and 0.32 pts/g at 21 is a second wasted year.
recommendations.rationale: Minutes collapsed from 9.1 to 4.8 while rate fell from 0.43 to 0.32. Raised five times since January with no movement. At 21 this is the development emergency on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Upshall at 21 went from 13.4 to 4.9 MPG and 0.33 to 0.29 pts/g; give him a genuine top-nine audition in camp or stop dressing him.
recommendations.rationale: Same pattern as Spezza: buried at 21 with no grade movement. Either he gets a real look or he is not part of the plan.

recommendations.summary: Nash's rate halved from 0.83 to 0.38 on flat minutes at 20; give him a full top-six audition at camp before writing him off as a system-fit problem.
recommendations.rationale: Minutes flat at 12.7 means the role did not change. The production did. At 20 the expected direction is up; this needs an answer before next season.

recommendations.summary: Chlup at 19 broke out at 0.88 pts/g on 18.2 MPG; lock him into the top nine permanently and consider him for top-six next year.
recommendations.rationale: Rate up and minutes up simultaneously at 19. This is genuine development, not a hot streak. Protect it.

recommendations.summary: No change now; plan around Mogilny at 36 declining from 1.62 to 0.81 with no future beyond this year.
recommendations.rationale: Age-appropriate decline. His 19 MPG at 36 is too much for a player whose rate is halving. Reduce his role in the final six games if possible.

recommendations.summary: No change now; Roberts at 38 going 1.29 to 0.88 is near the end. Plan the offseason without assuming he returns.
recommendations.rationale: Direction is down and he is 38. His production per minute has held better than raw rate suggests but the writing is on the wall.

recommendations.summary: No morale-driven line change needed; the room runs 89-99 and every player is in or near his minutes band.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza at 89 on 7.0 MPG is correctly banded as a depth center. Mogilny, Richards, Afinogenov and Chlup at 96 are each 2-4 points off the last save but recovering with wins. Jackman at 29.8 MPG has no morale issue; his problem is production, not happiness. No intervention is warranted before Carolina.

recommendations.summary: All four even-strength lines are built from players who suit their roles; no composition change warranted before Carolina.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has checking (Jackman 88) plus skill (Gaborik 97), L3 checks (Nash 92) and scores (Chistov 96), PP and PK units use the right personnel. L2's softness (checking 68) is the price of Mogilny/Afinogenov up front and is acceptable when getting offensive starts.

recommendations.summary: Fourth-line faceoff mean is 51 with a best of 52; Richards at 73 on L3 is the nearest fix and moving him breaks a functioning checking line.
recommendations.rationale: L4 faceoff best is 52 (Upshall), mean 51. The next-best draw man on the roster is Richards at 73, already anchoring L3 alongside Nash and Chistov. This is a structural gap that requires a transaction to fill.

recommendations.summary: Keep fourth-line shifts short; their stamina mean of 55 is the lowest on the roster and they will not hold up in extended minutes.
recommendations.rationale: L4 stamina mean 55, best 64. Richards at 87, Kaberle at 85 — the top six can handle length, the fourth cannot. Shorter shifts from this line in the third period is the adjustment.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour. Check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming per the standing order.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour at 92 OVR with ENDU 86, no tired icon in the brief. CAR shoots 3.1 a night and their skill is aged; Belfour handles this without help.

recommendations.summary: No lineup change. All quality players are dressed and the D slot order already matches our strongest pair against their strongest (Ozolinsh/Hill).
recommendations.rationale: We are 1-2 against CAR but 10-game win streak, 4.50 GF/gp to 1.60 GA/gp. They are old, slow, and shorthanded 3.3 times a night against our 35.7% PP. The existing structure exploits their weaknesses.

recommendations.summary: Sell list unchanged since March 23: Jackman, Klesla, Eminger. No movement in any rate.
recommendations.rationale: Jackman at 0.50 pts/g on 29.8 MPG is flat. Klesla at 0.36 on 15 MPG is his second declining year. Eminger drifted 0.44 to 0.38 season rate, expiring $1.2M.

recommendations.proposed: Sean Avery (LA, C, 25, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 93 FACE, $400K, 2y)
recommendations.summary: Pursue Avery via trade in July; he closes toughness, checking, and faceoffs in one move at $400K.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto has zero players at 80+ TOUG and one player at 80+ FACE. Avery at 83/88/93 simultaneously patches all three. LA at 48 points are sellers; Koltsov (23, 92 SPD) was the agreed lead piece per the March 19 package note.

recommendations.proposed: Marleau (SJ, 25, 89 base, 98 pts) or Gagné (PHI, 25, 86 base, 94 pts)
recommendations.summary: Sign one of Marleau or Gagné as a July UFA to replace the Mogilny/Roberts right-side production that walks.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny at 36 has fallen to 0.79 pts/g; Roberts at 38 is expiring. Together they produced a large share of the scoring. Both Marleau and Gagné are expiring from 63-point clubs per the March 16 note and will hit the UFA pool.

recommendations.summary: No roster changes for the playoffs — 122 points, two 90+ goalies, 10 scorers at 80+, 6 checkers at 80+.
recommendations.rationale: The only chips are Tucker and the 4th-rounder per the GM's March 19 order. The toughness gap is structural but has not stopped the team from winning 54 games. Nothing acquirable at this point changes the playoff outlook.

recommendations.summary: Spezza needs an offseason decision: play him top-nine next year or trade him. Five seasons of 5 MPG with POTE 99 is a wasted asset.
recommendations.rationale: Coach flagged this a sixth time. At 5.1 MPG he cannot develop. If the system has no room for him after Chlup's emergence and the RW signing, his trade value is highest while POTE 99 is still credible.

recommendations.summary: Execute the July 2005 renewal sequence: Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, Kaberle, Chistov, Abid on 5-6 year deals; Belfour and Roberts walk.
recommendations.rationale: 13 contracts worth $21.30M expire simultaneously. Walking Belfour ($6.50M) and Roberts ($2.70M) frees $9.20M, which covers raises for the seven young stars whose current salaries ($0.40M-$1.90M) are well below what their production commands.

recommendations.summary: Budget a $5-6M/season renewal for Chlup at July 2006; his current $2.34M expires with only 1 year remaining after this season.
recommendations.rationale: He is 19, POTE 95, 51 points on 64 games and rising. The no-mid-contract-renegotiation rule means we cannot extend early, so the only protection is having the money committed next summer before his next season inflates his asking price.

recommendations.summary: Chlup and Spezza must be top-nine centers by 2007-08 to absorb Sundin's declining minutes without a roster gap.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin is $8.40M for four more years after this season, age 34, POTE 60. His production will fall 20-30% by 2007. No trade is possible for that contract shape. The only solution is internal: Chlup at 19 with POTE 95 and Spezza at 21 with POTE 99 are the succession.

recommendations.summary: Renew Gaborik first in July on 5–6 years; he is 91 base, 23, 87 points at $1.10M and the most exposed contract on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: Every club sees a 23-year-old 91-overall at $1.10M. A 5-year deal locks the franchise right wing; a 1-year re-up only raises the price next July.

recommendations.summary: Renew Richards second on 5–6 years; 64 points at 24 and $1.00M is the league's cheapest young centre.
recommendations.rationale: Standing order from March 21 puts him second. No other club's 24-year-old centre has 64 points under $1M.

recommendations.summary: Renew Nash on 5 years; 20 years old, $1.20M, first-round upside, and the cheapest long-term lock available.
recommendations.rationale: At 20 he has the most time to develop of any expiring player. A 5-year deal costs less now than a bidding war later.

recommendations.summary: Renew Eminger on 5–6 years; POTE 99 at 21 is the reason the GM vetoed the Chara deal, and he is worth protecting through the same logic.
recommendations.rationale: GM's Jan 19 standing order: Eminger at POTE 99 is worth more to the timeline than established veterans. A short deal wastes that asset.

recommendations.summary: Renew Kaberle on 4 years; improving to 0.63 pts/g on 21.9 MPG at 27, but 4 years means he is 31 at expiry, not 33.
recommendations.rationale: Entering his prime per the coach, but at 27 his ceiling is approaching. Four years matches his current value to his remaining window.

recommendations.summary: Renew Abid on 3 years at $1.0–1.5M; TOUG 80 and CHKG 80 at $0.40M is the only structural toughness fix on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: The coach has flagged zero players with 80+ TOUG in stored grades six times. Abid is the fix and his current salary will not survive July unchanged.

recommendations.summary: Renew Upshall on 2 years; POTE 99 at 21 justifies patience, but 19 points in 61 games on 8.3 MPG does not justify a long deal.
recommendations.rationale: Coach flagged a wasted year with minutes collapsing from 13.4 to 5.1 MPG. Two years gives one more development window without locking a 78-overall to a 5-year contract.

recommendations.summary: Renew Chistov on 2 years; 98 SPEE and POTE 95 at 21 are the asset, but 20 points in 61 games is not a 5-year case yet.
recommendations.rationale: His speed profile (98/96/96) projects an NHL role if the rest catches up. Two years preserves team control without overcommitting.

recommendations.summary: Renew Colaiacovo on 2 years; POTE 99 at 22 but ENDU 50 and only 31 games means he needs a full development season before any longer commitment.
recommendations.rationale: The rawest of the depth four. If endurance has not improved by next December, his 72 base overall makes him expendable even with POTE 99.

recommendations.summary: Renew Alexeev on 2 years; 30 points in 55 games is the best production of the depth group and POTE 94 supports one more window.
recommendations.rationale: Outproduces Upshall and Chistov per minute. A 2-year deal at $1.10M is cheap for a 23-year-old wing with 94 potential.

recommendations.summary: Let Belfour walk at season end; 39 and $6.50M, the GM concluded a reduced deal will not be accepted, and the trade window closed March 19.
recommendations.rationale: The standing order from March 19 keeps him for the playoffs only. After June his role is done and $6.50M is the single largest savings available.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk at season end; 38, $2.70M, no role on a contender that already lacks toughness depth rather than scoring depth.
recommendations.rationale: March 21 standing order says he walks. The $2.70M freed is the margin that helps absorb the young core raises.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Heatley from ATL in July as the primary right-wing solution replacing Mogilny's decline and Roberts' departure.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base, 119 points in 70 GP, age 24, POTE 86, $1.10M expiring. ATL at 80 pts with 11 expiring cannot re-sign both him and Kovalchuk (129pts, age 21). He is the best RW available. The package is the problem — ATL wants picks and prospects and we hold one 4th.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Doan from PHX in July as the dual fix: right-wing scoring plus the toughness ceiling we have never had.
recommendations.rationale: 87 base, TOUG 82, CHKG 87, 55 pts in 73 GP, $2.40M expiring, age 28, POTE 80. Zero Toronto players carry 80+ TOUG in stored grades; Doan brings 82 with 87 checking. PHX at 80 pts with 14 expiring are likely out of the race and motivated to deal an expiring captain.

recommendations.summary: Test a double-package for Cammalleri and Frolov from LA — two age-22 wingers with POTE 98 and 96 on expiring deals from the league's most motivated seller.
recommendations.rationale: Cammalleri: 79 base, POTE 98, 51 pts/53 GP, $1.10M. Frolov: 77 base, POTE 96, 50 pts/54 GP, $1.10M. LA at 71 pts with 14 expiring and $52.43M payroll. Neither is proven but the potential grades are the highest available from any seller. $2.20M combined fills two top-six spots for five years.

recommendations.summary: Test whether VAN will deal Bertuzzi; if they are out of the race he is the most complete RW available at any price.
recommendations.rationale: 94 base, 119 pts in 75 GP, TOUG 89, CHKG 93, $2.60M expiring, age 30, POTE 58. Elite production plus elite toughness plus elite checking in one player. POTE 58 means grades are set and declining. VAN at 94 pts with $33.24M profit may re-sign rather than deal — uncertain.

recommendations.summary: Morrow is better than Doan on paper but DAL at 98 points is unlikely to sell; test anyway because $1.30M for 84 TOUG and 73 points is the best value on the board.
recommendations.rationale: 88 base, TOUG 84, CHKG 86, 73 pts in 58 GP, $1.30M expiring, age 26, POTE 86. Better grades, younger, cheaper than Doan. DAL at 98 pts with $8.49M profit and 7 expiring is a contender in a money squeeze — could deal to avoid a raise, or re-sign and push for the Cup.

recommendations.summary: Havlat remains the fallback top-six scoring target if Heatley stays at ATL — cheaper, younger, from a clear seller.
recommendations.rationale: 87 base, 93 pts in 75 GP, $900K expiring, age 23, POTE 84. OTT at 67 pts with 11 expiring are motivated. Plays LW not RW, but top-six scoring is top-six scoring regardless of side. Already flagged Feb 26.

recommendations.summary: Sign McKenna for the playoffs and next season as the cheapest toughness fix available — 95 TOUG at $400K from a seller.
recommendations.rationale: TOUG 95, $400K, 32 GP, PIT at 77 pts with 14 expiring. Will not play top six (5.3 MPG, 2 pts) but puts a 95-TOUG man on L4 at no cost. Our top-six TOUG ceiling is Jackman at 75; McKenna at 95 on L4 changes the physical profile of a series.

recommendations.summary: Sillinger is the best available faceoff man at FACE 92 but at 33 with POTE 56 he is a bridge while Chlup grows, not a solution.
recommendations.rationale: 86 base, FACE 92, 59 pts in 53 GP, $1.80M expiring, age 33. PHX at 80 pts, 14 expiring. Same club as Doan — if PHX sells, pursue both in one conversation. But adding a 33-year-old centre alongside Sundin at 34 is the wrong age profile; keep this as a backup only.

recommendations.summary: Conroy at FACE 87 and 86 points from the worst team in the league is the most likely faceoff target to actually be available.
recommendations.rationale: 85 base, FACE 87, 86 pts in 74 GP, $2.00M expiring, age 33, POTE 78. CGY at 58 pts with 10 expiring and $11.77M profit is the most motivated seller in the league. Same age concern as Sillinger but 86 points is real production. Fold into a CGY conversation where they have many players to offer back.

recommendations.summary: Avery at $400K and 2 years remains the cheapest multi-gap option but his 9 points in 74 games makes him a fourth-line grinder, not a top-six answer.
recommendations.rationale: 79 base, TOUG 79, FACE 90, CHKG 88, $400K, 2 years, age 25. Production is 9 pts in 74 GP (0.12 ppg). LA at 71 pts with 14 expiring. The Feb 16 deprioritization below Bell stands — grades are elite, ice says fourth line. Fold into a Cammalleri/Frolov LA package as a sweetener rather than a standalone target.

recommendations.summary: Trade Koltsov to LA for Avery, filling toughness, faceoffs, and checking simultaneously for $400K.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 48 points with 14 expiring and $52.43M payroll is the most desperate seller in the league; they get a 23-year-old with POTE 94 and elite speed. Avery's FACE 93 exceeds Sundin's 90 and his TOUG 83 is the highest available anywhere. Net payroll saving of $700K. Acceptance uncertain because the AI may value POTE 94 highly.

recommendations.current: Tucker (LW, 30, $1.30M, 2yr, CHKG 92) + Alexeev (LW, 23, POTE 94, 30pts/55GP, $1.10M, 1yr) + 4th round pick
recommendations.summary: Trade Tucker, Alexeev, and the 4th-rounder to Ottawa for Havlat, replacing Mogilny and Roberts production.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 67 points with 11 expiring deals cannot re-sign Havlat at $3-4M; they get a veteran body (Tucker 92 CHKG), a POTE-94 prospect (Alexeev, 30 points at 23), and a pick. Toronto gains a 23-year-old with 87 base and 93 points at $900K. Acceptance uncertain because OTT may want more than Tucker for a 93-point player.

recommendations.current: Koltsov (LW, 23, POTE 94, ACCE 96, $1.10M, 2yr) + Alexeev (LW, 23, POTE 94, 30pts/55GP, $1.10M, 1yr) + 4th round pick
recommendations.summary: Trade Koltsov, Alexeev, and the 4th to Phoenix for Doan, consolidating toughness and right-wing scoring into one deal.
recommendations.rationale: PHX at 80 points with 14 expiring and $47.81M payroll will likely miss the playoffs and prefers assets now over losing their captain for nothing. Doan's TOUG 82 and CHKG 87 make him the best available RW with real physicality. Do not do this if proposal 1 lands; both require Koltsov. Acceptance uncertain because PHX at $13.01M profit may not feel urgency.

recommendations.summary: Execute these trades only after locking Gaborik, Richards, Nash, and Eminger on 5-6 year deals in July.
recommendations.rationale: The GM's standing renewal order sequences the core first. You cannot trade a player whose contract you have not renewed if he is expiring; Koltsov at 2 years is safe but the renewal cluster's success determines whether the roster we are building around actually stays intact. All 13 expiring contracts worth $21.30M come due simultaneously in July.

recommendations.proposed: Spezza on the third line for remaining games
recommendations.summary: Move Spezza to the third line for the remaining 7 games to give him top-nine minutes before the offseason.
recommendations.rationale: 21 years old, POTE 99, 39 GP at 7.2 MPG on the fourth line, morale down to 89. I have raised this five times with no movement. Seven games is a small window but it gives us one real read on whether he can hold a top-nine role.

recommendations.proposed: Upshall on the third line alongside or rotating with Spezza
recommendations.summary: Give Upshall a look on the third line for the remaining 7 games to settle his roster question before the offseason.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99, 61 GP but only 8.3 MPG and 0.31 pts/g. He is invisible in the lineup. If 12-14 MPG on the third line does not lift his production, we stop treating him as a prospect next season.

recommendations.summary: No change to Chlup's role.
recommendations.rationale: 19 years old, 51 points in 64 games at 16.7 MPG on the second line, morale 96. He is earning every shift he gets.

recommendations.summary: No change to Gaborik's role.
recommendations.rationale: 90 points in 75 games, 20.3 MPG on the first line. He is the best player on the roster and is playing like it.

recommendations.summary: Accept that Stahle's season is a wash; plan real minutes for him next season.
recommendations.rationale: 20 years old, POTE 96, 4 GP all year. Seven games remain and even playing all of them leaves him at 11. The blue line is too deep to break him in now. This is an offseason planning note, not a this-season fix.

recommendations.summary: Chlup is the confirmed breakout: 0.84 pts/g on 18.1 MPG at 19, rising on both axes. Build next year's top nine around him.
recommendations.rationale: At 19, his rate went from 0.62 to 0.84 while minutes rose from 11 to 18.1. Production and load moving up together at that age is the signal you wait for.

recommendations.summary: Kaberle is improving: 0.54 to 0.63 pts/g, minutes from 19.4 to 21.9, at 27. He's entering his prime. Plan around him as the top-pair quarterback next year.
recommendations.rationale: A defenseman in his late 20s going the right way with rising minutes and rising production is rare. The GM called him a star in January; the trend confirms it.

recommendations.summary: Upshall's minutes collapsed from 13.4 to 5.1 MPG at 21 with production flat at 0.30. Flag for offseason: he's a wasted year unless something changes.
recommendations.rationale: Lost 8 minutes a night over 37 games and production barely moved, meaning the ice he did get wasn't productive either. Same pattern as Spezza.

recommendations.summary: Spezza at 0.33 pts/g on 5.1 MPG at 21 with POTE 99. Sixth time flagging. Offseason decision needed: does he fit this system or does he go?
recommendations.rationale: No movement in three months. The minutes aren't coming and the production confirms he can't force it.

recommendations.summary: Mogilny fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g at 36 while minutes rose to 19.3. Plan a right wing solution for next season.
recommendations.rationale: Age is doing what age does. The extra minutes aren't compensating for the rate decline. Roberts at 38 (0.88 on 21.4) is on the same clock.

recommendations.summary: Give Abid 17-18+ MPG by promoting him to a top-nine wing role for the final 7 games; his 0.88 pts/g on 14.4 MPG is a mismatch that will crack his 99 morale if left another month.
recommendations.rationale: 66 points in 75 games on the fourth line. His minutes rose from 12.6 to 14.4 since mid-March but the gap to a top-nine role remains. At 24 with this production rate, a calibre-based expectation of 17-20 MPG is being violated; morale hasn't moved yet but the structural risk is there.

recommendations.summary: No other player needs an ice-time adjustment for morale purposes.
recommendations.rationale: Everyone on the active roster sits at 96-99. The scratch players (Spacek at 89, Spezza at 89) are in the GM's development rotation and their levels are acceptable for depth roles.

recommendations.summary: L1 is well-balanced with elite scoring, good checking mean at 81, and Sundin winning draws at 90. No change.
recommendations.rationale: Jackman at 89 checking anchors it, Gaborik at 98/99 scoring carries the offense, Fischer adds 83 checking depth. Best unit on the roster in every relevant metric.

recommendations.summary: L2 is an offensive line and should be left alone. Checking at 69 mean is acceptable given L1 and L3 carry defensive matchups.
recommendations.rationale: McCabe at 83 checking is adequate for a second line. The unit's job is to score, and Mogilny at 92, Afinogenov at 90/91 scoring/playmaking do that. Chlup at 79 faceoffs handles draws.

recommendations.summary: Give L3 less of the game against quality opponents. Richards at 93 checking carries the unit alone; the other four don't suit a checking role.
recommendations.rationale: Eminger is at 0.17 pts/g over 6 games and Klesla is declining at 22. Only Richards performs checking, faceoff, toughness, and clutch roles. The line cannot do what its slot demands as a group.

recommendations.summary: No fourth-line faceoff solution exists on this roster. Best on L4 is 53, which forces top-six defensive-zone starts all season.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza at 53, Abid at 51. No bench center wins a draw. Richards at 74 is the next-best man and he anchors L3. Only a trade or draft fixes this.

recommendations.summary: Spezza at 53 faceoffs is below the threshold for an NHL center. If he's going to be one, he needs to build that skill this offseason.
recommendations.rationale: A prospect center at 53 faceoffs means he loses every draw he takes. Combined with L4's 51 mean, it confirms the line cannot start in its own zone.

recommendations.summary: K1 uses top skill players on the kill and K2 handles the heavy checking. Current split is sound.
recommendations.rationale: K1 at 77 checking mean is adequate for short-handed minutes from players already on the ice. K2 at 83 mean with Jackman at 89 is the true checking unit. Swapping would weaken one to strengthen the other.

recommendations.summary: Checking depth is adequate (5 players at 80+) but fragile. One injury to Jackman or Roberts leaves no 85+ checker to anchor both PK units simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: Jackman 89, Richards 93, Roberts 83, McCabe 83, Fischer 83. Five is enough for a healthy season. A single loss forces a downgrade that compounds across the lineup.

recommendations.summary: Leave all lines as they are. Our first pair is built to shut down Thornton, our top six overwhelms their weak third pair, and the only exposed unit (Eminger/Klesla vs Rolston) is mitigated by his wingers' inability to finish.
recommendations.rationale: Thornton's 92 OVR line meets Fischer/Jackman (both 90 CHKG) by auto-pairing. Gaborik (97) vs McGillis/Berard (81/81) is a 16-point gap. Gill/Moran at 72/68 are the weakest D pair we face all week. Changing any pairing breaks chemistry for no gain.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour if his fatigue icon is clear on screen; Aebischer if tired.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour at 93 OVR against BOS's 3.20 GF per game. Per standing order of January 19, check the fatigue icon before confirming.

recommendations.summary: Jackman's season is confirmed at 0.48 pts/g on 73 games. Sell him this offseason at $0.70M x 3 or restructure his role to under 25 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: The March 14 condition (hold below 0.50 through season's end) has been met. At 30 MPG his production cannot recover in this system. At $0.70M he carries maximum trade value for any club needing top-pair minutes cheaply.

recommendations.summary: Klesla's second consecutive declining season is locked: 0.36 pts/g at 23 on 75 games, down from 0.38 at 22. He goes this offseason.
recommendations.rationale: The Feb 21 condition (second declining year makes him tradeable) is met. At $0.90M x 2 he is still young enough to draw a third-pair offer.

recommendations.summary: Eminger at 0.37 pts/g on 57 games, expiring $1.20M. Sell at deadline or let walk. No change from February.
recommendations.rationale: Still well below the 0.45 threshold. No recovery happening.

recommendations.summary: McCabe at 0.79 pts/g over 75 games. No change; still firmly off the sell list.
recommendations.rationale: Slight drift from 0.83 but well above any sell threshold. $3.00M x 4 is expensive for the production, but he is delivering.

recommendations.summary: Avery is the only player who closes the zero-80+ toughness gap, the one-80+ faceoff gap, and adds a sixth 80+ checker simultaneously; the GM must decide if Koltsov is a chip before the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Zero Toronto skaters at 80+ TOUG. Avery at 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 93 FACE, $400K, 25 with 2 years left is the only known target that fixes all three. LA at 48 points are sellers but require Koltsov (POTE 94), which conflicts with the March 19 'everybody else we keep' order.

recommendations.summary: If no acquisition happens, slide Richards from L3 to L4 for faceoff duty; he is at 70 FACE and the next L4 option is 52.
recommendations.rationale: The coach flagged the L4 faceoff gap with the best available at 52. Richards at 70 is a 18-point upgrade on that line but leaves L3 without a draw-taker. This is the best in-house option.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker for playoff readiness as a sixth checker at 83 CHKG; he provides depth but does not fix the toughness gap at 70 TOUG.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker at 83 CHKG is the only unlined player above 80 in any role. He adds a body for injuries but his 70 TOUG means he does not close the structural gap.

recommendations.summary: No other role requires action: scoring has 10 at 80+, playmaking 11, speed 21, checking 5 lined, clutch 9, stamina 11, durability 4.
recommendations.rationale: Every role outside toughness and faceoffs is covered with multiple 80+ players. The only age concern is Mogilny at 36 and Roberts at 38 atop two lists, but that is a July question.

recommendations.summary: Sign Gaborik to a 5-6 year deal the week the season ends. He is 23, 87 pts in 74 games, $1.10M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Top scorer on a one-year deal at age 23 is the single largest contract risk on the roster. If he walks, no other TOR player under 30 replaces that point production.

recommendations.summary: Sign Richards to a 5-6 year deal. 64 pts in 72 games at 24, $1.00M, expiring.
recommendations.rationale: A 24-year-old centre producing second-line numbers on a $1M expiring deal will be poached or expensive in July. Lock him alongside Gaborik as the second priority.

recommendations.summary: Sign Nash to a 5-year deal at $3-4M. He is 20 with 35 pts in 61 games and POTE 95.
recommendations.rationale: Cheapest upside on the roster. Even if he does not develop into a star, five years of top-six winger depth at that price is cheap.

recommendations.summary: Sign Eminger to a 5-year deal. He is 21 with POTE 99, 21 pts in 56 games, $1.20M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Highest POTE on the blue line and the GM has already protected him from deadline trades. Five years locks the left side of the power play through age 26.

recommendations.summary: Sign Abid first among the depth group on 2-3 years. 66 pts in 74 games, TOUG 80, $0.40M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Cheapest player on the roster producing second-line points and carrying the only 80+ toughness on the team. He fills the structural toughness gap the Feb 19 note identified.

recommendations.summary: Sign Chistov, Upshall, Colaiacovo, and Alexeev to 2-3 year deals at $1.5-2.0M to stagger against the core locks.
recommendations.rationale: These four are $4.50M combined now with POTE between 94 and 99. Two- or three-year deals keep them through 2007 or 2008 and split the renewal burden across two summers.

recommendations.summary: Let Belfour and Roberts walk in July. Their $9.20M combined creates the payroll room for the young-core raises.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 39 on $6.50M, Roberts is 38 on $2.70M. Both are lined for playoff use per the GM's March 19 order. In July, let them go. Luongo and Ouellet cover the goalie depth; the forward spot is replaceable.

recommendations.summary: Sundin's $8.40M five-year deal through age 39 is the club's long-term payroll problem. No action now; flag for trade-bait by 2007-08.
recommendations.rationale: He is still producing at 83 pts in 74 games, but POTE 60 means his decline is near. The deal outlives the value by three years. There is nothing to do in 2005 because the contract is locked.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik to a 5-6 year deal on day one of July — he is 91 base, POTE 90, 23, on $1.10M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: He is the single highest-value renewal on the sheet. A 91-base right wing at 23 with POTE 90 on a $1.10M expiring deal will draw every contender in the market. The GM's own standing order from January flagged this as the most urgent re-signing.

recommendations.summary: Lock Nash to a 5-6 year deal — 20 years old, $1.20M expiring, core left wing.
recommendations.rationale: At 20 he has the longest runway of the entire core. Re-signing him on a one-year or two-year deal only ratchets his demands in 2006 when he will be 22 and more expensive.

recommendations.summary: Lock Eminger to a 5-6 year deal — 21, POTE 99, $1.20M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: The GM vetoed trading Eminger in January specifically because of his potential. If we let him hit the market at 22 after a breakout season, we replace him at triple the cost.

recommendations.summary: Lock Richards to a 5-year deal — 24, $1.00M expiring, second-line centre.
recommendations.rationale: Five years not six: he is 24, not 20, and the coach is already using him for faceoff duty at 73 FACE which is not a first-line number. Four or five years prices him as the second-line anchor he is without overpaying for a ceiling that is set.

recommendations.summary: Renew Kaberle on 3-4 years — 27, $1.90M, top-four defenseman whose ceiling is set.
recommendations.rationale: He is a solid top-four piece but at 27 his POTE is not driving his value anymore. A 3-4 year flat deal avoids paying a star's premium for a good-not-elite defenseman.

recommendations.summary: Lock Abid to a 3-year deal — 24, TOUG 80, CHKG 80, $0.40M expiring. The cheapest toughness on the sheet.
recommendations.rationale: Zero Toronto players carry 80+ stored TOUG. Abid is the only one and he costs $400K. Three years at a small raise closes the toughness gap structurally.

recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour a reduced deal — 39, $6.50M. If he declines (likely), let him walk.
recommendations.rationale: The GM's own read from January: Belfour will not accept a reduced contract. At $6.50M for a 39-year-old, he is the single largest payroll item expiring and freeing that money funds the Gaborik and Nash raises.

recommendations.summary: Let Roberts walk — 38, $2.70M, no path to meaningful minutes next season.
recommendations.rationale: At 38 and $2.70M he occupies a roster spot and payroll slot that a 21-year-old with POTE in the 90s would fill for half the money.

recommendations.summary: Renew Tellqvist on 2 years at a low salary — 25, POTE high 90s, $0.80M. Cheap backup or trade piece in 2007.
recommendations.rationale: The GM's standing order is to give him time to develop. Two years at $0.80M costs almost nothing and preserves either a quality backup or a tradeable asset with goalie-needy teams.

recommendations.summary: Renew Chistov on 3 years — 21, $1.10M. Young enough to develop, cheap enough to risk.
recommendations.rationale: Three years is the right term: if he breaks out we hold him cheap, if he stalls we have him through age 24 at a manageable salary.

recommendations.summary: Renew Colaiacovo on a 2-year show-me deal — 22, $1.10M, young defenseman who needs to prove he is top-six.
recommendations.rationale: Two years: if he earns a top-pair role we extend, if he does not we have a third-pair defender at $1.10M for one more year.

recommendations.summary: Renew Alexeev on a 2-year deal — 23, $1.10M. Coach is putting him in over Upshall for the final 8 games, which is the audition.
recommendations.rationale: Two years prices him as a depth forward who showed flashes. If his rate jumps over the final eight games we have him controlled through 25.

recommendations.summary: Wait on Upshall until the final 8 games finish. He competes with Alexeev for the same spot; sign the cheaper and younger one.
recommendations.rationale: At $1.20M he is more expensive than Alexeev's $1.10M and the coach is putting Alexeev over him. If Alexeev produces, Upshall becomes the odd man out.

recommendations.summary: Test STL on Reid for Tucker plus the 4th-rounder; at 83 FACE and POTE 93 on $600K expiring he is the only player in the league whose price matches our currency and whose grade fills the L4 draw gap.
recommendations.rationale: Reid is 77 base with 55 points in 63 games at 24, on $600K expiring from a 72-point STL club with 8 expiring deals and $10.25M profit. Tucker gives them a playable wing through the deadline and the 4th is our only asset. Acceptance uncertain because STL may keep a 24-year-old with POTE 93 for development.

recommendations.summary: Probe SJ on Stuart; 87 base, 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG, POTE 91, 25 years old, 48 points in 72 games, $1.80M expiring. The single best fit for our toughness gap but Tucker plus a 4th is likely insufficient.
recommendations.rationale: SJ is 65 points with 13 expiring contracts and no path to retaining him. The over-80 expiring mechanic means SJ gets a pick rather than losing an 87 for nothing, but their ask will likely exceed Tucker plus a 4th. Worth one test offer.

recommendations.summary: Explore CGY on Conroy for Tucker plus the 4th; 94 FACE at 33 on $2.00M expiring from the second-worst team in the league, a pure playoff rental that raises two lines above 70 FACE.
recommendations.rationale: CGY is 58 points with 10 expiring deals and $11.24M profit. The over-80 mechanic means they can trade an expiring 85-overall centre for a pick. Tucker is also expiring so CGY gets a rental plus a pick, which is thin but nonzero. Conroy's 94 FACE is the best available after Marchand, who costs more.

recommendations.summary: Avery remains the only player closing toughness (83 TOUG), checking (88 CHKG), and faceoffs (93 FACE) simultaneously on a cheap deal ($400K, 2 years left). LA wants Koltsov, whom the March 19 order locks. This is a GM decision: unlock Koltsov or play the spring without 80+ TOUG.
recommendations.rationale: The March 19 structural finding confirmed zero Toronto players at 80+ TOUG in stored grades. Avery is the only available fix. LA rejected Tucker explicitly. The Koltsov package at 23 with POTE 94 is what LA asked for. No other player on the board matches Avery's grade combination at that price.

recommendations.summary: Heatley (ATL, 91 base, POTE 85, 24, $1.10M expiring) is the highest-value expiring player in the league but ATL has $24.95M profit and no motivation to accept Tucker plus a 4th. Dropped from active pursuit.
recommendations.rationale: ATL cannot re-sign both Heatley and Kovalchuk but they have no financial pressure to sell cheap. Any offer below a first-round pick plus a prospect is unlikely to interest them.

recommendations.summary: Goalie targets (Theodore, Lalime, Cechmanek, Thibault) are all off the board because the GM closed all goalie monitoring on March 19 with Belfour and Luongo as the playoff pair.
recommendations.rationale: Theodore (MTL, 91 base, $5.50M expiring, 28) fits the Jan 15 order on paper but the March 19 order overrides it. No action.

recommendations.summary: Offer Tucker plus the 4th-rounder to CGY for Conroy; try the 4th alone first if the mechanic permits.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 58 points with 10 expiring deals fits the over-80 dump profile exactly. Conroy's 94 FACE turns our L4 draw problem from 52 into a second elite unit. At 33 with POTE 79 this is a playoff rental only. Acceptance uncertain because CGY may not value Tucker in a rebuild.

recommendations.summary: Probe STL for Reid as a secondary option; 24 years old with POTE 93 is worth one call even at low odds.
recommendations.rationale: Reid is the better long-term fit at 24 with 55 points in 63 games, but STL at 72 points with $10.25M profit has no reason to sell a productive cheap winger. Only works if STL misses the playoff bubble before March 29. Acceptance uncertain.

recommendations.summary: The GM needs to decide before March 29 whether Koltsov is a chip; Avery closes toughness, checking, and faceoffs simultaneously and no other target does.
recommendations.rationale: Coach confirmed zero Toronto skaters carry 80+ TOUG. Avery at 83/88/93 closes all three thin roles at $400K for two years. LA rejected Tucker and requires Koltsov per the March 19 note, which the GM's current order blocks. This is the GM's call to override or not.

recommendations.summary: If neither Conroy nor Reid lands, stand pat and keep the 4th-rounder for July drafting.
recommendations.rationale: At 53-12-4 the faceoff gap is manageable with Richards at 73 FACE sliding to L4, and the toughness gap does not end a playoff run. Spending the only draft pick on a rental centre who walks in July is worse than not spending it if the upgrade is marginal.

recommendations.summary: Close owed item #2. Luongo is on the roster at 93/25/$1.60M/2yr. DiPietro eliminated at 79 base. Goalie monitoring formally closed by GM on March 19.
recommendations.rationale: Both halves of the task are resolved and the mandate itself was withdrawn. No further work exists.

recommendations.summary: Put Alexeev back in the lineup for Upshall on the fourth line for the remaining 8 games.
recommendations.rationale: Alexeev is at 0.55 pts/g (30 in 55) compared to Upshall's 0.32 (19 in 60) on similar ice time. A player producing at that rate belongs in the lineup over one producing at half that.

recommendations.summary: Dress Spacek for the final 8 games even in a limited role; his morale at 89 is the lowest among our young players and he is 19 with POTE 91.
recommendations.rationale: His 10 MPG target is dead but the purpose now is reps at 19. Scratching a POTE 91 winger with 8 games left and no playoff pressure is pure waste.

recommendations.summary: No change this game for Spezza, but flag again: POTE 99, 7.4 MPG, fourth line, 38 GP, raised six times with zero movement.
recommendations.rationale: At 0.39 pts/g in 38 games the current production does not demand a top-nine slot today, but we are 8 games from season's end with a 21-year-old POTE 99 prospect at fourth-line minutes and no resolution either way.

recommendations.slot: left wing on the first line
recommendations.summary: Abid is still at 12.3 MPG with 0.81 pts/g. He needs 18+ before season's end or we waste a quality winger and risk his morale.
recommendations.rationale: His minutes fell from 20.1 to 12.3 since December while his rate stayed at 0.81. The March 16 flag has not been addressed.

recommendations.summary: Spezza's minutes dropped from 9.1 to 5.4 since December while his rate fell to 0.35. At POTE 99 this is a wasted year and we need a decision before April.
recommendations.rationale: 38 games played, 5.4 MPG, 0.35 pts/g. His role got smaller after the January flag, not bigger.

recommendations.summary: McCabe back on the sell list. 0.50 pts/g since December 1 at 29 with four years at $3M.
recommendations.rationale: The March 4 recovery read was a short window. The December-to-March window shows 1.42 falling to 0.50, which is third-pair production at a first-pair price.

recommendations.summary: Klesla is in a second consecutive declining season. 0.50 to 0.30 at 23 on flat minutes. Move him before his contract tightens the market.
recommendations.rationale: Two years of falling rate at an age when the expected direction is up. Minutes are flat at 14.6 to 14.9, so the role is not the excuse.

recommendations.slot: left wing on the first line
recommendations.summary: Gaborik's rate cooled from 1.42 to 1.06 but his minutes rose from 18.8 to 21.1. He is still the best player on this roster and the trend is a hot start settling, not a decline.
recommendations.rationale: 1.06 pts/g at 23 on rising minutes is elite. No action warranted.

recommendations.summary: Chlup at 0.84 pts/g on 18.2 MPG at 19 confirms the top-nine call. Keep feeding him minutes and do not crowd him with veterans.
recommendations.rationale: Rate rose while minutes doubled. That combination at 19 is rare.

recommendations.summary: No morale-driven minutes changes needed; the room is at 99 across the board and every sub-99 player is trending up.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza at 89 (up 3), Upshall at 92 (up 3), Alexeev at 92 (up 5) are the only players below 99 and all are gaining. Everyone else sits at 99 with positive movement. The team's results are lifting the room and no minutes adjustment is warranted with 8 games left.

recommendations.summary: Remove Jackman from K2 tonight against Buffalo to cut his load from 30+ to 26 MPG; keep him on L1 and P1.
recommendations.rationale: 30.4 MPG and 0.48 pts/g at age 24. His production collapsed under the load. Buffalo is 25-31; K2 checking mean drops from 82 to ~75 without him, a cost this opponent makes affordable. Protects his remaining even-strength production for the last 8 games.

recommendations.summary: Hold all four even-strength lines as they are.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has scoring (87/99) and checking (80/89) in balance. L2 is the offensive unit (scoring 85, playmaking 84). L3 carries checking depth (72/92) behind Richards. L4 at 51 faceoffs is the known void but no swap fixes it.

recommendations.summary: Roster lacks a fourth-line centre who wins draws. Best available is 52; Richards at 73 is the next man up and he anchors L3.
recommendations.rationale: L4 faceoff mean 51, best 52. This forces top-six centres into defensive-zone draws all season. No arrangement of current personnel solves it; offseason priority.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour if his fatigue icon is clear on screen; Aebischer if tired.
recommendations.rationale: Standing order from Jan 19: check the goalie-tired icon before confirming. Against a 2.90 GF/g club this is not a night to risk a tired netminder.

recommendations.summary: No line changes for BUF.
recommendations.rationale: Every TOR line has a clear OVR edge over its BUF counterpart. Their top line (82/86/88) meets Sundin/Roberts/Gaborik (89/86/96). Without Brunette their third line drops below 78 OVR. No matchup adjustment is warranted.

recommendations.summary: If the GM wants to dress Spacek for a look, this is that kind of game: 25-31-10 opponent, 9-0-1 TOR streak, 29-3 season goal differential in the series.
recommendations.rationale: BUF is not a quality opponent. The Jan 15 framework says development minutes belong in games we can afford. Spacek's season rate is dead but a 12-minute look in a blowout is harmless.

recommendations.summary: Sell Eminger at season's end. 0.38 pts/g in 56 games on an expiring $1.2M, eight scoreless games since Feb 26.
recommendations.rationale: His recovery collapsed permanently. 21 points in 56 games at 21 years old with one year left. He's a rental D for a contender at his current value.

recommendations.summary: Trade Klesla this offseason. 0.36 pts/g in 74 games on $0.90M x 2, declining for a second straight year.
recommendations.rationale: Age 23, 14.8 MPG, no production trajectory. His market value drops further if 2005-06 confirms him. Cheap to move now.

recommendations.summary: Reduce Jackman below 28 MPG next season. His 0.49 pts/g on 30.1 MPG is the load ceiling.
recommendations.rationale: Season rate has been flat at 0.48-0.49 since early March. At $0.70M x 3 he stays, but his production cannot recover at this workload.

recommendations.summary: Re-raise Avery with LA; the kill condition (toughness as a form artifact) is now disproven — zero Toronto players at 80+ stored TOUG.
recommendations.rationale: The Feb 21 trade was killed because the gap was thought to be form inflation. Current stored grades confirm 0 at 80+ TOUG team-wide. Avery closes TOUG (83) and FACE (93) simultaneously at $400K with two years left. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring are the most motivated seller in the league.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker nightly for penalty-kill and fourth-pair minutes; his 83 CHKG is the team's fifth-best and he currently plays zero minutes.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker is 83 CHKG, $1.3M, 30 years old, and in no unit on the lineup. The checking bench beyond Jackman/Roberts/McCabe is Fischer 82 and Upshall 80. Tucker at 83 is above both and contributes nothing sitting out.

recommendations.summary: Get Upshall to 10+ MPG for the final 9 games; his 80 CHKG at 21 is the depth behind Tucker and Fischer.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach already flagged this on March 16. Upshall is the only young checker on the roster (80 CHKG, 21). If he does not play now, he wastes a second development year and the checking bench is entirely 30+.

recommendations.summary: Toughness gap is confirmed structural: 0 players at 80+ TOUG. No internal fix exists. This is the one gap the deadline must address if we address any.
recommendations.rationale: Highest stored TOUG on the roster is Jackman at 75. The previous kill condition (form inflation) is disproven. The team has zero players who hit 80 in fighting, toughness, or the engine attributes that compose it.

recommendations.proposed: Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, Abid, Chlup
recommendations.summary: Lock the six young core players on 5-6 year deals the week contracts expire; their combined current salary is $5.34M and replacement cost after breakout seasons could exceed $20M on the open market.
recommendations.rationale: Thirteen contracts worth $21.30M expire in one July. Six of them are the franchise (Gaborik 86 pts, Richards 64 pts, Abid 66 pts, Nash POTE 95, Eminger POTE 99, Chlup POTE 95). Without 5-6 year locks they walk simultaneously and the 118-point roster dissolves. Payroll headroom exists: $23.25M profit covers renewal raises.

recommendations.summary: Extend Chlup before his contract expires next July; at 19, POTE 95, $2.34M, and 50 pts, his price in 2006 will be multiples of current salary.
recommendations.rationale: Two years remain but the rookie-window price ($2.34M at 19) disappears after a second top-nine season. The manual says lock stars 5-6 years immediately.

recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour before he becomes a free agent; at 92 base, expiring, $6.50M, he qualifies for the over-80 pick mechanic and is the only source of draft picks this club owns.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo (91 base, 25, 2 years) is the starter. Belfour at 39, $6.50M expiring, is the club's last over-80 pick-recovery asset. If he walks in July, Toronto gains zero and the fourth-rounder remains the only draft capital.

recommendations.summary: Ride out Sundin's five-year deal despite POTE 60 at 34; no mid-contract renegotiation exists and his 81 pts this year earn the $8.40M.
recommendations.rationale: $42M total cost over 5 years is locked. The only lever is a trade, but with 4 years remaining and age 34, no club will take that contract without Toronto paying draft capital it does not have.

recommendations.summary: Move Belfour today to Colorado for Morris or Hejduk, or to any non-playoff club for a draft pick; if he is not traded today, the over-80 pick-recovery value is lost permanently.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour at 92 base and $6.50M expiring is the only over-80 pick-recovery asset left. Colorado offered Hejduk; Morris (85 base, 26, $1.70M) is the better return. This is the last day trades are possible.

recommendations.proposed: Roberts to any non-playoff club for a draft pick
recommendations.summary: Move Roberts (38, $2.70M, over-80, expiring) today for a draft pick via the same mechanic that works for Belfour.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts is the second over-80 expiring asset. A non-playoff team takes his $2.70M for a season of veteran depth and Toronto recovers a pick. He has no role next season at 38.

recommendations.summary: If Belfour's return is a player (not a pick), send Tucker plus the 4th to Ottawa for Havlat today.
