recommendations.rationale: Havlat at 87 base, 23, 80 pts/63 GP on $900K expiring from a 60-point club with 11 expiring deals. Ottawa cannot keep him. This is the scoring upgrade for the playoff but requires the 4th to remain unspent.

recommendations.summary: Renew Gaborik on six years at season end; he is the most urgent summer signing.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base, 23 years old, 67 pts/45 GP, POTE 90. No mid-contract extension is possible, so July is the only window. A bidding war with no cap means he could walk.

recommendations.summary: Renew Eminger on six years at $1.20M; at 21 with POTE 99 he is the cheapest high-ceiling asset on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: Eminger's potential says he develops toward a top-pair defenseman. Locking him at $1.20M for six years costs almost nothing now and saves millions later.

recommendations.summary: Renew Kaberle on five or six years; he is the confirmed first-pair blueliner at 27.
recommendations.rationale: 0.62 pts/g on 21.7 MPG at 27, improving with age. The Coach has locked him for next season.

recommendations.summary: Renew Richards on five years; at 24 with 70 FACE he is the long-term third-line centre.
recommendations.rationale: He fills a role that is expensive on the market and is young enough to still develop. $1.00M is cheap for a two-way centre.

recommendations.summary: Renew Nash on three years, not five or six; his production rate halved at 20 and the answer is not yet clear.
recommendations.rationale: 0.43 pts/g at 20 on stable 12.7 MPG. The Coach flagged this for offseason review. Three years lets the next season determine his value before committing a star contract.

recommendations.summary: Renew Colaiacovo on three or four years as a second-pair blueliner.
recommendations.rationale: At 22 he is a dependable depth defenseman, not a top-pair piece. Do not overpay the term.

recommendations.summary: Renew Upshall on two years at $1.20M; cheap optionality on a player who has not yet proven himself at 21.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach says he needs 10+ MPG to develop or this is a second wasted year. Two years gives one more season before the decision is made at 23.

recommendations.summary: Renew Chistov on two years.
recommendations.rationale: At 21 with $1.10M, he is cheap depth with one more season to show he belongs.

recommendations.summary: Renew Abid on two years at $0.40M.
recommendations.rationale: His 80 TOUG and 80 CHKG fill the toughness role the Coach wants. $0.40M is nothing.

recommendations.summary: Renew Tellqvist on two years; he is the development goalie behind Luongo.
recommendations.rationale: GM standing order is to keep him and give him time. $0.80M is negligible. Two years lets the development continue without overcommitting.

recommendations.summary: If Belfour is not traded today, do not re-sign him in July. Offer one year at $3.5M max; he will decline or retire and that is the correct outcome.
recommendations.rationale: At 39 with $6.50M, he is the highest-paid player on a roster that does not need him. Luongo at 91 base with two years left is the starter. The GM's Feb 19 order to keep him was before the Feb 21 hedge and before the deadline forced the question.

recommendations.summary: If Roberts cannot be traded today, release him in July.
recommendations.rationale: 38 years old, $2.70M, no role on a contending roster next season.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Sean Avery from LA for Tucker ($1.3M expiring) as salary filler. Closes TOUG (83) and FACE (93) simultaneously at $400K for two years.
recommendations.rationale: Zero rostered players at 80+ TOUG; only Sundin at 90 FACE. Avery at 25 with 83 TOUG, 93 FACE, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2 years is the cheapest player in the league closing both gaps on a re-signable deal. LA at 69 points with 15 expiring contracts are the most motivated seller. No draft pick needed.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Havlat from OTT with the 4th-rounder plus a cheap expiring piece if Tucker goes to LA instead. 87 base, 80 pts/63 GP, $900K expiring at 23.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 67 points with 11 expiring cannot retain him. The Feb 26 package was Tucker + 4th. If Tucker ships to LA for Avery, the 4th plus a cheaper salary filler (Chistov $1.1M expiring) may work. OTT needs to shed contracts regardless.

recommendations.summary: Alternative to Havlat at lower cost: Reid from STL, 23, FACE 80, POTE 94, $600K expiring. STL at 71 points with 8 expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Closes the wing faceoff gap without spending the 4th if LA deal works. At 77 base with POTE 94 he is a two-way piece who develops for five more years. STL at $57.44M payroll with only $10.95M profit and 8 expiring deals has motivation to shed even a cheap player.

recommendations.summary: Flag for GM: Bell's Feb 25 kill was premised on faceoffs not being a real gap. The coverage phase now confirms zero 80+ TOUG on the roster. The premise is dead but the price problem (CHI profitable at $26.71M) remains.
recommendations.rationale: TOUG 95, CHKG 93, FACE 87, 80 base, 24, $900K, 2 years. The single best player for our structural needs. CHI will not sell cheap and we lack the capital tonight. July re-entry if CHI re-signs no one.

recommendations.summary: July UFA target confirmed. 89 base, 98 pts, 25, $1.60M expiring from SJ at 63 points with 13 expiring. No deadline trade path.
recommendations.rationale: The Mar 16 note confirmed SJ will not accept Belfour. With no third-party package identified and our protected core locked, the only path is July free agency. At $1.60M current salary with 5 years to offer, this is the highest-upside move available in four months.

recommendations.summary: Send Koltsov to LA for Avery to close the toughness and faceoff gap simultaneously on two years of control at $400K.
recommendations.rationale: Zero rostered players at 80+ TOUG in stored grades; Avery at 83 TOUG, 93 FACE, 88 CHKG is the only available player closing both. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring wants exactly what Koltsov offers: a 23-year-old at $1.10M with POTE 94 and ACCE 96/AGIL 92.

recommendations.summary: Send Tucker and the 4th-rounder to Ottawa for Havlat as a playoff scoring upgrade at second-line wing.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 67 points with 11 expiring contracts cannot retain Havlat ($900K expiring). Tucker's 92 CHKG and 88 TOUG are physical depth for a seller's rebuild plus a draft pick. Havlat's 80 points at 23 gives the lineup a second dynamic wing for the playoffs. Spends our only pick, so attempt Avery first.

recommendations.proposed: Morris (D, COL, 26, 85 base, 57 pts/65 GP, $1.70M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Exploratory: test Belfour for Morris with Colorado; do not execute without explicit GM approval given the Feb 19 goalie-stays stance.
recommendations.rationale: Colorado at 72 points has no reliable starter; Belfour's 2.27 GAA is the best on the market. Morris at 26 with 85 base and 57 points fills blue-line depth at a lower salary than Hejduk. However, Morris fails the GM's 'locked on reasonable salary for a couple of years' test because he is expiring.

recommendations.summary: Owed task #2 (Luongo monitoring and DiPietro tracking) is complete and requires no further action.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is rostered at 94 overall with 2 years and $1.60M. DiPietro reads 79 base at 52 GP, failing the high-90s standard. GM closed the goalie file on Feb 19.

recommendations.summary: Dress Spezza against CBJ. He is 21 with POTE 99, at 37 games and 7.5 MPG, and CBJ is 24-34.
recommendations.rationale: The GM's January 15th framework says development takes priority in games we can afford. CBJ at 24-34 is one. Spezza at 0.41 pts/g on garbage minutes has not been given a fair sample.

recommendations.summary: Give Stahle a three-game run starting against CBJ. Four games in a season at 20 and POTE 96 is burying him.
recommendations.rationale: When he plays he gets 17.8 MPG, so the system sees him as a top-pair defenceman. Four games is not enough to judge a 20-year-old either way. Start the run against the weakest opponent on the schedule.

recommendations.current: Gaborik, Chlup, Nash, Klesla, Eminger, Chistov, Upshall
recommendations.summary: The core young group is getting substantial games. No change needed for them.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik at 73 GP/20.4 MPG, Chlup at 62/16.6, Klesla at 73/14.8, Nash at 60/12.7, Eminger at 55/15.8, Chistov at 59/13.2, Upshall at 59/8.5. Everyone playing regularly and in proportion to their role.

recommendations.summary: Confirm Chlup as a permanent top-nine centre entering next season's lineup planning.
recommendations.rationale: 0.62→0.86 pts/g on minutes doubling from 11.0 to 18.0 across 49 games at 19. He's earning his ice, not just getting it.

recommendations.slot: left wing, second or third line
recommendations.summary: Give Chistov a larger role next season; he's been quietly developing at 21.
recommendations.rationale: 0.29→0.36 pts/g on 9.5→14.3 MPG. The direction is right for a 21-year-old winger. He's not a star but he's growing into a regular.

recommendations.summary: Spezza's development year is dead at 5.3 MPG. Raise a real offseason plan for him before his POTE 99 goes to waste for a second year.
recommendations.rationale: 0.43→0.38 pts/g on 9.1→5.3 MPG across 37 games at 21. Raised eight times with no movement. At this point it's not about tonight's game; it's about whether he has a role here next year.

recommendations.summary: Stop dressing Spacek for development purposes. His minutes are 5.2 and his year is over.
recommendations.rationale: 0.55→0.28 pts/g on 16.0→5.2 MPG across 50 games at 19. There's nothing to develop at five minutes. Use the roster spot for Chistov or Stahle.

recommendations.summary: Restore Abid's minutes to 18+ immediately. 0.82 pts/g on 12.4 MPG wastes him.
recommendations.rationale: His rate held (0.82 in 49 games since the minutes cut) while minutes dropped from 20.1 to 12.4. A player producing at top-six rates on fourth-line ice gets unhappy.

recommendations.summary: The offseason is the last window for Koltsov as a tradeable asset. His 0.28 pts/g over 25 recent games will price him as a bench player.
recommendations.rationale: 1.10→0.28 pts/g across the window. Any club evaluating him sees the trend, not the October hot start. 23 years old, but the chip is dying.

recommendations.slot: left wing / right wing, top six
recommendations.summary: Begin offseason planning for the end of Mogilny and Roberts. At 36 and 38 their rates (0.82, 0.86) won't hold next year.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny at 36: 0.82 pts/g on 19.2 MPG. Roberts at 38: 0.86 on 21.4 MPG. Both still productive but neither at 37 and 39. Chlup and Chistov are the internal replacements; external depth is the next question.

recommendations.summary: Nash at 20 needs an offseason system-fit review. His rate halved with flat minutes.
recommendations.rationale: 0.83→0.42 pts/g on 12.9→12.6 MPG. The role didn't change, the production did. That points to fit, not effort or opportunity.

recommendations.summary: The room is happy; no morale-driven changes needed.
recommendations.rationale: Almost every player is at 99 morale with upward movement. Spezza at 86 is scratched and that's a roster decision, not a line one. Spacek at 89 matches his 7.6 MPG to his 70-79 band. Abid at 99 has not slipped despite his low minutes.

recommendations.summary: All four even-strength lines and both PK units are built correctly for this roster; hold the sheet against CBJ.
recommendations.rationale: L1 checking mean 82 with Sundin at 91 faceoffs, L4 faceoff void at 52 mean persists but no bench player fixes it, K2 checking mean 84 is our strongest unit. Against a 24-34 opponent no matchup adjustment justifies breaking chemistry.

recommendations.summary: Fourth-line faceoff mean is 52 with a best of 53; we need a centre who wins draws off the bench.
recommendations.rationale: Richards at 75 is the next-best draw man and he anchors L3. No bench player above 54 in faceoffs exists on this roster. This forces top-six defensive-zone starts all season.

recommendations.summary: Roster toughness peaks at 77 (Jackman). We cannot build a physical fourth line that finishes checks.
recommendations.rationale: Abid at 72 is the only forward above 70 in toughness. Against physical teams we absorb hits rather than deliver them. This limits our ability to protect Gaborik and Kaberle on a per-shift basis.

recommendations.summary: Hold the lines as configured for CBJ.
recommendations.rationale: CBJ's top line is Marchant/Sanderson/Vyborny at 82/83/78 OVR and their scoring is 1.60 per game. The auto-pairing already gives our top two lines their weakest D pair and gives their top line our Fischer/Jackman pair. No slot reorder improves this.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour if his fatigue icon is clear on screen; Aebischer if tired.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour has started the last four wins and is at 93 OVR. He is 39 and the standing order requires checking the fatigue icon before every start. CBJ scores 1.60 per game so either goalie handles this workload.

recommendations.summary: Sell Eminger at season's end. Season rate 0.38 pts/g over 55 games at 21, contract expiring $1.20M, below the 0.45 threshold set January 26.
recommendations.rationale: Rate slipped from 0.44 in February to 0.38 now. He is not recovering and the contract runs out. Sell while there is something to sell.

recommendations.summary: Klesla second on the sell list. 0.37 pts/g at 22 over 73 games, declining each season. No payroll urgency at $0.90M x 2 but the trajectory says trade.
recommendations.rationale: Third year running the expected direction at his age is up and he goes sideways or down. $0.90M is cheap so no rush, but the asset is depreciating.

recommendations.summary: McCabe stays off the sell list at 0.81 pts/g over 73 games. Watch if he dips below 0.75 next season given four years left at $3.00M.
recommendations.rationale: Production is fine now. The concern is the contract length against a slight rate slide, not today's play.

recommendations.summary: Jackman confirmed sell-list pass at 0.49 pts/g on 30.3 MPG over 71 games. Not a sell at $0.70M, but his role must change next season or the minutes go elsewhere.
recommendations.rationale: Three weeks of data confirms the March 5 call. Cheap enough to keep, too overloaded to produce.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker nightly as the fourth checker; his 83 CHKG and 88 stored TOUG are the free internal fix for the bottom pair.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker is on the roster in no unit. Six players have displayed CHKG at 80+ but only three are lined as checkers (Jackman, Roberts, McCabe). Adding Tucker gives the coach a fourth without a trade.

recommendations.summary: Do not pursue a toughness trade. The displayed zero-at-80 gap is a form artifact; stored grades show six players at 80+ TOUG.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker's displayed TOUG is 70 against a stored 88, an 18-point engine-form drag. The whole club shows the same compression. No external target is needed to close a gap that does not exist on standing grades.

recommendations.summary: Slide Richards to third-line centre for faceoff duty; at 70 FACE he is the best draw-taker behind Sundin (90).
recommendations.rationale: Only one player clears 80 FACE. Richards at 70 with 85 P and 85 ENDU gives the third line both a center and secondary playmaking without costing anything externally.

recommendations.summary: Faceoff depth (1 at 80+) is a gap but not a deadline target. No available player justifies the package cost.
recommendations.rationale: Bell is a wing (GM killed Feb 25). Avery's 0.11 ppg kills his value. The game does not appear to weight faceoffs heavily enough to justify spending a pick on a 70-75 FACE player.

recommendations.summary: Durability at four players 80+ is thin but untradeable; accept it for the playoff run.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts 98, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92, Abid 90 are the only four clearing 80 INJU. Mogilny (36) and Roberts (38) lead the scoring group. The market does not price injury resistance, so no package recovers its cost.

recommendations.proposed: Gaborik, Eminger, Nash, Upshall, Chistov, Richards
recommendations.summary: Lock all six young-core players on 5-6 year deals in July 2005 before their breakout seasons raise their asks
recommendations.rationale: They carry $6.90M combined on expiring deals, produce 256 points combined, and all carry POTE 88+. A single-summer cluster of 13 expiring deals is the manual's named trap; locking the six who matter most before July eliminates the core of the problem.

recommendations.proposed: Kaberle on 2-3 years, Tucker on 2 years if he returns from injury
recommendations.summary: Sign Kaberle short at his current salary tier rather than locking a 27-year-old with POTE 75 into a long deal
recommendations.rationale: Kaberle is 27 with POTE 75 and 38 points in 64 games. His value peaks now; 5-6 years is the wrong term for a player whose ceiling is set. Two or three years at $2-2.5M is the right shape.

recommendations.proposed: A draft pick or a young player with years left
recommendations.summary: Move Belfour before season end via the over-80 expiring mechanic to recover a pick or a keeper, then let the $6.50M salary walk
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 92 base, 39, $6.50M with one year left. The GM is already exploring trade returns. The over-80 mechanic guarantees pick recovery even if the trade market softens. Luongo at 91 base and 25 is the replacement.

recommendations.summary: Sundin stays at 5 years locked; his succession is handled by Chlup (19, POTE 95, 50 pts) and Spacek (19, POTE 91)
recommendations.rationale: Sundin at 34, $8.40M, 5 years is the largest contract and the oldest lock, but Chlup is already producing 50 points in 61 games at 19. No action needed until the contract naturally ages out around 2009-10.

recommendations.summary: Accept Fischer's $3.70M x 4 years as dead money for now; revisit as salary-matching bait in 2007 when his value as a trade chip improves with other clubs' need for blueliners
recommendations.rationale: Fischer at 24 with 0.49 ppg and 4 years left is not tradeable in a winning window without taking a bad return. Waiting two years means his contract has 2 years left, making him useful as a salary-matching piece on a larger deal.

recommendations.summary: Move Belfour by March 18 — 92 base, $6.50M, 39, expiring. If he retires in July the value is gone.
recommendations.rationale: GM flagged retirement risk on Feb 21. Colorado offered Hejduk; Morris is younger and cheaper but also expiring, failing the GM's own term test. Either is better than zero.

recommendations.proposed: draft pick from a non-playoff club
recommendations.summary: Move Roberts to a non-playoff team for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic before March 19.
recommendations.rationale: 87 base, 38, $2.70M expiring. Toronto own no pick better than a 4th. Per the March 4 correction, send him to a team not in the playoff race.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Havlat (87 base, 80 pts/63 GP, $900K expiring) from Ottawa with Tucker plus the 4th-rounder.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 60 points with 11 expiring cannot retain him. If Belfour goes to Colorado for Hejduk, this becomes the secondary scoring upgrade using the 4th. If Belfour walks, this is the primary deadline move.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik (91 base, 23, $1.10M) on a 5-6 year deal at season end. Highest priority renewal on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: No mid-contract renegotiation possible. He is free in July. A 91-base 23-year-old will command a bidding war if untethered.

recommendations.summary: Lock Eminger (76 base, 21, $1.20M, POTE 99) on a 5-6 year deal at season end.
recommendations.rationale: GM-protected since Jan 19. At 21 with POTE 99, the cost today is trivial and the cost of losing him is a franchise blueliner.

recommendations.summary: Lock Richards (82 base, 24, $1.00M) on a 5-6 year deal at season end.
recommendations.rationale: Top-nine centre at 24 and $1.00M. A 5-6 year deal caps the cost at a price a team of his grade would never sign again.

recommendations.summary: Lock Nash (77 base, 20, $1.20M) on a 5-6 year deal at season end.
recommendations.rationale: 20 years old. Cheapest upside on the roster. Locking him long is a one-line insurance policy.

recommendations.summary: Renew Kaberle (84 base, 27, $1.90M) on 3-4 years.
recommendations.rationale: Prime age, established top-pair defenceman. Three or four years matches his stage without overcommitting to a 30+ contract.

recommendations.summary: Renew Tellqvist (77 base, 25, $0.80M) on 2-3 years.
recommendations.rationale: GM standing order: keep him, give him time to develop. High potential, $0.80M, no reason to let him walk.

recommendations.summary: Renew Abid (79 base, 24, $0.40M) on 2 years.
recommendations.rationale: 79 base at $0.40M is the cheapest roster player on the sheet. Two years is a formality.

recommendations.summary: Renew Colaiacovo (72 base, 22, $1.10M) on 2 years.
recommendations.rationale: Coach is putting him in the lineup this month. Two years at depth pricing keeps him while you see if he develops.

recommendations.summary: Renew Upshall (78 base, 21, $1.20M) on 2-3 years.
recommendations.rationale: Same age band as Eminger and Nash, one grade tier below. Renew short, reassess after a full season.

recommendations.summary: Let Alexeev (76 base, 23, $1.10M) walk at season end unless a roster hole opens.
recommendations.rationale: 23 years old and still 76 base. No trajectory suggests he becomes more than a filler. $1.10M is better spent elsewhere.

recommendations.summary: Explore moving Chistov (78 base, 21, $1.10M) before July if a club offers a pick or useful depth for him.
recommendations.rationale: 78 base at 21 is replaceable in the draft. If a deal exists by the deadline, take it; if not, renew short and keep monitoring.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Marleau before Friday; he is 25, 89 base, 98 pts/70 GP on $1.60M expiring from a 63-point club with 13 expiring deals and $19.46M profit.
recommendations.rationale: Solves the bottom-six scoring cliff and the centre depth problem simultaneously. At 25 with POTE likely high, he is the best dynasty player in the entire scan. SJ must move him or lose him for nothing in July.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Gagne before Friday; 25, 86 base, 94 pts/69 GP on $2.40M expiring from a club with $66.73M payroll and only $4.87M profit.
recommendations.rationale: PHI is the most financially desperate club in the league. Gagne at 25 costs them a $6M+ re-signing in July. At 92 speed and 79 injury resistance he can play alongside Gaborik or Sundin. Young enough for the dynasty.

recommendations.summary: Insurance target if Marleau and Gagne fail; 29, 89 base, 111 pts/71 GP (51 goals), $3.00M expiring from CHI at 63 points with 10 expiring and $27.19M profit.
recommendations.rationale: The single highest-scoring player available. At 29 he is a bridge piece, not a long-term answer, but 111 points wins playoff series tonight. Chicago's sell window is wide open.

recommendations.summary: Add-on to Gagne from the same desperate seller; 26, 85 base, 75 pts/60 GP on $1.00M with 92 speed, expiring.
recommendations.rationale: PHI must shed both to cut payroll. Sturm at $1.00M is nearly free salary-wise and provides top-six scoring depth at 26. Injured 50 is a concern in a 60-GP season.

recommendations.summary: Best Belfour return candidate; 29, 90 base, $3.60M expiring from SJ at 63 points with 13 expiring deals.
recommendations.rationale: Matches the Jan 15 order for a high-90s goalie from a non-contender. At $3.60M a 3-year re-signing at $4.5M is realistic. The obstacle: SJ has no need for Belfour at $6.50M and 39. A third club or a different return piece is required.

recommendations.summary: Summer target if a blue-liner leaves; 25, 87 base, 47 pts/70 GP carrying 30.5 MPG on $1.80M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: No roster gap tonight, but if Kaberle walks in July (his ceiling is set, short renewal likely), Stuart at 25 with 30 MPG is the replacement. SJ's sell window means a July approach on a cheap expiring contract.

recommendations.summary: Secondary wing option from the same Chicago window; 30, 87 base, 85 pts/71 GP, 95 speed, $3.00M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: At 30 he is a bridge not a dynasty piece, but the 95 speed and 85 points fill the right-wing slot alongside Gaborik immediately. Chicago will deal three wings if the package is right.

recommendations.summary: Close the Luongo/DiPietro monitoring task; it is complete and the live thread is Theodore.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is on our roster at 93/2yr/$1.60M. DiPietro is 79 base at 52 GP and permanently eliminated. Theodore (MTL, 91 base, expiring, non-contender) is the active high-90s target identified March 5.

recommendations.summary: Dress Spezza for the NYI game and any comfortable game in the last 10.
recommendations.rationale: 7.5 MPG, 37 games, POTE 99, age 21. His morale has dropped to 86, the lowest among all young players, which is the game telling us the lack of ice time is costing the locker room. The window to do anything this season is closing.

recommendations.summary: Give Colaiacovo more starts over Eminger for the remaining games.
recommendations.rationale: Both at 0.39 pts/g. Colaiacovo averages 17.9 MPG when playing versus Eminger's 15.9, meaning Colaiacovo produces the same at higher efficiency per minute. At 22 with POTE 99, the rotation no longer justifies his 43% share.

recommendations.summary: Chlup, Nash, Gaborik, Klesla, Eminger, Chistov and Upshall are all getting the minutes their production earns.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup at 50 pts/61 GP on L2, Nash at 35/59 on L3, Gaborik at 85/72 on L1 -- no one is being held back. Spacek at 7.8 MPG on L4 is the right fit at 19.

recommendations.summary: Give Abid back 18+ MPG for the last 10 games. He is at 0.84 pts/g on 12.6 MPG, which is a bench role for a player who is still producing.
recommendations.rationale: Abid's minutes dropped from 20.1 to 12.6 while his production stayed at 0.84 pts/g at age 24. A 0.84-rate winger on 12 minutes is a morale problem waiting to happen and wasted quality.

recommendations.summary: Get Upshall to 10+ MPG for the final 10 games or accept a second wasted development year at 21.
recommendations.rationale: Upshall is at 5.3 MPG with a flat 0.32 rate across 58 games. At 21 with 10 games left, another season of garbage minutes tells him nothing about his ceiling.

recommendations.summary: Flag Nash for offseason review: 0.43 pts/g at 20 on stable 12.7 MPG means his rate halved with no change in role. Determine if this is a system-fit issue or a ceiling.
recommendations.rationale: Nash went from 0.83 pts/g (first 24 games) to 0.43 (35 games since) on identical minutes. The role did not change, the production did. That is not explained by ice time and needs a deliberate look before next season.

recommendations.summary: No change. Chlup at 0.88 pts/g on 18 MPG at 19 is the confirmed breakout. Keep him in the top nine.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup went from 0.62 to 0.88 while minutes went from 11 to 18. At 19 that direction under more load is rare. He has earned permanent top-nine status.

recommendations.summary: No change. Kaberle at 0.62 pts/g on 21.7 MPG at 27 is improving with age. First pair locked for next season.
recommendations.rationale: Kaberle's rate rose from 0.54 to 0.62 while minutes went from 19.4 to 21.7. Most defencemen at 27 are plateauing; he is climbing. The GM's read on him was right.

recommendations.summary: No lineup change. Fischer's decline (0.63→0.44 at 24 on rising minutes) is a planning flag for the GM, not a tonight problem.
recommendations.rationale: GM's keeper per standing order from Jan 15. The trend is real but the response is offseason role adjustment, not a current lineup fix.

recommendations.summary: No morale-driven line or ice-time change needed; the room is at 92+ across the board except two development scratches whose trends are stable or positive.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza at 86 is the only player below 89 and he's a deliberate scratch trending flat. Spacek at 89 is up 5 in the last save. Every dressed player is at 92+ with no negative trend. No intervention required.

recommendations.summary: All four lines and both PK units are correctly composed for their jobs; no shuffling needed for NYI.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has the checking (Jackman 88, Roberts 82) plus the scoring (Gaborik 97). L2 is the offensive line by design with Mogilny 92 and Afinogenov 90. L3 gets Richards at 95 clutch for matchups. K1 and K2 both carry two players at 82+ checking. The only structural gap (L4 faceoffs at mean 50) is unfixable from the bench.

recommendations.summary: Play standard lines. No adjustment gives a meaningful edge against a 7.5% PP team we outscore by 1.2 per game.
recommendations.rationale: TOR is 51-12-4 with 3.40 GF and 1.40 GA per game vs NYI at 26-33-4, 2.20 GF, 2.50 GA. Their PP is 17/227 (7.5%). Peca (CHKG 88, AGGR 92) pressures our L2/D2 group but swapping D slot order to fix that removes Jackman SHPW 90 from the point on L1, a bigger offensive cost than the defensive gain.

recommendations.summary: Activate Tucker on the penalty kill and third pair immediately to split Jackman's checking load.
recommendations.rationale: Jackman at 87 CHKG is the only blueliner above 83; Tucker at 83 CHKG is the next best and currently in no unit. The coach wants Jackman's minutes cut but has no replacement lined.

recommendations.summary: Faceoffs remain the one unfixable internal gap: only Sundin at 90 FACE is above 80, with Richards at 70 the next option.
recommendations.rationale: No acquired player at the deadline will change a 7-10 point faceoff deficit in a seven-game series; this is a summer free-agency or draft priority, not a March problem.

recommendations.summary: Toughness gap is a form artifact, not a real deficiency; no external target needed.
recommendations.rationale: Feb 21 confirmed six players at 80+ stored TOUG. The displayed zero above 80 is form depression, identical to the Feb 24 reading. No trade currency should be spent on toughness.

recommendations.summary: The coach's own report contradicts itself on Spezza: dress him 8 of 11, then stop dressing him. At 37 GP and 5.3 MPG his season is done regardless.
recommendations.rationale: 37 games at 5.3 minutes averages 197 total minutes. He is not developing in this role. Plan for top-nine next season as the coach says, and stop dressing him now.

recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour before March 19 for a young player on a reasonable multi-year deal; his $6.50M and 92 base qualify him as the club's largest pick-recovery asset.
recommendations.rationale: 39 years old, $6.50M expiring, CONS 50. His 2.27 GAA and .916 SV make him a premium rental right now. The GM's Feb 21 order is to fetch someone 'good but locked on reasonable salary for a couple of years.' Luongo at 91 base, 25, $1.60M two years left is already on the roster and is the number one.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla ($3.60M, 36, 92 CHKG, expiring) before the deadline to a non-contender for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: Combined with Belfour, these are the only two assets that can recover a first or second rounder. Toronto holds no pick better than a fourth. Failing to move Svehla means entering the 2005 draft with that single fourth and no future lottery capital.

recommendations.proposed: Gaborik, Eminger, Nash, Richards, Kaberle on 5-6 year deals
recommendations.summary: At season end, lock the five Tier-1 players on 5-6 year deals immediately; they are $6.50M combined now and will cost $15-18M on long term, well within the $24.72M profit headroom.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik 85 pts at $1.10M, Eminger POTE 99 at $1.20M, Nash POTE 95 at $1.20M, Richards 63 pts/POTE 88 at $1.00M, Kaberle 38 pts at $1.90M. All are one-year expiring. If any walk in July the core fractures and the timeline resets.

recommendations.proposed: Chistov, Alexeev, Abid, Upshall, Colaiacovo, Tellqvist on 2-3 year deals
recommendations.summary: Give the Tier-2 prospects two-year deals with modest raises; they need development time before the club commits five years and $3M+ each.
recommendations.rationale: Six players with POTE 91-99 on expiring one-year deals at $0.40-1.20M. Two-year deals at roughly double current salary total about $7-9M and re-enter the market in 2007 when we can tell prospects from busts. This staggers the cluster across two summers.

recommendations.summary: Fischer ($3.70M, four years, 0.50 ppg declining) is dead money through 2009; not actionable before 2008, no moves available on a four-year deal in this game.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 90 says he should be more; 33 points in 66 games says he is not. The contract has three years left beyond this season. Flag for summer 2008 trade bait. Nothing to do now.

recommendations.summary: Execute the Belfour-to-Colorado-for-Hejduk trade before March 19; Colorado confirmed they would give Hejduk on Feb 21.
recommendations.rationale: Hejduk is 91 base, $2.50M, 2 years left. He meets the GM's own Feb 21 test: good player, reasonable salary, locked for a couple of years. Belfour at 39 and $6.50M walks for nothing in July if not moved by Friday.

recommendations.proposed: Any non-contender offering a pick or high-potential youth
recommendations.summary: Trade Roberts to a non-playoff team for a draft pick using the over-80 expiring mechanic before March 19.
recommendations.rationale: He is 87 base, over 80, expiring, not protected by the GM, and 38 years old. The March 4 standing order says non-playoff teams are the correct destination. If not moved he walks in July with no return.

recommendations.summary: Sign Gaborik to a 5-6 year deal immediately at season end; he is the highest-base expiring player on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base at 23 with POTE 90 means his value is rising. If he hits the market against the other 12 expiring players, the July cluster gives him leverage.

recommendations.summary: Sign Nash to a 5-6 year deal at season end; he is 20 and the cheapest long-term asset on the list.
recommendations.rationale: At 20 with one year left he is the easiest star to lock before his asking price moves. A 5-year deal now is the cheapest it will ever be.

recommendations.summary: Sign Eminger to a 5-6 year deal; GM has explicitly protected him and his potential says the ceiling is real.
recommendations.rationale: GM protected Eminger on Feb 19 specifically because POTE 99 at age 21 makes him the long-term answer on the blue line. Lock him before the cluster.

recommendations.summary: Sign Kaberle to a 5-year deal; he is 27, established, and the other half of the top pair.
recommendations.rationale: At 27 with 1 year left, his asking price will jump once other clubs see him available. Five years locks him through his prime.

recommendations.summary: Sign Richards to a 5-year deal; at 24 and $1.00M he is the cheapest core player relative to his role.
recommendations.rationale: Centre at 24 with a 70 FACE and top-nine role on $1.00M is the best value on the roster. A five-year lock at modest raise is non-negotiable.

recommendations.summary: Renew Tellqvist on 3 years; GM's Jan 15 order is clear that he stays and develops.
recommendations.rationale: GM ordered Tellqvist stays for development toward high-90s potential. Three years is enough runway without overcommitting at his current level.

recommendations.summary: Renew Abid on 2-3 years at or near current $0.40M; he is the only physical presence on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: 80 TOUG and 80 CHKG at $0.40M is the cheapest toughness in the league. Two years covers the next cycle without locking a role player long.

recommendations.summary: Do not execute the Havlat trade this deadline; Hejduk via Belfour already adds the top-6 winger needed.
recommendations.rationale: The Havlat target was built to solve depth scoring. With Hejduk (91 base) arriving via Belfour, adding another 87-base winger at the cost of Tucker and the only pick Toronto owns is redundant.

recommendations.summary: Lead deadline scoring target: 87 base, 80 pts in 63 GP, $900K expiring from 65-pt OTT. Package: Tucker + 4th-rounder.
recommendations.rationale: Fills the depth scoring gap the whole team is struggling with. OTT at 65 pts with 11 expiring and $32.13M profit are sellers. Tucker at 83 CHKG is free currency; Colaiacovo moving up and Stahle on the third pair absorbs his absence internally.

recommendations.summary: Best Belfour return meeting GM's 'locked on reasonable salary' test: 26, 85 base, 57 pts in 65 GP, $1.70M expiring from COL.
recommendations.rationale: GM's Feb 21 order: get someone good but young on a reasonable multi-year salary. Morris at 26 and $1.70M fits. COL at 91 pts need a goalie; Belfour's 2.27 GAA is premium. Fills the 30-33 age bracket and blue line depth simultaneously.

recommendations.summary: Cheapest faceoff gap closer: 23, FACE 80, POTE 94, $600K expiring from 69-pt STL.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin at 90 FACE is our only 80+ faceoff winner. Reid at FACE 80 gives a second. STL at 69 pts with 8 expiring are not in the race. At $600K a low-cost return suffices. Expiring so it's a playoff rental unless re-signed.

recommendations.summary: Better faceoff option than Reid at centre (FACE 89 vs 80): 27, 48 pts in 43 GP, $1.00M expiring from 72-pt ATL.
recommendations.rationale: A centre at FACE 89 pairs directly with Sundin for playoff matchups. ATL prioritizing Kovalchuk/Heatley; Savard is a secondary fire-sale piece. Pairs with any ATL conversation at minimal marginal cost.

recommendations.summary: Development blueliner from the league's second-worst club: 23, 77 base, 83 TOUG, POTE 90, $1.10M expiring from 55-pt MTL.
recommendations.rationale: MTL at 55 pts with 15 expiring in full teardown. At POTE 90 and 23, he fills the 24-29 bracket if re-signed in July. Costs a depth player. Not urgent this season but a cheap development asset if available.

recommendations.summary: Pick-recovery asset: 36, 92 CHKG, $3.60M expiring. Trade to any non-playoff team before March 19 for a 4th or 5th-rounder.
recommendations.rationale: Over-80 expiring mechanic recovers a draft pick. Feb 19 GM standing order says send rentals to non-playoff teams to avoid arming rivals. CGY, MTL, SJ, MIN, CHI all need a veteran blueliner for playoff insurance.

recommendations.summary: Highest-ceiling available player: 22, POTE 98, 1.17 ppg, $1.10M expiring from 67-pt LA with 15 expiring deals.
recommendations.rationale: LA are the deepest sellers in the league. But package construction is hard with one 4th and Belfour committed to the COL conversation. Keep alive as a stretch target; if LA say yes to Belfour + 4th, this is the best long-term outcome on the board.

recommendations.proposed: Morris (D, 26, $1.70M, expiring, 85 base, 57 pts/65 GP) from Colorado
recommendations.summary: Test Morris specifically with Colorado before accepting Hejduk; they lose Morris and Skoula both in July and need playoff goalie insurance now.
recommendations.rationale: COL at 91 points need a playoff-ready netminder; Belfour's 2.27 GAA and .916 SP in 21 GP fill that. COL lose both Morris ($1.70M) and Skoula ($1.40M) in July so moving Morris now costs them depth they were losing anyway. We save $4.80M net salary and acquire a 26-year-old 85-base defenseman re-signable at $2-2.5M.

recommendations.current: Tucker (LW, 29, $1.30M, 2yr, CHKG 92, not lined) + 4th-rounder to Ottawa
recommendations.proposed: Havlat (LW, 23, 87 base, 80 pts/63 GP, $900K, expiring) from Ottawa
recommendations.summary: Send Tucker plus the 4th to Ottawa for Havlat; OTT at 65 points with four expiring top-nine forwards cannot retain all of them.
recommendations.rationale: OTT's forward depth from q113: Alfredsson 92/expiring, Bonk 86/expiring, Smolinski 84/expiring, Havlat 87/expiring. They must cut one. Tucker at 92 CHKG and 2 years gives them the physical wing their roster lacks (best existing CHKG is Fisher at 85). We get 80 points from a 23-year-old at $900K; if he re-signs in July, we've locked a second-line winger for years. If not, we lose only a non-lining 29-year-old and a 4th.

recommendations.current: Svehla (D, 36, $3.60M, expiring, 92 CHKG) to a non-playoff team
recommendations.summary: Move Svehla to Atlanta (0 defensemen at 80+ CHKG, 72 points, non-playoff) for a late pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: Per the March 4 GM correction, non-playoff teams are the right destination to avoid strengthening a rival. ATL from q114 have 10 defensemen and zero at 80+, making them the league's worst D depth. The over-80 expiring mechanic should recover a pick. If ATL decline, PHX (74 pts, 2 D at 80+) is the next target.

recommendations.current: St. Jacques (D, 24, $800K, 2yr, POTE 94, 1 GP) to STL
recommendations.proposed: Reid (RW, 23, 77 base, FACE 80, POTE 94, $600K, expiring) from STL
recommendations.summary: Fallback if Havlat does not land: St. Jacques for Reid closes the faceoff gap at $200K net cost without spending the 4th-rounder.
recommendations.rationale: STL at 69 points from q114 have 8 defensemen and 2 at 80+; St. Jacques at POTE 94 gives them a development prospect. Reid's FACE 80 is the only available option below the 4th-rounder price. Risk: giving POTE 94 for an expiring rental. Only do this if Havlat falls through.

recommendations.summary: DiPietro monitoring is complete: 52 GP, 2.82 GAA, 87.1% SV, but 79 base overall fails the high-90s test. Theodore (91 base) remains the only target.
recommendations.rationale: The Jan 15 standing order requires a high-90s goalie from a non-contender. DiPietro at 79 base with 52 games of solid-but-not-elite work is eliminated on grade. Theodore at 91 from MTL (55 pts) is the sole remaining fit and was flagged March 5.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza at least 8 of the remaining 11 games in a fourth-line centre role.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99, 37 GP in 71, 34 consecutive scratches. At 21 with the highest scouting number on the roster, he cannot finish another year at 37 games.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle for at least 6 of the remaining 11 games on the third pair.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 96, 4 games in 71 at age 20. When he played he got 17.8 MPG, so the trust is there. He just needs to get dressed.

recommendations.summary: Swap Colaiacovo in for Klesla on the second pair for the remaining games after tonight.
recommendations.rationale: Colaiacovo at POTE 99, 31 GP, 17.9 MPG, 0.39 pts/g vs Klesla at 71 GP, 14.9 MPG, 0.37 pts/g and a second declining season. Both produce similarly but Colaiacovo is younger with a higher ceiling.

recommendations.summary: Hold Chlup, Nash, and Gaborik exactly where they are.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup 0.82 pts/g on 16.5 MPG, Nash 0.60 pts/g on 12.7 MPG, Gaborik 1.20 pts/g on 20.2 MPG. All three are outperforming their minutes. No intervention needed.

recommendations.summary: McCabe back on the sell list at the top: 0.49 pts/g over 71 games with effectively zero production since December.
recommendations.rationale: I pulled him off the sell list on March 4th based on a 0.83 rate that does not hold. Current season rate is 0.49 over 71 games on four years at $3M. He is the loudest D sell.

recommendations.summary: Spezza's season is dead at 37 GP and 5.3 MPG. Stop dressing him now and plan for him to play top-nine next season.
recommendations.rationale: At 21 with POTE 99, 5.3 MPG in 37 games develops nobody. The recent window shows near-zero minutes. Next season he needs a real role or he is another wasted year.

recommendations.summary: Koltsov's trade value is collapsing: 1.10 to 0.28 pts/g. Move him at the draft or the next window while any residual value exists.
recommendations.rationale: Any club sees the trend line, not the October start. At 23, the direction is down. The GM's chip needs to move before it is worthless.

recommendations.summary: Stahle finally played 4 games at 17.8 MPG after a full season of zero dressings. Carry him into next season with a top-pair audition camp.
recommendations.rationale: 4 games, 17.8 MPG, POTE 96 at 20. The 4-game window is too small to judge but the minutes suggest they trust him. He needs a full camp next season to confirm.

recommendations.summary: No change needed for Chlup: 0.87 pts/g over 60 games on 18 MPG at 19 years old is the trendline we want.
recommendations.rationale: He is already in the top nine by minutes and is outproducing the rate that got him there. Nothing to adjust.

recommendations.summary: Kaberle's rise from 0.54 to 0.64 pts/g on rising minutes confirms he is the top-pair defenceman for next season.
recommendations.rationale: Only blue-liner with both rate and load trending up. At 27, the trajectory is toward his prime. No adjustment.

recommendations.summary: No minute changes needed before Vancouver; the room is at 92 average with the entire core at 96 and rising.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza at 86 is the lowest on the club but trending +1 and scratched; his issue is roster construction, not a line adjustment I can make tonight. Everyone else sits above 89 with positive momentum from wins.

recommendations.summary: No composition changes needed; every unit is built from players suited to its role.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has checking support (Roberts 83, Fischer 83, Jackman 89) behind skill. L2 is offensive by design with Mogilny 92 and Afinogenov 90. K2 is the hardest unit (83 mean checking). The only structural gap is L4 faceoffs (mean 51) which no arrangement fixes — already on record.

recommendations.summary: No lineup change for Vancouver. The D pair slots already match their line strength.
recommendations.rationale: Fischer/Jackman (90 CHKG each) on D1 already face Bertuzzi (93 OVR) and Naslund (89 OVR) via auto-pairing with L1. D2 Kaberle/McCabe handle Morrison (82 OVR). D3 Eminger/Klesla handle the Sedins (72, 73 OVR). The structure is correct.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour, but check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming per the standing order.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour at 92 OVR is the right answer against Vancouver. No fatigue flag appears in the brief, but the Jan 19 standing order requires the visual check before every start.

recommendations.summary: No PK adjustment. Vancouver's power play is 31 for 210 (14.8%), the worst unit on the sheet.
recommendations.rationale: Their PP converts at 14.8%, well below the league average. Our K1 with Roberts, Fischer, Sundin and Chlup is overkill for that unit.

recommendations.proposed: reduce Jackman to 25-26 MPG in the final 11 games
recommendations.summary: Jackman's production is collapsing under his load — cut his minutes now to give him a chance to recover before the offseason.
recommendations.rationale: 0.48 pts/g on 30.4 MPG at 24 is a system-fit or burnout problem. The March 5 collapse finding has become his season. Fewer minutes may arrest the decline; keeping him at 30 guarantees it finishes the year below 0.45.

recommendations.summary: Eminger remains the first D to trade — 0.40 pts/g on an expiring $1.2M deal with no recovery in sight since February.
recommendations.rationale: Season rate 0.40 is below the 0.45 threshold set January 26. At 21 he has one year of control left and the recovery window is closing. Klesla (0.37 pts/g at 22, declining across two seasons) is next.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker for the remaining 12 games; his stored 83 CHKG gives the lineup a fourth checker without moving anyone.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker is not in any unit. His 83 CHKG is the fourth-highest on the roster after Jackman (87), Roberts (86) and McCabe (86). The coach's checking complaint is a displayed-grade form issue; the stored depth exists but Tucker is not being used to deploy it.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza 3 of the remaining 12 games at 10+ minutes; the seed is set and the coach has said this is his final ask.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza is at 86 morale on 7.5 MPG. With 112 points and the top seed locked, no game result is at risk. The coach has stated that if this is declined he will close the file for the year.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle for one game in the final 12 where the result is not the priority.
recommendations.rationale: One game costs nothing at 112 points and gives the coach a data point on a prospect he has flagged. Low-cost, low-risk.

recommendations.summary: The toughness gap (zero players at 80+ TOUG) is real but every external fix has been vetoed and the team is at 112 points without it.
recommendations.rationale: Chara is vetoed per Feb 19. Bell was killed as a wing-for-wing swap. Avery was deprioritised on 0.11 ppg. Tucker at 70 TOUG is the internal ceiling. The gap exists but the cost to close it at this deadline exceeds the marginal benefit for a team already in first place.

recommendations.summary: Faceoffs are thin with only Sundin at 90 FACE but Chlup (75 FACE, age 19) is developing and no acquisition is worth the deadline cost.
recommendations.rationale: The gap is one player deep and the solution is two seasons of Chlup's development rather than a pick spent on a stopgap. Roberts at 75 provides adequate second-option draws for a short playoff run.

recommendations.summary: Sign Gaborik to a 5-6 year extension at season end, targeting $4.5-5.5M per year.
recommendations.rationale: 84 points in 70 games at 91 base, POTE 90, currently $1.10M. A breakout year makes him unaffordable if he reaches the open market. Five years locks him through age 28.

recommendations.summary: Sign Eminger to a 5-6 year extension at season end.
recommendations.rationale: 21 years old, POTE 99, $1.20M expiring. The single highest-potential blueliner on the roster. His asking price jumps the moment his 52-game season is visible to every GM in the league.

recommendations.summary: Sign Nash to a 5-6 year extension at season end.
recommendations.rationale: 20 years old, POTE 95, 35 points in 57 games, $1.20M expiring. A top-six winger at a rookie price. Five-year lock secures him through age 25.

recommendations.summary: Sign Richards to a 5-year extension at season end.
recommendations.rationale: 61 points in 68 games at 24, POTE 88, $1.00M expiring. A second-line centre on a rookie salary. Without a lock he commands top-nine money from every team needing a centre.

recommendations.summary: Sign Upshall to a 5-6 year extension at season end.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 at 21, 18 points in 56 games, $1.20M expiring. Development is ahead of production; the next two years will likely bring a step-change that prices him out.

recommendations.summary: Sign Colaiacovo to a 3-4 year deal at season end rather than 5-6, to stagger the renewal cluster.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 but only 31 games played and 12 points at 22. A shorter deal tests whether he is a top-pairing defenceman before committing franchise-length money. Three years puts his next renewal in 2008, splitting the wall.

recommendations.summary: Sign Kaberle to a 2-3 year extension, not 5-6.
recommendations.rationale: 27 years old, POTE 75, 37 points in 62 games at $1.90M. Oldest of the expiring core with the lowest ceiling. Three years at $3-3.5M covers his remaining prime without a decline-risk commitment.

recommendations.summary: Sign Chistov to a 2-3 year extension at season end.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 95 at 21 but only 18 points in 56 games. Production does not yet justify franchise money. Two years at $1.5-2M keeps him cheap while he develops.

recommendations.summary: Move Belfour at the deadline to recover a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: 39 years old, $6.50M, expiring, Luongo is the starter. If he retires after the season the value walks. The mechanic converts him to a pick. This is the only compensation available given no draft capital.

recommendations.summary: Move Roberts at the deadline to recover a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: 38 years old, 70 points in 70 games, $2.70M expiring. Not a long-term piece. The over-80 mechanic turns a rental into a pick rather than nothing.

recommendations.summary: No action on Fischer this summer; four years at $3.70M are not tradeable with 0.41 pts/g.
recommendations.rationale: His contract has 3+ years left and his production collapsed from 0.63 to 0.41 pts/g. No club takes that salary at those numbers. This is a 2007 problem to solve when he is 26 and may have recovered.

recommendations.proposed: Colorado return, Morris preferred to Hejduk
recommendations.summary: Resolve the Belfour decision before March 19; test Morris (D, 26, 85 base, $1.70M) before taking Hejduk.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 39, $6.50M, 92 base and expiring; he is the only over-80 asset that recovers value before July, and Morris is younger and cheaper than Hejduk while filling our blue line.

recommendations.summary: Move Roberts (LW, 38, $2.70M) for a pick by the 19th; he is not part of the summer plan.
recommendations.rationale: At 38 on an expiring $2.70M he will not be re-signed, and the over-80 mechanic converts him to a pick before he walks for nothing.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik (RW, 23, $1.10M, 67 pts/45 GP, 91 base) to 5-6 years at season end.
recommendations.rationale: He is the most valuable young player on the roster and the first name in the expiring cluster; a short deal only ratchets his next demand.

recommendations.summary: Lock Richards (C, 24, $1.00M) to 5-6 years.
recommendations.rationale: He is core, cheap at $1.00M, and 24 is the age to buy his prime on a long deal before he reaches free agency.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle (D, 27, $1.90M) to 5-6 years.
recommendations.rationale: Top-pair defenceman at $1.90M; you extended McCabe to lock the blue line, and Kaberle is the same commitment.

recommendations.summary: Sign Nash (LW, 20, $1.20M) to 5-6 years.
recommendations.rationale: Twenty years old at $1.20M with the highest remaining development headroom on the roster; buy the whole curve now.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger (D, 21, $1.20M) to 5-6 years and Chistov (LW, 21, $1.10M) the same.
recommendations.rationale: Both are 21 at about $1.10M; the GM's order keeps the young defence, so lock them long before the cluster renews again.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Colaiacovo (D, 22, $1.10M), Upshall (RW, 21, $1.20M) and Alexeev (RW, 23, $1.10M) on 2-3 years; Abid (LW, 24, $0.40M) on 2.
recommendations.rationale: Short deals on the depth stagger the cluster so all 13 do not come due together, which is the trap the manual names.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Tellqvist (G, 25, $0.80M) to 3 years at season end.
recommendations.rationale: Your order keeps him, he is cheap at $0.80M, and the manual warns that clubs lose good goalies by forgetting to check them.

recommendations.summary: Doan (PHX, RW, 28, 87 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 93, 52 pts/67 GP, $2.40M expiring) is the best available player who closes the toughness gap while producing top-six scoring.
recommendations.rationale: PHX at 71 points with 14 expiring deals cannot retain him. He is four years younger than Fleury, costs $1.9M less, and produces 52 points versus 42. Package: Svehla (85 base, $3.60M expiring) gives PHX a veteran rental; or a young D plus the 4th.

recommendations.summary: Belanger (LA, C, 27, 82 base, FACE 97, $700K expiring, 11 pts/54 GP) is the cheapest and most direct faceoff answer at centre the coverage phase identified.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 65 points with 15 expiring deals moves any rental. FACE 97 is 7 points above the next-highest available (Savard at 89). At $700K, re-signing in July is trivial. He is a centre, so the Jan 25 wing-position objection that killed Bell does not apply.

recommendations.summary: Havlat (OTT, LW, 23, 87 base, 86 pts/69 GP, $900K expiring) remains the lead scoring target; OTT at 65 points with 11 expiring cannot retain him.
recommendations.rationale: Feb 26 package of Tucker plus the 4th still applies. Tucker is 29, 83 CHKG, not in any unit, so expendable. If the GM objects to sending a D to a seller, the 4th alone may be insufficient for a 23-year-old with 86 points.

recommendations.summary: Kovalchuk (ATL, LW, 21, 89 base, 114 pts/67 GP, $1.10M expiring) is the highest scorer available but does not fix toughness; ATL at 72 points must choose between him and Heatley.
recommendations.rationale: Scoring is covered by Gaborik (91 base, 84 pts), Afinogenov (90 base), Chlup (84 at 19). Adding Kovalchuk is a luxury. Only pursue if Doan falls through and ATL confirms they are keeping Heatley.

recommendations.summary: Komisarek (MTL, D, 23, 77 base, 72 pts/69 GP, POTE 91, $1.10M expiring) is the best player-to-cost ratio on the board but does not close the toughness gap (TOUG 76).
recommendations.rationale: 72 points from a 23-year-old defenseman is elite production. MTL at 55 points with 15 expiring cannot retain him. However the GM protected core defense in February; Komisarek would be a partner for Jackman, not a replacement. Requires offering young D, which may trigger the same objection.

recommendations.summary: Sulku (CGY, LW, 20, 75 base, TOUG 89, CHKG 87, POTE 92, $942K expiring) is a development project with elite toughness grades from the worst team in the league.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 54 points with 10 expiring deals is the most desperate seller. But at 20 with POTE 92 on $942K, they likely re-sign rather than move. Low confidence. Only relevant if no tougher target materializes.

recommendations.proposed: Morris (COL, D, 26, 85 base, 57 pts/65 GP, $1.70M, 1yr expiring)
recommendations.summary: Send Belfour to Colorado for Morris; saves $4.80M, fills D depth with a re-signable 26-year-old, hedges Belfour retirement risk the GM raised Feb 21.
recommendations.rationale: GM explicitly named Colorado as a buyer on Feb 21 and offered Hejduk as their price. Morris is younger, cheaper, and fills a position Toronto needs. Acceptance uncertain; test Morris first, fall back to Hejduk if refused.

recommendations.proposed: Doan (PHX, RW, 28, 87 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 93, 52 pts/67 GP, $2.40M, 1yr expiring)
recommendations.summary: Send Tucker plus the 4th to Phoenix for Doan; closes the toughness gap (stored TOUG max 75 vs Doan 88) and upgrades top-six scoring simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: PHX at 71 points projects to ~83 and misses the playoffs; 14 expiring deals means they cannot re-sign Doan. Tucker gives them a cheap veteran with 2 years of control at $1.30M. If PHX treats 71 as a playoff number, this fails and we pivot to Havlat.

recommendations.proposed: Havlat (OTT, LW, 23, 87 base, 86 pts/69 GP, $900K, 1yr expiring)
recommendations.summary: If Doan is unavailable, send Tucker plus the 4th to Ottawa for Havlat; 86 points from a 23-year-old at $900K is the best pure scoring upgrade on the board.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 65 points with 11 expiring deals are clear sellers. They cannot re-sign Havlat at 86-point market value ($4-5M). The same package that moves Doan moves Havlat, but only one can happen because both cost Tucker plus the 4th.

recommendations.proposed: A draft pick (over-80 pick-recovery mechanic; any destination)
recommendations.summary: Move Svehla to any club with roster capacity for a draft pick before March 19; his value walks in July if he is not re-signed and he is not in the playoff lineup.
recommendations.rationale: The over-80 pick-recovery mechanic converts an expiring veteran into a draft pick for a team with no cap pressure. Svehla at 36 and $3.60M has no role in Toronto's playoff structure. Non-playoff destination preferred per the GM's March 4 correction on rental dumping.

recommendations.summary: If Doan, Havlat, and Belfour-Morris all fail, keep the roster intact and trust Chlup (75 FACE, age 19) and Jackman (87 CHKG stored) to close the gaps next season.
recommendations.rationale: At 112 points the roster is good enough for a playoff run. The toughness gap is real but is managed through coach matchups in a short series. Paying above market to close one gap eight days before the deadline risks the July cluster re-signings by inflating expectations.

recommendations.summary: The Luongo/DiPietro monitoring task is closed. Luongo is ours; DiPietro fails the talent bar permanently.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is rostered at 93 overall with 2 years at $1.60M. DiPietro is 79 base and was never a candidate under the Jan 15 standing order for high-90s. Theodore (MTL, 91 base, expiring, non-contender) is the live target if the GM wants to pursue one.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle against Calgary on Sunday. Four games in 70 with 12 left is the biggest development waste on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 96 at age 20, averaged 17.8 MPG in his four appearances. Calgary is 22-38, which is exactly the opponent where the GM's standing order says development outranks winning.

recommendations.summary: Dress Alexeeve against Calgary and give him at least 12 MPG. 30 points in 55 games on 8.3 minutes a night is the best efficiency on the roster among young forwards.
recommendations.rationale: 0.55 pts/g on fourth-line minutes. Currently scratched. Against a 22-38 team this is a development-appropriate game to test him with real ice.

recommendations.summary: Sixth time: dress Spezza against Calgary. 37 games at 7.5 MPG at age 21 with the highest scouting number on the roster is a wasted year if nothing changes in these last 12.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99, 37 GP, currently scratched. Calgary at 22-38 is the type of opponent where development priority applies per the standing order.

recommendations.summary: Retire the 10 MPG season target for Spacek. It is mathematically unreachable from 8.1 with 12 games left.
recommendations.rationale: 47 GP at 8.1 MPG needs 525+ total minutes to hit 10 season average over 59 games. Even 15 MPG for all 12 remaining only reaches 9.5. Judge his year on recent production instead.

recommendations.summary: Koltsov's trade value is collapsing fast — 1.10→0.28 pts/g at 23 — and the offseason window to move him is shrinking.
recommendations.rationale: The GM designated him a trading chip on Jan 15. His recent production has dropped from 1.10 to 0.28 pts/g, meaning any club looking at him this summer sees the trend, not the hot October start. The chip is losing value every game.

recommendations.summary: Spezza at 5.3 MPG in 37 games at age 21 is a wasted year. Training camp next season needs a real minutes commitment or he stops being a project worth dressing.
recommendations.rationale: Season average of 5.3 MPG across 37 games at 21 with POTE 99. Raised since January with no movement. 12 games left means this season is gone. The offseason plan must resolve whether he gets 12+ MPG or gets cleared.

recommendations.summary: Chlup at 19 is the roster's cleanest riser: 0.62→0.85 pts/g on minutes doubling from 11 to 18. Treat him as permanent top-nine in offseason planning.
recommendations.rationale: Production up while load up at 19. The February breakout is confirmed by a second window of rising production. No lineup change needed now; this is a roster-construction note for next season.

recommendations.summary: Jackman at 24 on 30+ MPG is declining from 0.65 to 0.38 pts/g. If this holds through the offseason his role and minutes need rethinking.
recommendations.rationale: A 24-year-old D carrying 30 MPG should be trending up. He dropped from 0.65 to 0.38 while minutes rose from 30.1 to 30.6. Either burnout or system misfit, and the answer determines his value going forward.

recommendations.summary: Kaberle 0.54→0.63 pts/g at 27 is the GM's keeper confirmed by the trend. Leave him alone.
recommendations.rationale: Production rising with minutes rising at age 27. The only defenceman on the roster whose numbers are clearly improving. No intervention needed.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza 12+ MPG on the third line to lift him out of the 80s morale band where he's been stuck for weeks.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza at 86 morale with 7.5 MPG has been at this level since December and only moved +1. His grade penalty from the 80s band is costing us a point per attribute across the board. Nash at 12.7 MPG or Chistov at 13.2 MPG can share with him.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes needed. All units are appropriately staffed for their roles.
recommendations.rationale: L1 through L3 each have the right mix of tools for their job. PP1 has the best shooters, PP2 has Mogilny (92 scoring) leading. The only structural gap is L4 faceoffs (mean 51, best 53) which no rearrangement fixes.

recommendations.summary: Ice the same lines. CGY's back end is 73-79 and we've outscored them 10-3 in two meetings.
recommendations.rationale: CGY is 22-38-6 with no defenseman above 79 OVR. Our first pair (Fischer 89 CHKG, Jackman 89 CHKG) against Iginla's line is already the correct matchup via auto-pairing. Their PP is 9.3%. Nothing about this opponent rewards a change.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour, but check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming per the standing order.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour reads 92 OVR with 99 morale today. No fatigue flag visible in the lineup data, but the January 19 incident requires the screen check every time.

recommendations.summary: Sell Eminger at the deadline: 0.38 pts/g over 52 games at 21 with an expiring $1.2M, and his recovery in February did not hold.
recommendations.rationale: Season rate fell from 0.44 (Feb 26 flag) to 0.38 now. He is the first D on the sell list.

recommendations.summary: Klesla is sell #2: 0.37 pts/g at 22 with two years left. Flat since February with no sign of the age-22 improvement the season should bring.
recommendations.rationale: Rate has not moved since Feb 21 flag (0.38 then, 0.37 now). At 22 the expected direction is up; it is not happening. $0.90M x 2 means he is still cheap enough to move for a mid-round pick.

recommendations.summary: McCabe stays off the sell list. 0.81 pts/g over 70 games is unchanged from Mar 4 and he is carrying the top pair.
recommendations.rationale: Recovery from February held. $3M x 4 is a cap problem but not a performance problem.

recommendations.summary: Jackman stays but his minutes need cutting next season. 0.47 pts/g on 30.5 MPG at $0.70M x 3 is too cheap to trade and too overloaded to produce.
recommendations.rationale: The Mar 5 collapse flag (0.38 recent) is still the live number; the 0.47 season average is just dilution from early good games. The problem is workload, not asset value.

recommendations.slot: fourth-line left wing or spare forward
recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker every game; he is the roster's best forward checker (CHKG 92 stored, TOUG 88 stored) and is currently in no unit.
recommendations.rationale: The coach's checking-line gap is real only if Tucker stays home. He and Roberts (90) and Upshall (87) give three wingers at 87+ CHKG stored. This is free roster depth the coach has access to and is not using.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Reid (STL, RW, 23, FACE 80 shown, POTE 94, $600K expiring) as a faceoff-capable bottom-six centre; STL at 63 points are sellers.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin (90) is the only forward above 80 FACE on the roster. Chlup at 75 stored and Richards at 70 cannot take draws against opposing first lines in a playoff series. Reid gives a second 80+ option at 23 with room to grow.

recommendations.summary: No enforcer trade is needed. The toughness gap is a form artifact; ten Toronto forwards and defencemen carry stored TOUG 80+.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts 92, Jackman 89, Nash 88, Tucker 88, McCabe 85, Upshall 84, Eminger 83, Abid 80, St. Jacques 80, Klesla 80 on stored grades. The composite role score depresses these into a false 'zero at 80+' reading. Chase centres and scoring with deadline currency, not toughness.

recommendations.summary: Chlup at 0.73 pts/g in 58 games and 16.5 MPG at age 19 is the season's development success; his CHKG 79 stored is the ceiling for a second-line centre internally and that is acceptable.
recommendations.rationale: He cannot become an 85+ checker but his 85 overall, 42 points, and 75 FACE make him a legitimate second-line pivot for the next three years. No trade fixes the CHKG ceiling here; it costs too much for a marginal upgrade on a player who already plays 16 minutes.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik on 5 years at season-end renewal, not 2-3 years, because 83 points at age 23 makes him unaffordable in a 10-player bidding summer.
recommendations.rationale: 13 contracts worth $21.30M expire July 2005 simultaneously. Gaborik (23, 83 pts, $1.10M) must be identified as untouchable before the market opens or the ten renewals compete for each other's attention.

recommendations.summary: Lock Nash on 5 years at season-end renewal alongside Gaborik.
recommendations.rationale: Nash at 20, 35 pts, POTE 95, $1.20M is the second cheapest 5-year lock available. At 22 with 45 points he costs $4-5M; at 20 with 35 he costs $2.5-3.5M.

recommendations.current: Eminger, Upshall, Richards, Alexeev, Chistov, Colaiacovo, Abid, Kaberle
recommendations.summary: Sign the remaining eight expirers to 3-year deals, not 5, to stagger the next renewal wave into 2008.
recommendations.rationale: If all ten get 5-6 years, they all re-enter the market in 2010 simultaneously. At 3 years, Eminger is 24 (matchable RFA), Colaiacovo is 25 (development resolved), and the information value of three more seasons is free.

recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour before March 19 for at least one draft pick; do not release him in July.
recommendations.rationale: The club holds only a 4th-rounder. Belfour (92 base, expiring, $6.50M) qualifies for the over-80 pick-recovery mechanic. Without his move, Toronto has no 2005 pick to draft a goalie, which contradicts the GM's standing order to develop goaltending through the draft.

recommendations.summary: Flag Luongo (2006 renewal, POTE 97, 25) as the most important single re-signing after this summer's cluster.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is 2 years into a 2-year deal at $1.60M. He will be 27 with elite production on the market in July 2006 unless locked on 5-6 years at renewal. The manual warns that good goalies are lost by forgetting them.

recommendations.summary: Accept Sundin ($8.40M, 34, 5 years left) as a fixed cost and build around it rather than against it.
recommendations.rationale: A 34-year-old at POTE 60 with five years remaining has no trade market in this game. He is 14% of payroll and cannot move. All other decisions are made knowing this number is locked through 2010.

recommendations.proposed: Morris (COL, D, 26, 85 base, $1.70M) or Hejduk (COL, RW, 91 base, $2.50M)
recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour to Colorado by March 19; test Morris first, fall back to Hejduk.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 92 base, $6.50M, expiring, and the GM fears retirement. He walks in July if not moved. Morris is 26, 57 pts in 65 GP, and fills the blue line gap. Colorado need a goalie and have 89 points. Salary reduction of $4.80M if Morris lands.

recommendations.summary: Send Tucker plus the 4th-rounder to Ottawa for Havlat.
recommendations.rationale: Havlat is 87 base at 23 with $900K expiring; OTT at 63 points with 11 expiring deals cannot retain him. Tucker occupies no line role at 79 base and $1.30M. The 4th is our only pick.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik on a 5-6 year deal at season end.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base, 83 pts in 69 games, age 23, POTE 90, $1.10M expiring. He is the most valuable player on the roster and walks in July if unaddressed.

recommendations.summary: Lock Richards on a 5-6 year deal at season end.
recommendations.rationale: 82 base, 61 pts in 67 games, age 24, POTE 88, $1.00M expiring. Second center and the engine of the third line.

recommendations.summary: Lock Abid on a 5-6 year deal at season end, first among the group.
recommendations.rationale: 79 base, 65 pts in 69 games, age 24, POTE 94, on $400K. A 65-point player at $400K is the cheapest contract on the roster and he will command a multiple at renewal. Lock him before the market finds him.

recommendations.summary: Lock Nash on a 5-6 year deal at season end.
recommendations.rationale: 77 base, 35 pts in 56 games, age 20, POTE 95, $1.20M. Still developing, still 20. A five-year deal at his current rate buys his entire prime.

recommendations.summary: Lock Eminger on a 5-6 year deal at season end.
recommendations.rationale: 76 base, POTE 99, age 21, $1.20M. GM protected him explicitly on Jan 19. His ceiling is set high and the likelihood is real.

recommendations.summary: Lock Upshall (POTE 99), Chistov (POTE 95), Alexeev (POTE 94), and Colaiacovo (POTE 99) on 5-6 year deals at season end.
recommendations.rationale: All four are 21-23, all four carry POTE 94+, all four expire at $1.10-1.20M. None will be available again at that price. Group-sign them together to keep the process clean.

recommendations.summary: Renew Kaberle on a 2-3 year deal at a modest raise.
recommendations.rationale: 84 base, 27, POTE 75, $1.90M. His ceiling is close to where he is now. Two years at around $3M is fair and avoids a 5-year commitment to a player who will not improve much.

recommendations.summary: Renew Tellqvist on a 2-3 year deal.
recommendations.rationale: 77 base, age 25, POTE 91, $800K. GM wants to give him time. Two years gives him a full season as backup and a decision point without overcommitting.

recommendations.summary: Offer Roberts two years at a reduced salary; do not move him for a pick at the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: 87 base, 70 pts in 69 games, 1.01 ppg at age 38. The pick-recovery mechanic is available but a pick we cannot trade is worth less than the production the coach says we lack. If he rejects the reduced figure he walks in July — accept that risk.

recommendations.summary: Do not pursue Svehla, Theodore, or DiPietro at the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla (LA, 85, $3.60M) requires an asset we do not have without breaking the nine-player core. Theodore (MTL, 91, $5.50M) requires youth and picks; MTL want neither Belfour nor our depth. DiPietro (NYI, 50 GP this year) is not available — NYI at 68 points and 9th still see him as their starter.

recommendations.current: Belfour (G, 39, $6.50M, expiring, 92 base, 18-3-2.27 GAA in 21 GP)
recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour to Colorado for Chris Morris; COL tested this already and offered Hejduk as the return, so they will engage.
recommendations.rationale: COL at 65 points have no playoff goalie and already asked for one. Belfour's 2.27 GAA is their answer for April. Morris fills our blue-line depth hole (Jackman at 30.9 MPG needs a partner) and is 9 years younger than Hejduk at a third the salary. We save $4.80M and lose only Ouellet-as-backup as the cost.

recommendations.current: Tucker (LW, 29, $1.30M, 2yr, CHKG 92, TOUG 88, in no unit) + 4th-round pick (2005, from TOR)
recommendations.summary: Send Tucker and the 4th-rounder to Ottawa for Havlat, the best scoring upgrade available at the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 63 points with 11 expiring deals cannot re-sign Havlat. They get a 2-year physical winger (CHKG 92, TOUG 88) for their bottom six plus draft capital. We get a 23-year-old 87-base scorer at $900K who plays 20+ minutes. Tucker is currently in no unit, so we lose no ice time.

recommendations.current: Chistov (LW, 21, $1.10M, expiring, POTE 95, SPEE 89, 18 pts/55 GP)
recommendations.proposed: Reid (RW, 23, FACE 80 shown, POTE 94, 52 pts/57 GP, $600K, expiring)
recommendations.summary: Offer Chistov to St. Louis for Reid; he closes the faceoff gap (only Sundin is above 80 FACE on our roster) without spending the 4th-rounder.
recommendations.rationale: STL at 65 points with 8 expiring deals are sellers. They get a 21-year-old with POTE 95 and 89 speed, a higher-ceiling prospect than their own 23-year-old forward. We get FACE 80 with 52 points at $600K, which relieves Sundin against every opposing first line in the playoffs. The cost is a real prospect but the faceoff hole costs playoff series.

recommendations.summary: Goalie monitoring task is closed: Luongo is on the roster at 94, DiPietro (79 base, 3.64 GAA, 84.9% SV) is not a viable Belfour return.
recommendations.rationale: DiPietro's 21 GP this season produced 7-12 with a 3.64 GAA and 84.9% save percentage. He is 79 base at age 21 — the Jan 15 order called for a high-90s goalie. The Theodore target (MTL, 91 base, expiring) remains the correct exploration if the GM wants to move Belfour.

recommendations.summary: Last window: dress Spezza in at least 3 of the 13 remaining games where we are not going all out. If the GM declines this final ask, the year is closed and I will stop raising it.
recommendations.rationale: 21 years old, POTE 99, 37 GP on 7.5 MPG and 0.41 pts/g. Raised five times with no movement. 13 games is all that remains.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle for one game in the final 13 where the result is not the priority.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 96 at age 20 with 4 GP in 69 games. The 0 points in 4 games is noise at this stage. One look costs nothing.

recommendations.summary: Stop recommending a Spacek minutes bump. The 10 MPG season target is mathematically unreachable from 8.1 with 13 games left.
recommendations.rationale: 0.35 pts/g on 46 GP at 8.1 MPG. The year is settled. Morale 92 says he is not hurting.

recommendations.summary: McCabe goes to the top of the D sell list: 0.51 pts/g in the 45 games since December 1, 29 years old, 4 years and $3M remaining.
recommendations.rationale: The 0.83 season average includes a 1.42 opening window that is never coming back. His actual recent play on 22 MPG is below top-pair quality. Sell before the market prices the 0.51.

recommendations.summary: Jackman at 0.36 on 30.9 MPG at age 24 is a load problem, not a talent problem. Plan for a reduced role or a relief partner next season.
recommendations.rationale: Third consecutive window of declining production under rising load. At 24 with a top-pair workload his output should be going up. If it holds through the offseason his value as a number-one D drops a full tier.

recommendations.summary: Klesla stays second on the sell list: 0.31 pts/g recent at 22, a second consecutive declining year on flat minutes.
recommendations.rationale: Minutes unchanged (14.6 to 14.8) while production fell from 0.50 to 0.31. At 22 the expected direction under stable load is up. Two down years means this is his ceiling and we should get something before it erodes further.

recommendations.summary: Chlup at 0.76 pts/g on 18.1 MPG at age 19 is the development success of the season. Build the second line around him next year.
recommendations.rationale: Production up 23% while minutes increased 65%. At 19 that combination is rare and confirms the February breakout was real. He is a long-term top-nine centre.

recommendations.summary: No morale-driven line change for Edmonton; the room is fine with every dressed player at 92+.
