recommendations.rationale: Sundin at 96 on 19.9 MPG, Gaborik at 99 on 20.2, Jackman at 99 on 30.6: all at or above their expected minutes bands. The only player below 90 is Spezza at 86 on 7.5 MPG, but he is scratched and this is a maximize-quality night where he does not belong.

recommendations.summary: Spezza at 86 morale on 7.5 MPG needs 10+ minutes in games we can afford before the season ends, or accept his year is lost and stop carrying him.
recommendations.rationale: Morale dropped from 90 to 86 and has held there across multiple saves. At 7.5 MPG he is under his expected band, the same problem raised since January. If no games remain where we can afford his minutes, the answer is to stop dressing him and plan for next season.

recommendations.summary: Even-strength lines are correct for a maximize-quality night against Edmonton.
recommendations.rationale: L1 and L2 carry the team's scoring and speed. The GM's standing order is maximize quality against good opponents. No arrangement change improves this without breaking chemistry on the top two lines.

recommendations.proposed: Chlup, McCabe, Jackman, Abid (K2 promoted to K1)
recommendations.summary: Consider swapping K1 and K2 slot order so Jackman's 89 checking and McCabe's 83 anchor the first kill.
recommendations.rationale: K2 checking mean is 83 vs K1's 77. Jackman is the roster's best checker and he's currently on the second kill. The trade-off is losing Sundin's 90 faceoff on the first unit for defensive-zone draws.

recommendations.summary: No arrangement of this roster produces a checking line with three guys above 80. The best four checkers are spread across L1 and K2.
recommendations.rationale: Jackman 89, Roberts 83, McCabe 83, Fischer 83 are the roster's checking top four. Three are on L1 and one on L2. We cannot shut down an opponent's top line with any fourth unit.

recommendations.summary: Both PP units are well-constructed. P1 has scoring and speed 89/99, P2 has speed 90/94 and Mogilny at 92 scoring.
recommendations.rationale: No arrangement change improves either unit. They are the strongest and second-strongest collections of skill available.

recommendations.summary: Lines stay as-is for EDM.
recommendations.rationale: Auto-pairing puts Fischer-Jackman (84/85) against EDM's top line (Comrie 85), Klesla-Eminger (83/76) against their now-depleted third unit without Hemsky (out, returns 3/13). EDM's D reads 72-77 across three pairs; we outscored them 8-3 in two meetings. No adjustment improves the matchup.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour. Check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming per the standing order.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour at 93 OVR, 99 morale, shutout last start. EDM at 2.50 goals per game for the season is below-average offence with Hemsky out.

recommendations.summary: Sell order unchanged: Eminger first (0.39 pts/g, 51 GP, expiring $1.2M), Klesla second (0.38 pts/g, 69 GP, flat at 22).
recommendations.rationale: No defenceman's numbers moved enough in the last game to change the order. Jackman at 0.46 pts/g with 30.6 MPG is a concern but at $0.7M x 3 and no replacement for his minutes he is not a sell.

recommendations.summary: Toughness is the only role where we have zero players at 80+ on base grades (best: Jackman 75). Avery is the cheapest route to a first 80+ TOUG body.
recommendations.rationale: Feb 21 stored-grade reading of six players at 80+ TOUG is refuted by the March 7 shipped grades showing zero. The Tucker internal fallback (70 TOUG) does not close it. Avery at $400K with 2 years is the only player who fills this without spending significant draft capital.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker nightly: his 83 CHKG is our 4th-best checker and he is currently in no unit.
recommendations.rationale: Six players at 80+ checking but Tucker at 83 is unlined. With Roberts (38, 86 CHKG) declining, Tucker is the next man up for playoff minutes. This is a coach decision, not a trade.

recommendations.summary: Faceoff gap (L4 mean 51, best 75 at Chlup) is real but does not justify spending deadline currency when toughness is the more acute gap and we hold a single 4th-rounder.
recommendations.rationale: No available player fixes this without giving up the same currency needed for Avery. At 108 points the playoff run matters more than regular-season faceoff percentage on L4.

recommendations.proposed: Chara (OTT, 94 TOUG, 95 CHKG) — GM vetoed Jan 19
recommendations.summary: Chara remains the best player for this gap (94 TOUG on a club with zero above 75) but is vetoed. Avery is the fallback at 83 TOUG.
recommendations.rationale: The Chara veto was based on Eminger's potential (POTE 99) over Chara's ceiling, not on this role gap. The gap is now proven with shipped grades. Worth flagging to GM that the justification for the veto was developmental, not tactical.

recommendations.summary: Offer Gaborik, Richards, Nash and Eminger 5-6 year deals at season's end, budgeting $12-16M in combined salary to replace $4.50M of current cost.
recommendations.rationale: All four expire July 2005 together at $4.50M total. Gaborik at 83 pts/68 GP, Richards at 61/66, Nash at 35/55 and Eminger at POTE 99 cannot all hit UFA at once. Revenue of $86.75M absorbs the increase.

recommendations.summary: Sign Kaberle to a 3-4 year deal separate from the four-star cluster to spread renewal pricing across different conversations.
recommendations.rationale: Kaberle is 27, $1.90M expiring, 33 pts in 60 GP, POTE 75. He needs security but not a 6-year lock. Negotiating him independently avoids a single summer where five defensemen and forwards all demand raises at once.

recommendations.summary: Move Belfour before March 19 for a pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic; his $6.50M walks in July and Luongo is the starter.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 39, $6.50M, 1 year left, 92 base overall. Luongo at 91 base and 25 is the number one. The over-80 expiring asset mechanic converts Belfour into at least one draft pick if moved before the deadline.

recommendations.summary: Do not restructure Chlup's contract yet; he has two years left at $2.34M and the game does not allow mid-contract extensions.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup at 19 with POTE 95 and 41 pts/57 GP will command a raise in July 2006 when his deal expires. The Dec 29 urgency note is superseded by the Jan 15 confirmation that renegotiation is impossible mid-contract. His window is next summer.

recommendations.summary: Decide the Belfour destination before March 12; Colorado (Morris or Hejduk) is the named partner, and the pick capital dies if he passes the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 39, $6.50M, 92 base, expiring. He is the only over-80 pick-recovery asset on the roster and the 4th-rounder funding Havlat is gated by whether this trade lands.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Havlat from Ottawa for Tucker plus the 4th-rounder; he is 23, 87 base, 80 points in 63 games, and OTT cannot retain him at 60 points.
recommendations.rationale: The whole team is scoring less per the GM's Feb 19 diagnosis. Havlat is the lead target and the 4th-rounder is the only capital we hold — it goes to Havlat or to recovering Belfour's pick, not both.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Reid from STL for a cheap package; FACE 80, POTE 94, age 23, $600K expiring, closes the L4 faceoff gap the coach flagged.
recommendations.rationale: Coach reports L4 faceoff mean 51 with best 54. Reid at FACE 80 and 77 base is the single best faceoff-plus-potential target available and STL at 63 points are sellers.

recommendations.summary: Move Roberts to a non-contender before March 19 for a draft pick via the over-80 mechanic; do not renew him in July.
recommendations.rationale: He is 38, $2.70M, and the coach reports him declining. A pick now beats nothing in July. Send to a team outside the playoff race per the GM's March 4 instruction.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik to 5–6 years as the first summer action; 23 years old, 91 base, POTE 90, currently $1.10M.
recommendations.rationale: He is the highest-ceiling player on the expiring list and the cheapest to sign relative to production. A July bidding war on a 91-base 23-year-old is the worst outcome.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger to five years; 21, POTE 99, $1.20M current. The GM explicitly protected him from trade on January 19.
recommendations.rationale: He is the cornerstone defenceman of the next window. Five years at a reasonable raise keeps the blue line young and paired with Colaiacovo.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash to 5–6 years; age 20, $1.20M. Lock him at the current ELC-adjacent salary before he becomes expensive.
recommendations.rationale: At 20 he is the youngest core player. Five or six years at a low initial figure protects against the July cluster and preserves payroll flexibility.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle to five years; 27, $1.90M. His ceiling is set but he is the best offensive defenceman the club has tonight.
recommendations.rationale: Five years at 27 gives production through age 32. No replacement on the roster matches his power-play production.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards to five years; 24, $1.00M, provides centre depth and faceoff ability.
recommendations.rationale: Five years at 24 locks the second/third-line centre through his prime. Cheap relative to the gap he fills.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Colaiacovo to five years; 22, $1.10M. Pairs with Eminger on the development curve.
recommendations.rationale: At 22 with a year of experience he is on the same track as Eminger. Five years keeps the young defensive core together.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Abid to two years at $0.40M; his TOUG 80 and CHKG 80 make him the cheapest physical presence available.
recommendations.rationale: Four hundred thousand for an 80/80 toughness profile is value no trade can match. Two years because he is 24 with a ceiling near his current grades.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Tellqvist to two years at $0.80M; GM said give him time on January 15 and potential suggests high 90s.
recommendations.rationale: He saves no money but the GM's standing order is to let him develop. Two years gives one more season to judge.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Alexeev to two years; 23, 0.55 pts/g per the coach, $1.10M. Two years matches his uncertainty as a starter.
recommendations.rationale: Coach outproduces Chistov on less ice and wants him in. Two years at current salary is low risk with upside if he breaks out.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Smirnov to two years at $0.40M; he is 20 and the cheapest piece on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: Four hundred thousand at 20 costs nothing to retain. Depth wins cups.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Upshall to two years; age 21, $1.20M. Young depth with room to grow.
recommendations.rationale: Two years lets us judge whether he is top-nine or bottom-six before committing further.

recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour to Colorado for Derek Morris: 84 TOUG, 85 base, 26 years old, $1.70M expiring, fills the toughness gap the coverage phase identified.
recommendations.rationale: Morris is 26 with 84 TOUG and 58 points in 66 games. COL at 87 points need a goalie (GM confirmed they offered Hejduk for Belfour). Morris is younger, cheaper ($1.70M vs $2.50M), and fills our actual gap where Hejduk does not. Test this exact offer before accepting Hejduk.

recommendations.summary: Chase Shane Doan (PHX, 88 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 50 pts/65 GP, $2.40M expiring) if the Morris deal does not land.
recommendations.rationale: Doan is the best forward who closes the toughness gap. PHX at 69 points with 14 expiring cannot re-sign him. Non-contender so the rival-weakness logic holds. Cost is likely Tucker plus the 4th, which conflicts with Havlat.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Craig Conroy from CGY (94 FACE, 82 pts/66 GP, $2.00M expiring) for Chistov plus a late pick; fixes L4 faceoffs without spending the 4th.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 52 points with 10 expiring are the league's most motivated sellers. Conroy's 82 points make him a top-nine centre, not a specialist. Chistov (0.33 ppg, coach wants him benched) plus a 5th or 6th is a fair price for a rental.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Havlat (OTT, 87 base, 83 pts/67 GP, $900K expiring) with Tucker plus the 4th-rounder if Morris-for-Belfour closes and the pick is freed.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 63 points with 11 expiring cannot retain him. 83 points at 23 is the best scoring addition available. Requires the 4th plus Tucker, so it conflicts with Doan and Komisarek. Only one of these three can happen.

recommendations.summary: If ATL re-signs Kovalchuk, pivot to Marc Savard (88 FACE, 68 pts/64 GP, $1.00M expiring) as the faceoff-plus-scoring prize.
recommendations.rationale: Savard closes L4 faceoffs (88 vs our 51 mean) while producing 68 points. ATL at 68 points with 11 expiring will deal him. Folds into the same ATL conversation as Kovalchuk/Heatley.

recommendations.summary: Target Brandon Reid (STL, 80 FACE, 93 POTE, $600K expiring) as the cheapest faceoff fix if STL move him.
recommendations.rationale: STL at 63 points with 8 picks are rebuilding. Reid at $600K with FACE 80 and POTE 93 fixes L4 faceoffs at minimum cost. Risk: STL may keep him or demand a young player we want.

recommendations.summary: Komisarek (MTL, 23, 91 POTE, 70 pts/67 GP, $1.10M expiring) is the best D prospect available but requires St. Jacques plus Safronov plus the 4th.
recommendations.rationale: MTL at 53 points with 15 expiring cannot retain him. 70 points from a 23-year-old at 30 MPG shows he is NHL-ready. Expensive package for a 77-base player, and it conflicts with Havlat for the 4th.

recommendations.summary: Avery (LA, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, $400K, 2 years) is the cheapest toughness-plus-faceoff player; 7 pts in 66 games means he is a checker, not a scorer.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 65 points with 15 expiring are motivated. His 0.11 ppg is the worst production of any target here. At $400K with 2 years the downside is a healthy scratch; the upside is the only forward at 80+ TOUG available.

recommendations.summary: The Luongo/DiPietro monitoring task is closed: Luongo is on the roster at 91 base with 2 years, DiPietro was rejected Feb 6 (79 base, 3.65 GAA).
recommendations.rationale: Both halves of the overdue task from January 19 are resolved. No further action needed.

recommendations.proposed: Derek Morris ($1.70M, 26, D, 1yr expiring, 85 base, 84 TOUG, 58 pts/66 GP)
recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour for Morris to Colorado as a counter to their Hejduk proposal; Morris closes the toughness gap and saves $4.80M.
recommendations.rationale: COL at 87 points need a playoff goalie; Belfour's 18-3, 2.27 GAA, 0.916 SP is exactly that. Morris at 84 TOUG and 58 points from the blue line is the only player on the board who closes our #1 gap. The GM already has the conversation open from Colorado's Hejduk offer.

recommendations.proposed: Craig Conroy ($2.00M, 33, C, 1yr expiring, 94 FACE, 82 pts/66 GP)
recommendations.summary: Send Chistov to Calgary for Conroy; costs no pick and fills the L4 faceoff gap the coach cannot fix from the bench.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 52 points with 10 expiring deals will not re-sign a 33-year-old at $2M. Chistov is 21 with POTE 95 and 89 speed — a rebuild piece Calgary values. Conroy's 94 FACE turns our L4 mean of 51 into a real unit. Coach explicitly wants Chistov benched for Alexeev.

recommendations.current: Tucker ($1.30M, 29, LW, 2yr, 3 GP, 1 pt) + 4th round pick
recommendations.proposed: Martin Havlat ($900K, 23, LW, 1yr expiring, 87 base, 83 pts/67 GP)
recommendations.summary: Send Tucker plus the 4th to Ottawa for Havlat; 83 points from a 23-year-old at $900K is the best value on the deadline board.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 60-63 points with 11 expiring contracts cannot retain Havlat. Tucker gives them a 2-year-controlled 83-CHKG veteran they lack, plus a pick for their pipeline. We gain a legitimate top-six winger to pair with Gaborik. Uses our only pick so it is exclusive with other pick-dependent deals.

recommendations.summary: If all three deals fail, play the playoffs with the current roster and execute the coach's lineup moves (Alexeev over Chistov, Spezza 10+ MPG, Stahle dressed).
recommendations.rationale: At 108 points with Luongo (91 base), Gaborik (83 pts), and four D at 80+ CHKG, the toughness gap is a playoff liability but not a fatal one. No deadline action is required when the roster already produces at this level.

recommendations.summary: Close item #2: Luongo arrived at 91 base and DiPietro at 79 base never met the high-90s criteria; the goalie file is solved per the Feb 19 order.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 93 displayed, 42 GP, 2 years at $1.60M is the starter the club needed. DiPietro's 2.88 GAA at 79 base is not the profile the Jan 15 order sought. Theodore at 91 base remains a theoretical future target but the GM has ruled goalies solved.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza 10+ MPG in the next game we can afford (not tonight against Vancouver).
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99, 37 GP in 68, 7.5 MPG, 0.41 pts/g. At 21 with the highest scouting grade on the roster, 54% share is a wasted season. Quality-opponent rule keeps him out tonight; the next beatable opponent must see him at 10+.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev (0.55 pts/g) outproduces Chistov (0.33 pts/g) on less ice; put Alexeev back in the lineup.
recommendations.rationale: Alexeev has 30 points in 55 games on 8.3 MPG while scratched from the set lines. Chistov holds the slot at 18 points in 54 games on 13 MPG. The production gap justifies the swap on quality grounds.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle in at least two of the remaining games after tonight.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 96 at 20, 4 GP all season. His 17.8 MPG in those 4 shows trust when he plays. Against quality opponents the veteran rule holds; in the beatable games left, give him reps.

recommendations.summary: Spacek at 8.3 MPG season average: one more sustained 12+ MPG stretch or stop dressing him for the final stretch.
recommendations.rationale: The March 4 bump was given but not maintained. At 8.3 season MPG with roughly two weeks left, if the average doesn't reach 10 by season's end the year is written off. Either commit or free the spot.

recommendations.summary: Stop carrying Smirnov: zero games in 68 at POTE 70 and age 20 is not a development project, it's a roster spot being wasted.
recommendations.rationale: 0 GP, POTE 70, age 20. The staff has given him zero opportunities across two seasons of dressings. No games and no path to them means no reason to hold the roster entry.

recommendations.summary: Chlup's top-nine spot is permanent now, no more rotation back down.
recommendations.rationale: 0.62→0.75 pts/g on minutes doubling from 11 to 18 at age 19. Both lines moving the right direction under increased load is what a real breakout looks like. He's earned it.

recommendations.summary: Spezza's situation needs a GM decision this offseason: real minutes or a different plan.
recommendations.rationale: 0.38 pts/g on 5.3 MPG across 37 games since December at 21 with POTE 99. The year is functionally over for development. This is the sixth time I've raised it.

recommendations.summary: Watch Jackman's 31 MPG heading into the final stretch; if the trend holds through the season a role change is needed.
recommendations.rationale: 0.65→0.37 pts/g while load rose to 31.0 MPG. At 24 the direction is wrong. If he carries 31 minutes into the offseason the problem compounds.

recommendations.summary: Start planning around the Roberts and Mogilny years: both are at 38 and 36 and dropping fast.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts 1.29→0.89 on rising minutes (16.5→21.2) at 38. Mogilny 1.62→0.80 at 36. Neither reverses. Replacement need is one to two seasons away.

recommendations.summary: Klesla's second declining season is confirmed. He belongs on the sell list with Eminger and Salo.
recommendations.rationale: 0.50→0.32 pts/g at 22 with minutes flat at 14.8. Expected direction at his age is up. It went down with no load excuse.

recommendations.proposed: Dress Spezza at 10+ MPG in a game we can afford
recommendations.summary: Dress Spezza and give him 10+ MPG in a manageable game to pull him out of the 80s penalty zone.
recommendations.rationale: At 86 morale Spezza carries a minus-one to every grade. He's been there for weeks scratched. 10 MPG in a game we can afford is the only lever; otherwise accept the penalty as the cost of sitting him.

recommendations.summary: Everyone else is at 90 or above and getting the morale bonus. No changes needed.
recommendations.rationale: All other players sit at 92-100, which gives the +1 grade bonus. The room is in good shape heading into the final stretch.

recommendations.current: Spacek or Abid at C on L4
recommendations.summary: L4 faceoff mean is 51 with a best of 54. No available player fixes this from the bench.
recommendations.rationale: Richards at 74 is the next-best draw man and he is already anchoring L3. Chlup at 79 is buried on L2/P2/K2. The fourth line cannot win draws in either zone, which forces top-six defensive-zone starts.

recommendations.summary: Best toughness on the roster is 76 (Jackman). There is no enforcer at any position.
recommendations.rationale: For a playoff run against a physical opponent this becomes a matchup problem with no lineup solution. Flagging for offseason planning.

recommendations.summary: All four lines and both special teams units are built from players who suit their assignments. No composition change for Vancouver.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has offensive depth with defensive protection, L2 is a scoring line that fits its personnel, L3 is Richards' unit with speed wingers, L4 provides checking (mean 72). PP1 is loaded with Gaborik/Sundin/Kaberle/Jackman shooting; K1 and K2 have real checkers. The only fixable issue is the L4 faceoff void and it has no roster solution tonight.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour, roll all four lines as currently set. No changes.
recommendations.rationale: VAN's top line (Bertuzzi 89, Naslund 85) auto-pairs against Fischer-Jackman (both CHKG 90) via the line-1 pairing. Their depth (3rd/4th lines at 62-71 OVR) is below ours at every position. Their centres are all FACE 69 while ours average 81, so our season faceoff problem is neutralized tonight. Belfour is 92 OVR at 99 morale with no fatigue flag. Spacek on the fourth line faces VAN's weakest unit (Belanger 62, Sedin 68, Danton 65), so development and maximize align.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour in net.
recommendations.rationale: 92 OVR, morale 99, no fatigue icon shown. VAN scores 3.50 per game and is 8-1-1 in their last 10; this is the night for the best available netminder.

recommendations.summary: Top of the sell list: move Eminger before the deadline or lose him free.
recommendations.rationale: 0.40 pts/g in 50 games at 21, trending down from 0.44 on Feb 26. $1.20M expiring. He should be rising, not falling.

recommendations.summary: Second on the sell list: 0.38 pts/g at 22 with 2 years remaining is a declining asset the team is stuck with.
recommendations.rationale: Zero movement since February 21. 26 points in 68 games, 14.7 MPG. The expected direction at 22 is up and it isn't happening.

recommendations.summary: Third on the sell list: 0.39 pts/g in 31 GP on an expiring deal with nothing to build on.
recommendations.rationale: 12 points in 31 games at age 22. Expiring $1.10M. Move him for whatever is available or let him walk.

recommendations.summary: McCabe stays. 0.82 pts/g through 68 games at 29 is still top-pair production.
recommendations.rationale: Confirmed off the sell list since March 4. No change to make.

recommendations.summary: Jackman's 30.7 MPG needs to come down next season. Watch it through the final games.
recommendations.rationale: 0.47 pts/g at 30.7 MPG is a system-fit or burnout problem, not a talent problem. At $0.70M x 3 he's too cheap to sell, but the load must drop or his ceiling is set.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker nightly on L4; his 83 CHKG and 88 TOUG (stored) are the only free checking minutes on the roster and he is in no unit.
recommendations.rationale: The coach's checking group is six deep but Tucker sits unlined. Adding him as a seventh checker costs no ice from the top three lines and gives L4 a body with 83 displayed CHKG.

recommendations.summary: Faceoffs are unfixable internally: Sundin 90 is the only 80+ man; L4 mean is 51. A second 80+ faceoff centre is the top acquisition need behind Belfour.
recommendations.rationale: Best available internal option after Sundin is Chlup at 75. No trade package built from existing depth lifts the fourth-line draw above 65 without breaking L2 or L3.

recommendations.summary: Toughness gap is likely a form artifact — stored grades showed six at 80+ TOUG on Feb 21 — but it must be confirmed before any external toughness target is pursued or discarded.
recommendations.rationale: If stored TOUG really holds six above 80, the coach's ceiling-of-76 complaint is a temporary form dip and the deadline currency should go to scoring (Havlat) or the Belfour replacement instead.

recommendations.summary: The keystone: Belfour (39, $6.50M, 1yr, 0.927 SV) must move by March 19 or the pick capital is lost permanently. Decision needed this week.
recommendations.rationale: He is the highest-value asset on the roster at its trade peak (22-5, 2.06 GAA). Colorado offered Hejduk as an example of what they give up. The GM said he is hedging against retirement.

recommendations.summary: Scoring, playmaking, speed, clutch and stamina are all covered at 9+ players above 80; no acquisition is needed in those roles.
recommendations.rationale: Six scorers at 88+, eleven playmakers at 80+, twenty-one skaters at 80+ speed. The roster is built for a playoff run; the gaps are specialist (faceoffs, toughness confirmation, goalie insurance), not general.

recommendations.summary: Move Belfour for a draft pick before March 19; he is 92 base, $6.50M, expiring, and Luongo has the number-one job.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour at 92 base qualifies for the over-80 expiring pick-recovery mechanic. He is 39, earning $6.50M, and with Luongo at 91 base in net there is no reason to keep him past the deadline.

recommendations.summary: Move Roberts for a draft pick before March 19; at 38 with $2.70M and POTE 52 he is the second over-80 expiring asset.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts is 68 pts in 67 games at 38 — productive tonight but not re-signable at 39. His contract is $2.70M expiring and his over-80 base makes him a pick-recovery candidate.

recommendations.summary: Sign Gaborik to a 5-6 year deal at season end; 81 pts in 67 games at 23 with POTE 90 on a $1.10M salary is the core of the franchise.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik's market rate on a 5-6 year deal will be $4-6M. Locking him before July prevents a bidding war and anchors the young core's renewal schedule.

recommendations.summary: Sign Nash to a 5-6 year deal at season end; 35 pts in 54 games at 20 with POTE 95 is franchise-left-wing production on a $1.20M contract.
recommendations.rationale: At 20 with POTE 95, Nash's ceiling justifies the highest offer the club makes this summer. His asking price will be $3-4M on a five-year deal.

recommendations.summary: Renew Abid on a 4-5 year deal; 65 points in 67 games at $400K with POTE 94 is the most underpriced contract on the roster and the open market will correct that in July.
recommendations.rationale: A 24-year-old top-six winger at $400K is unsustainable. His market rate is $2-3M. Re-signing him before the cluster hits preserves the value.

recommendations.summary: Sign Richards to a 5-year deal at season end; 61 pts in 65 games at 24 with POTE 88 on $1.00M is a second-line centre the club must keep.
recommendations.rationale: Richards at 24 is entering his prime and his 61-point season prices him at $3-4M on renewal. Locking him prevents the core from losing two centres at once.

recommendations.summary: Sign Eminger to a 5-6 year deal at season end; POTE 99 at 21 on $1.20M is the most valuable defenseman the club has and he is a year away from free agency.
recommendations.rationale: Eminger has 20 pts in 49 games and POTE 99. At 21 the GM has said his ceiling is not set. His renewal at $2-3M over five years is the cheapest insurance on a top-pair defenseman.

recommendations.summary: Sundin's $8.40M five-year deal is a sunk cost; no trade partner takes it and he is still producing 74 pts at 34.
recommendations.rationale: The contract locks $42M over five years for a player who will be 39 at expiry. Nothing can be done about it now, but it is the number the GM must carry in every future renewal calculation.

recommendations.summary: Plan Chlup's extension for summer 2006; at 19 with POTE 95 and two years left, a full top-nine season next year doubles his asking price.
recommendations.rationale: He has 40 pts in 56 games already at 19. If he plays 70+ games next season his market rate jumps. The GM should be thinking about this before the 2006 season opens, not after.

recommendations.summary: Decide on the Belfour-to-Colorado package by March 12 so there is time to execute and to open the Havlat negotiation with the freed 4th-rounder.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 92 base, $6.50M, expiring, age 39, with retirement risk. Colorado named Hejduk as a return in February. This is the keystone: it frees the 4th for Havlat and brings a proven scorer into the lineup.

recommendations.summary: Open Havlat negotiations with OTT (Tucker + 4th-rounder) the moment the Belfour path is confirmed.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 63 points (22-31-9) cannot re-sign Havlat (23, 87 base, 80 pts, $900K expiring). Tucker is 29, in no unit, $1.30M. The 4th is the only pick we own and is available only if Belfour does not need it for pick recovery.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla to a non-playoff team for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic before March 19.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla is 36, 92 CHKG, $3.60M expiring. His value walks in July. A non-contender picks up a top checking D for the playoff push; we recover a round 3 or 4.

recommendations.summary: Check Roberts' base overall; if above 80, include him in the pick-recovery sweep at the deadline. If below 80, release in July.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts is 38, $2.70M expiring. If he clears 80 base, the over-80 mechanic gets us a pick. If not, he is dead money with no trade value.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik to a 5-6 year deal at season end. Expect demands of $4-5M given 91 base and 67 points in 45 games.
recommendations.rationale: He is 23 with POTE 90 on a $1.10M one-year deal. He is the most valuable player on the roster and cannot be locked early. Every team will chase him in July.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger to 5-6 years at season end. GM has protected him and his POTE 99 at age 21 makes him a franchise defenseman.
recommendations.rationale: 21 years old, POTE 99, $1.20M expiring. The GM vetoed trades including him on January 19. He is the long-term top-pair D alongside Kaberle.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards to 5 years at season end on a reasonable deal; he is 24, the third-line centre, and $1.00M.
recommendations.rationale: Young centre depth is hard to find. At 24 with 70 FACE he anchors L3. A 5-year deal prevents him hitting the market at his prime.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash to 5 years at season end; at 20 with $1.20M expiring he is cheap on a long deal.
recommendations.rationale: He is 20 years old. Even if his production is unproven, locking a 20-year-old on a 5-year deal at a young-contract price is the best structure available.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle to 4-5 years at season end; at 27 and $1.90M he is the established top-pair partner.
recommendations.rationale: He is the veteran D we built around. At 27 with production, a 4-5 year deal locks the position through the young core's development.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Colaiacovo to 3-4 years at season end; at 22 with 0.36 ppg he is depth, not a star, and a short deal preserves flexibility.
recommendations.rationale: Coach reports his 0.36 ppg across two February checks suggests this is his level. Four years at $1.10M is fair for a third-pair D with a year or two of growth left.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Tellqvist to 2-3 years at season end per GM standing order; give him time to develop with high-90s potential.
recommendations.rationale: GM stated on January 15 that Tellqvist stays and gets time. A 2-3 year deal at $0.80M is cheap and preserves the backup role.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Abid to 2 years at season end; $0.40M for a 24-year-old with 80 base TOUG/CHKG is the cheapest toughness on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: Coach says toughness ceiling is Jackman at 76, but Abid's stored base is 80 TOUG and 80 CHKG. At $0.40M he is a depth asset we should not lose.

recommendations.summary: If Belfour is not traded by March 19 and will not accept a reduced contract, let him walk. His $6.50M is the largest item in the expiring cluster.
recommendations.rationale: GM said on January 15 he would offer a reduced deal but 'he probably won't accept.' If the Colorado trade does not land by the deadline, there is no further move to make and the salary walks to zero by default.

recommendations.summary: Release Roberts at season end if he was not moved at the deadline; 38 years old, $2.70M, no path to production that justifies the money.
recommendations.rationale: At 38, even if he clears the 80-base threshold for a pick trade and misses, there is no reason to re-sign him. The $2.70M freed is better spent on the young core's raises.

recommendations.current: Belfour ($6.50M, expiring) to Colorado for Morris (85 base, 57 pts/65 GP, $1.70M, expiring) or equivalent young player on a multi-year deal
recommendations.proposed: Morris or best available from Colorado for Belfour
recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour to Colorado (86 pts, no playoff goalie) for the best player they offer — test Morris first, accept Hejduk as fallback.
recommendations.rationale: Colorado desperate for a Cup-ready backup; Belfour is 22-5, 2.06 GAA at peak value. We shed $6.50M expiring and get a rental blueliner with 57 points at $1.70M who fills our third pair for the playoff. GM already confirmed Colorado offered Hejduk, proving willingness.

recommendations.current: Tucker (no unit, $1.30M, 2yr) plus 4th-round pick to Ottawa
recommendations.summary: Send Tucker plus the 4th to Ottawa for Havlat — a 23-year-old at 1.27 ppg who gives us a second top-six wing for the playoff.
recommendations.rationale: Ottawa at 63 points with 11 expiring cannot retain Havlat; Tucker gives them a 92-CHKG veteran body with 2 years left. Tucker is in no unit (surplus). Havlat's 80 points in 63 games makes him the best available scoring addition.

recommendations.current: Svehla (36, 92 CHKG, $3.60M, expiring) to Montreal or other non-contender
recommendations.proposed: Draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic
recommendations.summary: Dump Svehla to Montreal (51 pts, worst in league) for a pick; non-contender per the March 4 standing order.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla is 36, expiring, $3.60M. The over-80 mechanic recovers a pick for any 80+ overall player a team will not re-sign. Montreal has 15 expiring deals and no reason to refuse a veteran body for nothing. Avoids sending him to a playoff rival.

recommendations.summary: If none of the three trades land, keep Belfour for the playoff run and enter July accepting the loss of $6.50M in pick capital — the core is intact and the team at 106 points does not need saving.
recommendations.rationale: The roster has six players at 88+ overall, a 2.06 GAA goalie, and the deepest youth core in the league. No deadline move is mandatory. The summer 2005 renewal cluster (14 players, $21.70M) is the real deadline and that is a July problem.

recommendations.summary: The Luongo/DiPietro monitoring task is closed: Luongo is on the roster at 93 base with 2 years and the GM declared goalies solved on Feb 19.
recommendations.rationale: Original target acquired. Luongo 91 base, 25, $1.60M, 2 years. GM's Feb 19 standing order: 'Goalies are solved. Done. Do not revisit that issue.' DiPietro at 80 is not relevant.

recommendations.summary: Dress Spezza and give him the third wing with 10+ minutes for the remaining 15 games.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 at 21, 0.41 pts/g in limited minutes, better per minute than Chistov (0.34) who plays ahead of him. 37 games at 7.5 MPG is a wasted development year with no recovery window until next season.

recommendations.summary: Run Stahle on the third pair for the remaining 15 games.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 96 at 20, 4 games all season. Colaiacovo is himself scratched most nights, so the third pair is open. Nothing to chase in the standings; this is the window.

recommendations.summary: Hold Spacek at 10+ MPG now that the March 4 bump is established.
recommendations.rationale: The GM took the bump last game. 19 with POTE 91 at 0.36 pts/g on 8.5 season MPG; one game at 12 does not fix the pattern. Keep pushing it up where the game allows.

recommendations.summary: Gaborik, Chlup and Nash have earned their roles and are getting them. No adjustment needed.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik 81 points at 20.1 MPG on the first line, Chlup 40 points at 16.3 MPG on the second at 19, Nash 0.65 pts/g on third-line minutes. All three are where their production puts them.

recommendations.summary: Smirnov at POTE 70 and zero games is not a development emergency. Leave him scratched.
recommendations.rationale: Lowest POTE on the young roster. Zero production signal to justify displacing anyone. Fine as a non-roster piece.

recommendations.summary: Give Spacek 12+ MPG in the next two games or accept that his year is over and stop dressing him.
recommendations.rationale: 0.30 pts/g on 6.0 MPG at 19 is a fourth-line production on a fourth-line shift. The Mar 4 bump was taken but no game followed, so it is still untested.

recommendations.summary: Either return Spezza to 10+ MPG in remaining games or accept the full scratch; at 21 with POTE 99 he has played 5.3 MPG since December.
recommendations.rationale: 0.43 to 0.38 pts/g on falling minutes, same finding since January 31, raised five times. The season is nearly over.

recommendations.summary: Plan offseason around Afinogenov's 0.72 pts/g at 25 and Jackman's 0.38 at 24; both should be trending up.
recommendations.rationale: Afinogenov dropped from 1.17 to 0.72 on flat minutes. Jackman dropped from 0.65 to 0.38 while his load rose to 31.2 MPG. Neither has an age excuse.

recommendations.summary: Colaiacovo at 0.36 pts/g across two checks in February suggests this is his level at 22, not a dip.
recommendations.rationale: 0.44 to 0.36 on minutes down from 18.9 to 17.5. Expected direction at 22 is up; it is flat or down.

recommendations.summary: The room is at 96-100 with a win streak lifting everyone; no morale intervention needed tonight.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin, Mogilny, Richards, Chlup, Gaborik, Jackman and the rest all posted +5 morale jumps. Spacek moved from -4 to +5 after the March 4 minutes bump. The lever is working where it's being pulled.

recommendations.summary: Spezza at 86 morale and 7.5 MPG is the one player losing this season; he needs 10+ MPG in a game we can afford or the year is wasted.
recommendations.rationale: 86 morale is frozen across the entire save. At 21 with 15 points in 37 games he's below the 10-MPG band his calibre demands. Raised five times with no action; this is now a roster-level decision.

recommendations.summary: All units are built correctly for their role; no composition change against BUF.
recommendations.rationale: P1 has the shooters, P2 has secondary skill, K2 is the physical kill unit with Jackman and McCabe (checking mean 76, toughness 68). L1 and L2 are scoring lines and their low checking means are by design.

recommendations.summary: L4 faceoff mean of 51 with a best of 54 is a roster gap we cannot fill without breaking L2 or L3.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin (90), Chlup (79), Roberts (75) and Richards (74) are the only centres above 74 and all are committed higher. Against strong-centre opponents this line gets hemmed in the defensive zone. Not fixable by moving anyone tonight.

recommendations.summary: Toughness ceiling across the roster is Jackman at 76; we have no enforcer-level presence.
recommendations.rationale: Jackman 76, McCabe 72, Roberts 71, Abid 71 is the full list above 70. We are a skill team that relies on structure for protection. If the GM wants a deterrent, it is a trade or signing target, not a lineup fix.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour. 92 OVR, no fatigue icon, morale 99.
recommendations.rationale: He carries no tired streak icon per the badge check, and this is a low-event opponent allowing 2.70 per game. Easy start.

recommendations.summary: Leave the defensive pair slot order as-is. Pair one faces BUF's best line, pair three hides Eminger against their weakest.
recommendations.rationale: Fischer+Jackman (combined 167) against Nolan-Drury-Briere (238) is already our best available. Eminger+Klesla against Gaustad-Brunette-Dumont (68/70/72) is the right hiding spot. No improvement possible from a swap.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes for this opponent. BUF is not a quality night; keep the young guys in and play the standard structure.
recommendations.rationale: 23-29-6, last-10 WLLOLLLLLW, PP under 10%. We've outscored them 24-2 in three games. This is a game where development priority applies per the GM's framework. Spacek and Nash are already dressed.

recommendations.summary: Eminger remains the top D sell: 0.41 pts/g over 49 games on an expiring $1.2M deal at age 21.
recommendations.rationale: His rate has fallen again from 0.44 on Feb 26 to 0.41 now. At 75 OVR and third-pair production he is worth more as a deadline asset than as a fourth-pair defenceman next season.

recommendations.summary: Klesla is the second sell candidate: 0.39 pts/g over 67 games at age 22, flat when he should be ascending.
recommendations.rationale: Season rate essentially unchanged from the 0.38 flagged Feb 21st. Two years at $0.90M for declining young D production is a bad hold.

recommendations.summary: No deadline acquisition needed for toughness — the zero-at-80+ reading is a form artifact, stored grades show six at 80+ TOUG.
recommendations.rationale: Feb 21 finding confirmed the displayed toughness gap is form-driven. Roberts 73 displayed but 80+ stored, McCabe 73 displayed but 80+ stored. No currency should be spent on a phantom gap.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker nightly — at 83 displayed CHKG (92 stored) he is the second-best forward checker on the roster and currently in no unit.
recommendations.rationale: The coach flags D-side checking depth but forward-side checking is also thin with Tucker idle. Putting him in costs nothing and frees a top-nine forward from defensive duty.

recommendations.summary: Dress Koltsov — 92 speed, not lined in any unit.
recommendations.rationale: He is the fourth-fastest player on the roster and sitting on the bench with nothing to do.

recommendations.summary: The D-side checking depth gap is real but not fixable at the deadline without violating the GM's protective orders on McCabe, Eminger, or paying for Chara who Ottawa will not sell.
recommendations.rationale: McCabe 86 and Fischer 82 are the only D under 36 at 80+ CHKG. Svehla 83 fills this role through the playoffs at 36. The summer problem is whether to re-sign Svehla or develop a replacement; no deadline option clears the GM's constraint set.

recommendations.summary: Lock the four cornerstone players on 5-6 years at season end; their current combined salary is $4.50M and each will command a significant raise.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik at 81 pts/$1.10M, Richards at 57 pts/$1.00M, Nash at 33 pts/$1.20M at age 20, Eminger at POTE 99/$1.20M. All expire July 2005. If they walk the team is rebuilt from scratch. 5-6 years keeps them through the 2007-08 prime window.

recommendations.proposed: 3-4 year deals to stagger against the core locks
recommendations.summary: Sign the second group on 3-4 years so they come up in 2008-09, not 2010, splitting the renewal cliff across two summers.
recommendations.rationale: All expire July 2005. Signing them on 5-6 years alongside the core creates a new 7-player cluster in 2010-11. Three-to-four-year terms stagger it. Kaberle at 27 (POTE 75) and Abid at 24 (65 pts, $0.40M, POTE 94) are the most urgent in this group.

recommendations.proposed: Move all three at the March deadline for draft picks and/or young players
recommendations.summary: Each is over-80 on stored grades with an expiring contract, making them the only path to recovering draft picks for a club that holds a single fourth-rounder.
recommendations.rationale: Combined salary $12.80M. The over-80 expiring mechanic converts each into at least one draft pick. This is both salary relief (offsetting the renewal raises) and the entire draft-capital strategy. Belfour is actively being explored by the GM for a Hejduk-type return from Colorado.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Havlat for Tucker plus the fourth-rounder before March 19.
recommendations.rationale: 23, 87 base, 80 pts/63 GP, $900K expiring. OTT at 63 pts with 11 expiring cannot retain him. Addresses the coach's team-wide scoring problem with a young, re-signable player who costs one pick.

recommendations.proposed: Igor Kravchuk or any 80+ CHKG D available
recommendations.summary: Komisarek (MTL, 23, 83 TOUG, POTE 90, $1.10M expiring) is the target if pick capital recovers from Belfour or Svehla trades.
recommendations.rationale: Coach needs a third D who checks 80+. Komisarek at 83 TOUG and POTE 90 at 23 fits. MTL at 51 pts with 15 expiring are the worst club in the league. Costs St. Jacques + Safronov + a pick we do not currently own.

recommendations.proposed: Trade Svehla for draft pick before March 19
recommendations.summary: Move Svehla (36, 92 CHKG, $3.60M expiring) to recover a draft pick before his value walks in July.
recommendations.rationale: Over-80 expiring assets recover picks per the known mechanic. Svehla is the second-best after Belfour. Shedding his $3.60M also addresses the payroll spike from the July renewal cluster.

recommendations.summary: LA hold Cammalleri (POTE 98, 1.17 pts/g) and Frolov (POTE 96, 1.18 pts/g) both at $1.10M expiring, age 22. Pursue one if Havlat falls through.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 65 pts with 14 expiring are motivated sellers. Either player is a top-six winger for five years at rookie money. Second priority behind Havlat due to higher acquisition cost.

recommendations.summary: Close the Belfour trade before March 19. Hejduk (32, elite scorer) addresses the scoring gap while recovering Belfour's value before retirement risk.
recommendations.rationale: GM set criteria on Feb 21: 'good but locked on reasonable salary for a couple of years.' Colorado offered Hejduk as example of willingness. If Belfour retires in July, we lose a 92-base asset for nothing.

recommendations.summary: Third priority: Bell (24, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, 80 base, $900K, 2 years) if Havlat and Cammalleri/Frolov both fail.
recommendations.rationale: CHI at 59 pts with 10 expiring are sellers. Bell closes toughness, checking, and faceoffs simultaneously on a cheap long deal. But costs R2 + Colaiacovo, which we cannot afford with one pick.

recommendations.current: Belfour (TOR, G, 39, 92 base, $6.50M expiring, 21-5 2.10 GAA 0.925 SV)
recommendations.proposed: Hejduk (COL, RW, top-line winger, multi-year reasonable salary)
recommendations.summary: Send Belfour to Colorado for Hejduk; if this lands the 4th stays for Havlat and payroll drops $6.50M.
recommendations.rationale: GM tested this trade directly and Colorado offered Hejduk. They need a goalie and have none. Belfour at 92 base is the best rental on the market. Hejduk meets the 'locked on reasonable salary' test GM set on Feb 21.

recommendations.current: Tucker (TOR, LW, 29, $1.30M, 3 GP, not in any unit) + 4th-round pick (TOR)
recommendations.proposed: Havlat (OTT, RW, 23, 87 base, 80 pts/63 GP, $900K expiring)
recommendations.summary: Send Tucker plus the 4th to Ottawa for Havlat; addresses the team-wide scoring dip with a 23-year-old at 1.27 pts/g.
recommendations.rationale: Ottawa at 63 points with 11 expiring contracts cannot re-sign Havlat. Tucker is dressed 3 games and sits in no unit. The 4th is our only pick. Net salary swing minus $400K this season, both expiring in July.

recommendations.proposed: Draft pick (second-round caliber via over-80 expiring mechanic)
recommendations.summary: Move Svehla to any contender for a draft pick before March 19; recovers a pick from a player we will not re-sign and sheds $3.60M.
recommendations.rationale: The over-80 expiring mechanic converts a high-rated expiring contract into a pick. Svehla at 92 CHKG fills a playoff D-side need for the buyer. We lose nothing after July and gain draft capital to fund a second acquisition.

recommendations.summary: The Luongo/DiPetro monitoring task is closed. Luongo is on our roster at 94 with two years at $1.60M. The goalie trade window is resolved.
recommendations.rationale: GM declared goalies solved on Feb 19. Luongo arrived at 94 overall, 2 years club control, $1.60M. DiPetro at 81 overall was never a high-90s target. Nothing further to monitor.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza 15+ MPG tonight against Ottawa; raised six times with no movement and his morale is the lowest young player on the roster at 86.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99, 37 GP, 7.5 MPG, 15 pts. At 21 with the top potential marking on the roster, 7.5 minutes develops nobody. Ottawa is 22-30 and this is a development night per the GM's framework.

recommendations.summary: Bump Spacek to 12+ MPG tonight against Ottawa.
recommendations.rationale: 43 GP, 8.5 MPG, POTE 91 at 19. Morale 92 but trending toward the floor if minutes stay here. Ottawa is a game we can afford to develop in.

recommendations.summary: Stahle needs at least 15 more games this season; 4 in 66 at POTE 96 and age 20 is the worst development waste on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: 17.8 MPG in his 4 appearances shows the staff trusts him. 16 games left is enough to get him to 20 if dressed tonight and every night we can afford it.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev is producing 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG and getting scratched; at 23 his development window is closing and he needs either a real role or a decision.
recommendations.rationale: 30 points in 55 games is above fourth-line production. He should either play 12+ MPG or be acknowledged as a depth piece with no further upside to chase.

recommendations.summary: No change for Chlup, Nash, Gaborik, Klesla, Eminger, Chistov, Colaiacovo, or Upshall.
recommendations.rationale: All are getting minutes proportional to their current production and age. Chlup 38 pts on L2 at 19, Nash 33 pts on L3 at 20, Gaborik 81 pts on L1 at 23 — earned and maintained.

recommendations.summary: Chistov at 21 is going up in both rate (0.29→0.34) and minutes (9.5→14.5) across 52 games; flag him as a growing piece in next-year planning.
recommendations.rationale: Both production and usage rising simultaneously at 21 is the signature of a player growing into a role. Nobody has raised him; he deserves a spot on the off-season short list.

recommendations.summary: Spacek is at 0.31 pts/g on 5.9 MPG in 43 games; the pattern has deepened since my last four raises. Either commit real minutes or stop dressing him.
recommendations.rationale: 0.55→0.31 pts/g and 16.0→5.9 MPG is a player whose development is stalling despite being on the roster. At 19 this year is recoverable only with actual ice time.

recommendations.summary: Spezza at 21 with 0.43→0.38 pts/g on 9.1→5.3 MPG across 37 games continues to waste his POTE 99 on fourth-line scraps.
recommendations.rationale: Same pattern as Spacek but one year older and higher potential. Raised since January 31 with no movement.

recommendations.summary: Koltsov's rate collapsed from 1.10 to 0.28 pts/g over 35 games at 23; his trade value is dropping fast. If he is a chip, trade him now.
recommendations.rationale: The 1.10 start was 10 games and is gone. 0.28 over 35 is the real number and any GM will see it too.

recommendations.summary: McCabe at 29 is at 0.50 pts/g across 66 games on a four-year $3M deal. He remains the loudest sell on the blue line.
recommendations.rationale: The 1.42 start in 24 games was unsustainable; 0.50 over 66 is who he is now. Four years and $3M for that is the biggest overcommitment on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Sundin (34), Mogilny (36), Roberts (38) and Svehla (36) are all aging together: rates down, minutes up. Plan the replacement block for next summer.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin 1.46→0.93, Mogilny 1.62→0.79, Roberts 1.29→0.88, Svehla 0.78→0.44. All four are declining at the same time. Chlup and Chistov are trending up; Klesla and Colaiacovo are not.

recommendations.summary: No morale intervention needed tonight. The room is at 92 or above for every player except Spezza (86), and no trend is negative.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza's morale has stabilized at 86 rather than continuing to slide. Everyone else is at 96 or 99 with positive movement. No player is under his expected minutes band by enough to cause a crack before tonight.

recommendations.summary: Abid's 15.9 MPG against a 90+ expectation (65 pts, 66 GP) is the next morale risk if results dip; monitor before the next losing streak.
recommendations.rationale: Abid at 99 morale is fine today, but he is 4 minutes under what his calibre expects. The first losing streak will put pressure on that. Not urgent tonight.

recommendations.summary: Kaberle stays on K2 because no better D exists; this is a depth gap, not a misassignment.
recommendations.rationale: K2 checking mean is 73 against 86 best, with McCabe (84) and Abid (83) carrying the unit and Kaberle the weak link. But Salo is at 0.18 pts/g, Colaiacovo at 72 OVR, and Stahle has zero games. No replacement improves the unit.

recommendations.summary: Only three centers win draws above 75% equivalent (Sundin 91, Chlup 80, Richards 75); a single injury to Richards or Chlup leaves no faceoff coverage below L1.
recommendations.rationale: L3 mean faceoff 58, L4 mean 52. Bottom six centers cannot win the draw in important situations. This costs zone entries and puts us behind on the puck in defensive-zone faceoffs.

recommendations.summary: All even-strength lines are composed correctly for their intended roles; no changes needed before OTT.
recommendations.rationale: L1 and L2 are offensive lines and have the scoring (82/81 mean) and playmaking (81/80 mean) to justify it. L3 is a speed-and-stamina line (speed 83, Richards 86 stamina) with Klesla as the single checker. L4 anchors on Abid (83 checking). P1 and P2 are clearly tiered by skill.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour. Check his fatigue icon before puck drop.
recommendations.rationale: 93 OVR against Ottawa's 2.70 goals per game and 11.7% PP. He will face fewer quality chances than almost any night this season.

recommendations.summary: No line changes for Ottawa.
recommendations.rationale: Our L1/D1 combination (Sundin 90, Gaborik 97, Roberts 87 / Fischer 84, McCabe 83) is the correct answer to their top line. Fischer's 94 speed and 91 checking handle Havlat. Our L3 (86/82/81) already outscores their L3 (78/76/76) by a clear margin. Rearranging helps nobody.

recommendations.summary: Give Spacek the fourth line tonight and let him play. Their L4 is 72/72/66, the softest assignment a 19-year-old can draw.
recommendations.rationale: Per the GM's framework, a 22-30-9 opponent is a night we can afford development. Spacek at 76 OVR against Schastlivy 72, Johnson 72, Prommersberger 66 is a favorable test he should want.

recommendations.summary: McCabe off the sell list at 0.83 pts/g over 66 games; Eminger remains first cut at 0.42, Salo second at 0.30, Klesla third at 0.36.
recommendations.rationale: McCabe's Feb 12 panic window (0.33) has been absorbed into a season rate of 0.83 (55 in 66). He is still the best producer on the blue line. Eminger unchanged at 0.42 pts/g on an expiring deal. Klesla marginally down from 0.38 to 0.36 at age 22 with flat minutes.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker nightly through March; his stored 84 TOUG and 88 CHKG are the free sixth checker this roster needs for playoff depth.
recommendations.rationale: Today's display reads him at 70/83 because engine form suppresses the whole club, but the stored grades are 84/88. At 83 displayed CHKG he already matches Svehla's 83. He is the sixth man the checking group is missing and costs nothing.

recommendations.summary: Do not spend trade currency on toughness this deadline; the 73 ceiling is a form artifact and stored grades carry six at 80+.
recommendations.rationale: The Feb 21 finding at high confidence established that stored TOUG is 80+ on six players, with the entire club reading 10-14 points depressed. Tucker at stored 84 confirms it. Chasing an external tough-guy for a gap that does not exist wastes the fourth-rounder or Tucker's own trade value.

recommendations.summary: Evaluate Salo (88 scoring, 30) in March games as playoff extra body; he is the highest-grade player not in any unit.
recommendations.rationale: Salo reads 88 on scoring and 30 years old, the same age as McCabe. He is not in any line slot. A playoff roster needs 7 D or 13 F and he is the best available bench player by grade.

recommendations.summary: Dress Koltsov (92 speed, 23) in at least half of the remaining 18 games; 92 SPEE with no evaluation plan wastes a roster spot.
recommendations.rationale: His 92 displayed speed is the second-best on the club behind Gaborik's 98. At 23 with no unit, the GM cannot grade him for next season's rotation in June if he never plays.

recommendations.summary: Build a tiered summer 2005 re-signing plan before the season ends: Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, Upshall on 5-6 years; Alexeev, Chistov, Colaiacovo, Abid, Smirnov on 2-3 years to split the renewal load across 2005 and 2007.
recommendations.rationale: 15 contracts worth $25.30M expire in the same July. All on 5-6 years means 10+ re-signings in July 2006 for the 2-year group (Chlup, Luongo, Klesla, Ouellet, Spezza, all POTE 95+) with no offsetting depth deals. Staggering depth onto 2-3 year terms pushes those renewals to 2007.

recommendations.summary: The age curve and payroll structure are sound: 26 players under 30, five veterans naturally rolling off within 24 months, and $24.28M profit funds the raises the young core will demand.
recommendations.rationale: 15 players at 23 or under, 11 at 24-29, only 5 at 34+. The veteran salary ($18.30M across Sundin, Mogilny, Svehla, Roberts, Belfour) expires or shrinks within two years, creating space for young-core raises without threatening profitability.

recommendations.summary: Spezza's POTE 99 and 5.3 MPG at age 21 means the club has a future top-six centre on the bench; if the plan depends on him being part of the core by 2006-07, he needs 12+ MPG now.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza has 15 points in 37 games on $1.00M with 2 years left (expires July 2006). If he is to be a cornerstone, development clock is ticking: by the time his contract is up he is 23 and still needs to prove top-six worthiness.

recommendations.summary: Decide on the Belfour-to-Colorado-for-Hejduk deal by March 10; this gates the Havlat package and recovers value from a 39-year-old who may retire.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 92 base, $6.50M expiring, and the only over-80 asset on the roster. If the deal lands, the 4th-rounder funds Havlat; if it doesn't, both upgrades are lost. GM's own Feb 21 note worries about losing him for nothing.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Havlat from Ottawa for Tucker plus the 4th-rounder once the Belfour decision is settled.
recommendations.rationale: Havlat is 23, 87 base, 80 points in 63 games, $900K expiring. OTT at 63 points with 11 expiring cannot retain him. He is the depth-scoring answer the roster lacks.

recommendations.summary: Move Roberts before March 19 for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts is 38, $2.70M, expiring, over 80. He is not in the playoff plan at 38 and not in the future plan at all. The mechanic converts him to a pick at no hockey cost.

recommendations.summary: Offer Gaborik a 5-6 year deal at season end; he is the first priority of July.
recommendations.rationale: At 23, 91 base, POTE 90, 67 points in 45 games on $1.10M, he is the best young player on the roster. If he hits the market he will be bid up beyond what we want to pay.

recommendations.summary: Offer Eminger a 5-6 year deal at season end alongside Gaborik.
recommendations.rationale: At 21, $1.20M, POTE 99, GM has explicitly protected him. Locking him long is the cheapest cornerstone we will ever sign.

recommendations.summary: Renew Kaberle on 5 years at season end.
recommendations.rationale: At 27 on $1.90M, he is in his prime as our top offensive defenseman. Five years locks the position without a July bidding war.

recommendations.summary: Renew Richards on 5-6 years at season end.
recommendations.rationale: At 24 on $1.00M, he is our long-term centre solution. Cheap, young, already deployed at third-line centre.

recommendations.summary: Renew Nash on 5 years at season end.
recommendations.rationale: At 20 on $1.20M, he is the youngest of the core five. Five years now means his deal does not cluster with Gaborik or Richards in three summers.

recommendations.summary: Do not renew Smirnov; clear the roster slot at season end.
recommendations.rationale: At 20, POTE 70, zero games played. The coach's read is correct: the spot is wasted. POTE 70 does not justify a roster slot over a POTE 90+ call-up.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla in the off-season via the over-80 mechanic; keep him for the playoffs.
recommendations.rationale: At 36, $3.60M, 92 CHKG stored, he is a pick-recovery asset. But gutting the top pair two weeks before the deadline weakens the playoff D-corps of a first-place team. Convert him in July instead.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Havlat (OTT, LW, 84 ovr, 82 pts/65 GP, $0.90M expiring, POTE 85, age 23) for Tucker plus the 4th-rounder.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 63 points with 11 expiring deals cannot retain him. Fills the depth-scoring gap with a player on our timeline. Package is already identified and costs only a player not in any unit plus our single pick.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Cammalleri (LA, RW, 79 ovr, 47 pts/43 GP, POTE 97, age 22, $1.10M expiring) for Koltsov plus a recovered pick from Svehla.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 64 points with 14 expiring deals cannot re-sign him over their own cap pressure. At 22 with POTE 97 he is re-signable for five years and fills a top-six wing permanently, unlike any rental. Koltsov (92 speed, not in any unit) is the natural return piece.

recommendations.summary: Monitor ATL's re-signing binary: if they keep Heatley over Kovalchuk (86 ovr, 105 pts/62 GP, $1.10M expiring, POTE 85, age 21), he becomes available for Koltsov plus Chistov.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 64 points with 11 expiring cannot retain both. Kovalchuk is the highest-scoring available player in the league. But acquiring him costs Koltsov AND Chistov (both POTE 95+) for a rental unless we commit $3-5M at renewal on top of the $25.30M July wall. Only pursue if ATL re-signs Heatley first.

recommendations.summary: Conroy (CGY, C, 76 ovr, 77 pts/64 GP, 94 FACE, $2.00M expiring, age 31) fills the faceoff gap and adds centre production from the worst team in the league, but costs a young asset for a rental.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 50 points, 10 expiring, desperate. He closes the faceoff gap (94 FACE) and adds 77 points of centre production tonight. But at 31 and expiring he is a pure rental, and any package CGY accepts uses a POTE 95+ prospect. Recommended only if the GM values this playoff run above Chistov's future.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla ($3.60M expiring, 36, 83 CHKG) for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic before March 19.
recommendations.rationale: At 36 with one year left he walks in July for nothing. The over-80 expiring mechanic converts him to a pick, which funds a second deadline package (Cammalleri or Komisarek) without spending the 4th already earmarked for Havlat. If he goes to a contender needing a checking D-man, they accept an aging body for a short-term boost.

recommendations.summary: Komisarek (MTL, D, 76 ovr, 70 pts/65 GP, POTE 91, age 23, $1.10M expiring) from MTL at 51 points with 15 expiring deals.
recommendations.rationale: MTL is the worst seller in the league with the most expiring deals. At 23 with POTE 91 and 70 points from the blue line he is a future top-pair defenceman. But this competes for the same assets as Cammalleri; the GM should choose one or the other based on whether the priority is wing depth or blue-line depth.

recommendations.summary: Send Belfour to Colorado for Hejduk now; the GM confirmed Colorado accepts this on Feb 21 and the deal is ready to execute.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour at 92 base with 18-3 2.27 GAA in 21 GP is exactly what a contender without a goalie needs for a Cup run. Colorado have no capable backup. We shed $6.50M, gain a top-line wing without spending the 4th-rounder, and free it for Havlat. The GM tested this trade on Feb 21 and Colorado said yes.

recommendations.proposed: Havlat (OTT, 23, 84 overall, 82 pts/65 GP, $900K expiring, POTE 85)
recommendations.summary: Send Tucker plus the 4th-rounder to Ottawa for Havlat; if rejected, add Salo ($2.60M, 2yr, not in any unit) to sweeten.
recommendations.rationale: Havlat is 82 points on $900K, 23 years old, and Ottawa at 63 points with 11 expiring deals cannot retain him. Tucker plays 3 games for us but gives Ottawa a checking wing with 2 years of team control for next season. The 4th-rounder is low value; Salo as an add clears $2.60M from our July renewal list and adds a body Ottawa can use.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla to a contender for a draft pick before March 7 so the pick is re-tradeable before the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla at 83+ displayed overall with 92 CHKG and 94 ENDU is a playoff-ready shutdown pair for any contender thin at the blue line. The over-80 expiring mechanic converts him to a pick. Must close by March 7 because picks need 10 games before re-use and the deadline is March 19. We shed $3.60M with no incoming salary. If the pick arrives, it funds Komisarek (MTL, 23, POTE 90, 83 TOUG, $1.10M expiring) from a 46-point seller.

recommendations.proposed: Kovalchuk or Heatley (ATL, free agency July 2005)
recommendations.summary: If no deadline deal lands, pivot to summer free agency: ATL cannot re-sign both Kovalchuk (89 base, 105 pts) and Heatley (91 base, 96 pts), so one will be available at no trade cost.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 64 points with 11 expiring deals face the same retention math in July. We can sign one to a 5-6 year deal with no trade currency required, only salary. This is the fallback plan if the three deadline proposals all fail.

recommendations.summary: Close the Luongo/DiPietro monitoring task. Luongo is our starter (94, 65 GP, 2yr deal) and DiPietro (82, 3.64 GAA) does not fit the high-90s target profile the GM set on Jan 15.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo played all 65 games and is locked for two years. DiPietro's 7-12 record and 0.849 SP in 21 games at age 23 with an expiring deal make him a low-80s backup, not the franchise goalie the GM wants from a non-contender.

recommendations.summary: Spezza must be reinstated to 12+ MPG in remaining games or traded before the deadline; his morale at 86 is now costing us a grade on every attribute.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 at 21 with 15 points in 37 games and 7.5 MPG. He's been raised six times with no movement. His morale at 86 is now in the band that subtracts from all grades, so keeping him scratched costs on-ice quality from the player we're trying to develop.

recommendations.summary: Stahle's movement from 0 to 4 games is the right direction; keep the slow ramp.
recommendations.rationale: He earned 17.8 MPG in his 4 appearances, showing the GM trusts him when he does play. At 20 with POTE 96 the priority is continuing to dress him, not forcing him into a full role.

recommendations.current: Chlup (54 GP, 16.1 MPG, 38 pts, L2, age 19)
recommendations.summary: Chlup is earning everything he's getting; 0.70 pts/g on 16.1 MPG on the second line is exactly where he belongs.
recommendations.rationale: 38 points in 54 games at 19 on the second line with morale at 96. No intervention needed.

recommendations.summary: Smirnov at POTE 70 is not a high-ceiling waste; he is a depth forward not yet ready for this level.
recommendations.rationale: Zero games at 20 with POTE 70 is a fair outcome for a player on the edge of this roster. Not every young player is owed games.

recommendations.summary: Plan next season around Chlup as a permanent top-nine forward at 17+ MPG.
recommendations.rationale: 0.62 to 0.73 pts/g with minutes up from 11.0 to 17.7 at 19. He is climbing while carrying a heavier load, which is the signal of a real breakout.

recommendations.summary: Chistov is growing into a third-line role: minutes up from 9.5 to 14.4 with his rate improving from 0.29 to 0.32.
recommendations.rationale: He is the young option that helps the L3 stamina problem. Give him the remainder of this season at 14+ MPG to confirm.

recommendations.summary: Spacek needs a decision this week: 12+ MPG or full scratch. 6.0 MPG at 0.32 pts/g at age 19 is a year wasted.
recommendations.rationale: Minutes collapsed from 16.0 to 6.0 and his rate halved from 0.55 to 0.32. Raised four times in February with no movement. This is the biggest development failure after Spezza.

recommendations.summary: Spezza at 5.3 MPG and 0.38 pts/g at 21 with POTE 99 is now a confirmed wasted year. He needs a real role next season or a roster decision.
recommendations.rationale: Minutes fell from 9.1 to 5.3 and rate from 0.43 to 0.38. Raised six times with no change in his usage.

recommendations.summary: McCabe is the loudest summer sell. 0.46 pts/g on the full window at 29, four years and $3M remaining.
recommendations.rationale: Season rate collapsed from 1.42 to 0.46. The January recovery note is dead. No defenceman playing 22 MPG for $3M should be at 0.46.

recommendations.summary: Salo at 0.17 pts/g on 14.6 MPG at age 30 is below fourth-pair production. Sell this summer.
recommendations.rationale: Rate collapsed from 0.40 to 0.17 while minutes fell from 20.3 to 14.6. Two years and $2.6M left on the contract. The cheapest meaningful cut behind McCabe.

recommendations.summary: Mogilny should not be playing 19.8 MPG at 36. Cut him to 15 or less and give those minutes to Chistov or Spacek.
recommendations.rationale: His rate halved from 1.62 to 0.81 while his minutes went up from 16.9 to 19.8. He is absorbing minutes the third line cannot carry, which is accelerating the decline.

recommendations.summary: Roberts at 38 went from 16.5 to 21.0 MPG while production fell from 1.29 to 0.85. Plan for a reduced role next season.
recommendations.rationale: Same pattern as Mogilny and Sundin: aging players absorbing minutes because L3 cannot absorb them. The trio is not sustainable at these loads.

recommendations.summary: Keep dressing Stahle for the remaining 17 games. Four games at 17.8 MPG is the start we needed at POTE 96.
recommendations.rationale: He had zero games through 49. Now at four. At 20 he needs every shift he can get before next season.

recommendations.summary: Eminger at 0.50 pts/g on the full window with minutes up from 15.0 to 17.0. His recovery is holding. Keep him in the lineup.
recommendations.rationale: Feb 19 recovery note is confirmed by the full-window trend. If he finishes above 0.50 we discuss his expiring contract. Below 0.45 the sell case returns.

recommendations.summary: The room is at 92+ across the board with the winning streak lifting everyone. No morale intervention needed tonight.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza at 86 is the only sub-90 and is ticking up (+1). Spacek and Alexeev surged +5 each to 92. The streak is doing the work a line change would otherwise have to do.

recommendations.summary: We need one more defenceman who checks in the 80+ range; our only two are McCabe and Fischer and they are already paired together on D1.
recommendations.rationale: D Pair 2 (Svehla, Kaberle) has no player above 83 checking -- neither appears on the role inventory. D Pair 3 (Eminger, Klesla) is young with no checking specialist either. Against quality opponents the auto-pairing sends this pair against the opponent's second line with nothing to match their skill. The gap is one 80+ checking D.

recommendations.summary: The forward lines are built correctly for their roles and no shuffle improves the unit attribute profile without breaking chemistry.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has grit and scoring, L2 has skill and faceoff from Chlup (80), L3 has depth and speed. Moving a checker to L2 means removing one from L1 or L3 and creating the same gap elsewhere.

recommendations.summary: P1 is built around possession and skill (scoring 82, playmaking 82, clutch 85) and the unit is coherent.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik at 98 scoring and 99 playmaking is the engine. Sundin provides the draw and the point shot. Roberts and McCabe screen and cycle. No change needed.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes for FLA tonight. Every line matchup favours us and their best centre is out until March 19.
recommendations.rationale: FLA without Nieuwendyk (81 OVR, FACE 94) has no line that out-talents ours. Their PP is 20/199 (10.1%). We are 3-0-0 in the season series, 11-5 in goals. The existing line construction already exploits the depth gap on every pair.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour unless his fatigue icon shows tired before puck drop.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour reads 93 OVR with morale 99 tonight. FLA scores 2.90 per game but 1.67 against us this season. No reason to hand this to Ouellet (82 OVR).

recommendations.summary: McCabe's recent window is 0.20 pts/g (1 pt in 5 games since Feb 21) but season rate of 0.82 still earns top-pair minutes. No change to his role.
recommendations.rationale: 0.82 pts/g at 22.8 MPG is still our best offensive D by 0.28. The cold streak is a trajectory concern for next season's $3M x 4 deal, not a reason to move him now.

recommendations.summary: Eminger stays on the sell list: 0.43 pts/g season, 0 points in 3 since Feb 21, expiring $1.2M.
recommendations.rationale: Season rate has not recovered since Feb 19 and continues drifting down. He will be a cheap UFCA in April if we don't get something.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker on the fourth line to give it 88 TOUG and 92 CHKG without spending currency.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker is in no unit with stored TOUG 88 and CHKG 92. The fourth line (Pesonen 67, Williams 67, Mowers 71) is the weakest assignment in the league per the coach. This closes the displayed toughness gap at zero cost.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla (36, 92 CHKG, $3.60M expiring) before March 19 to recover a pick before his value walks.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla's 83 displayed overall is form-depressed from his 85 base, but the key number is his $3.60M expiring salary at 36. The over-80 expiring pick-recovery mechanic applies. Eminger (21, POTE 99) is the long-term replacement.

recommendations.summary: Do not spend deadline currency on a faceoff centre; the game's faceoff mechanics are undecoded and the causal link to winning is unproven.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin 90 FACE, Chlup 75, Richards 70. The gap is real on the sheet but the GM already killed Bell/Doan as wing-based fixes. No centre at 85+ FACE is available cheaply. A first or second round pick is better spent on Havlat scoring.

recommendations.summary: Salo at 81 base and 70 CHKG is healthy depth who is not dressed; keep him available for injury cover on the blue line.
recommendations.rationale: With six defencemen on the roster (Kaberle, Svehla, Salo, McCabe, Fischer, Eminger), the playoff roster will need to carry five or six. Salo's 81 overall is the most underused asset on the blue line.

recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour, Svehla, and Roberts before March 19 to recover draft capital via the over-80 expiring mechanic; the club owns nothing better than a 4th-rounder today.
recommendations.rationale: Combined $12.80M in expiring salaries, combined age 113, combined POTE 157. Each qualifies for the pick-recovery trade. Recovering three picks in rounds 2-3 transforms the draft-capital position for the 2005-07 windows.

recommendations.current: Gaborik, Richards, Abid, Nash, Alexeev, Upshall, Chistov, Eminger, Colaiacovo, Kaberle
recommendations.summary: Re-sign all ten expiring young-core players at summer; Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, and Chistov on 5-6 years, the remainder on 3-4.
recommendations.rationale: Ten players worth $12.50M combined in expiring deals carry POTE 75-99 and produced 339 combined points this season. Letting even three of them walk at market price after breakout years costs multiple first-round picks to replace each.

recommendations.summary: Fischer at $3.70M for four more years is the worst contract on the roster (0.46 pts/g, POTE 90 unrealized) but cannot be renegotiated; revisit as trade bait in 2006 once his overall settles.
recommendations.rationale: No mid-contract renegotiation is possible. His POTE 90 at 24 means the production could still arrive. Building trade bait around him requires knowing his ceiling, which one more season will show.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Havlat from Ottawa for Tucker plus our 4th-rounder before March 19.
recommendations.rationale: Havlat is 87 base, 80 pts/63 GP, age 23, $900K expiring. Ottawa at 62 pts with 11 expiring deals cannot retain him. Tucker (29, 83 CHKG, in no unit) is a cost-free piece that helps Ottawa next season.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla before March 19 for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla is 36, $3.60M, 1 year remaining, over 80 overall. Any contender needing a top-four blueliner gives a pick for rental. We do not want him at renewal age.

recommendations.summary: If GM confirms the retirement hedge, trade Belfour for a young goalie on a reasonable salary before March 19.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 92 base, $6.50M, expiring, age 39. GM raised the possibility on Feb 21 as a hedge against retirement. Colorado wanted him and offered Hejduk. If not traded, he walks in July and we lose a pick-recovery asset worth $6.50M in salary relief.

recommendations.summary: Sign Gaborik to 5-6 years at season end before any bidding war.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base, age 23, 67 pts/45 GP pace, POTE 90, $1.10M. He is the most important contract on the roster and the cheapest star we will ever have at this price.

recommendations.summary: Sign Eminger to 5-6 years at season end.
