recommendations.rationale: Highest-upside available player in the league. ATL at 60 with 11 expiring cannot retain both. Toronto have no first-rounder so the package needs a player, but the GM protects current pieces. If ATL re-signs one, the other becomes reachable at lower cost.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Steve Begin from Buffalo: 84 TOUG, 92 CHKG, 81 FACE, 73 base, age 26, $936K, 2 years.
recommendations.rationale: Cheapest complete faceoff-plus-checking answer available. BUF at 61 points with 10 expiring are sellers. His production is unmeasurable this season but the grades at that price are the best available faceoff solution.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Jay Bouwmeester from Florida: 81 base, POTE 96, age 21, 22 pts/59 GP, $1.20M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Best young defenceman available. FLA at 52 points with 19 expiring is the NHL's most motivated seller. He closes nothing today but provides a decade of top-pair defence if he develops. Needs a meaningful package.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Barret Jackman from St. Louis: 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 80 base, age 23, $700K, 3 YEARS of control.
recommendations.rationale: Only elite-checking defenceman with multiple years of control. STL at 61 points with $56.63M payroll and $11.12M profit need to shed salary, but Jackman is cheap so their motivation is low. Requires attaching a salary dump like Svehla's $3.60M expiring to entice them.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker nightly instead of trading for toughness. His stored grades (84 TOUG, 88 CHKG) are the fourth body the coach flagged.
recommendations.rationale: The coverage phase's 'structural toughness gap' used today's displayed numbers. On stored grades, Toronto have six players at 80+ TOUG. Tucker at 84/88 in no unit is the free solution to the coach's injury-buffer concern. No trade needed.

recommendations.current: St. Jacques (D, 24, $0.80M, 2yr, 1 GP) + Safronov (D, 23, $0.90M, 3yr, 3 GP) + 4th round pick
recommendations.proposed: Komisarek (D, 23, $1.10M expiring, 69 pts/62 GP, 83 TOUG, 90 CHKG, POTE 90)
recommendations.summary: Trade two healthy-scratch defencemen and our only pick for the best player-to-cost ratio on the deadline board.
recommendations.rationale: MTL at 50 points with 15 expiring deals cannot re-sign Komisarek. Getting two young blueliners aged 23 and 24 plus a pick beats losing him for nothing in July. We shed $0.60M net and gain a 23-year-old with 69 points from the blue line.

recommendations.current: Chistov (LW, 21, $1.10M, 1yr, 16 pts/46 GP) + Upshall (RW, 21, $1.20M, 1yr, 17 pts/46 GP, CHKG 87)
recommendations.proposed: Mark Bell (C/LW, 24, $900K, 2yr, 83 FACE, 89 CHKG, 91 TOUG, 17.4 MPG)
recommendations.summary: Trade two young expiring forwards for a faceoff and checking specialist on a controllable deal.
recommendations.rationale: CHI at 51 points with 10 expiring deals and $24.65M profit are sellers. Bell's 83 FACE lifts our middle-six mean from 54 to above 70. We shed $1.40M net payroll. CHI gets two 21-year-olds with POTE 95 and 99 who can play bottom six immediately.

recommendations.proposed: A draft pick (round unknown; over-80 expiring mechanic)
recommendations.summary: Move Svehla for a draft pick before March 19 or lose the pick capital permanently in July.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla qualifies for the over-80 expiring mechanic. At 36 with a set ceiling his value peaks now. He is not protected by any standing order. $3.60M off payroll, a pick in return, no other asset required.

recommendations.summary: Owed item #2 is closed: Luongo is on our roster at 93, DiPietro is not sellable, and the GM has declared the goalie question solved.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo arrived February 6-7 and is our starter at 93 overall, 25 years old, 2 years and $1.60M. DiPietro at 79 base with a 3.65 GAA is not an acquisition target and NYI are not selling. No further action needed.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle and give him real minutes in the remaining 22 games; 4 GP at POTE 96 and age 20 is the worst waste on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: 4 games in 60 with no injury showing. Every week without a decision costs another game of development at his age.

recommendations.summary: Commit Spezza to a fixed fourth-line role at 10+ MPG for the final 22 games, or explicitly write off his development this season.
recommendations.rationale: 7.5 MPG, 0.41 pts/g, POTE 99, raised six times. The spot-duty pattern (play a game, scratch again) develops nobody. A clear plan either way is better than the current ambiguity.

recommendations.summary: Spacek at 9.7 MPG and trending up from 8.3 is acceptable; no further push needed this season.
recommendations.rationale: 19 points old, POTE 91, 0.43 pts/g, minutes rising. The GM's rotation philosophy explains the ceiling and the direction is right.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle every night for the remaining 22 games; he has 4 games under his belt now and needs volume.
recommendations.rationale: 0 points in 4 games at 17.8 MPG is acceptable at 20. The development plan requires at least 20 games before his first full off-season. Zero production is not the problem; zero games was.

recommendations.summary: Spezza gets 10+ MPG for the season run-in or is waived from the active roster; 5.3 MPG over 37 games is a wasted year at 21.
recommendations.rationale: Minutes collapsed from 9.1 to 5.3 while rate fell 0.43→0.38. The rotation philosophy has cost him 22 games worth of meaningful development this window. With 22 left, either the commitment changes or it needs to stop.

recommendations.summary: Same call as Spezza: Spacek needs 10+ MPG for the final 22 games or the development case for dressing him is dead.
recommendations.rationale: 0.55→0.38 pts/g, minutes down from 16.0 to 7.1. At 19, the season is nearly over and he has logged 7 minutes a night since December 1st.

recommendations.summary: Flag Klesla as a trade candidate if his season rate holds below 0.35 through the deadline. He is 22 and declining.
recommendations.rationale: 0.50→0.31 on flat minutes (14.9). At 22 the trend should be up. If it stays at 0.31 he is a third-pair defenceman, and his value is highest now before March confirms it.

recommendations.summary: No change. Chlup at 0.83 pts/g and 17.3 MPG is where he belongs and the trend is up.
recommendations.rationale: 0.62→0.83 pts/g, 11.0→17.3 MPG at 18 years old. He is arriving and needs stability, not tinkering.

recommendations.summary: Activate Spezza to the active roster in Spacek's slot; he needs 10+ MPG to stop bleeding morale.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza's morale is 86, the lowest on the team by 6 points, and has been flat at 7.5 MPG all season. At 21 with a 96 OVR he falls in the 17 MPG band and is receiving none of it. No other player on the roster is below 92.

recommendations.summary: All four lines, both power plays, and both kills are correctly built for the personnel available.
recommendations.rationale: L1 checks and scores, L2 scores and is matched against weaker opponents, L3 has speed and faceoffs, L4 checks and energizes. K1 has three of four best checkers plus the best faceoff man. P1 has the best shooter and puck-movers. No unit is taking a role it cannot fill.

recommendations.summary: Fourth-line faceoffs at 51 mean with nobody above 54 is a roster gap: four viable centres (Sundin 90, Chlup 79, Roberts 75, Richards 74) cannot cover five lines or cover injuries.
recommendations.rationale: L4 cannot win a defensive draw. If Richards goes down or is needed on a kill, L3 has no centre who can take a draw above 54. The trade deadline has passed but this is a summer priority: a third or fourth-line centre with 55%+ faceoffs.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo. 93 OVR against a 2.40-goal-per-game team is a routine night.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is at 93 OVR and 99 morale with no fatigue icon. MTL scores 2.40 per game and their last 10 shows 2-7-1. He should not be tested.

recommendations.summary: Keep all four forward lines as they are. Every unit outclasses its MTL counterpart.
recommendations.rationale: MTL's top line is 78/78/74 OVR. Our second line (88/84/84) is better than their first. No line-matching problem exists.

recommendations.summary: Keep the defensive pair order as is. Every auto-pairing favours us.
recommendations.rationale: MTL's best D pair (Komisarek 80, Markov 79) faces our top line (Roberts 86, Sundin 89, Gaborik 96). Shuffling would only weaken a mismatch that already goes our way.

recommendations.summary: If the GM wants to develop anyone, give Spacek more of the game tonight against a 16-35 opponent.
recommendations.rationale: MTL is 2-7-1 in their last 10 and scores 2.40 per game. Spacek at 75 OVR and 96 morale will face their third and fourth lines (Juneau 74, Gratton 69). Low-risk development minutes.

recommendations.summary: Defenceman sell list unchanged: McCabe first (0.40 pts/g since Jan 26 at 29 on $3M/4yr), Salo second ($2.6M/2yr, 0.32 pts/g at 30), Colaiacovo third (0.39, $1.1M expiring). Eminger off the list per Feb 19 finding.
recommendations.rationale: McCabe has added 4 points in 10 games since the Jan 26 checkpoint (0.40 rate vs 0.96 season at that time). The decline is not a blip. Eminger's recent window cleared 0.50 per the Feb 19 check and stands.

recommendations.proposed: Spezza at 12+ MPG on third line
recommendations.summary: Move Spezza back in and give him 12+ minutes; his morale at 86 is the only one below 90 among young players and his 0.41 pts/g rate justifies it.
recommendations.rationale: 37 GP at 7.5 MPG and 15 points for a 21-year-old with POTE 99 is wasted. His morale at 86 is the evidence that it is costing him. Sixth time raised.

recommendations.summary: Give Stahle a consistent spot on the third pair for the remaining 23 games; 4 GP at POTE 96 is the second-worst development situation on the roster after Spezza.
recommendations.rationale: 17.8 MPG in the 4 games he played shows the coaching staff trusts him when he goes out. He just needs the opportunity more often. 23 games left is the window before offseason planning.

recommendations.summary: Push Alexeev to 10+ minutes; his 0.55 pts/g rate on 8.3 MPG outproduces Koltsov on more ice.
recommendations.rationale: 30 points in 55 games at 23 — the development window is closing but the production is real. A marginal bump costs nothing to the line structure.

recommendations.summary: Smirnov stays scratched. POTE 70 at 20 does not earn games over anyone on this roster.
recommendations.rationale: Lowest potential grade among the young group. The scratch is correct and costs nothing developmentally.

recommendations.summary: Leave Spacek at 10 MPG on the fourth line. His 0.44 pts/g rate on 10 minutes is appropriate for a 19-year-old given the fourth line's endurance ceiling.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 91 at 19 does not demand more than fourth-line minutes yet. Pushing him past the L4 stamina limit (mean endurance 51) would hurt everyone on the line.

recommendations.summary: Plan Chlup as a top-six centre for next season; his 0.83 recent rate on 17 MPG at age 18 is a genuine breakout.
recommendations.rationale: 0.62→0.83 pts/g and 11→17 MPG simultaneously means both trust and production are climbing together. That is the rarest development pattern and it deserves a named role in the offseason plan.

recommendations.summary: Sell McCabe at the deadline; 0.49 recent pts/g at 29 on four years and $3M is the clearest exit on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: 1.42→0.49 is not a slump, it is the end of a production level. No February recovery has materialized. His trade value falls every game he plays at this rate.

recommendations.summary: Move Koltsov before the deadline; 0.28 recent pts/g at 23 means his trade value is vanishing.
recommendations.rationale: GM has him as a chip, and a chip that scored 0.28 per game in 25 recent outings fetches less each week. The 1.10 start is gone.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza 12+ MPG or a full scratch; 5.3 MPG at 0.38 rate with POTE 99 is wasted development time in his final young season.
recommendations.rationale: Rate fell from 0.43 to 0.38 while minutes fell from 9.1 to 5.3. He is neither developing nor contributing. The gap between these is the worst outcome.

recommendations.summary: Resolve Spacek: return to 12+ MPG or full scratch. At 19 his rate collapsed alongside his minutes (0.55→0.40, 16→7.4 MPG).
recommendations.rationale: He was producing at 0.55 as a 19-year-old on 16 MPG before being benched. Losing both ice time and confidence simultaneously is the worst development scenario.

recommendations.summary: Eminger is recovered and not a sell; recent window is 0.57 pts/g on 17.8 MPG, well above the 0.45 threshold set in January.
recommendations.rationale: First 23 games at 0.35, recent 21 at 0.57. The trade threshold is no longer relevant to his case. Keep developing him on the top pair.

recommendations.summary: Consider moving Alexeev if a fit emerges; 0.62→0.48 with minutes cut from 11 to 6 shows he is outside the plans at 23.
recommendations.rationale: Falling out of the lineup at 23 with a declining rate means his value is highest right now. Not urgent but worth monitoring for the right offer.

recommendations.summary: Watch Klesla closely in February; 0.50→0.31 at 22 on steady minutes suggests the game has caught up to him.
recommendations.rationale: A second-year defenceman going the wrong direction at 22 while getting the same ice is a structural problem, not a slump. If he stays under 0.35 through February he is depth, not a prospect.

recommendations.summary: Either return Spezza to the lineup at 10+ MPG in games we can afford or accept the full scratch; 7.5 MPG keeps him at 86 morale which costs 1 point on his overall.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza's 7.5 MPG is below the 10-MPG band for his calibre at 21. His morale of 86 (lowest on the roster) applies a -1 penalty to his displayed grade. Raised five times without movement; this is the last raise before I stop.

recommendations.summary: No other player needs a minutes adjustment for morale. The room sits at 92 or above across the board.
recommendations.rationale: The first line (Sundin, Gaborik, Roberts) at 96 are well above their expected minutes. Richards at 16.8 MPG and 96 morale is comfortable. Everyone else is at 99.

recommendations.summary: No change to L1 — Gaborik (98/99/99 scoring/playmaking/speed), Sundin (91 faceoffs), Roberts (84 checking) with McCabe and Fischer behind is the best-balanced unit we have.
recommendations.rationale: Every role is covered at a high level on this line. Breaking it for anything is a downgrade.

recommendations.summary: L2 stays as built despite 66 checking mean — Mogilny (94 scoring) and Afinogenov (92 playmaking) are there to score, and swapping them for checkers would gut our secondary offense.
recommendations.rationale: The checking weakness is a usage problem (auto-pairing puts D pair 2 with L2), not a personnel problem. The GM should watch where this line goes in the first period and pull it off the ice against Washington's top pair.

recommendations.summary: We have exactly four players with checking 83+ (Roberts, McCabe, Fischer, Abid) and they're spread across PK1, PK2, PP1 and two forward lines simultaneously — no injury buffer exists.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts and McCabe each appear on three units (even strength, a PK, and the PP). One injury and we have no fifth checker to backfill.

recommendations.summary: Only four players win faceoffs above 75 (Sundin 91, Chlup 80, Roberts 76, Richards 75). Our L4 faceoff unit is 54 mean — we lose every draw they take.
recommendations.rationale: Against Washington's centers, our bottom-six will be pinned in our own zone by draw losses. No in-house fix exists.

recommendations.summary: K2 stays as-is — Abid (83 checking) is the only upgrade available but removing him from L4 guts the only physical presence on our fourth line.
recommendations.rationale: McCabe carries K2 at 84 checking. Abid would add a second real checker but L4 (faceoff mean 54, toughness 61 mean) becomes toothless without him. The tradeoff isn't worth it for one game.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo in net against Washington.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 94 OVR is the only goalie who matches Kolzig at 93. The Jan 15 standing order says maximize quality against quality opponents, and Washington with Jagr (90) and Kolzig (93) qualifies.

recommendations.summary: Lines stay as they are. Our top three lines out-grade theirs on paper and the auto-pairing already puts Fischer/McCabe against Gonchar/Witt.
recommendations.rationale: Combined OVR of our lines 2 and 3 (505) versus theirs (468) is a 37-point gap. Washington's PP converts at 12%, so the PK needs no adjustment. No matchup-driven change exists that improves on what we already have.

recommendations.summary: Shop McCabe at the deadline: 0.86 pts/g in 59 games is a tradeable number at 29, but $3M x 4 makes him hard to move.
recommendations.rationale: Season rate continues sliding from 0.89 (Feb 12) to 0.86. At 29 with four years remaining, the window for return value is closing. Best to sell while the number still reads top-pair.

recommendations.summary: Trade Eminger at the deadline. 0.45 pts/g at 21 on an expiring $1.2M deal is a clean sell.
recommendations.rationale: Rate has been frozen at 0.45 since Feb 6 with no recovery. Expiring cheap deal on a 21-year-old with 20 points is the most movable asset on the blue line.

recommendations.summary: Colaiacovo is the secondary sell: 0.39 pts/g at 22, $1.1M expiring, already out of the lineup.
recommendations.rationale: 12 points in 31 games. Not dressing. Same profile as Eminger but less production. Clean deadline asset.

recommendations.summary: Salo is cut material: 0.33 pts/g, 30 years old, $2.6M x 2, not dressing.
recommendations.rationale: 8 points in 24 games. Not in the lineup. Two years and $2.6M of dead cap for zero contribution.

recommendations.summary: Toughness is the only gap that cannot be fixed internally: the roster's ceiling is Roberts at 73. Chara closes it with a 94 TOUG, 95 CHKG defenceman from a 52-point seller with 11 expiring deals.
recommendations.rationale: Zero players at 80+ TOUG on 28 skaters. Tucker at 70 is the best available internal option and still 10 below the threshold. Chara is 27, $1.70M expiring, producing 54 pts/56 GP — he closes checking and toughness and adds top-pair offence simultaneously.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker (83 CHKG) and Svehla (83 CHKG) into units for the remaining 23 games; three players with 80+ checking currently sit in no unit while Roberts at 38 carries the load.
recommendations.rationale: The coach's report flags Stahle at 3 appearances as the development priority, but the roster already has three 80+ checkers unused. Tucker at 29 and $1.30M is the floor toughness option; Svehla at 36 adds 83 CHKG and 94 ENDU on a cheap deal.

recommendations.summary: The faceoff gap (one 80+ player, next read 75) is thin but not actionable at the deadline: the GM's Jan 25 order killed Bell because both are wings, and Avery's 6 pts in 57 GP does not justify the cost for faceoffs alone.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin at 90 FACE carries the draw load. Chlup at 75 is the backup and takes draws when matched against softer centres. The gap is real but the only identified solutions are either wings (Bell, killed) or production failures (Avery). Better to accept 75 FACE on the second draw than spend capital on a 93 FACE with zero offence.

recommendations.summary: Belfour's 18-3, 2.27 GAA, 0.916 SV makes him the most valuable expiring asset on the roster via the over-80 pick-recovery mechanic. Decision needed by March 19 or the capital is lost.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 91 base, 40 GP is the starter with 2 years left. Belfour at 39 and $6.50M expiring has no path to a roster spot next year. Either he is playoff insurance for a cup run or he is a first-round pick. Both cannot be true.

recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour (92 base, $6.50M, expiring) for a draft pick before March 19 using the over-80 expiring mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: His 18-3, 2.27 GAA, 0.916 SP makes him the best rental on the market. Luongo is the starter. $6.50M recovered as a pick rather than $0 in July.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla (36, 85 base, $3.60M, expiring) via the over-80 expiring mechanic before July.
recommendations.rationale: 36 games, 24 points, scratched from the lineup. No role next season. $3.60M walks in July unless converted to a pick first.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik (23, 77 pts, $1.10M expiring, POTE 90) on a 5-6 year deal at renewal.
recommendations.rationale: Highest-scoring player on the roster. At $1.10M he is 7x underpriced for a 77-point winger. Locking him before July avoids a bidding war that could cost two first-rounders.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards (24, 55 pts, $1.00M expiring, POTE 88) on a 5-6 year deal at renewal.
recommendations.rationale: 55 points at 24 on a $1.00M deal. He is the future first-line centre with Sundin gone in five years. Losing him for nothing is the worst outcome available.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash (20, 32 pts, $1.20M expiring, POTE 95) on a 5-6 year deal at renewal.
recommendations.rationale: 32 points at 20 with POTE 95. His price doubles the moment he puts up 50 the next year. Lock him now at the $1.20M anchor.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger (21, POTE 99, $1.20M expiring) on a 5-year deal at renewal.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 at 21 with 44 games played. He is the single highest-upside defenceman on the roster. His contract expires the same summer as his first full season; lock him before he prices himself.

recommendations.summary: Fischer ($3.70M, 4yr, 0.48 ppg) is a sunk cost. Do not try to move him now.
recommendations.rationale: No club takes $3.70M for four years of a 24-year-old with declining production. He becomes trade-bait in summer 2008 if his POTE 90 ever translates. Absorb him; do not compound the loss by giving away a pick to dump him.

recommendations.summary: Move Roberts (38, $2.70M, expiring) via the over-80 expiring mechanic before July.
recommendations.rationale: 64 points in 59 games at 38 is productive but not repeatable. $2.70M converts to a pick rather than $0. He stays for the playoff run if needed, but the conversation opens in March.

recommendations.summary: Move Belfour before March 19 for a pick, a young defenceman, or as the centrepiece of a Chara package; he walks for nothing in July.
recommendations.rationale: 92 base, $6.50M expiring, only over-80 pick-recovery asset. Luongo (91 base, 2yr) is the starter. No trades after March 19.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla at the deadline for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic; he will not be re-signed at 36 on $3.60M.
recommendations.rationale: 36 years old, $3.60M expiring, above 80 overall. Kaberle, Eminger, Colaiacovo and Stahle are the defensive future. Walking in July wastes his value.

recommendations.summary: Move Roberts at the deadline for a pick or high-potential youth; at 38 and $2.70M he is not part of next season's plan.
recommendations.rationale: 38 years old, $2.70M expiring, over-80 mechanic applies. Mogilny is already declining at 35; the wing rotation goes young.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Chara before March 19: 27, 94 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 54 pts/56 GP, $1.70M expiring from a 52-point seller.
recommendations.rationale: Closes the toughness and checking gaps the coach flags and adds top-pair offence. Fund through Belfour rather than a first-round pick we do not own.

recommendations.summary: Sign Gaborik to 5-6 years on the day his contract opens; 91 base, 67 pts/45 GP, POTE 90, age 23 at $1.10M.
recommendations.rationale: Most urgent renewal on the roster. A bidding war in July against a player of his production and age is the worst outcome.

recommendations.summary: Sign Kaberle to 5-6 years; 26 years old, $1.90M, the defensive anchor for the next five.
recommendations.rationale: Core D at his prime age. Losing him in July would gut the blueline depth.

recommendations.summary: Sign Eminger to 5-6 years; 21 years old, POTE 99, the highest-potential defenceman on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: The GM vetoed Chara over Eminger in January because the 21-year-old with POTE 99 fits the timeline. At 21 with one year left he is vulnerable to offer sheets in July.

recommendations.summary: Sign Richards to 5-6 years; 24, C, $1.00M, the centre of the next window.
recommendations.rationale: At $1.00M and 24 the cost is trivial relative to his role. Lock him alongside Gaborik and Kaberle.

recommendations.summary: Sign Nash to 5-6 years; 20 years old, LW, $1.20M, entering his development window on an expiring deal.
recommendations.rationale: Age 20 on a one-year deal is the worst possible position. He is either a core piece or a trade chip; do not let him walk.

recommendations.summary: Sign Alexeev to 2-3 years; 23, RW, producing 0.55 pts/g, earning a top-nine role next season.
recommendations.rationale: Coach says he has earned 11-12 minutes when dressed. Two or three years gives time to see if he makes the jump without over-committing.

recommendations.summary: Sign Abid to 2-3 years at $0.40M; 24, 80 TOUG, 80 CHKG, the cheapest physicality available.
recommendations.rationale: Forty thousand for a 24-year-old enforcer who fills the toughness gap the coach flags. No reason to let him walk.

recommendations.summary: Sign Tellqvist to 2 years at $0.80M as Luongo's backup; 25, POTE in the high 90s, needs game time.
recommendations.rationale: The January standing order says give him time to develop. Two years with Luongo ahead is the right structure.

recommendations.summary: Let Smirnov go in July; 20 years old, zero games this season, the rotation has passed him over.
recommendations.rationale: Coach's February report: zero games all season at 20. Four more months without a shift does not develop anyone.

recommendations.summary: Do not renew Upshall or Colaiacovo yet; decide by April based on February-March production and draft-capital needs.
recommendations.rationale: Upshall at $1.20M for depth with unproven production; Colaiacovo is behind Eminger and Stahle on the D depth chart. Both are better used as deadline bait than re-signed.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Chara (OTT, D, 27, 94 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 54 pts/56 GP, $1.70M expiring) from a 57-point seller for Tucker plus Chistov plus the 4th, keeping Eminger untouched.
recommendations.rationale: Closes the toughness gap at its ceiling (94 vs our best of 73) and adds top-pair offence. OTT at 57 pts with 11 expiring cannot re-sign him and have no leverage. The January veto was about giving up Eminger; this price does not.

recommendations.summary: If Chara is not available at this price, pursue Bell (CHI, C, 24, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, $900K, 2yr) for Colaiacovo plus Safronov.
recommendations.rationale: Bell closes toughness, checking, and faceoffs in one move on a two-year deal with two years remaining. CHI at 51 pts with 10 expiring is rebuilding. The GM's Jan 25 veto was on the faceoff-only argument; the toughness and checking case is separate.

recommendations.summary: Komisarek (MTL, D, 23, 83 TOUG, 66 pts/58 GP, $1.10M expiring, POTE 90) is the best value on the board from MTL at 48 pts with 15 expiring deals.
recommendations.rationale: 83 TOUG raises the toughness ceiling, 66 points at 23 as a defenceman is first-pair offence, POTE 90 says he is not finished. MTL cannot re-sign him and will take young bodies or picks at almost any price.

recommendations.summary: Thornton (BOS, C, 25, 91 base, 82 TOUG, 80 FACE, 66 pts/40 GP, $4.00M expiring) is the most complete player available but BOS at 65 pts may not sell before late February.
recommendations.rationale: Closes toughness and faceoffs while adding 1.65 pts/g. At $4.00M he is a rental unless we extend. BOS profit of $28.17M means no financial pressure to deal; acceptance requires them to fall out of the race by mid-March.

recommendations.summary: Conroy (CGY, C, 31, 94 FACE, 63 pts, $2.00M expiring) from the worst team in the league (48 pts) fills the faceoff gap for a playoff run at minimum cost.
recommendations.rationale: 94 FACE is the second-best read available behind only Sundin. CGY at 48 pts with 10 expiring will deal him for Chistov plus the 4th. He does not close toughness but he is the cheapest fix for the faceoff cliff.

recommendations.summary: Kudroc (FLA, D, 28, 80 TOUG, 76 base, 30 pts/52 GP, $1.00M expiring, POTE 90) is a cheap toughness option from FLA's 19-player expiring class.
recommendations.rationale: 80 TOUG meets our threshold at the defenceman position. POTE 90 at 28 with 30 points suggests he has been underused. FLA at 50 pts with 19 expiring deals are in full teardown and will accept depth pieces.

recommendations.summary: Marleau (SJ, C, 25, 89 base, 78 pts/50 GP, $1.60M expiring) is the highest-production available player and replaces the declining Mogilny (0.87 pts/g) at first line.
recommendations.rationale: 78 points at 25 on a $1.60M expiring deal is the best production-to-cost ratio in the league. SJ at 55 pts with 14 expiring cannot keep him. Cost conflicts with the ATL Kovalchuk pursuit; choose one star target.

recommendations.summary: Savard (ATL, C, 27, 89 FACE, 48 pts/43 GP, $1.00M expiring) is the cheaper faceoff option if ATL deal him as a throw-in to the Kovalchuk or Heatley conversation.
recommendations.rationale: 89 FACE at $1.00M is half the salary of Conroy for similar faceoff value. ATL at 60 pts is in the race so they may keep him, but with 11 expiring and two stars they cannot retain everyone. Fold into any ATL negotiation.

recommendations.proposed: A draft pick (2nd or 3rd round) from a contender needing playoff goalie insurance
recommendations.summary: Move Belfour to a playoff team for a mid-round pick before March 19; Luongo is confirmed starter and Belfour's 18-3, 2.27 GAA, 0.916 SP value peaks now and dies on that date.
recommendations.rationale: The over-80 expiring mechanic converts him to a pick without requiring a hockey fit. No contender has a goalie above 93 who is also cheap and available. They add a quality backup for two months; we harvest pick capital from a contract we cannot re-sign and do not need. Payroll effect: minus $6.50M for us, plus $6.50M for them over 23 games.

recommendations.current: Tucker (29, $1.30M, 2yr, 3 GP, not lined) + St. Jacques (24, $0.80M, 2yr, 1 GP, POTE 94, surplus D) + 4th-round pick
recommendations.proposed: Chara (OTT, D, 27, 94 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 54 pts/56 GP, $1.70M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Give Tucker plus St. Jacques plus the 4th for Chara; closes the 21-point toughness gap (73 to 94) and adds 54 points of top-pair offence from a seller at 57 points.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 57 points with 11 expiring deals and $27.44M profit are in teardown and cannot re-sign him. They get two bodies (Tucker at 88 TOUG/92 CHKG shown, St. Jacques at 24 with POTE 94 and 84 CHKG) plus a marginal pick. Neither player is in the coach's lineup. Payroll: we give $2.10M and get $1.70M back, net minus $0.40M. Acceptance uncertain — OTT may prefer to keep him for the remaining games rather than rebuild now.

recommendations.current: Tucker (29, $1.30M, 2yr, 3 GP, not lined) + Safronov (23, $0.90M, 3yr, 3 GP, POTE 91, surplus D) + 4th-round pick
recommendations.proposed: Komisarek (MTL, D, 23, 83 TOUG, 66 pts/58 GP, POTE 90, $1.10M expiring)
recommendations.summary: If Chara does not land, give Tucker plus Safronov plus the 4th for Komisarek; 10 fewer toughness points than Chara but from a deeper teardown (MTL at 48 points, 15 expiring) at lower cost and one year younger.
recommendations.rationale: MTL cannot re-sign him and are in full rebuild collecting assets. Tucker gives them a veteran body, Safronov (23, POTE 91) is young D depth for their pipeline. We shed $1.10M net. Less impactful than Chara on the playoff run but more likely to be accepted given MTL's desperation. Mutually exclusive with Chara — same Tucker, same 4th.

recommendations.summary: Goalie acquisition task is complete; Luongo at 94 base is the answer, DiPietro is not available. Shift focus to moving Belfour before March 19.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is 40 GP, 2.87 GAA, 0.877 SV% on two years at $1.60M. DiPietro is 43 GP for NYI, 2.97 GAA, 0.870 SV% at 21 with POTE 99; they will not deal their starter. The only live goalie decision is Belfour's pick recovery before the deadline.

recommendations.summary: Chara is the only player who closes the zero-toughness gap; no internal fix exists.
recommendations.rationale: The roster has zero skaters above 80 TOUG (best is Roberts 73). Chara at 94 TOUG and 95 CHKG from a 52-point seller with 11 expiring deals is the single acquisition that solves the club's one structural hole.

recommendations.summary: Avery closes both the faceoff gap and the checking gap in one transaction at $400K for two years.
recommendations.rationale: Only Sundin (90 FACE) is above 80; Spacek and Chlup cannot win draws. Avery at 93 FACE and 88 CHKG is the cheapest player on the board covering two gaps simultaneously, from a 48-point LA club with 13 expiring deals.

recommendations.summary: Dress Svehla on the third pair; his 83 CHKG and 94 ENDU are the checking depth the coach says he lacks.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla is not in any unit despite carrying the third-highest checking grade on the roster. At 36 he is a season stopgap, not a plan, but he fills the immediate gap without a trade.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker nightly; 83 CHKG is the second-best checking grade on the roster and the coach reports a checking gap.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker has played 3 games all season. His 83 CHKG trails only Roberts (86) and McCabe (86). The coach flags a bottom-six checking gap; the fix is already on the roster and sitting out.

recommendations.summary: Scoring, playmaking, speed and clutch are all covered; no acquisition needed in these roles.
recommendations.rationale: Twelve skaters at 80+ in scoring and playmaking. Gaborik at 92/23 and Afinogenov at 90/25 are the future top two once the aging trio step down. The decline is real but the succession is in place.

recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour ($6.50M), Svehla ($3.60M) and Roberts ($2.70M) before March 19 using the over-80 expiring mechanic; recovers draft capital Toronto lacks and frees $12.80M.
recommendations.rationale: All three are 34+ with declining production and expiring deals. Without removing them, July re-signing the young core at market rates exceeds revenue. Belfour at 92 base is the peak-value rental; Svehla at 80+ and Roberts at 80+ qualify for the same pick-recovery mechanic.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik ($1.10M, 77 pts, POTE 90), Abid ($0.40M, 63 pts, POTE 94), Nash ($1.20M, 32 pts, POTE 95) and Richards ($1.00M, 55 pts, POTE 88) on five or six year deals this July.
recommendations.rationale: These four are the production core of the next three seasons at combined salaries of $3.70M. Their current prices are rookie-window artifacts; a bidding war in July doubles or triples them. Five-year locks at $2.5-4M each are below what the trade market would demand.

recommendations.summary: Sign Chistov, Eminger, Colaiacovo, Alexeev and Kaberle to three or four year deals to stagger renewals across 2007-08 and prevent a second contract cluster.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 95-99 on three of them makes them future trade assets if they develop, so locking at current prices ($1.10-1.90M) is the cheapest way to retain them. Three or four years prevents the 2008 renewal wave from colliding with Fischer's contract and the second-tier stars.

recommendations.summary: Move Belfour to Ottawa for Chara before March 19; if Ottawa declines, take a draft pick via the over-80 mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 92 base, $6.50M, expiring, 39, and we have Luongo as #1. His trade value peaks now (18-3 last playoffs, 2.27 GAA). After March 19 no trades are possible and the capital walks. Ottawa at 52 pts with 11 expiring deals needs a playoff goalie.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla (84 base, 36, $3.60M expiring) for a draft pick before March 19.
recommendations.rationale: Over-80 expiring asset. At 36 we are not re-signing him. Eminger at 21 with POTE 99 and Colaiacovo at 22 fill the minutes. Keeping him past the deadline loses the pick opportunity permanently.

recommendations.summary: Move Roberts (87 base, 38, $2.70M expiring) for a draft pick before March 19.
recommendations.rationale: Over-80 expiring asset. Production has fallen from 1.29 to 0.97 pts/g and he is 38. Koltsov at 1.09 ppg at 23 with 92 speed is his successor. No re-signing scenario exists at 38.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Sean Avery from LA for Tucker; closes the bottom-six checking-centre gap the Coach has flagged since January.
recommendations.rationale: Avery brings 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG at $400K for 2 years, age 25. LA at 48 pts with 13 expiring deals is a seller. Tucker is $1.30M, 83 CHKG, and currently in no unit — zero on-ice loss.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik on 5-6 years the day his contract opens (July).
recommendations.rationale: 91 base, 67 pts/45 GP, POTE 90, age 23, $1.10M. He is the most dangerous player we lose if a bidding war opens. No mid-contract extension is possible; July is the first and only window before free agency.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle on 5-6 years.
recommendations.rationale: Age 26, $1.90M, top-pair defenceman entering his prime. Star on the manual's 5-6 year rule.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash on 5-6 years.
recommendations.rationale: Age 20, $1.20M. Young winger with a long development runway; the roster needs him locked before his next contract ratchets.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger on 5-6 years.
recommendations.rationale: Age 21, POTE 99, $1.20M. The GM's explicit development priority over Chara at 27. Lock him long.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards on 5 years.
recommendations.rationale: Age 24, $1.00M, centre prospect. Young core lock per the staggered-renewal plan.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Tellqvist on 2 years as Luongo's backup.
recommendations.rationale: Age 25, 77 base, $0.80M. GM's Jan 15 order stands: give him time to develop. Two years keeps the cost low and preserves flexibility.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bell from Chicago as the primary deadline target: 91 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 83 FACE at $900K on two years closes all three structural gaps in one body at age 24.
recommendations.rationale: Bell is the only available player who fills toughness, checking and faceoffs simultaneously on a re-signable deal. CHI at 50 pts with 10 expiring contracts is a seller. Package: Colaiacovo (POTE 99, 21) plus Safronov. Eminger fills Colaiacovo's defensive slot internally.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Jackman from St. Louis as the best long-term toughness defenceman available: 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 29 pts/57 GP at 23 years old, $700K with three years remaining.
recommendations.rationale: Jackman is the only tough defenceman with three years of control left at $700K. STL at 56 pts with 9 expiring are not contending. Package: fourth-rounder plus Chistov or Safronov. His 29 points from the blue line at 23 is above-average offensive for a stay-at-home.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Chara from Ottawa at 85 base, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 55 pts/59 GP, $1.70M expiring, age 27 — the highest-value single rental a contender will accept in February.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 55 pts with 11 expiring deals is the ideal seller. Chara provides elite toughness and 55 points from the D position simultaneously. Attempt double acquisition with Havlat to give OTT more youth in return.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Komisarek from Montreal: 77 base but 66 points in 59 games at age 23 on $1.10M expiring with POTE 90. MTL at 48 pts cannot re-sign him.
recommendations.rationale: 66 points from a 23-year-old defenceman is the highest offensive output on the D-side board. His overall understates his game. Package: St. Jacques plus Safronov plus fourth-rounder. POTE 90 means re-signing him locks a top-pair defenceman for five years.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Conroy from Calgary as the rental faceoff centre: 85 base, 87 FACE, 70 pts/58 GP, $2.00M expiring, age 33. CGY at 46 pts is the worst team in the league.
recommendations.rationale: 70 points at 87 FACE is the best faceoff production on the board. Pure rental — 33 and expiring — but fills the gap for the playoff run. Cost: Chistov plus fourth-rounder. Only pursue if Bell falls through or we want depth beyond him.

recommendations.summary: Monitor Bates from NY Islanders: 94 FACE, 79 CHKG, 83 base, $900K expiring, age 29. Best faceoff grade in the league at the cheapest price.
recommendations.rationale: 94 FACE is the highest in the league. $900K is negligible. Only 30 pts in 43 GP but he is a specialist, not a scorer. NYI at 59 pts may be in the race and unwilling to sell. Check their position in late February before engaging.

recommendations.summary: Attach Savard from Atlanta to any ATL package as a faceoff add-on: 88 FACE, 58 pts/56 GP, $1.00M expiring, age 27.
recommendations.rationale: Savard folds into any Kovalchuk or Heatley conversation at no extra pick cost. ATL at 56 pts with 11 expiring will deal him. At 58 points for $1M he is below-market production.

recommendations.summary: Attach Havlat from Ottawa to the Chara conversation: 87 base, 75 pts/59 GP, $900K, age 23, POTE 86. Gives OTT more youth in return.
recommendations.rationale: 75 points at 23 for $900K is the best production-to-salary ratio on the board. OTT rebuilding at 55 pts will value youth over one more expiring contract. Double acquisition with Chara maximises OTT's return and gives Toronto top-six scoring.

recommendations.summary: Deprioritise Avery: his grades (90 FACE, 84 CHKG, 79 TOUG) are elite but his production is 6 points in 57 games at age 24. Do not spend a roster asset on 0.11 points per game.
recommendations.rationale: The earlier January note flagged him as a three-gap target on grades alone. The February production (6 pts in 57 GP) contradicts that. At $400K he is cheap to acquire but questionable to dress ahead of players who produce. Keep as a depth option only if Bell and Jackman both fail.

recommendations.summary: Kovalchuk (ATL, 97 pts/56 GP at 21, $1.10M expiring) remains the highest-scoring player on the board but requires a first-round pick or a core piece we will not give up. Do not chase without ATL signalling a fire sale.
recommendations.rationale: 97 points at 21 is the ceiling. But ATL at 56 pts has no pressure to sell immediately, and we own no pick better than a fourth-rounder. The package would need St. Jacques, Nash, or Gaborik, none of which the GM will trade. Dead unless ATL drops their ask.

recommendations.summary: Heatley (ATL, 91 base, 88 pts/53 GP, $1.10M expiring, age 24, POTE 86) faces the same constraint as Kovalchuk: no pick capital to fund the deal. Monitor only.
recommendations.rationale: 88 points at 24 with POTE 86 is elite. But ATL at 56 pts and our lack of picks beyond a fourth rounder makes this unreachable. If ATL rebuilds and asks for players only, revisit in March.

recommendations.proposed: Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 80 base, 91 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 83 FACE, $900K, 2yr)
recommendations.summary: Open CHI for Bell at Colaiacovo plus Safronov; Eminger fills Colaiacovo's slot internally.
recommendations.rationale: Bell closes the TOUG/FACE/CHKG gaps simultaneously at $900K through 2006-07. CHI at 50 pts with 10 expiring contracts is a seller; they collect a POTE 99 D at 22. Payroll impact: net save $1.10M on our side, CHI takes on $2.00M in salaries they can absorb (profitable at $26M). Acceptance uncertain — CHI is profitable and may want more.

recommendations.proposed: Chara (OTT, D, 27, 85 base, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 55 pts/59 GP, $1.70M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Offer OTT the Tucker+Salo dead-salary package for Chara as a two-month rental.
recommendations.rationale: Chara's 90 TOUG and 91 CHKG with 55 points is the single best gap-filler in the league and the only external answer to the toughness problem (nobody above 73 on our roster). OTT at 55 pts with 11 expiring deals is a seller; they gain $3.90M in two-year salaries they can use for roster depth or simply absorb. We dump $3.90M of dead weight (Tucker 1 pt in 3 GP, Salo scratched) for $1.70M of elite production. This does not involve Eminger and respects the Jan 19 veto. Acceptance uncertain — OTT at 55 points may not be desperate enough.

recommendations.proposed: Draft pick (minimum) plus a useful player from a contender needing playoff goalie insurance
recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour to a 1-3 seed with a shaky backup before March 19; minimum ask is the over-80 expiring pick.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour's 21-game sample (18-3, 2.27 GAA, .916 SP) makes him the best playoff goalie on the rental market. After March 19 he walks and we lose 92 base plus a pick for nothing. Luongo at 91 base with 2 years left makes him redundant. Payroll: $6.50M saved immediately. The over-80 expiring mechanic guarantees at least a draft pick if no player package materialises. This is the single deadline action with the most certain payoff.

recommendations.summary: Close the DiPietro/Luongo monitoring task. Luongo is here, DiPietro's development is healthy but irrelevant to our roster.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 91 base, 25, $1.60M with 2 years is the franchise goalie. DiPietro at 79 base / 2.94 GAA / 41 GP is a step below him at the same age, and we have no roster need a 79-base goalie fills.

recommendations.summary: Stahle needs regular games in these final 24; POTE 96 at 20 on 3 appearances is the biggest development gap on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: 3 GP in 58 games at POTE 96. When he played he got 20 MPG, so the coaching staff sees him as a top-pair option. He needs at least 15+ games by season's end to make the investment meaningful.

recommendations.summary: Spezza at POTE 99 and 21 needs 12+ MPG or a full season scratch; 7.5 MPG and a morale of 86 is the worst position on this roster.
recommendations.rationale: 15 points in 37 games on 7.5 MPG. Morale 86 is the lowest of any young player. The ice-time bands say a player at his calibre expects 17 minutes. The season is closing; either give him real minutes now or the year is wasted.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev is producing 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG; when he is dressed he has earned 11-12 minutes minimum.
recommendations.rationale: 30 points in 55 games on 8.3 minutes a night is the most efficient rate among the young players. At POTE 94 and 23, promoting his minutes would test whether he's a top-nine forward. No change to who dresses, just more ice when he's in.

recommendations.summary: Smirnov at POTE 70 and zero games is a fair reflection of his standing; he should not displace Stahle or Spezza for a look.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 70 is the lowest ceiling in the young group. At 20 with no games, the priority is Stahle (POTE 96) and Spezza (POTE 99) who are being underused despite higher files.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza 12+ MPG for the remaining games or stop carrying him as a development project.
recommendations.rationale: 5.3 MPG since December 1, rate at 0.38, POTE 99 at 21. Raised five times with no movement. At this rate he is a wasted year regardless of potential.

recommendations.summary: Plan around Chlup as a top-six winger for next season — he has outgrown a fourth-line role at 18.
recommendations.rationale: 0.79 pts/g on 16.9 MPG since December 1, up from 0.62 on 11.0 before. Both production and trust climbing simultaneously at 18. No grade change needed to see this.

recommendations.summary: Koltsov's trade value has collapsed to nothing; if he's still a chip, move him this week or accept him as a fourth-liner.
recommendations.rationale: Recent window 0.29 pts/g in 24 games after a 1.10 hot start in 10 games. Nobody pays for 0.29. The chip value the GM wanted in January is gone.

recommendations.summary: McCabe remains the top D sell candidate: 0.47 pts/g since December 1 at 29, $3M x4 remaining.
recommendations.rationale: Recent window has been 0.47-0.50 since late January with no recovery. Season rate drifting from 0.96 at 50 GP to ~0.86 at 58 GP. Kaberle and a recovering Eminger are the next two left D's.

recommendations.summary: Smirnov has zero games all season at 20. Either dress him for the remaining 24 games or acknowledge the rotation philosophy has passed him over.
recommendations.rationale: The GM's stated goal is developing young players. Smirnov is on the roster with zero games while other 20-year-olds rotate. He needs game time before his development window narrows further.

recommendations.summary: Keep dressing Stahle. Three games at 20 MPG is the right start; the January 'zero games' note is retired.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 96 at 20, finally getting 20 MPG. Zero points in 3 games is irrelevant. The development plan needed this first window and he has it now.

recommendations.summary: Mogilny at 35 has dropped from 1.62 to 0.87 pts/g. Plan next season's top six without him on the first line.
recommendations.rationale: Rate halved on flat minutes (19.2 MPG). This is age on a 35-year-old, not a slump. His contract situation and role need to reflect a second-line winger at best.

recommendations.summary: Spezza needs either 10+ mpg every night or a full scratch; 7.5 mpg at 71 OVR is wasting a 21-year-old with POTE 99.
recommendations.rationale: Morale at 86 and flat since December. At 7.5 mpg against a 10-mpg expectation he is under-minuted for his calibre. Raised five times with no movement. The GM needs to decide: play him or dress someone else.

recommendations.summary: Richards' drop from 99 to 96 is results-driven, not minutes-driven; he is at band (17.0 mpg, 86 OVR). No line change helps here.
recommendations.rationale: He is playing his expected minutes and producing 55 points in 56 games. The three-point morale dip tracks the team's recent losses. Winning fixes it.

recommendations.summary: Swap Klesla to pair 2 with Kaberle and drop Stahle to pair 3 with St. Jacques.
recommendations.rationale: CAR's second line has Brendl at SPEE 94, SHPW 93. Stahle at SPEE 69 cannot cover him. Klesla at SPEE 92, CHKG 77 can. Pair 3 then faces their weakest line (Heerema 71, Vasicek 76). The auto-pairing means this only works by reordering the D pair slot numbers.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo in net against CAR.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 94 OVR is six points better than Ouellet at 82. CAR scores 3.2 per game and is riding a five-game win streak. We lost the one meeting 2-6; we need the best goalie we have.

recommendations.summary: No forward line changes for this game.
recommendations.rationale: Our top six OVR range is 85-97 vs their 76-83. The PP at 37% (20/54) against their 17.6% is our best weapon. Chemistry on L1 and L2 matters more than any marginal matchup adjustment here.

recommendations.summary: McCabe remains the top D to sell at season's end: 0.86 pts/g at 29, $3.0M x 4, production declining every week since late January.
recommendations.rationale: 50 points in 58 games (0.86) down from 0.96 on January 26th. Four years of $3.0M for a declining 29-year-old is a cap problem and a wasted asset.

recommendations.summary: Eminger at 0.45 pts/g in 44 games is a sell to a contender for any return; no recovery since February 6th and his $1.2M expires this spring.
recommendations.rationale: Season rate unchanged at 0.45 from the Feb 6 reading. At 21 with an expiring deal, late-deadline value is close to nothing. Move him sooner.

recommendations.summary: Colaiacovo at 0.40 pts/g in 30 games, $1.10M expiring, development stalled at 22. Sell if we are sellers.
recommendations.rationale: 12 points in 30 games at 0.40 is third-pairing production from a 22-year-old who should be trending up. His OVR is 72.

recommendations.summary: Stahle has finally played: 3 games at 20.0 MPG after 49 with zero. Watch his February sample before deciding keep-or-trade on his $0.97M x 3.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 96 at 20 was wasting away. Three games is not enough to judge, but it breaks the streak and gives a starting point for season-end evaluation.

recommendations.summary: Kaberle stays. GM's standing call: star defenceman, keeper. 28 points in 50 games at 83 OVR.
recommendations.rationale: Already confirmed by the GM as untouchable. No reason to revisit.

recommendations.summary: Fischer stays. GM's standing call: very very good, not tradeable.
recommendations.rationale: Already confirmed by the GM. 26 points in 53 games at 84 OVR.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker every night; his 83 CHKG at 29 is the internal fix to the checking gap the coach flags.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker and Upshall are both in no unit. With them active the club has six 80+ checkers, which is adequate. Without them the active count is four and the coach is right that the line-up is soft.

recommendations.summary: Dress Upshall (21, 80 CHKG) on the fourth line for physical presence alongside Tucker.
recommendations.rationale: Eighty checking at 21 with no unit assignment is wasted. Two bottom-six grinders together give the fourth line a role it currently lacks.

recommendations.summary: Chara (OTT, 27, 94 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 54 pts/56 GP, $1.70M expiring) is the deadline target that closes toughness and adds elite offence from the blue line.
recommendations.rationale: Toughness is the only role with zero players above 80 on the roster, and nobody under 30 will develop into it. Ottawa at 52 points with 11 expiring deals is the seller. Acceptance uncertain but the fit is perfect.

recommendations.summary: Avery (LA, 25, 93 FACE, 88 CHKG, 83 TOUG, $400K, 2 years) closes toughness, checking and faceoffs simultaneously at the lowest price available.
recommendations.rationale: One player fixing three gaps at $400K on a re-signable deal. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring contracts are motivated. The Avery-for-Tucker package is already constructed.

recommendations.summary: Scoring, playmaking, speed and clutch are covered. No acquisition needed in these roles before the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Twelve players at 80+ in scoring and playmaking, 22 in speed. The age curve (Mogilny 35, Sundin 34) is a summer problem, not a February one.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik on 5-6 years before July; 77 pts at 22 on $1.10M expiring is the single most valuable contract decision the club faces.
recommendations.rationale: He is 22, produced 77 points in 57 games, and carries one year left. If he walks, the club loses its top scorer with no pick capital to replace him.

recommendations.summary: Lock Richards on 5-6 years; 24, 55 pts, $1.00M, one year left, POTE 88.
recommendations.rationale: He is the top-nine centre the club needs and his production justifies a long-term raise. Losing him in free agency with no picks to replace costs both present and future.

recommendations.summary: Move Belfour before the deadline or by March 19 for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic; Luongo is already the starter.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 39, $6.50M, expiring, and scratched. After March 19 no trades occur and he walks in July for nothing. This pick is the club's largest recoverable capital asset.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla for a draft pick before the deadline; 36, $3.60M, expiring, over-80 mechanic applies.
recommendations.rationale: He is 36 with one year left and 24 points in 36 games. The pick recovery mechanic is the only way to convert his remaining value. No re-signing is intended at this age.

recommendations.summary: Move Roberts for a draft pick before the deadline; 38, $2.70M, expiring, over-80 mechanic applies.
recommendations.rationale: He is 38 with one year left. Still productive at 63 points, but the club cannot re-sign at age 38. Converting him to a pick frees $2.70M and adds draft capital.

recommendations.summary: Lock Nash on 5-6 years; 20 years old, 32 points, $1.20M, one year left, POTE 95.
recommendations.rationale: He is 20 with POTE 95 and already contributing 32 points. His rookie-window price is $1.20M; after a full season at top-nine minutes his asking price rises sharply.

recommendations.summary: Lock Kaberle on 5-6 years; 26, 28 points, $1.90M, one year left, POTE 75.
recommendations.rationale: He is a top-pair defenceman entering his prime at 26. The ceiling is capped but his current production warrants a long deal before the July bidding war.

recommendations.current: Chistov, Colaiacovo, Alexeev, Eminger, Upshall, Abid, Tellqvist
recommendations.summary: Sign the second tier on 2-3 year deals to stagger renewals and avoid a second 15-player cluster.
recommendations.rationale: These seven players all expire in July. Putting them on 2-3 years splits the renewal burden across summer 2007 and 2008 and preserves payroll flexibility at $55-60M total.

recommendations.summary: No action on Fischer this season; four years at $3.70M is locked and there is no market for a declining 24-year-old at that salary.
recommendations.rationale: He dropped from 0.63 to 0.41 pts/g, but four years left means no team takes the contract without a steep discount. Revisit in summer 2008 as trade bait with whatever he has become by then.

recommendations.summary: Move Belfour (39, 92 base, $6.50M, expiring) by March 19 for a pick or young player. This is mandatory, not opportunistic.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo (91 base, 25, $1.60M, 2yr) replaces him. Belfour is the only over-80 expiring asset and the pick-recovery mechanic closes permanently at the deadline. No trades after March 19 means the capital is lost in July.

recommendations.summary: Chara (OTT, D, 27, 94 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 54 pts/56 GP, $1.70M expiring) is the lead deadline acquisition. Open talks with OTT in late February.
recommendations.rationale: He is the only available player closing the Coach's toughness gap (nobody above 71 on our roster) and bringing top-pair offence. OTT at 52 points with 11 expiring deals is motivated. Belfour or a pick plus youth is the likely currency.

recommendations.summary: Avery (LA, C, 25, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2yr) is the secondary target. The Feb 12 package (Tucker for Avery) costs no asset we want to keep.
recommendations.rationale: Closes the faceoff gap behind Richards at 72 and adds checking depth. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring deals are sellers. Tucker (29, $1.30M, 83 CHKG) is in no unit. If both Chara and Avery land, they complement each other without overlapping.

recommendations.summary: Svehla (D, 36, $3.60M, expiring) goes before or at the deadline: to a trade partner for salary matching, or for a bare pick via the over-80 mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: He is over 80, expiring, and $3.60M. Either he matches salary in a Chara or Avery deal or he generates a pick. No reason to let him walk in July.

recommendations.summary: Roberts (LW, 38, $2.70M, expiring) follows the same path as Svehla: salary match or bare pick.
recommendations.rationale: Over 80, expiring, $2.70M, 38 years old. Same over-80 mechanic as Belfour and Svehla. Three expiring over-80s in one window is unusual; all three should generate picks or salary relief.

recommendations.summary: Gaborik (RW, 22, 91 base, $1.10M expiring, POTE 90) gets a 5-6 year deal at renewal. He is the most valuable asset on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: No mid-contract renegotiation is possible, so the conversation starts at season end. A 5-6 year lock prevents a July bidding war. At 91 base and 67 pts/45 GP at 22, he is a franchise player.

recommendations.summary: Nash (20), Richards (24), Kaberle (26), Eminger (21, POTE 99) all lock on 5-6 years at renewal. Stagger start dates so they do not all hit the market the same July.
recommendations.rationale: These four plus Gaborik are the young core. All under 27, all $1.00M-$1.90M now. Five-year deals at current-era salaries is the cheapest insurance the game offers. Eminger was specifically protected by the GM on Jan 19.

recommendations.current: Chistov, Colaiacovo, Alexeev, Upshall, Smirnov, Abid, Tellqvist
recommendations.summary: Depth group renews on 2-3 years at or near current salary. Abid stays per the GM's Jan 25 toughness designation. Tellqvist (25, $0.80M, POTE high 90s) is the backup to Luongo.
recommendations.rationale: Seven players, combined $5.60M expiring, all 20-25. Shorter terms keep payroll flexible while we still have Luongo, Gaborik, and the core on long deals. Staggering against the core renewals prevents the 2004-12-17 problem of seventeen deals expiring at once.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Komisarek (MTL, D, 23, 77 base, 83 TOUG, 66 pts/58 GP, $1.10M expiring, POTE 90) from MTL (46 pts, 14 expiring, $17.71M profit).
recommendations.rationale: 1.14 points per game from a 23-year-old defenceman on an expiring $1.10M deal from the league's second-worst club. His 83 TOUG partially fills the toughness gap. MTL cannot retain 14 expiring players and a $53.20M payroll at that record.

recommendations.summary: Chara (OTT, D, 27, 85 base, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 54 pts/56 GP, $1.70M expiring) remains the primary toughness fix. OTT at 52 pts, 11 expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Highest-value deadline target per Feb 12 note. Displayed 90/91 is today's form reading; stored grades are mid-80s. OTT confirmed seller. The GM's prior veto was about the Eminger-in package structure, not about Chara himself.

recommendations.summary: Kovalchuk (ATL, LW, 21, 89 base, 94 pts/54 GP, $1.10M expiring) from ATL (54 pts, 11 expiring) fills the scoring need. Package must be player-funded since Toronto own no pick earlier than a fourth.
recommendations.rationale: Highest-scoring available player at 91 displayed ovr. ATL cannot keep both him and Heatley on expiring deals. The old first-rounder-plus-Koltsov package is dead; a new package needs Koltsov plus a roster piece or Belfour as the over-80 asset.

recommendations.summary: Heatley (ATL, RW, 23, 91 base, 87 pts/51 GP, $1.10M expiring) is the alternative to Kovalchuk from the same negotiation. Slightly higher base overall at 91.
recommendations.rationale: Same club situation as Kovalchuk. ATL must move one. Heatley at 91 base is the marginally better long-term asset, but Kovalchuk's 94 points in 54 games is the higher ceiling if form holds. Both are $1.10M expiring from a 54-point team.

recommendations.summary: Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 80 base, 91 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 83 FACE, $900K, 2 years) remains the cheapest re-signable toughness fix. CHI at 50 pts, 10 expiring.
recommendations.rationale: The Jan 25 veto killed the faceoff argument because he is a wing, but 91 TOUG at $900K for two years is the toughness case and that case is unchanged. The Jan 30 package (Colaiacovo plus Safronov) may still work since Eminger fills the vacated slot.

recommendations.summary: Belanger (LA, C, 27, 82 base, 96 FACE, 73 TOUG, $700K expiring, 11 pts/54 GP) is the best faceoff man in the league. LA at 54 pts with 13 expiring.
recommendations.rationale: 96 FACE at $700K is the cheapest fix for the Sundin insurance problem. The risk is LA fatigue: the Avery negotiation (Tucker for Avery) is already active per the Feb 12 note. Two packages to the same club in one window may not be feasible.

recommendations.summary: Havlat (OTT, LW, 23, 87 base, 72 pts/56 GP, $900K expiring) is the natural add-on to a Chara negotiation. Same club, same rebuild, same window.
recommendations.rationale: If Chara moves to Toronto, Havlat goes in the same conversation. The Jan 19 veto was about a specific package that included Eminger, not about Havlat. At $900K and 72 points from a 52-point team, he is a top-six winger for the price of a fourth-liner.

recommendations.summary: Avery (LA, C, 25, 79 base, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 94 FACE, $400K, 2 years) is in active negotiation. Closes all three gaps at $400K but produces only 6 pts/56 GP.
recommendations.rationale: Already being pursued via the Tucker-for-Avery package. He is not a scorer. His value is 83/88/94 in TOUG/CHKG/FACE at $400K for two years at 25. If the package closes, the toughness and faceoff gaps are solved simultaneously.

recommendations.summary: Do not pursue Daze (CHI, 29, 89 base, 95 pts/57 GP, $3.00M expiring) despite the league-leading point total.
recommendations.rationale: At 29 on $3.00M expiring with no recorded POTE above 86, he is a one-year rental with no re-signing path. Kovalchuk at 21 and $1.10M fills the same role with five more years of value.

recommendations.summary: Do not pursue Thornton (BOS, 25, 94 base, $4.00M, 73 pts/47 GP, UFA this July).
recommendations.rationale: BOS at 61 pts is not a clear seller, $4.00M is the highest ask on the board, and POTE 76 means his development is nearly complete. Kovalchuk at $1.10M and Heatley at $1.10M give more upside at a quarter of the cost.

recommendations.current: Klesla (22, D, POTE 97, $0.90M, 2yr) + Upshall (21, RW, POTE 99, $1.20M, 1yr) + 4th round pick
recommendations.proposed: Chara (27, D, 94 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 54 pts/56 GP, $1.70M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Offer Klesla, Upshall, and the 4th to Ottawa for Chara: closes toughness (94 TOUG) and checking (95 CHKG) and adds 54 pts/56 GP of top-pair offence from a 52-point seller with 11 expiring deals.
recommendations.rationale: OTT are in full rebuild and hoard young potential. Klesla at POTE 97 and Upshall at POTE 99 are two 21-22 year olds on combined $2.10M who give them exactly what they accumulate. We keep Eminger and Colaiacovo per the Jan 19 veto. Net salary increase $0.80M.

recommendations.current: St. Jacques (24, D, POTE 94, $0.80M, 2yr, 0 GP) + Safronov (23, D, POTE 91, $0.90M, 3yr, 0 GP) + 4th round pick
recommendations.proposed: Komisarek (23, D, 77 base, 83 TOUG, 66 pts/58 GP, $1.10M expiring, POTE 90)
recommendations.summary: Offer St. Jacques, Safronov, and the 4th to Montreal for Komisarek: a 23-year-old D with 66 pts/58 GP and 83 TOUG from a 46-point team with 14 expiring deals, netting $0.60M in salary savings.
recommendations.rationale: MTL cannot re-sign 14 expiring players and will deal a young D. St. Jacques and Safronov carry no GP for us (both in no unit) and give MTL two cheap POTE 90+ defenders on $1.70M. We get a top-pair blueliner in waiting who partially fills the toughness gap. Acceptance uncertain; MTL may want a forward.

recommendations.proposed: A draft pick from a playoff-contending club needing goalie insurance (round uncertain)
recommendations.summary: Move Belfour to a contender before March 19 for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic: he is surplus behind Luongo and Ouellet and walks in July if not traded, destroying the capital permanently.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo (91 base, 40 GP, 2yr) is the starter; Ouellet (1.91 GAA, 9 GP, 2yr) is the backup. Belfour saves no money and is the club's only over-80 expiring pick-recovery asset per the Feb 9 note. March 19 is the last game day for trades. The receiving team gets a 92-base netminder for the postseason at no long-term cost.

recommendations.summary: The goalie trade window task is resolved: Luongo is ours, DiPietro is not a target, and no other 90+ base goalie from a seller adds value over Luongo.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 91 base, 25, $1.60M, 2 years covers the Jan 15 mandate. DiPietro at 79 base with form-driven improvement and NYI at 59 points is not available. The remaining goalie question is Belfour's disposition, which is a separate deadline decision.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle for OTT and give him 12+ minutes; 2 games in 57 at POTE 96 and age 20 is the biggest waste on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: He gets 17.0 MPG when he plays, so the staff sees him. Against a 19-27 team there is no reason not to start accumulating games for a 20-year-old D.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza either 12+ MPG or a full scratch by decision, not by default; 7.5 MPG is neither development nor production.
recommendations.rationale: 0.41 pts/g on 7.5 MPG at 21 with POTE 99 means he is neither growing nor contributing. The GM needs to pick a direction in the final 25 games.

recommendations.summary: Reinstate Alexeev against OTT; 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG is the most efficient production among the young forwards and he is benched.
recommendations.rationale: 30 points in 55 games at 8.3 MPG says he is earning more ice than he gets. A 19-27 opponent is the right night to test him at 12+ minutes.

recommendations.summary: Leave Smirnov scratched; POTE 70 at age 20 with 0 games does not justify displacing anyone producing above that ceiling.
recommendations.rationale: His scouting number is modest. Forcing him in to fill a development slot would cost more than it gains.

recommendations.summary: Give Chlup power-play time and move him toward second-line centre duty for the final 25 games.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup at 18 went from 0.62 to 0.82 pts/g while minutes rose 11.0→16.5. He is outproducing the role he is in and needs top-nine responsibility to consolidate.

recommendations.summary: Spezza needs 12+ MPG for the remainder of the season or a full healthy scratch; 5.3 MPG is producing nothing at 21.
recommendations.rationale: Rate dropped 0.43→0.38 while minutes fell 9.1→5.3. Raised six times since January with no movement. A wasted year at his potential is the worst outcome available.

recommendations.summary: Either return Spacek to 12+ MPG or scratch him; 7.6 MPG at 0.39 pts/g develops nothing at 19.
recommendations.rationale: Minutes collapsed 16.0→7.6 and rate fell 0.55→0.39. A full year of bottom-six garbage-time hockey at 19 costs a year of development.

recommendations.summary: Keep Stahle dressed and playing; he finally appeared in 2 games at 17.0 MPG and needs more.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 96 at 20 as a defenceman. Two games is the start of what January 25th demanded. Stop and restart now undoes it.

recommendations.summary: McCabe is the deadline sell: 0.48 pts/g recent window on 21.6 MPG with four years at $3M remaining.
recommendations.rationale: His early-season 1.42 rate has collapsed to 0.48 across 33 games since December. No recovery signal. The contract makes him a financial anchor.

recommendations.summary: Do not sell Eminger at the deadline. His recent window (0.57 on 17.8 MPG) has the trend pointing back up from the threshold.
recommendations.rationale: Cumulative sits at roughly 0.455, right on the 0.45 line, but the last 21 games are producing 0.57. A 21-year-old trending up on $1.2M is a roster piece, not a fire-sale asset.

recommendations.summary: Plan next season's top six knowing the aging trio are declining: Mogilny 1.62→0.90, Sundin 1.46→0.94, Roberts 1.29→0.97.
recommendations.rationale: All three are getting more minutes while scoring significantly less. Richards (0.94) and Abid (1.11) are the only ones holding their rates. Next year cannot carry the same load.

recommendations.summary: No morale-driven line changes needed for Tuesday. The room is at 96+ across the active roster.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza at 86 is the sole outlier and has been raised five times; the GM's development rotation (Chlup on the second line) explains the minutes allocation. No other player is meaningfully under his expected band with slipping morale.

recommendations.summary: We lack a bottom-six centre who can check and win draws. Spacek is the current one at 8.3 MPG and cannot fill that role yet.
recommendations.rationale: L4 faceoffs mean is 51 and checking mean 64. Only Abid (80 checking) provides any defensive structure and he plays wing. No other unassigned forward on the roster clears 80 in checking.

recommendations.summary: Spacek needs 12+ MPG or a full scratch; 8.3 MPG develops nobody and hurts his morale expectations.
recommendations.rationale: Previously flagged February 9th with no movement. At 8.3 MPG and zero points in his last appearance, he's in no-man's land between development and deployment.

recommendations.summary: No change to L1, L2, or L3. Their composition matches their roles.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has elite skill with adequate checking, L2 is built to score, L3 is the most balanced unit with Richards providing stamina and clutch. Chemistry should hold.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo. 92 OVR against a team that scores 2.20 per game is the easiest assignment on the schedule.
recommendations.rationale: Ottawa fires 2.20 goals per game and their PP converts at 12.4%. Luongo's 96 glove and 96 agility handle their only real threat (Havlat at 99 speed, Alfredsson at 94 deking) without stress. Ouellet at 80 is a downgrade we do not need.

recommendations.summary: No line changes for this opponent. Our first line and first pair handle Ottawa's top unit; their depth is inferior to ours across all lines.
recommendations.rationale: Ottawa scores 2.20 per game with a 12.4% PP. Their first line (White 83, Havlat 86, Alfredsson 88) is the only unit above 82, and our auto-pairing puts Sundin/Gaborik/Roberts plus Fischer/McCabe against them. The series stands 2-0-0 TOR, 10-7 goals.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker in a bottom-six role for every remaining game; his 83 CHKG is free checking the coach is not using.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker at 83 CHKG and 29 is unlined. Upshall at 80 CHKG and 21 is also unlined. Either closes the checking gap from 6 to 7+ at 80+ without a trade.

recommendations.summary: Toughness is the only role with zero 80+ players on the roster (ceiling 73); no internal fix exists and this requires acquisition before the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts 73 and McCabe 73 are the team's best toughness ratings. Abid's Jan base TOUG 80 does not confirm in the Feb 9 group. Bell (95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, $900K, 2yr, CHI) or Avery (83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 93 FACE, $400K, 2yr, LA) are the only available closers.

recommendations.summary: Faceoffs are one deep at 80+ (Sundin 90 only); the other three lines lose the draw by default.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup at 75 is the next best and Richards at 70 handles third-line. Avery at 93 FACE closes this and toughness in one move. Bell at 87 FACE is slightly less of a faceoff fix but adds more toughness.

recommendations.summary: Avery (LA, C, 25, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2 years) closes both faceoffs and toughness at the lowest price available; LA at 48 points with 13 expiring contracts are motivated sellers.
recommendations.rationale: Cheapest player in the league closing three gaps simultaneously. Two years of control means he fits the re-signable young-core shape. Still unresolved since January — the GM has not opened this conversation.

recommendations.summary: Bell (CHI, LW/RW, 24, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, 80 base, $900K, 2 years) is the purest toughness play and still the best if Avery does not land.
recommendations.rationale: Only available player at 95 TOUG. Chicago are profitable at $26M so acceptance requires a real package (Colaiacovo plus Safronov, no R2 available). Unresolved since late January.

recommendations.summary: Scoring, playmaking, speed, clutch and stamina are all well-covered at 80+ with youth behind them; no acquisition needed in those roles.
recommendations.rationale: 12 players at 80+ scoring with Gaborik 22 and Afinogenov 25 as the future. 22 at 80+ speed. 9 at 80+ clutch. No gap to fill here.

recommendations.summary: Checking is carried by Roberts (38) and Svehla (36) alongside McCabe (29) and Fischer (24); once those two veterans move in 2006 the checking group drops to four players at 80+.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts 86 CHKG at 38 and Svehla 83 CHKG at 36 are both expiring or near-expiring. Fischer at 82 CHKG and 24 with POTE 99 should be the long-term answer but needs ice time to develop.

recommendations.proposed: 5-6 year extension at renewal in July
recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik, Nash, Richards, and Kaberle to 5-6 year deals on renewal in July; they cannot be touched mid-contract.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik (76 pts, $1.10M expiring, age 22), Nash (32 pts, $1.20M expiring, age 20), Richards (54 pts, $1.00M expiring, age 24), Kaberle (27 pts, $1.90M expiring, age 26) are the four highest-value young players expiring this summer. They cannot be extended before their contracts end; the renewal window in July is the only chance.

recommendations.summary: Move Belfour for draft picks before the March deadline using the over-80 expiring mechanic; Luongo is the starter.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 39, 92 base, $6.50M expiring, 21 GP behind Luongo (40 GP). He qualifies for the above-80 pick-recovery mechanic. No trades after March 19; he walks in July and the capital is lost. This is the single largest pick-generating asset on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla for a draft pick before the March deadline; Klesla (POTE 97, 56 GP) is his replacement.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla is 36, $3.60M expiring, 24 points in 35 games. He qualifies for the over-80 expiring mechanic and will not be re-signed. Klesla and Eminger fill his minutes at half the cost and 15 years younger.

recommendations.summary: Move Roberts for a draft pick before the March deadline if the price is right; he walks in July regardless.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts is 38, $2.70M expiring, 63 points in 56 games. He is still producing but will not re-sign at any reasonable age or salary. Trading him for a pick before the deadline converts two months of production into a future asset. Acceptance is uncertain because 63 points is meaningful production from a contender.

recommendations.summary: Fischer at $3.70M through 2008-09 is a future liability but cannot be moved now; no action until his production drops further.
recommendations.rationale: Fischer (24, 26 pts, declining from 0.63 to 0.41 pts/g, $3.70M, 4 years) is locked. No mid-contract renegotiation is possible. By summer 2007 he will be trade bait from a position of weakness; there is nothing to do today.

recommendations.summary: Move Belfour (92 base, $6.50M expiring) by March 19 for a draft pick or young player; after that date no trades exist and he walks in July taking $6.50M in pick-recovery value with him.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo (91 base, 25, 2yr) is the starter. Belfour is redundant and the over-80 expiring mechanic only works before the deadline. Open negotiations late February per GM's standing order.

recommendations.summary: Sign Gaborik (22, 91 base, $1.10M) to five to six years on July 1; he is a first-line winger on min-exempt money and the single most important re-signing on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: 67 points in 45 games at 91 base on $1.10M with one year left. No mid-contract renegotiation is possible; July 1 is the only window.

recommendations.summary: Sign Nash (20, $1.20M) to five to six years in July. Core winger at 20 on a second year of rookie money.
recommendations.rationale: Age 20, $1.20M, expiring. Same cluster as Gaborik and Eminger; locking them together avoids a renewal crisis in any future summer.

recommendations.summary: Sign Eminger (21, $1.20M, POTE 99) to five to six years in July. The GM protected him over Chara in January because his development curve is still open.
