recommendations.rationale: 21 years old with POTE 99 on $1.20M expiring. Five to six years locks the development window without a cap consequence since there is no cap.

recommendations.summary: Sign Kaberle (26, $1.90M) to five to six years in July. Top-pairing right-handed defenceman entering prime.
recommendations.rationale: 26 years old, $1.90M, expiring. Prime years ahead; five to six years keeps him through his best seasons.

recommendations.summary: Sign Richards (24, $1.00M) to five to six years in July. Centre, 24, $1.00M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: The coach slotted him at third-line centre for faceoff duty on January 25. That is a role for a player the club controls long-term.

recommendations.summary: Sign Tellqvist (25, $0.80M) to two to three years in July as backup to Luongo.
recommendations.rationale: GM protected him on January 15 for his high-90s potential. At $0.80M, a two-year deal is cheap insurance if Luongo needs rest.

recommendations.summary: Sign Colaiacovo (22, $1.10M) to three to five years in July, unless he is traded at the deadline as part of a Belfour package.
recommendations.rationale: 22-year-old defenceman on expiring $1.10M. If Belfour's return requires a player, he is the candidate; if not, renew.

recommendations.summary: Sign Upshall (21, $1.20M) to three to five years in July.
recommendations.rationale: 21, $1.20M, expiring. Young forward the club should control.

recommendations.summary: Sign Chistov (21, $1.10M) to three to five years in July, or trade at deadline if Belfour's return requires a young player.
recommendations.rationale: 21-year-old forward, expiring. Same logic as Colaiacovo: renew unless deadline needs require him as packaging.

recommendations.summary: Sign Abid (24, $0.40M) to two to three years in July. He fills the toughness gap the coach flags and costs nothing.
recommendations.rationale: 80 TOUG, 80 CHKG, $400K. The internal answer to the physicality gap. Cheap to retain, expensive to replace.

recommendations.summary: Sign Smirnov (20, $0.40M) to three to five years in July as a project at minimum salary.
recommendations.rationale: Coach wants a 10-game look to evaluate him. At $400K, even if he busts the cost is zero.

recommendations.summary: Sign Alexeev (23, $1.10M) to two to three years in July if his production holds; otherwise let him walk.
recommendations.rationale: 23-year-old RW, expiring. Not a core lock; two to three years is the right term for a player whose role is still being defined.

recommendations.summary: Do not buy at the deadline. The coach's flags are development problems (Stahle, Spezza, Smirnov, Safronov, Chlup need ice), not roster gaps. Abid closes toughness internally.
recommendations.rationale: 90 points, 17 ahead of second place, 26 games left. The roster is already the best in the conference. Adding a rental risks displacing a young player the coach explicitly needs to develop.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla (36, 85 base, $3.60M expiring) for a pick in the final week of February if a contender offers one; otherwise let him walk in July after the playoffs.
recommendations.rationale: Over-80 expiring mechanic applies. At 36 and $3.60M he will not be re-signed regardless. A pick now is worth more than nothing in July, but do not hold up Belfour's market for him.

recommendations.summary: Same logic for Roberts (38, 87 base, $2.70M expiring): take a pick if offered, otherwise he walks after the playoffs.
recommendations.rationale: 38 years old, 87 base, expiring. Will not be re-signed. The over-80 mechanic makes him tradeable for a pick until March 19.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Chara as the primary deadline target: 94 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 54 pts/56 GP, $1.70M expiring from a 52-point seller.
recommendations.rationale: The only player closing toughness and checking simultaneously while producing top-pair offence. OTT at 19-27-6 with 11 expiring deals and $26.98M profit is the most motivated seller on the board. Package must be player-based since TOR owns no picks beyond a 4th.

recommendations.summary: Open a conversation for Kovalchuk: 94 pts/54 GP, 21 years old, $1.10M expiring from a 54-point club that cannot re-sign him.
recommendations.rationale: Highest-scoring available player in the league at 21. ATL at 19-26-2 with 11 expiring and $20.31M profit must move someone. The binary with Heatley means only one is available; Kovalchuk is 2 years younger with 7 more points.

recommendations.summary: Monitor Thornton as a secondary target if BOS slips further: 92 overall, 89 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 73 pts/47 GP, $4M expiring, 25 years old.
recommendations.rationale: The most complete single player available. BOS at 60 points with $30.32M profit and 13 expiring deals are not desperate, so acceptance requires a significant package that TOR may not be able to fund without gutting depth. Pursue only if the BOS record deteriorates past 55 points.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Bell to close toughness (88), checking (86), and faceoffs (82) simultaneously at $900K with 2 years control.
recommendations.rationale: Only player filling all three gaps on a cheap, controllable deal. CHI at 18-27-8 with 10 expiring deals is a seller. Low scoring (20 pts) is acceptable for a bottom-six role. At 24, he fits the core timeline.

recommendations.summary: Rent Conroy for the playoff push: 94 FACE, 68 pts/56 GP, $2M expiring from a 44-point club that will move anyone.
recommendations.rationale: Best faceoff centre available by a wide margin. At 33 he is a rental, but the playoff faceoff gap is real and CGY at 17-31-6 with 10 expiring deals will accept almost anything. Costs a player TOR does not plan to keep plus the lone 4th-rounder.

recommendations.summary: Add Avery at $400K as a cheap faceoff specialist: 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 24 years old, 2 years remaining.
recommendations.rationale: Six points is not production but $400K for 93 FACE and 83 TOUG at age 24 on a 2-year deal is the cheapest structural fix in the league. LA at 16-25-6 with 13 expiring deals will deal anyone. Fits alongside Bell as a two-player solution to the faceoff gap.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Heatley only if ATL re-signs Kovalchuk: 87 pts/51 GP, 23, $1.10M expiring from the same seller.
recommendations.rationale: The ATL binary means one of these two is available, not both. Heatley at 87 points and 23 on $1.10M expiring is the fallback. If ATL re-signs both, the ATL target is dead entirely.

recommendations.summary: Consider Samsonov as the BOS target if Thornton is unobtainable: 82 pts/47 GP, 26, $1.90M expiring.
recommendations.rationale: Same club as Thornton, same seller situation, half the salary and 11 fewer points. A winger rather than a centre so he does not solve the faceoff gap. Lower priority than Chara or Bell on the same timeline.

recommendations.summary: Monitor Cammalleri as a young upside piece: POTE 97, 37 pts/34 GP, 22 years old, $1.10M expiring from LA.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 97 at 22 with 1.09 pts/g in limited games is the type of developmental asset that fits the roster shape. LA at 16-25-6 with 13 expiring deals will deal him. Lower priority than the immediate gap-fillers but worth a look in any multi-player package to LA.

recommendations.summary: Do not pursue Brashear, McCarthy, Domi, or Laraque as toughness solutions.
recommendations.rationale: Brashear costs $2.10M at 33 on a 2-year deal with 8 points. McCarthy is 32 with 3 points. Domi is on a 67-point ANA club with $28M profit that will not sell. Laraque is on a 73-point EDM club. Chara, Bell, and Thornton solve the gap with real hockey value attached.

recommendations.summary: Offer Chicago Colaiacovo plus Safronov for Bell: closes toughness, checking and faceoffs simultaneously at $900K with 2 years of control.
recommendations.rationale: Bell is the only available player at 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG and 87 FACE on $900K with 2 years. Chicago at 50 points with 10 expiring deals and $26M profit are sellers who need young blueliners. Colaiacovo (22, POTE 99, $1.10M) and Safronov (23, POTE 91, $0.90M, 3 GP this year) are the most expendable of our young D; Eminger and Klesla are protected. Payroll moves $900K in against $2.00M out, a net $1.10M saving. Acceptance uncertain.

recommendations.summary: Offer Calgary Chistov plus the fourth-rounder for Conroy: a 94 FACE rental for the playoff push at 68 points.
recommendations.rationale: Conroy at 94 FACE, 68 pts, 56 GP, $2.00M expiring from 44-point CGY with 10 expiring deals is the best available faceoff rental. Chistov (21, POTE 95, 16 pts, $1.10M expiring) and the fourth-rounder are assets Toronto does not plan to keep long-term. This is a pure rental: after the season Conroy is gone and the only pick is gone. Only worth it if the GM wants playoff insurance at centre behind Sundin.

recommendations.summary: Offer LA Tucker for Avery: 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG at $400K with 2 years left for a veteran checker in no unit.
recommendations.rationale: Avery at $400K with 2 years closes the faceoff and checking gaps for four seasons at minimal cost. Tucker (29, $1.30M, CHKG 92, TOUG 88, in no unit) gives LA a veteran the can use tonight. LA at 54 points with 13 expiring deals are the most motivated sellers. Try to bundle Avery with Belanger (LA, 90 FACE, 82 base, $700K expiring) if LA will move two centers. Net payroll: $400K in against $1.30M out, a saving.

recommendations.proposed: Second or third-round pick from a contender
recommendations.summary: Move Svehla (83 base, $3.60M expiring) or Roberts (84 base, $2.70M expiring, 63 pts) to a contender via the over-80 expiring mechanic for a draft pick each.
recommendations.rationale: Both players qualify for the over-80 pick-recovery mechanic and walk in July regardless. Svehla at 36 with 83 CHKG and Roberts at 38 with 63 points still have value to a contender. Draft capital is empty (one fourth-rounder). Every week they sit untraded is a week the pick capital is not rebuilt. Priority before Bell or Conroy because these are pure losses if not moved.

recommendations.summary: Spezza needs 12+ MPG in at least 10 of the remaining 26 games; scratch a depth winger to make room on nights we can afford it.
recommendations.rationale: 37 GP, 7.5 MPG, 0.41 pts/g at 21 with the club's highest scouting number. Raised six times with no movement. A seventh year at 7.5 MPG produces nothing.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle for at least 5 of the remaining 26 games; his 2 appearances averaged 17 MPG so he can handle the load.
recommendations.rationale: 2 games in 56 at age 20 with the same scouting number as Eminger. Klesla plays every night at 22; Stahle plays almost none at 20. Colaiacovo at 30 GP has 26 more games of development value sitting on the bench.

recommendations.summary: No change for Chlup, Nash, Gaborik or Klesla — all four are getting full development loads.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup: 18yo at 14.7 MPG on the second line, 0.71 pts/g. Nash: 13.2 MPG, 0.74 pts/g. Gaborik: 19.6 MPG, 1.36 pts/g. Klesla: 56 of 56 games. None need intervention.

recommendations.summary: Upshall is producing at fourth-line rates (0.38 pts/g) on fourth-line minutes (10.7 MPG). No promotion warranted.
recommendations.rationale: His rate has faded from 0.40 to 0.38 since January. The promotion signal from January 8th is gone.

recommendations.summary: Give Chlup first or second-line minutes for the remaining 26 games; he is producing 0.75 pts/g on 16.2 MPG at 18 and ready for a bigger role.
recommendations.rationale: His rate climbed from 0.62 to 0.75 while minutes rose from 11.0 to 16.2. No other player under 23 is showing that pattern.

recommendations.summary: Chistov's recent 0.43 pts/g on 15.3 MPG (up from 0.29 on 9.5) means he has earned a top-nine role for the rest of this season.
recommendations.rationale: Both production and minutes are climbing. At 21 this is a genuine development step, not a hot streak.

recommendations.summary: Reconsider trading Eminger: his recent 21 games produce 0.57 pts/g, well above the 0.35 he showed through December, suggesting the earlier collapse was a cold start.
recommendations.rationale: Season rate is 0.45 but the trend is clearly upward. Selling a 21-year-old at the bottom of a season he is finishing strong is poor timing. This reverses the Feb 6 threshold call if the trend holds through the final weeks.

recommendations.summary: Sixth time raising this: Spezza is at 0.38 pts/g on 5.3 MPG. Either give him 12+ minutes or accept this year is lost for his development.
recommendations.rationale: Rate fell from 0.43 to 0.38 and minutes from 9.1 to 5.3 over the same window. POTE 99 at 21 on 5 minutes a night.

recommendations.summary: No action on Koltsov; GM has designated him a trading chip. His recent 0.32 pts/g means the chip has little remaining value.
recommendations.rationale: Collapsed from 1.10 in 10 games to 0.32 in the 22 since. Keeping per GM standing order but noting the asset has depreciated.

recommendations.summary: Kaberle's trend (0.54→0.58 rate, 19.4→22.4 MPG) confirms the GM's judgement that he is the keeper and the top-pair anchor for next season.
recommendations.rationale: The only defenceman whose rate and minutes both climbed over this window.

recommendations.summary: Get Spezza from 7.5 to at least 12 MPG before his 86 morale turns into a real problem.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza is at 86, the lowest morale on the roster, on 7.5 MPG against a 17-minute band for a 21-year-old with POTE 99. Six weeks ago he was in the 90s. This is the one minutes clock ticking on the room.

recommendations.summary: All units are correctly built for their jobs; no shuffle fixes anything the roster already limits.
recommendations.rationale: L1-L3 balance offence and checking sensibly, P1/P2 have shooters and faceoff men, K1/K2 carry three 81-checking bodies and one 77. L4's low checking mean (64) is the only weak number but it plays fourth-line minutes against fourth-line opposition with no paired D, so the problem is who we have, not where they sit.

recommendations.summary: We have no faceoff specialist behind Richards (72). If Sundin or Chlup misses time we have no one who wins draws.
recommendations.rationale: Role inventory shows four skaters above 70 at faceoffs: Sundin 88, Chlup 77, Roberts 73, Richards 72. Everyone else is below 70. One centre who wins draws would remove a single-point-of-failure risk.

recommendations.summary: Nobody on the roster is above 71 toughness. We check but we do not intimidate.
recommendations.rationale: Toughness leaders are McCabe 71, Roberts 70, Abid 70, Fischer 69. No opponent's power forward fears our checking units. This is a structural weakness of the roster, not a lineup error.

recommendations.summary: Eminger crossed the 0.45 pts/g sell threshold on Feb 6 at 21 with an expiring $1.2M deal. Trade him at the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Season rate 19 points in 42 games (0.45). He is not on any line currently. Expiring deal at 21 means we lose him for nothing in summer unless we move him now.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo. Check Belfour's fatigue icon as routine but keep the G1 start.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is 93 OVR against a team that scores 3.00/gp with a 12.6% power play. This is the easiest start on the schedule and he needs reps at 25.

recommendations.summary: No lineup change. Current lines already give Chlup, Nash, Chistov, Spacek and Klesla real roles in a game we can afford to develop in.
recommendations.rationale: Chicago is 18-27-8 with 50 points. Their best forward is Daze at 87 and their best D is McCarthy at 77. The development framework applies: young guys are already in the lineup, their defense is too thin to punish us for it.

recommendations.summary: McCabe's rate has dropped from 0.96 to 0.89 this season with a 0.33 recent window; at 29 and $3.0M x4 he should be moved before his value erodes further.
recommendations.rationale: He was 48 pts in 50 GP on Jan 26 (0.96). Now 50 pts in 56 GP (0.89), meaning 2 pts in 6 recent games (0.33). No recovery is happening. At 29 with four years left on $3.0M, a trade now beats a sell-next-year at a discount.

recommendations.summary: Eminger confirmed at 0.45 pts/g (20 in 44), no February recovery; sell at deadline on his expiring $1.2M.
recommendations.rationale: Unchanged from Feb 6 finding. 75 OVR at 21 is enough to interest a cup team needing depth PP D. His rate will not improve in 10 games.

recommendations.summary: Colaiacovo at 0.40 pts/g on an expiring deal is a second expiring-D sell alongside Eminger.
recommendations.rationale: 12 points in 30 games, 71 OVR, age 22, $1.1M x1. He is behind Salo and Klesla on the depth chart and will not crack the lineup. A cup team needs a 7th D; we get a late-round pick.

recommendations.summary: McCabe, Fischer, Kaberle, Svehla and Klesla all stay in the lineup tonight; Chicago is 18-27 and this is a beatable night with our best available D.
recommendations.rationale: All five dress and carry morale at 99. No injuries on the blue line. The only changes this season should be at the deadline, not tonight.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bell (CHI, 24, 80 base, 91 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 83 FACE, $900K, 2yrs) as the primary February target; he closes toughness and faceoff gaps simultaneously on a keeper contract.
recommendations.rationale: No current player exceeds 73 TOUG; Bell's displayed 91 is the only available option above 85. His 83 FACE gives the fourth line a real draw man. At $900K and 2 years he is re-signable and affordable. Package: Colaiacovo plus Safronov; CHI acceptance uncertain at their $26M payroll.

recommendations.summary: Avery (LA, 25, 79 base, FACE 94, CHKG 88, TOUG 83, $400K, 2yrs) is the cheaper alternative if Bell's price is too high, but his ENDU 50 and PENA 93 limit his shift length and discipline.
recommendations.rationale: His 94 FACE is the best available by 11 points over Bell. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring deals are motivated sellers. ENDU 50 means 12-minute shifts at best; PENA 93 makes him a liability on the PK. He is the faceoff fix, Bell is the toughness fix.

recommendations.summary: Confirm Abid's current TOUG on the screen before opening negotiations for Bell; if his stored base is genuinely 80 and his displayed is just form-suppressed, dress him nightly and downgrade Bell from 'must' to 'nice-to-have'.
recommendations.rationale: Our Jan 25 reading put his base at TOUG 80 and CHKG 80, but he does not appear in the current 80+ toughness group on the Feb 9 screen. If 80 is real he is the internal fix at $400K and zero trade cost. If he has regressed below 80, the gap is real and Bell becomes mandatory.

recommendations.summary: Shop Ouellet (23, $900K, 2yrs, 1.88 GAA, 0.918 SV in 8 GP, POTE 97) in a February deal; he is a quality chip for a contender needing a backup and a third-stringer does not develop him.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo has the top job locked for two years. Ouellet's performance in limited action says he could start on a weaker club. A contender's backup job at 23 with POTE 97 is real development; sitting in Toronto is not.

recommendations.summary: Scoring, speed, and playmaking are covered today; do not spend capital on a second scorer before March.
recommendations.rationale: 12 players at 80+ in scoring and 22 at 80+ in speed. The age issue (Mogilny 35, Roberts 38) is a summer problem for re-signing and development, not a February trade-deadline problem. Gaborik at 92 and 22 and Afinogenov at 90 and 25 are the future.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik on a 5-6 year deal this July before he hits the market at 75 points on $1.10M.
recommendations.rationale: 22 years old, 75 pts in 55 GP, POTE 90, $1.10M expiring. At this production and price he is the most valuable roster asset on the open market in July. A five-to-six year lock keeps him through age 27-28.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards on a 5-6 year deal this July.
recommendations.rationale: 24, 54 pts in 53 GP, POTE 88, $1.00M expiring. He is the bridge between the young core and the aging top end. Without a long deal the 30-33 age gap widens further.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash on a 5-6 year deal this July.
recommendations.rationale: 20, 32 pts in 42 GP, POTE 95, $1.20M expiring. POTE 95 at age 20 is the second-highest on the roster behind Eminger. Lock now before a full 82-game season doubles his asking price.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger on a 5-6 year deal this July.
recommendations.rationale: 21, 20 pts in 44 GP, POTE 99, $1.20M expiring. The highest POTE on the roster. The GM vetoed Chara partly to protect Eminger's timeline; that makes the extension even more important.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Abid on a 5-6 year deal this July.
recommendations.rationale: 24, 63 pts in 55 GP, POTE 94, $0.40M expiring. He is producing on a fourth-line salary and closing the toughness gap the coach flagged. Even with a raise to $1.5-2.5M he is a bargain.

recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour for a draft pick before March using the over-80 expiring mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: 39, 92 base, $6.50M expiring. Luongo (91 base, 25, 2 years) is the starter. Belfour is the club's largest pick-recovery asset and frees $6.50M. Toronto holds only a fourth-rounder as draft capital.

recommendations.summary: Explore a trade for Sundin in summer 2005 while his production and trade value are near peak.
recommendations.rationale: 33, $8.40M, 5 years remaining, POTE 60, 63 pts in 55 GP. He will be 36 and costing $8.40M by 2007-08. Not an expiring asset, so the over-80 mechanic does not apply; a straight hockey trade or three-team deal is the route. Waiting until 35 halves the return.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle on a 2-3 year deal, not 5-6 years.
recommendations.rationale: 26, 27 pts in 47 GP, POTE 75, $1.90M expiring. POTE 75 means his ceiling is close. A 2-3 year deal at $2-2.5M covers two good seasons and avoids paying a starter's salary to a blueliner whose best is already visible.

recommendations.summary: Release or let Svehla walk this summer rather than re-signing.
recommendations.rationale: 36, $3.60M, scratched, POTE 55, 23 pts in 34 GP. He does not dress. Releasing saves $3.60M and the roster spot for a young defenceman.

recommendations.summary: Plan Chlup's 5-6 year extension for summer 2006; his current deal expires then and mid-contract renegotiation is not possible.
recommendations.rationale: 18, $2.34M, 2 years left, POTE 95, 31 pts in 44 GP. Game rules prevent renegotiation until the deal expires. By summer 2006 he will be 19 with a full season on his sheet. Budget a significant raise; at $2.34M he is already overpaid relative to his production but the POTE justifies the cap hold.

recommendations.summary: Do not execute trades at the March 19 deadline; hold the full roster for the playoff run.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto lead the East by 17 points with the deepest roster in the conference and own only a fourth-round pick. There is no need to fill that is not already covered internally (Abid for toughness, Ouellet for goalie depth), and no pick to fund an acquisition with.

recommendations.summary: After the playoffs, trade Belfour (92 base, 39, $6.50M, expiring) via the over-80 expiring mechanic for a first- or second-round pick.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 91 base replaces him as number one. Belfour is the largest pick-recovery asset on the roster; keeping him past the playoffs costs nothing because he has no years left.

recommendations.summary: Trade Svehla (85 base, 36, $3.60M, expiring) in July for a pick.
recommendations.rationale: Above 80, expiring, surplus to eight other defensemen. The over-80 mechanic converts him into draft capital we currently lack.

recommendations.summary: Trade Roberts (87 base, 38, $2.70M, expiring) in July for a pick.
recommendations.rationale: Same mechanic as Svehla: above 80, expiring, surplus to depth at 38. Three pick-recovery moves recover 3+ picks from a position where we own one fourth-rounder.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik (91 base, 22, $1.10M, expiring) on 5-6 years before July.
recommendations.rationale: Highest-base player on the roster at 91, age 22, and currently at the league minimum. Without a long deal he hits the market as a restricted-free-agent summer and every club with cap space calls.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle (84 base, 26, $1.90M, expiring) on 5-6 years.
recommendations.rationale: Premier offensive defenseman entering his prime years. At 26 and 84 base he is the roster's best blueliner by a wide margin over Eminger at 76 base.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards (82 base, 24, $1.00M, expiring) on 5 years.
recommendations.rationale: 82 base at age 24 on $1.00M is elite value. Five years locks a young top-six centre at a below-market salary through his entire prime.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash (77 base, 20, $1.20M, expiring) on 5-6 years.
recommendations.rationale: Age 20 with 77 base and room to grow. A five-year lock at current salary buys development for free.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger (76 base, 21, $1.20M, expiring) on 5-6 years.
recommendations.rationale: GM protected Eminger on January 19 over Chara because of his POTE 99 at 21. Five-year lock at $1.20M commits no risk and captures whatever the potential delivers.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Abid (79 base, 24, $400K, expiring) on 2-3 years.
recommendations.rationale: The internal toughness fix. At 24 with 79 base and $400K, a two-year deal is cheap insurance against the coach's fourth-line gap recurring.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Upshall (78 base, 21, $1.20M, expiring) on 2-3 years.
recommendations.rationale: 78 base at 21 is useful depth. Two years gives a read on whether he becomes a top-nine piece before committing longer.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Colaiacovo (72 base, 22, $1.10M, expiring) on 2-3 years.
recommendations.rationale: Depth defenseman at 22 with 72 base. Two years is the right length at this grade.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Alexeev (76 base, 23, $1.10M, expiring) on 2 years.
recommendations.rationale: 76 base at 23 is a middle-six forward with one more year of growth left. Two years matches the player.

recommendations.summary: Move Chistov (78 base, 21, $1.10M, expiring) in July if a fair offer arrives; otherwise renew on 2 years.
recommendations.rationale: He was already floated as trade bait (for Luongo, for Conroy, for Kovalchuk packages). At 21 with 78 base he has value to a rebuilding club. Decision depends on what else comes in by July.

recommendations.summary: Do not re-sign Smirnov (51 base, 20, $400K, expiring); release him.
recommendations.rationale: 51 base at 20 means he has not developed into an NHL-caliber player. The roster spot is better used by a drafted prospect or a free-agent signing.

recommendations.summary: Move Tellqvist (77 base, 25, $800K, expiring) in July or let him walk; he is the third goalie behind Luongo and Ouellet.
recommendations.rationale: The January 15 mandate was to give Tellqvist time to develop, but that was before Luongo arrived. With Luongo at 91 and Ouellet at 80 base with POTE 97, Tellqvist at 25 and 77 base has no path to games.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Mark Bell (CHI) to close the toughness and checking gaps on a two-year keeper deal at $900K.
recommendations.rationale: 91 TOUG, 89 CHKG at 24 with two years left. CHI at 48 points with 10 expiring and $23.59M profit are sellers. The coach has no player above 73 TOUG on the current roster. Package: Colaiacovo plus Safronov.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Barret Jackman (STL) at 23 on a three-year $700K deal to add 86 TOUG and 87 CHKG from the blue line.
recommendations.rationale: Jackman at 79 overall, 86 TOUG, 87 CHKG, 26 pts/53 GP, $700K, 3 years. STL at 48 points with 9 expiring are sellable. He is the Chara-type body the GM prefers at four years younger with two extra contract years, and respects the January veto on Chara.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Sean Avery (LA) at 24 on $400K with two years left as a faceoff-winning, physical fourth-line centre.
recommendations.rationale: 94 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG at $400K, two years, age 24. Production is 6 pts/54 GP and PENA 93 is a liability on the PK. LA at 54 points with 13 expiring are motivated sellers. The cost of being wrong is one cheap contract.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Craig Conroy (CGY) as a deadline rental centre if the GM wants production now over a keeper contract.
recommendations.rationale: 93 FACE, 67 pts/55 GP at 33 on $2.00M expiring. CGY at 44 points with 10 expiring. Costs Chistov plus a 4th, both assets the club does not plan to keep. Rental only; he walks in July unless a deal is struck at renewal.

recommendations.summary: Pursue the LA double (Cammalleri POTE 98, Frolov POTE 96, both 22 on $1.10M expiring) as a five-year top-six solution.
recommendations.rationale: Combined 76 points in 67 games at under 1.2 ppg each. LA at 54 points with 13 expiring cannot retain both. Package: Koltsov plus Chistov plus Ouellet. Acceptance uncertain; LA may want more for two POTE 96+ assets.

recommendations.summary: Robyn Regehr (CGY) at 84 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 24, $1.26M, three years is the backup option if STL decline Jackman.
recommendations.rationale: Slightly more expensive and less productive than Jackman but same profile: young tough D on a multi-year deal from a selling club. CGY at 44 points, 10 expiring.

recommendations.summary: Chara (OTT) at 88 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 54 pts/55 GP is reconsidered only if a cheaper package than the vetoed January proposal materialises.
recommendations.rationale: GM vetoed Chara+Havlat on Jan 19 for Eminger's timeline. That position holds. But 54 points from a D at 27 is top-pairing output and OTT at 52 points with 11 expiring and $26.28M profit are aggressive sellers. Only revisit if the cost is less than Colaiacovo plus Safronov.

recommendations.summary: Open negotiations with Chicago in late February: Colaiacovo plus Safronov for Bell, prepared to add St. Jacques if CHI push for a third piece.
recommendations.rationale: Bell closes the toughness and checking gap with the only keeper-grade option on the board. CHI at 48 points with $23.59M profit are selling; Colaiacovo at 22 with POTE 99 gives them a real asset. Base overall 80 means displayed 91 will regress and CHI may discount.

recommendations.proposed: Jackman (D, STL, 23, $700K, 3yr, 86 TOUG, 87 CHKG, 26 pts in 53 GP)
recommendations.summary: Open negotiations with St. Louis in late February: Koltsov plus St. Jacques for Jackman.
recommendations.rationale: Jackman at 23 on a 3-year $700K deal with 86 TOUG and 87 CHKG is the best value on the board. STL at 48 points with $14.63M profit are selling. Koltsov gives them a POTE 94 winger with 96 ACCE. Neither Koltsov nor St. Jacques contributes to the toughness gap.

recommendations.summary: Open negotiations with Los Angeles in late February: Chistov plus the fourth-rounder for Avery.
recommendations.rationale: Avery's 94 FACE fixes the fourth-line draw problem outright. LA at 54 points with 13 expiring are selling everything; Avery's 6 points in 54 games makes him replaceable. At $400K for 2 years the downside is negligible even though PENA 93 and ENDU 50 cap his role.

recommendations.proposed: Draft pick via over-80 expiring mechanic
recommendations.summary: Identify a contender with a goalie need and propose trading Belfour one-way for a draft pick before the March deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour qualifies for the over-80 expiring mechanic, the only route to recover pick capital after the Luongo deal spent the first-rounder. He frees $6.50M. Luongo is the starter. Acceptance depends on finding a contender who needs a backup and will absorb $6.50M.

recommendations.summary: Goalie monitoring task is closed; Luongo is on the roster at 91 base with 2 years left and DiPietro remains a re-signing target for NYI.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 39 GP, 91 base, $1.60M fulfills the Jan 15 mandate. DiPietro's 22-15-0 and 2.97 GAA is a form cycle on a base that hasn't moved from 79; NYI will re-sign him at $1.10M.

recommendations.summary: Note Turco (DAL, 94 base, $600K, expiring) as the only remaining high-90s goalie available cheap; revisit only if Luongo's development stalls.
recommendations.rationale: 94 base at $600K on an expiring deal is the cheapest elite goalie in the league. No action needed while Luongo is performing, but he is the fallback.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle every night from here to the deadline. Two games in 55 at POTE 96 and age 20 is the worst waste on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: Stahle logged 17 MPG in his only two appearances, so he can handle the minutes. Colaiacovo at 22 with 30 games already played can sit for stretches. Both are healthy.

recommendations.summary: Reinstate Spezza to the fourth line. Raised six times; POTE 99 at 21 with 7.5 MPG and zero current ice time is not a plan.
recommendations.rationale: 15 points in 37 games at 0.41 per game is not a player who has lost his job, and at 21 he needs consistent minutes to consolidate anything.

recommendations.proposed: Smirnov (dress for 10-game stretch on fourth line)
recommendations.summary: Give Smirnov a 10-game run on the fourth line. Zero games in 55 at age 20 tells us nothing about whether he has a future here.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 70 is modest, so the run should be short and observed, not a season-long project. The point is information, not development at a specific level.

recommendations.summary: Safronov at 23 with POTE 91 has 3 games. He needs to be in the dressings as a rotation option before the window closes.
recommendations.rationale: Less urgent than Stahle because he is older and the development return is smaller, but three games in a season is a roster spot going to waste.

recommendations.summary: Gaborik, Chlup, Klesla, Nash, Chistov, Alexeev, Eminger — all dressed, all playing, all producing. No changes needed.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik 55 GP / 75 pts, Chlup 44 GP / 31 pts at 18, Nash 42 GP / 32 pts, Alexeev 55 GP / 30 pts at 8.3 MPG. These guys are getting what they have earned.

recommendations.summary: Upshall sits and has earned it. 17 points in 45 games at 0.38 per game is fourth-line output. No promotion, no grievance.
recommendations.rationale: His rate has been below 0.40 all season. The spot is open and he has not taken it.

recommendations.summary: Promote Chlup to the second line for a look; he is producing 0.74 pts/g on 16 MPG and climbing.
recommendations.rationale: Only young player in the window improving on both axes. At 18, rate rising from 0.62 to 0.74 with minutes up from 11 to 16.

recommendations.summary: Spezza at 5.3 MPG is a non-developer; he needs 12+ minutes or the year is wasted.
recommendations.rationale: Rate 0.38 on 5.3 MPG in recent window, down from 0.43 on 9.1 MPG at Dec 1. Raised six times now with no movement.

recommendations.summary: Do not trade Eminger this week; his recent rate (0.57) is pulling his season rate back above the threshold.
recommendations.rationale: Recent window 0.57 pts/g in 21 games vs 0.35 in first 23. Season rate recovering from 0.45. My Feb 6 sell call was premature on the trend.

recommendations.summary: Spacek needs either a return to 12+ MPG or a full scratch; 8.3 MPG is producing nothing at 19.
recommendations.rationale: Rate fell 0.55 to 0.43 while minutes halved from 16.0 to 8.3. Development happens at 12+ or not at all.

recommendations.summary: The room is healthy at 86-100 with average 92; no line or ice-time change is needed for morale against Edmonton.
recommendations.rationale: Lowest morale is Spezza at 86, flat for weeks and holding despite 7.5 MPG. Everyone else is 90+. No player is showing a minutes-driven morale slide that a line move could fix tonight.

recommendations.summary: Current lineup is the right one for EDM; we are superior on every line and the auto-pairing gives our top units their weakest defensive pairs.
recommendations.rationale: EDM's D pairs read 70/71, 66/66, and 61/61. Our lines read 88/95/85, 83/83/87, and 84/80/79. Their PP is 17/157 (10.8%). We won the only meeting 4-0. No development sacrifice needed because the current lineup already includes Nash, Spacek, and Kaberle at full strength.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo. 92 OVR against a 2.40-goal team with an 82-OVR goalie in the other net.
recommendations.rationale: EDM scores 2.40 per game. Luongo's displayed grades (95 glove, 95 stick, 95 agility) are the best in our crease. No fatigue flag shown. The GM took this recommendation Feb 7 and it worked.

recommendations.summary: Trade Eminger at the deadline on his expiring $1.2M deal; he's holding at 0.45 pts/g with no upward movement.
recommendations.rationale: 20 points in 44 games (0.45 pts/g), 21 years old, 74 OVR, one year left at $1.2M. He crossed the threshold Feb 6 and hasn't recovered.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle for every remaining game; he has 2 GP this season and needs to accumulate experience at 20.
recommendations.rationale: 0 points in 2 games at 68 OVR, age 20, $0.97M for 3 more years. He is the cheapest long-term asset on the blue line and has been invisible all season.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker on a checking line; his 83 CHKG and 70 TOUG are the highest displayed toughness and checking on any unlined forward.
recommendations.rationale: Three 80+ checkers (Svehla 83, Tucker 83, Upshall 80) are all not lined. Tucker at 29 and $1.3M with 92 CHKG base is the coach's cheapest answer to the checking depth problem without a trade.

recommendations.summary: Dress Svehla for checking minutes; 83 CHKG and 94 ENDU in one 36-year-old body is the only internal bridge between checking and stamina.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla is 90 speed, 83 CHKG, 94 stamina, 36 years old, and not lined. If he is not part of the playoff plan he should be moved at the deadline for a pick per the over-80 expiring mechanic (his contract status needs confirmation, but his grades qualify him for that asset recovery).

recommendations.summary: Avery is the single cheapest player in the league closing toughness, checking, and faceoffs in one move; LA at 48 points with 13 expiring deals will listen.
recommendations.rationale: Zero 80+ TOUG on roster and one 80+ FACE (Sundin). Avery at 93/83/88 on $400K for two years at age 25 is a starting-calibre fix on a re-signable deal, not a rental. LA's motivation is confirmed.

recommendations.proposed: Bell (CHI, C, 24, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, 80 base, $900K, 2yr)
recommendations.summary: Bell closes the same gaps as Avery at higher raw toughness (95 vs 83) but at twice the salary; keep him as the secondary target if LA says no.
recommendations.rationale: Bell at 95 TOUG is the only available player who would make the roster carry a genuine 80+ enforcer. The package (Colaiacovo plus Safronov per the restructured ask) costs defence depth that Eminger at 21 with POTE 99 could replace.

recommendations.summary: Do not trade from the top six. Twelve players at 80+ scoring and 22 at 80+ speed is the roster's greatest strength and does not need reinforcement.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik 98 speed at 22, Afinogenov 96 at 25, Koltsov 92 at 23 — the speed curve is young and deep. Every asset spent should go toward toughness and faceoffs, not toward a role already filled.

recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour ($6.50M, 39, 92 base, expiring) for a draft pick at the deadline or in early July; Luongo (91 base, 25, POTE 97, 2yrs) is the starter going forward.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is the largest expiring contract on the roster at $6.50M and qualifies for the over-80 expiring pick-recovery mechanic. With Luongo already on the roster at 91 base and 25 years old, Belfour's $6.50M buys no future. The Jan 15 order to keep him predates Luongo's arrival.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik (91 base, 74 pts, $1.10M, age 22) on a 5-6 year deal in July at or near his current salary before his market price rises.
recommendations.rationale: He is the team's leading scorer at 74 points, 22 years old, on $1.10M with one year left. Mid-contract renegotiation is impossible, so July is the only window. A full season at 91+ base pushes his next ask to $4-5M minimum.

recommendations.current: Richards, Nash, Eminger, Colaiacovo, Chistov, Upshall
recommendations.summary: Lock Richards ($1.00M, 54 pts), Nash ($1.20M, 32 pts, age 20), Eminger ($1.20M, POTE 99, age 21), Colaiacovo ($1.10M, POTE 99, age 22), Chistov ($1.10M, POTE 95, age 21) and Upshall ($1.20M, POTE 99, age 21) on 5-6 year deals in July.
recommendations.rationale: Combined salary $6.80M today for six players with POTE 88-99 who will each cost $3-5M in three years. This is the single largest lever on the next three seasons.

recommendations.summary: Trade Svehla ($3.60M, 36, scratched, expiring) for a pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic; he plays no role now.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla is scratched, 36 years old, POTE 55, on $3.60M expiring. The over-80 mechanic converts him to draft capital which the club desperately lacks.

recommendations.summary: Trade Roberts (38, 61 pts, $2.70M, expiring) at the deadline to a contender for a pick and/or young player; his production still has rental value.
recommendations.rationale: At 61 points in 54 games he has genuine rental value for a playoff team. Toronto already have Abid (63 pts, $0.40M), Alexeev (30 pts, age 23) and Nash (32 pts, age 20) covering his minutes at a fraction of the cost and age.

recommendations.proposed: draft pick or pick + young player
recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour before March 19 for a draft pick using the over-80 expiring mechanic; Luongo (91 base, 2yr) has replaced him as the number one.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 92 base, 39 years old, $6.50M, expiring. The GM's Jan 15 'Belfour stays' order was predicated on needing a number one goalie; Luongo arrived and that premise is met. He walks in July for nothing if not moved by March.

recommendations.summary: Trade Svehla before March 19 for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic; four established defencemen remain after him.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla is 85 base, 36, $3.60M, expiring. After him Toronto still has McCabe (82 base, 4yr), Fischer (82 base, 4yr), Salo (83 base, 2yr), Klesla (78 base, 2yr) plus Eminger and Colaiacovo developing. We do not intend to re-sign a 36-year-old at $3.60M.

recommendations.summary: Trade Roberts before March 19 for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic; age 38 and $2.70M expiring makes re-signing wrong.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts is 87 base, 38, $2.70M, expiring. We have Gaborik (91), Sundin (90), Mogilny (90), Afinogenov (85) ahead of him on the wing. He walks in July for nothing if not moved now.

recommendations.summary: Offer Gaborik a five or six year deal the moment his contract expires in July; 91 base at age 22 on $1.10M is the roster's most valuable asset.
recommendations.rationale: 67 points in 45 games, POTE 90, age 22, base 91. Cannot renegotiate mid-contract so this is a July action. Prepare the offer now so a bidding war in July does not catch us unready.

recommendations.summary: Offer Kaberle five or six years in July; 84 base at age 26 on $1.90M is a top-pairing defenceman at below-market cost.
recommendations.rationale: Kaberle is the established top-pairing D on the roster at 26. His base of 84 puts him ahead of McCabe (82) and Fischer (82). Lock him before his value rises further.

recommendations.summary: Offer Richards five or six years in July; 82 base at age 24 with faceoff ability on $1.00M is the cheapest centre of his quality in the league.
recommendations.rationale: Richards at 82 base, 24, and $1.00M is the kind of player you cannot replace at his price. Five-year lock removes him from the market permanently.

recommendations.summary: Offer Eminger five years in July; 21 years old, POTE 99, $1.20M is the highest-upside defenceman on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: The GM kept Eminger over Chara specifically because his POTE 99 and age 21 make him the timeline asset. His contract expires this summer. Five-year lock at low cost is the only option that protects that investment.

recommendations.summary: Offer Nash five years in July; 77 base at age 20 with development upside on $1.20M.
recommendations.rationale: At 20 with a 77 base he has time to grow into a regular. Five years at his current price is cheap for a top-six wing if he develops even modestly.

recommendations.summary: Offer Abid two or three years in July at or near $0.40M; 79 base toughness and checking at four hundred thousand is the cheapest role player available.
recommendations.rationale: Base TOUG 80 and CHKG 80 at age 24 for $400K. Renew cheaply so the coach can dress him without a financial penalty.

recommendations.summary: Release Smirnov at season end; 51 base overall at age 20 after zero games in a full season means development has stalled permanently.
recommendations.rationale: Coach flagged him on Feb 6 for zero games. His base overall of 51 is below any useful role. The $400K is immaterial; the roster spot is not.

recommendations.summary: Offer Chistov, Upshall, Alexeev and Colaiacovo two-year deals in July at current salary or slightly below; all are depth players with no reason to overpay.
recommendations.rationale: All four are 76-78 base, ages 21-23, $1.10-1.20M. Two years keeps them cheap without overcommitting if they plateau. If one walks, replace with a draft pick collected at the deadline.

recommendations.summary: Do not buy a defenceman, scorer, or backup goalie at the deadline; the roster at 38-9-4 with four 85+ base forwards and four established 78+ base defencemen needs nothing.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik (91), Sundin (90), Mogilny (90), Afinogenov (85) up front. McCabe (82), Fischer (82), Salo (83), Klesla (78) on the back end plus Luongo (91) in net. The manual says if the roster is already strong, do nothing.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Sean Avery from LA to close toughness (83 TOUG), checking (88 CHKG), and faceoff (94 FACE) gaps in one move at $400K with two years of control.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto have zero players at 80+ TOUG and only Sundin above 75 FACE. Avery at 25 is the only available player closing all three gaps with years of control. LA are 16-24-6 with 13 expiring deals and will deal him for depth. Price should be a bottom-six forward plus a 4th.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Barret Jackman from STL: 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, age 23, $700K, three years left. The only long-term toughness answer on the blue line.
recommendations.rationale: Jackman at 23 already carries 30.7 MPG and 26 points. STL are 14-27-4 rebuilding. The three-year deal means STL will want a strong package — likely a top-4 defenceman or two young players. Toronto's candidates: Svehla ($3.60M expiring, 36) plus a young blueliner.

recommendations.summary: Target Mike Komisarek from MTL: 64 points in 54 GP, POTE 91, age 23, $1.10M expiring. Best production-to-cost ratio on the board.
recommendations.rationale: Komisarek is putting up 1.19 pts/game at 29.6 MPG for a 15-30-4 club. His POTE 91 and age 23 make him a five-year asset if acquired. MTL with 14 expiring deals are the league's most motivated seller. Risk: MTL may keep him as a core piece.

recommendations.summary: Kovalchuk at 92 points in 52 games, age 21, $1.10M expiring from ATL. Highest-ceiling target remaining after Luongo spend.
recommendations.rationale: ATL cannot keep both Kovalchuk and Heatley on expiring deals. Original package (R1 plus Koltsov) is dead because the R1 went to Florida. New package must be player-funded: Svehla ($3.60M, 36, expiring) plus Chistov plus a 4th gives ATL salary and a prospect.

recommendations.summary: Heatley at 85 points in 49 games, age 24, $1.10M expiring. ATL binary with Kovalchuk — whichever ATL does not re-sign becomes the sole target.
recommendations.rationale: Same ATL situation as Kovalchuk. Heatley is three years older with slightly less upside but the same immediate production. If ATL re-sign Kovalchuk, Heatley's price drops to a depth package.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Martin Havlat standalone from OTT: 71 points in 54 games, age 23, $900K expiring. The GM's Chara veto was about Eminger's cost, not Havlat's.
recommendations.rationale: The Jan 19 veto killed the Chara+Havlat package priced at Eminger plus Colaiacovo plus R2. A standalone Havlat priced with Chistov plus a 4th or Svehla as salary filler is a different calculus. OTT at 19-25-6 with 11 expiring are sellers.

recommendations.summary: Matt Walker from STL: 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, $500K expiring, age 24. A pure playoff-toughness rental at negligible cost.
recommendations.rationale: Walker produces almost nothing offensively (7 points in 42 games) but his 95 TOUG and 93 CHKG are the best in the league at his price. STL at 14-27-4 will take a 4th rounder plus a body. Solves the playoff-toughness problem for a single series.

recommendations.summary: Craig Conroy from CGY: 64 points, 87 FACE, $2.00M expiring, age 33. Rental centre who wins draws against Ottawa/Philadelphia/New Jersey.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 16-29-6 are the league's worst and will deal him. The Jan 30 price (Chistov plus a 4th) is affordable but competes with Avery for the same asset. Prefer Avery if LA engage because Avery has two years of control.

recommendations.summary: Jay Bouwmeester from FLA: POTE 95, age 21, 81 base, $1.20M expiring, 32 MPG. Long-term partner for whoever plays opposite Eminger in 2006-07.
recommendations.rationale: FLA at 17-27-7 with 19 expiring deals are the most desperate sellers in the league. Bouwmeester at 21 with POTE 95 and already a top-pairing player is the highest-ceiling defenceman available. The risk is FLA keeping him as a franchise piece.

recommendations.summary: Marc Savard from ATL: 57 points, 89 FACE, age 27, $1.00M expiring. Fold into the ATL conversation alongside Kovalchuk or Heatley.
recommendations.rationale: Savard fills the faceoff hole at age 27 on a re-signable deal. ATL with 11 expiring contracts are motivated. If a Kovalchuk or Heatley package needs another asset to balance, Savard can be added at marginal cost.

recommendations.summary: Checking does not require a trade. Svehla (83 CHKG), Tucker (83), and Upshall (80) are all unlined and available.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach's problem is usage, not personnel. Three 80+ checkers collecting a paycheck without dressed status. Dress two of them for the playoffs and the gap closes internally.

recommendations.summary: Move Belfour to a playoff contender for a first-rounder via the over-80 expiring mechanic; Luongo is the starter and the pick fills the draft capital hole.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour at 92 base and $6.50M expiring qualifies for pick recovery. A top-8 club needing goalie insurance gets the league's best GAA on a rental they won't re-sign. We get the first-rounder spent on Luongo, recovering draft ammunition that has been empty since January.

recommendations.current: Chistov (TOR, LW, 21, POTE 95, 89 SPEE, $1.10M expiring) + 4th round pick
recommendations.proposed: Sean Avery (LA, C, 25, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 94 FACE, $400K, 2 years)
recommendations.summary: Package Chistov and the 4th to LA for Avery, who closes toughness, checking, and faceoff gaps simultaneously on a two-year deal at $400K.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 16-24-6 with 13 expiring deals are rebuilding and should value a 21-year-old POTE 95 prospect at $1.10M over a bottom-six forward with 6 points in 53 games. Avery at 83 TOUG is the only displayed 80+ toughness player available on a re-signable deal. Chistov is one of seven POTE 94+ players we cannot dress every night.

recommendations.current: Smirnov (TOR, LW, 20, POTE 70, 0 GP, $0.40M expiring) + 4th round pick
recommendations.proposed: Matt Walker (STL, D, 24, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, $500K, 1 year)
recommendations.summary: Acquire Walker as a playoff rental for toughness and checking; STL will take a zero-GP prospect plus the 4th to clear his expiring salary.
recommendations.rationale: Walker at 95 TOUG and 93 CHKG is the single highest-displayed toughness and checking combination in the league. STL at 14-27-4 are selling and want to shed $500K. We give Smirnov who has played zero games and the 4th we were never going to use elsewhere. If both Avery and Walker land, the toughness gap closes twice.

recommendations.summary: Luongo monitoring task is complete; he is on the roster at 91 base with 2 years left. No further February tracking needed.
recommendations.rationale: The Jan 15 mandate to acquire a high-90s goalie from a non-contender is fulfilled. Luongo is 38 GP, 2.90 GAA, 87.3% this season at $1.60M with 2 years of control.

recommendations.summary: Decide by late February whether Belfour (90 base, $6.50M expiring, 2.27 GAA in 21 GP) stays as playoff insurance or becomes a March pick-recovery trade.
recommendations.rationale: He is the club's cleanest over-80 expiring player. The GM's standing order holds negotiations until late February. Either path is viable; the decision just needs to be made before the window opens.

recommendations.summary: Dress Spezza tonight against Montreal and give him 12+ minutes at third-line centre.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 at 21, 7.5 MPG and 0.41 pts/g in 37 games. Montreal at 15-30 is a development-friendly opponent. Sixth time raising this; if February passes without change his development year is wasted.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle tonight and give him real shifts, or put him on the trade list.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 96 at 20, 2 GP in 54 games. No path through Klesla, Eminger, McCabe, Svehla, or Colaiacovo this season. Montreal is a manageable opponent to start him.

recommendations.summary: No promotion for Upshall. Keep him fourth line or scratch him.
recommendations.rationale: Rate has slid from 0.69 to 0.38 across 45 games at 10.7 MPG. The development signal is fading. No reason to increase his load.

recommendations.summary: Ouellet cannot develop as a third-string goalie at 23 with POTE 97. Move him if a deal appears.
recommendations.rationale: 8 GP across 54 team games. He is behind Belfour and Luongo with no path to meaningful minutes here.

recommendations.summary: Spezza at 5.3 MPG is a sixth season at POTE 99 with no development happening. Give him 10+ minutes on a real line or accept this year is lost.
recommendations.rationale: Minutes fell 9.1 to 5.3 and rate fell 0.43 to 0.38 in the recent window. He is 21. The rotation philosophy covers Nash and Spacek sitting; it does not explain why Spezza is buried.

recommendations.summary: Eminger's recent window is 0.55 pts/g, above the 0.45 trade threshold. His season total crossed it but the trend is up, not down. Hold unless the final weeks reverse him.
recommendations.rationale: Brief shows 0.35 before Dec 1 rising to 0.55 since. The original sell call assumed a declining player. He is the opposite in the recent window.

recommendations.summary: Koltsov's recent rate is 0.33 pts/g. If he is being shopped at the deadline, the asking price should already reflect a collapsing rate.
recommendations.rationale: Brief shows 1.10 before Dec 1 dropping to 0.33 since. 21 games at 0.33 will kill any trade interest at his original value.

recommendations.summary: Chlup at 0.73 pts/g on 15.8 MPG at 18 is developing on schedule. Leave the second line intact and give him the rest of February.
recommendations.rationale: Rate up from 0.62, minutes up from 11.0. No intervention needed.

recommendations.summary: No morale-driven changes needed for Tuesday. The room is at 92 or above across the board except Spezza, who is a structural issue the GM controls.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza at 86 morale on 7.5 MPG is the only player below the 90 threshold. He has been at 86 for weeks with no movement; the cause is the development rotation the GM runs deliberately. Everyone else is 92+ with stable or rising morale.

recommendations.summary: Watch Mogilny's morale at 92; if it drops below 90 he loses his grade bonus and needs more minutes.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny is 92 on 17.8 MPG and 61 points in 50 games. At 90-calibre he expects 20 MPG. Two more points of slip and he drops into the minus-1 band at age 35. No change today but worth monitoring next save.

recommendations.summary: No player on the roster carries toughness above 69; we cannot field a physical fourth line or match an enforcer line.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts 69, McCabe 69, Abid 68, Fischer 68 is the entire top of the toughness chart. Against a club that dresses a 75+ enforcer we have no answer.

recommendations.summary: Fourth line faceoff win rate is 50/50; nobody on L4 can win a draw, so this line loses possession from the start of every shift.
recommendations.rationale: After Sundin (86) and Chlup (75), the next-best faceoff man is Richards at 70 who already centres L3. No fourth-line option exists on this roster.

recommendations.summary: Lines are correctly assembled for their roles; composition changes would cost chemistry without solving the gaps.
recommendations.rationale: L1 checks, L2 scores, L3 balances, L4 provides speed (74 mean). The unit grades match their intended function given available personnel.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo. 91 OVR against a 2.5-goal-per-game team is the easiest start on the schedule.
recommendations.rationale: Montreal scores 2.50 per game and their entire roster tops out at 79 OVR. Luongo at 91 gets a low-danger night that preserves his freshness for harder matchups.

recommendations.summary: No line changes for matchup reasons. Montreal has no player above 79 OVR; our top four (94, 87, 86, 84) overwhelm their top six without adjustment.
recommendations.rationale: Their first line is Koivu 79, Bulis 72, Sundstrom 68. Our first line is Gaborik 94, Sundin 87, Roberts 84. The quality gap is the widest on our schedule and no tactical adjustment improves it.

recommendations.summary: Trade McCabe before the deadline. His rate has dropped from 0.96 to 0.91 season-wide with a recent window near 0.25, and his $3.00M x 3 remaining years means value erodes every week.
recommendations.rationale: Jan 26 reading was 48/50 = 0.96. Brief today shows 49/54 = 0.91, meaning 1 point in 4 games (0.25 pts/g in that window). At 29 and declining, the trade window is closing.

recommendations.summary: Trade Eminger as a rental. He has added 0 points since February 6th, sitting at 0.44 season rate, below the 0.45 threshold set for him.
recommendations.rationale: Brief shows 19 pts in 43 GP = 0.44. My Feb 6 note set 0.45 as the trade line. He has not recovered. Expiring $1.20M at 21 makes him a useful rental for a contender needing a third-pair body.

recommendations.summary: McCabe stays on the top pair tonight against Montreal until a trade is completed.
recommendations.rationale: 0.91 season rate is still the best on the roster by a wide margin. Nothing changes in the lineup until a deal is done.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker nightly at 83 CHKG to fill the checking depth the coach flagged.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker has 83 checking and is in no unit. The coach has McCabe at 86 as the only lined 80+ checker. Tucker is the internal fix.

recommendations.summary: Dress Abid as the physical presence he was signed for; base TOUG 80 and CHKG 80 at 24 with 63 points in 49 games.
recommendations.rationale: He is on the roster in no unit. Even if his displayed toughness has dipped below 80 with form, he is the most physical forward available without a trade.

recommendations.summary: Dress Koltsov; 92 SPEED and 23 years old with no unit assignment is wasted depth.
recommendations.rationale: He is not lined per the brief. At 92 speed he gives the third or fourth line a breakaway threat no one else on the bottom six provides.

recommendations.summary: Avery at 93 FACE, 88 CHKG, 83 TOUG and $400K closes toughness, checking, and faceoffs in one move from a seller with 13 expiring deals.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 48 points is selling. Avery costs less than any other option closing all three gaps. Safronov or Chistov are the proposed returns.

recommendations.summary: Bell at 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE on $900K with two years left is the premium version of the Avery fix, younger and higher-ceiling on the toughness side.
recommendations.rationale: Chicago are profitable and not desperate, so acceptance requires Colaiacovo plus Safronov per the restructured ask. His 95 toughness is the only grade on the market that makes our top six genuinely physical.

recommendations.summary: Komisarek at 77 base, POTE 91, age 22, $1.10M expiring gives Toronto a shutdown partner for Kaberle and replaces Svehla at 36.
recommendations.rationale: MTL at 12-24-4 with 14 expiring contracts are in full rebuild. Our defensive age curve past McCabe is empty without him.

recommendations.summary: Luongo at 91 base, POTE 96, age 25, $1.60M with two years is the confirmed goalie mandate. Package: own R1 plus Chistov.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour at 39 and $6.50M expiring cannot be replaced internally at this level. Ouellet at 85 base is the ceiling without a trade. The GM's Jan 15 order says fetch a high-90s goalie from a non-contender; FLA at 91 fits.

recommendations.summary: Stahle at 20 with POTE 96 has played 2 games in 53. He needs 15+ MPG starting now or this year is lost.
recommendations.rationale: The coach flagged this. The numbers confirm it: 2 GP in a 53-game season at age 20 with the highest potential on the blue line after Eminger.

recommendations.summary: Spezza at 21 with POTE 99, morale at 86 (lowest on roster), averaging 7.5 MPG over six consecutive windows. He needs 12+ MPG or we lose a year.
recommendations.rationale: The coach's flag is correct. At 21 with the highest potential on the roster, five-to-nine minutes per night is not development.

recommendations.summary: Trade Belfour before the March deadline for a first-round pick using the over-80 expiring mechanic; Luongo has 37 starts this season and Belfour at 39, POTE 50, $6.50M is surplus.
recommendations.rationale: The GM's Jan 15 order had Belfour as number one. Luongo now carries 37 GP and Belfour 21. The pick drought (no R1 owned) is the binding constraint on all future moves; recovering one from an over-80 expiring asset is the only path to it.

recommendations.summary: Trade Svehla (36, $3.60M, POTE 55, scratched) and Roberts (38, $2.70M, POTE 52) before March for mid-round picks via the expiring mechanic; both are over 80 and neither is in the lineup.
recommendations.rationale: Together they free $6.30M and recover two picks. The roster has 16 players at 23 or under; it needs draft capital to maintain that depth, not veteran bodies at 36 and 38.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik, Richards, Nash, and Eminger on 5-6 year deals in July 2005 at the top of the budget; their combined current salary is $4.50M and renewed they cost $14-16M, affordable against $23.95M profit and $12.80M of freed veteran money.
recommendations.rationale: These four at ages 22, 24, 20, 21 with POTE 90, 88, 95, 99 are the core for the next five seasons. Staggering their terms across 5 and 6 years splits the next cluster. Without locking them, they walk in July and the 16-player youth core evaporates overnight.

recommendations.summary: Begin planning a Mogilny exit for this deadline or next July; at 35, $5.50M, POTE 55 with 61 points he has one more window to fetch a real return before the decline makes him untradeable.
recommendations.rationale: He produces now but POTE 55 at 35 means regression is guaranteed. At summer 2006 he will be 36 on $5.50M with a falling number. The pick recovery from Belfour and Svehla funds the replacement centre; Mogilny's trade return adds to it.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla (85 base, 36, $3.60M expiring) for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic before the March 19 deadline
recommendations.rationale: Svehla is over 80 and expiring; the guide notes this mechanic trades him for a pick without needing a motivated buyer. He is 36 and will not be re-signed, so his value is the pick he recovers plus $3.60M freed.

recommendations.summary: Move Roberts (87 base, 38, $2.70M expiring) for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic before the March 19 deadline
recommendations.rationale: Same mechanic as Svehla: 87 base, expiring, 38 years old. $2.70M freed, one more pick recovered. Together with Svehla this clears $6.30M and may recover the first-rounder Florida demands for Luongo.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik (RW, 22, 91 base, POTE 90, $1.10M expiring) on a 5-6 year deal at the start of free agency
recommendations.rationale: Best player on the roster at 91 base and 22 years old. At $1.10M he is massively underpaid for production and will attract every club in July. Staggered lock plan puts him in the 5-6 year tier.

recommendations.summary: Lock Kaberle (D, 26, $1.90M expiring) on a 5-6 year deal; he is the veteran top-pair blueliner the young D corps needs alongside Eminger
recommendations.rationale: 26 is the right age to lock long. Releasing him while Eminger (21, POTE 99) is still developing leaves the blue line thin. 5-6 years staggers against Eminger's renewal in a couple of seasons.

recommendations.summary: Lock Richards (C, 24, $1.00M expiring) on a 5-6 year deal
recommendations.rationale: 24 years old, faceoff duty on the third line, cheapest centre on the roster. The staggered core lock plan puts him in the 5-6 year group with Gaborik, Nash, and Kaberle.

recommendations.summary: Lock Nash (LW, 20, $1.20M expiring) on a 5-6 year deal
recommendations.rationale: 20 years old, first-round talent, core lock. 5-6 years at $1.20M is the cheapest possible lock for a future top-six winger.

recommendations.summary: Lock Eminger (D, 21, $1.20M expiring) on a 5-6 year deal
recommendations.rationale: GM vetoed trading Eminger for Chara on 2005-01-19, explicitly saying POTE 99 at 21 is worth more than Chara at 27. He is the future top-pair D and needs a long deal.

recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour (G, 39, $6.50M expiring) a reduced deal at renewal; plan for his departure if he declines
recommendations.rationale: GM's own standing order from Jan 15: 'I would offer him a reduced contract at renewal but he probably won't accept.' At $6.50M and 39, this is the single largest payroll item and the most likely departure.

recommendations.summary: No deadline blueliner needed; Eminger (21, POTE 99), Colaiacovo (22), and Stahle (20, POTE 96) cover next season's blue line
recommendations.rationale: The Coach flags Stahle at 2 GP in 53 games and needs ice time, but that is a lineup decision. The roster already has three young D with real potential; buying another at the deadline blocks their development and spends a pick we are trying to recover.

recommendations.proposed: Komisarek (MTL, D, 23, 80 ovr, 83 TOUG, 64 pts, POTE 91, $1.10M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Package Upshall plus 4th-rounder to Montreal for Komisarek when negotiations open late February
recommendations.rationale: MTL at 15-30-4 with 14 expiring deals will not re-sign a defenceman they can only rent; they collect youth. Upshall's POTE 99 is expendable because Spezza (POTE 99) and Chlup (POTE 95) already sit ahead of him. Commission closes the toughness gap from the blueline for five years.

recommendations.current: Colaiacovo (22, POTE 99, D, $1.10M) + Tucker (29, 92 CHKG, $1.30M, 3 GP)
recommendations.summary: Offer Colaiacovo plus Tucker to Ottawa for Havlat; OTT's $26M profit absorbs both salaries
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 18-25-6 with 11 expiring deals are comfortable sellers. Colaiacovo at POTE 99 gives them a long-term defenceman; Tucker at 92 CHKG fills their bottom-six immediately. Havlat's 70 points at 23 fills the secondary-scoring hole behind Gaborik without touching the core.

recommendations.current: Chistov (21, POTE 95, 16 pts, $1.10M) + Safronov (23, POTE 91, D, $0.90M)
recommendations.summary: Send Chistov plus Safronov to Calgary for Conroy as a pure faceoff rental through the playoffs
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 16-29-6 with 42 points are the worst team and motivated to shed salary. They get two players with three total team-years of control for an expiring 31-year-old. Conroy's 94 FACE is the only way to win draws against a first line that dumps in; Chistov's 16 points in 39 games is not core production at 21 when Alexeev (30 pts, POTE 94) already sits ahead.

recommendations.proposed: Luongo as starter through playoffs, Belfour as backup and insurance
recommendations.summary: Carry both Luongo (91, $1.60M, 2yr) and Belfour (92 base, $6.50M, expiring) through the playoffs; decide Belfour's renewal in July.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 18-3-0 in 21 starts; Luongo is morale 99 at 91 base. Toronto at 38-9-3 can afford the platoon and the $6.50M is expiring. No need to move either before July.

recommendations.summary: Put Spezza back in the lineup at third-line centre minimum 10 MPG; his morale at 86 is the lowest on the roster and he has POTE 99 at 21 with 7.5 MPG and a scratch.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza's 7.5 MPG and scratch status have held his rate at 0.41 pts/g while his morale drops. Every other scratched youngster has a reason (Koltsov is a chip, Upshall isn't producing, Smirnov has POTE 70). Spezza does not.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle and give him real minutes; 2 GP in 53 games at POTE 96 and age 20 is not development, it's neglect.
recommendations.rationale: Stahle played 17 MPG in his 2 appearances, showing the staff trusts him when he suits up. He needs consistent dressings before the deadline to build anything.

recommendations.summary: No changes needed for Gaborik, Nash, Chlup, Klesla, Eminger, Colaiacovo, or Chistov — they are all getting appropriate minutes and production for their age and role.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik leads the team in points (73 in 53). Nash at 20 is producing 0.80 pts/g on the third line. Chlup at 18 plays second-line minutes. The young D pair (Klesla, Eminger) and Colaiacovo are all in the lineup.

recommendations.summary: Upshall and Smirnov stay scratched — Upshall's 0.38 pts/g doesn't justify a promotion despite POTE 99, and Smirnov's POTE 70 is the lowest on the list.
recommendations.rationale: Upshall has had 45 games to show his POTE 99 and has 17 points on 10.7 MPG. Smirnov has zero games but the lowest scouting number among the young group. Neither warrants a lineup spot over producing players.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza 12+ MPG starting now; six consecutive windows at 5-9 MPG means he is losing a year.
recommendations.rationale: Minutes collapsed from 9.1 to 5.3 MPG, rate fell from 0.43 to 0.38 in 37 games. At 21 with POTE 99, 5.3 MPG is not development.

recommendations.summary: Dress Smirnov before the deadline; 20 years old and zero games in the entire season.
recommendations.rationale: Zero GP across both windows. Same situation Stahle was in before he finally got 2 games. At 20 he is wasting away.

recommendations.summary: Chlup stays where he is; 0.72 pts/g at 18 on 15.7 MPG is the right trajectory and don't disrupt it.
recommendations.rationale: Rate climbing from 0.62, minutes climbing from 11.0, still 18. Let him develop naturally.

recommendations.summary: Chistov earns his spot on the first line: 0.48 pts/g on 15.3 MPG, both up sharply.
recommendations.rationale: Rate doubled from 0.29 to 0.48 in 39 games while minutes rose from 9.5 to 15.3. He belongs there.

recommendations.summary: No morale-driven changes tonight; only Spezza is below 90 (at 86) and that is the GM's deliberate rotation.
recommendations.rationale: Every other player reads 92+ with stable or rising trends. No minutes-related morale issue exists that a line change would fix.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour if his fatigue icon is clear; Luongo at 91 is the fallback.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour's ENDU 94 and REBC 88 suit a low-event game where TB generates only 1.80 goals per game. If the tired icon shows, switch to Luongo whose AGIL 93 and SREC 89 match Khabibulin's 92 OVR.

recommendations.summary: No line changes for Tampa Bay.
recommendations.rationale: Auto-pairing gives us favorable matchups on lines 2-4 (their L3 centres at 69 OVR) and our L1 has Gaborik at 94 against their top line. TB's PP is 10.9% so no PK adjustment needed. Current assignment already has all key players in.

recommendations.summary: Trade Eminger at the deadline — he hit the 0.45 pts/g threshold I set on January 26th and his $1.2M deal expires in June.
recommendations.rationale: 19 points in 42 games (0.45 pts/g), 73 OVR at 21, expiring contract. I set this exact threshold on Jan 26th. He's there now.

recommendations.summary: Salo at $2.6M x 2 with 8 points in 22 games and not dressed is dead money. Find a buyer before June.
recommendations.rationale: 0.36 pts/g, 30 years old, 79 OVR, two years remaining on a $2.6M contract. He is not in the lineup and the production does not justify the money.

recommendations.summary: Stahle has played 2 games in 53. He needs to be dressed and used regularly or we lose a year on a POTE-96 defenceman at 20.
recommendations.rationale: 2 GP, 34 total minutes, 0 points. Age 20, 67 OVR, POTE 96. The Jan 25 note said 'at least one dressing before the deadline' — he has two now, that's not enough.

recommendations.summary: Colaiacovo is a secondary trade candidate: 69 OVR, 0.43 pts/g, expiring $1.1M. Bundle with Eminger or let walk.
recommendations.rationale: 12 points in 28 games at age 22 with 69 OVR. The ceiling is third-pair. Expiring deal means value in a trade now or nothing in July.

recommendations.summary: Avery closes the toughness and faceoff gaps simultaneously at $400K and age 25, the cheapest single move that addresses both structural holes.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto have zero players at 80+ toughness and one at 80+ faceoffs (Sundin, 33). Avery at 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG fills both. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring deals are motivated sellers.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker nightly; his 83 CHKG adds a seventh 80+ checker at no cost.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker is on the roster at 83 displayed checking and 29 years old but carries no unit assignment. He is the only internal fix to the checking depth problem.

recommendations.summary: Scoring, speed, stamina, clutch and playmaking are all covered with 9-22 players at 80+; do not spend trade assets on these roles.
recommendations.rationale: The roster has 12 scorers, 22 speed players and 12 stamina players above 80. The gaps are toughness (0 at 80+) and faceoffs (1 at 80+). Spend only on those.

recommendations.summary: There is no successor to Sundin at faceoffs; the next-best centre draws at 75. This gap widens every season he plays.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin at 33 is already declining (0.93 pts/g, down from higher). Chlup at 75 and Richards at 70 cannot replace his 90. By 2006-07 Toronto would have no 80+ faceoff man.

recommendations.summary: The two best checkers on the blue line are 38 and 36; the next-best is McCabe at 86 and declining. The defensive core needs youth within two seasons.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts 86 CHKG at 38 and Svehla 83 at 36 are both past their peak. Fischer at 82 is declining per the coach (0.63 to 0.41). Eminger at 21 with POTE 99 is the internal answer but needs time.

recommendations.summary: Belfour is covered today but is 39 on $6.50M with one year left. The backup depth is a 76-average Tellqvist and an 8-game Ouellet. Luongo remains the target but the R1 Toronto need is blocked.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is playing 0.911 SV and will not be here next year at this salary. Tellqvist averages 76 across his goalie grades. Ouellet at 86 GSH shows promise in 8 games. The Luongo package requires a first-rounder Toronto do not own.

recommendations.summary: Move all three expiring 30+ veterans at the March deadline for draft picks using the over-80 expiring mechanic; recovers draft capital from zero.
recommendations.rationale: Combined $12.80M in expiring salary, all above 80 overall, none planned for re-signing. Belfour is the standing-order trade target. Svehla is already scratched. Roberts has no future. Each qualifies independently for the pick-recovery mechanic.

recommendations.summary: Lock the five expiring core players on long deals in July; accept the salary bump from $6.40M combined to roughly $11-13M and remove them from the 2005 cluster permanently.
recommendations.rationale: All five expire the same summer with POTE 88-99. The manual's warning about simultaneous renewals is exactly this. Locking at once is the only fix since mid-contract renegotiation is impossible. At current production (Gaborik 72 pts, Richards 53, Nash 31 at age 20) their renewal prices will only rise.

recommendations.proposed: acquire young asset or pick in return
recommendations.summary: Plan to move Mogilny (35, $5.50M, 0.87 pts/g, 2 years left) at the next deadline or in July 2006 while he retains trade value.
recommendations.rationale: His production halved from 1.62 to 0.87 pts/g. At $5.50M over two remaining years that is $11.00M for a third-line winger. By the time his deal expires he is 37 and untradeable.

recommendations.summary: Set a diary entry for July 2007: Chlup becomes a free agent at 20 with POTE 95 and his $2.34M rookie salary gone. Lock immediately.
recommendations.rationale: At 18 with 28 points in 41 games, his next contract will be set by a full top-nine season. The 2-year window is his last cheap year after this one.

recommendations.summary: Execute the December 22 three-deal package: Mogilny+R2 for Jackman, R3 for Sillinger, Safronov+R4 for Sutton.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny has halved to 0.87 pts/g at 35 on multiple years of contract. The package dumps his salary, adds toughness (Jackman), faceoffs (Sillinger 96 FACE), and depth (Sutton) for zero first-round capital. It has been pending since December and remains the best value on the board.

recommendations.proposed: Craig Conroy (CGY, C, 31, 63 pts, 94 FACE, $2.00M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Acquire Conroy as a deadline rental for Chistov plus a fourth-rounder.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 40 points is a confirmed seller with $2.00M expiring. Conroy's 94 FACE and 63 points fill the centre depth gap for the playoff run. Chistov at 21/$1.10M is the most movable young asset not flagged for development by the Coach.

recommendations.current: Svehla (D, 36, $3.60M, over-80, expiring) + Roberts (LW, 38, $2.70M, over-80, expiring)
recommendations.proposed: Draft pick via over-80 expiring mechanic
recommendations.summary: Trade Svehla and/or Roberts to a contender before March 19 to recover a mid-round pick.
recommendations.rationale: Both are above 80, expiring, and will not be re-signed. The mechanic trades them for a pick. This recovers draft capital that Toronto currently lacks (best owned pick is a fourth-rounder). Combined $6.30M freed is budget for a summer goalie.

recommendations.current: Gaborik (RW, 22, 91 base, 67 pts/45 GP, $1.10M, 1 year left)
recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik to 6 years immediately at season end; this is the first call of the summer.
recommendations.rationale: At 91 base with POTE 90 on $1.10M he is the cheapest top-line winger in the league. A 5-6 year deal is standard for a star.
